\title[Continuous CLD-positive potentials]{Continuous CLD-positive potentials\\and mixed currents}
\author{}
\date{15 November 2026}

\begin{document}
\begin{abstract}
Let \(K\) be a non-Archimedean completion of a number field and let
\(X/K\) be smooth and quasi-projective. A finite continuous function on an
ordinary open of \(X^\an\) has positive Chambert--Loir--Ducros curvature
current if and only if it admits smooth positive approximations on a
fixed neighbourhood of each point. The proof combines restriction to
curves, deterministic complete-intersection approximation, contact
rigidity, and continuity of semipositive envelopes. Contact rigidity
identifies a continuous curve-positive metric from its contact with a
uniform Fubini--Study limit.
On a fixed regular model, sums of divisor test ideals and global generation
give one-sided \(O(m^{-1})\) Fubini--Study approximations for model-obstacle
envelopes. A single projective extension then completes local regularization. As consequences, continuous current-positive potentials admit
symmetric mixed products with any positive closed CLD current, and these
products depend only on their curvature currents. We also obtain a
projective curve criterion under a regular-model hypothesis and positivity
of the prescribed Yuan--Zhang local mixed measures.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle
\setcounter{tocdepth}{1}
\tableofcontents
\clearpage

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Positivity of a Chambert--Loir--Ducros current is a condition on smooth
test forms. To construct positive mixed products, one must also control
\(\ddc(uT)\) for each intermediate positive closed current \(T\).
Multiplication by a continuous potential is available, but positivity
after differentiation requires an additional argument. Local
approximation by smooth functions with positive curvature provides
that argument. The first question addressed here is whether the
current inequality itself supplies such an approximation.

\subsection{Local regularization}
Fix a number field \(k\), a non-Archimedean place \(v\), and
\(K=k_v\), with its given absolute value. Its valuation ring is \(R\).
Choose a uniformizer \(\pi\) and set \(\lambda=-\log|\pi|>0\).
All smooth forms, positive cones, and currents in this paper are those
of the first version of Chambert--Loir--Ducros \cite{CLD12}.
In particular, positivity of currents is dual to the positive cone
of \cite[Definition 5.1.1(c)]{CLD12}. An \emph{ordinary open} is open
in the Berkovich topology.

Let \(X/K\) be smooth of pure dimension \(n\), let \(O\subset X^\an\)
be an ordinary open, and let \(u:O\to\R\) be finite and continuous.
For \(n\geq1\), the condition \(\ddc[u]\geq0\) means
\begin{equation}\label{eq:current-positive}
 \langle\ddc[u],\eta\rangle
 =\int_O u\,\ddc\eta\geq0
 \quad\text{for every positive }\eta\in\Ac^{n-1,n-1}(O).
\end{equation}
Every compactly supported smooth test is allowed. For components of
different dimensions the condition is imposed componentwise, and there
is no curvature condition in dimension zero.

We write \(u\in\Ploc(O)\) if every \(x\in O\) has one ordinary
neighbourhood \(V\subset O\) on which there are smooth functions \(u_j\)
with \(\ddc u_j\geq0\) as forms and \(u_j\to u\) uniformly on compact
subsets of \(V\). The neighbourhood is fixed for the entire sequence.

\begin{theorem}[Local regularization]\label{thm:main}
Let \(K=k_v\) be a non-Archimedean completion of a number field, with
its given absolute value. Let \(X/K\) be smooth and quasi-projective,
\(O\subset X^\an\) an ordinary open, and \(u:O\to\R\) finite continuous.
Then the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The original CLD curvature current \(\ddc[u]\) is positive on \(O\)
in the sense of \eqref{eq:current-positive}.
\item The function \(u\) belongs to \(\Ploc(O)\).
\end{enumerate}
After shrinking the fixed neighbourhood of each point once, the
approximating sequence can be chosen decreasing and uniformly convergent
on that neighbourhood.
\end{theorem}

The implication from smooth positive approximation to current positivity
follows by testing locally uniform convergence against \(\ddc\eta\).
The reverse implication does not assume that \(u\) is a difference of
approachable functions. The field and continuity hypotheses remain in
force throughout the theorem; in particular, the assertion does not
concern arbitrary upper-semicontinuous potentials. The proof is completed
in \namedref{Section}{subsec:regularization-proof}.

\subsection{Contact rigidity}
The projective argument uses a criterion that identifies a metric from
its contact with a semipositive lower metric. Recall that a \emph{pure
Fubini--Study metric} on an ample line bundle \(L\) is given by weights
\(m^{-1}\max_i\log|s_i|\), where the sections \(s_i\) generate \(mL\).
A \emph{uniform FS limit} is a uniform limit of such metrics.
A continuous metric is \emph{curve-positive} if its pullback by every
algebraic morphism from a smooth \(K\)-curve has positive Chern current.
These conventions are developed in \namedref{Section}{sec:metrics-curves}.

\begin{contactintro}[\namedref{Theorem}{thm:contact}]
Let \(Y/K\) be smooth, projective, and integral of dimension \(n\ge1\),
and let \(L\) be ample. Let \(p\) be a uniform FS limit on \(L\), and let
\(r\) be a finite continuous curve-positive metric on \(L\). Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:contact-intro}
 r\ge p,\qquad \int_{Y^\an}(r-p)c_1(L,p)^n=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad r=p.
\end{equation}
\end{contactintro}

The metric \(p\) need not be constructed as an envelope of \(r\).
The criterion uses the Monge--Amp\`ere measure of the lower metric and
positivity of the upper metric only on curves. It therefore applies
before a higher-dimensional positive product for \(r\) is available.
The proof in \namedref{Section}{subsec:contact-proof} passes curve Green
identities through complete-intersection approximation and then
transfers the contact identity to smooth divisors.

\subsection{Continuous mixed currents}
A current is called \emph{closed} below if both \(d'T=0\) and \(d''T=0\).
Positive currents admit multiplication by continuous functions
(\namedref{Lemma}{lem:continuous-coefficients}). Thus, for a positive closed
current \(S\), the recursive rule
\begin{equation}\label{eq:recursive-product}
 \mathcal B_S()=S,\qquad
 \mathcal B_S(u_1,\ldots,u_m)
 =\ddc\bigl(u_1\mathcal B_S(u_2,\ldots,u_m)\bigr)
\end{equation}
is meaningful whenever its intermediate currents are positive.
This is the usual Bedford--Taylor construction.

\begin{theorem}[Continuous potentials on a positive closed background]
\label{thm:background-products}
Let \(K=k_v\), let \(X/K\) be smooth quasi-projective of pure dimension
\(n\), and let \(O\subset X^\an\) be an ordinary open. Let \(S\) be an
original CLD positive current of bidegree \((p,p)\), where \(0\leq p\leq n\), with
\(d'S=d''S=0\). Suppose \(0\leq m\leq n-p\) and
\(u_1,\ldots,u_m:O\to\R\) are finite continuous functions with
\(\ddc[u_i]\geq0\). Then \eqref{eq:recursive-product} defines a positive
closed current of bidegree \((p+m,p+m)\). It has the following properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item It is local, symmetric in the potentials, additive and positively
homogeneous in each potential and in the background.
\item If \(S_a\to S\) on every compact smooth test, where all \(S_a\)
are positive and closed of bidegree \((p,p)\), and the finite
continuous functions \(u_{i,a}:O\to\R\) converge to \(u_i\) locally
uniformly with \(\ddc[u_{i,a}]\geq0\), then
\[
 \mathcal B_{S_a}(u_{1,a},\ldots,u_{m,a})
 \longrightarrow\mathcal B_S(u_1,\ldots,u_m)
\]
on every compact smooth test.
\item Each potential enters only through its curvature current:
if \(w\) is finite continuous and \(\ddc[w]=\ddc[u_i]\), replacing
\(u_i\) by \(w\) leaves the product unchanged.
\end{enumerate}
In top degree the product is a positive Radon measure.
\end{theorem}

The recursion is described in \cite[Section 5.6.8]{CLD12}.
For continuous psh potentials, its positivity, continuity, and symmetry
are established in
\cite[Lemma 8.5.5 and Propositions 8.7.2, 8.7.4]{CLD25}.
\namedref{Theorem}{thm:main} allows us to start from current positivity alone.
Potential independence then has a short two-sided proof. If \(\ddc[h]=0\), then both \(h\) and \(-h\) satisfy
\namedref{Theorem}{thm:main}. For every positive closed \(T\) this gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-sided-intro}
 \ddc(hT)\geq0,\qquad -\ddc(hT)=\ddc((-h)T)\geq0,
 \qquad\text{hence }\ddc(hT)=0.
\end{equation}
No representation of \(h\) as a piecewise-linear or logarithmic function
is required. \namedref{Theorem}{thm:background-products} concerns continuous
potentials; it does not assert a monotone convergence theorem for
bounded discontinuous ones. The theorem is proved in
\namedref{Section}{subsec:mixed-current-proof}.

\subsection{Adelic mixed measures}
For the arithmetic application, use the rational boundary completion of
\cite[Sections 2.4--2.5]{YZ}. Its objects retain the specified
line-bundle identifications. A strongly nef object has a Cauchy
presentation by nef model objects, and an integrable object is a
difference of two strongly nef objects, with rational tensor powers
allowed. The order defining the completion compares the full
Cartier-and-metric boundary datum, as recalled in
\namedref{Section}{sec:adelic}.

\begin{theorem}[Positivity of the prescribed adelic mixed measure]
\label{thm:adelic}
Let \(k\) be a number field, \(v\) a non-Archimedean place, and \(K=k_v\).
Let \(U/k\) be smooth quasi-projective of pure dimension \(n\geq1\).
Let \(\overline L_1,\ldots,\overline L_n\) be rational integrable adelic
line bundles with their specified identifications in the boundary
completion of \cite[Sections 2.4--2.5]{YZ}. Suppose their local weights
at \(v\) are finite continuous and have positive original CLD curvature
currents. Then the signed measure prescribed in
\cite[Sections 3.6.7--3.6.8]{YZ} is positive:
\[
 c_1(\overline L_1)_v\cdots c_1(\overline L_n)_v\geq0
 \quad\text{on }U_K^\an.
\]
\end{theorem}

The signed measure is defined by expanding integrable presentations.
Its positivity follows by identifying that expansion with the local
positive product of the target weights. This conclusion concerns the
given measure and does not assert arithmetic nefness of the factors.
The comparison is given in \namedref{Section}{subsec:adelic-proof}.

\subsection{Relation to earlier work}
Chambert--Loir--Ducros distinguish distributional positivity from local
psh approachability in \cite[Definition 5.6.3 and Remark 5.6.4]{CLD12};
their stable products are treated in
\cite[Corollary 5.6.5 and Section 5.6.8]{CLD12}.
The later continuous psh class is defined by uniform closure
\cite[Definition 8.1.7]{CLD25}. We do not identify a continuous
current-positive function with a member of that class before proving
\namedref{Theorem}{thm:main}.

On curves, Wanner compares CLD and Thuillier subharmonicity
\cite[Corollaries 4.8 and 5.4]{Wanner}.
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff provide descent, harmonic tropicalizations,
and smooth approximation \cite{GJRforms,GJRcurves}.
The finite residue field is important here: weakly smooth functions
on the relevant curves are CLD-smooth. \namedref{Section}{sec:metrics-curves}
retains the passage from the original current inequality over \(K\)
to those curve results.

Torus-invariant pluripotential theory is developed in \cite{BGJK}.
Piecewise-linear semipositivity and positivity tested on curves are
studied in \cite{GRpl,GRpsh}, and Wu compares local approximation
classes in \cite[Appendix A]{Wu}. Our starting hypothesis is instead
the original current inequality \eqref{eq:current-positive} for an
arbitrary finite continuous potential on a smooth variety.

The envelope argument follows the test-ideal method of
Fang--Gubler--K\"unnemann \cite{FGK}, using the mixed-characteristic
test ideals of \cite{BMP}. We use test ideals of section divisors directly.
The comparison on a higher normal model allows an
obstacle on a higher normal model while subadditivity is applied on
a fixed regular model. It is not a direct application of
\cite[Theorems 5.1 and 7.1]{FGK}. Orthogonality, once continuity is
established, is \cite[Theorem 6.7]{BGM}.
The final adelic application identifies a measure already constructed
by Yuan--Zhang; it does not introduce another mixed measure.

\subsection{Proof strategy}
The proof separates restriction, contact, and envelopes so that none
uses regularization in a form still to be established.

\emph{Step 1: restrict the current inequality and extend locally.}
In a normal disc, let
\(\beta_N=\ddc R_{2,\varepsilon}(\log|t|,-N)\), where
\(R_{2,\varepsilon}\) is a smooth convex regularized maximum.
For the zero section \(i:B\hookrightarrow B\times D_s\),
Poincar\'e--Lelong and continuous multiplication give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:normal-limit-intro}
 \beta_N\longrightarrow i_*[B],
 \qquad u\beta_N\longrightarrow i_*[u|_B].
\end{equation}

\title[Classical psh functions and mixed currents]{Locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic functions\newline and mixed currents}
\author{}
\date{10 November 2026}

\begin{document}
\begin{abstract}
Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and let $X$ be a good,
Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth $K$-analytic space. We prove that
every locally bounded classically plurisubharmonic function on $X$
is locally a decreasing limit of semipositive rational piecewise-linear
functions defined over $K$ on one fixed neighborhood. We use this
regularization to construct mixed currents in the original
Chambert--Loir--Ducros calculus. The unweighted currents are symmetric,
closed and strongly positive. Their coefficient measures are Radon
measures on the analytic space, so multiplication by a locally bounded
classical weight uses its given Borel representative. These weighted
products are jointly continuous along decreasing sequences with locally
bounded limits, and the construction is compatible with \'etale
pullback of the potentials. The regularization proof uses curve slicing,
projective contact rigidity, and continuity of ample envelopes on
normal models. A fixed vertical correction for mixed-characteristic
test ideals provides the envelope estimate.
\end{abstract}
\maketitle

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}
Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$. A classically
plurisubharmonic function on a Berkovich $K$-analytic space is an
upper-semicontinuous function whose pullback to every analytic curve,
after any complete extension of $K$, is subharmonic \cite{GR}.
This definition tests positivity on curves and does not require the
function to have a smooth local expression. The question addressed here
is whether locally bounded functions in this class admit decreasing
piecewise-linear approximation, and whether their curvatures have mixed
products in the Chambert--Loir--Ducros calculus.

For continuous semipositive potentials, uniform approximation provides
the mixed products. A locally bounded classical potential may be
discontinuous. The recursive construction then requires multiplication
of a current by a Borel function, and its continuity requires a limit
theorem in which both that function and the current vary. We prove
these assertions for the original CLD test forms. The approximation
takes place over $K$ on a fixed neighborhood of each point; all weighted
products use the given pointwise representatives.

\subsection{Definitions and main results}\label{sec:main-results}

\begin{convention}\label[convention]{conv:spaces}
Fix a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$ with its prescribed absolute
value. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ and put $\lambda=-\log|\pi|$.
Unless another field is specified, $X$ is a good, Hausdorff,
boundaryless, quasi-smooth $K$-analytic space of pure dimension
$n\geq1$. All opens are ordinary topological opens. A real function
is \emph{locally bounded} if it is bounded above and below on a
neighborhood of every point. No replacement on a null or polar set
is made.
\end{convention}

\begin{definition}\label[definition]{def:classes}
For an ordinary open $U\subset X$, let $\Cb(U)$ be the real-valued, locally bounded,
upper-semicontinuous functions $u$ such that, for every complete
isometric extension $F/K$ and every morphism $C\to U_F$ from an
$F$-analytic curve, the pullback of $u$ is subharmonic in the sense
of \cite[Definition~4.1 and \S3]{GR}.

Let $\PLsp(U)$ denote the continuous real piecewise-linear functions
semipositive in the local model, or equivalently reduction, sense of
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GR}. Define $\Rb(U)$ to be the locally
bounded functions $u$ such that every point has one ordinary
neighborhood $V\subset U$ and a sequence
\[
 p_m\in\PLsp(V),\qquad p_m\downarrow u|_V.
\]
The neighborhood is independent of $m$. On an algebraic chart,
\emph{rational} PL means rational slopes and constants in
$\lambda\mathbb Q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{convention}\label[convention]{conv:forms}
We use the original CLD forms $A^{p,q}$ and their compactly
supported test spaces $A_c^{p,q}$, with the canonical calibration.
Put $D=\dd$. A current of bidegree $(k,k)$ acts on
$A_c^{n-k,n-k}$. A symmetric current is called \emph{strongly
positive} if it is nonnegative on weakly positive complementary
original forms. The weakly positive cone is tested by decomposable
vectors; the strongly positive cone is generated by decomposable
squares. These conventions concern the original test sheaf, not the
larger weakly smooth sheaf of \cite{GJR}.

A metric is written additively in weights $-\log\|e\|$, so its
curvature is $D[-\log\|e\|]$. On a projective variety a continuous
\emph{model-semipositive} metric means a uniform limit of nef
rational model metrics on the same identified line bundle.
A \emph{bounded classical metric} is a metric whose local weights
are classical and whose difference from a continuous reference
metric is bounded. A rational \emph{pure Fubini--Study metric},
abbreviated pure-FS, is given by a finite generating tuple
$s_0,\ldots,s_N$ of a tensor power $mL$, with local weight
\[
 \frac1m\max_i\bigl(\log|s_i/e^{\otimes m}|+c_i\bigr),
 \qquad c_i\in\lambda\mathbb Q .
\]
After replacing $m$ by a multiple, the constants can be absorbed
by multiplying the sections by powers of $\pi$.
\end{convention}

The recursive formula for mixed currents will involve multiplying a
current by a locally bounded, possibly discontinuous function. The
following condition specifies the measures used for that multiplication.

\begin{definition}[Coefficient Radon currents]\label[definition]{def:coefficient-radon}
A current $T$ is of \emph{coefficient Radon type} if each finite
original moment presentation represents its coefficient functionals
by signed Radon measures on the analytic domain, compatibly
with all original smooth scalar functions, relations between forms,
and common refinements. In particular, for every compact original
test $\eta$, there is a signed Radon measure $\mu_{T,\eta}$ with
\[
 \int a\,d\mu_{T,\eta}=\langle T,a\eta\rangle
 \quad\text{for every original smooth scalar }a.
\]
For a locally bounded Borel function $h$, multiplication is
defined by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:borel-multiplication}
 \langle hT,\eta\rangle=\int h\,d\mu_{T,\eta}.
\end{equation}
The compatibility requirements make this definition independent of
the chosen presentation. A measure only on one tropical image does
not suffice for this definition.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Local decreasing regularization]
\label[theorem]{thm:local-regularization}
For every ordinary open $U\subset X$,
\[
 \Cb(U)=\Rb(U).
\]
For $u\in\Cb(U)$, the local approximants may be chosen rational PL,
defined over $K$ on one fixed neighborhood. Both classes are stable
under decreasing sequences whose pointwise limit is locally
bounded.
\end{theorem}
\noindent\hyperref[proof:local-regularization]{Proof on
p.~\pageref{proof:local-regularization}.}

\Needspace{15\baselineskip}
\begin{theorem}[Mixed currents]\label[theorem]{thm:mixed-currents}
For $u_1,\ldots,u_k\in\Cb(U)$, $0\leq k\leq n$, there are
coefficient Radon currents
\begin{equation}\label{eq:recursive-current}
 T_0=[1],\qquad
 T_k(u_1,\ldots,u_k)=D\bigl(u_1T_{k-1}(u_2,\ldots,u_k)\bigr).
\end{equation}
They are symmetric, $\dpr$- and $\dpp$-closed, strongly positive,
and multilinear on the cone in the differentiated arguments. They agree
with the continuous CLD products whenever the potentials are
continuous and semipositive. They are independent of decreasing PL
regularization and commute with ordinary restriction and gluing.
For $u_0\in\Cb(U)$, the weighted current
\begin{equation}\label{eq:source-current}
 S_k(u_0;u_1,\ldots,u_k)=u_0T_k(u_1,\ldots,u_k)
\end{equation}
uses the Borel multiplication of
\Cref{def:coefficient-radon}.
\end{theorem}
\noindent\hyperref[proof:main-currents]{Proof on
p.~\pageref{proof:main-currents}.}

\begin{theorem}[Joint decreasing continuity]
\label[theorem]{thm:joint-monotone}
Suppose that, for $0\leq i\leq k$, the functions
$u_{i,j}\in\Cb(U)$ decrease pointwise to a locally
bounded function $u_i$. Then
\[
 S_k(u_{0,j};u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{k,j})
 \longrightarrow S_k(u_0;u_1,\ldots,u_k)
\]
on every form in $A_c^{n-k,n-k}(U)$. The corresponding unweighted
currents also converge. In top degree these are locally weak
convergences of Radon measures, against every continuous
compactly supported scalar function.
\end{theorem}
\noindent\hyperref[proof:main-currents]{Proof on
p.~\pageref{proof:main-currents}.}

\begin{corollary}\label[corollary]{cor:quasiprojective}
The preceding results apply on every ordinary open in the
analytification of a smooth quasi-projective $K$-variety. Local
boundedness there imposes no boundedness condition at a deleted
algebraic boundary.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}[The undifferentiated argument]\label[remark]{rem:source-slot}
A constant in a differentiated argument has zero curvature. A change
$u_0\mapsto u_0+c$ in the undifferentiated argument changes $S_k$ by $cT_k$.
Thus $S_k$ is symmetric in $u_1,\ldots,u_k$, but not in all its
arguments. The weighted current may be signed and need not be closed.
The hypothesis on the limit in \Cref{thm:joint-monotone} is
essential to the stated class; for example, the decreasing constants
$-j$ have no locally bounded limit.
\end{remark}

\subsection{Proof strategy and relation to earlier work}
The proof has two parts. We first pass from the curve condition to
local decreasing regularization. We then use this regularization to
construct the mixed currents and prove their continuity. The first
part uses only first-order currents and products of continuous metrics,
so it does not presuppose the products in \Cref{thm:mixed-currents}.

The continuous products come from uniform approximation by semipositive
model metrics. Approximation by Fubini--Study metrics and by smooth
semipositive metrics is supplied by
\cite[Corollary~7.6 and Theorems~7.8, 7.14]{BE}, in the current calculus
of \cite{CLD12}. To treat a discontinuous classical potential $v$, we
slice a test presentation by algebraic curves. The curve condition
applies over the completed residue fields of the slicing points, even
when those fields are nondiscretely valued. Thuillier's lisse
approximation and Dirichlet energy \cite[\S\S3.4--3.5]{Thuillier}
give a positive Laplacian on each curve. Integrating these Laplacians
gives the first-order current $D[v]$, its coefficient measures, and the
Green formulas needed below. The lisse functions are auxiliary
piecewise-affine potentials on skeleta; the tests remain original CLD
forms. We use the skeleton integration formulas of \cite{CLD25} on
their original unit-moment presentations.

The passage to regularization is made on a smooth projective
geometrically integral variety over a field in the finite unit-Gauss
tower class $\mathcal G_K$ of \Cref{def:gauss-fields}, with an ample
line bundle $L$. The contact theorem states that a bounded
classical metric $r$ and a continuous model-semipositive metric $p$
satisfy
\[
 r\geq p,\qquad \int (r-p)c_1(L,p)^n=0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad r=p
\]
pointwise. Its proof is an induction on dimension. The first-order
Green estimate controls the gap $r-p$ against smooth backgrounds.
A generic hyperplane then identifies its limit against the continuous
background and reduces the vanishing assertion to dimension $n-1$.
The hyperplane is defined over a unit-Gauss completion, which is why
the induction treats arbitrary data over all finite unit-Gauss towers
at once.

To obtain the approximants, choose continuous metrics
$\rho_\ell\downarrow r$ and take their semipositive envelopes
$s_\ell=P_L\rho_\ell$. Continuity and orthogonality of these envelopes
give
\[
 \int (\rho_\ell-s_\ell)c_1(L,s_\ell)^n=0.
\]
Apply contact to $\max(r,s_\ell)$ and $s_\ell$. Their nonnegative gap
is bounded by $\rho_\ell-s_\ell$, so contact gives
$r\leq s_\ell\leq\rho_\ell$ and hence $s_\ell\downarrow r$.
The envelope theorem is proved in \Cref{sec:normal-envelopes} on a
normal model. Its algebraic input is the corrected subadditivity
inequality of \Cref{thm:fixed-correction}; the vertical correction is
independent of the ideals and their exponents and therefore contributes
an error tending to zero after normalization by degree. To return to
a local potential, \Cref{lem:common-collar} realizes it, up to a
constant, as a metric weight on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

For the mixed-current construction, the induction is on exterior
degree. Strong positivity supplies coefficient Radon measures on the
analytic space, making $u_1T_{k-1}$ meaningful before we differentiate
it. To prove weighted convergence, we use Wu's top-degree theorem for
decreasing piecewise-linear potentials
\cite[Theorem~4.2(4)]{Wu}. A complementary test is reduced to products
of curvatures of auxiliary quadratic potentials. In middle degrees,
this reduction is only modulo the annihilator of decomposable squares.
Strong positivity kills that term in the current pairing, and the
corresponding coefficient measure remains zero after Borel
multiplication. Thus the reduction applies to every original
complementary test.

It remains to replace decreasing PL sequences by arbitrary decreasing
classical potentials. We first place the whole family on one projective
variety, using the common bounds supplied by its first terms and its
limits. A compact diagonal argument then chooses decreasing PL
approximants whose current pairings approach the required ones. Choosing
the common local domain before the approximants resolves the domain
dependence noted in \cite[Remark~4.6]{Wu} for this class of functions.

\Cref{sec:first-order,sec:contact} establish first-order positivity and
regularization; \Cref{sec:construction,sec:arbitrary-columns} construct
the products and prove decreasing continuity. \Cref{sec:localization}
transports these results to ordinary analytic charts and glues the
currents. \Cref{sec:etale} treats specified potential tuples under

S01_relative_monotone.tex \section{A common collar and weighted monotone convergence}
\label{sec:monotone}

The results of this section use the internal inputs listed in
Section~\ref{sec:inputs}. In particular, they do not assert an independent
proof of the regularization theorems in \textup{R} and \textup{B}.
All currents and test forms belong to the original CLD calculus.
Positivity means positivity in the cone used in \textup{R}, not strong
positivity. Set $D=d'd''$.

We first record the exact local consequence of the internal approximation
results that is needed below. A smooth psh function in this section has a
positive original $(1,1)$ curvature \emph{form}.

\begin{lemma}[A common domain for smooth majorants]
\label{lem:common-majorants}
Let $x\in U$, and let $u_{i,j}\downarrow u_i$ be finitely many decreasing
families in $\Cb(U)$ with locally bounded limits. After shrinking around
$x$, there is one ordinary neighborhood $W$, independent of $i,j$, with
the following property. Each of the functions $a=u_{i,j}$ and $a=u_i$
has smooth psh majorants $a_\nu$ on $W$ such that
\[
 a_\nu\geq a,\qquad a_\nu(x')\longrightarrow a(x')\quad(x'\in W).
\]
The majorants are bounded uniformly in $\nu$ on each fixed compact subset
after a finite prefix is discarded. If $a\leq M$ on a compact neighborhood
$C\Subset W$, its majorants may be chosen with $a_\nu\leq M+1$ on $C$.
The index discarded may depend on the function $a$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Use \textup{B}, Proposition 7.1, to work on one ordinary algebraic
neighborhood, with the original field and calibration. Apply \textup{B},
Lemma D.2, to the entire finite family of sequences, before choosing
approximants. It gives one projective variety, one ample line, one frame
on $W$, and bounded classical metrics whose weights on $W$ are the given
functions plus one fixed constant. By \textup{B}, Theorem 4.4, every such
metric is a decreasing limit of pure Fubini--Study metrics on this same
line. Their weights $p_\nu$ are continuous, satisfy $p_\nu\geq a$, and
decrease pointwise to $a$ after the fixed constant is removed.

Smooth each pure Fubini--Study metric uniformly, using \textup{R},
Lemma 3.2 and Proposition A.1. If the uniform error is at most
$\epsilon_\nu\downarrow0$, add $\epsilon_\nu$ to the smoothed weight.
The resulting smooth psh function $a_\nu$ satisfies
\[
 p_\nu\leq a_\nu\leq p_\nu+2\epsilon_\nu.
\]
This proves pointwise convergence and the majorant property.
On $C$, the increasing open sets $\{p_\nu<M+1/2\}$ cover $C$ whenever
$a\leq M$. Compactness gives a common index on $C$. Discard this prefix
and require $2\epsilon_\nu<1/2$. The same argument with any bound for
$a$ gives local uniform boundedness of the row. No monotonicity of the
\emph{smoothed} row is asserted or needed.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A smooth psh collar]
\label{lem:smooth-collar}
Under the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:common-majorants}, there are
compact polynomial norm boxes
\[
 x\in\operatorname{Int}C_1,\qquad
 C_1\subset\operatorname{Int}C_{\mathrm{mid}},\qquad
 C_{\mathrm{mid}}\subset\operatorname{Int}C_2\Subset W,
\]
a smooth psh function $b$ on a neighborhood of $C_2$, and a nonnegative
original smooth cutoff $\chi$ compactly supported in
$\Omega=\operatorname{Int}C_2$, with the following properties.
After adding one constant $c$ to all the original functions, put
\[
 v_{i,j}=\max\{u_{i,j}+c,b\},\qquad
 v_i=\max\{u_i+c,b\}.
\]
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $v_{i,j},v_i\in\Cb(\Omega)$ and $v_{i,j}\downarrow v_i$;
\item $v_{i,j}=u_{i,j}+c$ and $v_i=u_i+c$ on a neighborhood of $C_1$;
\item $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $C_{\mathrm{mid}}$;
\item all $v_{i,j},v_i$ equal $b$ on one fixed neighborhood of
      $\operatorname{supp}d'\chi\cup\operatorname{supp}d''\chi$;
\item each patched function $v$ has smooth psh majorants $v_\nu\geq v$
      converging pointwise to $v$, uniformly bounded on $\operatorname{supp}\chi$,
      and equal to $b$ on that same collar.
\end{enumerate}
The majorant rows in (5) need not be decreasing.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose the boxes by the construction in \textup{B}, Lemma D.2. In
particular, lower-bound polynomials have no zero near $C_2$. Choose
thresholds strictly between the defining thresholds for $C_1$ and
$C_{\mathrm{mid}}$. The finite maximum
\[
 b_0=\max\{0,\log|P_a^{N_a}/c_a|,
                     \log|d_l/Q_l^{M_l}|\}
\]
is zero on a neighborhood of $C_1$ and at least some $\delta>0$ on a
neighborhood in $C_2$ of $C_2\setminus\operatorname{Int}C_{\mathrm{mid}}$.
All its branches other than the zero branch are logarithms of analytic
units where they are active. A branch with a zero is strictly inactive
near that zero.

Apply the regularized maximum of \textup{R}, Proposition A.1, with
smoothing radius smaller than all the fixed gaps. The result $\widetilde b$
is an original smooth psh function: zero branches at polynomial zeros
are deleted by the exact inactivity property. On a neighborhood of
$C_1$, only the constant zero branch is active, so $\widetilde b=0$.
On the outer collar, $\widetilde b\geq\delta$.

The endpoint bounds give a constant $c$ and a finite $M$ such that
\[
 1\leq u_i+c\leq u_{i,j}+c\leq M
 \quad\hbox{on a neighborhood of }C_2.
\]
Multiply $\widetilde b$ by a positive constant so that the resulting $b$
is greater than $M+3$ on the outer collar. Choose $\chi$, with
$0\leq\chi\leq1$, equal to one near $C_{\mathrm{mid}}$ and compactly
supported in $\Omega$. Smooth cutoff existence and a finite localization
are part of the original CLD test calculus. Its derivative support lies
where the fixed outer-collar inequality holds.

Classical psh functions are stable under maxima and addition of constants.
This proves (1)--(4). To prove (5), apply Lemma~\ref{lem:common-majorants}
to the \emph{unpatched} function $a=u_{i,j}+c$ or $u_i+c$. Discard a
prefix so that its smooth psh majorants $a_\nu$ are at most $M+1$ on
$C_2$. Define
\[
 v_\nu=\operatorname{rmax}_{\epsilon_\nu}(a_\nu,b),
 \qquad \epsilon_\nu\downarrow0,
\]
with all radii less than the fixed collar gap. The regularized maximum
majorizes the ordinary maximum and has error at most $\epsilon_\nu$.
It is exactly $b$ on the collar because the other branch is inactive
there. These facts give all the assertions in (5).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Neither lemma supplies a strictly psh exhaustion of an arbitrary analytic
domain. The collar is constructed on a chosen small norm box. The closed
positive form used to detect a test below is chosen separately and may
be degenerate in directions not occurring in that test.
\end{remark}

\begin{lemma}[Green exchange on a common collar]
\label{lem:collar-green}
Let $Q$ be a symmetric positive $d'$- and $d''$-closed current of
bidegree $(n-1,n-1)$ on $\Omega$. Let $\chi\in A_c^{0,0}(\Omega)$.
Suppose that $a$ is smooth, $g$ is locally bounded Borel, and both equal
one smooth function $b$ on a neighborhood of
$\operatorname{supp}d'\chi\cup\operatorname{supp}d''\chi$.
Whenever $D(gQ)$ has coefficient Radon type, one has
\[
 \langle aD(gQ),\chi\rangle
 =\langle gD(aQ),\chi\rangle.
\]
In this statement positivity of $a$ and $g$ is not required.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Since $Q$ is closed and $a$ is smooth, $D(aQ)=Da\wedge Q$. The
definition of the distributional derivative gives
\begin{align*}
 \langle aD(gQ)-gD(aQ),\chi\rangle
  &=\langle gQ,D(\chi a)-\chi Da\rangle\\
  &=\langle Q,g\{aD\chi+d'\chi\wedge d''a
                         +d'a\wedge d''\chi\}\rangle.
\end{align*}
Every term in braces is supported in the collar. Substituting $a=g=b$
there makes the last expression
\[
 \langle bQ,D(\chi b)-\chi Db\rangle=0.
\]
The final equality follows by applying the same distributional identity
to the smooth pair $(b,b)$. The substitutions are valid identities of
coefficient measures. No derivative of the Borel function $g$ is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Monotonicity of the ordered trace integral]
\label{lem:trace-monotonicity}
Let $S$ have bidegree $(p,p)$, let $0\leq k\leq n-p$, and let
$\alpha$ be a smooth, positive, $d'$- and $d''$-closed form of bidegree
$(n-p-k,n-p-k)$ such that wedging it with a positive current preserves
positivity. Let $\chi\geq0$ be compactly supported in $\Omega$.

For $0\leq i\leq k$, suppose $f_i,g_i\in\Cb(\Omega)$,
$f_i\leq g_i$, and all these functions equal the same smooth psh
function $b$ near the derivative support of $\chi$. Assume that each
$g_i$ has the smooth majorants with this exact collar supplied by
Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth-collar}. Define, using the ordered products,
\[
 J(f_0;f_1,\ldots,f_k)
   =\langle f_0T_{S,k}(f_1,\ldots,f_k),\chi\alpha\rangle.
\]
Then
\[
 J(f_0;f_1,\ldots,f_k)
 \leq J(g_0;g_1,\ldots,g_k).
\]
Only existence and positivity of the ordered products are used here.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The case $k=0$ is measure monotonicity. For $k>0$, fix smooth psh
majorants $G_i\geq g_i$ with the common collar. First replace the weight
$f_0$ by $G_0$, using positivity of
$T_{S,k}(f_1,\ldots,f_k)\wedge\alpha$. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-green} with
\[
 Q=T_{S,k-1}(f_2,\ldots,f_k)\wedge\alpha
\]
to move $G_0$ into a differentiated position and $f_1$ into the weight.
The resulting current $DG_0\wedge Q$ is positive and closed. Replace
the weight $f_1$ by $G_1$, and repeat. At the end one obtains
\[
 J(f_0;f_1,\ldots,f_k)
 \leq\langle G_k\,DG_0\wedge\cdots\wedge DG_{k-1}\wedge S,
                     \chi\alpha\rangle.
\]
A final application of the same Green identity, together with
commutation of smooth even-degree factors, makes the right-hand side
$J(G_0;G_1,\ldots,G_k)$.

Now let the index of $G_k$ tend to infinity, keeping every other index
fixed. Bounded convergence against the fixed coefficient measures of
$S$ implies $D(G_kS)\to D(g_kS)$. The outer factors and the weight are
smooth and fixed, so this convergence can be tested directly. Next let
the index of $G_{k-1}$ tend to infinity. The background
$D(g_kS)$ is now fixed, so the same argument applies. Continue in the
order $k,k-1,\ldots,1$. Finally, with the ordered product fixed, let the
weight $G_0$ tend to $g_0$ by bounded convergence. The result is exactly
$J(g_0;g_1,\ldots,g_k)$ in its original order. At no step are two
discontinuous limits interchanged.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[An upper bound for decreasing weights]
\label{lem:upper-weight}
Let $P_j,P$ be positive coefficient Radon currents of one bidegree,
with $P_j\to P$ on all original compact smooth tests. Let $a_j\downarrow a$
be locally uniformly bounded functions. Suppose that, near the support
of a fixed positive compact test $\Theta$, every fixed $a_l$ has bounded
continuous majorants converging pointwise to $a_l$.
Then
\[
 \limsup_{j\to\infty}\langle a_jP_j,\Theta\rangle
       \leq\langle aP,\Theta\rangle.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $j\geq l$ and a continuous majorant $a_{l,\nu}\geq a_l$,
positivity gives
\[
 \langle a_jP_j,\Theta\rangle
       \leq\langle a_{l,\nu}P_j,\Theta\rangle.
\]
Keep $l,\nu$ fixed and pass to the limit in $j$, using \textup{R},
Lemma 3.1. Bounded convergence against the fixed positive Radon measure
$\mu_{P,\Theta}$ first allows $\nu\to\infty$ and then $l\to\infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Weighted decreasing continuity for a fixed arbitrary background]
\label{thm:relative-monotone}
Assume the internal inputs \textup{R} and \textup{B}. Let $S$ be any
symmetric positive original CLD current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on $U$,
separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed. Let $0\leq k\leq n-p$.
If $u_{i,j}\downarrow u_i$ in $\Cb(U)$ for $0\leq i\leq k$, with
locally bounded limits, then
\[
 u_{0,j}T_{S,k}(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{k,j})
 \longrightarrow
 u_0T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)
\]
on every original compact smooth complementary test form. The ordered
unweighted products have the corresponding joint decreasing continuity.
The background $S$ is fixed throughout.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $W_k$ for the weighted assertion with $k$ differentiated slots.
Bounded convergence for the fixed coefficient measures of $S$ proves
$W_0$. Distributional differentiation shows that $W_{k-1}$ implies
joint unweighted convergence in degree $k$. We prove $W_k$ assuming
this unweighted convergence.

The statement is local on compact test supports. Use a finite original
smooth partition to reduce to one test $\eta$ supported in a small
norm box $C_1$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth-collar}. Include in the chosen
ordinary neighborhood all the unit coordinates needed to present
$\eta$. Let these coordinates be $t_1,\ldots,t_N$, and set
\[
 \beta=\sum_{a=1}^N d't_a\wedge d''t_a,
 \qquad r=n-p-k,\qquad \alpha=\frac{\beta^r}{r!}.
\]
For $r=0$ set $\alpha=1$. The form $\alpha$ is closed and strongly
positive. In the fixed finite coefficient space it is a positive
definite trace form. After replacing $\eta$ by its symmetric part,
there is $C>0$ such that
\[
 \Theta_\pm=C\chi\alpha\pm\eta
\]
are positive original compact tests. This is precisely the matrix
domination used in \textup{R}, Lemma 3.1; additional scalar coordinates
are handled by pullback to a common refinement. No definiteness in
all possible moment directions is required.

Patch all the potentials to $v_{i,j},v_i$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:smooth-collar}, and put
\[
 P_j=T_{S,k}(v_{1,j},\ldots,v_{k,j}),\qquad
 P=T_{S,k}(v_1,\ldots,v_k).
\]
The induction hypothesis gives $P_j\to P$. Applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:trace-monotonicity} to the ordered tuples
$(v_0,\ldots,v_k)\leq(v_{0,j},\ldots,v_{k,j})$ yields
\[
 \langle v_0P,\chi\alpha\rangle
       \leq\langle v_{0,j}P_j,\chi\alpha\rangle.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:upper-weight} gives the reverse limsup inequality.
Consequently
\begin{equation}
 \label{eq:trace-limit}
 \langle v_{0,j}P_j,\chi\alpha\rangle
       \longrightarrow\langle v_0P,\chi\alpha\rangle.
\end{equation}
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:upper-weight} to $\Theta_+$ and $\Theta_-$.
Together with \eqref{eq:trace-limit}, the two resulting inequalities
give respectively the upper and lower bounds for
$\langle v_{0,j}P_j,\eta\rangle$. Thus this pairing converges to
$\langle v_0P,\eta\rangle$.

On a neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\eta$, the patched potentials
are $u_{i,j}+c$ and $u_i+c$. Ordinary locality of the recursion identifies
the differentiated products there with the original products, since
constants in differentiated slots vanish. Remove the constant $c$ from
the weight by the unweighted degree-$k$ convergence already established.
Finite summation over the test partition proves $W_k$.

This induction proves all $W_k$ and all allowed unweighted assertions.
It uses neither capacity nor energy convergence, nor any interchange
of two discontinuous approximation parameters.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Symmetry and the first-stage calculus]
\label{cor:full-calculus}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-monotone}, the currents
$T_{S,k}$ are symmetric in the differentiated arguments,
positive, symmetric as currents, and separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed.
They are additive and positively homogeneous in each potential, commute
with ordinary restriction and gluing, and are independent of the
regularization used to compute them. In particular,
\[
 D\bigl(uD(vS)\bigr)=D\bigl(vD(uS)\bigr)
 \qquad(u,v\in\Cb(U),\ p\leq n-2).
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
All assertions except permutation symmetry were proved for the ordered
recursion. Choose, locally on one fixed domain, continuous semipositive
PL approximants decreasing to each potential, as in \textup{B}.
Continuous arbitrary-background products are symmetric, by uniform
smooth approximation and fixed-continuous-multiplier convergence.
Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-monotone}, with a constant weight, passes this
identity to the given potentials. The recursion identifies the result
independently of the approximants and on overlaps.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Top-degree convergence as measures]
\label{cor:top-measures}
If $p+k=n$, the weighted convergence in
Theorem~\ref{thm:relative-monotone} holds against every compactly
supported continuous scalar function, locally as si

title: Second-round theorem and status increment
text:
S02_round2_status.tex \section{Second-round theorem and status increment}
\label{sec:r2-status}

This section updates, rather than replaces, the source-by-source comparison
in Section~\ref{sec:comparison}. The first-round statements remain frozen
with their original hypotheses. An earlier \texttt{OPEN} entry is closed
only by the particular second-round theorem cited below. No claim of
literature priority is encoded by \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}: that label records
a proof supplied in this project, relative to its accepted inputs.

\subsection{Two independent status axes and the fixed category}

The labels \texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN}, \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT},
\texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}, and \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} record provenance.
The labels \texttt{PROVED}, \texttt{CONDITIONAL}, \texttt{OPEN}, and
\texttt{FALSE} assess a precisely qualified proposed analogy. A theorem
proved under an explicit additional geometric hypothesis is
\texttt{PROVED} with that hypothesis; the corresponding general-domain
analogy is \texttt{CONDITIONAL} or \texttt{OPEN}. A counterexample to an
unrestricted assertion does not change the status of its qualified
replacement.

All local assertions retain the finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$, its
prescribed absolute value, and the allowed good, Hausdorff, boundaryless,
quasi-smooth pure-dimensional analytic spaces. Unless a narrower theorem
states otherwise, $S$ is an arbitrary \emph{fixed} symmetric current of
bidegree $(p,p)$, positive in the original CLD cone and separately
$d'$- and $d''$-closed. Products and current equalities are tested on
\emph{all original compactly supported smooth complementary CLD forms}.
Neither a change of positivity cone nor an enlargement of the test sheaf
is implicit. Put $q=n-p$; the relative top-capacity statements below use
$q\geq1$.

R and B remain \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}. In particular, the bounded
classical class and its $[1]$-background calculus are not second-round
discoveries. The completed geometric adelic nefness theorem A2 also
remains an \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT} under its own number-field,
integrability, and boundary hypotheses. The original classical, CLD,
GR, and GK theorems recorded in Section~\ref{sec:comparison} remain
\texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN} in their stated categories.

\subsection{Increment for the eleven Bedford--Taylor directions}

\begin{longtable}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.045\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.19\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.40\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.28\textwidth}@{}}
\hline
 & Target & Qualified second-round increment & Remaining qualification or obstruction\\
\hline
\endfirsthead
\hline
 & Target & Qualified second-round increment & Remaining qualification or obstruction\\
\hline
\endhead
1 & Locally bounded psh functions &
\texttt{PROVED / DIRECT\_COROLLARY}: upper regularizations of locally
uniformly upper-bounded classical families are classical, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-local-upper-envelope}; the projective bounded usc
obstacle envelope is Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-usc-obstacle}.
\texttt{PROVED / DIRECT\_COROLLARY}: original trace-current order determines
the actual bounded classical representative,
Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-current-faithfulness}. &
The new capacitary class is relative to $S$ and retains Borel
representatives. For $S=[1]$, every such class now has a unique
actual classical representative modulo local outer-capacity zero,
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-ambient-classical-representative}
(\texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}). Actual Borel values on the exceptional
set are not identified. No corresponding assertion for arbitrary
$S$ is made.\\[5pt]

2 & Positive closed currents and mixed products &
The arbitrary-fixed-$S$ bounded classical calculus is already
\texttt{PROVED} in R1. Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-completed-calculus} extends
it to $\mathcal A_{S,b}$, with well-defined Borel recursion,
quasi-everywhere independence, symmetry, and restriction/gluing:
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}. &
This does not define the wedge of two arbitrary positive closed
currents. Nor does it settle dependence only on the currents $D[u_i]$:
the general discontinuous potential-quotient assertion remains
\texttt{OPEN}.\\[5pt]

3 & Chern--Levine--Nirenberg estimates &
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}: the weighted $L^1$ estimate and uniform
truncation estimate of Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-weighted-l1}, under the
specified collar-trace integrability condition. The deep-sublevel
outer-capacity estimate and integrable-witness consequences are
\texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY},
Corollaries~\ref{cor:r2-normalized-witness} and
\ref{cor:r2-witness-outer-capacity}. &
The integrability hypothesis concerns an explicit trace of the fixed
$S$; it is not automatic for arbitrary $S$. Uniform exponential tails
and unbounded-weight stability from a uniform first moment alone are
\texttt{FALSE}, Propositions~\ref{prop:r2-no-exponential-tails} and
\ref{prop:r2-unbounded-weight-failure}.\\[5pt]

4 & Symmetry and weighted monotone convergence &
R1 already proves symmetry and weighted joint decreasing continuity
for actual bounded classical limits and fixed $S$.
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}: bounded increasing sequences converge
in outer relative capacity to their \emph{actual} Borel supremum,
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-increasing-cauchy} and
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-local-increasing}; weighted increasing continuity
in the completed class is Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-increasing-weighted}.
The ambient no-jump theorem
\ref{thm:r2-increasing-no-jump} identifies this supremum with its usc
regularization locally quasi-everywhere:
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-weak-closure-multipliers} proves the qualified
quasicontinuous multiplier passage through weak closure. &
Ambient no-jump and its common-collar energy equality are closed
questions in this record. Replacing the actual supremum by its
ambient usc regularization remains \texttt{FALSE} without
qualification for arbitrary $S$. Unrestricted varying-$S$ weighted
stability remains \texttt{FALSE}.\\[5pt]

5 & Locality and maximum principles &
R1 Borel maximum locality and ordinary restriction/locality remain
\texttt{PROVED}. Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-polar-restriction} proves that
$\mathbf1_P S$ and $\mathbf1_{P^c}S$ are separately closed for a
classical pole set $P$, and that BT products commute with this
restriction: \texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-maximal-ma-zero} proves local classical maximality
equivalent to $(Du)^n=0$ for the ambient background. &
Strict inequality sets of discontinuous potentials are Borel and
locally quasi-open, not automatically ordinary open. The polar
restriction theorem starts with a current defined on the entire
domain; it is not a general extension theorem for a current defined
only off the pole set.\\[5pt]

6 & Bedford--Taylor capacities &
\texttt{PROVED / DIRECT\_COROLLARY}: outer regularity on quasi-open
sets, Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-quasiopen-outer}, and the elementary
outer-capacity properties in Lemma~\ref{lem:r2-outer-facts}.
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}: two-sided local comparison with one
fixed relatively compact affine capacity domain,
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-domain-capacity-comparison}. For the ambient
capacity on an exhaustion domain, compact raw outer regularity and
compact continuity are Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-compact-capacity-continuity};
outer-capacity continuity for arbitrary increasing subsets of a
fixed relatively compact core is
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-outer-capacity-increasing-sets}.
Choquet capacitability and Borel outer regularity on that core are
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-local-choquet}. &
Raw compact outer regularity and the corresponding Choquet theory
for \emph{arbitrary relative backgrounds $S$} remain \texttt{OPEN}.
The ambient result retains the exhaustion-domain and fixed-core
scope. General-domain nondegeneracy remains \texttt{FALSE}; the R1
proper-space example still applies.\\[5pt]

7 & Quasicontinuity and capacity convergence &
R1 bounded quasicontinuity is retained. Theorems
\ref{thm:r2-increasing-cauchy} and \ref{thm:r2-completed-calculus}
give the increasing and capacitary-completion extensions.
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-extended-psh-qc} gives local finite
quasicontinuity and lower-truncation outer-capacity convergence for
every nontrivial extended classical psh function:
\texttt{PROVED / DIRECT\_COROLLARY} of the new polar-trace and
weighted estimates. &
Capacity precompactness of the full normalized continuous psh family,
and weighted BT stability under bounded pointwise convergence alone,
are \texttt{FALSE},
Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-capacity-noncompactness}. This counterexample
does not refute compact-set domination by the weak closure of the
admissible measure family.\\[5pt]

8 & Pluripolar and negligible sets &
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}: every original smooth ambient trace
vanishes on a nontrivial classical pole set,
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-ambient-polar-traces}.
\texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}: all ambient bounded BT coefficients avoid
such sets, and every locally pluripolar subset has local outer
capacity zero, Corollaries~\ref{cor:r2-ambient-bt-poles} and
\ref{cor:r2-ambient-polar-outer-zero}.
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-capacity-zero-polar-witness} constructs a
nontrivial witness for an outer-zero set. The resulting local
equivalence of pluripolar, outer-zero, and negligible sets is
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-polar-negligible-equivalence}.
Pole patching on one exhaustion domain is
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-exhaustion-domain-pole-patching}. &
These local ambient equivalences are \texttt{PROVED}.
Unqualified untwisted pole globalization on every analytic space is
\texttt{FALSE}, already on $\mathbf P^{1,\an}_K$.
Arbitrary relative backgrounds may charge ambient pluripolar sets;
their mass is governed by
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-polar-restriction}, not forced to vanish.\\[5pt]

9 & Comparison and domination &
The R1 compact-gap comparison theorem for arbitrary fixed $S$
remains \texttt{PROVED}.
\texttt{PROVED / DIRECT\_COROLLARY}: ambient strict-gap detection and
pointwise domination/uniqueness on the stated relatively compact
framed affine domains, Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-ambient-gap-detection}
and Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-pointwise-ambient}.
Relative atomic and smooth-factor detection criteria and explicit
faithful backgrounds are proved in
Propositions~\ref{prop:r2-relative-gap-detection} and
\ref{prop:r2-smooth-factor-condition}. &
Pointwise domination for arbitrary $S$ remains
\texttt{CONDITIONAL} on detection; the unrestricted version is
\texttt{FALSE} even for nonzero $S$ on a connected domain,
Example~\ref{ex:r2-nonzero-domination-failure}.
Capacity-modulo uniqueness and actual pointwise uniqueness are
distinct assertions.\\[5pt]

10 & Relative extremal functions &
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}: least upper bounds in the local
$S$-quasi-everywhere order, represented in $\mathcal A_{S,b}$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-local-capacitary-envelope}.
Ambient bounded usc obstacle envelopes follow directly from B;
orthogonality for bounded quasicontinuous usc projective obstacles
is Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-qc-orthogonality},
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}.
For the ambient background on an exhaustion domain, compact/open
extremal equilibrium formulas are Theorems
\ref{thm:r2-compact-extremal} and \ref{thm:r2-open-extremal};
arbitrary relatively compact sets satisfy the outer-capacity
total-mass formula \ref{thm:r2-arbitrary-extremal-mass}. &
The ambient and relative categories remain distinct. General
\emph{relative} equilibrium-measure/contact-set formulas and their
capacity identities remain \texttt{OPEN}; unrestricted replacement
of an $S$-capacitary envelope by the ambient envelope is \texttt{FALSE},
Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-negligible-positive}.\\[5pt]

11 & Monge--Amp\`ere and Dirichlet theory &
\texttt{PROVED / NEW\_PROVED}: the ambient local equivalence between
maximality and the homogeneous equation,
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-maximal-ma-zero}.
The explicit peak-barrier theorem
\ref{thm:r2-peak-dirichlet} gives a bounded classical solution of
$(DH_g)^n=0$, ordinary boundary values, uniqueness, and the boundary
sup-norm stability estimate under
Definition~\ref{def:r2-peak-barriers}.
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-dirac-dirichlet} gives an explicit continuous
solution and uniqueness for a single positive divisorial atom and
constant boundary data on the domains constructed with its barrier:
\texttt{PROVED / DIRECT\_COROLLARY}. &
As a general-domain analogy the Dirichlet conclusion is
\texttt{CONDITIONAL} on those explicit barriers. Their general
geometric construction, interior continuity for the Perron solution,
and existence for a general prescribed nonzero measure remain
\texttt{OPEN}. Bounded negative exhaustion domains are explicitly
defined and locally supplied; they are not silently assumed to have
peak barriers at every boundary point.\\[3pt]
\hline
\end{longtable}

\subsection{Scope distinctions that survive the second round}

\paragraph{Fixed backgrounds and controlled varying backgrounds.}
The primary calculus keeps $S$ fixed. The order-dominated replacement
in Proposition~\ref{prop:dominated-background-stability} allows
$0\leq S_j\leq C R_0$, $S_j\to S$, with one fixed positive closed
$R_0$ and a fixed differentiated tuple; its multiplier hypotheses
must also be retained. The second-round weak-closure multiplier
theorem instead requires uniform coefficient bounds by a fixed local
capacity and quasicontinuous weights. Neither statement removes the
counterexample in Corollary~\ref{cor:varying-background-false}.

\paragraph{Actual representatives and ambient upper regularization.}
An actual increasing supremum is now an element of the bounded
capacitary closure, and its BT products are established there. For the
ambient background, Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-increasing-no-jump} identifies
it with its ordinary usc regularization locally outside outer-zero
sets and proves the common-collar energy no-jump equality. More
generally, Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-ambient-classical-representative}
assigns each $a\in\mathcal A_{[1],b}$ a unique classical representative
$r_a$ modulo such sets. For an arbitrary Borel representative $a$,
$r_a$ need not equal $a^*$; arbitrary modifications on polar sets are
allowed in that capacitary class. This distinction does not affect
the actual increasing-supremum theorem.
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-local-capacitary-envelope} obtains a least upper
bound without taking an uncountable union of exceptional sets: each
competitor has its own quasi-everywhere comparison, and a countable
energy construction determines the resulting class. For an arbitrary
relative background $S$, the capacitary representative cannot in
general be replaced by the ambient usc envelope.

\paragraph{Raw capacity and outer capacity.}
For arbitrary $S$, the identity $C^*(E)=C(E)$ is proved for quasi-open
$E$; full raw compact outer regularity remains open. For $S=[1]$ on
an exhaustion domain, it is now proved for compact sets and for
every Borel subset of each fixed relatively compact core. The
ordinary-open proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-outer-capacity-increasing-sets}
supplies the additional continuity axiom needed for the local
Choquet theorem; compact continuity of $C^*$ alone would not supply
that proof. The raw-capacity closure criterion in
Proposition~\ref{prop:capacity-weak-closure} is therefore resolved
for the stated ambient compact stages but remains an exact target
for arbitrary relative $S$. The explicit potential-noncompactness
example has an admissible unweighted weak limit and does not refute
compact-set domination by the admissible measure family's weak closure.

\paragraph{Polar sets and arbitrary support.}
The general ambient pole-trace problem is now \texttt{PROVED}; it is
no longer a missing hypothesis in the ambient nonconcentration result.

arbitrary_background_quotient.tex \section{The arbitrary-background potential quotient}
\label{sec:r5-arbitrary-background-quotient}

Fix a finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$ with its original absolute
value. Let $U$ be an ordinary open in a good Hausdorff boundaryless
quasi-smooth $K$-analytic space of pure dimension $n$.
Throughout this section $D=d'd''$, the test forms are all original
compactly supported CLD smooth complementary forms, and positivity
is the original positive cone used in R. Every positive current
under consideration is symmetric. Strong and weak positivity are
not substituted for that cone.

Write $\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}(U)$ for the actual real functions
which are locally differences of two members of $\mathcal C_b$.
A function in $\mathscr{PH}(U)$ is a finite continuous function
whose two signs are classical psh. Such a function is locally
bounded. No quotient by a measure-null set occurs in either
definition.

\begin{theorem}[Regularity of the bounded classical curvature kernel]
\label{thm:r5-bounded-kernel-regularity}
If $u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U)$ and $D[u]=D[v]$ on every original
test, then the actual difference $u-v$ is continuous and belongs
to $\mathscr{PH}(U)$. More generally,
\[
 \ker\bigl(D:\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}(U)
                   \longrightarrow\mathcal D'^{1,1}(U)\bigr)
                         =\mathscr{PH}(U).
\]
The equality is an equality of spaces of actual functions.
It does not assert regularity for the kernel on all locally
integrable functions or on all abstract distributions.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} in the stated
bounded-classical scope, relative to the declared internal
inputs and the preceding proofs.

\begin{proof}
Let $H=u-v$. Theorem~\ref{thm:r5-all-extension-curve-harmonicity}
shows that after every complete extension $F/K$, the pullback
of $H$ along every allowed smooth analytic curve is an actual
continuous harmonic function. In particular it has the
algebraic-curve property required by
Theorem~\ref{thm:r5-continuity-from-curves}. That theorem applies
to the actual locally bounded $H$ and proves its ordinary
continuity on $U$.

Both $H$ and $-H$ are therefore upper semicontinuous. To check
the full curve quantifier, let $C\to U_F$ be an arbitrary
$F$-analytic curve map, including curves with boundary or
singularities. Its two pullbacks are continuous. In the
definition of subharmonicity on $C$, test further over any
complete extension $E/F$ by a smooth connected strict
$E$-curve mapping to $C_E$. The composite maps to $U_E$,
so the preceding harmonicity theorem makes both signs
subharmonic on that test curve. Smooth curves can be
localized in good Hausdorff boundaryless ordinary opens,
and subharmonicity is local. Definition 3.4 and \S4.1.3
of \cite{GR25} therefore give subharmonicity on the original
$C$. Thus the full classical psh condition holds for both
signs, including its boundary and nonsmooth curve tests.
They belong to $\mathcal C_b(U)$, and
$H\in\mathscr{PH}(U)$.

For a function in $\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}$ with zero
curvature, apply this argument on its local difference
presentations. Continuity and classical pluriharmonicity
are local and hence glue. Conversely, for
$H\in\mathscr{PH}$ the already established first-order
positive-current theorem applied to $H$ and $-H$ shows that
$D[H]$ and $-D[H]$ are positive. A symmetric current and its
negative can both be positive only if it is zero: on each
finite moment presentation every symmetric smooth test is
dominated in both signs by a positive control. Thus $D[H]=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Potential independence for every fixed positive closed background]
\label{thm:r5-arbitrary-background-potential-quotient}
Let $0\leq p<n$, and let $S$ be any symmetric original-positive
$(p,p)$-current on $U$, separately $d'$-closed and $d''$-closed.
For any $u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U)$,
\[
 D[u]=D[v]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D(uS)=D(vS).
 \tag{Q}
\]
All products by $u$ and $v$ are the actual coefficient-Radon
Borel products. The conclusion holds on every original compact
smooth test of bidegree $(n-p-1,n-p-1)$, including all original
moment refinements.

No smoothness, model origin, analytic-cycle representation, or
pre-existing BT representation is required of $S$.
For $p=n$ the corresponding differentiated statement is vacuous.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}. The final
positivity step is a direct use of the previously established
arbitrary-fixed-background first-order construction; the new
input is Theorem~\ref{thm:r5-bounded-kernel-regularity}.

\begin{proof}
Put $H=u-v$. Theorem~\ref{thm:r5-bounded-kernel-regularity}
gives $H,-H\in\mathcal C_b(U)$ as actual functions.
Apply the existing first-order BT construction, or explicitly
Proposition~\ref{prop:r5-prescribed-relative-first-order} to
the B-prescribed rows of $H$ and $-H$. For the arbitrary
fixed background $S$ it gives two positive separately
closed currents
\[
                         D(HS),\qquad D((-H)S).
\]
Borel multiplication and distributional differentiation are
linear, so the second is the negative of the first.
The positive-cone argument at the end of the preceding proof
makes this current zero on every original complementary test.
Linearity now gives $D(uS)-D(vS)=D(HS)=0$.

Only the already defined multiplication of a fixed positive
current by a locally bounded Borel function was used. In
particular no pullback of $S$, no regularization of $S$, and
no moving-background limit occurred.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Differentiated-slot descent]
\label{cor:r5-differentiated-slot-quotient}
Let $S$ be as above, let $0\leq k\leq n-p$, and let
$u_1,\ldots,u_k,v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathcal C_b(U)$.
If $D[u_i]=D[v_i]$ for every $i$, then
\[
              T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)
                    =T_{S,k}(v_1,\ldots,v_k)
\]
on all original tests.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of (Q)
and the frozen fixed-background BT calculus.

\begin{proof}
Replace one differentiated slot at a time. By symmetry of
the established mixed product, place the slot being changed
first. The product of the remaining slots with $S$ is one
fixed positive separately closed background. Apply (Q) to
this background and the two potentials in that slot.
After the finitely many replacements the displayed equality
follows. The case $k=0$ is the identity $S=S$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Positive currents with bounded classical local potentials]
\label{def:r5-classical-potential-current}
An original $(1,1)$-current $\alpha$ on $U$ has bounded
classical local potentials if every point has an ordinary
neighborhood $O$ and $a\in\mathcal C_b(O)$ such that
$\alpha|_O=D[a]$.
\end{definition}

These currents are positive and separately closed by B.
The definition is a local-potential condition, and it is not
asserted for all positive closed $(1,1)$-currents.

\begin{corollary}[A current-valued mixed operation with one arbitrary background]
\label{cor:r5-local-potential-current-products}
Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_k$ have bounded classical local
potentials on $U$, with $k\leq n-p$. There is a well-defined
original positive separately closed current
\[
                        \alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k\wedge S
\]
whose expression on any ordinary open carrying local potentials
$\alpha_i=D[a_i]$ is $T_{S,k}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$.
It is independent of all local potentials and is symmetric
in the $\alpha_i$. It has the restriction, gluing, additivity,
and positive homogeneity properties inherited from the
bounded-potential BT calculus.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}}.

\begin{proof}
Choose simultaneous local potentials on an ordinary cover.
On an overlap, both local potentials of each $\alpha_i$
have the same ambient original curvature current.
Corollary~\ref{cor:r5-differentiated-slot-quotient} gives equality
of the two local mixed currents on every original test.
The ordinary sheaf property for currents glues them uniquely.
Their positivity and separate closedness are local.
Symmetry and the linearity assertions follow from those
properties for the chosen local potentials; potential
independence removes the dependence on those choices.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pullback of bounded-potential curvature currents]
\label{cor:r5-potential-current-pullback}
Let $\alpha$ have bounded classical local potentials on an
allowed original $K$-space $X$. Let $L/K$ be any complete
extension and let $F:Z\to X_L$ be analytic with $Z$ allowed
over $L$. The local rule
\[
                      F^*\alpha=D[a_L\circ F],
                \qquad \alpha=D[a]\ \hbox{locally},
\]
defines an original positive separately closed $(1,1)$-current
on $Z$, independent of the chosen original-$K$ potentials.
Iterating the rule with the pullbacks of the original potentials
agrees with further scalar extension and analytic composition.
For maps between allowed original-$K$ spaces, this is the usual
intrinsic functoriality on the stated local-potential class.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of
Theorem~\ref{thm:r5-all-extension-analytic-kernel}.
This is a pullback for the specified local-potential class,
not for an arbitrary positive current.

\begin{proof}
On each inverse-image neighborhood, the actual function
$a_L\circ F$ has a prescribed smooth positive row pulled
back from its original-$K$ row. Its original curvature is
therefore positive and separately closed by the fixed-row
first-order argument. Two choices of $a$ on an original
overlap have equal ambient curvature; the all-extension
analytic kernel theorem gives equal displayed currents on
the whole inverse-image overlap. They glue uniquely.
Composition and extension commute with the actual
compositions of functions and with their original smooth
rows. Applying the same independence statement to the
original potentials proves the asserted compatibility.
When all intermediate spaces are over the original $K$,
the theorem also applies to every alternative bounded
classical potential on each intermediate space, giving
intrinsic functoriality there. Over an arbitrary new field,
the assertion about iteration is restricted to the induced
original-potential presentations; it is not an extension
of B to all new functions over that field.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Undifferentiated weights and limits.}
The quotient is for differentiated slots. An undifferentiated
weight is still an actual function: replacing it by another
function with the same curvature need not preserve a weighted
current. For example $D[0]=D[1]=0$, but $0S=0$ and $1S=S$
for every nonzero $S$. The seven established fixed-background
BT properties retain their original functional hypotheses.
This section does not turn arbitrary weak convergence of
curvature currents or arbitrary varying backgrounds into
weighted joint convergence.

\paragraph{Original tests and the remaining boundaries of scope.}
The operation above is an equality of ordinary original
CLD currents. It is not promoted to equality on all delta-test
forms. It does not define the wedge of two completely arbitrary
positive closed currents. An arbitrary permitted $S$ may still
charge an ambient pluripolar set. Neither the regularity
theorem nor the quotient proof requires that such concentration
be excluded.

title: Products in the continuous coefficient curvature module
text:
continuous_curvature_module_products.tex \section{Products in the continuous coefficient curvature module}
\label{sec:r6-continuous-curvature-module-products}

This section records a consequence of the represented-order theorem.
The input currents have a prescribed local finite potential
presentation. No product of completely arbitrary positive closed
currents is defined.

\begin{definition}
On an allowed ordinary open $U$, let $\mathscr M^1(U)$ be the
$C(U,\mathbf R)$-module of original coefficient-Radon $(1,1)$-currents
locally admitting a finite expression
\[
                         A=\sum_{\alpha}f_\alpha D[g_\alpha],
 \qquad f_\alpha\in C(U,\mathbf R),\quad g_\alpha\in\mathcal C_b(U).
\]
The expression is local; actual equality of currents is the equivalence
relation. Signed bounded classical potentials can be used after
expanding them into two classical parts. Its positive cone consists
of those represented currents which are positive in the original
middle CLD sense. Variable continuous coefficients need not preserve
separate closedness.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Positive products of continuously weighted curvatures]
\label{thm:r6-positive-continuous-module-products}
Let $S$ be any fixed allowed $(p,p)$-background and $r\le n-p$.
There is a well-defined symmetric $C(U,\mathbf R)$-multilinear map
\[
 \Phi_{S,r}:(\mathscr M^1)^r\longrightarrow
       \{\text{original coefficient-Radon $(p+r,p+r)$-currents}\}
\]
characterized on finite local presentations by
\begin{equation}
 \Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)
 =\sum_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r}
    \left(\prod_{i=1}^r f_{i,\alpha_i}\right)
    T_{S,r}(g_{1,\alpha_1},\ldots,g_{r,\alpha_r}).
 \label{eq:r6-continuous-module-product}
\end{equation}
It commutes with ordinary restriction and gluing. If every $A_i$ is
positive, its image is positive. In particular the map is increasing
in each slot when all the other slots are positive. When every slot
is $D[g_i]$, it is the frozen bounded BT product.

No separate closedness of the output is asserted for general
continuous coefficients. The map does not factor through every
higher-degree ordinary-current relation merely from its construction.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the new
bounded-difference positivity criterion and continuous-coefficient
relation theorem, with the positivity argument written out.

\begin{proof}
Each expression in \eqref{eq:r6-continuous-module-product} is a finite
sum of continuous multiples of positive coefficient-Radon currents.
Suppose the presentation of one slot is changed without changing its
original current. Fix one multi-index in the remaining slots and put
\[
 R=T_{S,r-1}(g_{1,\alpha_1},\ldots,
              \widehat{g_{i,\alpha_i}},\ldots,g_{r,\alpha_r}).
\]
This is an allowed positive separately closed background. The
zero-relation assertion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:r6-bounded-curvature-continuous-module}, applied to
$R$, makes the change in that slot zero. Multiplication by the
remaining continuous coefficient product and finite summation
preserve zero. Changing the slots one at a time proves presentation
independence. Finite linearity, scalar multiplication, symmetry of
the frozen BT tails, ordinary locality and gluing give the stated
module and sheaf properties.

For positivity fix a positive original compact complementary test
$\eta$. Use finitely many local presentations near its support and
nonnegative smooth localization; it suffices to treat one presentation.
All its coefficients are bounded by a fixed number $M\ge1$ on a
slightly larger compact neighborhood. For $0<\epsilon<1$, subdivide
the test support into finitely many ordinary neighborhoods on which
\[
                    |f_{i,\alpha}-c_{i,\alpha}|<\epsilon
\]
for suitable constants $c_{i,\alpha}$. On one such neighborhood put
\[
 H_i=\sum_\alpha(c_{i,\alpha}+\epsilon)g_{i,\alpha}.
\]
It is an actual bounded classical difference, and
\[
 D[H_i]=A_i+\sum_\alpha(c_{i,\alpha}+\epsilon-f_{i,\alpha})
                                      D[g_{i,\alpha}]\ge0.
\]
Theorem~\ref{thm:r6-positive-bounded-dsh-classical} therefore gives
$H_i\in\mathcal C_b$ on that neighborhood. Hence
$T_{S,r}(H_1,\ldots,H_r)\ge0$ there.

For every multi-index the scalar difference between its coefficient
in \eqref{eq:r6-continuous-module-product} and its coefficient in
$T_{S,r}(H_1,\ldots,H_r)$ has absolute value at most
$2r\epsilon(M+2)^{r-1}$. This follows by telescoping the product of
$r$ scalars, since each paired scalar differs by at most $2\epsilon$.
Let $R_0$ be the finite sum of all the positive BT tails in
\eqref{eq:r6-continuous-module-product}, without coefficients.
On this neighborhood the positive test cone therefore gives
\[
          \Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)
                   \ge -2r\epsilon(M+2)^{r-1}R_0.
\]
The same constant and the same $R_0$ work for every member of the
finite subdivision. Apply a nonnegative original smooth partition
to $\eta$, sum the inequalities, and let $\epsilon\downarrow0$.
The fixed control mass $\langle R_0,\eta\rangle$ is finite. The
pairing of $\Phi_{S,r}$ with $\eta$ is nonnegative. This proves
positivity on all original tests in the specified cone.

For monotonicity subtract the two products and telescope their
slots. Each term has one positive difference slot and all other
slots positive, so the proved positivity applies. The BT
specialization is its defining one-term presentation.
\end{proof}

\begin{example}[Borel coefficients do not preserve current relations]
\label{ex:r6-borel-curvature-module-failure}
The word continuous in the preceding module cannot be replaced by
bounded Borel, even when all potential functions are continuous.
Take the ordinary bidannulus
\[
 U=\{r<|T_1|<R,\ r<|T_2|<R\}\subset(\mathbf G_{m,K}^2)^{\an},
             \qquad 0<r<1<R,
\]
and let $Y=\{T_2=1\}\cap U$, $S=[Y]$, and
$g=\max\{0,\log|T_1|\}$. This is a continuous locally bounded
classical psh function. The frozen first-order analytic-divisor
nonconcentration theorem, applied to $D[g]$, gives
\[
                         \mathbf1_YD[g]=0
\]
as an ambient coefficient-Radon current. On the other hand, the
restriction and projection formulas for the subvariety background,
and the one-variable slope computation, give
\[
 \mathbf1_YD(g[Y])=D(g[Y])=i_*\delta_{\zeta_{0,1}}\ne0,
                  \qquad i:Y\hookrightarrow U.
\]
Here $\zeta_{0,1}$ is the radius-one Gauss point in the $T_1$ annulus;
the slope jump of $\max(0,\log|T_1|)$ is exactly one. An original
nonnegative compact smooth scalar test equal to one near this point
pairs with the displayed measure to give one. Thus the failure is
visible on original tests, not only on an enlarged test sheaf.
\end{example}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{FALSE}} for the proposed Borel
extension; the example is a \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY} of the frozen
polar-carrier obstruction and first-order nonconcentration. It is not
counted as a new counterexample mechanism. R5,
Corollary~\ref{cor:r5-universal-borel-kernel-strict} and
Remark~\ref{rem:r5-bounded-usc-kernel-obstruction}, already show why
arbitrary assigned bounded upper semicontinuous values must also be
excluded from the bounded-classical-difference positivity criterion.

\paragraph{What this construction does not settle.}
Independence of the degree-one presentations means that relations in
$\mathscr M^1$ may be substituted inside
\eqref{eq:r6-continuous-module-product}. It does not say that every
ordinary zero current formed from several curvature factors is such
a relation. The higher-degree analytic delta kernel remains a separate
problem. Nor is the output of a continuous coefficient product an
admissible new background unless its required positivity and separate
closedness are independently available.
