title: A differential module with actual piecewise smooth coefficients
text:
S06_pws_differential_curvature_module.tex \section{A differential module with actual piecewise smooth coefficients}
\label{sec:r10-pws-differential-module}

All currents and tests in this section are original CLD objects over
the fixed $K/\mathbf Q_p$ with its original absolute value.  Piecewise
smooth (PS) means the actual codimension-zero sheaf, with tangential
matching and the full actual moment equivalence, as in the frozen R6
PS multiplication theorem.  It does not mean an arbitrary Borel
coefficient array.  Backgrounds remain arbitrary original symmetric
middle-positive separately closed currents.

The inputs used below are precisely: the frozen R4 uniform normal-wall
variation estimate for positive separately closed currents; the frozen
weighted joint bounded BT theorem; the R6 canonical PS multiplication
and tangency theorem; and the codimension-zero case of the R6 anchored
Courant presentation.  No analytic positive-codimension relation
quotient is assumed.

The exact frozen pins are
\texttt{thm:r6-delta-module-generation} in
\texttt{\detokenize{delta_module_generation.tex}},
\texttt{lem:r6-level-tangency} and
\texttt{thm:r6-pws-multiplication} in
\texttt{\detokenize{pws_tangent_extension.tex}},
\texttt{lem:r4-wall-normal-factor} and
\texttt{thm:r4-piecewise-test-continuity} in
\texttt{\detokenize{potential_quotient_next.tex}}, and
\texttt{thm:relative-monotone} in the frozen foundational
\texttt{\detokenize{relative_monotone.tex}}.
Their full archived paths, SHA256 values, and exact uses are
recorded in \texttt{\detokenize{PWS_DEPENDENCY_CHECK.json}}.

\subsection{A simultaneous smoothing estimate with moving closed tails}

On a compact stage in one original moment presentation, the frozen
anchored construction writes every PS form as a finite sum of words
\[
 \alpha=
 F(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N)\,
 d'_P\lambda_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge d'_P\lambda_{i_a}
 \wedge d''_P\lambda_{j_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge d''_P\lambda_{j_b},
 \tag{P1}
\]
where the $\lambda_i$ are continuous real PL functions in those
moments and $F$ is smooth on a neighborhood of the relevant finite
coordinate image.  Finite sums and original smooth coefficient forms
are allowed.  The latter can also be included by adding the original
affine moment coordinates to the list in (P1).

Here is the exact use of the frozen generation theorem.  In its
codimension-zero case, every lifted constant full-dimensional
balanced cycle on a connected real neighborhood is a constant
multiple of the ambient integration current.  Its printed anchored
coefficient is $g(\lambda_A)d'_P\lambda_I\wedge d''_P\lambda_J$,
which is (P1).  Its Courant functions are continuous PL but need not
be convex.  Refining by their finitely many walls and adding a
sufficiently large positive sum of absolute affine wall functions
writes each one locally as
\[
                         \lambda_i=\lambda_i^+-\lambda_i^-,
 \tag{P2}
\]
with both $\lambda_i^\pm$ convex PL.  Indeed their gradient jumps
are bounded normal multiples along finitely many walls; a large
sum of absolute wall functions makes every jump nonnegative.
Convexity on all segments then proves (P2).  This is the PL case
of the frozen R6 continuous-PS difference lemma.

Use one nonnegative compact smooth convolution kernel of total mass
one and zero first moment, with radius $\varepsilon$, for all real representatives on a
slightly larger stage.  Write
$\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}^\pm=\lambda_i^\pm*\rho_\varepsilon$ and
$\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}=\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}^+
                       -\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}^-$.
Each positive row is smooth convex and decreases as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$, by the convexity/Jensen argument already
printed for PL slots.  The signed row is the convolution of
$\lambda_i$ itself.  It converges locally uniformly, and all its
first coefficient derivatives have one compact-stage bound.
Let $\alpha_\varepsilon$ be the smooth form obtained from (P1)
by these replacements.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform normal-factor error for the differentiated rows]
\label{lem:r10-pws-word-uniform-error}
Fix a compact original test stage, a PS form $\alpha$ as above,
and an original compact smooth complementary form $\eta$.
There are finitely many fixed original positive compact smooth
controls $\Theta_l$ and a constant $C$ such that, for every
allowed positive separately closed diagonal current $T$ of the
degree needed to pair $\alpha\wedge T$ with $\eta$,
\[
 \left|\mu_{(\alpha_\varepsilon-\alpha)\wedge T,\eta}\right|
        (\operatorname{supp}\eta)
 \le C\varepsilon^{1/2}\sum_l\langle T,\Theta_l\rangle.
 \tag{P3}
\]
The same estimate holds after multiplication by a Borel scalar
of absolute value at most one.  It applies to each word arising
by differentiating the coefficient part of (P1) once or twice.
All actual refinements are allowed by making a common original
moment presentation with the chosen test.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the
frozen R4 normal-factor variation estimate, with the required
special smoothing rows verified here.

\begin{proof}
Refine the finitely many PL subdivisions by one finite arrangement
of affine hyperplanes $\ell_H=0$.  Choose on each face an ambient
gradient from any incident chamber.  These are legitimate PS
representatives by the frozen tangency theorem.

Across a facet, continuity of $\lambda_i$ makes the difference
of its two constant gradients a scalar multiple of $d\ell_H$.
Compare two points at distance at most $\varepsilon$ by the
segment between them.  The successive gradient changes are
bounded normal multiples at the finitely many crossed walls.
Every crossed wall satisfies $|\ell_H(x)|\le C_H\varepsilon$
at the initial point $x$.  At a point on several walls the
same statement holds after choosing an incident chamber; its
ambiguity is a sum of the same conormals.  Averaging the
gradient differences against the kernel therefore gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 d'\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}-d'_P\lambda_i
       &=\sum_H b'_{i,H,\varepsilon}\,d'\ell_H,\\
 d''\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}-d''_P\lambda_i
       &=\sum_H b''_{i,H,\varepsilon}\,d''\ell_H,
 \end{split}
 \tag{P4}
\]
where the Borel coefficients have a common bound and are supported
in the indicated shrinking wall tubes.  All identities are
understood modulo the face conormal ambiguity, which every
allowed $T$ annihilates before Borel restriction.

The scalar functions $\lambda_{i,\varepsilon}-\lambda_i$ are
$O(\varepsilon)$ uniformly, so smoothness of $F$ on a compact
coordinate neighborhood gives the same bound for their scalar
coefficient error.  Expand the difference of the finite wedge
products in (P1) by replacing one factor at a time.  It is a sum
of an $O(\varepsilon)$ bounded coefficient form and bounded
forms with one factor $d'\ell_H$ or $d''\ell_H$, supported in
the corresponding wall tube.  All other first-derivative
coefficients are uniformly bounded.  Multiplication by the fixed
smooth $\eta$ preserves this description.

Original coefficient domination bounds the first part by
$C\varepsilon\sum_l\langle T,\Theta_l\rangle$.  The R4
normal-factor variation estimate bounds every remaining part by
$C\varepsilon^{1/2}\sum_l\langle T,\Theta_l\rangle$.
That frozen estimate is a total-variation estimate and already
permits arbitrary bounded Borel coefficients in its other
factors.  It therefore proves (P3) and its scalar-weight version.
If the complementary degree of $T$ is zero, only scalar words
can occur, and uniform scalar convergence proves the estimate
without a wall argument.

Replacing $F$ by one of its finitely many derivatives and
deleting or adding finitely many first-derivative letters gives
exactly the same coefficient description.  This proves the
assertion needed for once- and twice-differentiated words.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Weighted BT convergence against these moving PS rows]
\label{lem:r10-weighted-pws-moving-tails}
Let $T_m$ be any positive mixed bounded BT tail over a fixed
allowed background, whose finitely many classical slots decrease
to locally bounded limits, and let $T$ be the limiting tail.
Let $u_m\downarrow u$ be bounded classical weights with locally
bounded limit; a fixed bounded classical $u_m=u$ is allowed.
Let $\alpha_{\varepsilon_m}$ be one of the rows just constructed,
where $\varepsilon_m\downarrow0$.  Then
\[
             u_m\alpha_{\varepsilon_m}\wedge T_m
                          \longrightarrow u\alpha\wedge T
 \tag{P5}
\]
on every original compact smooth complementary test.
The assertion also holds with the fixed PS coefficient $\alpha$
in place of its moving row.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as the
weighted PS convergence used in the intrinsic extension.

\begin{proof}
Unweighted frozen BT convergence bounds the finitely many
positive controls of $T_m$ in (P3), uniformly in $m$.
The weights have a common finite compact-stage bound.
Thus (P3) shows that replacing
$\alpha_{\varepsilon_m}$ by $\alpha$ in (P5) has error tending
to zero, even after multiplication by $u_m$.

To handle the fixed $\alpha$, choose another fixed smoothing
parameter $\delta>0$.  The test
$\alpha_\delta\wedge\eta$ is original smooth, so the frozen
weighted joint theorem gives
\[
 \langle u_m\alpha_\delta\wedge T_m,\eta\rangle
                  \longrightarrow
 \langle u\alpha_\delta\wedge T,\eta\rangle.
\]
The errors in replacing $\alpha_\delta$ by $\alpha$ on either
side are uniformly $O(\delta^{1/2})$, by (P3) and the common
weight and control bounds.  First let $m\to\infty$ and then
$\delta\downarrow0$.  This proves both assertions.  In
particular the passage with a possibly discontinuous classical
weight uses the frozen weighted BT theorem; it is not inferred
from weak convergence of Radon measures against Borel tests.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Intrinsic derivatives and the corrected operator}

\begin{definition}[The full PS coefficient module over allowed backgrounds]
\label{def:r10-full-pws-background-module}
For $0\le a,b\le n$, let $\mathscr N_{\rm PS}^{a,b}$ consist
of original currents locally admitting a finite expression
\[
                         R=\sum_{\nu=1}^N\alpha_\nu\wedge S_\nu,
 \tag{P6}
\]
where each $S_\nu$ is an allowed arbitrary original positive
separately closed current and $\alpha_\nu$ is an actual PS form
of the needed bidegree.  Products in (P6) are the frozen
canonical PS products.  Equality means equality of original
currents on all original tests, not equality of witnesses.
Neither symmetry nor separate closedness of $R$ is assumed.
\end{definition}

Every such $R$ belongs to the frozen tangential Radon module,
even when it is not closed.  Indeed, write a PS multiplier by
its finite smooth-face/Borel-stratum formula.  For every original
smooth level $h=c$, both conormals annihilate the corresponding
restriction of each closed $S_\nu$ before any face restriction.
Bounded coefficient multiplication and further Borel restriction
preserve these zero measures, so the same conormal identities
hold for $R$.  The R6 PS multiplication theorem consequently
applies to $R$ itself.  Its finite face formula is intrinsic:
a zero coefficient-Radon current has zero coefficient measures,
which remain zero after each bounded coefficient multiplication.
Thus further PS multiplication and associativity do not depend
on a witness (P6), and do not require $R$ to be separately closed.

\begin{theorem}[Derivative-Radon closure with every interface retained]
\label{thm:r10-pws-derivative-radon-closure}
The module $\mathscr N_{\rm PS}$ is stable under actual PS
exterior coefficients, $d'$, and $d''$.  In particular
\[
                        R,\quad d'R,\quad d''R,\quad DR
                   \quad\hbox{are coefficient-Radon currents}.
 \tag{P7}
\]
Their derivatives are their intrinsic original distribution
derivatives.  They can be computed in any local anchored
presentation by the usual graded product rule, using the
following replacements for every continuous PL generator
$\lambda=\lambda^+-\lambda^-$ over a closed tail $T$:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 &d'&d''\\ \hline
 \lambda&d'_P\lambda&d''_P\lambda\\
 d'_P\lambda&0&-D(\lambda T)\\
 d''_P\lambda&D(\lambda T)&0 .
 \end{array}
 \tag{P8}
\]
In the bottom two rows the entry means insertion into that
word and absorption of the curvature into the closed tail;
$D(\lambda T)=D(\lambda^+T)-D(\lambda^-T)$.
Several curvature factors mean the frozen mixed BT products,
expanded linearly in their positive and negative slots.
All identities hold on every original test and every actual
moment refinement.  Degrees outside $0,\ldots,n$ are zero.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
intrinsic differential module and its interface formulas.
The existence of the undifferentiated module is
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT} from R6.

\begin{proof}
PS multiplication and its associativity are frozen inputs.
Consider one word $\alpha\wedge S$ in (P6), using (P1)--(P2),
and its smooth row $R_m=\alpha_{\varepsilon_m}\wedge S$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:r10-pws-word-uniform-error} gives
$R_m\to R$ in local coefficient variation on every fixed test.

Differentiate the smooth word once or twice.  A coefficient
derivative of $F$ creates another first-derivative letter.
Differentiating $d'\lambda_m$ by $d''$ gives
$-D\lambda_m$, and differentiating $d''\lambda_m$ by $d'$
gives $D\lambda_m$.  The other same-prime derivatives and
all derivatives of curvature factors are zero.  After
expanding (P2), every term in $d'R_m$, $d''R_m$, or $DR_m$
is another row of the type in Lemma
~\ref{lem:r10-pws-word-uniform-error} multiplied by a positive
closed BT tail over $S$, with at most two inserted convex
PL smoothing slots.  The signs are exactly the usual graded
signs; no derivative of a Borel face indicator is discarded.

Lemma~\ref{lem:r10-weighted-pws-moving-tails}, with weight
one, gives a coefficient-Radon limit for each finite term.
It is its stated PS coefficient times the bounded BT tail
of the limiting PL potentials.  Distributional differentiation
is continuous on the original test space, so these limits are
precisely $d'R$, $d''R$, and $DR$.  Their finite expressions
belong to $\mathscr N_{\rm PS}$, because every positive
mixed tail is again an allowed closed background.  This also
proves (P8).

The intrinsic distribution derivative is independent of every
choice of representative, subdivision, DC splitting, and
smoothing row.  The finite calculation therefore proves
the asserted independence rather than assuming it.
The frozen anchored presentation and PS multiplication apply
after every common actual refinement.  Localizing on compact
supports and gluing gives the full original test statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic corrected bounded insertion on the PS module]
\label{thm:r10-pws-corrected-bounded-insertion}
For $R\in\mathscr N_{\rm PS}^{a,b}$ and an original locally
bounded classical psh function $u$, with
$\max(a,b)+1\le n$, the intrinsic distribution
\[
 \mathfrak B_uR
    =D(uR)-d'(u\,d''R)+d''(u\,d'R)+uDR
 \tag{P9}
\]
is a coefficient-Radon current belonging to
$\mathscr N_{\rm PS}^{a+1,b+1}$.  For every witness (P6),
\[
                   \mathfrak B_uR
                         =\sum_\nu\alpha_\nu\wedge D(uS_\nu).
 \tag{P10}
\]
In particular (P10) is independent of that witness.
It is linear over actual PS exterior coefficients, local in
the ordinary topology, and commutes with $d'$ and $d''$ in
every permitted bidegree.  Iteration gives
\[
 \mathfrak B_{u_k}\cdots\mathfrak B_{u_1}R
        =\sum_\nu\alpha_\nu\wedge
                          T_{S_\nu,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k),
       \qquad \max(a,b)+k\le n.
 \tag{P11}
\]
These products are mixed symmetric and have joint decreasing
continuity on every original compact smooth test.
No middle-order preservation for an arbitrary positive
nonclosed member of $\mathscr N_{\rm PS}$ is asserted.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
PS coefficient extension, including bounded classical weights
which are not assumed continuou

title: PS coefficient caps and sharp conormal reconstruction
text:
S07_pws_curvature_generated_reconstruction.tex \section{PS coefficient caps and sharp conormal reconstruction}
\label{sec:r10-pws-curvature-reconstruction}

This section uses the intrinsic PS differential module of
Section~\ref{sec:r10-pws-differential-module}.  It removes the
smooth-coefficient restriction from the corrected cap criterion
and from the positive-curvature-generated reconstruction theorem.
It does not remove the independent capped-background relation
premise.  All backgrounds and final tests remain original over
the fixed field and absolute value.

\begin{lemma}[Corrected PS caps, full fibers, and every parameter]
\label{lem:r10-pws-corrected-cap-criterion}
Let $R\in\mathscr N_{\rm PS}^{a,b}$, and let $c\ge1$ satisfy
$\max(a,b)+c\le n$.  For any local original smooth rank-$c$
unit map $f$ and real parameter $\mathbf t$, define
\[
 \mathfrak C_{f,\mathbf t}R=
 \mathfrak B_{(\log|f_c|-t_c)_+}\cdots
 \mathfrak B_{(\log|f_1|-t_1)_+}R.
 \tag{PC1}
\]
For a PS witness $R=\sum_\nu\alpha_\nu\wedge S_\nu$, it has
the intrinsic factorization
\[
 \mathfrak C_{f,\mathbf t}R=j_*Q_R,\qquad
 Q_R=\sum_\nu j^*\alpha_\nu\wedge Q_{S_\nu}
 \tag{PC2}
\]
on the complete fiber from the frozen R9 theorem.
Here PS multiplication on the specified closed cap currents
$Q_{S_\nu}$ is the tangential coefficient product; no
auxiliary-field BT operation is defined.  The current $Q_R$
is independent of the witness and need not be closed.

For every fixed original compact smooth complementary test
$\eta$, the pairing
$\langle\mathfrak C_{f,\mathbf t}R,\eta\rangle$ is continuous
in $\mathbf t$.  For diagonal $R\in\mathscr N_{\rm PS}^{P,P}$
and $1\le c\le n-P$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every local corrected intrinsic rank-$c$ cap is zero
      for every real parameter, on every original intrinsic test.
\item Every local tuple of original analytic units satisfies
\[
                \omega_{g_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\omega_{g_c}
                                  \wedge R=0
 \tag{PC3}
\]
      on all original complementary tests.
\end{enumerate}
No symmetry, separate closedness, or positivity of $R$ is
required.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the PS
extension of the already printed smooth coefficient criterion.

\begin{proof}
Theorem~\ref{thm:r10-pws-corrected-bounded-insertion} gives
the finite sum $\sum_\nu\alpha_\nu\wedge
\mathfrak C_{f,\mathbf t}S_\nu$ on the original space.
Each latter cap has the frozen full-fiber factorization
$j_*Q_{S_\nu}$.

For clarity, the tangential product in (PC2) requires no new
complete-field intersection theory.  R9 supplies an actual
positive separately closed coefficient-Radon current $Q_{S_\nu}$
and all original tests on its specified complete fiber.
The elementary R6 level-tangency proof applies to that current:
bounded smooth cutoffs of a level force both conormal factors
to annihilate its coefficient restriction to the level.
Consequently the finite PS face formula defines
$j^*\alpha_\nu\wedge Q_{S_\nu}$ independently of incident
extensions.  Original moment units restrict to fiber units;
the same tangent-restriction argument respects zero PS
representatives and every further actual fiber moment.
On each Borel face the smooth projection formula then gives
the PS projection formula
\[
 j_*(j^*\alpha_\nu\wedge Q_{S_\nu})
                        =\alpha_\nu\wedge j_*Q_{S_\nu}.
\]
Finite summation proves (PC2).  Exact original full-fiber
lifting of every smooth intrinsic test makes this pushforward
injective.  Thus the intrinsic factor is unique, even though
it need not be separately closed.

Fix a compact parameter set and an original compact test.
The positive closed currents
$T_{\nu,\mathbf t}=\mathfrak C_{f,\mathbf t}S_\nu$ have
uniform bounds on each finite family of compact positive
controls: their pairings with those controls are continuous
by the frozen R9 continuous-cap theorem.  The uniform estimate
(P3) therefore approximates the fixed PS pairing
$\langle\alpha_\nu\wedge T_{\nu,\mathbf t},\eta\rangle$
uniformly on this parameter set by smooth coefficient pairings.
Those pairings are continuous by R9, so their uniform limit
is continuous.  This proves the claimed every-parameter
continuity without a continuity assertion for nonclosed
backgrounds imported from outside the PS module.

The original unweighted and compactly weighted parameter
averaging identities extend to these PS pairings in the
same way.  One may first smooth each coefficient, use the
frozen identity, and then pass by (P3), uniform compact
parameter mass controls, and dominated integration.  The
averaged closed currents themselves have finite compact
controls by the R9 parameter-kernel theorem.  Thus their
PS pairings converge on the other side as well.

If every cap is zero, unweighted local averaging gives
the corresponding smooth rank-$c$ wedge zero.
Conversely, if that wedge is zero, its product with every
compact continuous function of the parameter logarithms
is zero.  The weighted identity makes every compactly
weighted integral of each cap pairing zero.  A continuous
function with all those integrals zero is identically
zero.  This gives the cap equality at every parameter,
and exact intrinsic test lifting gives its full-fiber
version.  Finally the frozen original norm-preserving
smoothification converts arbitrary local unit tuples to
smooth parameter tuples with exactly the same logarithms,
hinges, and smooth rank-one forms.  This proves (PC3) and
its converse in the ordinary local topology.  All smoothing
and averaging arguments were made after adjoining the
chosen original test moments, so every actual refinement
is admitted.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[PS-weighted curvature generation]
\label{def:r10-pws-curvature-generated}
Let $\mathscr G_{\rm PS}^{a,b}$ be the PS submodule of
$\mathscr N_{\rm PS}^{a,b}$ locally generated by
$D(vS)$, where $S$ is any allowed original positive closed
background and
$v\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sm}\downarrow}$ is one of the
explicitly regularizable bounded classical slots defined
earlier.  Thus a member is locally a finite sum
$\alpha_\nu\wedge D(v_\nu S_\nu)$ with arbitrary actual
PS coefficients $\alpha_\nu$.
\end{definition}

Every positive-codimension prescribed pure cycle action,
multiplied by any actual PS coefficient, belongs to this
module: its finite signed PL presentation has at least
one regularizable convex PL slot.  The module is stable
under all PS coefficients and all permitted corrected
bounded insertions, by (P11) and mixed symmetry.  This
statement is a \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}; it does not
assert that every bounded classical potential is
regularizable.

\begin{lemma}[Conormal annihilation with PS coefficients]
\label{lem:r10-pws-generated-conormal-annihilation}
Let $R\in\mathscr G_{\rm PS}^{P,P}$ and $q=n-P$.
Let $0\le j<q$, $\ell=q-j$, and
$\Omega=\omega_{g_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge\omega_{g_j}$
for local original units.  If $n\le j+2\ell$, then
\[
                    \langle R,\Omega\wedge
                              s_{\ell,\ell}\gamma\rangle=0
 \tag{PC4}
\]
for every compact original prime form
$\gamma\in\mathscr A_c^{2\ell,0}$ on that open.
The assertion does not require $R$ to be symmetric or closed.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} in this
PS coefficient scope.

\begin{proof}
Take one term $\alpha\wedge D(vS)$ and a local smooth
decreasing approximation $v_m\downarrow v$.  The actual
form identity proved in the smooth conormal section says
\[
                    \Omega\wedge Dv_m\wedge
                                  s_{\ell,\ell}\gamma=0.
 \tag{PC5}
\]
On each actual tangent face, rank-deficient conormals
make $\Omega=0$.  Otherwise quotient by their $j$
covectors.  Its dimension is at most $n-j\le2\ell$.
The top alternating shuffle is annihilated by every
symmetric $(1,1)$ tensor, including the Hessian of $v_m$.
This proves (PC5) on the full actual form sheaf, including
the moments of each $v_m$ and of the test.

Canonical PS associativity and the smooth closed-background
rule make the corresponding pairing with
$\alpha\wedge D(v_mS)$ zero.  The fixed-PS version of
(P5), applied to the positive closed currents $D(v_mS)$,
passes this equality to $\alpha\wedge D(vS)$.
This use of PS test convergence is essential: the fixed
coefficient is not assumed smooth and is not differentiated.
Finite sums and ordinary localization prove (PC4).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The sharp PS-generated equality thresholds]
\label{thm:r10-pws-generated-thresholds}
Let $1\le P<n$, $q=n-P$, and $1\le c\le q$.
For currents in $\mathscr G_{\rm PS}^{P,P}$, let
$\mathscr G_{{\rm PS},c}$ denote the kernel of all local
$c$-fold smooth unit wedges (PC3), with
$\mathscr G_{{\rm PS},0}=\{0\}$.
Without a symmetry hypothesis, the universal kernel jump
from $c-1$ to $c$ is strict exactly when
\[
                              n>2q-c+1.
 \tag{PC6}
\]
For the symmetric submodule it is strict exactly when
both (PC6) holds and $q-c+1$ is even.  Accordingly the
sharp universal zero-detection ranges are
\[
 \begin{array}{ll}
 c\le h_{\rm all}(n,P)=\max(0,n-2P+1),
                      &\text{without symmetry},\\[2pt]
 c\le h_{\rm ex}(n,P)
       =\max\{q\bmod2,\ q-2\lfloor(P-1)/2\rfloor\},
                      &\text{with symmetry}.
 \end{array}
 \tag{PC7}
\]
Within the indicated range, every zero corrected rank-$c$
cap implies $R=0$ on all original tests.  Sharpness means
that the excluded universal implications have explicit
original torus witnesses; strictness is not asserted on
every individual analytic space.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
full PS coefficient class.  The threshold arithmetic and
sharp torus witnesses are already proved in the smooth
generated-response theorem and are not counted twice.

\begin{proof}
Put $j=c-1$ and $\ell=q-j$.  If $R$ has zero
$c$-fold wedges, then every $j$-fold compression
$T=\Omega\wedge R$ is Hessian-invisible.  The intrinsic
alternating quotient therefore says that its entire
pairing is determined by its pairings with
$s_{\ell,\ell}\gamma$.  This algebraic factorization
does not require separate closedness or positivity.
When $n\le j+2\ell$, these pairings vanish by (PC4).
Thus every $j$-compression is zero, which proves the
non-jump assertion.  In the symmetric case the same
factorization also vanishes for odd $\ell$ by the
printed prime--double-prime symmetry rule.

The strict-jump examples constructed in (X8)--(X9) and
(G10)--(G11) use smooth coefficients and hence already
belong to $\mathscr G_{\rm PS}$.  Their complete
original-refinement calculations are unchanged; the
nonsymmetric examples allow odd $\ell$ as well.
They prove exactly the opposite implications in (PC6).
Inducting the non-jump steps from $c$ to zero yields
the bounds (PC7), with the same elementary integer
calculation as before.  The cap statement follows from
the equivalence in Lemma
~\ref{lem:r10-pws-corrected-cap-criterion}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A PS variable-coefficient arbitrary-background reduction]
\label{cor:r10-pws-variable-relation-reconstruction}
Fix an allowed arbitrary original background $S$.  Let
$e$ be a finite compatible PS/PL presentation whose
prescribed response has diagonal degree $(P,P)$,
$1\le P<n$, and is a finite sum
\[
                R=\mathcal A_S(e)
                       =\sum_i\alpha_i\wedge\mathcal A(C_i)S,
 \tag{PC8}
\]
where every $\alpha_i$ is an actual PS form and every
constant pure cycle $C_i$ has positive codimension.
Fix $1\le c\le n-P$.  Suppose independently that the
same presentation acts by zero on every local original
pushed rank-$c$ cap background of $S$, at every real
parameter.  Then $R=0$ on every original complementary
test whenever $c\le h_{\rm all}(n,P)$; if $R$ is
symmetric, it suffices that $c\le h_{\rm ex}(n,P)$.
All statements allow every actual moment refinement.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
response reconstruction.  As an application to all
actual-zero presentations, it remains
\texttt{CONDITIONAL} on the printed capped-background
premise.

\begin{proof}
Every term of (PC8) belongs to
$\mathscr G_{\rm PS}$ by its positive-codimension PL
presentation.  The corrected operator is PS-linear.
Mixed symmetry of the frozen closed tails therefore
identifies each corrected cap of $R$ with the response
of the same presentation on the original capped $S$.
The premise makes these zero.  Apply the preceding
threshold theorem.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The exact progress and the remaining quotient gate.}
The derivative-Radon and interface gate for finite actual PS
coefficients has now been proved through (P3)--(P13); it
is no longer assumed in (PC8).  This does not identify
ordinary equality with equality on all GK delta tests.
Nor does an actual-zero analytic presentation automatically
supply the independent cap-background premise above.
Individual codimension-zero summands need not belong to
$\mathscr G_{\rm PS}$.  For a compatible actual-zero expression,
however, Proposition~\ref{prop:r10-actual-zero-codim-zero-removal}
uses the frozen global actual trigrading to discard their
already-zero PS sum.  Corollary
~\ref{cor:r10-actual-zero-full-ps-cap-reduction} therefore removes
the positive-cycle-codimension restriction in this actual-zero
application, while retaining the independent cap premise.
Theorem~\ref{thm:r10-ps-module-positivity} also proves middle
positivity on the finite actual PS module by closed conormal
penalties.  The unrestricted analytic relation implication and
reflection of middle order from actual signed cycle inequalities
remain the separate \texttt{OPEN} GQ/CTO gates.

title: Order-controlled intrinsic extensions and sufficient certificates for non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor actions
text:
proofs.tex \documentclass[11pt]{article}
\usepackage[a4paper,margin=28mm]{geometry}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm,mathtools,hyperref}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\newtheorem{corollary}[theorem]{Corollary}
\newtheorem{proposition}[theorem]{Proposition}
\theoremstyle{remark}\newtheorem{remark}[theorem]{Remark}
\newcommand{\M}{\mathcal M^1}
\newcommand{\Pp}{\Phi_{S,r}}
\newcommand{\D}{\mathrm D}
\newcommand{\supp}{\operatorname{supp}}
\title{Order-controlled intrinsic extensions and sufficient certificates\ for non-Archimedean Bedford--Taylor actions}
\author{Internal continuation after the R24 audit}
\date{14 November 2026}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\begin{abstract}
We establish quantitative order continuity of the already constructed
continuous-coefficient curvature products, identify their order completions
with actual currents, and extend the products uniquely to these completions.
We also prove that controlled approximation by already annihilated
degree-one forms suffices for the quadratic action obstruction to vanish.
These are consequences of accepted internal inputs, not a solution of the
general analytic relation problem. In particular, no density assertion,
new principal descent theorem, or claim of literature priority is made.
\end{abstract}
\tableofcontents

\section{Scope and precise inputs}

Work over the original finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$, with its unchanged
absolute value, on an ordinary open $U$ of a good, Hausdorff, boundaryless,
quasi-smooth analytic space, locally of pure dimension $n$. All equalities
of currents are on the full original compactly supported smooth CLD test
sheaf. All actual moment refinements are retained. Write $D=d'd''$ with
$d'd''=-d''d'$. An allowed background $S$ has bidegree $(p,p)$ and is
symmetric, middle-positive and separately closed. No stronger positive cone
or geometric presentation of $S$ is imposed.

The input sheaf $\M$ consists of symmetric coefficient-Radon $(1,1)$
currents locally admitting finite presentations
\[
 A=\sum_i f_iD[g_i],\qquad f_i\in C(U,\mathbf R),
\]
where $g_i$ are locally bounded original classical psh functions; signed
differences are handled by finite expansion. Equality is actual current
equality, not equality of formal expressions. Its positive cone is the
original middle cone. Frozen R6 supplies symmetric, positive,
$C(U,\mathbf R)$-multilinear products
\[
 \Phi_{S,r}:(\M)^r\longrightarrow\mathcal D'^{p+r,p+r},\qquad
 \Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)
 =\sum_{i_1,\ldots,i_r}\prod_j f_{j,i_j}
       T_{S,r}(g_{1,i_1},\ldots,g_{r,i_r}),
 \tag{I1}
\]
for $r\le n-p$. Values are coefficient-Radon currents. This operation is
ordinary-local and respects all representations and actual refinements.
For $r=1$ put $M_S=\Phi_{S,1}$. The same notation agrees with the frozen
degree-one action on genuine symmetric analytic delta-forms. On
nonsymmetric genuine $B^{1,1}$ arguments in (I3), $M_S$ denotes the
broader frozen QA degree-one action. All order estimates and completions
in this note are restricted to symmetric arguments.

We use the frozen finite-frame coefficient domination: if $R$ is positive
and $T$ symmetric with $-cR\le T\le cR$, then, for each fixed original
compact test $\eta$, there is a finite positive control
\[
 |\langle T,\eta\rangle|\le c\,N_{R,\eta}<\infty.       \tag{I2}
\]
On each finite moment presentation and compact stage this also controls
the coefficient measures. It follows by applying positivity to $cR\pm T$
and the fixed finite positive controls for $\eta$. These are the original
middle-cone controls, not an assertion about a stronger cone. In particular,
an order-bounded limit is coefficient-Radon, the cone is weakly closed,
and differential operators are continuous for distributional convergence.

Frozen QA supplies, for actual analytic $\beta\in B^{0,1}$ and
$\zeta\in B^{1,0}$,
\[
 M_S(d'\beta)=d'(\beta\wedge S),\qquad
 M_S(d''\zeta)=d''(\zeta\wedge S).                       \tag{I3}
\]
These are full derivatives with every polyhedral boundary term present.
Consequently $DM_S(d'\beta+d''\zeta)=0$.

The exact source files and hashes are in the accompanying dependency ledger.
These inputs are adopted in their frozen scope; the present note does not
independently reprove the entire R1--R24 chain.

\section{A sharp order estimate}

\begin{lemma}[Signed products controlled by positive products]\label{lem:order}
Suppose $Q_i\in\M$ are positive and
$-M_iQ_i\le A_i\le M_iQ_i$ for $M_i\ge0$. Then
\[
 -\Bigl(\prod_iM_i\Bigr)R_S\le
 \Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)\le
 \Bigl(\prod_iM_i\Bigr)R_S,
 \qquad R_S=\Phi_{S,r}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r)\ge0.             \tag{OC1}
\]
If $-M_iQ_i\le A_i,B_i\le M_iQ_i$ and
$-\delta_iQ_i\le A_i-B_i\le\delta_iQ_i$, then
\[
 -E R_S\le \Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)
               -\Phi_{S,r}(B_1,\ldots,B_r)\le E R_S,
 \qquad E=\sum_i\delta_i\prod_{j\ne i}M_j.             \tag{OC2}
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Put $A_i^\pm=(M_iQ_i\pm A_i)/2$. Each is a positive member of $\M$,
$A_i=A_i^+-A_i^-$ and $A_i^++A_i^-=M_iQ_i$. Expanding the product by
multilinearity gives a signed sum of positive currents. Its positive and
negative subsums are both bounded by the sum of all terms, which is
$\Phi_{S,r}(M_1Q_1,\ldots,M_rQ_r)$. More exactly, the unsigned sum
plus or minus the signed sum is twice one of those positive subsums.
This proves (OC1), including zero values of $M_i$. Telescope the difference
of the two products one slot at a time and apply (OC1) to each summand.
Adding the resulting order inequalities proves (OC2). No positivity of
a signed tail is assumed.
\end{proof}

The estimate holds for every allowed $S$ with the same numerical $E$.
The controlling mass $N_{R_S,\eta}$ depends on $S$ and the test; there is
no uniform bound on the masses of all backgrounds.

\section{Completion as actual currents}

For one positive $Q\in\M(U)$ set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_Q(U)&=\{A\in\M(U): -cQ\le A\le cQ\text{ for some }c<\infty\},\\
 \|A\|_Q&=\inf\{c:-cQ\le A\le cQ\}.
 \end{aligned}                                         \tag{OC3}
\]
The case $Q=0$ gives the zero space. Every finite presentation belongs
locally to such an ideal: after bounding its coefficients, a sum of the
positive curvatures in that presentation is a control. No one global
control on an arbitrary open is asserted.

\begin{theorem}[Faithful realization of each order completion]\label{thm:completion}
The norm completion $\widehat E_Q(U)$ embeds isometrically into actual
symmetric coefficient-Radon $(1,1)$ currents on $U$. Its image is exactly
the closure of $E_Q(U)$ in the order norm determined by $Q$ in the ambient
space of such currents. If the same actual current is obtained with
controls $Q$ and $R$, the two realizations agree in the completion for
$Q+R$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The gauge is a norm: if its value is zero, then $\pm A\le\epsilon Q$
for every $\epsilon>0$; (I2) on every test implies $A=0$.
The triangle inequality follows by adding order bounds. Weak closedness
of the cone also shows that the infimum defining a finite norm is attained.

If $(A_j)$ is order-Cauchy, (I2) makes its values Cauchy on every test.
The local finite-frame bound makes the limit a distribution and, on each
compact presentation, coefficient-Radon. Its symmetry and compatibility
between presentations pass to the limit. Write the resulting actual
current as $A$. If $\|A_j-A_k\|_Q\le\epsilon$ for $j,k\ge N$, let
$k\to\infty$ in the order inequalities to obtain
\[
                -\epsilon Q\le A_j-A\le\epsilon Q
                       \quad(j\ge N).                   \tag{OC4}
\]
Thus convergence is in the ambient order norm. If $A=0$, (OC4) says
the original sequence represents zero in the completion, proving
injectivity; (OC4) also proves the norm assertion and the characterization
of the image. Since $Q\le Q+R$ and $R\le Q+R$, both completion sequences
are Cauchy for the larger control. Their actual limits agree, so
injectivity for $Q+R$ identifies them.
\end{proof}

Define $\M_{\rm ord}$ locally: an actual symmetric coefficient-Radon
current belongs if every point has an ordinary neighborhood on which it
lies in one of these embedded completions. This is a sheaf by its local
definition and the sheaf property of currents. It is not a claim that a
single global order bound survives arbitrary gluing. Local addition uses
$Q+R$, and multiplication by continuous functions uses their local boundedness.

\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic extension of the mixed operations]\label{thm:extension}
The operations (I1) extend uniquely to symmetric locally
$C(U,\mathbf R)$-multilinear maps on $(\M_{\rm ord})^r$, continuous in
each common finite collection of local order controls. They are independent
of approximation sequences, controls and moment presentations, preserve
positivity, commute with ordinary restriction and gluing, and satisfy
(OC1)--(OC2). Their supports satisfy
\[
 \supp\Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)
       \subseteq\supp S\cap\bigcap_i\supp A_i.          \tag{OC5}
\]
If mixed products along one such approximation are separately closed,
their limit is separately closed. Separate closedness of the limit factors
alone is not claimed to imply this hypothesis.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Choose local controls $Q_i$ and Cauchy approximations $A_{i,j}$.
Their norms are bounded, so (OC2) and (I2) make the mixed products Cauchy
in coefficient measure on every fixed compact presentation. They have
a coefficient-Radon limit. Applying (OC2) to different approximations
proves uniqueness for these controls. For other controls $R_i$, replace
each by $Q_i+R_i$ and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:completion}; the same estimate
proves equality of the resulting limits. All algebraic properties follow
by taking limits of the frozen identities.

If $A_i\ge0$, (OC4) yields positive approximants
$A_{i,j}+\epsilon_{i,j}Q_i\ge0$ with $\epsilon_{i,j}\to0$.
They have the same limits. Positivity follows from (I1) and weak closedness
of the cone. Passing the order inequalities to the limit gives (OC1)--(OC2).
Restriction maps are contractive for the restricted controls. The local
constructions therefore agree on intersections and glue as ordinary
currents. On an open where one $A_i$ is zero, its completion class is zero
by Theorem~\ref{thm:completion}; multilinearity makes the product zero.
The same is true where $S=0$, proving (OC5). Distributional continuity
of $d'$ and $d''$ proves the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What the completion does not assert]
This is an intrinsic extension by a specified convergence mechanism.
We have not proved that it strictly enlarges $\M$, that all positive closed
currents belong to it, that products of arbitrary currents exist, or that
all actual higher-degree analytic relations are killed. The theorem does
not alter the carrier-CLN seminorm or its relation ideal. Closedness of
actions of arbitrary closed degree-one delta-forms remains a separate issue.
\end{remark}

\section{Controlled exact approximation and the quadratic obstruction}

For a finite actual PL relation
\[
 P=\sum_\nu c_\nu[h_\nu][g_\nu],\qquad
 \sum_\nu c_\nu D_\delta h_\nu\wedge D_\delta g_\nu=0,
\]
QA defines the symmetric actual degree-one primitive
\[
 \alpha_P=\frac12\sum_\nu c_\nu
       (h_\nu D_\delta g_\nu+g_\nu D_\delta h_\nu),
 \quad D_\delta\alpha_P=0,
 \quad\mathcal A_S(P)=DM_S(\alpha_P).                    \tag{OC6}
\]
The operation on the right is already defined, without assuming a
general degree-two action on delta-forms.

\begin{theorem}[Controlled approximation suffices]\label{thm:density}
Let $\alpha\in B^{1,1}(U)$ be symmetric. Suppose actual symmetric
degree-one forms $a_j$, a fixed positive $Q\in\M(U)$ and
$\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ satisfy
\[
 -\epsilon_jQ\le[\alpha]-[a_j]\le\epsilon_jQ,
 \qquad DM_S(a_j)=0\quad\text{for every allowed }S.      \tag{OC7}
\]
The data are chosen on one representative before $S$ and the tests.
Then $DM_S(\alpha)=0$ for every allowed $S$, with
\[
 |\langle DM_S(\alpha),\eta\rangle|
             \le \epsilon_j N_{M_S(Q),D\eta}.           \tag{OC8}
\]
One sufficient, non-circular choice is
$a_j=d'\beta_j+d''\zeta_j$ in the full actual delta sheaf.
In particular, (OC7) for $\alpha=\alpha_P$ proves
$\mathcal A_S(P)=0$ for all backgrounds in legal degree.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
R6 positive scalar-module transfer gives
$-\epsilon_jM_S(Q)\le M_S(\alpha)-M_S(a_j)\le
\epsilon_jM_S(Q)$. Apply (I2) to the fixed test $D\eta$.
Distributional duality, whose fixed convention sign disappears inside
absolute values, gives (OC8). The right side tends to zero for each $S$
and each test. No derivative convergence of coefficients is needed.
Formula (I3) proves the asserted sufficient exactness condition. Finally
use (OC6). The argument can also be applied on neighborhoods of each
point and then glued; it does not restrict a global full polar.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Fixed generators and no gauge condition on potentials]
Suppose on one representative
\[
 [\gamma]=\sum_{i=1}^N f_iD[g_i],\qquad
 A_j=\sum_{i=1}^N f_{i,j}D[g_i]=D[v_j],                 \tag{OC9}
\]
where the $g_i$ are finite continuous classical psh differences, all
coefficients are continuous, $f_{i,j}\to f_i$ locally uniformly, and
$v_j$ are finite continuous local classical psh differences. Then
$M_S(\gamma)$ is separately closed for every allowed $S$.
No uniform bound, normalization, or convergence of $v_j$ is required.
For genuine degree-one delta curvatures the local DC requirement for a
given continuous potential is also supplied by frozen AP.
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
Write $g_i=g_i^+-g_i^-$ and take the fixed positive represented control
$Q=\sum_i(D[g_i^+]+D[g_i^-])$. On a compactly contained ordinary
neighborhood, with $\epsilon_j=\max_i\|f_i-f_{i,j}\|_\infty$,
the error in (OC9) lies between $\pm\epsilon_jQ$.
Equivalently its action is a finite sum of uniformly small coefficients
times fixed coefficient-Radon currents $D(g_iS)$. Thus
$M_S(A_j)\to M_S(\gamma)$ on all tests. Scalar relation transfer gives
$M_S(A_j)=D(v_jS)$, which is separately closed. Distributional continuity
of both first derivatives proves the assertion. Locality handles the
whole representative.
\end{proof}

This corollary replaces the demand for one exact continuous potential
by a particular controlled approximation target. No such approximation
has been constructed for all RV/QT boundaries, and strict logical
weakening within that analytic class has not been established. RV4 and
the general AP boundary problem therefore remain open. A weak limit of
ambient currents alone does not satisfy the displayed order hypothesis.

\section{A directly verifiable first-order relation certificate}

\begin{proposition}[Scalar rows and actual support conormals]\label{prop:conormal}
Put $A_i=D[g_i]$ and $T_i=D(g_iS)$ for fixed finite continuous psh
differences $g_i$. Let $F_i=\supp A_i$ be the actual analytic support.
Then $\supp T_i\subset F_i$. If $h$ is original smooth and vanishes
on $F_i$, then $d'h\wedge T_i=d''h\wedge T_i=0$.

Suppose smooth covectors $\theta_i$ admit a finite identity on $U$
\[
 \theta_i=\sum_a f_{ai}\eta_a+\sum_j b_{ij}d'h_{ij},
 \qquad \sum_i f_{ai}A_i=0,
 \qquad h_{ij}|_{F_i}=0,                               \tag{SC1}
\]
with continuous scalar coefficients and original smooth $\eta_a,h_{ij}$.
Then $\sum_i\theta_i\wedge T_i=0$. The same assertion holds with
the columns exchanged. There is also the version in which $\theta_i$
and $\eta_a$ are actual PS covectors, $f_{ai},b_{ij}$ are continuous PS
scalars, and $h_{ij}$ remain original smooth, provided the displayed
identities are identities in the already established PS coefficient
module. No new product for arbitrary continuous covector coefficients
is inferred from that version.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
On $U\setminus F_i$ the scalar curvature relation $A_i=0$ transfers
by R6 to $T_i=0$, proving the support assertion. Multiplication by $h$
gives $hT_i=0$. Since $T_i$ is separately closed, the smoo

title: Polar witnesses and capacitability from ambient extremals
text:
S03_polar_converse_choquet.tex \section{Polar witnesses and capacitability from ambient extremals}
\label{sec:r2-polar-converse-choquet}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}, relative to the adopted
inputs and the preceding reviewed R2 theorems.}
The witness construction, arbitrary-set extremal mass formula, and
ordinary-open proof of increasing continuity are supplied below.
The Choquet and patching consequences are
\texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}. The two theorem groups
\textup{(N)} and \textup{(E)} are separated to display dependencies;
both have been proved in the preceding sections. Neither a general
Josefson theorem nor Borel outer regularity is an input.

\subsection{Domain and the two theorem inputs}

Let $V$ be a connected ordinary open with compact closure in a smooth
affine algebraic chart over the fixed finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$.
Assume that its ordinary boundary is nonempty and that there is
\[
 \rho\in\Cb(V)\cap C(\overline V),\qquad
 \rho<0\text{ on }V,\qquad \rho=0\text{ on }\partial V.
\]
Thus each negative sublevel of $\rho$ has compact closure in $V$.
All capacities in this section use the ambient background $[1]$ and
the \emph{fixed admissibility domain $V$}. Write
\[
 C(E)=\operatorname{Cap}_{[1]}(E;V),\qquad
 C^*(E)=\inf_{\substack{G\supset E\\G\text{ ordinary open in }V}}C(G).
\]
The first notation is initially for Borel sets; the second is defined
for arbitrary subsets. All Monge--Amp\`ere measures and their weak
limits use the original CLD scalar test functions.

For any subset $A\subset V$, define
\[
 \mathcal F_A=\{v\in\Cb(V):-1\leq v\leq0,\ v=-1\text{ on }A\},
 \qquad h_A=\sup_{v\in\mathcal F_A}v,\qquad U_A=h_A^*.
\]
The ordinary upper regularization $U_A$ is bounded classical by
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-local-upper-envelope}. The conditions $v=-1$
and $v\leq-1$ are identical for this normalized family. The raw
supremum is never substituted for its regularization without a
stated argument.

The two theorem groups are recorded separately to make the dependency
order explicit:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\Alph*)}]
\item[\textup{(N)}] For every locally uniformly upper-bounded family
of bounded classical psh functions, the difference between its actual
supremum and its ordinary usc regularization is contained locally in
a Borel set of ambient outer capacity zero. In particular a locally
uniformly bounded increasing sequence has its actual supremum equal
to its regularization outside such a set, and their values agree at
every ambient divisorial point. Local and fixed-domain null classes
are identified only through
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-fixed-domain-null-classes}.
These are Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-negligible-outer-zero},
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-increasing-no-jump}, and
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-divisorial-no-jump}.

\item[\textup{(E)}] If $G\Subset V$ is ordinary open, then $U_G=-1$
at every point of $G$, $U_G$ has ordinary boundary limit zero,
$\operatorname{supp}(DU_G)^n\subset\overline G$, and
\[
 \int_V(DU_G)^n=C(G).
\]
For a compact $K\Subset V$, the corresponding compact extremal
identity is
\[
 \int_V(DU_K)^n=C(K).
\]
The open-set identity concerns \emph{total mass}. It does not assert
$\int_G(DU_G)^n=C(G)$: the function is constant on $G$.
These are Theorems~\ref{thm:r2-open-extremal} and
\ref{thm:r2-compact-extremal}, with the domain and boundary
properties of Lemma~\ref{lem:r2-extremal-basics}.
\end{enumerate}

For every fixed $A\subset W\Subset V$, choose $a>0$ sufficiently
large that $a\rho\leq-1$ on $\overline W$. Then
\[
 b=\max(-1,a\rho)\in\mathcal F_A,
 \qquad b\leq U_A\leq0.
\]
This gives the ordinary boundary limit zero of $U_A$, uniformly for
all such $A$. In particular $\{U_A<-1+\eta\}\Subset V$ for every
$0<\eta<1$, with a common compact bound for fixed $W$ and $\eta$.
The capacity of $W$ is finite by relative CLN on a slightly larger
compact stage.

We also use the total-mass order of
Lemma~\ref{lem:r2-total-mass-order}: if $u\leq v\leq0$ are bounded
classical functions with ordinary boundary limits zero, then
$\int_V(Dv)^n\leq\int_V(Du)^n$, including infinite masses.

\subsection{A nontrivial pole witness for an outer-capacity-zero set}

\begin{theorem}[A witness on the specified exhaustion domain]
\label{thm:r2-capacity-zero-polar-witness}
Let $E\subset W\Subset V$ be an arbitrary subset with $C^*(E)=0$.
For every fixed ambient divisorial point $z\in V$ there is a nonpositive
extended classical psh function $\phi$ on $V$ such that
\[
 E\subset\{\phi=-\infty\},\qquad -1\leq\phi(z)\leq0.
\]
In particular the witness is not identically $-\infty$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose an ordinary $W'$ with
$\overline W\subset W'\Subset V$. From $C^*(E)=0$ choose ordinary
opens $O_j\supset E$ with $C(O_j)<2^{-j}$ and set
\[
 G_j=W'\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^jO_i,\qquad u_j=U_{G_j}.
\]
The $G_j$ decrease, while $-1\leq u_j\uparrow h\leq0$.
They share a lower barrier $b=\max(-1,a\rho)$ as above.
Their measures are supported in the one compact set
$\overline W'$, and their total masses tend to zero by \textup{(E)}.

Put $U=h^*\in\Cb(V)$. By \textup{(N)}, $h=U$ locally outside
sets of outer capacity zero. The actual increasing-limit theorem
\ref{cor:r2-local-increasing}, the completed calculus
\ref{thm:r2-completed-calculus}, and independence under such changes
of representatives give
\[
 (Du_j)^n\longrightarrow(DU)^n
\]
on all original compact scalar tests. Their vanishing total masses
imply $(DU)^n=0$. Also $b\leq U\leq0$, so $U$ has ordinary
boundary limit zero. Pointwise ambient domination
\ref{cor:r2-pointwise-ambient}, applied to $U$ and $0$, now gives
$U=0$ on $V$. Indeed all sets $\{U<-\epsilon\}$ are relatively
compact by the lower barrier, and $(DU)^n$ vanishes on the whole
strict gap.

By the divisorial part of \textup{(N)}, $u_j(z)\uparrow0$.
Choose a strictly increasing sequence $j_l$ such that
$u_{j_l}(z)>-2^{-l}$. The finite sums
\[
 \phi_m=\sum_{l=1}^m u_{j_l}
\]
are nonpositive classical psh and decrease with $m$. Their pointwise
limit $\phi$ is extended classical psh by the classical decreasing
closure, and $\phi(z)\geq-\sum_l2^{-l}=-1$.
For $x\in E$, every $G_j$ contains $x$ and the open-set extremal
satisfies $u_j(x)=-1$ exactly. Thus $\phi_m(x)=-m$ and
$\phi(x)=-\infty$. No integrability of the original set or a
global pole-patching theorem has been used.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The local zero-set equivalence on this domain]
\label{cor:r2-local-polar-equivalence}
On the same exhaustion domain, for every arbitrary $E\subset W\Subset V$,
\[
 C^*(E)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 E\subset\{\phi=-\infty\}
 \text{ for some nonpositive classical }\phi\text{ on }V,
 \ \phi\not\equiv-\infty.
\]
The implication from right to left is the already proved ambient
polar theorem, not a new nonconcentration hypothesis.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The forward implication is the theorem. For the reverse implication,
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-ambient-polar-outer-zero} gives local outer
capacity zero on every compact/domain pair. The fixed-domain
comparison \ref{cor:r2-fixed-domain-null-classes} gives $C^*(E)=0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Local negligibility in the ordinary topology]
\label{def:r2-local-negligibility}
Let $E$ be an arbitrary subset of an allowed ordinary open $U$.
It is locally negligible if every $x\in U$ has an ordinary
neighborhood $O\subset U$ and a nonempty locally uniformly
upper-bounded family $\mathcal F\subset\Cb(O)$ such that
\[
 E\cap O\subset
 \left\{\sup_{v\in\mathcal F}v<
                    \left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal F}v\right)^*\right\}.
\]
It is locally increasing-negligible if the family can be chosen as
one increasing locally uniformly bounded sequence in $\Cb(O)$.
Local pluripolarity means that every $x\in U$ has a connected ordinary
neighborhood $O\subset U$ and an extended classical psh function
$\phi$ on $O$, not identically $-\infty$ there, with
$E\cap O\subset\{\phi=-\infty\}$.
Local outer-capacity zero means that
\[
 \operatorname{Cap}_{[1]}^*(E\cap H;\Omega)=0
\]
for every permitted ordinary norm-box domain $\Omega\subset U$
and every compact $H\Subset\Omega$.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[Local polar, negligible, and outer-zero sets]
\label{cor:r2-polar-negligible-equivalence}
On every allowed ordinary open $U$, the following properties of an arbitrary subset
$E\subset U$ are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $E$ is locally pluripolar;
\item $E$ has local ambient outer-capacity zero;
\item $E$ is locally increasing-negligible;
\item $E$ is locally negligible.
\end{enumerate}
These are local witness assertions. A single global psh witness on
$U$ is not asserted.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) is
Corollary~\ref{cor:r2-ambient-polar-outer-zero}.
For (ii)$\Rightarrow$(i), fix $x\in U$ and use
Lemma~\ref{lem:r2-local-exhaustion-domains} in an ordinary algebraic
neighborhood to choose an exhaustion domain $V$ containing $x$.
Choose a connected ordinary $W$ with $x\in W\Subset V$ and an
ambient divisorial point $z\in W$. The local null-class comparison
gives $\operatorname{Cap}_{[1]}^*(E\cap W;V)=0$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-capacity-zero-polar-witness} supplies a
nonpositive classical witness $\phi$ on $V$, finite at $z$, whose
pole set contains $E\cap W$. Its restriction to $W$ is a
nontrivial classical witness, as required.

For (i)$\Rightarrow$(iii), shrink a connected witness neighborhood
if necessary and subtract a finite upper bound so that $\phi\leq0$.
The pole set $P=\{\phi=-\infty\}$ has empty ordinary interior by
Proposition~\ref{prop:r2-no-interior-poles}; hence the witness remains
nontrivial on every smaller connected ordinary neighborhood.
The actual bounded classical functions
\[
 w_N=1+\frac{\max(\phi,-N)}{N}
\]
increase to $\mathbf1_{P^c}$. Because $P$ has empty ordinary
interior, the ordinary usc regularization of this actual limit is
the constant one. Its discrepancy set is exactly $P$, which
contains the specified part of $E$. This proves increasing
negligibility. The implication (iii)$\Rightarrow$(iv) is immediate.

Finally (iv)$\Rightarrow$(ii) follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:r2-negligible-outer-zero}. To express it on a
prescribed compact/domain pair $(H,\Omega)$, restrict the local
witness families to smaller permitted domains contained in $\Omega$.
Choose countably many ordinary cores covering $E\cap H$; such a
choice exists in the locally second-countable finite $p$-adic
setting. Each core intersection has outer capacity zero on its
own domain and therefore on $\Omega$ by domain monotonicity.
Countable subadditivity gives the required zero capacity on $H$.
No uncountable union of exceptional sets is taken.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Pole patching on one exhaustion domain]
\label{cor:r2-exhaustion-domain-pole-patching}
On the same connected exhaustion domain $V$, let $E\subset V$
have local ambient outer-capacity zero. In particular this applies
to a locally pluripolar $E$. Then there is one nonpositive extended
classical psh function $\phi$ on $V$, not identically $-\infty$,
such that $E\subset\{\phi=-\infty\}$. No relative compactness
of $E$ itself is required for this conclusion.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Provenance: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}.}
The domain $V$ and its exhaustion hypothesis are retained.

\begin{proof}
Choose ordinary $W_m\Subset V$ increasing to $V$ and fix one
ambient divisorial point $z\in V$. Put $E_m=E\cap W_m$.
The fixed-domain null-class comparison gives $C^*(E_m)=0$.
The witness theorem gives nonpositive classical $\phi_m$ on $V$
with $E_m\subset\{\phi_m=-\infty\}$ and $\phi_m(z)\geq-1$.
The series
\[
 \phi=\sum_{m\geq1}2^{-m}\phi_m
\]
is a decreasing limit of nonpositive classical partial sums and
is therefore extended classical. It satisfies $\phi(z)\geq-1$,
so it is nontrivial. Every point of $E$ belongs to some $E_m$,
and the corresponding positive summand forces $\phi=-\infty$
there.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Why the domain qualification is essential]
Untwisted pole globalization on every analytic space is
\texttt{FALSE}. For example, the rational point $0$ of
$\mathbf P^{1,\an}_K$ is locally pluripolar, with local witness
$\log|t|$. A nontrivial global extended classical psh function
on this proper connected space attains a finite maximum and is
constant by the strong maximum principle
\cite[Theorem 6.1]{GR25}. It therefore has no
pole. The preceding corollary is globalization on the one
specified exhaustion domain; it is not that false unrestricted
assertion, nor a theorem about globally twisted psh functions.
\end{remark}

\subsection{An outer-capacity formula for arbitrary relatively compact sets}

\begin{theorem}[The extremal total-mass formula]
\label{thm:r2-arbitrary-extremal-mass}
For every arbitrary $A\subset W\Subset V$,
\[
 C^*(A)=\int_V(DU_A)^n<\infty.
\]
This assertion neither assumes Borel measurability of $A$ nor
identifies the raw capacity with its outer regularization beforehand.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
If $G\Subset V$ is ordinary open and contains $A$, then
$\mathcal F_G\subset\mathcal F_A$, hence $U_G\leq U_A\leq0$.
Both functions have boundary limit zero. The mass-order lemma and
\textup{(E)} imply
\[
 \int_V(DU_A)^n\leq\int_V(DU_G)^n=C(G).
\]
Taking the infimum over such $G$ gives
$\int_V(DU_A)^n\leq C^*(A)$. Relatively compact opens suffice here:
intersect any open cover with a fixed relatively compact open
neighborhood of $\overline W$. This also proves finiteness.

Since $h_A=-1$ on $A$, input \textup{(N)} shows that
\[
 A\cap\{U_A>-1\}\subset N
\]
for some set $N\subset W$ with $C^*(N)=0$. We may use a Borel
outer-zero cover of this defect if $A$ itself is not Borel.
Fix $0<\eta<1$ and put
\[
 G_\eta=\{U_A<-1+\eta\},\qquad
 v_\eta=\max\left(-1,\frac{U_A}{1-\eta}\right).
\]
The set $G_\eta$ is ordinary open and relatively compact, because
$U_A$ is usc and bounded below by the common exhaustion barrier.
The function $v_\eta$ is classical, has boundary value zero,
belongs to $[-1,0]$, and equals $-1$ on $G_\eta$. Consequently
\[
 \frac{U_A}{1-\eta}\leq v_\eta\leq U_{G_\eta}.
\]
Twice applying the mass-order lemma gives
\[
 C(G_\eta)=\int_V(DU_{G_\eta})^n
 \leq\int_V(Dv_\eta)^n
 \leq(1-\eta)^{-n}\int_V(DU_A)^n.
\]
Finally $A\subset G_\eta\cup N$. Monotonicity and subadditivity
of outer capacity, and its equality with raw capacity on ordinary
open sets, imply
\[
 C^*(A)\leq C(G_\eta)
 \leq(1-\eta)^{-n}\int_V(DU_A)^n.
\]
Let $\eta$ decrease to zero. The two inequalities prove the formula.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The missing continuity axiom and the Choquet conclusion}

\begin{theorem}[Continuity from below on arbitrary subsets of a core]
\label{thm:r2-outer-capacity-increasing-sets}
If $A_j\subset A_{j+1}\subset W\Subset V$ are arbitrary subsets
and $A=\bigcup_jA_j$, then
\[
 C^*(A)=\lim_j C^*(A_j).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $U_j=U_{A_j}$; these bounded classical functions decrease
with $j$. By \textup{(N)}, each defect
$A_j\cap\{U_j>-1\}$ is contained in an outer-zero set $N_j$.
The countable union of the $N_j$ has outer capacity zero.
For $\epsilon>0$, choose one ordinary open set $G$ containing
that union with $C(G)<\epsilon$.

Fix $0<\eta<1$ and put
\[
 O_j=G\cup\{U_j<-1+\eta\}.
\]
These are \emph{increasing ordinary open sets}, since the $U_j$
decrease. Each $O_j$ contains $A_j$. The truncation estimate in
the preceding proof and its mass formula give
\[
 C(O_j)\leq\epsilon+
      (1-\eta)^{-n}C^*(A_j).
\]
The raw capacity is continuous from below on Borel sets, directly
from its definition as a supremum of Radon measures. Applying
this only to the increasing \emph{open} sets $O_j$ yields
\[
 C^*(A)\leq C\Bigl(\bigcup_jO_j\Bigr)
       =\lim_j C(O_j)
       \leq\epsilon+(1-\eta)^{-n}\lim_j C^*(A_j).
\]
Let $\epsilon$ and then $\eta$ decrease to zero. Monotonicity
supplies the reverse inequality.

This is the ordinary-open argument of the classical capacitability
proof, \cite[\S8, Theorem 8.2]{BT82}, with its analytic hypotheses
proved separately here. An infinite interse

closed_parameter_bands.tex \section{Closed parameter bands and an original-current Radon calculus}
\label{sec:r12-closed-parameter-bands}

Fix the original finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$ and its original
absolute value. Let $U$ be an ordinary open in a good, Hausdorff,
boundaryless, quasi-smooth, pure $n$-dimensional $K$-analytic space.
All currents and tests in this section are original CLD objects.
In particular, an equality is required on every original compact
smooth complementary test, allowing every actual moment refinement.
No equality on an enlarged GK delta-test sheaf is asserted.

Let $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ be original analytic units, set
\[
 s_i=\log|f_i|,\qquad s=(s_1,\ldots,s_c):U\longrightarrow J\subset\mathbf R^c,
 \qquad
 \Omega_s=\bigwedge_{i=1}^c(d's_i\wedge d''s_i),
 \tag{PB1}
\]
where $J$ is a real open containing the image under consideration.
No rank, independence, submersion, saturation, or product hypothesis
on $s$ is imposed in this section. The original smooth functions
$s_i$ satisfy $Ds_i=0$ and their prime and double-prime differentials
are separately closed.

\begin{definition}[Parameter-annihilated currents]
\label{def:r12-parameter-annihilated}
A coefficient-Radon current $R$ on $U$ is \emph{$s$-annihilated} if
\[
                 d's_i\wedge R=d''s_i\wedge R=0
                         \qquad(1\le i\le c).
 \tag{PB2}
\]
An allowed $s$-background is an $s$-annihilated, original symmetric
middle-positive, separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed diagonal current.
The adjective describes a proved extra structure of a derived
current; it does not restrict the background $S$ in OPEN-GQ.
\end{definition}

For every arbitrary original allowed $(p,p)$-background $S$ with
$p+c\le n$, the derived current $\Omega_s\wedge S$ is an allowed
$s$-background. Indeed $\Omega_s$ is smooth, strongly positive and
separately closed, so its wedge preserves the original middle cone;
every conormal in (PB2) is repeated in this product. This uses no
regularization or replacement of $S$. It also covers all cases where
$\Omega_s$ happens to vanish because of moment-rank degeneracy.

\subsection{The Borel parameter algebra preserves closedness}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded smooth approximation for finitely many parameter measures]
\label{lem:r12-parameter-L1-approximation}
Let $\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_N$ be finite positive Radon measures on a
compact subset of $J$, and let $b:J\to\mathbf R$ be Borel and
bounded on a neighborhood of that subset. There are smooth real
functions $b_m$ on $J$, with one common bound, such that
\[
                   \sum_{j=1}^N\int|b_m-b|\,d\nu_j\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{PB3}
\]
If $b\ge0$, the $b_m$ can be chosen nonnegative. No measure in this
statement is assumed to be nonatomic.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN}} as elementary
Radon regularity; the short proof fixes precisely the version used.

\begin{proof}
Replace the finite family by its sum. Truncate $b$ to its fixed
bound on a compact neighborhood and approximate it in $L^1$ by
bounded simple functions. Inner and outer regularity approximate
each indicator by a continuous function between zero and one.
Continuous compactly supported functions on $J$ can be uniformly
approximated by smooth functions by convolution after a compact
cutoff. Truncation with a smooth approximation to the scalar
clipping map keeps a common bound and, when required, nonnegativity.
A diagonal choice proves (PB3).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Closed Borel bands and differential commutation]
\label{thm:r12-closed-parameter-bands}
Let $R$ be an allowed $s$-background. For every locally bounded
Borel $b:J\to\mathbf R$, the intrinsic coefficient multiplication
$b(s)R$ is separately closed and $s$-annihilated. It is middle-positive
if $b\ge0$. In particular, for every Borel $E\subset J$,
\[
                            R_E:=\mathbf1_{s^{-1}(E)}R
 \tag{PB4}
\]
is a genuine positive separately closed original current.

More generally, let $u$ be an original locally bounded Borel scalar
such that $T=D(uR)$ is coefficient-Radon. Then $T$ is $s$-annihilated
and, on all original tests,
\[
                         D\bigl(u\,b(s)R\bigr)=b(s)D(uR).
 \tag{PB5}
\]
Thus (PB5) applies in particular to every frozen locally bounded
classical BT insertion into $R$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the original
closed-band calculus. The coefficient-Radon nature and positivity of
the frozen bounded BT insertion are \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}.

\begin{proof}
First take $b$ smooth. Its differentials are combinations of the
$d's_i$ and $d''s_i$. Consequently
\[
 d'b(s)\wedge R=d''b(s)\wedge R=Db(s)\wedge R=0.
 \tag{PB6}
\]
The distributional product rule and separate closedness of $R$
give separate closedness of $b(s)R$. Conormality follows immediately
from (PB2). For a compact original test $\eta$ complementary to $T$,
the smooth identity
\[
 D(b(s)\eta)=b(s)D\eta+d'b(s)\wedge d''\eta
                    -d''b(s)\wedge d'\eta+Db(s)\wedge\eta
\]
and (PB6), still valid after scalar multiplication by $u$, imply
\[
 \langle b(s)D(uR),\eta\rangle
   =\langle uR,D(b(s)\eta)\rangle
   =\langle uR,b(s)D\eta\rangle.
 \tag{PB7}
\]
This is (PB5) for smooth $b$.

For Borel $b$, fix one arbitrary compact original test stage. Choose
finite coefficient-Radon frames controlling $R$ on the supports of
the test and its required derivatives. Push the total variations of
these finitely many coefficient measures forward by $s$; they are
finite Radon measures on the real parameter space. Apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:r12-parameter-L1-approximation}. The resulting
$b_m(s)R$ converge to $b(s)R$ against every pairing needed for the
closedness equation of that test. Distributional differentiation is
continuous, so closedness passes to the limit. Multiplication of the
already zero coefficient measures in (PB2) proves conormality.
Positive scalar multiplication proves middle positivity when $b\ge0$.

For (PB5), include in the same finite controlling family the
coefficient measures of $T$ on $\operatorname{supp}\eta$ and those
of $R$ on $\operatorname{supp}D\eta$. The common compact bound on
$u$ then gives convergence of both sides of (PB7). This proves
(PB5) without inferring convergence against a discontinuous weight
from weak current convergence alone. The approximating functions
may depend on the test: since that test was arbitrary, the resulting
intrinsic equality holds on the whole original test sheaf. No
countability assumption on the collection of all refinements is
needed.

Finally, separate closedness of $d's_i,d''s_i$ gives directly, as
distributions,
\[
 d's_i\wedge D(uR)=D(u\,d's_i\wedge R)=0,
 \qquad
 d''s_i\wedge D(uR)=D(u\,d''s_i\wedge R)=0.
 \tag{PB8}
\]
This proves the asserted conormality of $T$. All arguments involve
intrinsic original forms and coefficient measures, and hence are
unchanged after any actual refinement containing the chosen data.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A closed current-valued Radon resolution]
\label{cor:r12-current-valued-parameter-resolution}
The assignment $E\mapsto R_E$ is countably additive on Borel sets
in every original compact-test pairing. Its local coefficient
variation is controlled by that of $R$. Every $R_E$ is separately
closed and positive. For all permitted bounded classical tuples,
\[
 T_{R_E,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)
       =\mathbf1_{s^{-1}(E)}T_{R,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k).
 \tag{PB9}
\]
If $E_1,\ldots,E_N$ form a finite Borel partition on the parameter
range under consideration, then $R=\sum_iR_{E_i}$ and every bounded
mixed BT product has the corresponding exact finite decomposition.
The same conclusions hold for countable partitions whenever a
compact test is fixed and the sums are interpreted in coefficient
variation.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}}.

\begin{proof}
Coefficient-Radon multiplication gives countable additivity and the
variation bound. The theorem gives positivity and closedness of each
band. Apply (PB5) repeatedly: every positive mixed tail is separately
closed, coefficient-Radon, and $s$-annihilated by (PB8). This proves
(PB9). Sum the resulting coefficient measures over a partition.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{What is and is not a fiber construction.}
The resolution (PB4) retains every Borel set, including individual
parameters and atoms. It does not discard an exceptional parameter
set. It is a current-valued measure on the parameter space, not a
construction of BT products over a completed residue field. Its band
currents live on the original $U$, are carried measure-theoretically
by $s^{-1}(E)$, and use every original test there. Their topological
supports are only asserted to lie in the closure of that carrier.
No conditional fiber current on a new analytic field is asserted.

The conormal hypothesis is essential. A general Borel restriction
of a closed current need not be closed. Moreover, the frozen R10
annular example shows that arbitrary Borel scalar coefficients
cannot commute with curvature insertion: for the unit Gauss point
$\xi$, $\mathbf1_{\{\xi\}}[U]=0$ but
$\mathbf1_{\{\xi\}}D((\log|T|)_+[U])=\delta_\xi$.
That example does not contradict (PB5), because $[U]$ is not
annihilated by $d'\log|T|$ and $d''\log|T|$.

\paragraph{Frozen inputs and exact scope.}
Only the frozen original coefficient-Radon calculus, smooth form
Leibniz rules, positivity under strongly positive smooth wedges,
and bounded arbitrary-background BT theorem are used. The R10
source \path{signed_descent/pws_differential_curvature_module.tex}
is used for its explicit warning against unrestricted Borel
coefficient linearity; its finite PS module is not enlarged
without the separate proof above. No R/B/A2 proof is re-audited.
