title: Disintegration into original ambient currents
text:
original_current_disintegration.tex \section{Disintegration into original ambient currents}
\label{sec:r12-original-current-disintegration}

The closed parameter bands admit a genuine local disintegration,
but its conditional currents remain on the original ambient
$K$-analytic space. They are not currents on a newly introduced
residue-field analytic space. This distinction is essential for
using the frozen arbitrary-background BT theorem without changing
its field or its test sheaf.

Throughout this section $U$ is second countable in addition to the
standing original hypotheses. The conclusion is ordinary-local on
every space in the project: every point has an ordinary neighborhood
of this kind, as proved below. Let $s:U\to J\subset\mathbf R^c$ be
the original parameter map, and let $R$ be an allowed $s$-background.

\subsection{A countably cofinal system of original smooth tests}

\begin{lemma}[Local countability does not discard actual refinements]
\label{lem:r12-countably-cofinal-original-tests}
Every point of an allowed original analytic space has a second
countable ordinary neighborhood. On any such $U$, the original
compact smooth CLD test spaces in all bidegrees admit a countable
cofinal family of finite moment-and-cutoff presentation stages.
Each stage is a quotient of a separable smooth coefficient space,
has a countable dense subset, and has a countable dense subset in
its original middle-positive cone. All equality kernels between
the stages can likewise be checked on countably many dense
coefficient relations.

More precisely, every original compact test, including a test
initially represented after an arbitrary actual refinement, is a
finite sum of tests in these stages. Approximation within each
stage is in its usual smooth coefficient topology on one fixed
compact support. No assertion about all GK delta-tests is made.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the exact
original-test cofinality used in the conditional-current argument.
The original smooth cutoff/partition and common-moment properties
are frozen \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}s.

\begin{proof}
The finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$ is separable as a metric field.
Every $K$-affinoid algebra is a quotient of a generalized Tate
algebra in finitely many variables. Polynomials with coefficients
in a fixed countable dense subfield, followed by passage to the
quotient, give a countable dense subset of that Banach algebra.
This argument also applies to non-strict radii: finite polynomials
are dense in the defining weighted completion.

The Berkovich spectrum of a separable affinoid algebra is compact
metrizable. Indeed a countable dense set of functions determines
each bounded multiplicative seminorm, and all remaining evaluations
are uniform limits of these evaluations, since
$\bigl||f(x)|-|g(x)|\bigr|\le\|f-g\|$. The spectrum embeds
continuously and injectively in a countable product of compact
real intervals. Compactness and the Hausdorff property identify
its topology with that induced metric topology. By goodness, an
ordinary point has an affinoid neighborhood; its ordinary interior
is the required second countable neighborhood.

On a second countable good $U$, choose a countable collection of
affinoid neighborhoods whose ordinary interiors form a basis.
To construct it, for each member of a countable topological basis
cover its points by affinoid interiors contained in that member,
and choose a countable subcover. Choose a countable dense subset
$D_B$ of each resulting affinoid algebra $\mathcal O(B)$.
Whenever $g$ is an analytic unit on a neighborhood of $B$, choose
$g_0\in D_B$ with
\[
 \|g-g_0\|_B<\min\left\{\inf_{x\in B}|g(x)|,\|g^{-1}\|_B^{-1}\right\}.
 \tag{DI1}
\]
The right side is positive by compactness and invertibility. The
ultrametric inequality gives $|g_0|=|g|$ on $B$, and the Neumann
series applied to $1+g^{-1}(g_0-g)$ makes $g_0$ a unit there. Their actual
logarithmic moment functions and their original differentials
therefore agree exactly on the ordinary interior. Thus every finite
actual moment tuple on a compact local stage is replaceable, after
finite ordinary localization, by a tuple from a countable family.
This applies equally to arbitrary extra units in a refinement.

Fix countably many original smooth cutoffs for pairs of basis
neighborhoods with nested compact closures, equal to one on the
smaller compact and supported in the larger. The frozen cutoff
theorem supplies each such choice. Include the finitely many
moments used by each cutoff in the countable family; finite unions
and finite common refinements remain countable. A finite collection
of these cutoffs covers the support of any test. Normalizing their
sum on a neighborhood of that support yields a finite smooth
partition and reduces the test to compact stages in the stated
countable family.

For a fixed tuple and cutoff, write its coefficient arrays on
real coordinate neighborhoods. Use a countable exhaustion by
rational real balls and compact coordinate cores. The corresponding
$C^\infty$ coefficient spaces are separable metrizable spaces;
finite products and their quotients have the same property. The
actual zero-form conditions on a fixed moment image are closed
linear conditions, obtained by restrictions to its relevant tangent
spaces. The smooth coefficient relations comparing two stages can
be imposed on their countable common refinements; their kernels
are separable subspaces. Choose a countable dense subset in each
such kernel. The preimage of the middle-positive cone is likewise
a subspace subset of a second countable metric coefficient space,
and hence is separable; choose dense positive representatives.
These choices prove all countability assertions. No rationality of
the real coefficients of a test is required: only density within
its fixed smooth presentation is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A recalled Radon disintegration construction]
\label{lem:r12-Radon-conditional-measures}
Let $M$ be a locally compact second countable Hausdorff space,
$s:M\to J$ continuous, and $\mu$ a finite positive Radon measure.
Put $\nu=s_*\mu$. There is a measurable family of positive Radon
probability measures $\mu_a$, for $\nu$-almost every $a$, carried
by $s^{-1}(a)$, such that for every nonnegative Borel $F$,
\[
                       \int_M F\,d\mu
                          =\int_J\left(\int_M F\,d\mu_a\right)d\nu(a).
 \tag{DI2}
\]
The identity also holds after insertion of any bounded Borel
parameter weight. Integrable signed functions are allowed.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN}} as the usual
Radon conditional-measure theorem. The construction below records
the countable version needed here, using Radon--Nikodym and Riesz
representation only.

\begin{proof}
Take a countable dense rational vector lattice in $C_0(M)$, enlarged
to include a compact approximate unit $\chi_m\uparrow1$, and products
with pullbacks of a countable determining algebra in $C_c(J)$.
For each chosen $f$, the signed measure
$E\mapsto\int_{s^{-1}(E)}f\,d\mu$ is absolutely continuous with
respect to $\nu$. Choose its Radon--Nikodym derivative $g_f$.
Outside one null set the maps $f\mapsto g_f(a)$ are rational-linear,
positive, bounded by $\|f\|_\infty$, and satisfy
\[
                  g_{\phi(s)f}(a)=\phi(a)g_f(a).
\]
There are only countably many identities and inequalities to impose.
Extend by continuity to $C_0(M)$ and apply Riesz representation to
obtain $\mu_a$ of mass at most one. The approximate unit and
monotone convergence show that its mass equals one almost everywhere:
the increasing limit of $g_{\chi_m}$ has integral $\nu(J)$ and is
bounded above by one. The displayed multiplication identity then
gives $s_*\mu_a=\delta_a$, first on the determining continuous
algebra and then on Borel sets. Thus $\mu_a$ is carried by
$s^{-1}(a)$.

The derivatives $g_f$ supply measurability and (DI2) on the chosen
algebra. Uniform approximation extends these assertions to
$C_0(M)$; the monotone-class theorem extends them to nonnegative
Borel functions. Multiplication by a bounded Borel function of
$s$ gives the weighted version. The signed assertion follows from
positive and negative parts. No regularity of a conditional density
in $a$ is asserted.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Conditional currents retain the entire original test sheaf}

\begin{theorem}[Disintegration of a parameter-annihilated original current]
\label{thm:r12-original-current-disintegration}
Let $R$ be an allowed $s$-background on second countable $U$.
There is a finite positive Radon control measure $\nu$ on $J$ and
a measurable family of original currents $R_a$ on the same $U$
such that, for $\nu$-almost every $a$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item $R_a$ is symmetric, middle-positive, separately $d'$- and
$d''$-closed, coefficient-Radon, and $s$-annihilated;
\item its coefficient measures are carried by $s^{-1}(a)$;
\item for every Borel $E\subset J$ and every original compact
smooth test $\eta$,
\[
               \langle R_E,\eta\rangle
                    =\int_E\langle R_a,\eta\rangle\,d\nu(a).
 \tag{DI3}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Local coefficient variations of the family are $\nu$-integrable.
The exceptional set can be chosen once for all original tests and
all actual moment refinements. For the chosen control measure $\nu$,
the family is unique up to one $\nu$-null set as original currents.
At every parameter atom of positive $\nu$-mass,
\[
                       R_a=\nu(\{a\})^{-1}R_{\{a\}}.
 \tag{DI4}
\]
The normalization measure is not claimed to be canonical; the
closed-band current-valued measure $E\mapsto R_E$ is canonical.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for original
all-test currents. This is not an auxiliary-field current theorem.

\begin{proof}
Choose the countably cofinal stages of
Lemma~\ref{lem:r12-countably-cofinal-original-tests}. On each stage,
use a finite constant exterior coefficient frame with a fixed
compact cutoff. The coefficient-Radon property gives finitely many
finite signed Radon measures representing all its test pairings.
List the resulting countable collection as $(\mu_j)_{j\ge1}$,
including finitely many positive domination controls on every stage.
The measure
\[
            \mu=\sum_{j\ge1}
                    \frac{2^{-j}}{1+\|\mu_j\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}|\mu_j|
 \tag{DI5}
\]
is finite positive Radon and dominates every listed coefficient
measure by a fixed constant depending on its index. Thus every
fixed compact coefficient frame is bounded by $C\mu$, not merely
absolutely continuous without quantitative control.
If $R=0$ the theorem is trivial; otherwise discard any
zero summands and put $\nu=s_*\mu$.

Write $\mu_j=g_j\mu$ using Borel versions of their Radon--Nikodym
densities, and disintegrate $\mu$ by the preceding lemma. Outside
one $\nu$-null set all $\int|g_j|\,d\mu_a$ are finite. Put
$\mu_{j,a}=g_j\mu_a$. On a given stage these finitely many signed
Radon measures define an order-zero functional on its smooth
coefficient arrays.

We check that these functionals give an original current, rather
than independent unrelated functions on the chosen stages. For
each of the countably many dense zero-form relations from the
cofinality lemma, its original coefficient measure is zero, hence
its conditional pairing is zero almost everywhere. Impose all
these equalities outside one null set. Each conditional stage
functional is continuous for the smooth coefficient topology,
by its finite coefficient-variation bound, so it kills the entire
closed relation kernel. The same reasoning on common stages
identifies any two representations. Consequently the functionals
extend to one coefficient-Radon original current $R_a$ on all
compact original smooth tests. The measure construction proves
(DI3), first on the countable stages and then on every test.
Its finite stage variations are integrable because
\[
                 \int_J\int|g_j|\,d\mu_a\,d\nu
                                           =\int|g_j|\,d\mu<\infty.
 \tag{DI6}
\]

For every positive test in the chosen countable dense family,
positivity of every $R_E$ in (DI3) forces
$\langle R_a,\eta\rangle\ge0$ almost everywhere. Impose these
countably many inequalities simultaneously; continuity on each
stage gives positivity on its full middle-positive cone. Thus
$R_a$ is middle-positive, not merely positive on decomposable or
strongly positive tests. The same countable argument applied to
the symmetry identities gives symmetry.

Every $R_E$ is separately closed by the new closed-band theorem.
For each test $\alpha$ in a countable dense source stage,
(DI3) applied to $d'\alpha$ gives
\[
                      \int_E\langle R_a,d'\alpha\rangle\,d\nu=0
                           \qquad\text{for all Borel }E.
\]
Its integrand is therefore zero almost everywhere. Impose the
countably many prime and double-prime equations and extend by
continuity of the differentials on each source stage. This proves
separate closedness on all original tests. The identical argument
for $d's_i\wedge R_E$ and $d''s_i\wedge R_E$ proves (PB2) for
$R_a$. The support assertion follows from that of $\mu_a$.
Set $R_a=0$ on the one exceptional null set if a family indexed by
every parameter is desired; no potential function is changed.

Uniqueness follows from (DI3) on a countable determining family:
two families have equal pairings there almost everywhere, and
continuity then identifies their original currents. Applying (DI3)
to $E=\{a\}$ proves (DI4). A null exceptional set cannot contain
an atom of positive $\nu$-mass. All refinements were included in
the exact cofinality lemma, so the conclusion is not a statement
only on the initial countable moment names.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The scope of the conditional object.}
Each $R_a$ is an original $K$-current on $U$, tested by the entire
ambient original sheaf, including moments with genuine mixed
dependence on any parameter and fiber coordinates. The theorem
does not identify it with a current on $Y$, on a norm-level
polyhedron, or on a completed-residue-field analytic fiber.
It asserts no inverse to a geometric pushforward. Its use in the
next section is legitimate precisely because the frozen BT theorem
already permits every original positive separately closed current
on $U$, including these conditional ones.

title: A capacitary completion with an intrinsic bounded current calculus
text:
band_capacitary_completion.tex \section{A capacitary completion with an intrinsic bounded current calculus}
\label{sec:r12-band-capacitary-completion}

Assume (CB1)--(CB2) and the containing-affinoid hypothesis
(BQ4). Thus $R$ is still an original arbitrary middle-positive
separately closed conormal current of remaining degree $k\geq1$.
Put
\[
 \mathcal A_0=\mathcal A_s^{\rm band,ct}(V),\qquad
 \gamma_0(E)=\sup_{h\in\mathcal A_0}\widetilde\mu_h(E),\qquad
 \gamma_1(E)=C_R^{\rm band}(E;V,s).
 \tag{BC1}
\]
The distinction is essential: $\mathcal A_0$ uses continuous
actual branches, whereas $\gamma_1$ allows all bounded actual
classical branches. Both capacities use their entire displayed
tester families, and both are finite on compact sets. Write
$\gamma_i^*$ for ordinary-open outer regularization, $i=0,1$.
Then $\gamma_0\leq\gamma_1$, but equality is not assumed.

We give one construction for either fixed choice $i\in\{0,1\}$.
The self-generated case $i=0$ has the exact unchanged-outer-capacity
conclusion. The stronger full-band control $i=1$ has only the
one-sided comparison printed below.

The bounded recursive completion method itself is an explicitly
frozen input: R11 \path{capacity/barrier_relative_completion.tex},
\path{lem:r11-analytic-bounded-completion}, transfers R2
\path{capacitary_closure.tex}, \path{prop:r2-completion} and
\path{thm:r2-completed-calculus}, to the original analytic setting.
The proofs below verify that method for the new band seed and
its two distinct capacities. They do not claim the first bounded
arbitrary-background capacitary completion.

\begin{definition}[The two explicitly normalized capacitary completions]
\label{def:r12-band-capacitary-completion}
Let $\mathfrak B_i(V)$ be the closure of $\mathcal A_0$ among
Borel functions $V\to[0,1]$, modulo equality outside a locally
$\gamma_i^*$-null set, for local convergence in outer
$\gamma_i$-capacity. Thus a defining row satisfies
\[
 \gamma_i^*\bigl(H\cap\{|h_m-h|>\delta\}\bigr)\longrightarrow0
       \quad(H\Subset V\text{ compact},\ \delta>0),
       \qquad h_m\in\mathcal A_0.
 \tag{BC2}
\]
No ambient classical psh representative of $h$ is required or
asserted. Affine normalization extends the construction to any
fixed bounded real range when that is needed.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Concrete completeness and quasicontinuity]
\label{thm:r12-band-completion-metric}
Each $\mathfrak B_i(V)$ is a complete metrizable space of actual
Borel classes. Its members are locally ordinary-open outer
$\gamma_i$-quasicontinuous. It is closed under finite convex
combinations, maxima and the bounded operation
$\max(f,g-\epsilon)$ for $\epsilon\geq0$.

For an increasing compact exhaustion
$H_l\subset\operatorname{Int}(H_{l+1})$ of $V$, one compatible
metric is
\[
 \begin{split}
 d_i(f,g)&=\sum_{l\geq1}2^{-l}\,\kappa_{i,l}(f,g),\\
 \kappa_{i,l}(f,g)&=\inf\{\epsilon>0:
  \gamma_i^*(H_l\cap\{|f-g|>\epsilon\})\leq\epsilon\}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{BC3}
\]
The terms lie in $[0,1]$ because all functions are normalized.
Only a countable compact exhaustion of the ordinary geometry is
used here; there is no countable-cofinal replacement of the
capacity tester family.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the concrete
completions of this seed class.

\begin{proof}
The affinoid space is metrizable over the original separable
field, as in the exact test-countability argument (DI1), so its
ordinary open $V$ has the stated compact exhaustion. The union
bound for the two error sets and countable subadditivity of
$\gamma_i^*$ give the triangle inequality for each
$\kappa_{i,l}$, and hence for $d_i$. Vanishing distance is
equivalent to equality outside a locally outer-null set: test
the difference at thresholds $1/m$ and take the countable union.
The same threshold argument shows that metric convergence is
exactly (BC2).

The entire space of normalized Borel classes is complete for
this metric. Indeed take a Cauchy row and select a subsequence,
still denoted $f_j$, such that
\[
 \gamma_i^*(H_j\cap\{|f_{j+1}-f_j|>2^{-j}\})<2^{-j}.
\]
Choose ordinary open covers $G_j$ of these error sets with
$\gamma_i(G_j)<2^{1-j}$. The late-tail unions have capacity
tending to zero. Off their limsup, the successive differences
are eventually bounded by the summable sequence $2^{-j}$ on
each compact core. Thus $f_j$ has a finite pointwise Borel
limit there, lying in $[0,1]$. Set the limit equal to zero on
the outer-null limsup. Uniform tail convergence outside the
late open union proves local capacity convergence, and the
Cauchy property returns the whole row to the same limit.
The closed seed closure $\mathfrak B_i(V)$ is therefore complete.

Each seed member is outer-$\gamma_1$-quasicontinuous by (BQ2),
and hence is outer-$\gamma_0$-quasicontinuous. For a capacity
limit of seed members, use the same fast-subsequence construction.
On a fixed compact remove a late union of the error covers and
also open quasicontinuity exceptions for the countably many
approximants, assigning summable arbitrarily small capacities.
Outside their union the approximants are continuous and converge
uniformly. Their limit is continuous there. This proves the
asserted quasicontinuity for either completion, and also proves
that changing values on an outer-null set has no effect on it.

The seed is closed under the printed finite operations: refine
finitely many countable parameter partitions and apply the
corresponding maximum or convex operation to their continuous
actual classical branches. The outputs remain normalized. These
operations are continuous for local capacity convergence, by
their pointwise Lipschitz inequalities and a finite union of
error sets. Taking seed limits proves the closure statements.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Construction on all original tests, before any compact restriction}

\begin{theorem}[Intrinsic bounded products in the completion]
\label{thm:r12-completed-band-products}
For $h_1,\ldots,h_j\in\mathfrak B_i(V)$ and $0\leq j\leq k$,
the recursion
\[
 \widehat T^{,i}_{R,0}=R,\qquad
 \widehat T^{,i}_{R,j}(h_1,\ldots,h_j)
    =D\bigl(h_1\widehat T^{,i}_{R,j-1}(h_2,\ldots,h_j)\bigr)
 \tag{BC4}
\]
is well-defined on the actual Borel quotient and gives original
symmetric middle-positive, separately closed, conormal
coefficient-Radon currents. It is independent of all defining
rows. For every original compact complementary test $\eta$,
\[
 \left|\mu_{\widehat T^{,i}_{R,j}(\mathbf h),\eta}\right|(E)
                \leq C_\eta\gamma_i^*(E)
                         \qquad(E\subset V\text{ Borel}),
 \tag{BC5}
\]
where the constant is independent of the normalized completed
tuple. For a diagonal top product the exact constant is one:
\[
       \widehat\mu^{,i}_h(E)
           :=\widehat T^{,i}_{R,k}(h^{[k]})(E)
                          \leq\gamma_i^*(E).
 \tag{BC6}
\]
The products are symmetric and multilinear in the usual bounded
positive-cone sense after affine normalization. They agree with
the seed products, annihilate a constant differentiated slot,
and have original smooth-factor compatibility. They are local
on ordinary opens for equality of the Borel entries modulo the
specified outer-null sets.

Every equality is on every original compact smooth complementary
test and every actual moment refinement. Ordinary-current
equality is not promoted to equality on extra GK delta tests.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for this completed
bounded current calculus. Frozen bounded products enter only at
the actual seed level.

\begin{proof}
First observe that (BQ5) for seed tuples holds with the smaller
$\gamma_0$, not merely with $\gamma_1$. Its proof averages a
finite seed tuple and one normalized original smooth compensator;
that average is still in $\mathcal A_0$. Thus every seed
coefficient has the bound $C_\eta\gamma_0(E)$, and hence the
bound $C_\eta\gamma_i(E)$ for either choice of $i$.
The same argument at degree zero controls the original background
coefficients, so multiplication of $R$ by a bounded Borel
$\gamma_i$-class is intrinsic.

Induct on $j$. Assume the tail current $Q$ is constructed and
all its seed approximating tails $Q_m$ converge to it on original
tests, with (BC5). Each $h_1$ has the proved quasicontinuity.
The proof of the weighted weak-passage lemma (BQ6)--(BQ7) applies
unchanged when the limit coefficient bound is $C_\eta\gamma_i^*$:
its fixed exceptional sets are ordinary open, on which
$\gamma_i^*=\gamma_i$, and its varying-multiplier estimate uses
outer capacity already. Therefore
$h_{1,m}Q_m\to h_1Q$ on all original tests. Applying
distributional $D$ proves convergence of the seed products to
the intrinsic right side of (BC4).

The seed coefficient variations are uniformly bounded on compact
sets. Their distributional limit consequently has order-zero
Radon coefficients and is the same original current. Positivity,
symmetry, separate closedness and the conormal identities pass
on arbitrary original tests. For each fixed coefficient measure,
variation lower semicontinuity on an ordinary open $G$ gives
\[
        |\mu_{\widehat T,\eta}|(G)
                 \leq\liminf_m|\mu_{T_m,\eta}|(G)
                 \leq C_\eta\gamma_i(G).
 \tag{BC7}
\]
One first tests continuous compact scalar factors; original
smooth scalar density and the uniform coefficient bounds justify
this passage from current convergence. Individual Radon outer
regularity then proves (BC5) on every Borel $E$. In particular
the new current ignores the specified outer-null sets, validating
all Borel multiplications at the next induction step. For a
diagonal top tuple the seed measure bound is exactly
$\widetilde\mu_{h_m}\leq\gamma_i$; the identical open passage
and Radon outer step prove (BC6).

The recursion proves independence of defining rows. Symmetry and
the bounded affine-cone multilinear identities follow by passing
the corresponding seed identities through simultaneous defining
rows. For a smooth slot the distributional Leibniz identity and
separate closedness of the tail give the usual smooth wedge.
A constant slot gives zero for the same reason. Ordinary locality
follows by induction from the local distributional recursion and
coefficient nullity of the exceptional set. No varying weak limit
has been restricted to a compact set or to a discontinuous
equality indicator in this construction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Capacity and intrinsic joint decreasing continuity]
\label{thm:r12-completed-band-continuity}
For tuples in $\mathfrak B_i(V)$, local outer-$\gamma_i$-capacity
convergence in every slot implies convergence of every mixed
current (BC4) on all original tests. Bounded Borel weights may
also vary in local outer $\gamma_i$-capacity, provided their
limit is locally outer-$\gamma_i$-quasicontinuous; the weighted
current convergence then holds as well.

In particular, if finitely many normalized completed rows
$h_{a,m}\downarrow h_a$ pointwise on their Borel representatives
and each $h_a\in\mathfrak B_i(V)$, all mixed products and
the stated weighted versions converge. No monotonicity of any
chosen actual or band-pasted defining witnesses is required.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the completed
class with its printed topology and limit-membership condition.

\begin{proof}
Every completed entry is quasicontinuous and every completed
mixed tail has the outer bound (BC5). The weighted weak-passage
proof therefore applies exactly as in the construction of (BC4).
Induction on the tuple length proves the first assertion, now
for completed rather than merely seed rows. The weighted
conclusion is the same lemma applied to the resulting mixed
currents.

For decreasing rows, remove one ordinary open set of arbitrarily
small $\gamma_i$-capacity so that the countably many entries
and their finitely many limits are all continuous on the fixed
compact complement. This uses summable error budgets and the
proved quasicontinuity. Dini's theorem gives uniform convergence
there. Hence the rows converge in local outer $\gamma_i$-capacity,
and the first assertion applies. Membership of the limit is an
explicit hypothesis; an arbitrary pointwise infimum is not
declared a member without a separate capacity-limit argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strict maximum carriers and the equality-side inequality]
\label{thm:r12-completed-band-maximum-carriers}
Let $u,v,z_1,\ldots,z_b\in\mathfrak B_i(V)$, let
$w=\max(u,v)$, and suppose $a\geq1$, $a+b\leq k$. Then
\[
 \mathbf1_{\{u>v\}}\widehat T^{,i}_{R,a+b}(w^{[a]},\mathbf z)
    =\mathbf1_{\{u>v\}}\widehat T^{,i}_{R,a+b}(u^{[a]},\mathbf z).
 \tag{BC8}
\]
Moreover the full middle-positive current inequality holds:
\[
 \begin{split}
 \widehat T^{,i}_{R,a+b}(w^{[a]},\mathbf z)
 \geq{}&\mathbf1_{\{u\geq v\}}
                    \widehat T^{,i}_{R,a+b}(u^{[a]},\mathbf z)\\
       &+\mathbf1_{\{u<v\}}
                    \widehat T^{,i}_{R,a+b}(v^{[a]},\mathbf z).
 \end{split}
 \tag{BC9}
\]
No restricted current in these formulas is asserted separately
closed. In top degree, finite maxima therefore preserve any
fixed original positive-measure subsolution lower bound.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for this completion.
The proof parallels the frozen carrier method, but uses the
newly established band-capacity continuity rather than assuming
it for the larger class.

\begin{proof}
At the seed level refine finitely many countable band partitions.
On each band the continuous actual branches have an ordinary
open strict comparison locus. Frozen ordinary locality gives
the maximum identity there; (PB9) and the positive band sum give
the seed version of (BC8).

Choose seed defining rows for the completed tuple and their
maxima. Let $\chi_\epsilon$ be a continuous Lipschitz scalar
cutoff which is zero on $(-\infty,\epsilon]$, one on
$[2\epsilon,\infty)$, and nondecreasing between. Multiply the
seed strict-carrier identity by
$\chi_\epsilon(u_m-v_m)$. These bounded weights converge in
local capacity to $\chi_\epsilon(u-v)$, whose limit is
quasicontinuous. The completed weighted continuity theorem
passes the identity. Let $\epsilon\downarrow0$ using a fixed
rescaled cutoff. Bounded convergence for every original
coefficient measure gives (BC8).

Put $w_\epsilon=\max(u,v-\epsilon)$. This belongs to the
completion and converges uniformly to $w$, hence in local
capacity. Apply (BC8) on its two strict carriers. The shift
can be normalized by replacing $u,v$ by
$(u+\epsilon)/(1+\epsilon),v/(1+\epsilon)$, so the identity
uses only already constructed normalized entries and their
proved affine compatibility. Positivity on the remaining
restriction gives, before any limiting operation,
\[
 \widehat T^{,i}(w_\epsilon^{[a]},\mathbf z)
 \geq\mathbf1_{\{u\geq v\}}\widehat T^{,i}(u^{[a]},\mathbf z)
       +\mathbf1_{\{u<v-\epsilon\}}\widehat T^{,i}(v^{[a]},\mathbf z).
\]
The first right-hand current is fixed, retaining any equality
mass. The second increases on every positive original test as
$\epsilon\downarrow0$. The left side converges by the proved
capacity theorem. This yields (BC9) on the full middle-positive
dual cone. In top degree the two indicators partition the
finite Borel locus, and all relevant measures ignore its
outer-null complement; the subsolution assertion follows.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact capacity statement and the remaining cofinality gate}

For Borel $E$ define
\[
                \widehat\gamma_i(E)
                  =\sup_{h\in\mathfrak B_i(V)}\widehat\mu_h^{,i}(E).
 \tag{BC10}
\]
\begin{theorem}[Outer capacity is unchanged for the exact seed]
\label{thm:r12-band-completion-outer-capacity}
For every Borel $E\subset V$,
\[
 \gamma_0(E)\leq\widehat\gamma_0(E)\leq\gamma_0^*(E),
 \qquad
 \widehat\gamma_0(G)=\gamma_0(G)\quad(G\text{ ordinary open}),
 \qquad
 \widehat\gamma_0^*=\gamma_0^*.
 \tag{BC11}
\]
For the full-band-control completion only the following is
asserted without an extra cofinality theorem:
\[
 \gamma_0(E)\leq\widehat\gamma_1(E)

b1_finite_hausdorff_saturated_sets_second_proof.tex \section{A restricted positive Borel result from a uniform Hausdorff estimate}
\paragraph{Author and status.}
Independent derivation and audit by task \texttt{/root/b1\_positive\_routes}.
\texttt{PROVED-INTERNAL}, conditional only on the already audited original
local linear trace lemma. This is a restricted positive result, not the
general B1 theorem and not a claim of worldwide novelty.

Retain the fixed original $K$, absolute value, original $n$-torus with
$n\ge2$, the strict Laurent box $V$, normalized moments
$\tau:V\to Q=(-1,1)^n$, and the smooth strongly positive background
$S=\beta^{n-1}[X]$ used in the preceding sections. Thus $q=1$ and
\[
 \tau_*(Da\wedge S)=\gamma\Delta g_a,
 \qquad\gamma=(n-1)!\lambda^{n-2},
\]
for every original normalized tester $0\le a\le1$, with canonical convex
trace $0\le g_a\le1$. Fix a compact set $P\Subset Q$ and set
$d=\operatorname{dist}(P,\mathbf R^n\setminus Q)>0$.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform local ball and Hausdorff control]
There is a constant $M_{n,P}<\infty$, independent of the original tester,
such that every Borel $F\subset P$ satisfies
\[
 C_S^*(\tau^{-1}F;V)
       \le M_{n,P}\gamma\,\mathcal H^{n-1}(F).
 \tag{HR1}
\]
The Hausdorff measure has any one fixed standard normalization; its
normalizing factor is absorbed in $M_{n,P}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Every convex $g:Q\to[0,1]$ is Lipschitz with constant at most
$L=2/d$ on the $d/2$ neighborhood of $P$. Indeed, at a point of that
neighborhood, moving toward either sign of any unit vector by a distance
approaching $d/2$ remains in $Q$; the subgradient inequality bounds every
directional component of the subgradient by $2/d$.

Choose a fixed smooth nonnegative cutoff $\eta$ on $\mathbf R^n$, equal
to one on the unit ball and supported in the ball of radius two. For
$z\in P$ and $0<\rho<d/8$, let
$\eta_{z,\rho}(x)=\eta((x-z)/\rho)$. Positivity of the Radon measure
$\Delta g$ and distributional integration by parts imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 \Delta g(B(z,\rho))
 &\le\int\eta_{z,\rho}\,d\Delta g
   =-\int\nabla g\cdot\nabla\eta_{z,\rho}\,dx\\
 &\le L\|\nabla\eta\|_{L^1(\mathbf R^n)}\rho^{n-1}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{HR2}
\]
All supports remain in the protected region where the common Lipschitz
bound is valid. The identity is legitimate for locally Lipschitz $g$;
no trace theorem on sphere boundaries is used. The original linear trace
identity consequently gives
\[
 C_S(\tau^{-1}B(z,\rho);V)
       \le\gamma L\|\nabla\eta\|_1\rho^{n-1}.
 \tag{HR3}
\]

Cover $F$ by countably many open balls centered in $F$, of radii less
than $d/8$. The original open union of their inverseimages contains
$\tau^{-1}F$. For every original tester, its mass on that union is at
most the sum of its masses on the individual inverseimages, so (HR3)
bounds the raw capacity of this union by the sum of the right sides.
Taking the infimum over arbitrarily fine ball covers proves (HR1),
using the ball-cover characterization of Hausdorff measure and absorbing
its fixed dimensional normalization into $M_{n,P}$. The capacity being
estimated is always the original open outer capacity; it is not replaced
by a Hausdorff capacity or a smaller tester class.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Borel inner regularity for finite-Hausdorff saturated sets]
Let $B\subset P$ be Borel with $\mathcal H^{n-1}(B)<\infty$, and let
$E=\tau^{-1}B$. Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad C_S^*(E;V)
      =\sup_{H\subset E,\ H\text{ compact}}C_S^*(H;V).\quad}
 \tag{HR4}
\]
In fact compact inverseimages $H=\tau^{-1}F$, with $F\subset B$ compact,
already suffice for the supremum.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The finite Borel measure
$A\mapsto\mathcal H^{n-1}(A\cap B)$ on $\mathbf R^n$ is Radon.
Consequently, for every $\epsilon>0$, there is a compact
$F\subset B$ such that $\mathcal H^{n-1}(B\setminus F)<\epsilon$.
This uses ordinary regularity of a single finite Borel measure on
Euclidean space, not regularity of the capacity under investigation.

The moment map is proper over compact subsets of $Q$, hence
$\tau^{-1}F$ is an original compact subset of $E$. Countable
subadditivity of the original outer capacity and (HR1) give
\[
 C_S^*(E;V)
 \le C_S^*(\tau^{-1}F;V)
        +C_S^*(\tau^{-1}(B\setminus F);V)
 \le C_S^*(\tau^{-1}F;V)+M_{n,P}\gamma\epsilon.
\]
For clarity, the subadditivity used here follows directly from the
definition: choose original open supersets of the separate sets with
raw capacities arbitrarily close to their outer capacities, take their
union, and use countable subadditivity of every tester measure before
taking the tester supremum. It is ordinary subadditivity, not the
strong-subadditivity assertion refuted above.

Since (HR1) makes the left side finite, letting $\epsilon\downarrow0$
proves the upper bound by the compact supremum. The reverse bound is
monotonicity. No increasing-sequence continuity of the outer capacity
is used.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Exact limitations.}
The theorem concerns full moment-saturated sets $\tau^{-1}B$, with $B$
inside one fixed protected compact stage and of finite
$\mathcal H^{n-1}$ measure, for this specific smooth strongly positive
background and remaining degree one. It does not cover arbitrary
Borel subsets of the original Berkovich space, arbitrary closed
backgrounds, or higher remaining degrees. In particular a Borel subset
of $\tau^{-1}B$ need not be the inverseimage of any Borel subset of $B$;
no such extension is asserted. Likewise $\sigma$-finiteness alone gives
no uniform small Hausdorff remainder and cannot be substituted for
finiteness without an additional argument. No global exhaustion or
boundary-tail theorem is obtained.

The estimate also gives outer capacity zero for every saturated
$\mathcal H^{n-1}$-null set in the protected stage. This is compatible
with the failure of strong subadditivity: regularity and submodularity
are distinct properties. General B1 remains OPEN.

title: One-sided background order suffices for the restricted Hausdorff theorem
text:
b1_one_sided_order_hausdorff_extension.tex \section{One-sided background order suffices for the restricted Hausdorff theorem}
\paragraph{Status.}
\texttt{PROVED-INTERNAL}, a direct consequence of the already audited
Hausdorff estimate and degree-one background linearity. This appendix
is separate from the proof sources already sent for review.

Retain the original domain, fixed field and absolute value, normalized
tester class, moment map $\tau$, and $S_0=\beta^{n-1}[X]$ with $q=1$.
Let $S'$ be an allowed background on the same ordinary representative.
Suppose that for a constant $C<\infty$ the actual residual current
\[
                       CS_0-S'
\]
is an allowed symmetric middle-positive separately $d'$- and
$d''$-closed background. No positive lower bound for $S'$ is required.
Then for every protected compact $P\Subset Q$ and Borel $B\subset P$
with $\mathcal H^{n-1}(B)<\infty$, the original outer capacity defined
using $S'$ satisfies
\[
 C_{S'}^*(\tau^{-1}B;V)
   =\sup_{H\subset\tau^{-1}B,\ H\text{ compact}}C_{S'}^*(H;V).
 \tag{OH1}
\]
Compact sets of the form $H=\tau^{-1}F$ with $F\subset B$ compact suffice.

\begin{proof}
For every original normalized psh tester $a$, the bounded linear
recursion and positivity of the residual background give
\[
 0\le Da\wedge S'\le C\,Da\wedge S_0.
\]
Taking suprema over the unchanged testers and then infima over the
unchanged original open neighborhoods yields
$C_{S'}^*(E;V)\le C\,C_{S_0}^*(E;V)$ for every relevant set $E$.
The protected-stage Hausdorff estimate therefore gives, for every
Borel $F\subset P$,
\[
 C_{S'}^*(\tau^{-1}F;V)
       \le C M_{n,P}\gamma\mathcal H^{n-1}(F).
\]
Choose compact $F\subset B$ with
$\mathcal H^{n-1}(B\setminus F)<\epsilon$, using inner regularity of
the single finite Radon measure $\mathcal H^{n-1}|_B$. Ordinary
subadditivity for the original $S'$ outer capacity gives
\[
 C_{S'}^*(\tau^{-1}B;V)
 \le C_{S'}^*(\tau^{-1}F;V)+C M_{n,P}\gamma\epsilon.
\]
Properness of $\tau$ over compact real sets makes $\tau^{-1}F$ compact.
Letting $\epsilon\downarrow0$ and using monotonicity proves (OH1).
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Range of the extension.}
The hypothesis is an actual current-order statement with an allowed
positive closed residual, valid on the original representative and all
original tests. It is not inferred from smoothness of $S'$ or comparison
of scalar coefficients in one selected tropicalization. In particular,
the moment form $\beta$ need not control extra directions introduced by
actual refinements. The theorem still requires a protected compact
stage, a moment-saturated Borel set, finite Hausdorff measure, and
remaining degree one. It does not promote these conclusions to arbitrary
allowed backgrounds or arbitrary original Borel sets. General B1
remains OPEN.

title: Closed relative truncation products of unbounded classical potentials
text:
relative_nonpolar_truncation.tex \section{Closed relative truncation products of unbounded classical potentials}
\label{sec:r11-relative-truncation}

Throughout this section $K/\mathbf Q_p$ is the fixed original finite
extension with its original absolute value.  The space $X$ is good,
Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth and purely $n$-dimensional; $U$ is
ordinary open.  The background $S$ is an arbitrary original symmetric
CLD middle-positive, separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed current of
degree $(p,p)$.  Write
\[
 T_{S,I}(\mathbf u)=\bigwedge_{i\in I}D u_i\wedge S
\]
for the frozen bounded Bedford--Taylor product; $T_{S,\varnothing}=S$.
Products are always the original current products.  This notation
asserts neither a quotient for all actual delta-form presentations nor
equality against additional GK delta tests.

The following frozen inputs are used: bounded mixed products, their
weighted decreasing convergence, relative CLN, the bounded energy and
chain identities, and strict Borel maximum locality.  These are
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}, with sources R4 and the R2--R3 modules
preserved in the R10 archive.  In particular R3,
\texttt{pluripolar\_zero\_extension.tex}, is not reproved below: its
closed exceptional-set hypothesis does not apply directly to the
possibly nonclosed pole sets in the present construction.

\subsection{First derivatives and a plateau estimate}

\begin{lemma}[First-order coefficient measures for bounded potentials]
\label{lem:r11-bounded-first-order}
Let $T$ be any allowed original positive closed current of degree
$(P,P)$, $d=n-P\geq1$, and let $v$ be a locally bounded classical
psh function.  The currents $d'(vT)$ and $d''(vT)$ are coefficient-Radon.
For an original $(d-1,d)$-test $\alpha$, choose on its compact stage a
nonnegative smooth cutoff $\chi=1$ near its support and a positive
moment control $\beta=\sum_a d't_a\wedge d''t_a$.  There is a finite
constant $C_\alpha$ such that, for every bounded Borel $b$,
\[
 \left|\int b\,d'(vT)\wedge\alpha\right|^2
 \leq C_\alpha
 \left(\int\chi\,\Gamma_T(v)\wedge\beta^{d-1}\right)
 \left(\int\chi b^2\,\beta^d\wedge T\right).
 \tag{NP1}
\]
There is the analogous double-prime inequality.  Here
\[
 \Gamma_T(v)=\tfrac12D(v^2T)-vD(vT)
\]
is the frozen positive bounded-energy current.  For every $C^1$
function $F$ on a neighborhood of the bounded range under consideration,
\[
 d'(F(v)T)=F'(v)d'(vT),\qquad
 d''(F(v)T)=F'(v)d''(vT).
 \tag{NP2}
\]
These statements are local on ordinary opens and include arbitrary
additional actual moment coordinates used in $v$ or the tests.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the
frozen weighted bounded calculus, with the first-order passage detailed
here to make the later Borel restrictions legitimate.

\begin{proof}
Choose bounded smooth decreasing regularizations $v_m$ on a fixed
neighborhood of the compact stage.  The bounded energy identity and
weighted joint decreasing convergence give
\[
 \int\chi\,\Gamma_T(v_m-v_l)\wedge\beta^{d-1}\longrightarrow0
                    \quad(\min(m,l)\longrightarrow\infty).
 \tag{NP3}
\]
This is the calculation in R4,
\texttt{prop:r4-classical-in-energy}: expand the energy of the
difference; the four weighted curvature terms have the same limit
and cancel, and its squared-function term tends to zero against fixed
coefficient measures.  The calculation uses bounded local calculus,
not the later global faithful energy construction.

For smooth $v_m-v_l$ the positive coefficient matrix of $T$ and
measure Cauchy--Schwarz bound the total variation of every fixed
coefficient of $d'((v_m-v_l)T)$ by a constant times the square root
of (NP3).  It follows that the first derivatives converge in local
coefficient total variation.  Since $v_mT\to vT$ on all original
tests by bounded convergence against the fixed coefficients of $T$,
the limit is $d'(vT)$.  The smooth coefficient inequality passes to
this total-variation limit and gives (NP1); it also gives the inequality
with a Borel restriction inserted into both positive factors.  Borel
weights are permitted by Radon measure Cauchy--Schwarz, not by an
assertion that a Borel-restricted background is closed.

The smooth identity for $F(v_m)$ passes to distributions.  On its
right-hand side the derivative measures converge in total variation,
the multipliers are uniformly bounded, and $F'(v_m)\to F'(v)$
pointwise.  Dominated convergence for the fixed limiting derivative
measure proves (NP2).  The double-prime argument is identical.
Finite partitions handle tests requiring several presentations.
The control $\beta$ only uses the fixed test coordinates; adjoining
the units used by each individual approximation preserves its positive
coefficient inequality.  No common finite moment for the entire
infinite sequence is assumed.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[No first-order energy on the zero plateau]
\label{lem:r11-zero-plateau}
With $T$ as above, let $v\geq0$ be bounded classical psh.  Then
\[
 \mathbf1_{\{v=0\}}\Gamma_T(v)=0,\qquad
 \mathbf1_{\{v=0\}}d'(vT)=
 \mathbf1_{\{v=0\}}d''(vT)=0.
 \tag{NP4}
\]
All restrictions concern coefficient measures on the actual ordinary
space.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} by the following
short bounded-energy argument; no general assertion about an arbitrary
Borel level set of a current is assumed.

\begin{proof}
For $\varepsilon>0$ set
\[
 g_\varepsilon=\max(v-\varepsilon,0),\qquad
 h_\varepsilon=v-g_\varepsilon=\min(v,\varepsilon).
\]
The functions $v$ and $g_\varepsilon$ are bounded classical, and $h_\varepsilon$
is their bounded difference.  For any fixed nonnegative compact
smooth $\chi$ and its moment control, the bounded energy identity gives
\begin{align*}
 0\leq\int\chi\Gamma_T(h_\varepsilon)\wedge\beta^{d-1}
 &\leq \tfrac12\varepsilon^2
     |\mu_{T,D\chi\wedge\beta^{d-1}}|(\operatorname{supp}\chi)\\
 &\quad+\varepsilon\int\chi
       \bigl(D(vT)+D(g_\varepsilon T)\bigr)\wedge\beta^{d-1}.
\end{align*}
The last masses are uniformly bounded as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$
by relative CLN, since $0\leq g_\varepsilon\leq v$.  The displayed
quantity therefore tends to zero.  Upper semicontinuity of $v$
makes $\{v<\varepsilon\}$ ordinarily open.  On that open
$h_\varepsilon=v$, so ordinary locality identifies their energy
currents there.  It follows that the restriction of the positive
energy current to $\{v=0\}$ is zero, for every original positive
control.  The restricted form of (NP1) now makes every first-order
coefficient zero on that same set.  Refining the moment presentation
does not change any of these identities.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Consistent truncations and closedness}

Let $u_1,\ldots,u_k\leq0$ be extended classical psh functions,
$1\leq k\leq n-p$.  Put
\[
 u_{i,j}=\max(u_i,-j),\qquad
 E_j=\bigcap_{i=1}^k\{u_i>-j\},\qquad
 T_j=T_{S,\{1,\ldots,k\}}(\mathbf u_j),\qquad
 R_j=\mathbf1_{E_j}T_j.
 \tag{NP5}
\]
The sets $E_j$ are Borel and need not be ordinarily open.  The
restriction $R_j$ need not be closed.

\begin{definition}[Finite relative truncation mass]
\label{def:r11-finite-truncation-mass}
The tuple has locally finite relative truncation mass if for every
original compact positive coefficient control $\Theta$ of degree
$(n-p-k,n-p-k)$ one has
\[
                         \sup_j\langle R_j,\Theta\rangle<\infty.
 \tag{NP6}
\]
It suffices to impose (NP6) on the finite positive controls dominating
each original compact test stage; the quantifier ranges over every
stage and its actual moment refinements.  In particular it is not a
single selected tropical trace bound.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Closed relative truncation product]
\label{thm:r11-closed-nonpolar-product}
Under (NP6), the increasing coefficient limit
\[
 \mathcal N_S(u_1,\ldots,u_k)=\lim_{j\to\infty}R_j
 \tag{NP7}
\]
is a well-defined original symmetric middle-positive,
separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed coefficient-Radon current of degree
$(p+k,p+k)$.  If
$P=\bigcup_i\{u_i=-\infty\}$, then
\[
 \mathbf1_P\mathcal N_S(\mathbf u)=0,
 \qquad
 \mathbf1_{E_j}\mathcal N_S(\mathbf u)=R_j.
 \tag{NP8}
\]
The construction is ordinary-local, symmetric in the potentials,
compatible with all original tests and actual moment refinements,
and independent of any cofinal choice of separate truncation levels.
For locally bounded potentials it is the frozen bounded BT product.
The background $S$ is arbitrary throughout.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}.  The finite-mass
condition is an explicit necessary condition for the coefficient limit
to be a current; the new conclusion is its separate closedness across
all truncation interfaces, including a possibly nonclosed pole set.

\begin{proof}
For $l\geq j$, strict Borel maximum locality applied successively in
each slot gives
\[
                       \mathbf1_{E_j}T_l=\mathbf1_{E_j}T_j.
 \tag{NP9}
\]
Consequently $R_l-R_j$ is positive.  The local bounds (NP6) and the
finite positive controls yield Radon limits of all diagonal coefficient
measures; polarization gives the remaining coefficients.  Their linear
and refinement identities pass to the limits.  These same controls
give continuity on every original compact test stage.  Thus (NP7)
defines a current $N$, and (NP8) follows from (NP9) and monotone
measure convergence.  Its coefficients are carried by the union
of the $E_j$, which is $U\setminus P$.

If $p+k=n$, closedness is automatic by degree.  Suppose
$d=n-p-k\geq1$.  Fix an original $(d-1,d)$-test $\alpha$,
and choose $\chi,\beta$ on a compact stage as in (NP1).  Set
\[
 \psi=\sum_{i=1}^k u_i,\qquad
 v_j=\max(0,1+\psi/j),\qquad a_j=2v_j-v_j^2.
 \tag{NP10}
\]
The functions $v_j$ are actual bounded classical psh, between zero
and one.  This follows either by bounded decreasing approximation of
the summands or the extended classical maximum property.  They
increase to one on $U\setminus P$ and vanish on $P$.
Since all $u_i\leq0$, the set $F_j=\{v_j>0\}=\{\psi>-j\}$
is contained in $E_j$.  In particular, for $r=1,2$,
\[
 v_j^rT_j=v_j^rN,\qquad a_jT_j=a_jN.
 \tag{NP11}
\]
These are coefficient identities: on $F_j$ use (NP9), and on its
complement the multipliers vanish.  They do not assert closedness of
either Borel restriction.

The bounded energy identity, compact Stokes and positivity give
\begin{align*}
 B_j&:=\int\chi\Gamma_{T_j}(v_j)\wedge\beta^{d-1}\\
 &=\tfrac12\langle v_j^2T_j,D\chi\wedge\beta^{d-1}\rangle
      -\int\chi v_jD(v_jT_j)\wedge\beta^{d-1}\\
 &\leq\tfrac12|\mu_{N,D\chi\wedge\beta^{d-1}}|
                      (\operatorname{supp}\chi)=:B<\infty.
 \tag{NP12}
\end{align*}
In the last line we used (NP11).  Thus the bound does not require
uniform mass of the uncut currents $T_j$ at their moving interfaces.

By (NP2), $d'(a_jT_j)=2(1-v_j)d'(v_jT_j)$.  Lemma
\ref{lem:r11-zero-plateau} allows the first-order factor to be
restricted to $F_j$.  Apply (NP1) with the Borel multiplier
$\mathbf1_{F_j}(1-v_j)$.  Equations (NP9) and (NP12) yield
\[
 |\langle d'(a_jT_j),\alpha\rangle|^2
 \leq4C_\alpha B
       \int\chi(1-v_j)^2\,\beta^d\wedge N
                       \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{NP13}
\]
Dominated convergence applies to the fixed finite coefficient measure
on the right, because $N$ has no coefficient mass on $P$.
At the same time (NP11) and dominated convergence give $a_jT_j\to N$
on all original tests.  Distributional continuity now implies
$d'N=0$.  The double-prime estimate proves $d''N=0$.

The construction and proof commute with ordinary restriction and
common actual refinement.  For separate level vectors, the same
strict Borel locality gives a directed consistent family; diagonal
integer levels are cofinal.  This proves independence of that choice
and symmetry.  If all potentials are locally bounded, their
truncations agree with them on any fixed compact neighborhood once
the levels are large enough, proving compatibility with bounded BT.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Background linearity and pole restrictions]
\label{cor:r11-nonpolar-background-restriction}
On the finite-mass domain of the preceding theorem, $\mathcal N_S$
is additive and nonnegative-real homogeneous in the original positive
closed background.  If $A$ is a complete classical pole set, then
\[
 \mathbf1_A\mathcal N_S(\mathbf u)
                    =\mathcal N_{\mathbf1_A S}(\mathbf u).
 \tag{NP14}
\]
The right side is defined by the same truncations and automatically
has locally finite coefficient mass.  If $S$ has no coefficient mass
on any local pluripolar set, the same is true of $\mathcal N_S$.
For arbitrary $S$, (NP8) only removes the poles of the stated tuple.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} using the
frozen complete-pole restriction theorem for bounded products.

\begin{proof}
Background linearity holds at every truncated level and passes through
the increasing positive limits.  The frozen pole restriction identity
gives $\mathbf1_A T_j=T_{\mathbf1_A S,k}(\mathbf u_j)$;
the restricted background is separately closed by that theorem.
Restrict also to $E_j$ and take the increasing coefficient limits.
The required mass bounds are inherited from $N$.  Localizing the
result to a complete pole witness proves the final assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Potential additivity can fail over a polar background]
\label{prop:r11-nonpolar-additivity-failure}
For every $n\geq2$ there are an allowed original $n$-dimensional
ordinary domain, a positive closed background $S$ of degree $(1,1)$,
a bounded classical $u$, and an extended classical $v$ for which all
three relative truncation products exist and
\[
 \mathcal N_S(u+v)=0=\mathcal N_S(v),
                   \qquad \mathcal N_S(u)\ne0.
 \tag{NP15}
\]
Thus unrestricted additivity in unbounded potentials, while retaining
every polar background component, is false for (NP7).
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the explicit
original example; the unrestricted additivity assertion is
\texttt{FALSE}.  This is not a counterexample to the frozen bounded
multilinearity theorem.

\begin{proof}
Take an ordinary product of the open unit disc in coordinate $z$
and $n-1$ bounded open annuli in unit coordinates $t_1,\ldots,t_{n-1}$.
Let $Z=\{z=0\}$ and $S=[Z]$.  Put
\[
 v=\log|z|,\qquad
 u=\tfrac12(\log|t_1|)^2-C,
\]
where $C$ makes $u\leq0$ on the domain.  The logarithm is an extended
classical psh function, with value $-\infty$ on $Z$; $u$ is bounded
classical and its curvature on $Z$ is the nonzero original positive
form $d'\log|t_1|\wedge d''\log|t_1|$.  Hence $D(uS)\ne0$;
one can test it with a nonnegative compact product test in the
remaining annular directions.  The ordinary original product
calibration has positive degree, so the pairing is strictly positive.

Each truncated product over $S$ is supported on $Z$, by ordinary
locality of the frozen calculus.  The finite loci of $v$ and $u+v$
are disjoint from $Z$.  Their cut currents $R_j$ are therefore zero
at every level.  This gives (NP15) and all its mass assertions.
The example uses a special background only to disprove the universal
additivity assertion; no restriction on $S$ was used in the theorem.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The remaining unrestricted issue.}
Theorem~\ref{thm:r11-closed-nonpolar-product} does not make (NP6)
automatic for every extended classical tuple.  Nor does it identify
relative polar null sets with ambient pluripolarity for every background.
The finite-energy criterion in the next section gives a checkable large
domain on which the uncut products also converge and the usual
recursive differential identity survives.

title: An intrinsic no-loss boundary class and its mixed top calculus
text:
capacity_tail_boundary_class.tex \section{An intrinsic no-loss boundary class and its mixed top calculus}
\label{sec:r11-capacity-tail-boundary-class}

Retain the original field, analytic space, arbitrary background $S$,
ordinary domain $V$, and $q=n-p\geq1$ from
Section~\ref{sec:r11-unbounded-comparison}. Every potential below is
negative extended classical psh, with its actual values retained.
The capacity always has the fixed tester domain $V$. The results
of this section concern top-degree measures. They do not construct
all lower-degree products without the separate energy hypotheses.

\begin{lemma}[Compact conservation of truncation mass]
\label{lem:r11-compact-truncation-conservation}
If $\mathrm{BG}(u,0)$ holds, then $\mu_u$ in (UC3) is locally
finite, without assuming absence of truncation loss. More precisely,
fix $M>0$ and $H\Subset V$, set
$K_M=\overline{\{u<-M\}}\Subset V$, and choose an original smooth
compact function $0\leq\chi\leq1$ which is one on an ordinary
neighborhood of $H\cup K_M$. Then for integers $j,l>M$,
\[
                       \int\chi\,d\mu_{u,j}
                           =\int\chi\,d\mu_{u,l}.
 \tag{BC1}
\]
In particular $\sup_j\mu_{u,j}(H)<\infty$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as a compact
conservation statement for unbounded actual potentials, using only
the frozen bounded telescoping identity and original compact Stokes.

\begin{proof}
Outside $K_M$ one has $u\geq-M$, hence $u_j=u_l=u$ there.
The bounded mixed calculus gives
\[
 \mu_{u,j}-\mu_{u,l}
   =D\left((u_j-u_l)
       \sum_{r=0}^{q-1}(Du_j)^r(Du_l)^{q-1-r}\wedge S\right).
 \tag{BC2}
\]
Every product in the parentheses is a frozen original positive
closed product. Its bounded Borel multiplier is zero outside
$K_M$, so the entire current in parentheses has support in $K_M$.
Pair (BC2) with $\chi$. Since $D\chi$ vanishes near $K_M$,
the pairing is zero, proving (BC1). Fixing one $l>M$ bounds
the nonnegative masses on $H$ for every $j>M$; the remaining
finitely many $j$ have finite mass. The increasing restricted
measures in (UC3) have the same bound on $H$, proving local
finiteness of their limit. No bound for a lower-degree truncation
product is inferred from this top-degree Stokes argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The no-loss zero-boundary class]
\label{def:r11-no-loss-boundary-class}
Set
\[
 \mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)
   =\{u\in\mathcal F_{S,\mathrm{loc}}(V):
                                      \mathrm{BG}(u,0)\}.
 \tag{BC3}
\]
The notation records compact strict negative sublevels, not an
unstated ordinary boundary regularity hypothesis.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[An exact capacity-tail criterion]
\label{thm:r11-capacity-tail-criterion}
Let $u$ satisfy $\mathrm{BG}(u,0)$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)$;
\item $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to\infty}
              t^q\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{u<-t\};V)=0$;
\item $\displaystyle\lim_{j\to\infty}\nu_{u,j}(V)=0$.
\end{enumerate}
The capacity in (2) can equivalently be replaced by its ordinary-open
outer regularization. If these conditions hold, then
$\mu_{u,j}-\mu_u$ is a finite signed measure on $V$ for every
sufficiently large $j$, and
\[
 \begin{split}
 t^q\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{u<-t\};V)
       &\leq2^q\mu_u(\{u<-t/2\}),\\
 \nu_{u,j}(V)&\leq4^q\mu_u(\{u<-j/4\}),\\
 \|\mu_{u,j}-\mu_u\|_{\mathrm{TV}(V)}
       &\leq(4^q+1)\mu_u(\{u<-j/4\})\longrightarrow0.
 \end{split}
 \tag{BC4}
\]
The measures themselves need not have finite total mass near the
boundary; their difference is supported in one fixed compact set
for all sufficiently large $j$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}. The condition in
(2) is expressed solely through the frozen bounded capacity.

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:r11-compact-truncation-conservation} supplies local
finiteness automatically. For $j>M$, the discarded measure is
carried by $\{u\leq-j\}\subset K_M$. Thus (1) and (3) are
equivalent. Under (1), (UC20) with $v=0$ and $\delta=t/2$
gives the first inequality of (BC4). Its right side tends to zero:
for large $t$ the carrier lies in the fixed compact $K_M$, on
which $\mu_u$ is finite, and the decreasing carriers intersect
in the $\mu_u$-null pole set. Upper semicontinuity makes
$\{u<-t\}$ ordinary open, so its raw and outer capacities agree.
This proves (2).

Conversely, the bounded function $h_j=1+u_j/j$ is a normalized
capacity tester and $\mu_{u,j}=j^q\mu_{h_j}$. Therefore
\[
 \nu_{u,j}(V)
    \leq j^q\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{u<-j/2\};V).
 \tag{BC5}
\]
Condition (2) makes this tend to zero and proves (3).
Combining (BC5) with the first inequality of (BC4), at $t=j/2$,
gives the second. The measures agree on $\{u>-j\}$; on its
complement their variation difference is at most the sum of their
masses. The second inequality and
$\{u\leq-j\}\subset\{u<-j/4\}$ give the last bound in
(BC4). All these tail sets lie in $K_M$ for large $j$, as claimed.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A solid convex cone of actual potentials]
\label{thm:r11-solid-boundary-cone}
The class $\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)$ contains $0$ and has the
following closure properties.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $u$ belongs to the class and $v$ is any negative extended
classical psh function with $u\leq v\leq0$, then $v$ belongs
to the class.
\item If $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ belong to the class and $a_i\geq0$,
then $\sum_i a_i u_i$ belongs to the class, with zero-coefficient
terms omitted.
\item Finite maxima of its members belong to the class.
\end{enumerate}
No continuity, smoothness, geometric origin or full-support
assumption is imposed on $S$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}. These are
closure assertions for the explicit no-loss class, not for all
unbounded classical psh functions.

\begin{proof}
For (1), $\{v<-t\}\subset\{u<-t\}$ gives both the compact
boundary-gap condition and the capacity-tail criterion.
For (2), assume $A=\sum_i a_i>0$. The elementary inclusion
\[
 \left\{\sum_i a_i u_i<-t\right\}
                  \subset\bigcup_{i:a_i>0}\{u_i<-t/A\}
 \tag{BC6}
\]
gives compact sublevels and
\[
 t^q\operatorname{Cap}_S
          \left(\left\{\sum_i a_i u_i<-t\right\};V\right)
 \leq A^q\sum_{i:a_i>0}
       (t/A)^q\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{u_i<-t/A\};V)
                       \longrightarrow0.
\]
The sum is an extended classical psh function by the frozen
curve definition and positivity. The zero sum is immediate.
Finally a finite maximum is classical psh and dominates any one
of its members, so (1) proves (3).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Top mixed products without a superlinear energy assumption}

\begin{theorem}[A positive mixed top calculus in the boundary class]
\label{thm:r11-boundary-mixed-top-calculus}
For $u_1,\ldots,u_q\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)$ put
\[
 M_j=T_{S,q}(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{q,j}),\qquad
 E_j=\bigcap_{i=1}^q\{u_i>-j\}.
\]
The increasing consistent restrictions define a locally finite
positive measure
\[
            M(u_1,\ldots,u_q)=\lim_j\mathbf1_{E_j}M_j.
 \tag{BC7}
\]
It gives zero mass to the union of the $q$ pole sets. The uncut
measures converge to it in total variation on the whole domain,
in the sense of a finite signed difference:
\[
               \|M_j-M(u_1,\ldots,u_q)\|_{\mathrm{TV}(V)}
                                           \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{BC8}
\]
Independent canonical truncation levels have the same limit as
their minimum tends to infinity. The resulting product is symmetric,
additive and positively homogeneous in every slot on this cone, and
\[
 M(u_1,\ldots,u_q)
   ={1\over q!}\sum_{I\subset\{1,\ldots,q\}}
        (-1)^{q-|I|}\mu_{\sum_{i\in I}u_i}.
 \tag{BC9}
\]
Here the empty sum has zero top measure. Every equality is an
equality of actual Borel measures, and hence holds against every
original compact smooth scalar test and all its actual refinements.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}. This top-degree
result requires no superlinear weighted energy estimate and does
not assert the corresponding lower-degree recursive calculus.

\begin{proof}
Let $w=\sum_i u_i$ and $s_j=\sum_i u_{i,j}$. The solid-cone
theorem puts $w$ in $\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)$. The exact identity
\[
                      \max(s_j,-j)=\max(w,-j)=w_j
 \tag{BC10}
\]
holds: if no slot is truncated then $s_j=w$, while if a slot is
truncated then $s_j\leq-j$. Strict Borel maximum locality thus
identifies the top measure of $s_j$ with $\mu_w$ on $\{w>-j\}$.
As $-qj\leq s_j\leq0$, capacity normalization gives
\[
 \mu_{s_j}(\{w\leq-j\})
       \leq(qj)^q\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{w<-j/2\};V)
                                     \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{BC11}
\]
The mass of $\mu_w$ on the same compact tails tends to zero.
Hence $\mu_{s_j}\to\mu_w$ in total variation on $V$.

The positive bounded mixed expansion gives $q!M_j\leq\mu_{s_j}$.
The complement of $E_j$ is contained in $\{w\leq-j\}$.
Equation (BC11) therefore makes the discarded part
$\mathbf1_{V\setminus E_j}M_j$ tend to zero in mass. Frozen
strict maximum locality gives consistency on $E_j$, exactly as
in (UC2). Their increasing limit is bounded locally by the
already bounded family $\mu_{s_j}/q!$, so is locally finite.
Its mass on $V\setminus E_j$ tends to zero, since these tails
are eventually compact and decrease to the union of the pole sets.
This proves (BC7)--(BC8).

For completeness consider independent levels $l_i\geq m$. Fix
$M>0$ and let $K=\overline{\{w<-M\}}$. Whenever all levels
exceed $M$, all the truncated slots agree with their actual values
outside $K$. A slot-by-slot bounded telescoping identity and
compact Stokes, exactly as in (BC2), show that the integral of
the mixed measure against any fixed cutoff $\chi=1$ near $K$
is independent of all the levels. Passing to the common-level
limit using (BC8) shows that this integral equals $\int\chi\,dM$.
For $m>M$, strict locality gives equality with $M$ on $E_m$,
whereas $V\setminus E_m\subset K$. Subtracting these equal
cutoff integrals yields
\[
 T_{S,q}(u_{1,l_1},\ldots,u_{q,l_q})(V\setminus E_m)
                            =M(V\setminus E_m).
\]
Consequently the total variation of the difference is at most
$2M(V\setminus E_m)$, which tends to zero. This proves independence
of the truncation rates.

Bounded polarization gives (BC9) at level $j$. For every subset
$I$, the preceding argument with $s_{I,j}=\sum_{i\in I}u_{i,j}$
shows $\mu_{s_{I,j}}\to\mu_{\sum_{i\in I}u_i}$ in total
variation; the empty subset contributes zero. Passing in the finite
polarization identity proves (BC9).

Here is also a direct justification of all multilinearity claims.
For any finite family in the cone and fixed positive coefficients
$c_i$, put $A=\sum_i c_i$ and $c=\min_i c_i>0$. With
$s_j=\sum_i c_i u_{i,j}$ and $w=\sum_i c_i u_i$ one has
\[
                    \max(s_j,-cj)=\max(w,-cj).
\]
The preceding locality proof applies, and its discarded mass is
at most $(Aj)^q\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{w<-cj/2\};V)$, which
tends to zero by the tail criterion. Thus the positive bounded
polynomial expansion of $\mu_{s_j}$ passes to the limit for
every set of coefficients. Comparing coefficients in these finite
polynomial identities proves additivity and positive homogeneity
in each slot, with zero coefficients omitted. Symmetry is inherited
from the bounded products. No signed current order or PS quotient
is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform tails above one no-loss lower barrier]
\label{lem:r11-uniform-upper-tail}
If $u,v\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)$ and $u\leq v\leq0$,
then for every $t>0$,
\[
                 \mu_v(\{v<-t\})
                      \leq2^q\mu_u(\{u<-t/2\}).
 \tag{BC12}
\]
The right side is finite, and tends to zero as $t\to\infty$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} from the
one-sided comparison theorem and the solid boundary cone.

\begin{proof}
Scaling and addition of constants have their expected action on
(UC3): $\mu_{au-b}=a^q\mu_u$ for $a>0$, $b\geq0$.
Indeed, on each $\{u>-k\}$ and for $j>ak+b$, write
$au_k-b=\max((au-b)_j,-ak-b)$ and apply strict maximum
locality and bounded scaling. Exhaust the finite-value locus;
both sides vanish on its complement.
Now $2u$ belongs to the boundary class and
$\mathrm{BG}(2u,v-t)$ holds because its positive-margin gaps lie
in compact strict negative sublevels of $u$. Moreover,
\[
       \{-\infty<v<-t\}\subset\{2u<v-t\}
                                      \subset\{u<-t/2\}.
\]
Apply (UC10) to $2u,v-t$ and use the scaling and translation
identities. The omitted set $\{v=-\infty\}$ is $\mu_v$-null
by its definition; no literal strict-gap inclusion at a common
pole is asserted. This proves (BC12). The limiting assertion follows
from local finiteness on a fixed compact tail and zero mass on
the pole set.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Joint decreasing continuity in the boundary class]
\label{thm:r11-boundary-joint-decreasing}
For $1\leq i\leq q$, suppose $v_{i,l}$ are negative extended
classical psh functions and
\[
              v_{i,l}\downarrow u_i\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)
                         \quad\hbox{pointwise on }V.
 \tag{BC13}
\]
Then every $v_{i,l}$ belongs to the same boundary class, and
\[
       M(v_{1,l},\ldots,v_{q,l})
                       \longrightarrow M(u_1,\ldots,u_q)
 \tag{BC14}
\]
against every original compact smooth scalar test. No uniform
superlinear energy bound is needed. The conclusion is ordinary
current convergence, not convergence on arbitrary delta tests.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} in this top-degree
no-loss boundary class.

\begin{proof}
Membership follows from upward stability. Put $w=\sum_i u_i$
and $w_l=\sum_i v_{i,l}$, so $w\leq w_l\leq0$. Let
$M_l=M(v_{1,l},\ldots,v_{q,l})$ and let $M_{l,k}$ be the
bounded mixed product with every slot truncated at $-k$.
They agree by strict locality on
$E_{l,k}=\bigcap_i\{v_{i,l}>-k\}$. The positive mixed expansion
and (BC12) give
\[
 M_l(V\setminus E_{l,k})
 \leq {1\over q!}\mu_{w_l}(\{w_l\leq-k\})
 \leq {2^q\over q!}\mu_w(\{w<-k/4\}).
 \tag{BC15}
\]
In the last step use $\{w_l\leq-k\}\subset\{w_l<-k/2\}$
before applying (BC12).
The sum of the $q$ bounded truncated slots lies in $[-qk,0]$.
Also $V\setminus E_{l,k}\subset\{w\leq-k\}$. Capacity
normalization, the positive expansion and the first inequality
of (BC4) therefore give
\[
 M_{l,k}(V\setminus E_{l,k})
 \leq{(qk)^q\over q!}\operatorname{Cap}_S(\{w<-k/2\};V)
 \leq{q^q4^q\over q!}\mu_w(\{w<-k/4\}).
 \tag{BC16}
\]
The right sides are independent of $l$ and tend to zero.
Because the measures agree on $E_{l,k}$, their sum bounds the
total variation of $M_l-M_{l,k}$ on all of $V$.

For fixed $k$, the bounded functions
$\max(v_{i,l},-k)$ decrease jointly to $\max(u_i,-k)$.
Frozen bounded joint decreasing continuity gives convergence of
$M_{l,k}$ against every original compact smooth test as
$l\to\infty$. Apply the uniform tail bounds to the two ends
of this convergence, then let $k\to\infty$ and use (BC8) for
the limiting tuple. This proves (BC14) for the full original
test family. The two limits are separated by explicit uniform
total-variation bounds; no varying-background continuity or
unproved capacity regularity is inserted.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Outer-capacity domination in the boundary class]
\label{cor:r11-boundary-outer-domination}
Let $u\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)$ and let $v$ be any
negative extended classical psh function. The strict actual gap
$A=\{u<v\}$ is relatively quasi-open for the fixed capacity:
for each $\eta>0$ there is an ordinary open $G\subset V$ with
$\operatorname{Cap}_S(G;V)<\eta$ such that $A\cup G$ is
ordinary open. In particular,
\[
                 \operatorname{Cap}_S^*(A;V)
                              =\operatorname{Cap}_S(A;V).
 \tag{BC17}
\]
If either $\mu_u(A)=0$ or
$\mathbf1_A\mu_u\leq\mathbf1_A\mu_v$, then
\[
                        \operatorname{Cap}_S^*(A;V)=0.
 \tag{BC18}
\]

then $\operatorname{Cap}_S^*(\{u\ne v\};V)=
