first_energy_capacity_topology.tex \section{Quantitative first-energy convergence in every local capacity}
\label{sec:r11-first-energy-capacity-topology}

Retain the strict analytic box, background extension and
$\mathcal E^1$ hypotheses of
Section~\ref{sec:r11-global-first-energy}.
All functions below are actual negative classical members
of that class; all capacities use the full original tester
class. Put $d=q+1$ and $\alpha_q=2^{-q}$.
The symmetric discrepancy $\mathscr I_S$ is (GE18).
At a joint pole, a difference is used only as a Borel
coefficient representative; all involved products and
capacities annihilate that pole union.

The bounded common-collar predecessors are the frozen R3
\texttt{energy\_convex\_blocks.tex},
\texttt{thm:r3-I-capacity}, and
\texttt{strong\_relative\_topology.tex}.
They already contain the positive discrepancy, the mixed
energy transfer recurrence, and bounded relative energy
topologies. The new scope here is the global unbounded
first-energy class, uniform control over its energy testers,
the analytic all-local domain extension, and critical
endpoint continuity without a prescribed common collar.

\begin{theorem}[A uniform first-energy tester estimate]
\label{thm:r11-first-energy-uniform-tester}
For $u,v,\psi\in\mathcal E^1$, put $w=u+v$ and
$M=\max\{e_1(w),e_1(\psi)\}$. Then
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \int_V|u-v|\,d\mu_\psi
   \leq 2^{(q-1)\alpha_q}
          \mathscr I_S(u,v)^{\alpha_q}M^{1-\alpha_q}.
 \quad}
 \tag{EV1}
\]
The conclusion is zero if $M=0$. For a mixed top measure
in place of $\mu_\psi$, the positive expansion of the sum
of its $q$ potentials gives the same estimate divided by
$q!$, with that sum as $\psi$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} in the
unbounded global first-energy class.

\begin{proof}
Write $h=u-v$. For $0\leq k\leq q-1$ set
\[
 J_k=\int_V\Gamma_{N(\psi^{[k]},w^{[q-1-k]})}(h).
 \tag{EV2}
\]
These are finite nonnegative numbers by (GE7). The positive
expansion of $Dw=Du+Dv$ and (GE18) give
$J_0\leq2^{q-1}\mathscr I_S(u,v)$.
For $k\leq q-2$, full mixed energy symmetry exchanges one
$\psi$ slot with one $h$ slot. Expanding that latter
$h=u-v$ in the background gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 J_{k+1}
 &=\int\Gamma_{N(u,\psi^{[k]},w^{[q-2-k]})}(h,\psi)
   -\int\Gamma_{N(v,\psi^{[k]},w^{[q-2-k]})}(h,\psi)\\
 &\leq\left[J_k\,
       \mathcal I_S(\psi^{[k+2]},w^{[q-1-k]})\right]^{1/2}
 \leq(J_kM)^{1/2}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{EV3}
\]
For the middle inequality apply energy Cauchy--Schwarz in
each of the two positive backgrounds and then Cauchy--Schwarz
to the resulting two nonnegative summands. Their first
diagonal masses add to $J_k$, and their second diagonal
masses add to the displayed mixed energy. The last inequality
is the constant-one Holder inequality (GE10). Thus
\[
 J_{q-1}\leq J_0^{2^{-(q-1)}}M^{1-2^{-(q-1)}}.
 \tag{EV4}
\]
When $q=1$ this is just the identity $J_{q-1}=J_0$.

The real-span element
$|h|=2\max(u,v)-u-v$ has the exact energy identity
$\Gamma_Q(|h|)=\Gamma_Q(h)$ for every background $Q$
in (EV2). To justify it in the present class, use canonical
bounded truncations of $u,v,\max(u,v)$ and the background
slots. At level $j$ one has
$\max(u_j,v_j)=\max(\max(u,v),-j)$.
The bounded absolute-value chain and the zero energy of
the level $\{u_j=v_j\}$ prove the identity at that stage.
Endpoint local total-variation convergence (PG11) passes
it to the unbounded currents. Both are already globally
finite by (GE7).

Global Green, followed by Cauchy--Schwarz, now yields
\[
 \int|h|\,d\mu_\psi
  =-\int\Gamma_{N(\psi^{[q-1]})}(|h|,\psi)
       \leq J_{q-1}^{1/2}e_1(\psi)^{1/2}.
 \tag{EV5}
\]
Combine this with (EV4), the bound on $J_0$, and
$e_1(\psi)\leq M$. If $M=0$, the mixed Holder estimate
already makes the integral zero. The mixed-measure
assertion follows from
$q!M(\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_q)\leq\mu_{\sum_i\psi_i}$.
\end{proof}



\begin{theorem}[Quantitative capacity control on every compact/domain pair]
\label{thm:r11-first-energy-all-local-capacity}
Fix a compact $K\Subset V$ and choose $A_K>0$ so that
$A_K\rho<-2$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Set
\[
 B_K=2A_K^q\mu_\rho(V),\qquad
 \Lambda_K(u,v)=\max\{e_1(u+v),B_K\}.
 \tag{EV6}
\]
For $\delta>0$ put
$G_\delta(u,v)=\{u<v-\delta\}\cup\{v<u-\delta\}$,
using actual extended comparisons. Then
\[
 C_S(K\cap G_\delta(u,v);V)
    \leq\frac{2^{(q-1)\alpha_q}}\delta
          \Lambda_K(u,v)^{1-\alpha_q}
                      \mathscr I_S(u,v)^{\alpha_q}.
 \tag{EV7}
\]
If $K\subset\operatorname{Int}_X K'\Subset V$, the same
bound for $K'$ bounds the outer capacity of
$K\cap G_\delta(u,v)$.

Consequently for every ordinary $\Omega\subset V$ and
compact $K\Subset\Omega$, and every $M_0<\infty$, there
is a finite constant $C_{K,\Omega,M_0,S}$ such that
$e_1(u),e_1(v)\leq M_0$ implies
\[
 C_{S|\Omega}^*(K\cap G_\delta(u,v);\Omega)
       \leq\frac{C_{K,\Omega,M_0,S}}\delta
                            \mathscr I_S(u,v)^{\alpha_q}.
 \tag{EV8}
\]
This is the complete all-local capacity topology, by the
proved analytic affinoid domain comparison, not an assumed
identification of two admissibility domains.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as a
global-energy estimate for all original local testers.

\begin{proof}
For a normalized tester $0\leq a\leq1$ on $V$ put
$\psi=\max(a-2,A_K\rho)$.
It is bounded in $[-2,0]$, has compact negative sublevels,
and agrees with $a-2$ near $K$.
Comparison with $cA_K\rho$ for $c>1$ gives
$\mu_\psi(V)\leq A_K^q\mu_\rho(V)$ after $c\downarrow1$.
Thus $\psi\in\mathcal E^1$ and $e_1(\psi)\leq B_K$,
uniformly in the original tester $a$. Ordinary locality
gives $\mathbf1_K\mu_a=\mathbf1_K\mu_\psi$.
The joint pole set has raw capacity zero, so it has zero
mass for $\mu_a$. On its complement, Chebyshev and (EV1)
give
\[
 \mu_a(K\cap G_\delta(u,v))
       \leq\delta^{-1}\int|u-v|\,d\mu_\psi
       \leq\frac{2^{(q-1)\alpha_q}}\delta
             \Lambda_K(u,v)^{1-\alpha_q}
                          \mathscr I_S(u,v)^{\alpha_q}.
\]
Take the full tester supremum to prove (EV7).

To obtain the outer bound, fix $\eta>0$. Outer
quasicontinuity on $K'$ and outer nullity of the poles
give an ordinary open $O$ with $C_S(O;V)<\eta$ such
that both potentials are finite and continuous on
$K'\setminus O$. In the relative space
$\operatorname{Int}_X K'\setminus O$ the strict gap is
open. Hence there is an ordinary open $H\subset
\operatorname{Int}_X K'$ such that
$H\setminus O=G_\delta(u,v)\cap
(\operatorname{Int}_X K'\setminus O)$.
The open set $H\cup O$ covers $K\cap G_\delta$ and is
contained in $(K'\cap G_\delta)\cup O$. Therefore
\[
 C_S^*(K\cap G_\delta;V)
              \leq C_S(K'\cap G_\delta;V)+\eta.
\]
Let $\eta\downarrow0$ and use (EV7) on $K'$.

Finally choose $K'$ inside $\Omega$ and an ordinary open
core containing $K$ compactly in $\Omega$. The outer
domain comparison (AL9) multiplies this estimate by a fixed
geometric constant. Minkowski (GE11) gives
$e_1(u+v)\leq2^{q+1}M_0$, proving (EV8).
No general Borel raw/outer equality is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The strong first-energy topology]
\label{thm:r11-strong-first-energy-topology}
For any $u,v\in\mathcal E^1$,
\[
 \left|e_1(u)^{1/d}-e_1(v)^{1/d}\right|^d
                                      \leq\mathscr I_S(u,v).
 \tag{EV9}
\]
For a sequence $u_j\in\mathcal E^1$ and an actual
$u\in\mathcal E^1$, the following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathscr I_S(u_j,u)\to0$.
\item $u_j\to u$ in all-local truncated original capacity
and $e_1(u_j)\to e_1(u)$.
\end{enumerate}
The forward implication gives outer-capacity convergence
of the full actual gaps on every compact/domain pair.
This theorem describes convergence to an already specified
actual class member; it does not assert classical
representability of every Cauchy sequence.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
unbounded class. The bounded fixed-collar energy topology
was already frozen in R3.

\begin{proof}
Put $a=e_1(u)^{1/d}$ and $b=e_1(v)^{1/d}$.
Expand the definition (GE18), then use the constant-one
mixed Holder inequality on its two cross terms:
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathscr I_S(u,v)
 &=e_1(u)+e_1(v)
       -\mathcal I_S(u,v^{[q]})-\mathcal I_S(v,u^{[q]})\\
 &\geq a^d+b^d-ab^{d-1}-ba^{d-1}
       =(a-b)(a^{d-1}-b^{d-1})\geq|a-b|^d.
 \end{split}
 \tag{EV10}
\]
The last inequality follows by the binomial expansion after
ordering $a,b$. Thus (1) implies energy convergence and a
uniform energy bound. The capacity estimate (EV8) gives
all the asserted forward capacity conclusions.

Conversely suppose (2). In particular the energies are
uniformly bounded. For each bounded weight truncation and
each original compact cutoff, the proved local bounded-weight
capacity continuity gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \liminf_j\mathcal I_S(u_j,u^{[q]})&\geq e_1(u),\\
 \liminf_j\mathcal I_S(u,u_j^{[q]})&\geq e_1(u).
 \end{split}
 \tag{EV11}
\]
Here is the order of limits: first replace the
undifferentiated weight by $-\max(\cdot,-L)$ and insert a
compact nonnegative cutoff; the original bounded-weight
continuity passes $j\to\infty$. Then let the cutoff
increase to one and $L\to\infty$, using positivity.
The derivative slots are controlled by the uniform power
energy hypothesis through the already proved top capacity
stability theorem. Thus neither line presupposes critical
weighted continuity.

The optimal Holder upper bounds are respectively
$e_1(u_j)^{1/d}e_1(u)^{q/d}$ and
$e_1(u)^{1/d}e_1(u_j)^{q/d}$, both tending to $e_1(u)$.
Thus both cross integrals converge to $e_1(u)$.
The first line of (EV10) now proves (1).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Critical mixed energy and weighted-current continuity]
\label{thm:r11-strong-critical-mixed-continuity}
Let $u_{i,j},u_i\in\mathcal E^1$ for $0\leq i\leq q$,
and assume $\mathscr I_S(u_{i,j},u_i)\to0$ for every slot.
Then
\[
 \mathcal I_S(u_{0,j},\ldots,u_{q,j})
                  \longrightarrow\mathcal I_S(u_0,\ldots,u_q),
 \tag{EV12}
\]
and the finite positive measures
\[
 (-u_{0,j})M(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{q,j})
                      \longrightarrow(-u_0)M(u_1,\ldots,u_q)
 \tag{EV13}
\]
converge against every bounded original smooth scalar test
on $V$, including tests without compact support. In
particular there is neither a critical pole residue nor
escaped boundary energy. No common pointwise lower barrier
is required in this statement.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}. The
strong discrepancy hypothesis is substantive; the critical
failure in (PS7) concerns mere capacity convergence with
a uniform energy bound.

\begin{proof}
By (EV9), every slot has uniformly bounded first energy.
Telescope the fully symmetric multilinear integral
$\mathcal I_S$ one slot at a time. Move each changing
slot to the undifferentiated position by (GE5).
The absolute value of that difference is bounded by
$\int|u_{i,j}-u_i|M(\mathbf z_j)$ for a mixed tuple
of unchanged or already changed slots. Its positive
expansion is at most $1/q!$ times the diagonal product
of their sum. That sum has uniformly bounded energy by
(GE11). Estimate (EV1) makes each of the finitely many
differences tend to zero. This proves (EV12).

Write $M_j=M(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{q,j})$ and $M$ for its
limit. The same estimate gives
\[
                  \int|u_{0,j}-u_0|\,dM_j\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{EV14}
\]
For $u=u_0$, put $u^R=\max(u,-R)$. Since $u^R-u\geq0$,
the nonnegative discrepancy satisfies
\[
 0\leq\mathscr I_S(u,u^R)
       =\int(u^R-u)(d\mu_u-d\mu_{u^R})
       \leq\int(u^R-u)\,d\mu_u\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{EV15}
\]
The last limit is dominated convergence against the finite
first-energy weight $(-u)\mu_u$.
Apply (EV1) to $u,u^R$ and to the uniformly bounded-energy
sum of the differentiated slots of $M_j$. This proves
$\sup_j\int|u-u^R|\,dM_j\to0$; the same holds for $M$.
The constants are uniform because $e_1(u^R)\leq e_1(u)$
by energy monotonicity and all other energies are bounded.

For fixed $R$, local bounded-weight capacity continuity
gives $(-u^R)M_j\to(-u^R)M$ on every original compact
scalar test. Use the preceding uniform weight tail and
(EV14) to pass $R\to\infty$. This proves local convergence
in (EV13). Their total masses converge by (EV12).
Positive finite Radon measures with local convergence
and convergent full masses are tight: choose a compact
original cutoff whose integral in the limit is arbitrarily
close to the full limit mass, and pass its local integral.
This controls the complements uniformly for all large $j$.
It follows that every bounded original smooth scalar test,
with no compact-support restriction, has the same limit.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Energy-dual maximizing sequences are strongly Cauchy]
\label{cor:r11-dual-maximizing-Cauchy}
Let $\mu$ be a positive Radon datum with
$D=\mathfrak d_1(\mu)<\infty$ as defined in (DO1).
For $\mathcal F_\mu(u)=\mathscr A_S(u)-\int u\,d\mu$,
\[
 0\leq\sup_{u\in\mathcal E^1}\mathcal F_\mu(u)
               \leq\frac q{q+1}D^{(q+1)/q}<\infty.
 \tag{EV16}
\]
Every maximizing sequence is uniformly bounded in first
energy and is Cauchy for $\mathscr I_S$ and in every local
outer capacity. This does not assert the existence of an
actual classical limit or a classical Dirichlet solution.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as a
compactness estimate in the unbounded nonlinear class;
the representation and equation gates remain explicit.

\begin{proof}
Positive homogeneity and the definition of $D$ give
$\int(-u)\,d\mu\leq D e_1(u)^{1/d}$.
If $e_1(u)=0$, scale $u$ by an arbitrary positive number
in (DO1) to obtain the same zero conclusion.
Thus, with $x=e_1(u)^{1/d}$,
\[
                \mathcal F_\mu(u)\leq-x^d/d+Dx.
\]
Maximizing this real polynomial gives (EV16), and it tends
to $-\infty$ as $x\to\infty$. Since $0$ is admissible,
every tail of a maximizing sequence has
$\mathcal F_\mu(u_j)\geq-1$ and hence
\[
          e_1(u_j)\leq
             \max\{2d,(2dD)^{d/(d-1)}\}.
 \tag{EV17}
\]
Discarding finitely many terms gives uniform energy for
the sequence.

The frozen bounded common-collar midpoint argument now
applies to the proved global variation (GE16), giving
\[
 \mathscr A_S\left(\frac{u+v}2\right)
       -\frac{\mathscr A_S(u)+\mathscr A_S(v)}2
            \geq\frac q{4^{q+1}}\mathscr I_S(u,v).
 \tag{EV18}
\]
For completeness the midpoint Green formula is
$\frac q2\int_0^1\min(t,1-t)
 \int\Gamma_{N(u_t^{q-1})}(u-v)\,dt$.
On $[1/4,3/4]$, positive mixed expansion bounds its
energy integrand below by $4^{-(q-1)}\mathscr I_S(u,v)$.
The interval length and the scalar weight give exactly
the constant in (EV18). All global energy integrals
are finite by (GE7).

The datum integral is affine, so it cancels in the midpoint
gap. If $L=\sup\mathcal F_\mu$, then
\[
 \frac q{4^{q+1}}\mathscr I_S(u_j,u_l)
        \leq L-\frac{\mathcal F_\mu(u_j)+
                              \mathcal F_\mu(u_l)}2\longrightarrow0.
\]
The uniform energy bound and (EV8) give the all-local
outer-capacity Cauchy conclusion. Producing an actual
classical representative of that completed class, and
valid admissible variations that identify its curvature
with the datum, are not proved by this argument. The
compact-source obstruction (DO9) prevents omitting those
gates in a universal classical existence assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Strong first-energy convergence controls every graded endpoint]
\label{cor:r11-strong-first-energy-graded-endpoints}
Let $u_{i,j},u_i\in\mathcal E^1$ be a finite family with
$\mathscr I_S(u_{i,j},u_i)\to0$ in every slot. For
$w_j=\sum_i u_{i,j}$ one has
\[
 \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_j\int_R^\infty
                 t^q C_S(\{w_j<-t\};V)\,dt=0.
 \tag{EV19}
\]
Consequently all three convergence assertions (GS3), and
the double-prime first-order assertion, hold with
$\sigma=1$ and weak inequalities in their degree/weight
conditions. They hold on every original compact
complementary test and every actual moment refinement,
without a common pointwise lower barrier. These are

title: Relative Perron envelopes of arbitrary strong completed families
text:
strong_completed_perron.tex \section{Relative Perron envelopes of arbitrary strong completed families}
\label{sec:r11-strong-completed-Perron}

Retain exactly the strict analytic box, background extension
and full strong first-energy class of
Section~\ref{sec:r11-strong-completed-comparison}.
The background is the unchanged arbitrary original symmetric
middle-positive separately closed $S$.
Write $f\preceq g$ if $f\leq g$ locally outside an
ordinary-open outer $S$-capacity-null set. This order concerns
the completed Borel representatives. No ordinary ambient
upper regularization is used.

The frozen R2 relative capacitary envelope theorem is
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT} in its bounded scope. Theorem
\ref{thm:r11-barrier-relative-Perron} extends an actual family
above one prescribed actual power-energy barrier. The theorem
below instead permits an arbitrary nonempty family of strong
completed first-energy potentials, with no common actual lower
barrier. Its countable selection is proved directly by global
energy minimization over finite maxima.

\begin{theorem}[The full strong completed relative envelope]
\label{thm:r11-strong-completed-Perron}
Let $\mathscr F\subset\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_{\rm str}(V)$
be any nonempty family, possibly uncountable. Let
$\mathscr F^\vee$ consist of all nonempty finite maxima of
its members, and put
\[
                    L=\inf_{w\in\mathscr F^\vee}\widehat e(w).
 \tag{SE1}
\]
There is a unique relative class
$H\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_{\rm str}(V)$ with the following
least-upper-bound properties:
\[
 \begin{split}
 &f\preceq H\qquad(f\in\mathscr F),\\
 &\bigl[f\preceq g\text{ for every }f\in\mathscr F,
                      \ g\text{ Borel}\bigr]
                                      \Longrightarrow H\preceq g.
 \end{split}
 \tag{SE2}
\]
The exceptional set in the first line may depend on $f$;
there is no uncountable-union nullity assertion.

There are countably many selected members of $\mathscr F$
whose cumulative finite maxima $v_j$ satisfy
\[
                  v_j\uparrow H,\qquad
                  \widehat I(v_j,H)\longrightarrow0,
                  \widehat e(H)=L.
 \tag{SE3}
\]
Here the actual increasing Borel limit may be used as the
representative of $H$. More generally, every sequence
$w_j\in\mathscr F^\vee$ with $\widehat e(w_j)\to L$
converges strongly to $H$ and therefore has all the critical
current and mixed-energy limits (IC11)--(IC13).
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for arbitrary
completed families and their full energy boundary class.

\begin{proof}
Finite maxima are members of the strong completion by (CC1).
Their energies are nonnegative, and one fixed family member
has finite energy. Thus $0\leq L<\infty$.
Choose $w_j\in\mathscr F^\vee$ with
$\widehat e(w_j)\leq L+1/j$, and put
\[
                            v_j=\max(w_1,\ldots,w_j).
 \tag{SE4}
\]
Each is still a finite maximum of members of the given family.
It increases with $j$, and energy monotonicity gives
$L\leq\widehat e(v_j)\leq\widehat e(w_j)$.
The increasing-closure theorem
\ref{cor:r11-strong-monotone-closure} therefore gives its
actual Borel limit $H$ in the strong completion, with strong
convergence and $\widehat e(H)=L$.
Only countably many members of the given family occur in all the
selected $w_j$; this proves the countable assertion in (SE3).

Fix an arbitrary $f\in\mathscr F$ and set $z_j=\max(v_j,f)$.
Then $z_j\in\mathscr F^\vee$ and
\[
                       L\leq\widehat e(z_j)
                                      \leq\widehat e(v_j).
\]
The strong maximum continuity (CC2) gives
$z_j\to z:=\max(H,f)$ strongly. Hence
$\widehat e(z)=L=\widehat e(H)$.
Since $H\leq z$, the ordered discrepancy estimate (CI1)
gives
\[
               0\leq\widehat I(H,z)
                      \leq\widehat e(H)-\widehat e(z)=0.
 \tag{SE5}
\]
Separation of the completed classes implies $z=H$
locally outside an outer-null set. Thus $f\preceq H$.
This argument fixes one $f$ at a time, as required by (SE2).

Now let $g$ be any Borel upper bound in the sense of the
second line of (SE2). It bounds each of the countably many
selected family members outside its corresponding null set.
Their countable union is locally outer-null. Off that union,
$g$ bounds every $v_j$ and hence their actual pointwise
limit $H$. This proves leastness among Borel upper bounds,
without requiring $g$ to be psh or completed.
Two such least upper bounds bound each other, so their
relative classes agree.

Finally, every $w\in\mathscr F^\vee$ satisfies $w\preceq H$,
by the first line of (SE2) and finite subadditivity.
For any sequence whose energies tend to $L$, (CI1) gives
\[
             0\leq\widehat I(w_j,H)
                    \leq\widehat e(w_j)-\widehat e(H)
                                      \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{SE6}
\]
The strong continuity theorem supplies all the current and
critical weighted-measure limits claimed in the statement.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Subsolution envelopes and Borel upper constraints]
\label{cor:r11-strong-Perron-subsolution}
Let $\nu$ be a fixed positive Radon measure on $V$ and
$\psi$ a Borel upper constraint. If the preceding nonempty
family satisfies
\[
                    \widehat\mu_f\geq\nu,
                    \qquad f\preceq\psi
                                  \quad(f\in\mathscr F),
 \tag{SE7}
\]
then its canonical relative envelope satisfies
\[
                             \widehat\mu_H\geq\nu,
                             \qquad H\preceq\psi.
 \tag{SE8}
\]
The current inequality holds on every original compact smooth
scalar test and every actual moment refinement. A finite total
mass for $\nu$ is not needed; the printed Radon hypothesis is
local. No equality $\widehat\mu_H=\nu$ or contact support
assertion is inferred.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for full strong
completed subsolution families; it is a consequence of the
new finite-maximum and envelope theorems.

\begin{proof}
The completed weak maximum inequality, proved with its full
middle-positive cone and equality-side mass, shows that every
finite maximum of members of $\mathscr F$ has top measure at
least $\nu$. In particular $\widehat\mu_{v_j}\geq\nu$ for
the selected increasing sequence (SE4).
Its strong convergence passes every original compact scalar
test, so positivity gives $\widehat\mu_H\geq\nu$.
All measures are locally Radon; no global mass subtraction
or unproved boundary tightness is needed for this inequality.
The least-upper-bound property (SE2), or the countable selected
members directly, gives $H\preceq\psi$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The distinction from an ambient Perron construction.}
This theorem supplies a canonical relative least upper bound
and a retained source lower bound inside the complete strong
class. The ordinary upper semicontinuous envelope can still
lose the relative mass, as in the all-power counterexample
(PO1)--(PO7). Moreover the exact strong completed compact-source
obstruction (SO1)--(SO6) prevents promoting (SE8) to a universal
source equation. These are separate issues from the proved
existence of this Borel relative envelope. General raw-capacity
outer regularity, unrestricted ordinary-boundary Dirichlet
existence, GQ and low-real-degree CTO remain outside the claim.

title: A complete barrier-constrained nonlinear variational problem
text:
completed_barrier_variational_problem.tex \section{A complete barrier-constrained nonlinear variational problem}
\label{sec:r11-completed-barrier-variational}

Retain the strict analytic box and background extension
(TC1)--(TC2), with the original arbitrary symmetric
middle-positive separately closed $(p,p)$-current $S$.
Set $q=n-p\geq1$, $d=q+1$, and fix an actual
$a\in\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(V)$.
Write $\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a$ for the Borel relative
completion of Definition~\ref{def:r11-barrier-completion}.
The background remains $S$; only the potential class
is enlarged by the stated capacity completion.

The frozen predecessor is R4
\path{completed_variational_retraction.tex}.
It treats a bounded completed problem with a fixed
collar, and already distinguishes its constrained
variational condition from an arbitrary source equation.
The result here is an unbounded global first-energy
problem with one actual power-energy lower barrier,
using the new critical continuity and sharp midpoint
modulus.  It does not claim a new bounded Hilbert
projection theorem.

\subsection{Global geometry in the completed order interval}

For completed potentials with actual first-energy
lower barriers, define
\[
\begin{split}
 \widehat B(u_0,\ldots,u_q)
    &=\int_V(-u_0)\widehat N(u_1,\ldots,u_q),\\
 \widehat e(u)&=\widehat B(u^{[q+1]}),\qquad
 \widehat A(u)=-\widehat e(u)/d,\\
 \widehat I(u,v)
    &=\widehat e(u)+\widehat e(v)
       -\widehat B(u,v^{[q]})-\widehat B(v,u^{[q]}).
\end{split}
 \tag{BV1}
\]
The integrals are finite by (RC14).  They use the
actual Borel multipliers, with the joint pole set
annihilated by every coefficient.

\begin{lemma}[Completed energy geometry and separation]
\label{lem:r11-completed-first-energy-geometry}
The form $\widehat B$ is symmetric, nonnegative and
multilinear on the completed positive cone.
The function $\widehat A$ is concave along every
segment, and
\[
 \widehat A\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)
      -\frac{\widehat A(u)+\widehat A(v)}2
                    \geq c_q\widehat I(u,v)\geq0,
 \qquad c_q=\frac{1-2^{-q}}{2(q+1)}.
 \tag{BV2}
\]
Moreover
\[
 \widehat I(u,v)=0
       \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 u=v\text{ locally outside a set of outer }S
                         \text{-capacity zero}.
 \tag{BV3}
\]
On $\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a$ one has
$0\leq\widehat e(u)\leq e_1(a)$.
For a segment $u_t=(1-t)u+tv$,
\[
             \frac{d}{dt}\widehat A(u_t)
                    =\int_V(v-u)\,d\widehat N_q(u_t).
 \tag{BV4}
\]
All signed integrals in this formula are absolutely
convergent.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}}
of the new global critical completion theorem,
the actual first-energy geometry and its sharp
midpoint estimate.  The separation assertion is
proved explicitly to avoid assuming an ambient
classical representative.

\begin{proof}
Choose classical defining rows for all the
finitely many completed slots, retaining their
fixed actual barriers.  Formula (RC14) passes
each global mixed energy and every diagonal
energy to its completed value.  It therefore
passes symmetry, positive multilinearity,
the constant-one Holder inequality, concavity,
and (SM8).  For $u\geq a$, choose its defining
rows above $a$.  Actual energy monotonicity
gives $e_1(u_l)\leq e_1(a)$, and (RC14)
gives the stated bound.

If $\widehat I(u,v)=0$, the same convergence
gives $I(u_l,v_l)\to0$ for their classical
defining rows.  These rows have uniformly
bounded energy.  The all-local outer-capacity
estimate (EV8) makes every actual gap between
$u_l$ and $v_l$ tend to zero in capacity.
The defining convergence of each clipped row,
and the capacity-small deep sublevels of the
fixed barriers, give the same conclusion for
the completed gap.  The level-set triangle
inequality then makes each positive gap of
$u-v$ outer-null.  A countable union proves
the forward implication of (BV3).
Conversely, outer-null changes preserve every
completed current and every actual integrable
multiplier by (RC4)--(RC8), so the expression
in (BV1) is zero.

Finally positive multilinearity makes
$\widehat A(u_t)$ a finite polynomial in $t$.
Differentiate its $d$ symmetric slots.
This is (BV4), with integrability from the
completed mixed-energy bound.  No distributional
product of two unbounded differences is being
introduced by this scalar calculation.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Finite diffuse data integrate barrier-bounded capacity limits]
\label{lem:r11-barrier-diffuse-integration}
Let $\mu$ be a finite positive Radon measure on $V$
which vanishes on every Borel set of zero ordinary-open
outer $S$-capacity.  Suppose
\[
                              \int_V(-a)\,d\mu<\infty.
 \tag{BV5}
\]
If $u_j,u\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a$ converge in the
defining local truncated outer capacities, then
\[
                           \int_V|u_j-u|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{BV6}
\]
In particular this integral is independent of the
chosen relative representatives.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}
in the unbounded barrier completion; the underlying
finite-measure capacity argument is detailed below.

\begin{proof}
A finite measure that vanishes on outer-null Borel
sets is sequentially absolutely continuous for this
outer capacity.  Otherwise choose Borel $E_j$ with
capacities tending to zero but $\mu(E_j)\geq\epsilon$,
and pass to a subsequence with summable capacities.
The limsup has outer capacity zero by countable
subadditivity.  On the other hand, continuity from
above of the finite measure applied to the decreasing
tail unions gives its mass at least $\epsilon$.
This is a contradiction.

The actual pole set of $a$ is outer-null and hence
$\mu$-null.  Off it the inequalities
$a\leq u_j,u\leq0$ imply
$|u_j-u|\leq-a$.
On a fixed compact set remove a deep sublevel of $a$;
its capacity and hence its $\mu$ mass can be made
small.  On the complement full values agree with
one fixed truncation, whose convergence in capacity
and the preceding sequential absolute continuity
give convergence in $\mu$ measure.
Exhaust $V$ by compact sets and use finiteness of
$\mu$ to obtain convergence in measure on all of $V$.
The integrable bound $-a$ in (BV5) then gives
$L^1(\mu)$ convergence: every subsequence has an
almost-everywhere convergent further subsequence,
and dominated convergence applies to it.
This proves (BV6) for the whole sequence.
The same null-set argument proves representative
independence.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A unique completed barrier-constrained maximizer]
\label{thm:r11-completed-barrier-maximizer}
For every datum satisfying Lemma
\ref{lem:r11-barrier-diffuse-integration}, the functional
\[
      \widehat{\mathcal F}_\mu(u)
            =\widehat A(u)-\int_Vu\,d\mu,
              \qquad u\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a,
 \tag{BV7}
\]
has a maximizer, unique modulo local outer
$S$-capacity zero.  Its value lies between zero
and $\int(-a)\,d\mu$.
Denote its relative class by $\Pi_a(\mu)$.
Every classical maximizing sequence in the
actual interval $\{a\leq u\leq0\}$ is Cauchy
in all local outer capacities and converges to
this completed class.
The maximizer is characterized by the precise
variational inequality
\[
 \int_V(v-u)\,d\bigl(\widehat N_q(u)-\mu\bigr)
               \leq0
       \quad\bigl(v\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a,\ u=\Pi_a(\mu)\bigr).
 \tag{BV8}
\]
The inequality is equivalent to maximality, and
all its integrals are absolutely convergent.
It is not asserted to be the unrestricted
current equation $\widehat N_q(u)=\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}
for the unbounded completed order interval and
arbitrary original $S$.

\begin{proof}
The zero potential is admissible and has functional
value zero.  Since $\widehat e(u)\geq0$ and
$-u\leq-a$, every value in (BV7) is at most
$\int(-a)\,d\mu<\infty$.
For any completed $u$ its classical defining
rows converge in energy by (RC14) and in
$L^1(\mu)$ by (BV6).
Thus the supremum over the completed interval
equals the supremum over its actual classical
members.

Choose a classical sequence approaching this
finite supremum $L$.
Every term has first energy at most $e_1(a)$.
The midpoint remains in the same actual interval.
Its linear datum term cancels from the midpoint
gap, so (SM8) gives
\[
 c_q I(u_j,u_l)
       \leq L-\frac{\mathcal F_\mu(u_j)+
                              \mathcal F_\mu(u_l)}2\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{BV9}
\]
The local capacity estimate (EV8) makes the
sequence Cauchy in the defining topology.
The fixed-barrier completeness theorem gives
a limit $u\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a$.
Global critical energy continuity (RC14) and
(BV6) give
$\widehat{\mathcal F}_\mu(u)=L$.
This proves existence without an ambient upper
regularization or a classical compactness claim.

If $u,v$ are both maximizers, (BV2) and the
affinity of the datum integral give
$c_q\widehat I(u,v)\leq0$.
By (BV3) they are the same relative class.
The same Cauchy argument and uniqueness apply
to every classical maximizing sequence.

For any completed competitor $v$, the segment
$u_t=(1-t)u+tv$ stays in the interval.
The derivative at $t=0$ is the left side of
(BV8), by (BV4) and (BV6).
Maximality gives its nonpositive sign.
Conversely concavity gives the upper tangent
inequality for (BV7); (BV8) therefore makes
every competitor's value at most the value
at $u$.  The data integrals are controlled
by (BV5), and all curvature integrals by
the completed mixed-energy bound.
This proves both the characterization and
the claimed integrability.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Data stability and retraction on the finite-mass image]
\label{thm:r11-completed-barrier-data-stability}
Let $\mu,\nu$ satisfy (BV5) and the same
finite BT-diffuse hypotheses, and define
\[
                    \delta_a(\mu,\nu)
                         =\int_V(-a)\,d|\mu-\nu|.
 \tag{BV10}
\]
Then
\[
 \widehat I(\Pi_a(\mu),\Pi_a(\nu))
       \leq\delta_a(\mu,\nu).
 \tag{BV11}
\]
In particular, if $\delta_a(\mu_j,\mu)\to0$,
the completed maximizers converge in every
local outer capacity, every original mixed
current, and all the fixed-barrier weighted
limits of (RC8) and (RC14).

If $b\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a$ and its top
measure $\mu_b=\widehat N_q(b)$ has finite
total mass, then it satisfies the stated
datum hypotheses and
\[
                                \Pi_a(\mu_b)=b
 \tag{BV12}
\]
in the relative capacity quotient.
If the actual barrier has finite total top mass
and positive first energy, the constant one
in (BV11) is optimal for that same barrier,
domain and background.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}
for the quantitative completed variational map.
The term retraction means exactly (BV12).

\begin{proof}
Write $u=\Pi_a(\mu)$ and $w=\Pi_a(\nu)$.
Use $w$ as a competitor in (BV8) for $u$,
and $u$ as a competitor for $w$.
Adding the two resulting inequalities gives
\[
 0\leq\widehat I(u,w)
       \leq\int_V(u-w)\,d(\nu-\mu)
       \leq\int_V(-a)\,d|\nu-\mu|.
\]
The last inequality uses $|u-w|\leq-a$.
This proves (BV11).  The two-competitor argument
is the frozen bounded retraction mechanism;
the newly justified unbounded integrals and
completed interval make it applicable here.

For clarity, the passage from $\widehat I\to0$
to local capacity convergence is also valid
for completed rows.  Approximate each pair
by classical rows with their fixed barrier.
Their energies and discrepancies converge
by (RC14).  Apply (EV8) to the classical
rows, use the level-set triangle inequality
and the defining capacity convergence, and
then decrease its intermediate gap threshold
to the requested one.  The resulting bound
is the same fixed-interval capacity modulus.
Thus (BV11) gives the stated convergence,
and (RC8), (RC14) give all the current
and weighted conclusions.

For (BV12), outer-capacity control of the
completed current on each compact stage
shows that $\mu_b$ is BT diffuse.
Also
$\int(-a)\,d\mu_b=\widehat B(a,b^{[q]})<\infty$.
Its finite total mass is the printed
additional assumption.
The completed tangent inequality for
$\widehat A$ gives
\[
 \widehat A(v)-\widehat A(b)
                    \leq\int(v-b)\,d\mu_b .
\]
Thus $b$ maximizes (BV7) for datum $\mu_b$.
Uniqueness proves (BV12).
Finally, if $\mu_a$ has finite total mass and
$e_1(a)>0$, take $\mu=\mu_a$ and $\nu=0$.
The retraction identity gives $\Pi_a(\mu_a)=a$,
and $\Pi_a(0)=0$ because the objective is
$-\widehat e/d\leq0$.
Then
$\widehat I(a,0)=e_1(a)=\delta_a(\mu_a,0)$,
proving the stated optimality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A completed variational maximizer need not solve the source equation]
\label{prop:r11-completed-maximizer-source-obstruction}
For the precise smooth moment-Laplacian background
(DO6), with $n\geq2$ and $q=1$, take the
nonzero compact smooth source (DO9).
For every actual
$a\in\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(V)$, the
maximizer $\Pi_a(\mu)$ exists, but
\[
                            D(\Pi_a(\mu)\,S)\ne\mu .
 \tag{BV13}
\]
More generally no member of
$\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_a$ has that source.
Thus the implication from completed variational
maximality to an unrestricted original source
equation is \texttt{FALSE}, even after the
classical representative requirement is relaxed
to this relative completion.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}
as the extension of the frozen compact-source
obstruction to the new barrier completion.
It refines the earlier actual-class obstruction
without replacing its proof.

\begin{proof}
The datum (DO9) is finite and dominated by a
fixed multiple of the full normalized BT
capacity, so it is BT diffuse.
Equation (DO4), with $s=1$ and $v=a$,
gives $\int(-a)\,d\mu<\infty$.
The existence theorem therefore applies.

Suppose a completed member $u$ had
$D(uS)=\mu$, and choose classical defining
rows $a\leq u_j\leq0$.
Their Gauss traces $g_j=u_j\circ\sigma$
are finite convex functions on the real
box $Q$, by the frozen trace theorem.
The actual barrier has a finite convex
Gauss trace on all of $Q$, by the
finite-trace argument in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:r11-power-compact-source-obstruction}.
Hence on every compact subbox the $g_j$
have uniform upper and lower bounds.
Elementary convex slope bounds give
equicontinuity on each smaller compact
subbox.  A diagonal finite-net argument
therefore supplies a subsequence converging
locally uniformly to a finite convex $g$.

The completed weighted current convergence
in degree zero gives $u_jS\to uS$ on
every original compact test.
For each real $\phi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$,
the exact original calibration now yields
\[
 \langle t_*D(uS),\phi\rangle
     =\lim_j\int_Q g_j\Delta\phi\,dy
     =\int_Q g\Delta\phi\,dy
     =\langle\Delta g,\phi\rangle.
 \tag{BV14}
\]
The purported source has compact tropical
support.  The frozen R10 convex compact-source
rigidity makes $g$ affine and $\Delta g=0$.
Equation (BV14) would therefore give
$t_*\mu=0$, contradicting the nonzero
positive source (DO9).
This proves (BV13) throughout the completed
interval.
It uses the full-original degree-zero
convergence before testing the pushforward;
no toric-only definition of the currents
or auxiliary-field quotient is substituted.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The remaining equation gate is concrete.}
The theorem proves existence, uniqueness, source
stability and a retraction for a nonlinear
constrained relative problem.
Its Euler condition is exactly (BV8).
Promoting that inequality to equality against
every original test requires additional
admissible variations or a different potential
class.  Proposition
\ref{prop:r11-completed-maximizer-source-obstruction}
shows that this promotion is not a technical
consequence of the completion already built.
The finite signed diffuse relative linear
Dirichlet problem uses the larger specified
energy class and remains compatible with
this obstruction.

title: The energy obstacle map and its contact defect
text:
energy_obstacles_and_contact_defects.tex \section{The energy obstacle map and its contact defect}
\label{sec:r12-energy-obstacles}

Keep exactly the strict original analytic Laurent box and background
extension \textup{(ED1)}.  Thus $S$ remains an arbitrary original
symmetric CLD middle-positive separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed
$(p,p)$-current, $q=n-p\ge1$, and $d=q+1$.  No factorization of
$S$ is imposed in this section.  Write
\[
 \mathscr C=\widehat{\mathcal E}^{1}_{\rm str}(V),\qquad
 \mathbb D_S=\mathscr C-\mathscr C,\qquad
 r(u)=e(u)^{1/d},\qquad E(u)=e(u)/d.
 \tag{OC1}
\]
The Banach norm $\|\cdot\|_{\rm ed}$, its literal Borel
realization, and the curvature functional
$J(u)(h)=-\int h\,d\widehat\mu_u$ are the proved R12
\textup{(ED2)--(ED11)}.  Their proof does not use the obstacle
map constructed below.  The R11 strong relative Perron theorem
\textup{(SE1)--(SE6)} is an \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}.
All orders are relative Borel orders modulo local ordinary-open
outer $S$-capacity zero, denoted by $\preceq$.  All measures are
the original measures on the full original test sheaf.

\begin{definition}[An obstacle in the energy-difference space]
\label{def:r12-energy-obstacle}
For $f\in\mathbb D_S$ put
\[
 P(f)=\sup_{\rm rel}\{v\in\mathscr C:v\preceq f\},
 \qquad \mathfrak E(f)=E(P(f)).
 \tag{OC2}
\]
The supremum is the R11 relative least upper bound among Borel
classes.  It is not the ordinary upper semicontinuous
regularization of a pointwise supremum.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[A global obstacle map and quantitative continuity]
\label{thm:r12-global-energy-obstacle}
The definition is valid for every $f\in\mathbb D_S$.  Its value
$P(f)$ is the greatest member of $\mathscr C$ below $f$, and
\[
 P(f)\preceq f,\qquad P(u)=u\quad(u\in\mathscr C),\qquad
 r(P(f))\le\|f\|_{\rm ed}.
 \tag{OC3}
\]
The map $P$ is order preserving, positively homogeneous and
superadditive in the relative order, hence order concave.
For $f,g\in\mathbb D_S$, set
$R=\max(r(P(f)),r(P(g)))$.  Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 |r(P(f))-r(P(g))|&\le\|f-g\|_{\rm ed},\\
 I(P(f),P(g))&\le R^q\|f-g\|_{\rm ed},\\
 \|J(P(f))-J(P(g))\|_*
       &\le\sqrt q\,R^{(2q-1)/2}\|f-g\|_{\rm ed}^{1/2}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{OC4}
\]
At $R=0$ the second and third left sides are zero.  In
particular, norm convergence of obstacles gives strong
convergence of their envelopes and dual-norm convergence of
their original curvature functionals.  Norm continuity of
$P$ with values in $\mathbb D_S$ is not claimed.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
global energy-difference obstacle domain and its quantitative
estimates, in every degree and for arbitrary original $S$.

\begin{proof}
Write $f=a-b$ with $a,b\in\mathscr C$.  Since $b\preceq0$,
one has $a\preceq f$.  The family in \textup{(OC2)} is therefore
nonempty.  R11 \textup{(SE2)} gives its relative envelope in
$\mathscr C$ and keeps it below the Borel upper constraint $f$.
Thus the envelope itself belongs to the family and is its
greatest member.  In particular $P(u)=u$ on the cone.
Energy monotonicity gives $r(P(f))\le r(a)$; infimizing over
decompositions proves the last assertion of \textup{(OC3)}.

Increasing the obstacle increases its competitor family.
Positive rescaling maps competitor families bijectively onto
each other, and $P(0)=0$ handles scale zero.  Also
$P(f)+P(g)\in\mathscr C$ lies below $f+g$, proving
superadditivity and hence concavity.

For the estimates write $f-g=a-b$, $a,b\in\mathscr C$, and
put $u=P(f)$, $v=P(g)$.  Since
\[
 u+b\preceq f+b=g+a\preceq g,\qquad
 v+a\preceq g+a=f+b\preceq f,
\]
both are legitimate cone competitors.  Consequently
\[
                        a\preceq u-v\preceq-b.
 \tag{OC5}
\]
In particular $u\succeq v+a$ and $v\succeq u+b$.
Energy monotonicity and Minkowski give
$r(u)\le r(v)+r(a)$ and $r(v)\le r(u)+r(b)$.
Infimizing proves the first estimate in \textup{(OC4)}.

The literal mixed integrals and \textup{(OC5)} give the sharper
signed estimate, without inserting an absolute-variation norm,
\[
 \begin{split}
 I(u,v)&=J(u)(u-v)-J(v)(u-v)\\
       &\le J(u)(a)+J(v)(b)\\
       &\le r(a)r(u)^q+r(b)r(v)^q
        \le R^q(r(a)+r(b)).
 \end{split}
 \tag{OC6}
\]
Taking the infimum gives the second estimate.  Combine it with
the proved integrated Cauchy--Schwarz bound
$\|J(u)-J(v)\|_*\le\sqrt q R^{(q-1)/2}I(u,v)^{1/2}$
to obtain the third.  The bound in \textup{(OC3)} controls
$R$ on a norm-convergent obstacle row.  All subsequent
strong current and weighted limits are therefore the full
original limits of R11, not only selected moment pairings.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[A finite convex obstacle energy]
\label{prop:r12-convex-obstacle-energy}
The function $\mathfrak E:\mathbb D_S\to[0,\infty)$ is
finite, convex, order decreasing and positively homogeneous
of degree $d$.  It is locally Lipschitz, with the precise bound
\[
       |\mathfrak E(f)-\mathfrak E(g)|
           \le\max(r(P(f)),r(P(g)))^q\|f-g\|_{\rm ed}.
 \tag{OC7}
\]
Its restriction to $\mathscr C$ is the original first energy
$e/d$.  Its convexity is a statement on all of $\mathbb D_S$;
it does not declare the polynomial extension $B(f^{[d]})/d$
convex outside the potential cone.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}.

\begin{proof}
Finiteness, order decrease and homogeneity follow from
\textup{(OC3)} and the corresponding cone energy properties.
For $0\le s\le1$, the order concavity of $P$ gives
\[
 P((1-s)f+sg)\succeq(1-s)P(f)+sP(g).
\]
Apply energy monotonicity, followed by convexity of $E$ on
the cone, to obtain convexity of $\mathfrak E$.  Finally,
$|x^d-y^d|/d\le\max(x,y)^{d-1}|x-y|$ for $x,y\ge0$.
Use the first line of \textup{(OC4)} and $d-1=q$ to obtain
\textup{(OC7)}.  The norm bound \textup{(OC3)} makes this a
local Lipschitz estimate on the entire Banach space.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Contact defects and exact subgradients}

Call a continuous linear functional $\ell\in\mathbb D_S^*$
\emph{order reversing} if $h\succeq0$ implies $\ell(h)\le0$.
This is order on Borel scalar differences, not an identification
of positivity cones for differential forms.  Every literal
positive measure datum $\ell_\mu(h)=-\int h\,d\mu$ with finite
integrals and a continuous extension to $\mathbb D_S$ has this
property.  Write
\[
 \partial\mathfrak E(f)=\{\ell\in\mathbb D_S^*:
 \mathfrak E(g)\ge\mathfrak E(f)+\ell(g-f)
                      \text{ for every }g\in\mathbb D_S\}
 \tag{OC8}
\]
for the Banach subdifferential, and retain the cone polar
$\mathscr C^\circ$ of \textup{(NI5)}.

\begin{definition}[Relative contact defect]
\label{def:r12-relative-contact-defect}
For $f\in\mathbb D_S$, with $u=P(f)$, put
\[
 \mathfrak Q(f)=\int_V(f-u)\,d\widehat\mu_u
                         =J(u)(u-f)\ge0.
 \tag{OC9}
\]
The integral is literal and finite: $f-u$ is a finite sum of
cone differences, and all its absolute mixed first-energy
integrals are finite.  Its nonnegativity uses $u\preceq f$
and the fact that the original completed measure ignores the
relative null set.  Vanishing means the relative Borel
contact identity
$(f-u)\widehat\mu_u=0$; no ordinary support regularity is
part of this definition.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The obstacle subdifferential and contact criterion]
\label{thm:r12-obstacle-subdifferential}
Let $f\in\mathbb D_S$ and $u=P(f)$.  A functional
$\ell\in\mathbb D_S^*$ belongs to $\partial\mathfrak E(f)$
if and only if all three conditions hold:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \ell\text{ is order reversing},\\
 \ell-J(u)\in\mathscr C^\circ,
                   \qquad (\ell-J(u))(u)=0,\\
                         \ell(f-u)=0.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{OC10}
\]
Every such functional has $\|\ell\|_*=r(u)^q$.
In particular,
\[
       \boxed{\quad J(P(f))\in\partial\mathfrak E(f)
                        \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
                         \mathfrak Q(f)=0.\quad}
 \tag{OC11}
\]
For $u\in\mathscr C$, one always has
$J(u)\in\partial\mathfrak E(u)$.

If $\ell$ is additionally in the strong-continuous dual
$\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*$, the middle line of
\textup{(OC10)} is equivalent to $u=\Pi(\ell)$ by the
proved R12 normal-decomposition theorem.  Strong continuity
is not being asserted for every Banach subgradient.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
precise original arbitrary-background obstacle energy.  This is
a contact/variational characterization; it does not assert
that the contact defect vanishes.

\begin{proof}
Suppose first that $\ell\in\partial\mathfrak E(f)$.
For $h\succeq0$ and $t>0$, order decrease gives
$\mathfrak E(f+th)\le\mathfrak E(f)$.  The subgradient
inequality then gives $t\ell(h)\le0$, proving order reversal.
Since $P(u)=u$ and $E(u)=\mathfrak E(f)$, the competitor
$g=u$ in \textup{(OC8)} gives $\ell(u-f)\le0$.
But $u-f\preceq0$ and order reversal give the opposite
inequality.  Hence $\ell(f-u)=0$.

Restricting \textup{(OC8)} to $v\in\mathscr C$ now gives
\[
                        E(v)\ge E(u)+\ell(v-u).
 \tag{OC12}
\]
Along the cone segment $u+t(v-u)$ the polynomial energy
has derivative $J(u)(v-u)$ at zero.  Applying
\textup{(OC12)}, dividing by $t>0$ and letting $t\downarrow0$
gives $(\ell-J(u))(v-u)\le0$.  The competitors $0$ and
$2u$ yield $(\ell-J(u))(u)=0$, and then the same inequality
is the polar condition.  This proves necessity.

Conversely assume \textup{(OC10)}.  Cone convexity and its
first derivative give
\[
 E(v)\ge E(u)+J(u)(v-u)\ge E(u)+\ell(v-u)
                                     \quad(v\in\mathscr C).
\]
For arbitrary $g\in\mathbb D_S$ use $v=P(g)\preceq g$.
Order reversal gives $\ell(P(g)-u)\ge\ell(g-u)$, so
\[
 \mathfrak E(g)\ge E(u)+\ell(g-u)
                 =\mathfrak E(f)+\ell(g-f).
\]
The equality uses $\ell(f-u)=0$.  This proves sufficiency.

Order reversal makes $\ell(v)\ge0$ on the nonpositive cone.
The polar condition gives
$0\le\ell(v)\le J(u)(v)\le r(v)r(u)^q$.
The exact dual norm formula \textup{(ED10)} proves
$\|\ell\|_*\le r(u)^q$.  If $u\ne0$, evaluation on
$u/r(u)$ gives equality because $\ell(u)=e(u)$.
For $u=0$, the upper bound gives the same conclusion.
Finally $J(u)$ is order reversing, its normal residual is
zero, and its last condition in \textup{(OC10)} is exactly
$-\mathfrak Q(f)=0$.  This proves \textup{(OC11)} and
the assertion at cone points.  The final equivalence is
precisely the already proved normal-decomposition theorem
with its stated continuity gate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Zero-mass slack does not move a cone envelope]
\label{cor:r12-zero-mass-obstacle-slack}
If $u\in\mathscr C$, $g\in\mathbb D_S$, $g\succeq0$, and
$\int g\,d\widehat\mu_u=0$, then
$P(u+g)=u$ and $\mathfrak Q(u+g)=0$.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of
the frozen ordered energy separation and the new obstacle definition.
It is recorded as a valid nontrivial contact mechanism, not as
unrestricted orthogonality.

\begin{proof}
Put $v=P(u+g)$.  Then $u\preceq v\preceq u+g$.
Thus $\int(v-u)\,d\widehat\mu_u=0$ and convexity gives
$E(v)\ge E(u)+J(u)(v-u)=E(u)$.  Energy monotonicity gives
the reverse inequality.  The frozen ordered discrepancy bound
$I(u,v)\le e(u)-e(v)$ makes $u=v$ as relative classes.
The contact defect is then the assumed zero integral.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Directional loss, source equations and failure of orthogonality}

For $u\in\mathscr C$ and $h\in\mathbb D_S$, define the
one-sided defect
\[
 \mathfrak d_u(h)=
 \lim_{t\downarrow0}
       \frac{\mathfrak E(u+th)-E(u)}{t}-J(u)(h).
 \tag{OC13}
\]
Convexity and local Lipschitz continuity make the limit finite.
Since $J(u)$ is a subgradient, the defect is nonnegative.
It is positively homogeneous and subadditive, being a convex
directional derivative minus a linear functional.

\begin{theorem}[A first-order contact gate and its exact loss]
\label{thm:r12-first-order-contact-gate}
For $u,h$ as above, put $v_t=P(u+th)$ and
$G_t=u+th-v_t\succeq0$ for $t>0$.  Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 &\mathfrak E(u+th)-E(u)-tJ(u)(h)\\
 &\quad=
 \underbrace{E(v_t)-E(u)-J(u)(v_t-u)}_{\ge0}
                       +\int_VG_t\,d\widehat\mu_u\ge0,
 \end{split}
 \tag{OC14}
\]
and
\[
 \mathfrak E(u+th)-E(u)-tJ(u)(h)
       \le t(J(v_t)-J(u))(h)+\mathfrak Q(u+th).
 \tag{OC15}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \mathfrak d_u(h)
       \le\liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\mathfrak Q(u+th)}{t}.
 \tag{OC16}
\]

Let $\mu$ be a positive Radon datum whose literal integration
functional $\ell_\mu\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*$ is defined
on every energy difference, and let $u=\Pi(\ell_\mu)$.
If, for every original compact smooth scalar $\phi$ and both
signs, one has
\[
                  \mathfrak Q(u\pm t\phi)=o(t)
                                     \quad(t\downarrow0),
 \tag{OC17}
\]
then $\widehat\mu_u=\mu$ on every original compact smooth
scalar test, after every actual moment refinement.
Condition \textup{(OC17)} is a sufficient first-order contact
criterion, not a condition proved for general obstacles or data.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
defect identities and \texttt{CONDITIONAL} for the source
conclusion under the explicit geometric contact criterion.
This condition is stated using the independently constructed
envelope and its own curvature, not by assuming the desired
source equality.

\begin{proof}
All integrals are finite by the mixed first-energy inequality.
Subtract $tJ(u)(h)$ from the convex tangent remainder at $u$.
Since $v_t-u-th=-G_t$ and $J(u)=-\int(\cdot)\,d\widehat\mu_u$,
this gives exactly \textup{(OC14)}.  The tangent inequality
at $v_t$ instead gives
$E(v_t)-E(u)\le J(v_t)(v_t-u)$.
Substitute $v_t-u=th-G_t$ to obtain \textup{(OC15)}.
The third estimate of \textup{(OC4)} gives
$J(v_t)\to J(u)$ in the actual dual norm.  Divide
\textup{(OC15)} by $t$ and let $t\downarrow0$; the error
$(J(v_t)-J(u))(h)$ tends to zero.  This proves
\textup{(OC16)}, including the possibility that its right
side is infinite.

For the datum assertion, order reversal and the normal
decomposition give $\ell_\mu\in\partial\mathfrak E(u)$
by \textup{(OC10)}.  Thus
\[
 \mathfrak d_u(h)\ge(\ell_\mu-J(u))(h)
                                    \quad(h\in\mathbb D_S).
 \tag{OC18}
\]
Every original compact smooth $\phi$ belongs to $\mathbb D_S$
by the exact all-degree finite-mass difference construction
R11 \textup{(HC14)--(HC15)}.  Assumption \textup{(OC17)},
\textup{(OC16)} and nonnegativity make both
$\mathfrak d_u(\phi)$ and $\mathfrak d_u(-\phi)$ zero.
Apply \textup{(OC18)} in both signs to get
$\ell_\mu(\phi)=J(u)(\phi)$.  The literal integral
definitions give the original source identity on every
such test.  The choice of $\phi$ was unrestricted in the
original sheaf, so actual refinements are included.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A nonzero variational residual forces an obstacle kink]
\label{cor:r12-normal-residual-obstacle-kink}
For the positive datum and maximizer of the preceding theorem,
put $n=\ell_\mu-J(u)$.  For every $h\in\mathbb D_S$ the
right and left directional slopes of $\mathfrak E$ at $u$
have a gap at least $|n(h)|$.  If $n(h)>0$, then
\[
 \mathfrak d_u(h)\ge n(h)>0,
 \qquad
 \liminf_{t\downarrow0}\frac{\mathfrak Q(u+th)}{t}\ge n(h).
 \tag{OC19}
\]
If the source equation fails on an original compact smooth
test, the direction $h$ can be chosen to be such a test,
with its sign changed if necessary.  In that case universal
relative obstacle orthogonality and two-sided differentiability
of this obstacle energy at the maximizer are both false.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as a
quantitative contact interpretation of the normal residual.

\begin{proof}
Both $J(u)$ and $\ell_\mu$ are subgradients at $u$.
The right slope in direction $h$ is at least the larger of
$J(u)(h)$ and $\ell_\mu(h)$, whereas the left slope is at
most their smaller value.  Their difference is at least
$|n(h)|$.  Equation \textup{(OC18)} gives the first bound
in \textup{(OC19)}, and \textup{(OC16)} gives the second.
Distinct original Radon measures are distinguished by an

title: A Banach space of differences of strong energy potentials
text:
energy_difference_banach.tex \section{A Banach space of differences of strong energy potentials}
\label{sec:r12-energy-difference}

\paragraph{Exact standing hypotheses and frozen inputs.}
Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be the original finite extension with its original
absolute value. Let $X$ be good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth,
and pure of dimension $n$. Choose a compact original affinoid domain
$B\subset X$, functions $f_a,g_b\in\mathcal O(B)$ and positive real
thresholds $R_a,r_b$, such that
\[
 K_0=\{|f_a|\leq R_a,\ |g_b|\geq r_b\}
                         \Subset\operatorname{Int}_X(B),\qquad
 V=\{|f_a|<R_a,\ |g_b|>r_b\}\ne\varnothing .
 \tag{ED1}
\]
Let $S$ be an arbitrary original symmetric CLD middle-positive,
separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed $(p,p)$-current on an ordinary
neighborhood of $K_0$. Put $q=n-p\geq1$ and $d=q+1$.
No strong positivity, geometric representation or approximation of
$S$ is assumed. Every current below is tested on the full original
CLD test sheaf, with every actual moment refinement.

Write $\mathscr C=\widehat{\mathcal E}^{1}_{\rm str}(V)$ for the
precise R11 strong completion, with its encoded approximation
boundary condition. Its elements are nonpositive Borel potentials
modulo local ordinary-open outer $S$-capacity zero. We use the R11
inputs (GE10)--(GE18), (IC10)--(IC22), (CC1)--(CC11), (CI1)--(CI8)
and the completed extension of (EV1). They provide, respectively,
the symmetric global mixed energy, its positive energy matrices,
the complete strong cone, its intrinsic original currents, and its
monotone closure. All these statements are \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}
in their printed R11 scopes.

For $u_0,\ldots,u_q\in\mathscr C$, abbreviate
\[
 B(u_0,\ldots,u_q)=\int_V(-u_0)\,\widehat N_q(u_1,\ldots,u_q),
 \quad e(u)=B(u^{[d]}),\quad r(u)=e(u)^{1/d}.
 \tag{ED2}
\]
The frozen inequalities are $B(\mathbf u)\leq\prod_i r(u_i)$ and
$r(u+v)\leq r(u)+r(v)$. The zero-energy class is zero. Completed
potentials are finite outside outer-null sets; all differences below
are formed there and assigned any finite Borel value on the joint
exceptional set. In particular no expression $(-\infty)-(-\infty)$
is used as a pointwise number.

\begin{definition}[Energy-difference space and its norm]
\label{def:r12-energy-difference}
Let $\mathbb D_S=\mathscr C-\mathscr C$ be the real vector space of
such Borel differences modulo local outer-capacity equality. Define
\[
 \|h\|_{\rm ed}
   =\inf\{r(a)+r(b):a,b\in\mathscr C,\ h=a-b\}.
 \tag{ED3}
\]
This is a norm defined by the energy cone, not the discrepancy $I$.
It is not declared to be the ordinary supremum norm or a Hilbert norm.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Continuous extension of the mixed energy]
\label{lem:r12-difference-mixed-extension}
There is a unique symmetric real $d$-linear form on $\mathbb D_S$
extending $B$, and it satisfies
\[
       |B(h_0,\ldots,h_q)|\leq\prod_{i=0}^q\|h_i\|_{\rm ed}.
 \tag{ED4}
\]
Moreover $\|u\|_{\rm ed}=r(u)$ for every $u\in\mathscr C$.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the full
unbounded cone-difference construction; the mixed energy bound on
the positive cone is the explicit frozen input.

\begin{proof}
Expand each difference into its two cone terms and extend by the
finite multilinear expansion. If $a-b=a'-b'$, then
$a+b'=a'+b$ in the original relative cone. Separate additivity of
the frozen $B$ therefore makes the expansion independent of that
presentation, one slot at a time. Positive real homogeneity and
changing the signs of differences give real multilinearity.
For specified decompositions $h_i=a_i-b_i$, the triangle inequality
and cone Holder give the bound $\prod_i(r(a_i)+r(b_i))$.
Taking independent infima proves (ED4).

The definition gives $\|u\|_{\rm ed}\leq r(u)$. Applying (ED4)
to the diagonal tuple gives $e(u)\leq\|u\|_{\rm ed}^{d}$, so the
reverse inequality follows. This argument also covers zero energy.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Actual Borel realization and Banach completeness]
\label{thm:r12-energy-difference-Banach}
Formula (ED3) is a norm, $\mathbb D_S$ is complete for that norm,
and $\mathscr C$ is a closed convex cone in this Banach space.
Norm convergence implies convergence in the full local outer
$S$-capacity topology. More precisely, with
$C_0=d2^d$, one has
\[
 C_S^*(\{|h|>t\};V)\leq C_0 t^{-d}\|h\|_{\rm ed}^{d}
                    \qquad(h\in\mathbb D_S,\ t>0).
 \tag{ED5}
\]
For $u,v\in\mathscr C$,
\[
 I(u,v)\leq\bigl(r(u)^q+r(v)^q\bigr)\|u-v\|_{\rm ed}.
 \tag{ED6}
\]
The result does not identify this norm topology with the strong
discrepancy topology on $\mathscr C$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}.

\begin{proof}
The infimum in (ED3) is finite. Minkowski on $\mathscr C$ proves
the triangle inequality; switching the two cone terms proves
symmetry, and homogeneity follows by rescaling decompositions.
The R11 capacity integral bound $J_1^*(u)\leq2^d e(u)$ and
monotonicity of the sublevels give
\[
 \frac{t^d}{d}C_S^*(\{u<-t\};V)
       \leq\int_0^t s^{d-1}C_S^*(\{u<-s\};V)\,ds
       \leq2^d e(u).
\]
For $h=a-b$, the set $\{|h|>t\}$ is contained, modulo an
outer-null set, in $\{a<-t\}\cup\{b<-t\}$. Hence its outer
capacity is at most $C_0t^{-d}(r(a)^d+r(b)^d)$, bounded by
$C_0t^{-d}(r(a)+r(b))^d$. Infimizing proves (ED5), and shows
that a zero seminorm has the zero relative Borel class. Local
outer-null sets here also have zero outer capacity in the fixed
domain: use a countable compact exhaustion and the R11 domain
comparison on its cores. The same comparison transfers norm
convergence to every smaller-domain original capacity.

We prove completeness inside the space of actual Borel differences,
rather than introducing an abstract completion with unidentified
elements. For a norm-Cauchy sequence choose a subsequence $(h_j)$
whose successive increments have decompositions
\[
 h_{j+1}-h_j=a_j-b_j,\qquad
 \sum_{j\geq1}(r(a_j)+r(b_j))<\infty.
 \tag{ED7}
\]
Write $h_1=a_0-b_0$. The partial sums
$A_N=a_0+\sum_{j=1}^N a_j$ and
$B_N=b_0+\sum_{j=1}^N b_j$ decrease as Borel potentials,
outside one countable union of outer-null sets. Their energy
roots are bounded by the corresponding sums of roots, so the
R11 decreasing-closure theorem (CI8) gives strong limits
$A,B\in\mathscr C$. Apply the same theorem to each tail series.
It yields $A-A_N,B-B_N\in\mathscr C$ and
\[
 r(A-A_N)+r(B-B_N)
          \leq\sum_{j>N}(r(a_j)+r(b_j))\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{ED8}
\]
The identities with the tails hold on the common finite locus,
hence in the relative Borel quotient. Thus $h=A-B\in\mathbb D_S$
is the norm limit of the subsequence and of the original Cauchy
sequence. No abstract vector invisible to Borel capacity has been
adjoined.

For $u,v\in\mathscr C$, multilinearity gives
\[
 I(u,v)=B(u-v,u^{[q]})-B(u-v,v^{[q]}).
\]
Apply (ED4) to obtain (ED6). If a sequence in $\mathscr C$
converges in norm to $h\in\mathbb D_S$, its energy roots are
bounded by the norm triangle inequality and the preceding lemma.
Equation (ED6) makes it strongly Cauchy. R11 completeness supplies
a limit $u\in\mathscr C$. The norm limit and the strong limit
have the same local capacity class by (ED5) and the R11 strong
topology theorem. Thus $h=u$, proving norm closedness.
Convexity is the frozen cone addition property.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Curvature as an energy-dual functional]
\label{def:r12-dual-curvature}
For $u\in\mathscr C$ put
\[
       J(u)(h)=B(h,u^{[q]})=-\int_Vh\,d\widehat\mu_u
                      \qquad(h\in\mathbb D_S).
 \tag{ED9}
\]
The displayed integral is literal and absolutely convergent: for
$h=a-b$, $|h|\leq(-a)+(-b)$ off a common null set, and the
two mixed first energies are finite. The current measure ignores
that exceptional set. Thus $J(u)$ is a genuine functional in
$\mathbb D_S^*$, with its original current interpretation.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Exact dual norm and strong continuity of curvature]
\label{thm:r12-dual-curvature-continuity}
For every continuous linear functional $\ell$ on $\mathbb D_S$,
\[
 \|\ell\|_*=
     \sup_{\substack{a\in\mathscr C\\r(a)\leq1}}|\ell(a)|.
 \tag{ED10}
\]
For $u\in\mathscr C$ one has $\|J(u)\|_*=r(u)^q$.
For $u,v\in\mathscr C$ and $R=\max(r(u),r(v))$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \|J(u)-J(v)\|_*&\leq qR^{q-1}\|u-v\|_{\rm ed},\\
 \|J(u)-J(v)\|_*&\leq\sqrt q\,R^{(q-1)/2}I(u,v)^{1/2}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{ED11}
\]
At $R=0$ both sides mean zero; for $q=1$ the power $R^0$ is
one. In particular strong convergence of potentials gives norm
convergence of their source functionals, in every remaining degree.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the precise
Banach dual and quantitative all-degree source map. The integrated
positive energy matrices used in the proof are frozen inputs.

\begin{proof}
If the supremum in (ED10) is $L$, a decomposition $h=a-b$
gives $|\ell(h)|\leq L(r(a)+r(b))$. Taking the infimum yields
$\|\ell\|_*\leq L$; the reverse follows from
$\|a\|_{\rm ed}=r(a)$. Equation (ED4) bounds the norm of
$J(u)$ by $r(u)^q$. For $r(u)>0$, evaluation on $u/r(u)$
gives equality; if $r(u)=0$, the class and functional are zero.

The finite telescoping expansion gives
\[
 (J(u)-J(v))(h)
    =\sum_{l=0}^{q-1}B(h,u-v,u^{[l]},v^{[q-1-l]}).
 \tag{ED12}
\]
Equation (ED4) proves the first bound in (ED11).
For the sharper strong-topology bound define
\[
 H(f,g)=\sum_{l=0}^{q-1}
                 B(f,g,u^{[l]},v^{[q-1-l]}).
\]
This is a positive semidefinite bilinear form on $\mathbb D_S$.
Indeed each summand is the integrated energy form with the
fixed completed positive closed mixed background. Positivity on
finite differences follows from R11 (GE7), passed through the
global mixed-energy convergence (IC13). It is not a pointwise
Alexandrov--Fenchel assertion. We have
\[
 H(u-v,u-v)=I(u,v),\qquad
 H(a,a)\leq q r(a)^2R^{q-1}\quad(a\in\mathscr C).
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz for this positive semidefinite form and (ED12)
bound the functional on every $a$ with $r(a)\leq1$.
Equation (ED10) proves the second bound. Strongly convergent
rows have bounded energy roots by R11, so the final assertion
follows. Every construction used the intrinsic original products;
no special tropical trace was substituted for their test sheaf.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Two different source distances.}
When signed measure integration defines the corresponding continuous
functionals, their difference norm is
\[
 \delta_*(\mu,\nu)
     =\sup_{\substack{a\in\mathscr C\\r(a)\leq1}}
                    \left|\int_V(-a)\,d(\mu-\nu)\right|.
 \tag{ED13}
\]
This is not the R11 absolute-variation distance (VF11), which has
$\int(-a)\,d|\mu-\nu|$ inside the supremum. The latter dominates
(ED13) whenever it is defined, and can be strictly stronger.
The signed cancellation in (ED13) is essential to (ED11).
The Banach space and its curvature map do not prove an analytic
PS/PL presentation quotient, or equality on additional GK delta tests.

title: Closed nonlinear source images and a dual normal decomposition
text:
nonlinear_dual_source_geometry.tex \section{Closed nonlinear source images and a dual normal decomposition}
\label{sec:r12-nonlinear-dual-source}

Keep exactly (ED1), the unchanged arbitrary original $S$, and the
Banach space $\mathbb D_S$ of the preceding section. Its positive
potential cone is denoted $\mathscr C$ even though its Borel
representatives are nonpositive functions. Write $J$ for (ED9),
$r(u)=e(u)^{1/d}$, and $\|\cdot\|_*$ for the genuine operator
dual norm (ED10). In particular this is not the absolute-variation
distance of R11 (VF11).

\begin{theorem}[A complete curvature-dual metric and closed source image]
\label{thm:r12-closed-full-source-image}
The image $J(\mathscr C)$ is norm closed in $\mathbb D_S^*$.
The formula
\[
                 d_J(u,v)=\|J(u)-J(v)\|_*
 \tag{NI1}
\]
defines a complete metric on $\mathscr C$, inducing precisely the
R11 strong discrepancy topology. For $u,v\in\mathscr C$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 I(u,v)&\leq(r(u)+r(v))d_J(u,v),\\
 d_J(u,v)&\leq\sqrt q\,
     \max(r(u),r(v))^{(q-1)/2}I(u,v)^{1/2}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{NI2}
\]
No common dominating measure and no fixed actual lower barrier
are required. The assertion concerns all $q\geq1$ and the full
original test category on the stated domain.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}}. R11 (OI1)--(OI3)
proved closedness only inside a fixed dominated interval for its
stronger absolute-variation distance; neither restriction occurs here.

\begin{proof}
Multilinearity gives the exact identity
$I(u,v)=(J(u)-J(v))(u-v)$. The dual inequality and
$\|u-v\|_{\rm ed}\leq r(u)+r(v)$ prove the first estimate.
The second is (ED11). Thus $d_J=0$ gives $I=0$ and equal
relative classes. Symmetry and the triangle inequality come
from the dual norm, not from an asserted triangle inequality
for $I$.

For completeness, mixed Holder also gives the explicit root bound
\[
 I(u,v)\geq\bigl(r(u)-r(v)\bigr)
                   \bigl(r(u)^q-r(v)^q\bigr)
                \geq|r(u)-r(v)|^{q+1}.
\]
The first inequality follows by bounding the two mixed terms in
$e(u)+e(v)-B(u,v^{[q]})-B(v,u^{[q]})$ separately. The second
is the elementary inequality $x^q-y^q\geq(x-y)^q$ for
$x\geq y\geq0$. Hence convergence to a fixed potential in
$I$ automatically bounds the energy roots.

Suppose $J(u_j)$ is norm Cauchy. Its norms are bounded, so
$r(u_j)^q=\|J(u_j)\|_*$ bounds the energy roots. The first
estimate in (NI2) makes $(u_j)$ strongly Cauchy. R11 strong
completeness gives $u\in\mathscr C$ with $I(u_j,u)\to0$.
Its energy roots remain bounded, and the second estimate gives
$J(u_j)\to J(u)$ in norm. Every norm limit of image elements
is consequently in the image, proving closedness and metric
completeness. The same inequalities prove equivalence of the
two convergences: strong convergence bounds the roots by the
frozen energy-root estimate, whereas $d_J$ convergence bounds
them by the exact dual norm identity. These arguments also
identify their Cauchy sequences.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Source approximation on every original test]
\label{cor:r12-original-source-approximation}
Let $u_j\in\mathscr C$ and suppose their source functionals
$J(u_j)$ converge in $\mathbb D_S^*$ to $\ell$. Then there is
a unique $u\in\mathscr C$ with $J(u)=\ell$, and $u_j\to u$
strongly. If a specified original Radon measure $\mu$ satisfies
\[
                 \ell(\phi)=-\int_V\phi\,d\mu
            \quad\text{for every original compact smooth scalar }\phi,
 \tag{NI3}
\]
then $\widehat\mu_u=\mu$ on all such tests, after every actual
moment refinement. All other strong current and weighted limits
of R11 (IC11)--(IC13) hold as well.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}}.

\begin{proof}
Closedness supplies $u$ and the quantitative estimates supply
strong convergence. Every original compact smooth scalar is an
element of $\mathbb D_S$: R11 (HC14)--(HC15) writes it as the
exact difference of two actual bounded finite-mass common-collar
potentials. That construction is valid for all $q$, not only
for its separate Hilbert-space consequence. Thus (ED9) and
(NI3) give equality on the complete original scalar test sheaf.
Original smooth scalar density and Radon regularity identify
the same measures. The strong calculus supplies the other
limits. This is an approximation criterion, not a claim that
every source admits such image approximants.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The strong-continuous energy dual]
\label{def:r12-strong-continuous-dual}
Let $\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*$ consist of those
$\ell\in\mathbb D_S^*$ for which
\[
  u_j,u\in\mathscr C,\ I(u_j,u)\to0
                 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ell(u_j)\to\ell(u).
 \tag{NI4}
\]
This is a continuity requirement on the actual strong cone.
It is not automatically imposed on every Banach-dual functional.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[A closed dual class containing every curvature]
\label{lem:r12-strong-dual-closed}
The class $\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*$ is a norm-closed linear
subspace of $\mathbb D_S^*$, and $J(\mathscr C)$ is contained
in it. Consequently the norm-closed linear span of all curvature
functionals is contained in this class.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the
proved Banach realization and frozen strong tester estimate.

\begin{proof}
Linearity is immediate. A strongly convergent row has bounded
$r(u_j)$, hence is bounded in $\mathbb D_S$. If $\ell_m\to\ell$
in norm, the error $|(\ell-\ell_m)(u_j-u)|$ is uniformly small
for large $m$. Fixing $m$ then invokes (NI4), proving closure.
For fixed $v\in\mathscr C$, the completed R11 tester estimate
(EV1) bounds $|J(v)(u_j-u)|$ by
$\int|u_j-u|\,d\widehat\mu_v\to0$. Its constants are finite
on the bounded-energy family. This proves the curvature assertion.
\end{proof}

Let
\[
 \mathscr C^\circ
   =\{n\in\mathbb D_S^*:n(v)\leq0\text{ for every }v\in\mathscr C\}.
 \tag{NI5}
\]
This is the polar of the potential cone in the specified dual,
not an identification of any two current-positivity cones.

\begin{theorem}[All-degree variational normal decomposition]
\label{thm:r12-nonlinear-normal-decomposition}
For every $\ell\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*$, the functional
\[
                F_\ell(v)=\ell(v)-e(v)/d\qquad(v\in\mathscr C)
 \tag{NI6}
\]
has a unique maximizer $u=\Pi(\ell)$. Every maximizing sequence
converges strongly to $u$. Equivalently, there is a unique pair
$(u,n)$ with
\[
       \ell=J(u)+n,\qquad
       u\in\mathscr C,\quad n\in\mathscr C^\circ,
                           \quad n(u)=0.
 \tag{NI7}
\]
The residual also lies in $\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*$.
Define the nonnegative support gauge
\[
       p(\ell)=\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathscr C\\r(v)\leq1}}\ell(v).
 \tag{NI8}
\]
Then
\[
 \begin{split}
 e(u)&=\ell(u),\qquad r(u)^q=p(\ell)\leq\|\ell\|_*,\\
 \sup F_\ell&=\frac qd\,p(\ell)^{d/q}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{NI9}
\]
If $\ell$ is nonnegative on $\mathscr C$, then
$p(\ell)=\|\ell\|_*$. No assertion that the residual $n$ vanishes
is part of this theorem.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for arbitrary
strong-continuous signed dual data and every remaining degree.
The midpoint existence mechanism is explicitly inherited from
R11; the Banach source class and exact normal decomposition
are the new extension. This is not unrestricted source solvability.

\begin{proof}
Since $|\ell(v)|\leq\|\ell\|_*r(v)$,
$F_\ell(v)\leq\|\ell\|_*r(v)-r(v)^d/d$. Thus its supremum
$L\geq F_\ell(0)=0$ is finite, and every maximizing sequence
has bounded energies. In the midpoint gap the linear term
cancels. The frozen sharp inequality gives
\[
 c_q I(v_j,v_k)
     \leq L-\tfrac12(F_\ell(v_j)+F_\ell(v_k))\longrightarrow0,
 \quad c_q=\frac{1-2^{-q}}{2d}.
\]
Strong completeness provides $u\in\mathscr C$. Its energy
converges, and (NI4) passes the datum term, so $F_\ell(u)=L$.
The same midpoint estimate proves uniqueness and convergence
of every maximizing sequence. Actual classical strong density
also gives the same supremum over the frozen actual class.

The continuous $d$-linear extension $B$ makes $e/d$ a polynomial
on $\mathbb D_S$ whose differential at $u$ is $J(u)$.
Only segments inside $\mathscr C$ are used for maximization.
Their first variation gives
\[
                   (\ell-J(u))(v-u)\leq0\qquad(v\in\mathscr C).
 \tag{NI10}
\]
Conversely convexity of $e$ on the cone makes this sufficient.
Taking the competitors $0,2u$ gives $(\ell-J(u))(u)=0$.
Then (NI10) is precisely the polar condition in (NI7).
Conversely (NI7) implies (NI10). The pair is unique because
the maximizer is unique and $n=\ell-J(u)$. Its strong continuity
follows from the preceding lemma.

Scaling along $tu$ gives $e(u)=\ell(u)$, also when $u=0$.
For each $v\in\mathscr C$, the polar inequality gives
$\ell(v)\leq J(u)(v)\leq r(v)r(u)^q$. Thus
$p(\ell)\leq r(u)^q$. If $u\ne0$, evaluation on $u/r(u)$
gives the reverse inequality; if $u=0$, the polar condition
and the allowed zero tester give $p(\ell)=0$. This proves
(NI9). Finally (ED10) says
$\|\ell\|_* =\max(p(\ell),p(-\ell))$; if $\ell\geq0$ on
the cone, the latter second term is zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[A quantitative nonlinear retraction of source functionals]
\label{thm:r12-source-retraction}
Put $\mathcal P(\ell)=J(\Pi(\ell))$ on
$\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*$. This is a retraction onto the norm-closed
image $J(\mathscr C)$, and is positively homogeneous of degree one.
For $\|\ell\|_*,\|m\|_*\leq R$, with $R>0$, one has
\[
 \begin{split}
 I(\Pi(\ell),\Pi(m))&\leq2R^{1/q}\|\ell-m\|_*,\\
 \|\mathcal P(\ell)-\mathcal P(m)\|_*
                         &\leq\sqrt{2qR}\,\|\ell-m\|_*^{1/2}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{NI11}
\]
The first inequality has the more precise right side
$(\ell-m)(\Pi(\ell)-\Pi(m))$. If
$n=\ell-\mathcal P(\ell)$ and $R=\|\ell\|_*>0$, then
\[
 \left(\sqrt{qR+\|n\|_*}-\sqrt{qR}\right)^2
 \leq\operatorname{dist}_*(\ell,J(\mathscr C))\leq\|n\|_*.
 \tag{NI12}
\]
In particular a nonzero residual is a quantitative obstruction to
source-image approximation, not merely a failure of one chosen
maximization algorithm.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for this nonlinear
all-degree dual retraction and the exact image-approximation gap.
It is not asserted to be a Hilbert metric projection.

\begin{proof}
If $\ell=J(a)$, the pair $(a,0)$ satisfies (NI7), so uniqueness
gives the retraction. Homogeneity of $J$ gives
$\Pi(t\ell)=t^{1/q}\Pi(\ell)$ and
$\mathcal P(t\ell)=t\mathcal P(\ell)$ for $t\geq0$;
the case $t=0$ is the zero class.

Write $u=\Pi(\ell)$ and $v=\Pi(m)$. Use $v,u$ as the
competitors in their two inequalities (NI10), and add. It yields
$I(u,v)\leq(\ell-m)(u-v)$. Duality bounds this by
$\|\ell-m\|_*(r(u)+r(v))$; (NI9) bounds the roots by
$R^{1/q}$. The second line of (NI11) now follows from (ED11).
If $R=0$ both projections are zero.

Let $\delta$ be the distance in (NI12). Since $J(0)=0$,
$\delta\leq R$. Choose $\eta_j\in J(\mathscr C)$ with
$\delta_j=\|\ell-\eta_j\|_*\to\delta$. Their norms are
at most $R+\delta_j$. Retraction and (NI11) imply
\[
 \|n\|_*\leq\delta_j+
               \sqrt{2q(R+\delta_j)\delta_j}.
\]
Passing to the limit and using $\delta\leq R$ gives
$\|n\|_*\leq\delta+2\sqrt{qR\delta}$. Solving this
quadratic inequality in $\sqrt\delta$ gives the lower bound.
The upper bound uses the particular image element $\mathcal P(\ell)$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Source equations and scope.}
For an actual measure datum whose literal integration defines $\ell$,
the equation in the completed class holds exactly when the residual
is zero. The decomposition does not assert that an arbitrary positive
Radon datum has that property. The R11 compact-source obstruction
still gives nonzero residuals, and the new higher-degree cap-lift
obstruction supplies further examples. No ambient classical
representative, ordinary pointwise boundary trace, analytic GQ,
or low-real-degree CTO is inferred.
