geom13_central_background_cap_audit.md # Central degree-one backgrounds: the missing cap comparison

Author: `r13_codim_two_geometry`.

Status: **failure-route and dependency audit, not a new theorem**. The definitions below use retained calculus. No local potential, numerical class, restriction to a curve, or cap representation is constructed for an arbitrary allowed current. The later Round 13 MT--LE--PT results do construct a protected real transpose and its critical tangents, and identify their relevant pairing; Section 7 records that progress separately from the still missing cap comparison. Independent internal review elsewhere is not peer review or formal certification.

## 1. The residual under investigation

In the supplied smooth integral normal-three model and fixed finite closed-cell quadratic class of PA, the new ordinary cover gives zero action away from the original generic model point `y`. PA's separately reviewed current argument shows that, for an arbitrary allowed degree-one background `S`, the remaining action is

\[
\mathcal A_S(P)=c_S(P)\,\delta_y.
\]

The original finite field extension, absolute value, ordinary domains, middle positivity, separate closedness, original compact smooth tests, and all actual refinements remain fixed. The problem is to prove `c_S(P)=0` for every such `S`. Covering the puncture does not determine that scalar.

The finite actual relation and `S` are already given objects on the original analytic space. Temkin reduction, a residue curve, and a tropical source fan are geometric devices used to calculate particular expressions; none is a replacement domain for the arbitrary current.

## 2. What the cap construction permits us to define

Fix finitely many actual projective cap potentials `q_L` supplied by PC/AD/GT on one common ordinary neighborhood of `y`. They are actual continuous locally bounded classical psh functions. The retained fixed-background bounded BT theorem defines the positive top-degree measure

\[
\mu_{S;L,M}=Dq_L\wedge Dq_M\wedge S.
\]

Its atom

\[
m_S(L,M):=\mu_{S;L,M}(\{y\})
\]

is therefore a well-defined nonnegative real number for this chosen pair of actual cap potentials. Symmetry and finite signed multilinearity are inherited from the frozen BT calculus. These assertions do **not** require a current on the residue model, a tangent current, or a restriction of `S` to a curve.

At this stage the notation records the chosen actual caps and their domains. It must not silently be interpreted as a bilinear form on numerical divisor classes of the residue model. In particular, nonnegative entries of a finite cap matrix do not imply that the matrix is positive semidefinite on arbitrary signed coefficient vectors; positivity applies to the stated positive mixed products.

## 3. What AD/GT actually calculate

AD10--AD12 calculate the complete trace-weighted one-cycle output of the specified pair of caps. The calculation retains all actual divisorial sources, all marks, primitive radial stretching, and the protected old differential factor. GT extends that calibration in its stated model dimension and uses whole cap powers and exact polarization for the numerical rows.

Those results calculate known actual cap products and their pairings with the particular trace tensors and original smooth tests allowed in their statements. They do not take an arbitrary degree-one current `S`, restrict it to each marked residue curve, and identify its values with a numerical divisor class. The latter operation has not been defined or justified by those source comparisons.

In particular, the following are different assertions:

1. A known actual cap one-cycle has the calibrated residue intersection weights.
2. An arbitrary allowed `S` has a curve restriction, model normal-star trace, or actual cap representation compatible with all refinements.
3. The atomic quantities `m_S(L,M)` depend only on the numerical complete-intersection class `L·M`.
4. Those numerical quantities determine `c_S(P)` for every actual quadratic zero in the stated class.

The first is a retained theorem in its precise scope. The second through fourth need additional proofs.

## 4. The circularity in a proposed numerical class of `S`

Suppose one tries to assign a class `alpha_S` on a projective model of the residue field by requiring

\[
m_S(L,M)=\alpha_S\cdot L\cdot M.
\]

Before this is a definition, every relation among the proposed numerical complete-intersection classes must be shown to give the same relation among the actual atomic BT quantities. A relation among algebraic intersection rows or normal cap source weights alone does not provide that implication for an arbitrary `S`.

The missing implication transports a quadratic relation among actual curvature factors through the arbitrary background. It is precisely of the form that the intrinsic action-descent problem asks to prove. Declaring numerical factorization in order to prove that descent would therefore assume the missing compatibility.

Finite-field Picard torsion and the same-field finite unit-lifting theorem solve algebraic lifting and finite divisor-row problems. They do not define this current-to-class map. Likewise, a principal or numerical relation on a selected residue model is not an equality against every original complementary test with arbitrary `S` merely because its scalar numerical rows vanish.

## 5. The exact weak-approximation route already available

The frozen R6 source defines

\[
\mathcal W^1(V)=\overline{\{[\sigma]:\sigma\in B^{1,1}(V),
\ [\sigma]\text{ is symmetric, original-positive and separately closed}\}}^{\rm weak}
\]

using **all** original compact smooth tests on one fixed ordinary domain `V`. Nets are allowed, but the domain does not shrink with the net. Membership in `W^1_loc` means such a fixed domain exists near each point.

R6's fixed-continuous-slot lemma proves weak continuity of the BT insertion of any fixed finite continuous psh list when positive closed backgrounds vary on that same domain. Finite signed continuous DSH expansions and the fixed PS test estimates retain the applicable finite signed expressions. Thus weak approximation of the background is a legitimate mechanism for this fixed residual problem; no new weak-continuity theorem is needed here.

R6's full actual delta-test theorem gives presentation-independent action for backgrounds in `W^1_loc`. In particular, the actual zero relation has zero action for that subclass. The frozen manuscript explicitly does **not** identify `W^1_loc` with the whole allowed positive closed cone.

Consequently a sufficient new geometric result would be one of the following, each proved on an original fixed ordinary neighborhood:

- membership of the arbitrary degree-one `S` in `W^1_loc`;
- a decomposition into a background in that class and an error whose pairing with this fixed residual is proved zero;
- an approximation in a weaker, explicitly specified topology which is nevertheless proved to preserve `c_S(P)`.

A finite approximation on each punctured tube does not provide any of these at the center. Pointwise or numerical convergence on a selected source fan is not the required original-test convergence.

## 6. Known geometric subclasses do not settle the arbitrary background

A cap curvature `Dq_L` already has an actual continuous bounded local potential. A first Chern current of an actual locally continuously metrized line bundle likewise has such a potential on an ordinary local frame domain, when its stated semipositivity hypotheses place that potential in the retained classical class. These backgrounds are therefore already handled by the potential or weak-closure results. Producing more such cap or metric examples does not prove that a given arbitrary `S` is among them.

R6 also includes locally effective Cartier backgrounds, with singularities and original multiplicities, through the original Poincaré--Lelong formula and same-domain logarithmic truncations. It includes the displayed smooth flags, integrable-potential subclasses, and admissible diffuse barycenters. Each retains its own hypotheses. None supplies an arbitrary-current potential theorem.

## 7. What the completed critical-tangent comparison proves and leaves open

The subsequent Round 13 MT theorem defines the real bidimension-two current `T` by the original smooth test functional `T(eta)=S(t^*eta)` on a protected moment domain. Properness uses the entire inverse image of each compact target support. This is an exact transpose of original tests; it is not an arbitrary analytic pushforward of currents and does not discard other points in the central moment fiber.

Middle positivity and both closedness equations pass to `T`. Its trace satisfies the proved critical bound `mu_T(B_r)=O(r^2)`, with finite density `nu=lim mu_T(B_r)/r^2`. The critical rescalings `T_delta=delta^2(a_delta)_*T` have subsequential positive closed conic limits `T_0`. The density need not be zero, and `O(r^2)` is not replaced by `o(r^2)`.

LE constructs the complete homogeneous first-jet energy `Z_0` from genuine ambient scalar PL jets. The all-face coefficient error is `O(r)`, so the critical trace estimate removes the higher-jet contribution with error `O_S(delta)`. PT then identifies the remaining original scalar with every realized critical tangent:

\[
c_S(P)=-\langle T_0,Z_0\wedge D\rho\rangle.
\]

This last passage retains wall mass. Its quantitative compatible-PS approximation uses normal diagonal strip mass `O(epsilon)` and mixed normal variation `O(sqrt(epsilon))`; the mechanism is retained R4/R6 machinery, explicitly checked again for the real tangent interface. The full original Borel coefficient module identifies the transpose pairing on all face values. Smooth weak convergence alone would not have justified this step.

The remaining comparison would have to show that these **realized** paired functionals lie in a proved annihilator of the leading class of every actual zero, for example through a same-field actual cap/model realization or a complete approximation theorem. MT--LE--PT do not put an arbitrary `S`, or its critical transpose tangent, in `W^1_loc`; they do not define a numerical divisor class or prove that the available curve-cap rows span every realized paired functional. Nor is every positive closed real cone on the same geometric fan asserted to arise from an original background.

Thus the first unproved geometric step is an **arbitrary-background realization or paired-completeness theorem**. Pullback of an arbitrary current to a marked residue curve remains unavailable merely from positivity and separate closedness. The residue reduction is not an analytic map through which that arbitrary current may be pushed. Another slope normalization does not resolve this remaining gate.

## 8. Exact retained sources

All paths in this subsection are relative to the verified Round 12 parent, except the PA path.

| Input | Source and exact location | SHA-256 |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed arbitrary-background BT, positivity, symmetry, locality; potential independence | `frozen/selected_inputs/round11/frozen/selected_inputs/r6_scalar_and_degree_one_full_source.tex`, `sec:r6-inputs`, authorized/frozen items 1--3 | `fb87839085e500b446d9cc512e5bfca6b8f31de0b8ddf8721d9192d60f9942b0` |
| Same-domain weak class and fixed-slot continuity | Same R6 source, `def:r6-delta-weak-closure`, `lem:r6-fixed-continuous-slots-varying-background`, `prop:r6-delta-weak-class-bt-stability` | Same bound R6 source |
| Actual presentation-independent delta action for the class | Same R6 source, `thm:r6-full-delta-test-extension`, including its explicit background hypothesis | Same bound R6 source |
| Geometric examples and potential limitations | Same R6 source, `cor:r6-smooth-flag-full-delta`, `thm:r6-integrable-classical-delta-background`, `cor:r6-cartier-delta-background`, and their scope paragraphs | Same bound R6 source |
| Quadratic action and coefficient-Radon boundary | `frozen/selected_inputs/round11/frozen/selected_inputs/qa_degree_one_and_quadratic_transgression.tex`, QA10--QA11 and its following proof; QA16--QA19 | `a6e8081c94d77b31a4bcf2c5eabd359a105cb03fd5a43f9ec8fe18d2cefdea2d` |
| Complete normalized marked-cap output | `notes/cap_actual_trace_weighted_one_cycle_detectors.tex`, AD10--AD12 and the surrounding source/calibration hypotheses | `18963e3aa2c09685a4d30245edd7de897bd8277d617bcff17829e60aecd9e0ae` |
| Whole projective cap powers and finite numerical rows | `notes/cap_all_dimension_projective_top_caps.tex`, GT1--GT6 and the actual top-cap/detector statements | `15df0170f7d55d7f003edf6d8f4d486d57f46076bf98781dcbe75695ad5a7ca4` |
| New punctured action and the stated central scalar | Round 13 `notes/cap13_punctured_quadratic_action_and_point_residual.tex`, PA6 and PA9--PA10; use the final independently reviewed source hash from its index | Versioned in the Round 13 cap index |

No new external density theorem or local-potential theorem has been imported in this audit. General arbitrary-background central cancellation remains **OPEN**.

## 9. Round 13 critical-pairing update

The following are paths in the present Round 13 directory. These are independently reviewed source results, not new claims of this audit.

title: An intrinsic normal current and its local-unit harmonic drift
text:
intrinsic_normal_current_and_harmonic_drift.tex \section{An intrinsic normal current and its local-unit harmonic drift}
\label{sec:r18-intrinsic-normal-current}

\paragraph{Status and contribution boundary.}
The statements here are \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY} consequences of the
local operator LO, its exact energy identity, the separately normal
stratum tangency lemma RS0, and the frozen original smooth presentation
quotient SG8.  They give a genuine original symmetric order-zero current
for each fixed mixed tail of a full polar.  The current is separately
normal, with explicitly retained boundary measures.  Separate closedness
is \emph{not} asserted.  Its boundary is exactly a local-unit harmonic
defect which the printed global full-polar axioms have not yet been
shown to annihilate.  No general signed PL relation descent follows.

The duality and analytic-descent researchers independently developed
the weighted normality route and then compared its algebra; they are
construction contributors to this section.  Author-separated review is
recorded separately.  The root researcher checked its scope and signs
but did not supply a proof of the missing harmonic gate.

Keep the original \(U,F,L,C,\Lambda,b\) and the fixed arbitrary global
DC tails \(v_3,\ldots,v_b\) of LO.  Work on a pure-dimensional
component of \(U\) of dimension \(n\ge1\); the construction is local
on components.  The local scalar operation \(\mathscr L\), signed
biderivation \(\Gamma\), drift measures \(a_i\), and symmetric
Hessian coefficient measures \(B_{ij}\) are exactly LO6--LO17.

All real calculations use the two independent exterior columns of
HF9, with no cross-column sign.  In bidimension \((1,1)\) the
normalization factor in HF10 is one.  When we display test boundary
operators, we define them explicitly by
\[
       (\partial_LT)(\alpha)=T(d_L\alpha),\qquad
       (\partial_RT)(\beta)=T(d_R\beta)
 \tag{NC1}
\]
for bidegrees \((0,1)\) and \((1,0)\), respectively.  The
corresponding graded signs in an original-current differential convention
can then be applied without changing any vanishing or normality claim.

\subsection{Weighted real pushforwards have finite separate boundaries}

Let \(t:V\to\mathbb R^m\) be any local actual unit moment on an
ordinary open \(V\subset U\).  The coefficients supplied by LO8
are compatible under protected restrictions, and hence are locally
finite measures on \(C\cap V\).  Choose any real original
\(\xi\in A_c^{0,0}(V)\), with no requirement that it be a function
of \(t\).  Define the compact real matrix measure and current
\[
 \mu_{ij}^\xi=t_*(\xi B_{ij}),\qquad
 T_{t,\xi}(\eta)=\sum_{i,j}\int_{\mathbb R^m}\eta_{ij}\,d\mu_{ij}^\xi.
 \tag{NC2}
\]
Only compactly supported analytic coefficient measures are pushed, so
no ambient properness assertion is needed.

\begin{proposition}[Exact weighted divergence identity]
For every \(j\), in the distributional sense on \(\mathbb R^m\),
\[
       \sum_i\partial_i\mu_{ij}^\xi
            =t_*\bigl(\xi a_j+\Gamma(\xi,t_j)\bigr).
 \tag{NC3}
\]
The right side is a finite compactly supported signed Radon measure.
By symmetry the same identity applies to the other tensor column.
Thus \(T_{t,\xi}\) is a compact separately normal real double current
of bidimension \((1,1)\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^m)\).  Choose an original
compact smooth \(\rho\) in \(V\), equal to one near
\(\operatorname{supp}\xi\), and put
\(u=\widetilde{\rho t_j}\),
\(h=\widetilde{\xi\phi(t)}\), extending both by zero to \(U\).
These are compact original smooth functions and hence are in
\(\mathcal D(U)\).  LO17 and the locality of \(\mathscr L\)
and \(\Gamma\) give
\[
             \int_{C\cap V}\xi\phi(t)\,da_j
                      =-\int_{C\cap V}\Gamma(\xi\phi(t),t_j).
 \tag{NC4}
\]
Indeed \(u=t_j\) near the support of \(h\); every difference
outside that neighborhood pairs to zero by the proved carrier-germ
locality.  The derivation identity LO16 and the local formula LO15
expand the right side as
\[
 -\int\phi(t)\,d\Gamma(\xi,t_j)
                   -\sum_i\int\xi\,\phi_i(t)\,dB_{ij}.
 \tag{NC5}
\]
Rearranging (NC4)--(NC5) is exactly (NC3), with the usual negative
sign in the definition of a distributional derivative.
The measures \(\xi a_j\) and \(\Gamma(\xi,t_j)\) have compact
support in \(C\cap\operatorname{supp}\xi\), by locality, and
are finite there.  Their pushforwards are therefore finite.  Since
\(B_{ij}=B_{ji}\), the two column divergences have the same type
of bound.  With the test-boundary convention (NC1), the real
boundary coefficients are the negatives of the measures in (NC3).
No cutoff derivative has been omitted: it is the entire explicit
term \(\Gamma(\xi,t_j)\).
\end{proof}

For an actual affine refinement \(t=At'+c\) on \(V\), LO10 and
ordinary coefficient pushforward yield
\[
                        p_*^{\rm tensor}T_{t',\xi}=T_{t,\xi},
             \qquad p(y')=Ay'+c,
 \tag{NC6}
\]
with no rank hypothesis.  This comparison uses the same actual
analytic coefficient \(\xi\); it does not transport a full polar
between ordinary domains.

\subsection{The whole original smooth form quotient is respected}

\begin{lemma}[Zero smooth presentations are annihilated with arbitrary analytic weights]
Let \((t,\eta)\) be a smooth \((1,1)\) presentation on \(V\),
and let \(\xi\in A_c^{0,0}(V)\).  If its original smooth form
is zero on an ordinary neighborhood of
\(C\cap\operatorname{supp}\xi\), then
\[
                         T_{t,\xi}(\eta)=0.
 \tag{NC7}
\]
Real compact cutoffs equal to one near the compact coefficient
support may be inserted in \(\eta\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Cover \(C\cap\operatorname{supp}\xi\) by finitely many original
compact affinoid domains \(K_\ell\) contained in the given zero
neighborhood and in \(V\).  The exact full-image smooth quotient
SG8 and its sheafification argument imply that \(\eta\) restricts
to zero on each full image \(t(K_\ell)\).  These images are compact
finite polyhedral sets by the same original moment-image theorem
used in SG.  A common finite subdivision makes their union
\(Z\) a finite polyhedral set with
\[
            \operatorname{supp}T_{t,\xi}
                      \subset t(C\cap\operatorname{supp}\xi)\subset Z.
\]
By (NC3), the real current has finite separate boundary measures.
RS0 therefore makes its coefficient density tangential in both
columns on every relative open cell of the chosen subdivision.
The restriction of \(\eta\) to each such cell is zero, so its
pairing with the corresponding Borel restriction of the coefficient
measures is zero.  Finite addition proves (NC7).  The argument retains
all mass on lower-dimensional faces; it neither discards face terms
nor declares the restrictions themselves closed.  All forms paired
here are smooth, so no product of two singular currents has been
introduced.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[An intrinsic symmetric separately normal current]
There is a unique original symmetric order-zero current
\(\mathcal T_{\Lambda;v_3,\ldots,v_b}\) of bidimension \((1,1)\)
on \(U\), supported on \(C\), with the local presentation rule
\[
 \mathcal T\bigl(\xi\,t^*\eta\bigr)
                         =T_{t,\xi}(\eta)
                         =\sum_{i,j}\int_{C\cap V}
                                                \xi\,\eta_{ij}(t)\,dB_{ij}
 \tag{NC8}
\]
for every original compact smooth scalar \(\xi\) in a local
actual moment chart and every smooth real \((1,1)\)-form \(\eta\).
It is defined on the full original compact smooth CLD test sheaf,
with every actual local moment refinement.  It satisfies
\[
       \mathcal T(d'h\otimes d''u)=\int\Gamma(h,u)
 \tag{NC9}
\]
whenever the displayed form has compact support in a protected local
chart, with the same formula after finite ordinary partition of unity.

For compact original tests of the form
\(\alpha=\sum_j h_jd''t_j\) and
\(\beta=\sum_i k_i d't_i\), its test boundaries are
\[
          (\partial_L\mathcal T)(\alpha)=-\sum_j\int h_j\,da_j,
          \qquad
          (\partial_R\mathcal T)(\beta)=-\sum_i\int k_i\,da_i.
 \tag{NC10}
\]
They are original coefficient-Radon currents.  Thus \(\mathcal T\)
is separately normal; the boundary measures have not been set to zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Consider first two local presentations of the same original smooth
form.  On their overlap, pass to the actual joint unit moment;
(NC6) identifies the projected coefficient pairings.  Their difference
is a zero smooth presentation, annihilated by (NC7) with each arbitrary
compact analytic weight.  Thus the local rule (NC8) is independent
of the moment presentation.  If an auxiliary scalar cutoff equal to
one near the compact support of an actual form is changed, its
difference multiplies a zero actual form; (NC7) again gives independence.
The rule consequently glues through a finite original smooth partition
of unity on each compact test support.  This is the ordinary sheaf
construction for currents, with compatibility proved before gluing.

On every fixed local test stage, the finite variations of \(B_{ij}\)
bound the pairing by finitely many coefficient supremum norms.  This
proves order-zero continuity in the original test topology.  The
coefficient measures are supported on \(C\), giving the asserted
support.  Symmetry is \(B_{ij}=B_{ji}\) in the HF two-column
convention.  Formula (NC9) is LO15 in a common actual moment, and
then follows globally by the proved presentation compatibility.
All charts in this construction are original local charts; none of
their units is assumed to extend to the fixed larger \(U\).

For one compact coefficient \(h\) in a local chart, repeat (NC4)
with \(\xi=h\) and the real test equal to one near the relevant
compact image.  Equivalently apply LO17 with a compact extension of
\(t_j\) equal to it near \(\operatorname{supp}h\).  This gives
\[
                    \int\Gamma(h,t_j)=-\int h\,da_j.
 \tag{NC11}
\]
The differential of \(\alpha=\sum_j h_jd''t_j\) is
\(\sum_j d'h_j\otimes d''t_j\) in the specified convention.
Equations (NC9) and (NC11) prove the first formula (NC10).  The
second follows in the same way from symmetry.  Arbitrary compact
original tests of these bidegrees admit finite such local
presentations and a subordinate partition of unity, so the formulas
prove coefficient-Radon bounds for both boundaries on every fixed
original test stage.  Their well-definedness on the original quotient
also follows directly because they are boundaries of the already
defined original current \(\mathcal T\).  This completes the
normality assertion without presupposing it on the analytic space.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The exact unresolved closedness condition}

For this fixed full polar and tail, the following are equivalent:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \partial_L\mathcal T=0\quad\hbox{and}\quad\partial_R\mathcal T=0;\\
 \mathscr L(\log|g|)=0\quad\hbox{on every ordinary local domain
 on which }g\hbox{ is an original analytic unit}.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{NC12}
\]
Indeed vanishing of all local drift measures makes (NC10) zero on
every test.  Conversely, one zero boundary tested against
\(h\,d''\log|g|\), with all compact original smooth \(h\), kills
the corresponding drift measure by Radon uniqueness.  Symmetry then
kills the other boundary as well.

The full global harmonic generator proves this only when the local
unit logarithm agrees along the local carrier with a globally
\(F\)-harmonic element of \(\mathcal D(U)\); whole-domain unit
moments are one such case.  The general local-unit condition (NC12)
is \texttt{OPEN} for arbitrary full polars in the present argument.
No counterexample satisfying the entire original full-polar ideal has
been supplied.  In particular the weighted-cutoff counterexample FC6
is not a failure of (NC12): it concerns a different, nonsymmetric
ordered functional.

Separate normality does not justify setting the double boundary to
zero.  The scalar identity \(\int\mathscr L(h)=0\) and the
energy identity merely give the usual cancellation between the drift
term and the divergence of the second-order coefficient; they do not
supply an additional independent equation.  No use of
\(\partial_L\partial_R\mathcal T=0\) is made here.

\paragraph{Why this remains short of the signed analytic relation theorem.}
The construction solves a smooth localization interface: a fixed
original full polar determines an actual order-zero current with
finite separate boundaries, on every original local smooth chart and
actual refinement.  It neither identifies that current as an allowed
positive background nor proves that its drift vanishes.  Even
separate closedness, if later proved, would not by itself identify a
zero curvature relation with a zero primitive pairing.  Singular
PL boundary cancellation and the appropriate primitive or exactness
bridge would still require proof.  No convolution is declared
zero-preserving, no norm level replaces the absolute carrier, and
no ordinary-current identity is promoted to all GK delta tests.
KC12 and variable-PS/CTO remain \texttt{OPEN}.

\paragraph{Exact dependencies.}
LO6--LO17 supply the original analytic coefficient measures, all local
actual affine covariance, the biderivation and compact energy identity.
RS0 is the explicit tangency lemma for finite separate boundaries.
SG8--SG9 supply only the full-image smooth presentation definition,
compact original moment-image polyhedrality and its ordinary
sheafification argument.  The present proof uses none of the
unproved signed analytic relation quotient or full-polar localization
claims.  Exact source hashes and author-separated reviews are recorded
in the adjacent ledger.

title: Scalar descent through quasi-étale uniformization
text:
harmonic_uniformization_source_audit.tex \section{Scalar descent through quasi-\'etale uniformization}
\label{sec:r24-harmonic-uniformization}

\paragraph{Status and authorship.}
The scalar assertions proved below are \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY} of the
specified primary results.  They are not an arbitrary-current descent
theorem and do not settle KC12.  The independent-audit agent constructed
this deduction after the root requested a source audit.  The root
independently proposed the same Galois-saturation repair after being
informed of the relevant passage in Ducros.  Neither participant is an
author-independent reviewer of this deduction.  A separate review is
required before it is used as an accepted input.

\subsection{Definitions and exact external interfaces}

Let $k$ be a complete nontrivially valued non-Archimedean field.  In its
application to this project, $k$ is the original $K$, or a finite
extension used only in scalar analytic geometry, with the given
absolute value extended and never renormalized.  All spaces in the
descent assertion are good, Hausdorff and strictly $k$-analytic.

The notation $\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X)$ has the geometric
meaning of Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, Definition~5.1: on a covering by
strictly analytic domains the function is a finite real linear
combination of logarithms of absolute values of analytic units on
those domains.  This definition concerns functions on the full
analytic domains.  It is not a definition in terms of a selected
skeleton or a chosen finite set of ordinary current tests.  We use
the following primary inputs, with their original hypotheses.

\begin{enumerate}
\item Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, arXiv:2111.05741v3, Definition~5.1,
Remark~5.2 and Lemma~5.4: geometric real PL functions are G-local and
are preserved by analytic pullback.  Proposition~5.11, printed
pp.~34--35, gives descent along finite, flat, surjective morphisms of
good strictly analytic spaces.  Corollary~5.12, printed p.~36, gives
descent after extension to the completion of an algebraic extension.
\item Ducros, \emph{Families of Berkovich spaces}, Theorem~5.4.6 and
the reduction in the proof of Proposition~9.1.1(c), printed
pp.~118--120 and~177, give the following local form.  A quasi-\'etale
morphism can be covered G-locally on its source by strict affinoid
domains $D$ admitting a factorization
\[
 D\lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow Z
 \lhook\joinrel\longrightarrow X,                         \tag{HU1}
\]
where $D$ is an analytic domain of $E$, $Z$ is a connected strict
affinoid domain of $X$, and $E\to Z$ is connected finite \'etale.
One may use finitely many such pieces when the source is compact.
The same proof explicitly passes to a connected finite Galois cover
of $Z$ dominating $E$.
\item Ducros, Proposition~9.1.1, printed pp.~177--178: if $Y$ is
quasi-compact and $\Gamma$-strict, $X$ is separated, and a coherent
sheaf on $Y$ is $X$-flat with quasi-finite support, its image is a
compact $\Gamma$-strict analytic domain of $X$.  We use only the case
of the structure sheaf of a strict affinoid domain of a finite
\'etale cover, with $\Gamma=\{1\}$.  Such a domain maps
quasi-\'etale, and hence flat, to the base.
\item Temkin, arXiv:1503.05729v2, Theorem~3.3.1 and
Corollary~3.3.2, printed p.~12, together with the rigid/Berkovich
translation in \S3.4: a compact quasi-smooth strictly $k$-analytic
space has, after a finite extension $l/k$, a surjective
quasi-\'etale affinoid cover possessing a \emph{strictly semistable}
formal $l^\circ$-model.  It is this statement, retaining the chosen
strictly semistable model, that is used below.  The separate wording
of Theorem~3.4.1 says only that the maximal affine model is
semistable; that wording alone is not silently strengthened.
\item Gubler--Rabinoff, arXiv:2506.13548v2,
Definition~7.1 and Proposition~7.2(6),(7), printed pp.~34--35:
classically pluriharmonic scalars are preserved by base extension and
analytic pullback.  Proposition~7.8, printed p.~36: on a good,
quasi-compact strictly analytic space having a strictly semistable
formal model, every classically pluriharmonic scalar is geometric
real PL.
\end{enumerate}

Here \emph{classically pluriharmonic} means that both $h$ and $-h$
are classically psh in the curve-test sense of the last reference.
No identification with an arbitrary continuous ordinary-current
harmonic witness is included in that definition.

\subsection{Galois saturation and scalar PL descent}

\paragraph{Proposition (compact quasi-\'etale scalar descent).}
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a surjective quasi-\'etale morphism between compact
good Hausdorff strictly $k$-analytic spaces.  For every real function
$h$ on $X$,
\[
 h\circ f\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(Y)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 h\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X).                   \tag{HU2}
\]
The assertion is about the given function on all analytic points.
It does not assert that $f$ has an interior lift over each point of
$X$, nor that $f$ becomes finite on an ordinary neighborhood of
every target point.

\paragraph{Proof.}
Analytic pullback proves the reverse implication.  Assume the left
side.  By HU1 and compactness, choose finitely many strict affinoid
source domains $D_i$ covering $Y$, with factorizations
$D_i\hookrightarrow E_i\to Z_i\hookrightarrow X$ as in HU1.
The finite family can be obtained from finitely many source
neighborhoods covered by the local affinoid pieces; thus it is an
actual G-cover and not just a collection of selected points.
It suffices to prove the assertion on the image of each $D_i$.
Fix one piece and omit its index.

Choose a connected finite Galois cover $q:\widetilde E\to Z$
dominating $E\to Z$, and write $G=\operatorname{Aut}_Z(\widetilde E)$.
Let $\widetilde D$ be the inverse image of $D$.  It is a compact
strict affinoid domain of $\widetilde E$.  The composite
$\widetilde D\to Z$ is quasi-\'etale: analytic-domain embeddings and
finite \'etale maps are quasi-\'etale, and this property is stable
under composition.  In particular it is flat and has
zero-dimensional fibers.  Ducros, Proposition~9.1.1, applied to
$\mathcal O_{\widetilde D}$ therefore shows that
\[
 C=q(\widetilde D)=f(D)
 \quad\hbox{is a compact strict analytic domain of }Z.    \tag{HU3}
\]
It is consequently also an analytic domain of $X$.

For every analytic point $z\in Z$, the Galois group acts transitively
on the points of $q^{-1}(z)$.  This is the usual finite-Galois-cover
fiber property, and is also the property used in the Galois
saturation in Ducros's proof of Proposition~9.1.1(c).  More
explicitly, after tensoring the finite \'etale fiber algebra with
$\mathscr H(z)$, its geometric points form a $G$-torsor.  The
absolute Galois group of $\mathscr H(z)$ commutes with this action;
therefore $G$ is transitive on its orbits, equivalently on the field
factors of that finite \'etale algebra.  Each finite extension of the
complete valued field $\mathscr H(z)$ has its unique extended
absolute value, so these factors are exactly the analytic fiber
points.  Hence
\[
 q^{-1}(C)=\bigcup_{g\in G}g(\widetilde D).              \tag{HU4}
\]
Indeed, any point on the right maps to the image of $\widetilde D$;
conversely, a point above $z\in C$ is a conjugate of some chosen
point of $\widetilde D$ above $z$.  Both sides carry their induced
analytic-domain structure in $\widetilde E$, and analytic-domain
structures on a fixed subset are unique.  The union in HU4 is
finite.  No points lying on domain boundaries have been removed.

Put $\widetilde h=h\circ q$ on $\widetilde E$, where $h$ is restricted
to $Z$.  Its restriction to $\widetilde D$ is geometric real PL by
pullback from $D$.  Since $q\circ g=q$, the function $\widetilde h$
is $G$-invariant.  Transporting the presentation on $\widetilde D$
by each $g$ proves that $\widetilde h$ is geometric real PL on every
$g(\widetilde D)$.

For clarity, no goodness assumption is needed for the possibly
non-affinoid union in HU4.  Cover $C$ by strict affinoid domains $V$.
For each such $V$, the space $q^{-1}(V)$ is strict affinoid and
$q^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite \'etale and surjective.  Its intersections
with the finitely many domains $g(\widetilde D)$ form a finite
analytic-domain cover.  Restriction of the preceding PL
presentations and G-locality show that
$\widetilde h|_{q^{-1}(V)}$ is real PL.  Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff,
Proposition~5.11, now gives $h|_V\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(V)$.
G-locality gives $h|_C\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(C)$, understood
through this affinoid cover if necessary.

Finally, the finitely many compact analytic domains $f(D_i)$ cover
$X$, because the $D_i$ cover $Y$ and $f$ is surjective.  They form a
finite G-cover of $X$.  Applying G-locality once more proves HU2.
\hfill$\square$

\paragraph{What the saturation accomplishes.}
The finite \'etale map used for descent is
$q^{-1}(V)\to V$, after $V$ has been recognized as an actual target
analytic domain.  It need not map back into the \emph{single}
original source piece $D$.  The equality of the scalar pullback on
all its Galois conjugates supplies PL presentations on the additional
pieces.  Thus this proof is not a domination of the original
quasi-\'etale cover by an ordinary finite \'etale cover, and it makes
no assertion of descent for an arbitrary current originally given
only on $D$.

\subsection{The scalar consequence of altered uniformization}

\paragraph{Corollary (classical pluriharmonic scalars are geometric
real PL in the compact strict quasi-smooth case).}
Let $X$ be a compact good Hausdorff quasi-smooth strictly
$k$-analytic space.  Every classically pluriharmonic real function
on $X$ belongs to $\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X)$:
\[
 \operatorname{PH}_{\mathrm{cl}}(X)
       \subseteq\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X).       \tag{HU5}
\]
In particular this holds over the original $K$.  It also yields the
corresponding local assertion at a point admitting a compact strict
quasi-smooth analytic neighborhood on which the scalar is
classically pluriharmonic.

\paragraph{Proof.}
Use Temkin, Corollary~3.3.2 and \S3.4, to choose a finite extension
$l/k$ and a surjective quasi-\'etale morphism
$p:Y\to X_l$ with $Y$ affinoid and possessing a strictly semistable
formal model over $l^\circ$.  The original absolute value is merely
extended to $l$.  The scalar
$h_l\circ p$ is classically pluriharmonic by
Gubler--Rabinoff, Proposition~7.2(6),(7).  Their Proposition~7.8
shows that it is geometric real PL on $Y$.  Apply HU2 over $l$ to
obtain $h_l\in\operatorname{PL}_{\mathbf R}(X_l)$.  Finally,
Gubler--Jell--Rabinoff, Corollary~5.12, descends this property along
the finite algebraic extension $l/k$ and gives HU5.
All steps concern scalars and their analytic pullbacks.  No current
over $l$ is constructed or imported. \hfill$\square$

\subsection{Boundary pressure test and the remaining KC interfaces}

Let $\varpi\in K$ satisfy $0<|\varpi|<1$, and consider the compact
annulus and its two closed subannuli
\[
 \begin{split}
 B&=\{|\varpi|\leq |T|\leq |\varpi|^{-1}\},\\
 B_-&=\{|\varpi|\leq |T|\leq1\},\qquad
 B_+=\{1\leq |T|\leq |\varpi|^{-1}\}.
 \end{split}                                                    \tag{HU6}
\]
The map $B_-\amalg B_+\to B$ is surjective and quasi-\'etale.
The unit Gauss point is in the ordinary interior of $B$ and on the
analytic boundary of both displayed source domains.  Thus the
shortcut asserting an ordinary interior lift for every point of a
surjective quasi-\'etale compact cover is \texttt{FALSE}.  This is
the already frozen R19 UF5 example, not a new counterexample family.
It does not contradict HU2: $B_-,B_+$ themselves are a finite
target G-cover, and scalar PL presentations glue on that cover.
The associated R19 UF6--UF8 current example explains why discarding
the boundary is nevertheless invalid for arbitrary-current action.

The following conclusions are deliberately \emph{not} part of HU5.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A finite continuous scalar with ordinary $D[h]=0$ has not,
by the definition alone, been identified with a classically
pluriharmonic scalar.  Any use of HU5 for KC harmonic witnesses must
pin a valid comparison in exactly that scalar class.  No general
positivity-to-regularization implication is inferred from the
abstracts of the cited papers.
\item Geometric real PL on a G-cover is not yet a single global
unit-log expression on a prescribed ordinary domain.  A
residue/Picard argument, when applicable, must retain its own exact
hypotheses and ordinary-germ quantifiers.
\item HU2 and HU5 construct neither pullback nor descent for
arbitrary allowed positive currents along the quasi-\'etale map.
They do not localize a previously chosen full carrier polar.
\item No conclusion about mixed KC harmonic generators with
arbitrary companion potentials, the full carrier-CLN seminorm, or
the actual signed PL relation ideal follows just from scalar
recognition.  No ordinary-current equality is promoted to an
arbitrary action on GK delta tests.
\end{enumerate}

Accordingly the original same-germ KC12 implication and the
variable-PS/CTO gates retain status \texttt{OPEN}.  The precise
topological obstruction to the naive three-result concatenation is
repaired for geometric scalar PL descent by HU2; it is not repaired
for arbitrary-current descent by the same argument.

title: Continuous potentials and the scalar-boundary action gate
text:
S21_continuous_potentials_and_scalar_boundary_action_gate.tex \section{Continuous potentials and the scalar-boundary action gate}
\label{sec:r24-scalar-boundary-action}

\paragraph{Status and purpose.}
This is a \texttt{FAILED\_ATTEMPT} audit within the frozen RV route.
The action implications proved below are \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}
consequences of the exact R6 degree-one theorem.  The required
continuous-potential existence statement remains \texttt{OPEN}.
The scalar rank-one interpretation tested below is \texttt{FALSE}
in its stated scope, but it has neither the centered homogeneity
nor the hypotheses of RV15.  No principal theorem or new
counterexample-family count is assigned to this note.  In particular
we do not prove KC12, quadratic Aeppli exactness, or CTO.

Fix the original finite extension \(K/\mathbf Q_p\), its unchanged
absolute value, and an original good, Hausdorff, boundaryless,
quasi-smooth space.  On a sufficiently small ordinary representative
\(V\) assume the dimension is the constant \(n\).
The notation \(B^{p,q}\) denotes the actual Mihatsch delta-form
sheaf, with every actual local refinement retained.  We use the
anticommuting CLD convention \(D=d'd''\), and write \([\alpha]\)
for the ordinary current of an already existing delta-form.
The potential space \(\mathcal D(V)\) is the unchanged space of
finite continuous differences of locally bounded original classical
psh functions.  Every background \(S\) below is symmetric,
middle-positive, and separately \(d'\)- and \(d''\)-closed.
No stronger positive cone or model origin is imposed on \(S\).

\subsection{An ordinary scalar potential already suffices for action}

Write \(M_S(\alpha)\) for the canonical total-degree-one action
of R6, Theorem \texttt{r6-arbitrary-background-degree-one-delta}.
The following observation does not require its potential to define
an actual delta-form.

\begin{proposition}[Continuous-potential action comparison]
Let \(\alpha\in B^{1,1}(V)\) be symmetric.  Suppose there is
\(v\in\mathcal D(V)\) such that
\[
                         [\alpha]=D[v]
             \quad\hbox{as ordinary currents on }V.       \tag{AP24.1}
\]
Then, for every allowed original \(S\) of degree \((p,p)\),
\(0\le p<n\),
\[
                         M_S(\alpha)=D(vS).               \tag{AP24.2}
\]
This is an equality on all original compact smooth complementary
tests.  It holds in every actual presentation and refinement.
Consequently \(M_S(\alpha)\) is separately closed and, whenever
the degree is legal, \(D M_S(\alpha)=0\).
The same assertion is valid for germs: choose the representative
and the potential once, before quantifying over backgrounds and
tests.  No equality on GK delta tests is asserted.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
R6, Lemma \texttt{r6-degree-one-hessian-presentation}, gives
locally a finite presentation
\[
                  \alpha=\sum_{i=1}^{N} f_iD_\delta g_i,
                                                               \tag{AP24.3}
\]
where each \(f_i\) is continuous piecewise smooth and each
\(g_i\) is a continuous local difference of continuous classical
psh functions.  On a compact test support use finitely many such
ordinary neighborhoods and a subordinate original smooth partition.
The actual embedding and continuous multiplication give
\(
 [\alpha]=\sum_i f_iD[g_i]
\)
on each neighborhood.  Subtract (AP24.1).  The resulting ordinary
relation is
\[
                     \sum_i f_iD[g_i]-D[v]=0 .             \tag{AP24.4}
\]
All coefficients in this relation are continuous; the coefficient
of the last curvature is the constant \(-1\).
Expand each local DC potential into its two original psh components.
R6, Theorem \texttt{r6-continuous-curvature-module}, applies to
this exact relation and gives
\[
                     \sum_i f_iD(g_iS)-D(vS)=0 .           \tag{AP24.5}
\]
By the definition and already proved independence of \(M_S\),
the first sum is \(M_S(\alpha)\).  This proves (AP24.2)
locally and on every partitioned test, hence on the whole test.

Both first derivatives of \(D(vS)=d'd''(vS)\) vanish by the
distributional identities \((d')^2=(d'')^2=0\) and
\(d'd''=-d''d'\).  This does not differentiate a nonsmooth
coefficient informally: \(vS\) is a well-defined current by
continuous multiplication with a coefficient-Radon current, and
all derivatives here are distributional.  The R6 statement is
ordinary-local and already independent of all actual refinements,
so no additional test or chart reduction is used.  The germ
assertion follows by choosing a representative for (AP24.1).
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Automatic local DC regularity of a continuous potential]
In the proposition it is enough that \(v\) be finite continuous
and satisfy (AP24.1).  For every point \(x\in V\), one may
choose an ordinary neighborhood \(V_x\subset V\), before
choosing \(S\), on which \(v\in\mathcal D(V_x)\).
The action identity (AP24.2) then holds on all of \(V\) by
ordinary locality.  We do not assert a global DC decomposition
on a previously prescribed \(V\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose one finite presentation (AP24.3) about \(x\), and shrink
once so that all \(g_i=g_i^+-g_i^-\) have continuous psh
components on that representative.  Choose a relatively compact
ordinary neighborhood \(V_x\) inside it.  The continuous
coefficients are bounded there.  With
\(G=\sum_i(g_i^++g_i^-)\), take a finite \(C\ge0\)
such that \(|f_i|\le C\) on \(V_x\).  Positivity of the
individual curvatures and (AP24.1) give
\[
                -CD[G]\le D[v]\le CD[G]
                    \quad\hbox{on }V_x.                  \tag{AP24.5a}
\]
The functions \(CG+v\) and \(CG-v\) are finite continuous
and have positive original curvature.  The exact frozen R6
lemma \texttt{r6-continuous-positive-classical} makes them
classical psh, locally and hence on \(V_x\).  Therefore
\[
              v=\tfrac12\bigl((CG+v)-(CG-v)\bigr)
                              \in\mathcal D(V_x).          \tag{AP24.5b}
\]
This construction depends on \(\alpha,v,x\), but not on a
background or test.  Apply the proposition on each \(V_x\).
The two sides of (AP24.2) are intrinsic ordinary currents on
\(V\), since multiplication of \(S\) by the given continuous
\(v\) is already defined.  The local identities consequently
glue, proving the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A weaker sufficient target after the RV reduction]
Let \(A\) be the symmetric finitely piecewise-constant PS germ
in RV12, with full \(d'A=0\), and use the accepted PH/QT
preparation.  Thus, on one ordinary representative,
\[
       q\in\mathcal D(V),\qquad
       \gamma\in B^{0,0,1}(V),\qquad
       D_\delta q=A-\gamma .                              \tag{AP24.6}
\]
If \([\gamma]=D[v]\) for some \(v\in\mathcal D(V)\), then
\[
             M_S(A)=D((q+v)S),\qquad D M_S(A)=0            \tag{AP24.7}
\]
for every allowed \(S\), in every legal degree.  In particular
the QA obstruction of \(A\) vanishes for all
\(0\le p\le n-2\).  This conclusion does not require
\(\gamma=0\), a piecewise-linear potential for \(\gamma\),
or an actual delta-form structure on \(v\).
By the preceding corollary it is enough to have a finite
continuous \(v\) satisfying the ordinary current equation,
with local DC decompositions obtained after initial shrinking.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
QT1--QT3 prove (AP24.6), including the full boundary term
\(\gamma\), and prove that the finite piecewise-quadratic
\(q\) is locally an original convex difference.  It follows that
\([A]=D[q+v]\).  Apply the proposition to \(\alpha=A\).
Alternatively, the proposition for \(\gamma\), the frozen
identity \(M_S(D_\delta q)=D(qS)\), and linearity give the
same equality.  The chosen \(V,q,v\) precede every subsequent
choice of \(S\) and compact test.
\end{proof}

Here is the exact quadratic application if the other RV gate has
also been supplied.  For a finite signed PL quadratic polynomial
\(P=\sum_j a_j[h_j][g_j]\), let
\[
 Z=\sum_j a_j E(h_j,g_j),\qquad
 E(h,g)=\tfrac12(d'_Ph\wedge d''_Pg+d'_Pg\wedge d''_Ph).
                                                               \tag{AP24.8}
\]
The frozen Leibniz identity gives
\(
 \widetilde\tau(P)=\tfrac12D_\delta(\sum_j a_jh_jg_j)-Z
\).
QA therefore gives
\(
 \mathcal A_S(P)=-D M_S(Z)
\).
If the exact balanced lift RV4 has been provided, RV5--RV8 replace
\(Z\) by a separately closed \(A\), changing it by full
\(d'\)- and \(d''\)-exact degree-one forms whose QA action is
zero.  Under the additional potential hypothesis in (AP24.6),
(AP24.7) now gives \(\mathcal A_S(P)=0\) for every allowed
\(S\).  This implication is conditional on both existence steps.
It supplies no carrier-CLN certificate: the unchanged IF
action/full-polar distinction prevents that further inference.
Common additional signed mixed tails may be absorbed into \(S\)
by finite positive-tail expansion in legal degrees.  Unrelated
termwise tails are not identified by this observation.

\subsection{The first-derivative relation which is still missing}

For a pure scalar codimension-one \(\gamma\), the R6 module
presentation can be chosen in the form (AP24.3) with continuous
PS \(f_i\) and finite continuous PL \(g_i\).  Every
\(D_\delta g_i\) is fully separately closed.  Thus full
\(d'\gamma=0\) says
\[
               \sum_i d'_Pf_i\wedge D_\delta g_i=0
                         \quad\hbox{in }B^{2,1}(V).        \tag{AP24.9}
\]
For each fixed allowed \(S\), the already proved Radon Leibniz
rule gives the legal ordinary identity
\[
               d'M_S(\gamma)
                    =\sum_i d'_Pf_i\wedge D(g_iS).         \tag{AP24.10}
\]
Indeed each \(D(g_iS)\) is a finite signed expansion of allowed
positive separately closed coefficient-Radon currents, to which
R6's continuous-PS Radon product rule applies.  No boundary of
\(D_\delta g_i\) has been discarded in (AP24.9), and no
derivative of a moving approximation is used in (AP24.10).

The implication from (AP24.9) to vanishing of the right side of
(AP24.10) has not been proved.  R6's scalar-coefficient theorem
applies to \(\sum_i f_iD[g_i]\), not to this covector-coefficient
relation.  We do not define an action on an arbitrary
\(B^{2,1}\) object by writing the right side and assuming
presentation independence.  The ambiguity RV10, where a normal
one-form times a nonzero cap is zero, also prevents unrestricted
coefficient extraction.  If the implication were established for
these particular \(\gamma\), it would already imply their QA
action vanishes, without proving RV15's stronger zero assertion.

\subsection{Why the represented curvature interval does not create a potential}

There is an available order bound, but not the necessary
surjectivity theorem.  On a relatively compact subdomain where
(AP24.3) is fixed, expand \(g_i=g_i^+-g_i^-\) into continuous
psh functions and set \(G=\sum_i(g_i^++g_i^-)\).
Choose \(C\) larger than the absolute values of all coefficients
there.  Positivity of the individual curvatures gives
\[
                       -C D[G]\le[\gamma]\le C D[G].      \tag{AP24.11}
\]
For the RV/QT scalar boundary \(\gamma=A-D_\delta q\), symmetry
and full separate closedness hold.  Hence
\(CD[G]\pm[\gamma]\) are positive separately closed ordinary
currents.  They have not thereby acquired continuous scalar
potentials.

The exact compact set in R6's curvature-interval theorem is
\[
 \mathscr A(G,C;V)
  =\{D[u]:u\in\mathscr P(G,C;V)\},                         \tag{AP24.12}
\]
where \(\mathscr P\) consists of already existing normalized
continuous psh potentials with the specified ambient order bound.
Its weak compactness and closedness show that a weak limit of
members of this represented family remains represented.  Neither
its definition nor its proof identifies it with all positive
closed currents between \(0\) and \(CD[G]\).
To use it here one must first construct a net of represented
curvatures, on the same \(V\) and in a common such interval,
converging on every original test to the required current.
No such net has been constructed.  R6's continuous-positive
converse and HU/HL scalar harmonic recognition start with a
continuous function; they do not supply the missing function
from the current (AP24.11).

\subsection{Intersecting cap branches do not form a rank-one coefficient space}

The following elementary original pressure test limits a possible
interpretation of the desired coefficient sheaf.  It is not a
counterexample to RV15 or to the continuous-potential existence
target.  Work on an ordinary two-torus polyannulus about the joint
radius-one Gauss point \(x\), with
\[
 s_i=\log|T_i|,\qquad
 C_i=D((s_i)_+[U])\quad(i=1,2).                            \tag{AP24.13}
\]
These are genuine positive separately closed original currents,
the ordinary currents of pure scalar codimension-one delta-forms.
Their supports are the complete normal Gauss fibers, by the
frozen CM1/R9 support theorem.  In particular the points
\(\eta_{1,r}\), for \(r>1\) close to one, lie in
\(\operatorname{supp}C_1\) and outside
\(\operatorname{supp}C_2\); the points \(\eta_{r,1}\) have
the reverse property.  Both actual Gauss-radius paths converge
to \(x\).

If \(a,b\in\mathbf R\) with \(a\ne b\), there is no finite
continuous scalar \(c\) on any ordinary representative of this
germ such that
\[
                      aC_1+bC_2=c(C_1+C_2).                \tag{AP24.14}
\]
To prove this, near \(\eta_{1,r}\) the current \(C_2\) is
zero.  Equality would give \((c-a)C_1=0\) there.  A continuous
scalar multiplying a nonzero positive coefficient-Radon current
can vanish only by being zero on its support: otherwise its
nonzero fixed sign on a small neighborhood is detected by a
positive compact test.  Thus \(c(\eta_{1,r})=a\).
Similarly \(c(\eta_{r,1})=b\).  The two limits and continuity
force \(c(x)=a=b\), a contradiction.

Consequently closedness does not turn a multi-branch cap system
into one continuous scalar coefficient relative to its sum, even
before asking for a locally constant coefficient.  Both weights
in this diagnostic are constant and there is no centered
homogeneous vanishing hypothesis.  Also its currents already have
the explicit continuous PL potential
\(a(s_1)_++b(s_2)_+\).  The test only rules out this rank-one
substitution for a branch-sensitive cycle module.  It adds no
KC or RV counterexample.

\subsection{The geometric continuation step is not supplied by tameness alone}

On a fixed full-rank calibrated refinement, a pure scalar
codimension-one presentation of \(\gamma\) can be reduced to
effective scalar coefficients on its cut-cells.  Full
\(d'_P\gamma=0\) makes each such coefficient constant along
that cell.  Artificial subdivision merely restricts this same
coefficient.  A different actual refinement can, however, change
the calibrated branches and their weighted sums.  Across genuine
incidences the closed-cycle condition is a balancing condition;
it is not an assertion that all branch coefficients are one
scalar.  The preceding pressure test explains that distinction
on original analytic data.

The required additional theorem would give a refinement-compatible
cycle-coefficient object for this fixed finite presentation,
with enough ordinary-local specialization toward \(x\) to
force its closed section to vanish when its centered coefficients
vanish there.  We have constructed neither that specialization
nor a finite detector for all later local refining domains.
This is a precise remaining proof step, not a new defined theory.
UR rules out replacing it by a tangent lift of the old Euler
vector on every local cell.  Its counterexample boundary is not
closed and therefore does not decide this coupled continuation
question.

The primary tameness results checked during this attempt have
narrower typed conclusions.  Hrushovski--Loeser's
\emph{Non-archimedean tame topology and stably dominated types},
in the 166-page author version, Theorem 13.4.1, proves local
contractibility of \(B_F(X)\) for a definable subset \(X\) of
an algebraic variety.  This does not identify our absolute
signed-cycle support or its effect

title: A background-independent closed certificate for relation descent
text:
carrier_cln_relation_certificates.tex \section{A background-independent closed certificate for relation descent}
\label{sec:r12-carrier-cln-certificates}

The preceding conditional construction does not itself prove the
analytic relation quotient. Here we give a quantitative sufficient
certificate which involves only actual functions on a closed carrier,
not a choice of positive background. Its completion is taken in a
potential norm controlled by relative CLN. The missing assertion is
whether actual analytic relations supply this certificate.

Fix an allowed original ordinary open \(U\), and let
\(\mathcal D(U)\) be the real vector space of finite continuous
locally bounded classical psh differences. Write
\[
                \mathcal P^b(U)=\operatorname{Sym}^b_{\mathbb R}
                                      \mathcal D(U),\qquad b\ge1.
 \tag{KC1}
\]
A monomial \(h_1\cdots h_b\) here is a \emph{formal curvature
polynomial}; its prescribed action on a positive closed \(Q\) is
\(L_{h_1}\cdots L_{h_b}Q\). It is not ordinary multiplication of
the resulting currents. The frozen signed bounded calculus makes
this action well-defined, symmetric and linear in each factor.
Every finite cycle presentation under consideration, with its
prescribed finite convex-PL representation, has such a polynomial
representative after expanding its specified convex differences.
We do not quotient (KC1) by the unknown actual analytic kernel.

Let \(F\subset U\) be closed. Call \(h\in\mathcal D(U)\)
\(F\)-harmonic if, near each point of \(F\), its values on \(F\)
agree with a finite continuous original function whose original
current curvature is zero. Define \(\mathcal Z_F^b\) to be the
linear span of the following explicitly permitted relations:
\begin{enumerate}
\item monomials having one \(F\)-harmonic factor;
\item monomials \(h_1\cdots h_b\) whose ordinary pointwise product
      is zero on \(F\);
\item finite identities already zero in a common ambient real
      PL cycle algebra, with their original moment pullbacks.
\end{enumerate}
The third item invokes only the frozen ambient functional calculus.
An identity only known after actual analytic pullback is not an
allowed generator. Local versions on ordinary neighborhoods of
the carrier are permitted when applying the resulting assertion
to a correspondingly localized test.

\begin{lemma}[The finite carrier certificate]
\label{lem:r12-finite-carrier-certificate}
If \(Q\) is any original middle-positive separately closed
background carried by \(F\), then
\[
                              \mathcal A_Q(Z)=0
                              \qquad(Z\in\mathcal Z_F^b)
 \tag{KC2}
\]
in every permitted degree, on all original tests and refinements.
The same is true after any additional finite signed mixed tail.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the
ordinary harmonic quotient, (LT7), and the frozen ambient action.

\begin{proof}
Every mixed tail remains carried by \(F\), by ordinary support
locality. For an \(F\)-harmonic factor, replace it locally on \(F\)
by its original harmonic witness in multiplication with that tail.
Their coefficient products agree before applying \(D\), and the
frozen original harmonic potential quotient kills the insertion.
Finite signed positive-tail expansion treats signed tails. A
pointwise zero-product monomial is exactly (LT7), whose induction
uses the ordinary open where its first factor is nonzero.
Ambient relations act by zero by the printed frozen input.
Linearity and ordinary locality prove (KC2).
\end{proof}

\subsection{Relative CLN with bounds only on the actual carrier}

For a compact \(L\Subset U\), define
\[
 \|h\|_{F,L}=\sup_{F\cap L}|h|,\qquad
 \operatorname{osc}_{F,L}u
          =\inf_{c\in\mathbb R}\sup_{F\cap L}|u-c|.
 \tag{KC3}
\]
Both quantities are set to zero if \(F\cap L\) is empty.
The latter is a centered oscillation, not the uncentered
supremum minus infimum.

\begin{lemma}[A carrier-only mixed estimate]
\label{lem:r12-carrier-only-CLN}
Fix an original compact complementary test \(\eta\) for a
length-\(b\) insertion and the degree of the background.
There is a fixed larger compact stage \(L\Subset U\), finitely
many compact positive coefficient controls \(\Xi_\ell\) on that
stage, and \(C_\eta<\infty\), independent of \(F,Q\) and of the
potentials, such that
\[
 \left|\left\langle L_hL_{u_2}\cdots L_{u_b}Q,\eta\right\rangle\right|
 \le C_\eta\left(\sum_\ell\langle Q,\Xi_\ell\rangle\right)
       \|h\|_{F,L}\prod_{j=2}^b\operatorname{osc}_{F,L}u_j.
 \tag{KC4}
\]
Here \(Q\) is positive and separately closed, carried by \(F\);
\(h\in\mathcal D(U)\); and \(u_2,\ldots,u_b\) are continuous
locally bounded original classical psh on the same \(U\).
The empty product when \(b=1\) is one. Every additional actual
refinement of \(\eta\) is allowed.

For positive tuples the corresponding usual local coefficient
CLN estimate likewise uses only the centered bounds on \(F\cap L\).
For the signed first factor in (KC4), only the displayed test
pairing estimate is asserted, not coefficient total-variation
control by its small supremum.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the
frozen finite-control relative CLN proof, with its carrier
restriction made explicit.

\begin{proof}
Choose the usual \(b\) nested compact stages between the support
of \(\eta\) and \(L\). Every positive mixed tail is carried by
\(F\): neither multiplication by a continuous scalar nor
distributional differentiation enlarges the support.
In the one-step control (LT2), multiplication by the potential
is consequently estimated by its supremum on \(F\cap L\), not
by values outside that carrier. The same fixed positive trace
controls and cutoff derivatives work; their construction does
not use the potentials. Iterating proves the carrier-only
positive CLN bound. Subtracting an arbitrary constant from any
psh slot preserves classicality and changes no insertion.
Taking the infimum over these finitely many constants gives the
centered bounds in (KC3).

For (KC4), put \(T=L_{u_2}\cdots L_{u_b}Q\). It is positive,
separately closed and carried by \(F\), and
\[
               \langle L_hT,\eta\rangle=\langle hT,D\eta\rangle.
\]
Finite original coefficient domination bounds this last pairing
by \(\|h\|_{F,L}\) times the compact coefficient controls of \(T\).
The just proved positive-tail estimate controls these by the
right side of (KC4). No estimate for the variation of \(D(hT)\)
has been inferred from a bounded scalar multiplier.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The carrier-CLN relation seminorm]
\label{def:r12-carrier-cln-seminorm}
For \(P\in\mathcal P^b(U)\) and a compact \(L\Subset U\), put
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|P\|^{\rm cln}_{F,L}
  &=\inf
       \sum_{\nu=1}^N |c_\nu|\,\|h_\nu\|_{F,L}
                  \prod_{j=2}^b\operatorname{osc}_{F,L}u_{\nu j},\\
 P&=Z+\sum_{\nu=1}^N c_\nu h_\nu u_{\nu2}\cdots u_{\nu b},
             \qquad Z\in\mathcal Z_F^b .
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{KC5}
\]
The infimum ranges over all displayed finite decompositions.
Their identities are formal polynomial identities,
or identities in the explicitly permitted frozen ambient cycle
quotient. Each \(h_\nu\) lies in \(\mathcal D(U)\), and each
\(u_{\nu j}\) is continuous locally bounded classical psh on \(U\).
The infimum is finite: expand each difference in all but its
first slot. Finite concatenation and scaling show that (KC5)
is a seminorm on the displayed formal quotient. It depends on
the original functions and the closed set \(F\), but not on \(Q\).
It is not declared to be a seminorm on actual analytic delta-forms.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The closed carrier certificate annihilates every background]
\label{thm:r12-carrier-cln-zero-certificate}
For every \(Q\) in Lemma~\ref{lem:r12-carrier-only-CLN},
\[
          |\langle\mathcal A_Q(P),\eta\rangle|
          \le C_\eta\left(\sum_\ell\langle Q,\Xi_\ell\rangle\right)
                                      \|P\|^{\rm cln}_{F,L}.
 \tag{KC6}
\]
In particular, if the seminorm is zero on every required enlarged
compact stage, then \(\mathcal A_Q(P)=0\) on all original tests,
simultaneously for every allowed background carried by \(F\).
Finite certificates may be replaced by arbitrarily small
remainders in (KC5); no background regularization is needed.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for this
background-independent closed-certificate principle. It is a
sufficient relation test, not identification of the analytic kernel.

\begin{proof}
For any decomposition in (KC5), the \(Z\)-term vanishes by (KC2).
Apply (KC4) to each remaining term, sum, and take the infimum.
The controls and \(C_\eta\) are fixed before that decomposition,
so they do not grow with its number of terms or its real
subdivision complexity. This gives (KC6). Zero seminorm kills
each arbitrary original compact pairing. The stage may depend
on that test, as in ordinary current equality; there is no
restriction to a fixed finite moment test family.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A conditional all-unit route back to the pure-cycle quotient}

For a tuple of original units \(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)\) on an
ordinary open \(O\subset U\), put \(s_i=\log|f_i|\) and define
\[
 Q_{f,\mathbf a}(S)
       =T_{S,c}((s_1-a_1)_+,\ldots,(s_c-a_c)_+),\qquad
 F_{f,\mathbf a}
       =\operatorname{supp}Q_{f,\mathbf a}([O]).
 \tag{KC7}
\]
The second set is the \emph{absolute cap carrier}, not the whole
norm level. Frozen R7 positive-zero descent gives
\[
                    \operatorname{supp}Q_{f,\mathbf a}(S)
                                            \subset F_{f,\mathbf a}.
 \tag{KC8}
\]
Indeed on the ordinary complement the positive point cycle has
zero absolute actual pullback, so its prescribed action on every
allowed \(S\) vanishes. For smooth original parameter maps,
frozen R9 identifies this carrier with the complete joint Gauss
fiber and supplies its all-original-test factorization. We use
only (KC8); no new-field quotient is assumed.

\begin{proposition}[A uniform carrier-certificate criterion]
\label{prop:r12-carrier-certificate-pure-cycle-quotient}
Let \(P\) represent a finite pure degree-\(b\) PL cycle expression
on \(U\), let \(S\) have arbitrary allowed degree \(p\), and put
\(P_0=p+b<n\), \(q=n-P_0\). Choose an integer
\[
       1\le c\le
       \max\{\,q\bmod2,\ q-2\lfloor p/2\rfloor\,\}.
 \tag{KC9}
\]
Suppose that for every ordinary localization and every tuple of
\(c\) original units, the following background-independent
condition holds: for Lebesgue-almost every parameter \(\mathbf a\),
\[
                      \|P\|^{\rm cln}_{F_{f,\mathbf a},L}=0
 \tag{KC10}
\]
on every compact stage required by (KC6). A countable exhaustion
on a local affinoid neighborhood may be used for these stages.
Then \(\mathcal A_S(P)=0\) for every such arbitrary \(S\), on
all original tests and all actual refinements.

This proposition does not assert (KC10) for every actual-zero
presentation. It concerns pure cycle expressions; variable PS
coefficient relations are not silently reduced to this statement.
If \(q=0\), or the right side of (KC9) is zero, it supplies no
positive-rank cap criterion.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{CONDITIONAL}} for the analytic
quotient implication, with the stated reduction completely proved.

\begin{proof}
For fixed \(f,\mathbf a\), (KC8) makes its relative cap an allowed
positive closed background carried by \(F_{f,\mathbf a}\).
The closed-certificate theorem gives
\(\mathcal A_{Q_{f,\mathbf a}(S)}(P)=0\) for almost every parameter.
For each original compact test, these particular pairings are
continuous in \(\mathbf a\): expand the fixed \(P\) into finitely
many bounded convex-PL tuples, adjoin the Lipschitz hinge tuple,
and apply the frozen joint local-uniform bounded BT theorem.
Consequently they vanish at every parameter. This uses the
canonical cap-derived family, not continuity postulated for an
arbitrary Radon disintegration.

The frozen signed coarea identity now gives
\[
       \bigwedge_{i=1}^c(d's_i\wedge d''s_i)
                         \wedge\mathcal A_S(P)=0
                         \quad\text{for every such original tuple}.
 \tag{KC11}
\]
Its commutation with the pure response follows from signed mixed
symmetry; no coefficient derivative is suppressed. The response
is symmetric and has regularizable curvature depth \(b\), because
its original finite PL representatives have \(b\) such slots.
The sharp depth-sensitive all-unit detector (HD7)--(HD8), with
total degree \(P_0=p+b\) and retained depth \(b\), has threshold
exactly (KC9). It therefore gives zero on the entire original
test sheaf. Neither fixed-moment caps alone nor tests only on a
chosen Gauss section have been used.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The attempted degree-two proof and its exact stopping point.}
For two nonzero positive degree-two cycles with the same actual
pullback on a full ordinary three-dimensional-image germ, write
their difference using a fixed finite polynomial \(P\).
Actual zero implies zero after multiplication by every actual cap,
and hence zero on each corresponding absolute integration cap.
This is valid also for a genuinely nonmatroidal,
non-simplicial-polytopal germ; it is not the missing step.

The attempted next implication was
\[
 \mathcal A_{Q_{f,\mathbf a}([O])}(P)=0
       \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
                       \|P\|^{\rm cln}_{F_{f,\mathbf a},L}=0.
 \tag{KC12}
\]
It has not been proved. The estimate (KC6) goes in the opposite
direction and cannot be reversed. A vanishing signed cap cycle
does not by itself provide a finite pointwise zero-product
decomposition, harmonic ordinary traces, or approximations of
these with a small carrier remainder. Disintegration only
represents the already defined response measures; it does not
construct such potential identities. Replacing the correct
carrier by a norm level invokes the false assertion (CQ9),
while reversing coarea into closed division invokes (CQ5).

Thus (KC12), restricted to presentations already actual-zero on
the original ordinary germ and with the full actual refinements
retained, is a precise additional analytic-to-carrier closure
gate. Its status is \texttt{OPEN}; the proposed automatic use
of (KC6) to prove it is a \texttt{FAILED\_ATTEMPT}.
No new nonmatroidal degree-two quotient, no pair of actual-equal
positive cycles with different arbitrary-\(S\) actions, and no
low-degree signed order transfer has been established here.
The exact frozen \(\Gamma_4\) quotient is not counted anew.

\paragraph{Dependencies and non-circularity.}
The proofs use only frozen original bounded BT, its finite-control
relative CLN estimate, its continuous harmonic quotient and
ambient PL action; the carrier zero-product lemma (LT7);
the positive-zero cap support input of R7; frozen R8/R9 coarea
and parameter continuity; and the independently proved R12
depth detector. They use neither OPEN-GQ nor OPEN-CTO, no
\(\mathcal W_{\rm loc}\) density, and no arbitrary-background
BT theory over a completed residue field. The new seminorm is
defined before any actual analytic relation quotient.
