title: Conditional arbitrary-companion transfer from intrinsic harmonic locality
text:
S23_conditional_harmonic_locality_and_arbitrary_companion_transfer.tex \section{Conditional arbitrary-companion transfer from intrinsic harmonic locality}
\label{sec:r24-harmonic-locality-arbitrary-companions}

\paragraph{Status.}
This is a \texttt{CONDITIONAL} deduction with zero new principal
theorem count. Its explicit antecedent is the still open intrinsic
harmonic-locality assertion IL20 for genuine original full polars.
The scalar recognition HL3 and the HC equivalence identify that
antecedent with the corresponding original local-unit drift gate
NC12/HE7 in their printed setting. No proof of that antecedent is
supplied here. The purpose is to replace the global-comparator
shortcut disproved by BC with an exact, sufficient local-measure
interface, while retaining every fixed-domain quantifier.

All fields, norms, spaces and ordinary opens are original. The
spaces \(\mathcal D\), the closed carrier \(F\), compact stage \(L\),
formal symmetric powers, relation generators and seminorms are
exactly KC1--KC5. In particular a full polar is a polar of that
entire seminorm, not a real conormal current selected independently.

\subsection{The precise assumption}

Choose an original ordinary \(U\) in a good affinoid interior.
For every closed carrier \(F\subset U\), every compact
\(L\Subset U\), every degree \(m\ge2\), every genuine original
unit full polar \(\Lambda\) of \(q^{U,m}_{F,L}\), and arbitrary
fixed \(u_3,\ldots,u_m\in\mathcal D(U)\), IR and IL give a finite
signed measure \(\nu_{u,u_3,\ldots,u_m}\) supported on
\(C=F\cap L\), characterized by
\[
 \Lambda([k][u][u_3]\cdots[u_m])
       =\int_C k\,d\nu_{u,u_3,\ldots,u_m}
       \qquad(k,u\in\mathcal D(U)).                         \tag{LC24.1}
\]
We assume, on this same \(U\), the following assertion:
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 u\in\mathcal D(U),\quad W\subset U\text{ ordinary open},\\
 u|_{F\cap W}\text{ has original continuous harmonic trace
 witnesses locally at every point}\\
 \Longrightarrow\quad
 \nu_{u,u_3,\ldots,u_m}|_W=0 .
 \end{gathered}                                             \tag{LC24.2}
\]
All choices in the preceding paragraph are quantified in this
assumption. It concerns restriction of a measure already defined
from \(\Lambda\), not restriction of \(\Lambda\) to a new
localized relation quotient.

\subsection{Strict geometric defect gives local harmonicity without global witnesses}

Let \(\pi:Y\to U_*\) be an original finite \'{e}tale surjection
of degree \(d\ge1\), let \(x\in U_*\), and fix a global analytic
unit \(g\) on \(Y\). GP prepares one ordinary \(U\ni x\),
a power frame \(e\) of the finite algebra, and a finite analytic
gallery from its flag to the flag of \(ge\).
Every relevant prefix and adjacent-exchange coordinate minor is
a unit on the complete actual ordering cover \(q:Z_U\to U\).
This preparation depends on \(\pi,g,x\), not on a later weight
\(w\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\), degree, carrier, compact stage, polar,
or downstream tail. The additional finite coefficient selection
in CW is not used here.

For an adjacent exchange use the notation
\[
 a=W\wedge u,\quad b=W\wedge v,\quad
 \alpha=\log\|a\|_w,\quad \beta=\log\|b\|_w,\quad
 c=\log\|W\|_w,\quad d_0=\log\|W\wedge u\wedge v\|_w,
                                                               \tag{LC24.3}
\]
where the norms on the actual ordering cover are the diagonal
sheet norms with weights pulled back from \(w\). Their prefix
formulas are finite maxima of sums of those weights and logarithms
of the protected analytic minors. FS4--FS5 therefore descend all
four functions as members of \(\mathcal D(U)\), for arbitrary
\(w\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\).
Set
\[
                         H=\alpha-\beta,\qquad
                         K_0=\alpha+\beta-c-d_0\ge0.        \tag{LC24.4}
\]
The last inequality is the exact exterior-norm inequality proved
in FG/CW; it is pointwise on all original analytic points.

\begin{lemma}[Local harmonicity of the strict-defect function]
For every \(w\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\), the descended scalar \(H\)
is original current-harmonic locally on the ordinary open
\(\{K_0>0\}\subset U\). No global harmonic comparator on \(U\)
is asserted.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix an original point \(z\) of the ordering cover above
\(y\in\{K_0>0\}\). The strict exterior inequality in CW18--CW20
applies with the continuous positive weights of this \(w\).
Choose a coordinate \(I\) maximizing the weighted norm of \(a\).
The strict determinant inequality makes it a maximizer for \(b\)
as well, and gives
\[
          \|a/a_I-b/b_I\|_w<q_I
\]
at \(z\), where \(q_I\) is the weight of that coordinate.
Both normalized vectors have \(I\)-coordinate \(1\).
The strict inequality persists on an ordinary neighborhood of
\(z\), since the weights are continuous and \(a_I,b_I\) are
protected analytic units. The ultrametric inequality then gives
equality of the two normalized vector norms throughout that
neighborhood. Consequently
\[
                          q^*H=\log|a_I/b_I|               \tag{LC24.5}
\]
there. The exterior-norm identity used to pass from the prefix
defect to this inequality is the same finite Gaussian-elimination
identity in CW18; it uses no PL presentation of \(w\).

There are finitely many actual points over \(y\). Apply (LC24.5)
near each of them. Finite properness allows one ordinary
neighborhood \(V\ni y\) whose complete inverse image lies in
the union of these neighborhoods. Thus \(q^*H\) and
\(-q^*H\) are classically psh on all of \(q^{-1}(V)\).
The finite-surjective scalar descent theorem used in FS, applied
separately to the two signs, makes \(H|_V\) classically
pluriharmonic. HL3 identifies it with an original continuous
current-harmonic function, and indeed with a local original
unit-logarithm sum. This is a scalar descent on the complete
finite inverse image. No arbitrary current has been pulled
through the finite map, and no full polar has been localized.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Conditional exchange with every downstream tail retained}

Assume (LC24.2) on the prepared \(U\). For any full polar and
any fixed additional \(\mathcal D(U)\)-tails, the preceding
lemma and (LC24.2) show that the measure with distinguished tail
\(H\) is zero on \(\{K_0>0\}\).
Its remaining support is contained in \(\{K_0=0\}\).
Equation (LC24.1) therefore gives
\[
                 \Lambda([K_0][H]R)=0                    \tag{LC24.6}
\]
for every formal monomial \(R\) in arbitrary downstream
\(\mathcal D(U)\)-factors. The total degree is at least \(2\);
the measure is finite and \(K_0\) is continuous, so this
integration on its support is legitimate.

For \(b\ge2\), put \(A=\alpha-c\), \(B=\beta-c\) and
\(T=d_0-c\). The real polynomial
\[
 A^b+(T-A)^b-B^b-(T-B)^b
\]
is divisible by \((A-B)(A+B-T)\). Indeed it vanishes at
\(A=B\) and at \(A=T-B\); these are relatively prime linear
polynomials in \(\mathbf R[A,B,T]\).
Their product is \(H K_0\), and the quotient is homogeneous of
degree \(b-2\). This is an exact formal polynomial identity
in the degree-one space \(\mathcal D(U)\).
Expanding the quotient into finitely many monomials, multiplying
by any extra monomial \(R\), and applying (LC24.6) proves that
every full polar annihilates the adjacent power-sum difference
times \(R\). CV2 yields
\[
 q^{U,b+\deg R}_{F,L}
 \left(
   \bigl([\alpha-c]^b+[d_0-\alpha]^b
        -[\beta-c]^b-[d_0-\beta]^b\bigr)R
 \right)=0.                                                 \tag{LC24.7}
\]
For \(b=1\) the displayed difference is literally zero.
At joins between two analytic adapted frames for the same flag,
the prefix logs change by logarithms of global base unit
determinants. Expanding powers then gives the exact harmonic
factor certificates, including all factors in \(R\).
Summing (LC24.7) along the fixed gallery gives UT5, and hence
UT7, for every \(w\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\), without a fixed
finite-unit PL restriction. In degree \(d=1\), this conclusion
already follows from the global unit factor and needs no exchange.

\subsection{The original KC limit still has a uniform budget}

We record explicitly why the remainder of UT is valid for these
arbitrary companions. Define the specific sorted polynomial
\(B_b^\pi\) and its polarization \(\mathcal T_b^\pi\) by UT2.
The invariant Courant argument in UT2--UT3 was already proved
for arbitrary \(\mathcal D(Y_U)\)-inputs: its auxiliary invariant
finite PL expressions lie in \(\mathcal D\) by lattice closure,
and FS descends them. Its error terms are literal full-carrier
zero-product generators, even after multiplication by arbitrary
downstream tails.

Fix \(F,L\), and put \(C=F\cap L\). If \(C\) is empty,
all relevant KC costs are zero. Otherwise fix
\(v=p-r\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\) with one global original psh
difference decomposition. Let \(\Delta_{I,k}\) be the protected
prefix minors of \(e\), and set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 D_C&=\max_{k,I}\|\log|\Delta_{I,k}|\|_{q^{-1}(C)},\\
 M_C&=d\bigl(\|p\|_{\pi^{-1}(C)}
                    +\|r\|_{\pi^{-1}(C)}\bigr)+D_C.
 \end{aligned}                                               \tag{LC24.8}
\]
The lifts are complete compact inverse images. For \(N\ge1\),
the invariant maxima
\[
 \max_{|I|=k}\left(
     \sum_{i\in I}p_i+\sum_{i\notin I}r_i
                      +N^{-1}\log|\Delta_{I,k}|\right)
                                                               \tag{LC24.9}
\]
are finite continuous psh functions on the ordering cover and
descend psh by FS. At \(k=0\) use \(\operatorname{Tr}_\pi r\)
and the empty minor of logarithm zero. Their differences give
\(N^{-1}(L_k^e(Nv)-L_{k-1}^e(Nv))\).
Omitting the minor term gives the corresponding order statistic
\(a_k(v)\). Their uniform difference on \(C\) is at most
\(2D_C/N\), and both chosen psh-difference decompositions have
total centered oscillation cost at most \(2M_C\).
These facts use only \(v=p-r\), not a finite PL presentation.

If \(R=\prod_{j=1}^{\ell}[z_j]\), choose each fixed
\(z_j=p_j-r_j\), and put
\(J_j=\operatorname{osc}_C p_j+\operatorname{osc}_C r_j\).
The exact KC telescope UT12--UT14 gives
\[
 q^{U,b+\ell}_{F,L}
 \left(\bigl(N^{-b}C_b^e(Nv)-B_b^\pi(v)\bigr)R\right)
 \le
 \frac{2dbD_C}{N}(2M_C)^{b-1}\prod_{j=1}^{\ell} J_j.              \tag{LC24.10}
\]
Here \(e\) in \(C_b^e\) denotes the fixed frame and
\(\ell=\deg R\).
Empty carrier stages have zero cost; zero oscillation budgets
and \(b=1\) have the same conventions as UT14.

Put \(h=\log|g|\). The conditional UT7 just proved can be
iterated at the weights \(Nv+jh\) for every integer \(j\):
all these weights belong to \(\mathcal D(Y_U)\).
For each fixed integer \(M\), forward or reverse telescoping
gives
\[
 q^{U,b+\deg R}_{F,L}
 \left(
  \bigl(C_b^e(N(v+Mh))-C_b^e(Nv)\bigr)R
 \right)=0 .
\]
Apply (LC24.10) to the two fixed functions \(v+Mh,v\),
and let \(N\to\infty\). This yields
\[
 q^{U,b+\deg R}_{F,L}
        \left((B_b^\pi(v+Mh)-B_b^\pi(v))R\right)=0
                    \quad(M\in\mathbf Z).                 \tag{LC24.11}
\]
The same initial \(U\), frame and finite gallery are used for
all \(N,M,v\). No limit in the analytic relation ideal is asserted;
the conclusion follows from the displayed numerical bound in
the unchanged seminorm.

The Vandermonde inversion at \(M=1,\ldots,b\), using UT3,
gives
\(q(\mathcal T_b^\pi(h,v,\ldots,v)R)=0\).
Finite polarization in \(v\) gives the conclusion for unrelated
\(v_2,\ldots,v_b\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\). The zero-product
certificate errors remain legal after \(R\).
For \(b=1\), the trace is the global harmonic function
\(\log|\operatorname{Norm}_\pi g|\), so the result is direct.

\begin{proposition}[Conditional arbitrary-companion unit transfer]
For the fixed original finite \'{e}tale cover, point \(x\) and
global unit \(g\), choose the GP representative \(U\) before all
weights, degrees, carriers, stages, polars and downstream tails.
If (LC24.2) holds on this same \(U\), then for every \(b\ge1\),
every \(v_2,\ldots,v_b\in\mathcal D(Y_U)\), every closed
\(F\subset U\), every compact \(L\Subset U\), and every finite
formal downstream monomial \(R\) in \(\mathcal D(U)\),
\[
 q^{U,b+\deg R}_{F,L}
       \bigl(\mathcal T_b^\pi(\log|g|,v_2,\ldots,v_b)R\bigr)=0.
                                                               \tag{LC24.12}
\]
The degree-one case does not require the assumption.
\end{proposition}

The proof above is the complete deduction. When \(F\) is an
actual absolute cap carrier, it is kept unchanged. KC6 gives
the action consequence in all permitted degrees for every
original symmetric middle-positive separately closed background,
all original smooth complementary tests, and every actual
refinement. This is only the forward consequence of the
conditional certificate; no new positive-current pullback is used.

\subsection{Remaining gate and relation to the branch obstruction}

BC shows that the global-harmonic-comparator replacement for
(LC24.2) cannot hold uniformly for all upstairs weights, even
for one fixed quadratic cover and one fixed unit. The present
proof asks instead for local annihilation of the already existing
original Radon measure. The strict-defect function need not
extend harmonically to \(U\). Thus BC does not refute the
antecedent of this proposition.

Conversely, this proposition does not prove that antecedent.
It does not transfer an arbitrary upstairs function whose trace
is merely locally harmonic along the whole lifted carrier:
such a function need not be one global unit logarithm.
Nor does it transfer every allowed ambient generator in all its
original local-presentation quantifiers. Therefore full ST19,
finite-cover reverse carrier-CLN comparison, LG7, KC12 and CTO
remain \texttt{OPEN}. The result is a conditional implication
between explicit existing gaps, not a new abstract definition
or a general annihilation theorem.

\paragraph{Construction and review roles.}
The root supplied the conditional local-measure replacement for
the BC-false global-comparator route. The polar-duality researcher
checked and wrote its complete strict-defect descent, all-tail
exchange and quantified UT deduction. Neither is an independent
reviewer of this source. Their earlier authorship of GP, CW,
UT, IR/IL/NC is input provenance only. Any author-separated
review of this new deduction is recorded against exact bytes.

title: Constructed ordinary quadratic descent in finite residue rank at most two
text:
ordinary_quadratic_residue_rank_two.tex \section{Constructed ordinary quadratic descent in finite residue rank at most two}
\label{sec:r11-ordinary-residue-two}

\paragraph{Purpose and promotion rule.}
The normal-surface construction is useful for the intrinsic problem
only after it returns to an arbitrary original ordinary germ. This
section supplies that return and the full controlled approximants.
Its status is fixed by the source-bound composition review recorded
in the result register. In particular the NS assembly is a necessary
proved dependency, not an unrecorded conjecture in the statement.
The result is quadratic and belongs to the fixed finite closed-cell
PS class. It leaves higher coupled relations and residue rank at
least three open.

Let \(X\) be good, Hausdorff, boundaryless and quasi-smooth over
the original finite \(K/\mathbf Q_p\) with its original absolute
value. Fix \(x\in X\), and work on an ordinary representative
of pure dimension \(n\). Fix a finite original unit tuple
\(f=(f_1,\ldots,f_N)\). Its graded moment field and ranks are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathscr F_f(x)&=\widetilde K^{\mathrm{gr}}
          (\widetilde f_1(x),\ldots,\widetilde f_N(x)),\\
 d_f(x)&=\operatorname{trdeg}^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\widetilde K^{\mathrm{gr}}}
                         \mathscr F_f(x),\\
 r_f(x)&=\dim_{\mathbf Q}\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbf Q}
  \{-\log|f_j(x)|+\mathbf Q\log|K^\times|\}_{j=1}^N,\\
 s_f(x)&=d_f(x)-r_f(x).
\end{aligned}
\tag{OR1}
\]
The retained FM theorem proves that \(s_f\) is the transcendence
degree of the finitely generated field of normalized old residues.
In particular \(s_f(x)\le s_K(x)\). No finite generation of the
full residue field of \(\mathcal H(x)\) is required.

The scalar family below consists of finitely many continuous PL or
continuous PS functions through this fixed tuple, with smooth
extensions near the closed cells of one finite coefficient complex.
Their complete original moment image, including all lower strata,
is part of the presentation. SE supplies ambient scalar extensions
when the functions are initially given only on that image.

\begin{theorem}[Ordinary quadratic descent in finite residue rank two]
\label{thm:r11-ordinary-quadratic-residue-two}
Suppose the fixed finite scalar presentation
\[
                    P=\sum_\nu c_\nu[h_\nu][k_\nu]
\tag{OR2}
\]
is an actual signed quadratic analytic zero, meaning
\[
             \kappa_2(P)=\sum_\nu c_\nu
                 D_\delta h_\nu\wedge D_\delta k_\nu=0,
                    \qquad s_f(x)\le2.
\tag{OR3}
\]
For every fixed \(1<\kappa<2\), there are an original ordinary
neighborhood \(U_x\), a finite actual original-unit refinement,
and a continuous finite-PS ambient covector on its complete moment
image whose strain is the energy
\[
 Z_P=\tfrac12\sum_\nu c_\nu
       (d'_Ph_\nu\wedge d''_Pk_\nu+
                         d'_Pk_\nu\wedge d''_Ph_\nu).
\tag{OR4}
\]
In particular \(Z_P=d'\beta_Z+d''\zeta_Z\) in the full actual
degree-one module on \(U_x\).

Put
\[
 u=\sum_\nu c_\nu h_\nu k_\nu,\qquad
 A_0=\tfrac12D_\delta u,\qquad \alpha_P=A_0-Z_P.
\tag{OR5}
\]
Then
\[
 \alpha_P=d'\bigl(\tfrac12d''u-\beta_Z\bigr)+d''(-\zeta_Z).
\tag{OR6}
\]
There are one fixed positive represented control \(Q=D[q]\),
actual symmetric full-exact approximants
\(a_j=d'B_j+d''C_j\), and \(\epsilon_j\downarrow0\),
chosen before every subsequent background, test and refinement,
with
\[
\begin{aligned}
 -\epsilon_jQ&\le[\alpha_P]-[a_j]\le\epsilon_jQ,\\
 -\epsilon_jD(qS)&\le M_S(\alpha_P)-M_S(a_j)
                                      \le\epsilon_jD(qS).
\end{aligned}
\tag{OR7}
\]
Here \(S\) ranges over all original symmetric middle-positive
backgrounds separately closed under \(d'\) and \(d''\), in all
legal degrees. The inequalities and identities use all original
compact smooth complementary CLD tests and every actual refinement,
including rank degeneration. Explicit choices are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a_j&=A_0-e_{\delta_j},&
 \epsilon_j&=C\delta_j^{(2-\kappa)/2},\\
 B_j&=\tfrac12d''u-\beta_{\delta_j},&
 C_j&=-\zeta_{\delta_j},
\end{aligned}
\tag{OR8}
\]
where \(e_\delta=d'\beta_\delta+d''\zeta_\delta\) is the
constructed smooth regular-energy approximation and
\(\delta_j\downarrow0\) is sufficiently small.

For every such original \(S\) of bidegree \((p,p)\),
\(0\le p\le n-2\), the action satisfies
\[
                         \mathcal A_S(P)|_{U_x}=0.
\tag{OR9}
\]
The relation presentation, \(\kappa\), and the chosen ordinary
truncation may affect the construction. Later backgrounds, tests
and refinements do not affect its control or require the inequality
\(s_f\le2\) again.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Step 1: a regular equation on the exact finite-rank target.}
The retained QA/QP transgression gives
\[
                        D_\delta Z_P=-\kappa_2(P)=0,
                         \qquad D[Z_P]=0.
\tag{OR10}
\]
Apply SE and FM to precisely the fixed finite presentation. They
construct an actual smooth map \(F:U\to Y\), a point \(y=F(x)\),
and a target tuple \(\tau\) such that
\[
 \dim Y=d_f(x),\qquad r_K(y)=r_f(x),\qquad s_K(y)=s_f(x),
                    \qquad t_f=E(t_\tau\circ F)
\tag{OR11}
\]
on every point of an original ordinary source neighborhood.
The map \(E\) is a fixed rational affine map. Composing the
finite scalar extensions with \(E\) gives a regular finite-PS
energy \(Z_Y\) with
\(Z_P=F^*_{\mathrm{coeff}}Z_Y\) on every source face.

The retained SD compact-test operator applies to the actual smooth
map and this regular tensor. It gives \(D[Z_Y]=0\) on an ordinary
target neighborhood. This is the original-test equation, obtained
using compact vertical forms and actual finite etale packets.
No arbitrary current or arbitrary original background is pushed
forward. The relation \(P\) itself need not descend as a target
delta-algebra relation; the regular equation is the required input.

\emph{Step 2: the target has an actual complete-image primitive.}
If \(s_f\le1\), the retained UQ construction already supplies the
primitive, including its zero- and one-dimensional cases. Suppose
\(s_f=2\). The explicit FM construction is
\[
                 Y=\mathbf G_{m,K}^{r_f,\mathrm{an}}
                              \times Y_0^{\mathrm{an}},
\tag{OR12}
\]
where \(Y_0\) is the smooth integral hypersurface lift of the
finite separable residue extension used by FM. After the displayed
finite localizations, it is the generic fiber of a smooth integral
\(K^\circ\)-surface with integral special fiber. Its generic
special-fiber point has residue field exactly the chosen normalized
residue field \(L\), and value group exactly \(|K^\times|\).
The point \(y\) is its Gauss extension at the \(K\)-free values
of the retained old value-basis tuple. These statements are checked
in the separate FM-to-NS landing interface; they are stronger than
merely comparing the two numerical invariants in (OR11).

Adjoin finitely many algebraic target units to make the residue
surface a closed torus subvariety with function field \(L\), and
retain all old scalar coordinates by SA. The new norms agree on
one ordinary target neighborhood, with their exact initial forms
and saturated integral graph. This is an allowed target refinement;
its units pull back to actual original source units. No additional
factorization of arbitrary later source units through \(F\) is
claimed or needed.

The hypotheses of the NS assembly theorem
\ref{thm:r11-ns-finite-ps-strain} now hold. Its conewise primitives
are constructed by CE/SP, its central trace is removed by the
original SS cap calculation and CU, and its sourcewise residual
flux is treated by RCF on the whole actual cycle. Actual normalized
NCB curve blocks, simultaneous Picard units, two complete-source
separations, and all-radius TP/AX invisibility give the full joint
incident-span values. NL then constructs an ambient covector
\(\Lambda_Y\) on the complete image. Thus the premise required by
PR has been proved, including every lower face. It is not supplied
by a current kernel, an unverified normal-star identification, or
an assumption that the old-coordinate obstruction matrix vanishes.

\emph{Step 3: return the finite coefficients to the original source.}
Write the final target tuple as \(H=(H_1,\ldots,H_m)\) and
\(\Lambda_Y=\sum_i b_i(z)\,dz_i\). Put \(t=t_{H\circ F}\),
and define on an ordinary source neighborhood
\[
 \beta_Z=\tfrac12\sum_i b_i(t)d''t_i,
                 \qquad \zeta_Z=-\tfrac12\sum_i b_i(t)d't_i.
\tag{OR13}
\]
The actual source enlargement retains both \(f\) and \(H\circ F\).
Every source moment face maps linearly into a target coefficient
face. The target strain equality restricts along this linear map,
including when its rank drops. The anchored degree-one Leibniz
formula therefore proves the identity in (OR4). This is the exact
PR coefficient return. It involves no pullback of current order.
The full scalar Leibniz formula then gives (OR5)--(OR6).

\emph{Step 4: construct the required control on the source itself.}
Shrink once so that the source moment-image closure lies in a
bounded region inside the ambient domain of \(\Lambda_Y\).
Convolve the fixed continuous finite-PS coefficient functions there.
Substitute the resulting smooth covectors into (OR13), obtaining
\(e_\delta=d'\beta_\delta+d''\zeta_\delta\).
The retained source-side SB/PSO estimate uses the finitely many
coefficient facet equations \(\ell_H\), their fixed potentials
\(|\ell_H|^\kappa\), and a fixed strictly convex quadratic term.
It constructs one continuous psh \(q\) and gives
\[
        \pm([Z_P]-[e_\delta])
                  \le C\delta^{(2-\kappa)/2}D[q],
\tag{OR14}
\]
together with the original all-background module estimate.
All finite closed-cell bounds and all-face identities needed for
that estimate were supplied by the explicit target covector and
its coefficient return. Neither existence of an approximating
sequence nor existence of its fixed positive control is assumed.

Now use (OR8). The exact cancellation
\[
                         \alpha_P-a_j=e_{\delta_j}-Z_P
\tag{OR15}
\]
proves (OR7). Its approximants are full first-order exact, while
retaining the entire possibly singular \(A_0\). The two distinct
requirements of OC7 have therefore been constructed. Alternatively,
apply the retained all-background degree-one action to (OR6);
separate closedness, nilpotence and anticommutation give the action
identity (OR9) directly.

Finally, any later original compact test has a finite actual common
refinement with the constructed source tuple. Each new face maps
into a face of the complete certificate, and the finite-dimensional
semipositive inequalities restrict through its tangent map. The
fixed scalar-module control then gives every allowed original
background. This argument uses the same \(q\), neighborhood and
finite original construction. No bound on the ranks of the enlarged
test or refinement tuple is imposed.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[An intrinsic ordinary locus]
\label{cor:r11-intrinsic-residue-two-locus}
At every original point with \(s_K(x)\le2\), every fixed finite
quadratic actual-zero presentation in the stated continuous PL/PS
class satisfies the theorem. The rational rank and the Abhyankar
defect are unrestricted. In particular the conclusion concerns
ordinary non-saturated analytic germs of rational rank at least
two whenever their fixed relation has \(s_f\le2\).
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
FM proves \(s_f(x)\le s_K(x)\). The theorem is local at the
original point and its construction depends on the finite relation,
not on an ambient saturation assumption. Apply it to each fixed
presentation. This is a pointwise germ conclusion, not a passage
from a dense set to a current identity.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Exact limits.}
The complete carrier of a prescribed KC12 seminorm has not been
replaced, and this theorem does not assert that stronger full
certificate. One fixed common bounded BT curvature tail may be
absorbed in \(S\) in its legal degrees; a common finite signed PL
tail uses its retained finite positive expansion. Different termwise
tails and arbitrary higher coupled relations are not covered.
The original notions of middle, strong and weak positivity remain
distinct. General residue rank at least three, variable-PS/CTO,
ordinary-to-GK tests, and the whole intrinsic gluing and naturality
interface remain separate tasks. Only \(e_\delta\) is asserted
smooth; the full approximants \(a_j\) retain \(A_0\), consistently
with the R24 VE obstruction.

\paragraph{Exact inherited sources.}
SE, FM, SD, PR, UQ, QP and the selected QA/SB/PSO inputs are frozen
with their byte hashes in the selected-input index. The additional
new dependencies are the FM-to-NS structural landing and the
source-bound NS assembly. The result register records their precise
status and the independent internal composition review. This is
not peer review or formal certification.

title: An intrinsic quadratic transgression class modulo full first-order exactness
text:
intrinsic_quadratic_transgression_quotient.tex \section{An intrinsic quadratic transgression class modulo full first-order exactness}
\label{sec:r11-intrinsic-quadratic-transgression}

\paragraph{Purpose and scope.}
OR makes a quadratic actual-zero presentation full first-order
exact in finite residue rank at most two.  This section records
the resulting intrinsic quotient interface.  It is a formal
consequence of that proved analytic construction and the retained
QP identities; it does not posit a new primitive or approximation
theorem.  The quotient is the full degree-one module modulo
first-order exact terms.  It is not called Aeppli cohomology:
the representatives below need not be \(D_\delta\)-closed.

Keep the original finite \(K/\mathbf Q_p\), its original norm,
and the project's good, Hausdorff, boundaryless quasi-smooth
spaces with their ordinary topology.  All scalar functions below
belong locally to the fixed finite continuous PL/PS closed-cell
class of OR/QP.  The words ``locally'' and ``sheaf'' permit an
ordinary cover of such finite presentations; they introduce no
uncontrolled variable-PS rule or infinite formal sum on one germ.

\subsection{The existing modules and the quadratic image}

Here \(\mathscr B^{a,b}=B^{a,b}_{\rm Mih}\) is exactly the
genuine analytic Mihatsch delta-form sheaf, in total bidegree,
fixed in the opening of the archived QA source.  This is an
existing actual analytic quotient with all actual moment
refinements.  It is not a new sheaf inferred from the sought
arbitrary-background differential calculus.  The precise archived
inputs are QA8--QA9: they define
\(d'B^{0,1}+d''B^{1,0}\) as an ordinary image sheaf,
state that its full derivative \(D_\delta\) is zero, and
explicitly use the already defined map
\(D_\delta:B^{1,1}\to B^{2,2}\).  QA12--QA13 put the
quadratic transgression and its derivative in those same sheaves;
QP4--QP5 extend that fixed scalar class from PL to the present
finite continuous PS class.

In particular \(\mathscr B^{0,1},\mathscr B^{1,0},
\mathscr B^{1,1}\) contain the \(d''u\), constructed
covectors, full Cartier terms and regular energies used by PR.
Their existing full derivatives have nilpotence, anticommutation
and ordinary restriction compatibility.  We set
\(\mathscr C^{2,2}_{\rm act}=\mathscr B^{2,2}\).
This notation neither defines an action of an arbitrary background
on \(B^{2,2}\) nor identifies \(B_{\rm Mih}\) with the
algebraic GK sheaf.  Those separate interfaces are not assumed.

Take images and quotients in sheaves of real vector spaces:
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathscr J^{1,1}
    &=\operatorname{im}_{\rm sh}
          (d':\mathscr B^{0,1}\to\mathscr B^{1,1})
      +\operatorname{im}_{\rm sh}
          (d'':\mathscr B^{1,0}\to\mathscr B^{1,1}),\\
 \mathscr Q^{1,1}&=\mathscr B^{1,1}/\mathscr J^{1,1}.
 \end{split}
\tag{IQ1}
\]
Thus a section has zero class precisely when it is locally full
first-order exact.  This is a sheaf quotient, not the assertion
that every such section is one globally exact expression.
Nilpotence and anticommutation give
\[
 D_\delta(d'\beta+d''\zeta)=0,
       \qquad
 \overline D:\mathscr Q^{1,1}\longrightarrow
                                  \mathscr C^{2,2}_{\rm act}.
\tag{IQ2}
\]

Let \(\mathscr P_2\) be the sheaf of finite real quadratic
presentations in the stated scalar class, with the usual real
bilinearity and symmetry of \([h][k]\).  Equivalently one may
sheafify the corresponding symmetric-square presentation space.
The coefficients are real constants, not arbitrary scalar functions.
Put
\[
 \begin{split}
 P&=\sum_\nu c_\nu[h_\nu][k_\nu],\\
 \kappa_2(P)&=\sum_\nu c_\nu
                          D_\delta h_\nu\wedge D_\delta k_\nu,
       \qquad
 \mathscr K_2=\operatorname{im}_{\rm sh}\kappa_2.
 \end{split}
\tag{IQ3}
\]
A section of \(\mathscr K_2\) has local finite presentations;
it need not have a single finite presentation on the entire open
set.  QP supplies the real linear transgression expression
\[
 \begin{split}
 \alpha_P&=\tfrac12\sum_\nu c_\nu
             (h_\nu D_\delta k_\nu+k_\nu D_\delta h_\nu),\\
 u_P&=\sum_\nu c_\nu h_\nu k_\nu,\qquad
 A_{0,P}=\tfrac12D_\delta u_P,\\
 Z_P&=\tfrac12\sum_\nu c_\nu
      (d'_Ph_\nu\wedge d''_Pk_\nu+
                       d'_Pk_\nu\wedge d''_Ph_\nu),\\
 \alpha_P&=A_{0,P}-Z_P,\qquad
 D_\delta\alpha_P=\kappa_2(P).
 \end{split}
\tag{IQ4}
\]
The ordinary scalar identities already make IQ4 compatible with
the stated bilinearity and symmetry of the presentation space.

\begin{theorem}[Canonical germ class in residue dimension at most two]
\label{thm:r11-intrinsic-quadratic-germ-class}
Let \(x\) be any original point, in arbitrary ambient dimension,
with \(s_K(x)\le2\).  There is a canonical real linear map
\[
 \tau_{2,x}:\mathscr K_{2,x}\longrightarrow\mathscr Q^{1,1}_x,
       \qquad
 \tau_{2,x}(\kappa_2(P))=[\alpha_P]=-[Z_P],
\tag{IQ5}
\]
independent of the finite original presentation of its input.
It satisfies
\[
                          \overline D\,\tau_{2,x}
                                      =\operatorname{id}.
\tag{IQ6}
\]
Its image is exactly the subspace of quadratic transgression
classes.  On that image \(\overline D\) and \(\tau_{2,x}\)
are inverse isomorphisms.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take two finite germ presentations \(P,P'\) of the same actual
quadratic curvature.  Shrink ordinarily so that both are defined,
with one finite union unit tuple \(f\) and one common finite
closed-cell subdivision.  Their difference is an actual zero:
\(\kappa_2(P-P')=0\).  FM's bound gives
\[
                         s_f(x)\le s_K(x)\le2.
\tag{IQ7}
\]
OR applied to this entire difference constructs, on an ordinary
neighborhood, the full identity
\[
                  \alpha_P-\alpha_{P'}=d'\beta+d''\zeta.
\tag{IQ8}
\]
Consequently their classes in IQ1 agree.  This proves
well-definedness for germs, including presentations originally
given in different actual unit coordinates.  Real linearity
follows from the linear expression IQ4 after taking a finite
common refinement.

The full singular term is legitimately exact in this quotient:
\(A_{0,P}=d'(\tfrac12d''u_P)\).  Hence
\([\alpha_P]=-[Z_P]\).  This is an equality of quotient classes
using the complete term \(A_{0,P}\), not a claim that the full
polar has a smooth or continuous double primitive.  Applying
IQ2 and IQ4 gives IQ6.  Every quadratic transgression class is
represented by some \(\alpha_P\), so it lies in the image
of \(\tau_{2,x}\); IQ6 proves the inverse assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[An ordinary sheaf morphism on analytic surfaces]
\label{thm:r11-intrinsic-surface-transgression-sheaf}
On an ordinary open set of pure dimension at most two, the germ
maps above assemble to a canonical morphism of sheaves of real
vector spaces
\[
                   \tau_2:\mathscr K_2\longrightarrow
                                    \mathscr Q^{1,1},
              \qquad \overline D\circ\tau_2=\operatorname{id}.
\tag{IQ9}
\]
It commutes with ordinary restriction and is independent of all
actual coordinate refinements used to represent its input.  More
generally the same assertion holds on any ordinary open set on
which \(s_K(x)\le2\) at every point.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The analytic dimension inequality gives
\(s_K(x)\le\dim_xX\le2\), so the preceding theorem applies
at every point.  If \(\omega\in\mathscr K_2(U)\), choose
an ordinary cover \(U_i\) and finite local presentations
\(\omega|_{U_i}=\kappa_2(P_i)\).  On each overlap the
germs of \([\alpha_{P_i}]\) and \([\alpha_{P_j}]\) agree
by IQ8.  Since \(\mathscr Q^{1,1}\) is a sheaf, these
classes glue uniquely to a section on \(U\).  Different
local covers and presentations give the same section by the
same germ calculation.  This defines \(\tau_2\).

All formulas are local and real linear, so they commute with
ordinary restriction and addition.  The identity in IQ9 is
checked on the local finite presentations by IQ4.  The proof
glues quotient classes; it does not choose one globally compatible
family of the primitives in IQ8 or one global positive control.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The fixed-background quadratic ordinary action factors]
\label{cor:r11-intrinsic-quadratic-action-factor}
In the surface sheaf scope above, let \(S\) be an allowed
original background in a legal degree.  The local formula
\[
       \omega=\kappa_2(P)\longmapsto
       \mathfrak A_{S,2}(\omega):=D\bigl(M_S(\alpha_P)\bigr)
                                      =A_S(P)
\tag{IQ10}
\]
defines a real linear ordinary-current action independent of the
local finite presentation.  It is compatible with ordinary
restriction of \(S\) and \(\omega\), and uses every original
compact smooth complementary test and every actual refinement.
The corresponding assertion holds at an arbitrary-dimensional
stalk with \(s_K(x)\le2\).
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For a difference of presentations, IQ8 and the retained QP
first-order scalar-module identity give
\[
 D M_S(\alpha_P-\alpha_{P'})
   =D\{d'(\beta\wedge S)+d''(\zeta\wedge S)\}=0.
\tag{IQ11}
\]
Separate closedness of \(S\), nilpotence and anticommutation
are exactly the hypotheses of that identity.  Thus the local
current formulas agree on overlaps.  Their ordinary current
gluing, or the explicit compact-test partition in SQ, proves
the assertion.  The all-test and refinement quantifiers are
those already proved in OR/QP; no new test class is added.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The finite-union condition cannot be omitted}

At a general higher-residue point, two presentations can each
have finite residue rank at most two while their combined tuple
has larger residue rank.  For example, at the original Gauss
point of \(\mathbb G_{m,K}^3\), the unit tuples
\((u_1,u_2)\) and \((u_2,u_3)\) have residue fields
\(k(\bar u_1,\bar u_2)\) and \(k(\bar u_2,\bar u_3)\),
each of transcendence degree two.  Their union has the field
\(k(\bar u_1,\bar u_2,\bar u_3)\), of transcendence degree
three.  This is a rank diagnostic, not a counterexample to
intrinsic descent.

Accordingly, at an arbitrary original point the comparison of
two specific presentations in IQ8 is proved whenever their
\emph{joint} finite tuple satisfies \(s_f(x)\le2\).  Separate
rank bounds on the two presentations do not justify that step.
The stalk hypothesis \(s_K(x)\le2\) is what makes every finite
union safe and hence gives the canonical map on the entire
quadratic image stalk.  No ordinary open locus is inferred merely
from a pointwise residue-rank bound.

\paragraph{Exact interface boundaries.}
The sheaf morphism IQ9 is a quadratic transgression class modulo
full first-order exactness.  It is not a section of the ordinary
Aeppli cohomology sheaf for a nonzero curvature: its derivative
is the input \(\omega\), not zero.  It is real linear, not a
module map over variable smooth or PS scalar coefficients.  Its
canonical status refers to the displayed finite transgression
formula; no uniqueness among all abstract right inverses of
\(\overline D\) is asserted.

This result proves ordinary restriction and quotient-sheaf locality
for the indicated quadratic image.  It does not construct the full
graded intrinsic differential algebra, impose new functoriality
under arbitrary analytic maps, assert equality on all GK delta
tests, solve arbitrary higher coupled relations or variable-PS/CTO,
or replace any absolute cap carrier.  The local fixed controls
and singular terms remain exactly those supplied by OR/PR.

\paragraph{Source-bound dependencies.}
OR: \texttt{ordinary\_quadratic\_residue\_rank\_two.tex}, SHA-256
\texttt{0a11b646bf6a95afa8b710d2271c0c933fea626fe014e9fde2f1fe7db044f599};
QP: the immutable Round 10
\texttt{fixed\_finite\_ps\_quadratic\_extension.tex}, SHA-256
\texttt{9177fb95c0a2467e06b30ea2829a04c7f165e32abcc9c5d9ac082ec436b9115d}.
The exact existing-sheaf input is the immutable selected QA source
\texttt{qa\_degree\_one\_and\_quadratic\_transgression.tex},
SHA-256
\texttt{a6e8081c94d77b31a4bcf2c5eabd359a105cb03fd5a43f9ec8fe18d2cefdea2d},
especially its opening scope, QA8--QA13, and the proof following
QA11, which already states factorization through the full quotient
\(B^{1,1}/(d'B^{0,1}+d''B^{1,0})\).  The retained R6 full
source at SHA-256
\texttt{fb87839085e500b446d9cc512e5bfca6b8f31de0b8ddf8721d9192d60f9942b0}
identifies this original analytic sheaf as \(B_{\rm Mih}\) in
\texttt{sec:r6-delta-faithfulness}, with its original field and
ordinary topology.  No arbitrary-current faithfulness is used here.

Beyond those existing definitions, the new deduction uses
QP4--QP9, their ordinary restriction statement, OR's full
first-order exactness for the difference relation, and the
ordinary sheaf quotient.  The original analytic proof and
source-bound independent review of OR remain indispensable.

title: Ordinary normal tubes of a marked residue curve
text:
geom13_marked_curve_normal_tubes.tex \section{Ordinary normal tubes of a marked residue curve}
\label{sec:r13-cc-marked-curve-tubes}

Put \(R=K^\circ\), choose a uniformizer \(\pi\), and put
\(k=R/(\pi)\).  We retain the original field and its absolute value.
Let \(q\geq1\), and let \((Y,y)\) be a smooth integral model germ
of relative dimension \(q+1\), as in GE1.  Thus
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal H(y)}=F,
 \qquad \operatorname{trdeg}_kF=q+1,
 \qquad |\mathcal H(y)^\times|=|K^\times|.
 \tag{CC1}
\]
Let \(V/k\) be a smooth integral model of \(F\), and let
\(C\subset V\) be a smooth proper integral curve.  Suppose that,
near the generic point \(\eta_C\), the curve is the transverse
intersection of labelled smooth prime divisors
\(D_1,\ldots,D_q\).  Choose their local equations
\(z_1,\ldots,z_q\in F\) at \(\eta_C\), and write
\(F_C=k(C)\).  Degrees of closed points of \(C\) are taken over
\(k\), including its full constant-field factor.

A finite norm-one central unit list \(a_1,\ldots,a_b\) is called
adapted to this curve and these normal parameters if
\[
 \bar a_j=z_1^{n_{1j}}\cdots z_q^{n_{qj}}u_j,
 \qquad n_{ij}\in\mathbf Z,
 \quad u_j\in\mathcal O_{V,\eta_C}^{\times}.
 \tag{CC2}
\]
Put \(g_j=u_j|_C\in F_C^\times\).  In particular every central
unit whose residue is a unit at \(\eta_C\) is adapted, with all
\(n_{ij}=0\).  This includes the simultaneous lifts supplied by ML.

\subsection{The exact zero slice}

Choose \(t\in\mathcal O_{V,\eta_C}^{\times}\) whose restriction
to \(C\) is a separating transcendence parameter.  The conormal
sequence makes
\(dz_1,\ldots,dz_q,dt\) a basis at \(\eta_C\).  A standard
etale neighborhood consequently has the form
\[
 B_0=\left(k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_q,T,G_0^{-1}][\Theta]/Q_0\right)_{H_0},
 \qquad \operatorname{Frac}(B_0)=F.
 \tag{CC3}
\]
The polynomial \(Q_0\) is monic, its derivative is invertible on
the selected chart, and all localizers are nonzero at \(\eta_C\).
After further localization in \(T\), its zero slice has a selected
coprime factorization
\[
 Q_0(0,T,\Theta)=p_0(T,\Theta)r_0(T,\Theta),
 \qquad k(T)[\Theta]/p_0=F_C.
 \tag{CC4}
\]
Invert the complementary factor on the selected component.  Lift
the coefficients to \(R\), choosing the lift so that
\[
                    Q(0,T,\Theta)=P(T,\Theta)R_0(T,\Theta)
                    \quad\hbox{exactly}.
 \tag{CC5}
\]
The modification used in DT4 works with the tuple \(Z\) in place
of its single variable: subtract the original zero specialization
and add the prescribed product.  This preserves the reduction and
monicity.

Let \(\mathscr W\) be the selected lifted smooth model defined by
\(Q=0\).  Let \(\mathscr C_0\) be the selected smooth affine
\(R\)-curve defined by \(P=0\), with all zero-slice localizers
inverted.  Write \(C_0=\mathscr C_{0,K}^{\rm an}\), and let
\(v\) be its generic special-fiber point.  Then
\[
 \widetilde{\mathcal H(v)}=F_C,
 \qquad |\mathcal H(v)^\times|=|K^\times|.
 \tag{CC6}
\]
The point \(v\) is considered in the boundaryless analytic curve
\(C_0\), with its ordinary neighborhoods.  Its proper residue
curve is the given \(C\), since both have function field \(F_C\).

\begin{theorem}[Ordinary normal product near every positive radius block]
\label{thm:r13-cc-ordinary-product}
There is an original ordinary comparison between the central
generic point of \(\mathscr W\) and \((Y,y)\), inducing the
specified residue-field identity.  The coordinates \(Z_i\) become
actual central units with residues \(z_i\).

In the selected chart there is a continuous family
\[
 x_C(r_1,\ldots,r_q),\qquad 0<r_i<1,
 \tag{CC7}
\]
identified, near every compact block
\(B\Subset(0,1)^q\), with the relative multivariable Gauss family
over \(v\) in \(\mathbf G_m^{q,\rm an}\times_K C_0\).
The identification is an isomorphism between ordinary open
subdomains and preserves \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_q,T\).
As all \(r_i\to1^-\), the family converges ordinarily to the
central point, uniformly with respect to the ratios of
\(-\log r_i\).  Hence a sufficiently short full collar lies
in any prescribed central ordinary comparison neighborhood.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The central comparison is the dimension-independent argument of
GE6.  Lift the finite residue generators on the original model,
solve the simple root by the ordinary analytic root lemma, and
compare the two etale parameter maps.  Their central completed
fields have the same residue field and the same discrete value
group as \(K\).  Successive \(\pi\)-adic residue approximation
makes the induced field inclusion surjective.  The pointed etale
germ theorem then gives an ordinary local isomorphism.

On the product side let \(\Theta_0\) be the zero-slice root.  At
each relative Gauss point over \(v\), (CC5) gives
\[
 |Q(Z,T,\Theta_0)|\leq\max_i r_i<1,
 \qquad |Q_\Theta(Z,T,\Theta_0)|=1.
 \tag{CC8}
\]
Every selected localizer and complementary factor has norm one.
On a compact block the first bound is uniformly less than one.
Ordinary continuity therefore gives a neighborhood on which the
Newton inequalities are uniform.  The retained analytic root
lemma gives the unique root \(\Theta\) in the prescribed strict
Hensel ball.  Solving \(P(T,\Theta_0)=0\) near \(\Theta\)
constructs the inverse.  Uniqueness proves the two compositions
are the identity after ordinary shrinking and glues the maps on
overlapping blocks.  This argument uses no independence condition
on the radii.

For convergence, complete the selected coordinate ring along the
normal ideal.  The simple root construction embeds it in the
formal series ring over the zero-slice coefficient algebra.  Its
reduction embeds the integral local chart into
\(F_C[[z_1,\ldots,z_q]]\).  If an integral function \(b\) has
nonzero reduction, some coefficient of its normal expansion has
nonzero residue in \(F_C\), and hence norm one at \(v\).
All coefficients have norm at most one.  For one such exponent
\(\alpha\),
\[
          r^\alpha\leq |b(x_C(r))|\leq1.
 \tag{CC9}
\]
After dividing a general nonzero integral function by its maximal
\(\pi\)-power, the same estimate applies.  Quotients give
convergence of every regular-function seminorm.  This proves
ordinary convergence, and the lower bound depends only on
\(\alpha\), not on ratios among the positive logarithmic radii.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The coefficient field at commensurable radii}

\begin{lemma}[The full Gauss residue extension]
\label{lem:r13-cc-gauss-residue}
For \(r\in\mathbf R_{>0}^q\), let \(K_r\) be the completion of
\(K(Z_1,\ldots,Z_q)\) for its Gauss norm.  Put
\[
 \Lambda_r=\{(a_0,a)\in\mathbf Z^{q+1}:
                     |\pi|^{a_0}r^a=1\}.
 \tag{CC10}
\]
If \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_d\) is a basis of \(\Lambda_r\),
the residues of the corresponding monomials
\(\pi^{\ell_{j0}}Z^{\ell'_j}\) are algebraically independent,
and
\[
 \widetilde {K_r}=k(U_1,\ldots,U_d),\qquad
 |K_r^\times|=|K^\times|r_1^{\mathbf Z}\cdots r_q^{\mathbf Z}.
 \tag{CC11}
\]
At \(x_C(r)\) one has
\[
 \widetilde {\mathcal H(x_C(r))}=F_C(U_1,\ldots,U_d),
 \qquad |\mathcal H(x_C(r))^\times|=|K_r^\times|.
 \tag{CC12}
\]
For a closed point \(p\in C\), its base change to
\(k(U_1,\ldots,U_d)\) remains one closed point of degree
\(\delta_p=[\kappa(p):k]\), and all orders of functions in
\(F_C^\times\) at that point are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The associated graded field of a Gauss rational-function field
is the graded fraction field of
\(\operatorname{gr}K[\widetilde Z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,
\widetilde Z_q^{\pm1}]\).  A degree-one Laurent monomial has
exponent in \(\Lambda_r\).  Factoring one monomial from any
homogeneous numerator and denominator shows that the degree-one
subfield is exactly \(\operatorname{Frac}(k[\Lambda_r])\).
The exponent group is free, so this is the displayed rational
function field.  Distinct Laurent monomials in a basis have
distinct exponents, proving algebraic independence.  Completion
adds no initial forms: every nonzero completed element has an
approximation with strictly smaller error than its norm.

The identical calculation with the coefficient field
\(\mathcal H(v)\), whose residue and value group are (CC6),
gives (CC12).  The analytic product isomorphism transports that
calculation to the actual point.  In particular the relative
value-group index is one at every radius vector.

Finally \(\kappa(p)\otimes_k k(U)=\kappa(p)(U)\), a field of
degree \([\kappa(p):k]\).  Flat base change of the smooth curve
preserves its local uniformizer and the orders of functions
defined over \(k\).  The corresponding proper residue curve
over \(\widetilde {K_r}\) is \(C_{k(U)}\), with the displayed
function field.  This also explains the extra residue variables
at commensurable radii.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Finite central normalization and the complete local source}

Choose a finite tuple of rational functions on \(C\) which,
together with the \(g_j\), generates \(F_C\).  Lift each through
\(\mathcal O_{V,\eta_C}\twoheadrightarrow F_C\) to a unit,
and then to an actual central analytic unit by the retained
finite residue-unit lifting theorem.  Denote the resulting
enlarged adapted list again by \(a_1,\ldots,a_N\).
Choose actual rational units \(R_j\) near \(v\) on \(C_0\)
with residues \(g_j\).

\begin{theorem}[All-radii split tuple and complete marked block]
\label{thm:r13-cc-complete-marked-block}
There is \(r_*<1\) such that for each compact nonempty block
\(B\Subset(r_*,1)^q\) one ordinary product-comparison domain
contains the Gauss source over \(B\) times a neighborhood of
the complete curve source germ at \(v\), and on that domain
\[
 \left|\frac{a_j}{\prod_i Z_i^{n_{ij}}}-R_j\right|<|R_j|,
 \qquad
 t_{a_j}=\sum_i n_{ij}t_{Z_i}+t_{R_j}.
 \tag{CC13}
\]
The normalized graded initial forms agree there.

For the completed tuple
\(\mathcal A=(Z_1,\ldots,Z_q,a_1,\ldots,a_N)\), the entire
full-rank source in this domain is the relative Gauss product
of the complete curve source of \(\mathbf R\) with the radial
parameter domain.  Its lattice and calibration are the product
lattice and product calibration.  The graph (CC13) has integral
index one on every face and every quotient by the radial lattice.

Let
\[
 M=\bigcup_j\operatorname{Supp}\operatorname{div}_C(g_j),
 \quad b_p=(\operatorname{ord}_p(g_j))_j,
 \quad m_p=\gcd_j |\operatorname{ord}_p(g_j)|,
 \quad v_p=b_p/m_p.
 \tag{CC14}
\]
This is a finite marked set with at least two points, because the
residue tuple contains a nonconstant function.  At every core point over
\(B\), the complete labelled transverse normal one-cycle is
\[
              \sum_{p\in M}\delta_pm_p
                              [\mathbf R_{\geq0}v_p].
 \tag{CC15}
\]
Each label is an actual branch germ.  Repeated geometric ray
images are aggregated only after their labelled calibrations.
For every normalized coordinate,
\[
       w_p(v_p)_j=\delta_p\operatorname{ord}_p(g_j),
       \qquad w_p=\delta_pm_p.
 \tag{CC16}
\]
Every branch of the completed tuple is retained, including those
whose projection to an earlier tuple is zero or rank deficient.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Represent \(u_j\) by a quotient regular and nonzero at
\(\eta_C\).  In the lifted chart its specialization to the zero
slice is a curve unit with residue \(g_j\).  Its difference from
that specialization belongs to the normal ideal in the formal
expansion; it has norm less than one at every positive-radius
core point.  Any other chosen lift \(R_j\) differs by a
zero-residue function at \(v\).  Finally the original central
unit and its chosen rational residue representative have ratio
with residue one at \(y\), so their difference has smaller norm
on an ordinary neighborhood of \(y\).  Convergence (CC9) puts
one full collar for the finite list inside this neighborhood.
These facts prove the strict inequality at every core point, including commensurable radii.  Continuity and compactness
extend it to one ordinary domain over \(B\).

For the split tuple \((Z,\mathbf R)\), the retained TP graded-rank
argument applies with \(q\) radial variables and a one-dimensional
factor.  Indeed full graded rank \(q+1\) forces rank one in the
curve coordinates and graded independence of all \(q\) radial
coordinates over the whole completed coefficient field.  This
is exactly the relative Gauss criterion.  Conversely a relative
Gauss point over a rank-one curve source has the required rank.
This identifies the entire source, at every radius vector.
The finite graph (CC13) has a coordinate projection as an
integral retraction, so it changes neither source rank nor any
of the stated lattice indices.  The product calibration is the
actual curve calibration times the primitive torus calibration
one.  The relative Gauss parameterization is continuous by the
maximum formula.  Applying the topological tube lemma to its
source parameter space over the compact set \(B\) gives a common
curve-source neighborhood.  No Cartesian basis for arbitrary
ambient ordinary neighborhoods is used.

The curve source at the interior point \(v\) is the complete
proper-residue-curve source of the retained AC/FP/NCB theorems.
Its visible branches are exactly the finite divisor support in
(CC14), and there is one actual source halfedge in each such
branch.  Its branch degree is \(\delta_p\), its coarse index is
one, and its primitive stretching is \(m_p\).  Thus its weight
is \(\delta_pm_p\).  The product-source identity gives the same
labelled normal block at every point over \(B\).  Alternatively,
(CC11)--(CC12) compute directly the curve field after a radial
base change: the marked points keep degree \(\delta_p\), their
orders are unchanged, and the relative value-group index remains
one.  No residue-field equality with \(F_C\) is asserted when
\(d>0\) in (CC10).

Finally the radial columns are
\(l_i=(e_i,n_{i1},\ldots,n_{iN})\).  Projection to the first
\(q\) coordinates splits their lattice integrally.  Its quotient
is identified with the normalized curve-coordinate lattice by
subtracting \(\sum_i n_{ij}t_{Z_i}\).  This proves the primitive
normal formula (CC16) and retains every completed branch.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite adapted enlargements]
\label{cor:r13-cc-adapted-enlargement}
For any further fixed finite adapted central unit list, the theorem
holds on a common collar and common finite source subdivision.
Its marked set is the union of the old divisor supports with the
new ones.  At an old mark, if \(m'_p\) is the new gcd, then
\(m'_p\mid m_p\); forgetting the new coordinates maps the new
primitive ray with index \(m_p/m'_p\), and
\[
              (m_p/m'_p)\,\delta_pm'_p=\delta_pm_p.
 \tag{CC17}
\]
A new mark has zero old transverse order vector and remains an
actual branch of the enlarged block.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Apply (CC13) to the union of the two finite lists and intersect
their ordinary domains.  The residue order vectors are enlarged
by adjoining rows, and their projection is exactly the old order
vector.  Dividing by the respective gcd gives (CC17).  The
canonical finite local source structure supplies a common
subdivision for these finitely many unit-log functions.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The old tangent index}

\begin{proposition}[Factorization of the source projection index]
\label{prop:r13-cc-tangent-index}
Suppose projection to an earlier moment lattice maps the completed
radial lattice \(\mathbf Z^q\) injectively to \(A\mathbf Z^q\)
in a saturated rank-\(q\) lattice \(N_T\).  Put
\(i_T=[N_T:A\mathbf Z^q]\).  On a transverse branch with nonzero
old quotient image, let \(m_p^{\rm old}\) be the primitive
stretching of its integral order vector in the saturated old
quotient lattice.  Then the full source projection index on that
branch is
\[
                       i_T\,m_p^{\rm old}/m_p,
 \tag{CC18}
\]
and the projected calibration is
\(\delta_p i_Tm_p^{\rm old}\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let \(L\) be the lattice generated by the projected radial
columns and the projected completed primitive transverse vector.
Its intersection with \(N_T\) is \(A\mathbf Z^q\), since the
transverse quotient vector is no

title: Relative Stokes with common tangential strains
text:
cap13_common_strain_stokes_and_raw_hessian.tex \section{Relative Stokes with common tangential strains}
\label{sec:r13-common-strain-stokes}

The local equation relevant to a positive face involves primitives on
all incident half-products.  Equal tangential strains suffice for its
boundary calculation.  Their tangential primitive traces may differ
by affine Killing fields.  Keeping these fields in the Green formula
gives the full relation Hessian at a completed curve star.

\subsection{The half-products and the boundary tensor}

Let $T$ be a real vector space of dimension $d\geq1$, with fixed
lattice measure, and let $B\subset T$ be a bounded convex open
polytope.  Let $N$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space and
let
\[
 \Sigma=\sum_{i\in I}w_i[\mathbb R_{\geq0}v_i],\qquad
 v_i\ne0,\qquad \sum_iw_iv_i=0,
 \tag{CS1}
\]
be a finite labelled balanced one-cycle.  Each $v_i$ is primitive
for its specified ray lattice.  The real weights may be signed in
the real statement.  Distinct labels are retained even when their
vectors coincide.  Put $W_i=T\oplus\mathbb Rv_i$.  On the closed
half-product $B\times[0,\epsilon)v_i$ let
\[
 b_i(t,s)=\sum_{a=1}^d b_{i,a}(t,s)\,dt_a+c_i(t,s)\,ds
 \tag{CS2}
\]
be continuous and finite piecewise smooth, with smooth extensions
near the closed cells and locally bounded first derivatives.  All
coefficient walls are included, including walls meeting $s=0$.
Write $A_i=e(b_i)=\operatorname{sym}(db_i)$, using distributional
derivatives.  Continuity makes its first derivative the bounded
cellwise derivative, with no coefficient-jump measure.

Assume the tangential boundary covectors have one common strain:
\[
       e_T\bigl(b_i(t,0)|_T\bigr)=A_T
       \quad\hbox{as distributions on }B\quad(i\in I).
 \tag{CS3}
\]
Their values need not coincide.  Define the normal flux and the
$N$-valued tangential covector
\[
 z(t)=\sum_iw_ic_i(t,0),\qquad
 B_a(t)=\sum_iw_ib_{i,a}(t,0)v_i.
 \tag{CS4}
\]

\begin{lemma}[The unmatched trace is a Killing tensor]
\label{lem:r13-weighted-killing-trace}
For every $\lambda\in N^*$, the covector
$\sum_a\lambda(B_a)dt_a$ is an affine Killing covector on $B$.
Equivalently,
\[
 \partial_aB_b+\partial_bB_a=0
       \quad\hbox{distributionally for all }a,b.
 \tag{CS5}
\]
For any fixed index $i_0$, each difference
$K_i=b_i(\cdot,0)|_T-b_{i_0}(\cdot,0)|_T$ is likewise affine
Killing.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Apply $e_T$ to CS4.  By CS3 the result is
$A_T\otimes\sum_iw_iv_i=0$.  This proves CS5.  For completeness,
if $k_a$ are distributional coefficients satisfying
$\partial_ak_b+\partial_bk_a=0$, then
\[
 2\partial_a\partial_bk_c
 =\partial_a(\partial_bk_c+\partial_ck_b)
  +\partial_b(\partial_ak_c+\partial_ck_a)
  -\partial_c(\partial_ak_b+\partial_bk_a)=0.
 \tag{CS6}
\]
Thus every coefficient is affine on the connected convex set
$B$, and its linear part is alternating.  This conclusion applies
to $\lambda(B)$ and, by CS3, to every $K_i$.  In particular it
already includes all tangential coefficient walls.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Common-strain product Stokes]
\label{thm:r13-common-strain-stokes}
For every smooth compactly supported ambient function $\chi$ on
a neighborhood of the truncated product and every constant
symmetric tangent form $\Omega$ of bidegree $(d-1,d-1)$,
\[
 \sum_iw_i\int_{B\times[0,\epsilon)v_i}
                       A_i\wedge D\chi\wedge\Omega
       =-\int_B z\,D_T\chi_0\wedge\Omega,
 \qquad \chi_0(t)=\chi(t,0).
 \tag{CS7}
\]
The support of $\chi$ stays away from the outer boundaries.
Here $D=d'd''$, with the positive product orientation and the
original primitive ray parameters.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Let the symmetric matrix $C^{ab}$ represent the tangent dual
$\Omega$.  The complete half-product Green formula FS6 gives,
on the branch $i$,
\[
 \int A_i\wedge D\chi\wedge\Omega
 =\int_B\sum_{a,b}C^{ab}
 \bigl(b_{i,a}(t,0)\,\partial_b\partial_s\chi_i(t,0)
              -c_i(t,0)\,\partial_a\partial_b\chi_0(t)\bigr)dt,
 \tag{CS8}
\]
where $\chi_i(t,s)=\chi(t,sv_i)$.  Full continuity of $b_i$
on its half-product removes every internal-wall term in that
formula.  Its integrand before taking the boundary is the full
contraction
\[
 \sum_{a,b}C^{ab}
   \bigl((A_i)_{ab}(\chi_i)_{ss}
          +(A_i)_{ss}(\chi_i)_{ab}
                     -2(A_i)_{as}(\chi_i)_{bs}\bigr).
 \tag{CS9}
\]

Put $\xi(t)=d_N\chi(t,0)\in N^*$.  The sum of the first
boundary terms in CS8 is
\[
       \int_B\sum_{a,b}C^{ab}
                       \langle\partial_b\xi(t),B_a(t)\rangle dt.
 \tag{CS10}
\]
Integrate once in $t$.  This is legitimate distributionally,
so no tangential wall term is omitted.  Since $C$ is symmetric,
CS5 makes the result
\[
 -\frac12\int_B\sum_{a,b}C^{ab}
                   \langle\xi,\partial_bB_a+\partial_aB_b\rangle dt
 =0.
 \tag{CS11}
\]
The remaining terms in CS8 are precisely the right side of
CS7.  Thus the tangent cancellation occurs after integration;
it requires the common tangential strain in CS3, rather than
a common tangential primitive value.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Intrinsic Hessians and the complete relation space}

The normal flux depends on a quotient section, whereas its full
tangential Hessian does not.  To state this, start with an ambient
space $W$ and its tangent subspace $T$.  The normal vectors are
in $W/T$, and a common linear section identifies them with the
$v_i$ used above.  The incident space is
$W_i=T+\mathbb Rv_i$.

\begin{lemma}[Section and primitive-gauge invariance]
\label{lem:r13-flux-hessian-invariance}
Under CS3, changing the common linear section of $W\to W/T$
changes $z$ by an affine function on $B$.  Changing any branch
primitive by a strain-preserving affine Killing covector also
changes $z$ by an affine function.  Consequently
$\operatorname{Hess}_Tz$ is independent of these choices.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Two sections differ by a linear map $L:W/T\to T$.  The new
normal lift is $v_i+Lv_i$, so
\[
 z'-z=\sum_iw_i b_i(t,0)|_T(Lv_i)
      =\sum_iw_iK_i(t)(Lv_i).
 \tag{CS12}
\]
In the second equality the common $b_{i_0}$ contribution vanishes
by balancing.  Each $K_i$ is affine by the preceding lemma;
hence CS12 is affine.  The same proof allows individual changes
$v_i\mapsto v_i+t_i$ whose weighted sum $\sum_iw_it_i$ is zero.
For a strain-preserving change on a branch, CS6 in the full
half-product variables gives an affine Killing field.  Its
normal evaluation along $s=0$ is affine in $t$, proving the
second assertion.
\end{proof}

Define the complete labelled normal relation space and raw
incident relation space by
\[
 R_\Sigma=\ker\left(\mathbb R^I\longrightarrow N,
                         (a_i)\longmapsto\sum_ia_iv_i\right),
 \quad
 \mathcal K=\ker\left(\bigoplus_iW_i\longrightarrow T\oplus N\right).
 \tag{CS13}
\]
For $a\in R_\Sigma$ and $u=(u_i)\in\mathcal K$ put
\[
 z_a(t)=\sum_i a_i b_i(t,0)(v_i),\qquad
 \mathcal F_u(t)=\sum_i b_i(t,0)(u_i).
 \tag{CS14}
\]
Every sum map here retains simultaneous relations among all
incident spaces.  It is not replaced by pairwise intersections.

\begin{proposition}[The exact Hessian reduction]
\label{prop:r13-raw-hessian-reduction}
Under CS3, the full Hessian of every raw defect vanishes if and
only if $\operatorname{Hess}_Tz_a=0$ for every
$a\in R_\Sigma$.  More precisely, write uniquely
$u_i=t_i+a_iv_i$.  Then $\sum_it_i=0$, $a\in R_\Sigma$, and
\[
        \mathcal F_u(t)=z_a(t)+\sum_iK_i(t)(t_i).
 \tag{CS15}
\]
The second term is affine.  The correspondence therefore
identifies the effective full relation Hessian with the linear
map
\[
 R_\Sigma\longrightarrow\mathcal D'(B,\operatorname{Sym}^2T^*),
                    \quad a\longmapsto\operatorname{Hess}_Tz_a.
 \tag{CS16}
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Use the fixed splitting $T\oplus N$.  The condition
$\sum_iu_i=0$ separates into the two assertions in the
statement.  Subtracting $b_{i_0}(\sum_it_i)=0$ yields CS15.
Conversely every $a\in R_\Sigma$ is represented by the raw
relation $u_i=a_iv_i$.  This proves both directions and the
linear description CS16.  In particular, tangential duplicate
relations contribute only affine functions even when their
primitive traces have not been aligned.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[One balanced relation gives the full Hessian]
\label{cor:r13-single-balance-full-hessian}
Assume $R_\Sigma=\mathbb Rw$, and suppose
\[
 \sum_iw_i\int A_i\wedge D\chi\wedge\Omega=0
       \quad\hbox{for all }\chi,\Omega\hbox{ in CS7}.
 \tag{CS17}
\]
Then every $\mathcal F_u$ has zero full distributional Hessian
on $B$.  Equivalently, every raw relation defect is affine on
$B$, including across its coefficient walls.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Choose $\chi(t,n)=\varphi(t)\psi(n)$, where $\varphi$ is
arbitrary compact smooth on $B$ and $\psi=1$ near zero.
CS7 and CS17 give
$\int_Bz\,D_T\varphi\wedge\Omega=0$.  All constant symmetric
tangent duals occur, so this is
$\operatorname{Hess}_Tz_w=0$.  Since $w$ spans the entire
$R_\Sigma$, the preceding proposition proves the assertion.
The joint test symbols are the actual pairs
$w\otimes C$, for every symmetric $C$; they span
$R_\Sigma\otimes\operatorname{Sym}^2T$.
\end{proof}

More generally, if actual complete test constructions supply
CS17 for balanced vectors $w^{(1)},\ldots,w^{(r)}$ on the
same coefficient system, their conclusions detect exactly the
restriction of CS16 to their linear span.  Equality of that
span with $R_\Sigma$ is the required finite test.  A list of
separately spanning scalar functions does not supply this
condition on the actual balanced vectors.

\subsection{Normalized marked curves}

Let $C/k$ be a proper smooth integral curve over the original
finite residue field.  Retain its full constant field and put
$\delta_p=[\kappa(p):k]$.  For a finite marked set $M$ with
$|M|\geq2$,
let $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in k(C)^\times$ have divisor supports
in $M$, and let
\[
 \nu_p=(\operatorname{ord}_p g_j)_j\ne0,
 \qquad \nu_p=m_pv_p,
 \qquad m_p\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\quad v_p\text{ primitive}.
 \tag{CS18}
\]
Assume the marked divisor rows of the chosen functions span
the degree-zero hyperplane
\[
 \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}
       \{(\operatorname{ord}_pg_j)_{p\in M}:1\leq j\leq m\}
             =\delta^\perp\subset\mathbb R^M.
 \tag{CS19}
\]
The retained finite-field Picard construction supplies such
functions.  If several prescribed curves lie on one supplied
smooth projective integral model, ML supplies their exact
simultaneous restrictions in the same ambient function field.

\begin{lemma}[Primitive conversion and complete relation kernel]
\label{lem:r13-curve-primitive-kernel}
For $w_p=\delta_pm_p$, the labelled column map
$(a_p)\mapsto\sum_pa_pv_p$ has kernel $\mathbb Rw$.
For the normalized curve parameter $u=-\log|z_p|$ and primitive
image parameter $s=m_pu$, a logarithm with curve order
$\operatorname{ord}_p g$ has primitive slope
\[
 h_p(g)=\frac{\operatorname{ord}_p g}{m_p},
      \qquad w_ph_p(g)=\delta_p\operatorname{ord}_p g.
 \tag{CS20}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The matrix with columns $\nu_p$ has kernel $\mathbb R\delta$
by CS19.  Since its columns are $m_pv_p$, rescaling the columns
gives the asserted kernel.  Substituting $u=s/m_p$ in the
linear branch logarithm proves CS20.  In particular all marks
remain labelled; CS19 also excludes a zero column.  Distinct
marks cannot yield the same primitive ray, since their
coordinate difference would be a kernel vector with entries
of both signs, whereas all $w_p$ are positive.
\end{proof}

The equality $w_p=\delta_pm_p$ in an analytic application is
the actual source calibration, to be supplied by its ordinary
comparison theorem.  CS20 describes its conversion and does
not replace the calibration.  The tangent-face lattice is
the saturated actual lattice.  Any index of its projection
to an older, nonsaturated tangent face remains in that separate
projection formula.

\subsection{Original ordinary tests and tangent-only sources}

We state the analytic application with a finite actual source
presentation.  Let $U$ be an ordinary original analytic
neighborhood, and suppose a fixed finite moment refinement has
a protected calibrated product presentation over $B$ with
labelled main cycle $\Sigma$ as in CS1.  Every added complete
source cycle is balanced, and its old coefficient image is
contained in the same tangent plane.  The retained tangent
coordinates split the actual tangent lattice.  The represented
tensor on such an added source is the literal pullback of
$A_T$.  Require that all compact ambient tests
$\chi\Omega$ used above are realized as original compact
smooth CLD tests on $U$, and that integration uses the complete
source sum with its actual weights.  These are the ordinary
protection and source-comparison hypotheses.

\begin{theorem}[Actual raw-Hessian detector on a completed curve block]
\label{thm:r13-actual-completed-curve-detector}
Suppose the main branch primitives satisfy CS2--CS3, and their
strains represent an ordinary current $Z$ for which
$D[Z]=0$ on every original compact complementary smooth CLD
test on $U$.  If its calibrated main curve star satisfies
CS18--CS19 with actual weights $w_p=\delta_pm_p$, then every
raw incident defect has zero full distributional Hessian on
$B$.  No tangential primitive alignment is needed before this
calculation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix one main tangent trace $b_0$ with $e_Tb_0=A_T$.  On every
additional source use its pullback.  Because the old coefficient
image lies literally in the tangent plane, its strain is the
represented pullback of $A_T$.  In the quotient splitting given
by the retained tangent projection, its normal trace is zero.
The common $b_0$ tangent boundary terms cancel on that whole
balanced source cycle.  If a different quotient section is
used, the lemma on section changes gives the same Hessian
statement.  All source labels and their absolute carriers have
remained in the integral.

The original current equation and the complete source formula
therefore give CS17 for the main cycle.  Its primitives only
need CS3, by the common-strain Stokes theorem.  The curve
primitive-kernel lemma gives $R_\Sigma=\mathbb Rw$, so the
single-balance corollary yields the full raw relation Hessian.
Each symmetric tangent dual is tested together with this same
complete actual one-cycle.  All internal coefficient walls are
already included in CS8--CS11.
\end{proof}

On a positive codimension-one face of a three-dimensional normal
fan, the base $B$ includes both old tangent variables and the
two directions along that face.  The theorem thus tests the
entire Hessian in those variables, including angular and mixed
entries.  Suppose these local Hessian identities cover the whole
connected convex product of the old tangent base with the
relative interior of the positive face, using one fixed finite
coefficient system.  If that system extends continuously to the
central normalized face, the affine expressions agree on
overlaps.  The zero-central-value condition then removes their
constant and old tangent-linear terms.  This gives JF7 on that
whole face.  A single compact box away from the central face
only gives the local affine conclusion of the theorem.  The finite
skew-gauge membership JF8 and the raw systems on other faces
remain distinct finite equations.

\paragraph{Proof inputs.}
The half-product identity is the reviewed FS6--FS9 in
\texttt{finite\_ps\_relative\_stokes.tex}, retained in Round 12
under the frozen Round 11 inputs.  The raw relation convention
is JF3 of Round 12.  The finite Picard row construction is
PP7--PP11 of the retained pointed Picard theorem; the finite
simultaneous ambient restriction theorem is ML of Round 12.
The new deductions here are the cancellation CS10--CS11 with
unequal tangential primitive traces, the section-invariant full
relation Hessian CS12--CS16, and their actual completed-curve
combination under the stated complete source hypotheses.
