title: Final-separator descent and normalized local angular gauges
text:
cap13_final_separator_raw_descent.tex \section{Final-separator descent and normalized local angular gauges}
\label{sec:r13-final-separator-raw-descent}

The completed marked curve will be kept as the \emph{old} coefficient
chart when the last source-separating functions are added.  This order
matters.  Contracting new sources only to the tangent plane of the
pre-completion chart does not control mixed relations involving its
new Picard coordinates.

\subsection{A linear descent statement for the entire labelled star}

Let $T$ and $N$ be finite-dimensional real vector spaces.  Let
$v_p\in N\setminus\{0\}$, $p\in M$, be a finite labelled family
such that
\[
 \ker\bigl(\mathbf R^M\longrightarrow N,\ (a_p)\longmapsto
                    \sum_pa_pv_p\bigr)=\mathbf Rw,
       \qquad w_p>0.
 \tag{SD1}
\]
Write $W_p=T\oplus\mathbf Rv_p$.  On a connected convex open
base $B\subset T$, let $b_p$ be continuous finite piecewise smooth
covectors on the respective half-products, with common tangential
strain.  Their traces are denoted $\beta_p=b_p|_T$ and their
primitive normal traces $c_p=b_p(v_p)$.  Fix $p_0\in M$ and put
\[
 \beta_0=\beta_{p_0},\qquad
 K_p=\beta_p-\beta_0,\qquad z_w=\sum_pw_pc_p.
 \tag{SD2}
\]
By CS6 every $K_p$ is affine Killing on $B$.

Consider a second finite labelled incident system
$W'_\alpha\supset T'$ in an ambient space $W'$, and a linear
map
\[
 \pi:W'\longrightarrow T\oplus N,
                    \qquad \pi|_{T'}:T'\xrightarrow{\sim}T.
 \tag{SD3}
\]
Partition its labels into sets $I_p$, $p\in M$, and $I_0$ such
that
\[
 \pi(W'_\alpha)\subset W_p\quad(\alpha\in I_p),
   \qquad \pi(W'_\alpha)\subset T\quad(\alpha\in I_0).
 \tag{SD4}
\]
No independence among the final spaces or between these sets is
assumed.  Labels with zero old normal image remain in $I_0$.
Choose the pulled-back traces
\[
 b'_\alpha=\pi^*b_p\quad(\alpha\in I_p),\qquad
 b'_\alpha=\pi^*\beta_0\quad(\alpha\in I_0).
 \tag{SD5}
\]
The second expression is defined on the relevant ordinary image
contained in $T$, rather than by restricting an arbitrary current
to $T$.

\begin{theorem}[Every mixed raw Hessian descends to the old flux]
\label{thm:r13-sd-mixed-raw-hessian}
If $\operatorname{Hess}_Tz_w=0$, then every raw defect for the
\emph{whole} final labelled system has zero full Hessian on
$B'=(\pi|_{T'})^{-1}B$.  This includes simultaneous relations
mixing different old marks with arbitrary silent labels.
The conclusion also holds for any other continuous finite-PS
branch primitives with the same strains as SD5.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Take $u'=(u'_\alpha)$ with $\sum_\alpha u'_\alpha=0$.
For $\alpha\in I_p$ write uniquely
\[
 \pi u'_\alpha=t_\alpha+a_\alpha v_p,
 \qquad A_p=\sum_{\alpha\in I_p}a_\alpha,
 \tag{SD6}
\]
and put $t_\alpha=\pi u'_\alpha$ for $\alpha\in I_0$.
Applying $\pi$ to the relation gives
$\sum_\alpha t_\alpha=0$ and $\sum_pA_pv_p=0$.
Thus $A=cw$ for a real constant $c$.  The final raw defect is
exactly
\[
 \begin{split}
 \sum_\alpha b'_\alpha(u'_\alpha)
   &=\sum_pA_pc_p+
       \sum_p\sum_{\alpha\in I_p}K_p(t_\alpha)\\
   &=c z_w+
       \sum_p\sum_{\alpha\in I_p}K_p(t_\alpha).
 \end{split}
 \tag{SD7}
\]
The terms involving the common trace $\beta_0$ cancel because
$\sum t_\alpha=0$.  The remaining evaluations of the fixed
vectors $t_\alpha$ in affine Killing fields are affine.  This
proves the asserted Hessian vanishing, with every mixed relation
retained.  The difference of two primitives with the same strain
on a connected convex half-product is affine Killing by CS6 in
all its variables.  Its boundary evaluation on $u'_\alpha$ is
affine, proving the last assertion.
\end{proof}

The statement requires no decomposition of the final raw kernel
into separate source kernels.  In particular it is stronger than
testing each balanced source independently.  Conversely it
requires SD4 relative to the \emph{completed} old columns: making
silent labels tangent only after forgetting those columns is
insufficient for SD6.

\subsection{An explicit normalized gauge on one whole positive face}

Assume now $T=T_0\oplus E$, with $\dim E=2$, and let
$B=B_0\times\operatorname{relint}(\gamma)$, where $B_0\subset T_0$
is connected and convex and $\gamma\subset E$ is a convex
two-dimensional cone.  All functions extend continuously to
$B_0\times\{0\}$ and satisfy the central normalization
\[
        b_p(t,0,0)|_{T_0}=b_{T_0}(t),\qquad
        b_p(t,0,0)|_{E\oplus\mathbf Rv_p}=0,
 \tag{LG1}
\]
with one common covector $b_{T_0}(t)$; it need not be zero.
Their regularity is the closed-cell regularity of CS.  Assume
$\operatorname{Hess}_Tz_w=0$ on the \emph{whole} $B$.

\begin{theorem}[A local normalized angular gauge]
\label{thm:r13-lg-normalized-angular-gauge}
There are constant alternating forms on the three-dimensional
normal spaces $E\oplus\mathbf Rv_p$, extended by zero on
$T_0$, whose associated linear Killing corrections make every
raw incident defect zero along $B$.  These corrections preserve
the strains and LG1.  After this correction, the branch
covectors admit a common ambient covector trace on $B$.
Pulling the corrected primitives through SD3--SD5 gives the same
conclusion for the whole final system.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By CS6, $K_p$ is an affine Killing covector on $T_0\oplus E$.
Its value is zero on $B_0\times\{0\}$ by the common central
value in LG1.  Write
$K_p(y)=a_p+\Omega_py$ with $\Omega_p$ alternating.  Vanishing
on the nonempty open tangent set implies $a_p=0$ and
$\Omega_pT_0=0$.  Alternation also removes all mixed
$T_0$--$E$ entries.  Thus
\[
              K_p(t,x)=\Omega_p^E x,
                   \qquad \Omega_p^E\in\bigwedge^2E^*.
 \tag{LG2}
\]
Add the Killing covector $-\Omega_p^E x$ on branch $p$,
extended independently of its primitive transverse variable
$s$.  This makes all tangential traces equal to $\beta_0$.
It leaves every $c_p$ and hence $z_w$ unchanged.

The affine function $z_w$ vanishes at $(t,0)$ for every
$t\in B_0$, again by LG1.  Consequently
\[
                              z_w(t,x)=\ell(x)
                         \quad\text{for some }\ell\in E^*.
 \tag{LG3}
\]
On one chosen branch $p_0$, add the further Killing covector
\[
       \kappa_{p_0}(x,s)
           ={s\over w_{p_0}}\,\ell
                  -{\ell(x)\over w_{p_0}}\,ds.
 \tag{LG4}
\]
Here $s$ is the primitive parameter with tangent vector $v_{p_0}$.
Its coefficient matrix is alternating, so its strain is zero.
At $s=0$ its tangential trace is zero, while its contribution to
the weighted normal flux is $-\ell(x)$.  All corrected branches
therefore have the same tangential trace and flux zero.  Every
raw relation vanishes by CS15 and SD1.

The restriction map from the ambient dual of
$T+\operatorname{span}\{v_p\}$ to the finite direct sum of the
$W_p^*$ has image exactly the annihilator of its raw sum kernel.
The corrected traces belong to that image.  A fixed linear
right inverse on this image supplies one ambient covector trace,
continuous and finite-PS in the base variables.  For the final
system use its pullback through $\pi$; each silent branch takes
the common tangent restriction.  All corrections vanish at
$(x,s)=0$, so LG1 is preserved.
\end{proof}

The gauge is local to the one positive face.  Different faces
may require different constant alternating forms on a shared
three-cone.  The existence of a single set of cone gauges valid
at all faces is still the separate JF8 equation.  Local gauges
on every nonzero angular neighborhood do not prove that equation.

\subsection{Finite projection of a supplied actual curve block}

The following use of projection is a calculation on one original
analytic source.  It is not a proper pushforward statement for
an arbitrary current.  Let a fixed adapted tuple $a$ have
radial rank two on an actual curve block supplied by FC and CC.
For calculation, enlarge it by the two CC normal parameters and
a finite generating family for $k(C)$.  These are actual units
on the same ordinary neighborhood.  CC identifies the whole
source of this calculating tuple as the Gauss product, with
the marked calibration $\delta_pm_p$ at every radius.

\begin{lemma}[Calibrated finite projection without a new global completion]
\label{lem:r13-sd-finite-calculating-projection}
The complete top-dimensional source contribution of $a$ on this
ordinary block is the coordinate projection of that entire
calibrated calculating source.  A branch of projected rank less
than three contributes zero to every top-degree form pulled
back from $a$.  A full-rank projected branch has the factor
\[
             i_T\,{m_p^{a}\over m_p},
             \qquad
        \delta_pm_p\,i_T\,{m_p^{a}\over m_p}
                    =\delta_pi_Tm_p^{a},
 \tag{SD8}
\]
where $i_T$ is the saturated tangent lattice index and
$m_p^{a}$ the stretching in the saturated old normal quotient.
All coincident branch images are summed only after their labels
and these factors have been retained.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Retention of $a$ means that every full-rank $a$ source is a
full-rank source of the calculating tuple.  CC identifies all
the latter sources on the specified ordinary block.  The
sourcewise coordinate-refinement formula retained in GP and
CC18 therefore computes the full $a$ contribution.  A
top-degree differential form pulled back through a map of rank
less than three is literally zero on that branch; no current
restriction is being used.  On a full-rank branch, the exact
sequence of tangent and normal lattices gives SD8, precisely as
in CC18.  The ordinary domain and the same analytic source are
unchanged by this calculation.  The calculating coordinates
need not be added to the global tuple on every other source.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Actual detector after one final separator}

\begin{lemma}[Finite normal Newton preparation after the last separator]
\label{lem:r13-sd-finite-normal-newton}
Fix an SP completed curve block with its two rational normal
parameters $z_1,z_2$.  A further fixed finite list of rational
functions in $F$ is adapted after a finite rational conical
subdivision of the positive two-face and regular toroidal
modification.  More precisely, remove the finite one-dimensional
angular tie rays of its normal Newton diagrams.  Each remaining
two-dimensional sector has one leading normal monomial for
each numerator and denominator, with coefficient in
$k(C)^\times$.  The regular two-cones of a finite refinement
are attached to smooth proper curves $C'$ with
$k(C')=k(C)$, hence $C'\simeq C$.  On each such curve the
new functions are adapted, and the old normalized marked orders
are unchanged under this identification and the old coordinate
projection.  Any new mark outside the old marked support has
zero old completed normal column.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Write each rational function as $A/B$ with nonzero
$A,B\in\mathcal O_{V,\eta_C}$.  Complete this regular
two-dimensional local ring and choose a coefficient field.
It is $k(C)[[z_1,z_2]]$.  The support of each nonzero
series has finitely many minimal elements for the coordinatewise
partial order on $\mathbf N^2$: induction on the first
coordinate, retaining only successive strict decreases of the
second, proves this elementary finiteness.  Every exponent
dominates a minimal one.  Therefore every strictly positive
weight takes its minimum on that finite set.  The finitely
many equal-weight rays divide the positive quadrant into
sectors with a unique leading exponent for every $A$ and $B$.
Taking the union over the finite function list gives one finite
rational fan.

Perform the regular toroidal subdivision used in FC.  On each
regular two-cone the pullback of a series is its selected
normal monomial times a unit: every other exponent differs
by a nonnegative vector in the dual cone, and at least one
of its two normal exponents is positive.  The same assertion
holds in the local ring, by faithful flatness of its completion.
Taking the quotient gives the adapted expression for $A/B$.
Over the generic point of $C$, the new two-cone is a split
toric fixed point.  Its residue field is precisely $k(C)$.
Its curve closure is thus birational to $C$; the proper smooth
curve identification follows.  Monomial normal parameters
can be chosen from the original rational $z_1,z_2$ on these
generic charts.  The old normalized residue functions are
then the same functions of $k(C)$.  If other trivializations
are used, SH gives the equivalent common shear, and the old
normal coordinate projection is unchanged.

In particular all old normalized residue functions have order
zero at a point outside their old divisor supports.  New
functions may make such a point visible, but its old completed
normal column remains zero.  Their own finite supports add
only finitely many marks.  The tie rays and all subdivision
boundary rays are lower-dimensional faces; no conclusion of
the two-dimensional-sector statement is assigned to them.
\end{proof}

For an actual analytic unit of norm one at the central point,
first use its rational residue representative.  Their ratio
has residue one, so a strict ordinary inequality gives equal
norms and normalized initial forms on a common central
neighborhood.  This is the finite replacement step of FC.
The lemma therefore applies to the final FA and protection
coordinates without assuming in advance that they were adapted
to the old curve.

We formulate the geometric combination on the supplied
three-dimensional central model of FC, with any supplied
calibrated old tangent factor.  Start with finitely many
specified original two-faces.  Prepare their proper smooth
marked curves by FC.  Apply SP simultaneously and retain the
resulting completed tuple $j$.  Each specified block now has
its old labelled columns $v_p$, weights $w_p=\delta_pm_p$, and
kernel SD1.  All original coefficient coordinates are retained.

\emph{Only after this completion}, apply FA to the whole compact
full source $S_j$, and retain its finite separating coordinates
in a tuple $h$.  Any further finite protection coordinates are
retained too.  Choose a common finite source/target subdivision
for this final tuple.  On the positive two-face pieces considered
below its $j$ projection has rank two and lies in the specified
old two-face.  Work in one sufficiently short common collar;
every face in the conclusion is a whole connected positive
prepared piece of this collar, not an isolated compact box.

\begin{theorem}[Complete positive-face detector with the last separator]
\label{thm:r13-sd-actual-final-separator-detector}
Assume the original coefficient tensor $Z$ has continuous
finite-PS branch primitives as in CS, with common tangential
strain, and that $D[Z]=0$ against every original compact smooth
complementary CLD test.  Use the protected complete calibrated
source presentation of GP, the finite face preparation and
rank alternative of FC, and the all-radius comparison of CC.
Then, over each of the above positive rank-two pieces:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the full distributional Hessian of the old completed
      flux $z_w$ vanishes, including all angular, old tangent,
      and mixed entries;
\item every raw Hessian for the \emph{entire final incident
      system}, including mixed core/satellite relations and
      all zero-old-image labels, vanishes;
\item if the fixed branch system extends to the central face
      with LG1, there is the normalized local angular gauge
      of LG2--LG4 and a continuous finite-PS ambient covector
      lift on a neighborhood of that positive face.
\end{enumerate}
The finite calculating enlargements in the preceding lemma are
used only to evaluate source contributions.  They do not
require a further global Picard completion or a repeated
separator/completion process.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix a compact box in a positive prepared piece.  FC is applied
with \emph{old tuple $j$}.  Because $h$ separates the complete

text:
geom13_uniform_surface_tuple_collar.tex \section{A fixed surface tuple on a nonempty outer divisor collar}
\label{sec:r13-fixed-surface-tuple-collar}

Keep the original finite extension \(K/\mathbf Q_p\), its norm,
and the divisor tube of DT and AF.  The central model has
dimension three, the supplied divisor is \(D\), its actual
surface factor is \((Y_D,v)\), and its normal parameter is
\(Z\).  The surface point has the original discrete value
group.  Write \(q_D(r)\) for the actual relative Gauss point
with \(|Z|=r\).  All ordinary domains below are domains in
these original analytic spaces.

\subsection{One finite set of controls for every outer annulus}

The proof of AF1 uses a finite list of zero-slice functions
on an ordinary surface neighborhood \(W_0\ni v\).  Its
invertible coefficient and localizer functions \(u_i\) have
\(|u_i(v)|=1\); its other coefficient functions \(a_j\) have
\(|a_j(v)|\leq1\).  Inverse functions needed in the estimates
are included among the \(u_i^{\pm1}\).  This list is fixed by
the given finite central conditions and standard etale chart.
For every compact interval \(I\Subset(r_*,1)\), the argument
chooses a number \(c_I>1\), sufficiently close to one, and
uses only the surface restrictions
\[
       c_I^{-1}<|u_i|<c_I,\qquad |a_j|<c_I.
\tag{UA1}
\]
The constants \(M\), the finitely many divisor orders, and
the preliminary threshold \(r_*<1\) are independent of
\(I\).  Bounds such as \(r_+c_I^{M+2}<1\) determine how
close \(c_I\) is to one; they do not change the list of
functions.

Choose a finite tuple of surface units \(C\) as follows.
Retain every \(u_i\).  If \(|a_j(v)|=1\), retain \(a_j\),
after restricting its unit domain.  If \(|a_j(v)|<1\),
retain \(1+a_j\).  Every coordinate of \(C\) has norm one
at \(v\).  Shrink \(W_0\) once so all these are actual
units.  Put \(t_C=-\log|C|\), coordinatewise.

\begin{lemma}[Fixed controls and a fixed protected central fiber]
\label{lem:r13-fixed-controls-protected-fiber}
Let \(F\) be any fixed finite surface tuple retaining \(C\),
and apply GP once on a prescribed ordinary neighborhood of
\(v\) in \(W_0\), retaining \(F\).  Denote the protected
tuple by \(G\), its central value by \(b=t_G(v)\), and its
compact entire central fiber by \(E=t_G^{-1}(b)\).  Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every point of \(E\) satisfies \(|u_i|=1\) and
\(|a_j|\leq1\).
\item For every \(c>1\), one may narrow the target bands
around \(b\), without changing any unit, so their complete
ordinary inverse image satisfies
\(c^{-1}<|u_i|<c\) and \(|a_j|<c\).  The closed narrower
bands still have compact inverse image in the original
interior.  The entire central fiber and all its source
germs remain unchanged.
\item For every \(I\Subset(r_*,1)\), the actual AF product
isomorphism exists on a product containing the relative
Gauss family over all of \(E\), with the narrowed surface
bands of the second assertion.  It satisfies the original
finite central conditions at every analytic product point.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
All coordinates of \(C\) have their norm-one values on
\(E\).  In the case \(|a_j(v)|<1\), the ultrametric
inequality gives
\[
                |a_j|=|(1+a_j)-1|\leq1
                       \quad\hbox{on }E.
\tag{UA2}
\]
The other assertions in the first item follow directly
from the retained coordinates.  To prove the second item,
choose \(1<c'<c\) and restrict the \(C\)-coordinate bands
to \((c'^{-1},c')\).  For a shifted coordinate, its upper
bound gives \(|a_j|\leq\max(|1+a_j|,1)<c'\).  Use still
smaller bands for the closed target closure if necessary.
All these bands contain \(b\), so they retain exactly the
same entire central fiber.  GP supplies compactness and
the interior property before narrowing, and these properties
persist.  Source germs depend on the tuple and an ordinary
neighborhood of their points, not on the widths of bands
containing their central value.

For the last assertion use the AF estimates with the same
finite functions, but on a neighborhood of \(E\) satisfying
UA1.  They are inequalities for zero-slice analytic functions
and hold at every analytic product point.  For an open
interval \(J\) with \(I\Subset J\Subset(r_*,1)\), choose
\(c_I\) so that all strict Newton and divisor-domination
inequalities AF4--AF8 hold.  Cover the compact surface set
by finitely many affinoid neighborhoods contained in the
allowed narrower bands.  Newton iteration on the products
gives the selected root; uniqueness in its Hensel ball
glues the roots and the inverse zero-slice maps.  Taking
ordinary interiors gives the required product.  The same
finite basic central inequalities AF2 place its entire
image in the prescribed original ordinary domain.  This
proof uses the fixed bounds on \(E\); it does not require
that an arbitrary surface neighborhood contain \(E\).
\end{proof}

\subsection{The interval-independent finite preparation}

Fix the initial finite surface coefficient tuple of AF9,
of full normal rank two, and adjoin \(C\).  Keep the fixed
finite closed-cell PS hypotheses of NSA: smooth extensions
near every closed coefficient cell, compatible prescribed
face restrictions, and bounded first derivatives on each
smaller compact truncation.  Bounds are taken only after
an annular interval and truncation have been chosen.

\begin{proposition}[Finite surface preparation before the radial interval]
\label{prop:r13-surface-preparation-before-interval}
In this fixed AF setting, the unit tuple in the annular
NSA construction can be chosen before the compact radial
interval.  More precisely, there is one finite surface
tuple \(H\), consisting of units of norm one at \(v\)
after original-constant normalization, and one fixed
finite sequence of surface geometric preparations, with
\(H\) the last protected tuple on its fixed surface
unit domain.  Write \(E_H=t_H^{-1}(t_H(v))\) for its
entire compact central fiber.  These data have
the following property.  For every
\(I\Subset(r_*,1)\), the construction yields a continuous
finite-PS ambient covector \(\Lambda_I\) in the coordinates
\((Z,H)\) on an ordinary neighborhood of the entire
product over \(I\) and \(E_H\), with
\[
                    t_{(Z,H)}^*e(\Lambda_I)=T,
                       \qquad e=\operatorname{sym}d,
\tag{UA3}
\]
whenever the represented tensor satisfies the original
current equation on the AF product.  This is the complete
ordinary image identity, with all its lower faces.  The
tuple \(H\) and the geometric choices do not depend on
\(I\); the coefficient operators, ordinary truncations
and bounds may depend on \(I\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We specify the choices in the order in which their data
become available.  Every protection performed in this
proof retains \(C\).  Thus Lemma~\ref{lem:r13-fixed-controls-protected-fiber}
permits it to be made once on the surface and used in
every later annular interval by changing only target bands.
Every ordinary localization used for residue identities,
unit domains or full-rank fiber isolation is a fixed
surface localization.  It can be imposed before that
protection.  All analytic domains are common domains of
finitely many such requirements.

\emph{Entry and the full trace space.}
Perform the first CE protection for the fixed old surface
tuple.  Its complete finite central source fiber and every
projected satellite ray are now fixed.  Insert those rays
once to obtain CE's rational normal fan \(\Sigma_0\).
In particular this subdivision is not recomputed when
the tangent interval changes.  The finite-dimensional
space of continuous homogeneous functions linear on
\(\Sigma_0\) is defined by rational face equations.
Choose CG's rational ambient PL/DC extension basis for
this entire space, rather than for the span of the
coefficient functions on one particular interval.

SC applies to that fixed rational family and constructs
its actual cap units, numerical matrix, rational kernel
basis and RB unit representatives before any coefficient
vector is chosen.  All these functions therefore can be
chosen now.  Adjoin them and make the next fixed surface
localization and protection required for SS.  These steps
fix the old tuple \(\tau\) for NSA.  On each later
interval CE and SP construct the conewise primitives;
CG's affine projector is chosen on that interval.  The
resulting central trace lies in the already prepared
full space.  SS and CU use the same fixed cap and unit
families to normalize it.  Their arbitrary compact
tangent tests and the complete protected source sums
are legitimate by the preceding lemma.  Changing the
affine projector changes coefficients, not the PL
basis, caps or units.

\emph{Core, source separation and transverse bases.}
Apply SA to the frozen \(\tau\), then BG, SN and the
source-exhaustion theorem.  Their smooth proper surface,
finite boundary graph, actual node coordinates and
selected-factor localizers depend only on that tuple.
Choose the first FA family on its complete full source
star, with the finite algebraization coordinates retained.
Make the corresponding fixed surface localization and
protection.  Choose the full finite marked sets on all
tracked divisor curves, and choose RT's Picard basis for
the entire weighted zero-sum space on each such set.
SL lifts these functions simultaneously, with residue
one on the other tracked divisors.  Include the finite
SA coordinates required for these functions.

No value of a primitive or a trace function is used in
these choices.  The weighted spanning tree can likewise
be fixed now.  On a later interval RCF computes the
sourcewise flux coefficients, and the tree chooses the
rotation coefficients.  RT is its fixed real linear
map on the resulting entire trace family.  Thus none
of these differential steps adds a unit.  The actual
new-mark and primitive-index checks in NSA are checks
of these fixed finite coordinate maps.  They apply on
every interval with the same labels and weights.

The intermediate protection coordinates cause no new
coefficient-dependent algebraic choice: their norms
are constant on an ordinary surface germ at \(v\).
They can be retained in the fixed pre-Picard tuple,
as NSA does.  Their selected main-source residues are
constants after normalization.  Their additional
protected source germs and projected rays have already
been fixed by the corresponding protection; the NSA
satellite argument retains them in each source sum.

\emph{Final preparation.}
Freeze the tuple containing the preceding coefficients,
caps, kernel units, nodes, first separators, Picard units
and algebraization coordinates, and retain every earlier
protection coordinate before the last protection.
Choose the final FA/CS
separating family and any finite SA completion.  Localize
the complete old full-rank central fiber once.  Perform
the last surface protection, retaining \(C\) again.
Call this last protected tuple \(H\).  All earlier
coordinates have already been retained; there is no
additional coordinate choice after this protection.

For a specified interval, narrow the finitely many
protected target bands using UA1 and the lemma, take
a common smaller normal truncation, and run NSA's
coefficient operations on a real tangent interval
containing \(-\log I\).  The complete image proof of
NSA checks every actual incidence, including the
additional protected sources.  The narrowed target
bands contain \(t_H(v)\), hence their full inverse
image contains the entire same compact fiber \(E_H\).
The fixed-control lemma supplies an AF product over
that whole fiber for the chosen interval.  Its final NL extension
uses only the fixed finite coordinate spaces; the
closed-cell coefficient subdivision and its analytic
extensions may be restricted to the chosen interval.
NL does not select a new analytic unit.  This proves
UA3.  Intersecting the real coefficient cells with a
new tangent interval or with a fixed geometric cone
changes a real subdivision only; no unit is selected
from those coefficient walls.  There are finitely
many geometric stages, and
all have been fixed before the interval.  The full
fixed-tuple assertion follows.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Central lift first, then every sufficiently outer interval}

\begin{theorem}[A nonempty central-compatible punctured collar]
\label{thm:r13-central-compatible-punctured-collar}
Let a fixed central finite coefficient presentation on
the original threefold have the AF closed-cell PS
pullback, and assume \(D[T]=0\) on its original ordinary
domain against all original compact smooth complementary
CLD tests.  Then there are one finite actual central
unit tuple \(\widehat H\), retaining the original
coefficient tuple and \(Z\), and a number \(r_0<1\),
such that the following holds for every compact
\(I\Subset(r_0,1)\).

There is an ordinary neighborhood \(U_I\) of the
entire actual interval \(q_D(I)\), and a continuous
finite-PS ambient covector \(\widehat\Lambda_I\)
in the fixed \(\widehat H\)-coordinates, with smooth
closed-cell extensions and bounded first derivatives
on a smaller fixed truncation, whose strain pulls
back to \(T\) on the complete ordinary image and
every lower face.  Consequently there are smooth
full-exact forms
\[
       a_{I,\eta}=d'\beta_{I,\eta}+d''\zeta_{I,\eta},
              \qquad \epsilon_{I,\eta}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{UA4}
\]
and one fixed positive control \(Q_I=D[q_I]\) on
that domain satisfying the original NSA4 order and
all-background inequalities.  For each \(I\), the
tuple, covector, control and approximation precede
every later allowed symmetric middle-positive
separately \(d'\)- and \(d''\)-closed background,
every original compact complementary smooth test,
and every actual refinement, including rank loss.
The central tuple \(\widehat H\) is independent of
\(I\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Prepare the fixed surface tuple \(H\) of the preceding
proposition.  Normalize its central surface values
by constants in the original \(K\).  For each of its
finitely many residue functions in \(k(D)^\times\),
choose a unit of the residue local ring at \(D\)
mapping to it, and lift that function to an actual
unit at the original threefold point using the
finite same-field unit lifting theorem.  These
central units have divisor order zero at \(D\).
Use DT8 for their exact norm and normalized
initial-form comparison with the prescribed
surface units; the finite ordinary comparison
of two surface lifts with the same residue is
included as well.  The construction uses the
original field and its original norm throughout.

Apply AF1 to this now fixed enlarged central list.
It supplies a threshold \(r_0<1\), enlarged to
include the initial \(r_*\), and for every
\(I\Subset(r_0,1)\) an actual product domain
\(\mathcal A_J\times W_I^{\rm lift}\), with
\(I\Subset J\) and \(v\in W_I^{\rm lift}\),
on which all surface coordinates in \(H\) have
the exact norms of their central lifts.  The
original coefficient coordinates retain their
fixed integral affine graph formulas involving
\(Z\).  Every radial value is included.

Run the preceding proposition on the same
interval, using the original finite central
conditions.  It gives \(\Lambda_I\) on a
product neighborhood
\(\mathcal A_{J'}\times W_I^{\rm strain}\)
of the relative Gauss interval.  Shrink the
two open radial intervals so both still
contain \(I\).  The ordinary surface
intersection
\[
       W_I^{\rm lift}\cap W_I^{\rm strain}
                          \ni v
\tag{UA5}
\]
is nonempty.  Both products use the same
selected zero-slice comparison, by Newton
uniqueness.  Hence they intersect in an
actual product containing \(q_D(I)\).
This is the required nonvacuity: the interval
was chosen after the final central-lift
threshold, and no new coefficient unit is
selected afterward.  Extra finite controls
used to describe the lift domain impose
only an ordinary restriction; they are not
inputs to another scalar trace construction.

On this intersection the exact coordinate
identities transport \(\Lambda_I\) to
\(\widehat\Lambda_I\).  Pullback through
their fixed integral

title: Forcing an entire completed divisor fiber into its ordinary product
text:
geom13_divisor_fiber_product_localization.tex \section{Forcing an entire completed divisor fiber into its ordinary product}
\label{sec:r13-divisor-fiber-product-localization}

Use the algebraic standard etale divisor chart of DT and the
fixed surface preparation of UA.  This section adds finitely
many central coordinate functions.  Their purpose is to
recognize the selected product by inequalities on the entire
moment fiber.  No assumption on the moment rank of another
point in that fiber is made.

Write \(T=(T_1,T_2)\), let \(\Theta\) be the selected etale
coordinate on the original threefold chart, and let
\(\Theta_0\) be the surface coordinate.  The fixed equations
are
\[
 Q(Z,T,\Theta)=0,\qquad P(T,\Theta_0)=0,
 \qquad Q(0,T,\Theta)=P(T,\Theta)R_0(T,\Theta).
\tag{UF1}
\]
All coefficients lie in \(R[T,G^{-1}]\), after including
finitely many selected localizers.  The functions \(T_i\),
\(\Theta_0\), the relevant localizers, and the selected
derivative and complementary factors have norm one at the
surface point \(v\).  This is the zero-slice chart used in
DT.  Passing to a smaller such chart or multiplying a
coordinate by an original constant does not change the
construction.  In a degree-one or trivial etale presentation,
if the selected \(\Theta_0\) has zero residue, replace both
\(\Theta_0\) and \(\Theta\) by their sum with one.  This
integral coordinate change makes their core norms one and
preserves UF1 and its derivative conditions.

\subsection{Rational coordinates which recognize a surface neighborhood}

\begin{lemma}[A finite rational neighborhood packet]
\label{lem:r13-rational-neighborhood-packet}
Let \(W\) be an ordinary neighborhood of \(v\) in this
surface chart.  Let \(h_1,\ldots,h_s\) be finitely many
actual surface units of norm one at \(v\).  There are a
smaller ordinary neighborhood \(W'\subset W\), rational
functions \(r_j\) with
\[
                         |h_j|=|r_j|\quad\hbox{on }W',
\tag{UF2}
\]
and finitely many pairs of integral polynomial functions
\(A_a(T,\Theta_0),B_a(T,\Theta_0)\), all of norm one
at \(v\), such that any surface point at which all the
selected chart localizers have norm one and
\[
                       |A_a|=|B_a|=1\quad\hbox{for every }a
\tag{UF3}
\]
belongs to \(W'\) and satisfies \(|h_j|=1\) for every
\(j\).  Denominators involving the fixed localizers are
cleared in the displayed polynomials.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
SA, or its single-function residue approximation step,
replaces each \(h_j\) by a rational surface function
with the same norm on one ordinary neighborhood of
\(v\).  Intersect these finitely many neighborhoods
with \(W\).  The topology of an affine algebraic
analytification is generated by norms of its regular
functions.  Choose a finite basic algebraic open
neighborhood inside that intersection.  Include upper
bounds for a finite affine coordinate-generating tuple
if a fixed bounded chart is desired.  Every nonzero
regular function has nonzero value at the generic
model point \(v\); its value is in \(|K^\times|\).
Normalize it by an original constant to have norm
one.  Retaining its norm-one equality implies all
the strict inequalities defining that basic open.

Include these finitely many normalized rational
functions and the \(r_j\).  Each has norm one at
the generic special-fiber point.  It can be written
as a quotient of two functions in a fixed smooth
integral affine model ring with nonzero reductions.
Indeed cancel the common \(\pi\)-order of its
numerator and denominator in the localization at
that generic point, and add finitely many
nonzero-reduction localizers.  Clearing these
localizers gives integral polynomial numerator
and denominator representatives, each with norm
one at \(v\).  Retain both.  Their norm-one
equalities give the required rational-function
equalities, placing the point in the chosen basic
open and giving \(|r_j|=1\).  Call that open
\(W'\).  Equation UF2 proves the last assertion.
\end{proof}

For each polynomial in this packet, define its direct
central lift by substituting \(\Theta\) for
\(\Theta_0\), without changing its coefficients:
\[
       \widehat A_a=A_a(T,\Theta),\qquad
       \widehat B_a=B_a(T,\Theta).
\tag{UF4}
\]
Their residues are nonzero along \(D\), so these
are norm-one actual units on a common ordinary
neighborhood of the original central point.

\begin{lemma}[The entire fiber has a selected zero-slice point]
\label{lem:r13-entire-fiber-zero-slice}
There is a finite actual central tuple \(J_D\)
containing \(Z\), the chart coordinate and localizer
functions, the direct lifts in UF4, and the selected
polynomial derivative, with the following property.
On a sufficiently outer collar, if an original point
\(x\) in their common ordinary chart satisfies
\[
                    t_{J_D}(x)=t_{J_D}(q_D(r)),
                             \qquad r<1,
\tag{UF5}
\]
then it belongs to the selected ordinary product
tube and its zero-slice point \(x_0\) belongs to
\(W'\) and satisfies \(|h_j(x_0)|=1\) for all \(j\).
This assertion includes arbitrary moment ranks and
all commensurable radial values.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
If \(P(T,\Theta)\) is not identically zero on the
central chart, retain it as another actual unit,
after original-constant normalization if necessary.
It is nonzero at the central generic point, so
its unit domain contains one ordinary central
neighborhood.  If it is identically zero, no
coordinate is needed for it.  Retain
\(P_\Theta(T,\Theta)\), and the finite zero-slice
and chart localizers, in addition to UF4.  Every
norm-one function in this list is indeed norm
one at \(q_D(r)\): on the product,
\(|\Theta-\Theta_0|<1\), and integral polynomial
evaluation preserves every nonzero reduction.
Also
\[
 |P(T,\Theta)(q_D(r))|<1,
 \qquad |P_\Theta(T,\Theta)(q_D(r))|=1.
\tag{UF6}
\]
This is the selected DT Hensel comparison.  The
finite collar merely places all points and unit
domains in the original central chart.

Equation UF5 gives exactly these inequalities
at \(x\), together with \(|Z(x)|=r<1\),
\(|T_i(x)|=|\Theta(x)|=1\), and norm one for
every retained localizer.  Coefficients of \(P\)
therefore have norm at most one.  Hensel's lemma
in the complete field \(\mathcal H(x)\) gives
the unique root \(\theta_0\) with
\[
                       |\theta_0-\Theta(x)|<1.
\tag{UF7}
\]
If \(P(T,\Theta)\) is identically zero, take
\(\theta_0=\Theta(x)\).  This root defines
the surface point \(x_0\); all selected
localizers remain nonzero there.

Integral polynomial evaluation in UF7 gives
\[
 |A_a(T,\theta_0)-\widehat A_a(x)|<1,
 \qquad
 |B_a(T,\theta_0)-\widehat B_a(x)|<1.
\tag{UF8}
\]
Their central norms at \(q_D(r)\) are one,
so UF5 and UF8 give UF3 at \(x_0\).  The
preceding lemma gives \(x_0\in W'\) and
\(|h_j(x_0)|=1\).

Finally the polynomial \(Q\) has a unique
selected root within distance less than one
of \(\theta_0\).  Its Newton inequalities
follow from UF1, \(|Z|<1\), the retained
derivative and complementary factor norms,
and the same integral coefficient bounds.
The original \(\Theta(x)\) is that root.
The values \(Z(x),T(x),\theta_0\) in
\(\mathcal H(x)\) specify a joint seminorm,
and hence an \(\mathcal H(x)\)-valued
point of the analytic product.  Its two
underlying factor points alone would not
specify that product point.  Locally these
root constructions are analytic: continuity
gives strict Newton margins, and iteration
converges on an affinoid neighborhood.  Root
uniqueness glues the resulting inverse
analytic map to the product.  Composing
with the selected product map fixes
\(Z,T\), and fixes \(\Theta\) by the
preceding unique-root argument, so the
composition is the identity.  Thus
the conclusion is membership in an actual
ordinary product domain.  No graded-rank
count has been used.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The complete central image near the supplied ray}

Take \(H\) to be the fixed final protected surface
tuple in the proof of UA.  Its unit domain is fixed
before the annular interval.  For each interval
\(I\), the NSA construction is valid on the full
inverse image of a target neighborhood of
\(t_H(v)\) in that domain.  In particular it
contains the entire central \(H\)-fiber in any
fixed smaller unit domain.  This is the final
GP complete-image conclusion of NSA, retained
in UA's fixed geometric preparation.

Choose \(W\) inside that fixed unit domain,
and apply the packet lemma to every coordinate
of \(H\).  Include direct central representatives
of the rational functions \(r_j\) as well as
their separate numerators and denominators in
\(J_D\).  Near every point of the fiber in
UF5, their norms equal those of the surface
\(H\)-coordinates, by UF2 and the strict
polynomial estimates UF8.

\begin{theorem}[Completed core-ray fiber localization]
\label{thm:r13-completed-ray-fiber-localization}
For the fixed divisor and fixed central finite-PS
tensor in UA, there is one finite central
refinement \(F\), and a protected ordinary
central domain, such that for every compact
interval \(I\) in one sufficiently outer
collar the following hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The entire \(F\)-moment fiber over every
\(t_F(q_D(r))\), \(r\in I\), is contained
in an ordinary domain carrying the transported
NSA covector.  The same assertion holds for
every actual source in these fibers, including
points whose earlier moment rank is only two
or less.
\item There is an open target neighborhood
\(\mathcal O_I\) of
\(\{t_F(q_D(r)):r\in I\}\) whose complete
ordinary inverse image lies in that domain.
On its complete image the transported finite-PS
covector has the full all-face strain identity.
It has the fixed-control approximation and
all-background conclusions of UA for this
interval.
\end{enumerate}
One finite refinement works for a supplied
finite list of divisors and their respective
core rays.  The statement concerns neighborhoods
of those completed core rays; it does not
assert that they include every new ray which
projects to an earlier ray.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Retain \(J_D\), all original coefficient
coordinates, and the finite rational
representatives just specified.  Apply one
central GP on their common original ordinary
domain.  Call the completed tuple \(F\)
and its compact protected closure \(D_0\).
The protecting coordinates are constant on
an ordinary neighborhood of the original
central point, so every sufficiently short
core ray is retained unchanged.  All core
values in a sufficiently outer collar lie
inside the open protected target box.

Let \(x\) be any point in the entire
\(F\)-fiber over a core value.  Projection
to \(J_D\) gives UF5.  The preceding lemma
places its zero-slice point in the fixed
surface unit domain and in the entire
central \(H\)-fiber.  UA's fixed-control
lemma puts that full protected fiber inside
the valid AF product for the chosen radial
interval.  The final NSA primitive is valid
there on the complete image.  The direct
central lifts and UF8 transfer it on an
ordinary neighborhood of \(x\).  The
surface covector is a single ambient
formula \(\Lambda_I\); these transferred
formulas therefore agree wherever their
domains overlap.  Take their union as the
ordinary domain in the first assertion.
This argument has not removed a source
according to its rank.

The inverse image in \(D_0\) of the
compact set of core values for \(I\)
is compact and, by the first assertion,
is contained in that ordinary domain.
The closed complement in \(D_0\) has
compact moment image, disjoint from those
core values.  An open target neighborhood
avoiding this compact image and contained
in the original protected box is the
required \(\mathcal O_I\).  Protection
ensures that its full inverse image is
computed inside \(D_0\), and hence lies
in the stated ordinary domain.

The coefficient identity was transported
on every face, so it holds on this entire
inverse image and on every later retaining
refinement, including rank degeneration.
Apply the same strain smoothing argument
as in UA on a smaller protected truncation.
For finitely many supplied divisors, take
the union of the finite packets before
the final central GP and the maximum of
their finitely many radial thresholds.
Projection to each packet proves its
fiber assertion separately.  No further
iteration of surface preparation is
required for this finite list.
\end{proof}

text:
cap13_punctured_quadratic_action_and_point_residual.tex \section{Ordinary punctured quadratic action on a supplied normal-three germ}
\label{sec:r13-punctured-quadratic-action}

\paragraph{Scope and dependency convention.}
This section concerns the supplied original-field smooth integral
threefold model germ of BP and TC.  Its centre is denoted by $y$,
its original value group is $|K^\times|$, and
$F=\widetilde{\mathcal H(y)}$ has transcendence degree three over
the original finite residue field $k$.  The germ is ordinary, and
all later neighborhoods are ordinary.  The scalar presentation is
in the fixed finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS class of OR and
EN.  In particular, its coefficient functions have smooth
extensions near the closed cells of a finite rational complex.
No assertion about an arbitrary unsupplied threefold germ, higher
coupled relations, variable-PS closure, or GK tests is made here.

The inputs are the source-bound retained theorems OR, QA/QP,
EN/ES, BP, TC and FA, and the present-round FC, CC, SP, AH,
CS, SD/LG, UA and UF theorems.  The ordinary-locality statement
OL is also used.  Every use below preserves the complete actual
source and every original compact complementary smooth CLD test.
The improvement is an ordinary open-cover composition for the
action.  It does not construct one primitive on the whole
puncture or solve its global Killing descent problem.

Let $f$ be the original finite scalar tuple and write
\[
 P=\sum_\nu c_\nu[h_\nu][k_\nu],\qquad
 \kappa_2(P)=\sum_\nu c_\nu
             D_\delta h_\nu\wedge D_\delta k_\nu=0.
 \tag{PA1}
\]
Put
\[
 Z_P=\tfrac12\sum_\nu c_\nu
   (d'_Ph_\nu\wedge d''_Pk_\nu+
                         d'_Pk_\nu\wedge d''_Ph_\nu).
 \tag{PA2}
\]
The exact quadratic transgression gives $D[Z_P]=0$.  First adjoin
finitely many normalized residue generators of $F$ to $f$, so
the entry tuple has the full required residue rank.  Apply the
finite EN--AN/ES construction once, and freeze its final completed
tuple as $\tau$.  ES1 supplies the corrected conewise primitives
on every cone of this final complete ordinary image.  In
particular these include new cones created by its central unit
completion: the final paragraph of the ES proof pulls an EN
primitive from a containing old face, even for a rank-losing
projection, and then subtracts the common ambient correction.
There is no repeated central completion in this argument.
Later refinements only pull back these fixed data.  Its old
complete source is
\[
                  P_\tau=S_\tau=\{x:d_\tau(x)=3\}.
 \tag{PA3}
\]
The symbol $P_\tau$ in this section denotes a source set, and
is different from the formal relation $P$ in PA1.
Apply FA to a compact old source star in $P_\tau$, obtaining
$h=(\tau,g)$.  Its asserted injectivity is on $P_\tau$ only.
There is no assertion that $t_h$ embeds all of $S_h$.
Neither the old tuple $\tau$ nor the inventory $P_\tau$ will
be enlarged during the following cover argument.

\subsection{A genuine ordinary neighborhood at a top-cone point}

The next observation supplies the precise ordinary input at top
interiors.  It avoids assuming that a selected source cone is
already the complete ordinary moment image.

\begin{lemma}[Ordinary containment in a prepared top plane]
\label{lem:r13-top-plane-ordinary-containment}
Let $p$ be a closed triple point of a prepared TC model and let
$q_p(t_1,t_2,t_3)$ be its actual family, with all $t_a>0$.
Suppose the fixed old tuple is monomial there, with order matrix
$A$ of rank three.  Then at every sufficiently short positive
point $q=q_p(t)$ there is an ordinary neighborhood $V_q$ such
that
\[
                         t_\tau(V_q)\subset\operatorname{im}A.
 \tag{PA4}
\]
All positive radius vectors are included.  In particular no
rational-independence restriction is made.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose an integral basis $m_1,\ldots,m_b$ of the lattice of
rows annihilating $A$.  In the selected integral TC formal
chart each $\tau^{m_i}$ has normal exponent zero.  Its
constant residue $a_i$ belongs to the finite field
$\kappa(p)$ and is nonzero.  Let $H_i(T)\in K^\circ[T]$
lift the monic minimal polynomial of $a_i$ over $k$, with
unit constant term.  The formal expansion of
$H_i(\tau^{m_i})$ has constant coefficient divisible by
the original uniformizer.  Every coefficient not divisible
by that uniformizer has positive total normal degree.
At three radii strictly smaller than one, its Gauss norm
is therefore strictly smaller than one.  More explicitly,
after clearing a denominator with unit constant term, it
is bounded by the maximum of $|\pi|$ and the three radii.
The denominator has norm one.  The finite actual-to-formal
comparison of TC thus gives
\[
                  |H_i(\tau^{m_i})(q)|<1.
 \tag{PA5}
\]
Continuity makes all these inequalities hold on one ordinary
neighborhood of $q$.  For an element of norm less than one
the unit constant term of $H_i$ dominates, while for an
element of norm greater than one its monic leading term
dominates.  Hence PA5 forces $|\tau^{m_i}|=1$ there.
The common real kernel of the $m_i$ is $\operatorname{im}A$,
which proves PA4.  The argument uses a strict actual
inequality at each point, rather than a density argument.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Top-interior local action]
\label{cor:r13-top-interior-local-action}
At every positive point in the relative interior of a prepared
old top cone there is an ordinary neighborhood on which the
relation in PA1 has zero action for every allowed background.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
EN supplies a continuous finite-PS covector on the closed old
cone, with the full prescribed strain, including coefficient
walls.  At a point in its relative interior choose a small open
set in its three-plane.  Extend the covector to an ambient
neighborhood by a linear retraction to that plane.  PA4 and
continuity give an ordinary neighborhood whose whole old moment
image lies in this open set of the plane.  The pulled covector
therefore has exactly the old energy strain at every ordinary
point and on every later face, also when the later tangent map
loses rank.  Add back the actual ambient exact ES correction.
QA then gives the claimed action equality.  Alternatively the
retained source-side regularization gives a fixed positive
control on each smaller local truncation.  A choice of primitive
on any other old cone is unnecessary here.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The fixed old inventory and its ordinary cover}

\begin{theorem}[Punctured action on the supplied normal-three germ]
\label{thm:r13-punctured-quadratic-action}
Under the supplied model and finite scalar hypotheses above,
there is an ordinary representative $U$ of $y$ such that for
every original symmetric middle-positive background $S$,
separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed, of legal bidegree $(p,p)$,
\[
                   \mathcal A_S(P)|_{U\setminus\{y\}}=0,
                         \qquad p=0,1.
 \tag{PA6}
\]
The equality holds on all original compact complementary smooth
CLD tests and all actual refinements.  Different members of the
ordinary cover used to prove PA6 may have different finite unit
tuples, covectors and positive controls.  The neighborhood $U$
and its cover are chosen for the fixed relation before choosing
$S$ or a later test.  Its absolute carrier is not changed.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We record the finite preparation and the ordinary coverage
separately, since they have different roles.

\emph{1. Fix the old source once.}
Use a compact source truncation in the analytic interior.  The
canonical source has a finite polyhedral structure, its moment
map has finite fibers, and its germ at $y$ is exhausted by the
finitely many closed TC cones.  The faithful coordinates $h$
embed precisely this old source truncation.  They are retained
whenever an actual point on it is compared with a model point.
Because its central moment fiber is finite, an ordinary
shrinking isolates its central point $y$ from the other points
of that fiber.  In faithful coordinates the germ is a finite
star with this single centre.  TC's uniform all-angle ordinary
convergence places a common short star in this shrinking.

Every later unit in the finite central geometric preparation
lists is defined near $y$ and restricts to a rational PL
function on $P_\tau$ by the canonical unit-log property.
Consequently a finite list of these units gives a common finite
subdivision of this same old star.  Equivalently, after putting
the list in a common enlarged source complex, $P_\tau$ is the
old subcomplex described by its canonical old-rank condition,
with that common subdivision.  The old set is not replaced by
the enlarged full source.  Actual coincident labels are compared
using $h$, not merely their old geometric image.  A test chosen
later may use units defined only on a punctured local member;
it is handled there by its actual common refinement, and is not
inserted into this central geometric inventory.

\emph{2. Cover the positive two-dimensional old pieces.}
There are finitely many labelled two-faces in the chosen old
subdivision.  FC prepares each by a proper residue curve and
two positive normal parameters, over the original field.  Apply
SP to these finitely many original curve blocks, retaining all
old coordinates and all marked points.  Apply the last faithful
separator after this Picard completion, with that completed tuple
as the old tuple for the FC source alternative.  SD then applies
to the entire final incident source: main branches, subdivisions,
new zero-old-column marks, and ordinary-plane satellite pieces
all remain present.  Its raw-kernel descent and LG correction
give an actual ambient local strain lift on every resulting
open positive two-dimensional sector.

There are only finitely many exceptional angular rays here.
Indeed SD's finite normal Newton lemma is applied to a fixed
finite list of final functions, once for each of the finitely
many old curve blocks.  It removes finitely many rational
one-dimensional tie walls and makes a finite regular toroidal
subdivision.  The all-radius CC comparison and AH projection
calibration justify SD on every open sector, including
commensurable parameters and all full sources over it.  The
ordinary neighborhood in SD is a neighborhood of the actual
point on the old face, with the complete moment image used in
the strain equality.  It is not a current restricted to the
curve or to a selected skeleton.

\emph{3. Cover the remaining finite ray families.}
Take all old one-faces, the finite Newton tie rays of step 2,
and all rays introduced by the finite geometric subdivisions.
This is still a finite list in the fixed old source star.
The regular monomial refinement in FC realizes each as a
divisor on a smooth projective SNC model.  The normalized old
$\tau$-character residues on this divisor generate a field of
transcendence degree two: at a free point of the old ray its
old graded rank is three and its value rank is one.  The
monomial valuation comparison identifies these residues with
the restrictions on the realized divisor.  Thus the DT Gauss
family itself belongs to $S_\tau$ at free radii, and at all
radii by continuity and closedness.  Faithfulness is applied
only after this old-source membership has been established.
Equality of the finite monomial coordinate norms and the
retained faithful coordinates then identifies its actual radial
family with the old family.  This is also the boundary
identification in TC; it holds at all radii by continuity after
identification at free parameters.

Apply UA and UF to each of these finitely many divisors and
to the pulled old energy.  They give a common short outer collar
and, for every compact interval in it, an ordinary neighborhood
of the entire completed core fiber carrying the transported
surface covector.  In particular every positive point of every
listed old ray has an ordinary neighborhood with a full strain
lift and zero action for every original $S$.  The local tuple
for one ray need not be used in the proof at another ray.
Choosing an interval around each radial value covers every
sufficiently short positive point.  Finiteness of the divisor
list permits a common initial shortening; compact subintervals
need not have one common primitive or coefficient bound.

\emph{4. Cover the top interiors.}
The remaining positive old points lie in relative interiors of
prepared top cones.  BP/TC and the finite monomial subdivision
make the fixed old functions monomial there.  The preceding
top-plane lemma and corollary give an ordinary all-background
action neighborhood at each such point, at every positive
radius vector.  Coefficient walls inside a top cone are covered
by its full EN covector; when a geometric subdivision records
them as faces, steps 2--3 supply the same local conclusion.

\emph{5. Cover the complement of the old source.}
At an ordinary point $x\notin P_\tau$ one has
\[
                     d_f(x)\le d_\tau(x)\le2,
                  \qquad s_f(x)\le2.
 \tag{PA7}
\]
OR therefore supplies an ordinary action-zero neighborhood of
$x$, with the original scalar tuple $f$ used for its rank
condition.  OR already retains arbitrary later tests and
refinements; their enlarged ranks need not satisfy PA7.

No recursively growing source inventory is required in this
step.  A new point revealed by units used in one local proof
is either outside $P_\tau$ and covered by PA7, or is a point
of the already classified old star.  In the latter case it
is a top, two-face, or ray point treated above.  If it is a
point of $P_\tau$ over the faithful old coordinates of a
specified core point, faithfulness on $P_\tau$ identifies it
with that actual point.  UF then includes it in the same
completed fiber.  Distinct new rays with other final coordinates
are not claimed to lie in UF's one product tube.

\emph{6. Use ordinary locality.}
After the finite common shortenings, every point of
$U\setminus\{y\}$ belongs to one of the ordinary neighborhoods
in steps 2--5.  This is a cover of actual points of the ordinary
puncture.  It is stronger than a cover of free parameters or of
an angular link.  For an original compact smooth test supported
in the puncture choose a finite subordinate original smooth
partition of unity.  Each localized test is annihilated by the
corresponding local action theorem.  OL gives PA6, using the
same fixed $S$ on each member.  Linearity of the action permits
their sum, and every local equality already allowed the
test's own actual common refinement.  This proves PA6 without
a global covector, a global fixed control, or a pushforward of
the arbitrary background.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{What this composition does not conclude.}
The finite cover argument is for the action on a punctured
ordinary domain.  It does not identify a full global primitive
for $Z_P$, remove the central point, prove a KC12 seminorm
certificate, or establish the general actual analytic relation
descent theorem.  In particular PK's real global Killing
obstruction does not contradict PA6, and PA6 does not remove
that obstruction from a demanded global primitive.

\subsection{The exact point-supported remainder}

\begin{lemma}[Separately closed order-zero currents at one point]
\label{lem:r13-point-supported-order-zero}
Let $X$ be an original allowed pure $n$-dimensional space and
let $T$ be a coefficient-Radon current of bidegree $(a,b)$,
supported at one actual point $y$.  If $d'T=0$ and $a<n$,
then $T=0$.  If $d''T=0$ and $b<n$, the same conclusion
holds.  Thus a separately closed such current is zero unless
$(a,b)=(n,n)$; in top degree it is $c\delta_y$ for a scalar
$c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For each fixed local smooth form $\xi$, the scalar functional
$u\mapsto T(u\xi)$ is a Radon measure, by the coefficient-
Radon property.  Its support is contained in $\{y\}$.
Consequently it depends only on $u(y)$.  In one common local
moment presentation, an arbitrary test can therefore be
replaced, for its pairing with $T$, by its form with constant
coefficients at $t(y)$, multiplied by a cutoff equal t

title: The protected background transpose and its critical tangent currents
text:
joint13_protected_background_trace_and_tangents.tex \section{The protected background transpose and its critical tangent currents}
\label{sec:r13-protected-background-trace}

The positive background in the remaining threefold Dirac
problem has degree one.  On a protected finite moment domain
its exact action on pulled-back smooth tests is a positive
closed real supercurrent of bidimension two.  Its trace has
quadratic growth.  This supplies a uniform critical bound,
without assuming a local potential for the background or
discarding any part of a moment fiber.

\subsection{An exact transpose on a complete proper moment domain}

Let \(U\) be an original ordinary domain of pure dimension
three, and let \(t:U\to\Omega\subset\mathbf R^N\), \(N\ge2\), be one
finite actual moment map on a GP-protected domain.  Thus
\(\Omega\) is open, and
\[
       t^{-1}(L)\text{ is compact in }U
                         \quad(L\Subset\Omega\text{ compact}).
\tag{MT1}
\]
The inverse image in MT1 is the entire ordinary inverse
image.  It is not an old-source inverse image.  Let \(S\)
be any original symmetric middle-positive separately
\(d'\)- and \(d''\)-closed current of degree \((1,1)\)
on \(U\).  Define, for every compactly supported smooth
real \((2,2)\)-superform \(\eta\) on \(\Omega\),
\[
                       \langle T,\eta\rangle
                              =\langle S,t^*\eta\rangle.
\tag{MT2}
\]

\begin{proposition}[Middle positivity and both closedness equations]
\label{prop:r13-protected-background-transpose}
Formula MT2 defines a symmetric middle-positive real
supercurrent of bidimension \((2,2)\), hence bidegree
\((N-2,N-2)\), with
\[
                       d'T=d''T=0.
\tag{MT3}
\]
For \(\beta=\tfrac12D|x|^2\), its positive trace measure
is
\[
             \mu_T=\tfrac12T\wedge\beta^2,
 \qquad
 \mu_T(A)=\tfrac12
       \bigl(S\wedge t^*\beta^2\bigr)(t^{-1}(A))
\tag{MT4}
\]
for relatively compact Borel subsets \(A\) of \(\Omega\).
Every coefficient measure of \(T\) has total variation
bounded by a fixed dimensional multiple of \(\mu_T\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
MT1 makes \(t^*\eta\) an original compact smooth CLD
test.  On each fixed compact support the finite pullback
is continuous in the usual smooth test topology, proving
that MT2 is a current.  Column exchange commutes with
this pullback, giving symmetry.  If \(\alpha\) is a
smooth real \((2,0)\)-form, the standard signed form
\(\alpha\wedge J\alpha\) is middle-positive and so is
its pullback.  The assumed original middle positivity
of \(S\) therefore gives exactly middle positivity of
\(T\).  No equivalence with weak or strong positivity
in the ambient dimension \(N\) has been used.

Pullback commutes with both first derivatives.  Compact
support remains inside \(U\) by MT1, so applying either
closedness equation of \(S\) to a pulled-back test proves
MT3.  In particular no source cutoff has been inserted:
such a cutoff could have introduced an additional boundary
derivative, whereas MT2 uses the whole protected inverse
image.

The scalar functional obtained by testing against
\(\varphi\beta^2/2\) is a positive Radon measure.
The equality for smooth \(\varphi\) in MT2 identifies
it with the proper measure transpose in MT4, and hence
gives that equality for Borel sets.  In a constant
\((2,0)\) basis the cocoefficient measures form a
positive-semidefinite matrix.  Its diagonal sum is the
trace, and polarization bounds each off-diagonal
variation by one half the sum of the two corresponding
diagonal measures.  This gives the asserted coefficient
control, with the fixed orientation and basis constants.
\end{proof}

This construction is an exact finite-presentation test
transpose.  It does not assert a higher-degree analytic
action, a pushforward formula for an arbitrary cap carrier,
or that tests in this one target replace all original tests.
The current \(S\) still has its original complete carrier.
In particular MT4 includes background mass at every point
of the relevant moment fiber, regardless of its old rank.

\subsection{The exact quadratic trace estimate}

Translate \(t(y)\) to zero and fix
\(\overline{B_{r_0}(0)}\subset\Omega\).  Let
\(M_T(r)=\mu_T(B_r(0))\).  The following is the
bidimension-two case of the real Lelong monotonicity
calculation; the normalization is recorded explicitly.

\begin{theorem}[Quadratic growth and finite critical density]
\label{thm:r13-protected-quadratic-trace-growth}
The function
\[
                         r\longmapsto\frac{M_T(r)}{r^2}
\tag{MT5}
\]
is nondecreasing for \(0<r<r_0\).  Consequently
\[
 \begin{split}
 M_T(r)&\le \frac{M_T(r_0)}{r_0^2}\,r^2,\qquad 0<r<r_0,\\
 \nu(T,0)&=\lim_{r\downarrow0}\frac{M_T(r)}{r^2}
                                      \quad\text{exists and is finite}.
 \end{split}
\tag{MT6}
\]
No assertion that \(\nu(T,0)=0\) is part of the theorem.
In particular \(\mu_T(\{0\})=0\), while the density
in MT6 can be positive.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First suppose \(T\) is smooth.  On an annulus write
\(r=|x|\) and use
\[
 D r=\frac{\beta}{r}
                -\frac{d'r\wedge d''r}{r}.
\tag{MT7}
\]
On the sphere of radius \(r\), the first differential
\(d'r\) pulls back to zero.  Stokes, using \(d'T=0\),
therefore gives for \(0<a<b<r_0\)
\[
 \frac{M_T(b)}{b^2}-\frac{M_T(a)}{a^2}
             =\frac12\int_{a<|x|<b}T\wedge(D|x|)^2\ge0.
\tag{MT8}
\]
To check the constant, apply Stokes first to
\(T\wedge\beta^2\), and note on a sphere that
\(d''(|x|^2/2)=r\,d''r\) and
\(\beta=r\,Dr\) after tangential pullback in
the Stokes boundary expression.  The resulting boundary
identity is
\[
 \frac{M_T(r)}{r^2}
       =\frac12\int_{|x|=r}T\wedge d''r\wedge Dr.
\]
Subtract this identity at \(a\) from that at \(b\),
and apply Stokes on the annulus, where \(r\) is smooth.
This proves MT8 without introducing any product of
\(D|x|\) at the origin.
The integrand on the annulus is positive: \(Dr\)
is semipositive and its square is strongly positive,
so it may be paired with the middle-positive \(T\).

For a general coefficient-Radon current convolve its
coefficients by a nonnegative compact smoothing kernel,
inside a slightly smaller ball.  The resulting currents
are smooth, middle-positive and separately closed.
Their trace measures converge weakly to \(\mu_T\).
At radii whose spheres have zero trace mass, MT8
passes to the limit.  There are at most countably
many exceptional radii.  Approximation of arbitrary
open balls from below by nonexceptional radii gives
the monotonicity in MT5 for all \(a<b\).  The finite
measure on the fixed larger compact ball gives MT6;
letting \(r\downarrow0\) also gives the absence of
an atom of the trace itself.
\end{proof}

The printed statement of Lagerberg's Proposition 3.4
omits the word closed, but its Stokes proof and the
following corollary use closedness.  MT3 is imposed
and proved here.  Middle positivity is also essential
for coefficient control: Lagerberg's Remark 3.3
exhibits a weakly positive nonzero tensor with zero
trace.  No such weaker cone is substituted in MT4.

The exponent two is sharp.  A positive integration
current of a complete real two-plane has
\(M_T(r)=c r^2\), with \(c>0\).  Thus MT6
supplies the critical bound required for a first-jet
replacement in CR; it does not supply CR5's little-o
bound for the leading homogeneous term.

\subsection{Compactness and conicity of critical tangent currents}

For \(\delta>0\), let \(a_\delta(x)=x/\delta\)
and define on \(a_\delta(\Omega)\)
\[
                  T_\delta=\delta^2(a_\delta)_*T.
\tag{MT9}
\]
The pushforward here is only the ordinary real dilation
of a real supercurrent.  Equivalently, each coefficient
measure transforms as
\[
                    (\mu_{IJ})_\delta(A)
                                =\delta^{-2}\mu_{IJ}(\delta A).
\tag{MT10}
\]
The factor in MT9 accounts for both columns of a
\((2,2)\) test; it is not a change of the original
non-Archimedean absolute value.

\begin{corollary}[Critical tangents are positive closed cones]
\label{cor:r13-critical-tangent-current-compactness}
For every sequence \(\delta_j\downarrow0\), a subsequence
of \(T_{\delta_j}\) converges on all compact smooth
real tests to a global middle-positive separately
closed supercurrent \(T_0\) of bidimension two.
Every such limit satisfies
\[
       \mu_{T_0}(B_R(0))=\nu(T,0)R^2\quad(R>0),
       \qquad \lambda^2(a_\lambda)_*T_0=T_0
                                      \quad(\lambda>0).
\tag{MT11}
\]
When the original complete moment-image germ is contained
in a closed cone \(C\), each limit is supported in \(C\).
The tangent limit need not be unique or polyhedral.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For any fixed \(R>0\), MT6 gives
\[
 \mu_{T_\delta}(B_R)
       =\delta^{-2}M_T(\delta R)
       \le R^2 M_T(r_0)/r_0^2
\tag{MT12}
\]
for small \(\delta\).  MT4 bounds every coefficient
measure on each compact ball.  Weak compactness of
Radon measures and a diagonal selection on increasing
balls give a subsequential current limit.  Positivity,
symmetry and both closedness equations pass to smooth
tests.  Cone support is preserved under dilation and
under this limit.

The left side of MT12 converges numerically to
\(\nu(T,0)R^2\).  The open- and closed-ball
inequalities for weak measure convergence, followed
by \(R-\epsilon\uparrow R\) and
\(R+\epsilon\downarrow R\), show that the limit
measure has exactly that ball mass.  In particular
it charges no sphere and no atom at the origin.

Apply the annular identity MT8 to \(T_0\), by the
same local regularization argument.  Its constant
normalized ball mass gives
\[
                T_0\wedge(D|x|)^2=0
                                 \quad\text{on }\mathbf R^N\setminus\{0\}.
\tag{MT13}
\]
In an orthonormal frame whose first vector is radial,
\(D|x|\) is \(|x|^{-1}\) times the identity on the
orthogonal hyperplane and is zero on the radial vector.
The middle-positive cocoefficient matrix of \(T_0\)
is positive semidefinite on two-vectors.  MT13 makes
its whole tangential two-vector block zero; positivity
then makes every row and column meeting that block
zero.  Only two-vectors containing the radial direction
remain.  In current-form notation this is
\[
                    \iota'_E T_0=\iota''_E T_0=0,
                      \qquad E=\sum_i x_i\partial_{x_i}.
\tag{MT14}
\]
The origin has zero coefficient mass, so these identities
hold globally.  The one-column Cartan identity and
\(d'T_0=0\) now imply, for every distributional
coefficient \(\mu_{IJ}\) of bidegree \((N-2,N-2)\),
\[
             E\cdot\partial\mu_{IJ}+(N-2)\mu_{IJ}=0.
\tag{MT15}
\]
Equivalently
\(\int(E\varphi+2\varphi)\,d\mu_{IJ}=0\)
for every compact smooth scalar \(\varphi\).
Differentiating
\(\lambda^{-2}\int\varphi(x/\lambda)\,d\mu_{IJ}(x)\)
therefore gives zero.  This is exactly the dilation
identity in MT11, by MT10.
\end{proof}

The conicity conclusion constrains the possible critical
backgrounds, but it does not put them in the retained
analytic weak delta-background class \(\mathcal W_{\rm loc}\).
It also does not prove that their full paired action on
the leading finite-PS tensor vanishes.  Such a density
or annihilation assertion is a further theorem.

\paragraph{Primary sources and original inputs.}
The real trace and monotonicity formulas were checked
directly in A.~Lagerberg, \emph{Super currents and tropical
geometry}, arXiv:1008.2856v1, Definition 3.1,
Propositions 3.2 and 3.4, and Remark 3.3, pp.~19--20,
\url{https://arxiv.org/pdf/1008.2856}.  The closed-current
scope and exponent are also explicit in F.~Elkhadhra
and K.~Zahmoul, \emph{Lelong--Jensen formula,
Demailly--Lelong numbers and weighted degree of positive
supercurrents}, arXiv:1809.00992v2, Theorem 1 and
Corollary 2, p.~11,
\url{https://arxiv.org/pdf/1809.00992}.  MT2--MT4 use
the retained original GP compactness and middle-positive
coefficient-Radon interface.  The critical scaling and
conicity deduction are recorded above with their full
normalizations.
