title: Leading-energy reduction of the central quadratic residue
text:
cap13_leading_energy_and_paired_residual.tex \section{Leading-energy reduction of the central quadratic residue}
\label{sec:r13-leading-energy-residual}

This section follows PA and the protected background trace theorem
MT.  The space is the supplied original-field normal-three model,
the scalar presentation is the fixed finite continuous closed-cell
PL/PS class, and $P$ is the actual quadratic zero of PA1.  For an
arbitrary allowed degree-one background $S$, PA has proved
\[
                     \mathcal A_S(P)=c_S(P)\delta_y.
 \tag{LE1}
\]
The purpose here is to remove all higher coefficient jets from
this scalar remainder and to state its exact paired finite-
dimensional obstruction.  No trace of $S$ on a curve, no tangent
current of $S$, and no weak approximation of $S$ by classical
potential backgrounds will be assumed.

\subsection{Protected scalar first jets and all-face control}

Choose once the scalar ambient extensions supplied by SE, after
a common finite coefficient refinement.  Translate their central
logarithmic argument to zero.  Every cell whose closure does not
contain zero can be omitted after one shrinking.  The resulting
finite star consists of rational polyhedral cones.  If $h$ is
one of the continuous scalar extensions and $h_C$ is its smooth
extension on a closed cell $C$, define
\[
                 h^{[1]}(v)=d h_C(0)(v),\qquad v\in C.
 \tag{LE2}
\]
The constant $h(0)$ is omitted.  Differentiating the equality of
two scalar restrictions on a common face shows that LE2 agrees
there.  Thus $h^{[1]}$ is an actual continuous homogeneous PL
scalar in the old original moments.  Real coefficient slopes
are allowed, as in the original signed scalar class.  Its
piecewise differential has the prescribed tangential restriction
on every face.  The same construction applies to every $k_\nu$.

Set
\[
 Z_0=\tfrac12\sum_\nu c_\nu
   \left(d'_P h_\nu^{[1]}\wedge d''_P k_\nu^{[1]}
       +d'_P k_\nu^{[1]}\wedge d''_P h_\nu^{[1]}\right).
 \tag{LE3}
\]
This is a genuine regular finite-PS $(1,1)$ form in the
degree-one module, with constant coefficient tensors on the
cones and their consistent tangential face pullbacks.  It is
not a collection of independent coefficients on selected source
cells.  Choosing scalar extensions fixes the construction; only
their restrictions on realized directions enter LE3.  In
particular any two such extensions agreeing on the complete
ordinary image have the same directional tangent restrictions
on its finite central star.

Apply GP on a prescribed ordinary neighborhood where these
scalar identities hold, retaining the complete scalar tuple.
Write $F$ for the protected tuple, $b=t_F(y)$, and
$z=t_F-b$.  For a sufficiently small target ball, its entire
closed inverse image is compact in the original analytic
interior.  The whole central fiber, including points other
than $y$ and all lower moment ranks, is retained.  Put
\[
              \beta=\sum_{j=1}^{N}d'z_j\wedge d''z_j.
 \tag{LE4}
\]
Here and below a displayed target form denotes its original
moment pullback when used on the analytic space.

\begin{lemma}[Leading-energy error in the full regular order module]
\label{lem:r13-leading-energy-full-order}
There are constants $C$ and $r_0>0$, depending only on the
fixed finite scalar presentation and the protection, such that
on the complete inverse image of $|z|\le r<r_0$,
\[
                  -Cr\,\beta\ \le Z_P-Z_0\le Cr\,\beta.
 \tag{LE5}
\]
These are regular coefficient inequalities in the original
middle positive cone.  They pull back through every actual
refinement, including rank loss, and give the corresponding
original order inequalities after multiplication by every
allowed background.  No source point or charged coefficient
face has been removed.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For every fixed closed cell, Taylor's formula and its bounded
second derivatives give
\[
   |d h_C(v)-d h_C(0)|\le C_h|v|,
              \qquad |d h_C(v)|+|d h_C(0)|\le C_h.
 \tag{LE6}
\]
The finite maximum of the constants works for the whole star.
The old scalar coordinate vector is a fixed linear projection
of $z$, so its norm is at most a fixed multiple of $|z|$.
Subtracting the two products in the energy therefore gives
an operator norm bound $C|z|$ for the symmetric tensor on
each closed cell.  All tangential face restrictions are the
same restrictions of the scalar first jets used in LE2.
Thus the bound also holds on every lower face, even where
normal derivatives from different cells do not agree.

An operator norm bound relative to the Euclidean form in LE4
is precisely LE5.  Pullback by a linear tangent map preserves
both semipositive inequalities; it does not require an inverse
or a nonzero rank.  The original all-background regular-PS
order theorem therefore gives the asserted module inequalities
on all original tests.  The estimate is evaluated at every
ordinary point of the complete protected inverse image.  In
particular, the other points of its central fiber are not
discarded by using the distinguished point $y$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Only the leading tensor contributes at the critical scale}

Let $\rho\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R^N)$ be one fixed function
equal to one on a neighborhood of the closed unit ball and
supported in the ball of radius two.  For sufficiently small
$\delta>0$ put
\[
                  \chi_\delta=\rho(z/\delta).
 \tag{LE7}
\]
Protection makes this a compact original smooth scalar test,
without multiplying it by an additional source cutoff.  It is
one near the entire central fiber, in particular near $y$.

MT defines the positive Radon trace measure on the real target
by compact original pullback tests.  Denote it here by
$\mu_{S,F}$, with the harmless fixed normalization
$\mu_{S,F}(B)=\langle S,1_{z^{-1}(B)}\beta^2/2\rangle$.
MT proves that
\[
       \frac{\mu_{S,F}(B_r)}{r^2}\quad\hbox{is nondecreasing
       in }r,
       \qquad
       \nu_{S,F}:=\lim_{r\downarrow0}
                       \frac{\mu_{S,F}(B_r)}{r^2}<\infty.
 \tag{LE8}
\]
The convention for the factor $1/2$ only rescales this trace
and its density together.  MT uses the full compact protected
fiber, so separate closedness is not lost to a source cutoff.
The density in LE8 need not be zero.

\begin{theorem}[First-jet determination of the central action]
\label{thm:r13-leading-energy-residual}
For every allowed degree-one $S$ in the unchanged original
scope,
\[
 c_S(P)=-\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}
           \left\langle M_S(Z_0),D\chi_\delta\right\rangle.
 \tag{LE9}
\]
More precisely, for some fixed $C_P$ and every sufficiently
small $\delta$,
\[
 \left|c_S(P)+\langle M_S(Z_0),D\chi_\delta\rangle\right|
       \le C_P\delta^{-1}\mu_{S,F}(B_{2\delta})=O_S(\delta).
 \tag{LE10}
\]
The tensor $Z_0$ in this formula is the full paired energy
tensor in LE3.  Its two marginal families cannot be tested
or saturated separately.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The quadratic transgression gives
$\mathcal A_S(P)=-D M_S(Z_P)$: the other term
$\tfrac12D_\delta\sum c_\nu h_\nu k_\nu$ is already full
first-order exact and is killed after applying $D M_S$.
Pairing LE1 with LE7 therefore yields
\[
                    c_S(P)=-\langle M_S(Z_P),D\chi_\delta\rangle.
 \tag{LE11}
\]
This equality uses the current derivative sign of the retained
QA convention.  It holds for every sufficiently small $\delta$,
not just a subsequence.

The target Hessian of $\rho(z/\delta)$ has coefficient norm
at most $C_\rho\delta^{-2}$ and is supported in $B_{2\delta}$.
By LE5 the coefficients of $Z_P-Z_0$ are at most $C_P\delta$
there.  The matrix of their wedge product on
$\bigwedge^2\mathbf R^N$ is consequently bounded in norm by
$C\delta^{-1}$.  The form $\beta^2$ is strictly middle
positive on this exterior square.  It follows that
\[
 \pm\bigl((Z_P-Z_0)\wedge D\chi_\delta\bigr)
       \le C\delta^{-1}1_{B_{2\delta}}\beta^2.
 \tag{LE12}
\]
The bound is meant coefficientwise with the actual finite-PS
face values; it can equally be paired as a Borel Radon bound.
Every later tangent pullback preserves the inequality.
Multiplication by the original middle-positive $S$ and the
canonical regular-PS module action prove LE10.  This uses no
identification of middle, weak and strong positivity.
Finally LE8 implies $\mu_{S,F}(B_{2\delta})=O_S(\delta^2)$,
so the right side tends to zero.  All wall and central-fiber
contributions have been retained in this estimate.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Two precise sufficient central cancellations]
\label{cor:r13-leading-energy-cancellations}
Each of the following hypotheses implies $c_S(P)=0$ and
hence the full action identity on $U$ in PA:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the protected moment density $\nu_{S,F}$ is zero;
\item the leading energy $Z_0$ has an actual full-exact
degree-one identity on an ordinary neighborhood containing
the protected central fiber,
\[
                         Z_0=d'\beta_0+d''\zeta_0.
 \tag{LE13}
\]
\end{enumerate}
The second is a condition only on the finite homogeneous
leading tensor.  It does not require a full-exact identity
or a single controlled approximating sequence for the original
variable tensor $Z_P$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The same matrix bound without the $O(\delta)$ error gives
$|\langle M_S(Z_0),D\chi_\delta\rangle|
\le C\delta^{-2}\mu_{S,F}(B_{2\delta})$.
In the first case its limit is zero.  In the second case QA's
first-derivative commutation and nilpotence give
$D M_S(Z_0)=0$, so its pairing is zero for every small
$\delta$.  Apply LE9.  PA already gives the punctured
vanishing required to conclude on the whole domain.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[A concrete all-background first-jet range]
\label{cor:r13-linear-first-jet-quadratic-action}
Suppose every $h_\nu^{[1]}$ and $k_\nu^{[1]}$ is the
restriction of a single ambient linear form.  This holds, in
particular, when the closed-cell first derivatives of each
fixed scalar extension agree at the centre.  Then
\[
                         \mathcal A_S(P)=0
 \tag{LE13a}
\]
on the supplied ordinary model germ for every allowed original
background and every legal degree, on all original compact
smooth tests and actual refinements.  Higher scalar jets may
remain only finite PS, and no primitive for the full variable
energy $Z_P$ is required.  The first derivatives need agree
only at the centre: on punctured coefficient walls their
jumps may be nonzero, with size $O(|z|)$.  No $C^1$
regularity on a whole neighborhood is imposed.  The globally
smooth or globally $C^1$ subclass is not claimed as new;
the deduction here is from this pointwise central jet
condition and the PA--MT--LE composition.

More generally the same conclusion holds whenever the
\emph{combined} leading tensor $Z_0$, on every actual face,
is the restriction of one ambient constant symmetric tensor,
or differs from such a tensor by certified actual homogeneous
full-exact symbols.  The individual scalar first jets need
not be linear in this more general criterion.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Under the first hypothesis LE3 is a constant ambient symmetric
tensor $A$.  The ambient covector $b(z)=Az$ has
$e(b)=A$.  In the convention of QA this gives the concrete
full-exact identity
\[
 A=d'\!\left(\tfrac12\sum_j b_j(z)d''z_j\right)
        +d''\!\left(-\tfrac12\sum_j b_j(z)d'z_j\right).
\]
It is an identity on the whole ordinary moment domain and
survives every rank-losing tangent pullback.  Apply the second
case of the preceding corollary for degree-one backgrounds.
The lower-degree conclusion is already PA.  The proof is
unchanged when only the combined paired tensor is constant,
or when a finite sum of certified full-exact symbols is
subtracted from it first.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The finite paired residual functional}

Choose a finite-dimensional real vector space $\mathcal V$
of actual regular homogeneous degree-zero finite-PS $(1,1)$
forms in the protected coordinates, containing $Z_0$.  For
example take the span of the genuine paired product symbols
formed from the finite first-jet scalar list in LE2, together
with finitely many selected certified homogeneous exact symbols,
and then impose actual degree-one equality.  This construction
does not presume that an arbitrary face-compatible tensor
collection has an actual ambient presentation.  Fix a norm
on this finite coefficient space.  Let
$\mathcal E\subset\mathcal V$ be any linear subspace whose
members have certified actual identities of the form LE13 on
the complete protected neighborhood.  Ambient constant tensors
are examples.  A finite continuous piecewise-linear ambient
covector with its full all-face strain identity supplies another
certified member.  A collection of independent branch covectors
without joint compatibility does not.  The exact identities may
be given on an ordinary neighborhood of the entire compact
central fiber: properness then puts the support of every
sufficiently small LE7 cutoff in that neighborhood.  Indeed,
otherwise a sequence in its compact complement with target
values tending to zero would have a central-fiber limit in
that complement.

Define
\[
 \lambda_{\delta,S}(E)
       =-\langle M_S(E),D\chi_\delta\rangle,
                        \qquad E\in\mathcal V.
 \tag{LE14}
\]

\begin{proposition}[A full paired finite residual criterion]
\label{prop:r13-paired-finite-residual}
The family LE14 is bounded in $\mathcal V^*$ and vanishes
on $\mathcal E$.  Every cluster functional $\lambda_S$ satisfies
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 \lambda_S\in(\mathcal V/\mathcal E)^*,\qquad
                  \lambda_S([Z_0])=c_S(P),\\
 |\lambda_S([E])|\le C\nu_{S,F}\,
                 \operatorname{dist}(E,\mathcal E).
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{LE15}
\]
Consequently all cluster functionals have the same value on
the particular paired class $[Z_0]$, even if their values on
other classes differ.  Central cancellation is exactly their
annihilation of this class.  No limit current of $S$ is needed
to state or prove this criterion.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On the finite-dimensional space $\mathcal V$, the maximum
coefficient norm on the finite cone list is bounded by a
constant times the chosen norm.  The matrix estimate used
above gives
\[
        |\lambda_{\delta,S}(E)|
          \le C\|E\|\delta^{-2}\mu_{S,F}(B_{2\delta}).
 \tag{LE16}
\]
MT makes this family bounded, so finite-dimensional compactness
gives subsequential cluster functionals.  For $E\in\mathcal E$,
QA makes $D M_S(E)=0$ on the ordinary domain containing
the support of every sufficiently small cutoff, so LE14 is
zero.  It follows that all these functionals, and their limits,
factor through the quotient.  Apply LE16 to $E-E_0$ for
$E_0\in\mathcal E$, pass to the limit using LE8, and take
the infimum.  The fixed factor from $2\delta$ is absorbed
in $C$.  LE9 proves their common value on $Z_0$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Exact remaining gate and protected scope.}
The new conclusion is the unconditional $O(\delta)$ removal
of the higher scalar jets, after PA and MT.  It does not
show that the leading formal quadratic presentation is itself
an actual analytic zero; that stronger linearization assertion
is not used.  It does not identify the realized residual
functionals in LE15 with the full dual of a fixed old Killing
obstruction space.  The retained PR/QS examples already warn
against that identification: legal zero-preserving action data
do not read every nonzero fixed-old stress.  Nor do the available
curve caps prove that their realized paired rows span the
required class in every later actual refinement.

The all-background remaining statement is that the realized
functionals LE15 annihilate $[Z_0]$ for every actual zero in
PA1.  Positivity and separate closedness supply the critical
finite bound LE8, and actual full-exact symbols supply its
known annihilator.  They do not supply that final paired
annihilation.  In particular $O(\delta^2)$ is not replaced
by $o(\delta^2)$, and no restriction of the current order to
a selected curve or to a radial source family is performed.

\paragraph{Dependencies.}
The new analytic input beyond PA is

title: Compatible piecewise-smooth tests and critical tangent pairings
text:
cap13_compatible_ps_tangent_pairing.tex \section{Compatible piecewise-smooth tests and critical tangent pairings}
\label{sec:r13-compatible-ps-tangent-pairing}

The currents in the first part of this section are real
supercurrents on an open subset $\Omega\subset\mathbf R^N$,
with $N\ge2$.  They are symmetric, middle-positive,
separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed, and have bidimension
$(2,2)$.  Write
\[
             \beta=\sum_i d'x_i\wedge d''x_i,
                      \mu_T=\tfrac12T\wedge\beta^2.
 \tag{PT1}
\]
All coefficient measures are controlled by this trace, as in
MT4.  No weak/strong positivity identification is made.

\paragraph{Nonduplication status.}
The uniform $O(\sqrt\epsilon)$ piecewise-test approximation
mechanism is retained: R6,
\texttt{lem:r6-weighted-pws-error}, records it as a direct
corollary of R4 Lemmas 71.1--71.2 and Theorem 71.4, even
with bounded Borel multipliers.  Its real bidimension-two
proof is written below to verify precisely the tangent-limit
interface used here.  The nodal construction likewise makes
the retained Courant scalar generation explicit in the
homogeneous constant-tensor case.  These mechanisms are not
counted as new principal theorems.  The new composition is
their use with MT and LE to give the complete realized
critical-tangent pairing in PT11.

A \emph{compatible finite-PS test} is a compactly supported
ambient $(2,2)$ form on a finite polyhedral complex covering
a neighborhood of its support, with smooth extensions near
the closed cells, whose tangential pullbacks agree on every
common face.  This is a supplied genuine ambient presentation,
not independent coefficient data attached to different source
labels.  Bounded first derivatives on a slightly larger
compact neighborhood follow from the finite closed-cell data.

\subsection{Uniform control of normal factors near a wall}

Let $H=\{\ell=0\}$ be an affine hyperplane, with
$|d\ell|=1$, and put
$n'=d'\ell$, $n''=d''\ell$.  A $(2,2)$ coefficient
tensor belongs to its \emph{normal-factor subspace} if it
lies in
\[
 I_H=n'\wedge\Lambda^{1,2}
                     +n''\wedge\Lambda^{2,1}.
 \tag{PT2}
\]
This is exactly the kernel of tangential restriction to $H$.

\begin{lemma}[Normal strip bounds]
\label{lem:r13-normal-strip-bounds}
Fix compact sets $K\subset\operatorname{int}K'\Subset\Omega$.
For every such $T$ and every sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 (T\wedge n'\wedge n''\wedge\beta)
       (K\cap\{ |\ell|\le\epsilon\})
             &\le C\epsilon\,\mu_T(K'),\\
 |\langle T,\psi\rangle|
             &\le C\|\psi\|_\infty\sqrt\epsilon\,
                              \mu_T(K')
 \end{split}
 \tag{PT3}
\]
whenever the bounded Borel test $\psi$ is supported in that
strip and takes values in $I_H$.  The constants depend on
the fixed geometry and cutoff, not on $T$.  The coefficient
measures involving at least one normal two-vector index have
zero restriction to $H$ itself.  The trace $\mu_T$ may
nevertheless charge $H$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Choose $0\le\chi\in C_c^\infty(\operatorname{int}K')$
equal to one near $K$.  Choose smooth convex functions
$u_\epsilon$ on the real line such that
\[
 u_\epsilon''(s)\ge\epsilon^{-1}
          \quad (|s|\le\epsilon),\qquad
 |u_\epsilon(s)|\le C(1+|s|)
 \tag{PT4}
\]
on the fixed relevant range, with $C$ independent of
$\epsilon$.  For instance rescale one convex smoothing
of $|s|$ whose second derivative has compact support and
is bounded below on the unit interval.  Then
$D(u_\epsilon\circ\ell)=u_\epsilon''(\ell)n'\wedge n''$.
Positivity and closedness give
\[
 \begin{split}
 \epsilon^{-1}
   (T\wedge n'\wedge n''\wedge\beta)
          (K\cap\{|\ell|\le\epsilon\})
 &\le\langle T,\chi D(u_\epsilon\circ\ell)\wedge\beta\rangle\\
 &=\langle T,(u_\epsilon\circ\ell)D\chi\wedge\beta\rangle\\
 &\le C\mu_T(K').
 \end{split}
 \tag{PT5}
\]
The last inequality follows from the bounded scalar function
in PT4 and the fixed middle-order bound for $D\chi\wedge\beta$.
This is a distributional Stokes identity with smooth functions;
no current is restricted to the wall in deriving it.

Use an orthonormal frame with first covector $d\ell$.
The cocoefficient matrix of $T$ is positive semidefinite on
two-vectors.  Its diagonal entries whose index contains this
first covector are bounded by the normal trace in PT5; its
other diagonal entries are bounded by the total trace.
For a Borel set $B$, positivity and Radon polarization give
\[
           |\mu_{IJ}|(B)
                   \le\sqrt{\mu_{II}(B)\mu_{JJ}(B)}.
 \tag{PT6}
\]
Each coefficient of an $I_H$-valued tensor has such a normal
index in at least one column.  Apply PT5 to that diagonal
entry and the trace bound to the other.  The finite sum of
coefficient estimates proves the second inequality of PT3.
Letting $\epsilon\downarrow0$ proves the assertion on $H$.
It only removes normal-factor coefficient measures there,
not the tangential trace mass.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A finite-wall approximation with all lower faces retained}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform smooth approximation of compatible tests]
\label{lem:r13-uniform-compatible-ps-approximation}
Let $\theta$ be a compatible finite-PS compact test.  There
are compactly supported smooth coefficient convolutions
$\theta_\epsilon$ in one fixed compact neighborhood and a
constant $C_\theta$ such that
\[
       |\langle T,\theta-\theta_\epsilon\rangle|
                 \le C_\theta\sqrt\epsilon\,\mu_T(K')
 \tag{PT7}
\]
for every current in the stated class.  The pairing with
$\theta$ is independent of ambient representatives of its
lower-face values.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Take the finite list of affine hyperplanes containing the
coefficient facets, and refine by their arrangement.  Fix
one smooth closed-cell extension for each resulting full
cell.  At a point of a lower face, choose an incident full
cell to give a bounded Borel representative.  Any two such
choices differ by a sum of tensors in $I_H$ for hyperplanes
containing that face: adjacent incident cells have this
property by tangential compatibility, and the local full
cell adjacency through facets is connected.  Alternatively
the kernel of restriction to the face is the sum of the
ideals generated by its conormals.  PT3 makes all these
differences pair to zero on the face.  The chosen Borel
representative therefore gives the canonical pairing.

Extend by zero outside a fixed compact neighborhood of the
support, where the original test already vanishes.  Let
$\theta_\epsilon$ be its coefficient convolution with a
smooth kernel supported in $|a|\le\epsilon$.
For a generic translation vector $a$, traverse the segment
from $x$ to $x-a$.  Within cells, its total smooth variation
is at most $C|a|$.  At a crossed facet $H$ the jump is in
$I_H$, because its tangential restriction is zero.  All
these jump coefficients are uniformly bounded by the finite
closed-cell bounds.  The hyperplane crossed by the segment
has distance at most $|a|$ from $x$.  A generic segment
crosses at most one facet of each of the finitely many
hyperplanes; crossings at lower faces can be omitted from
the translation integral, since they form a Lebesgue-null
set of translations.  If $x$ itself lies on lower faces,
the initial choice of incident cell is handled by the same
finite incident-cell chain just used above.

In a fixed coordinate basis this proves the decomposition
\[
       \theta_\epsilon-\theta
             =R_\epsilon+\sum_H J_{H,\epsilon},
 \tag{PT8}
\]
where $\|R_\epsilon\|_\infty\le C\epsilon$, each
$J_{H,\epsilon}$ is a bounded Borel $I_H$-valued tensor
with norm at most $C$, and its support lies in a fixed
multiple of the $\epsilon$-strip around $H$.  Indeed the
conormal of an affine hyperplane is constant, so transporting
a jump from its crossing point to $x$ preserves membership
in $I_H$.  A fixed linear splitting of this finite-dimensional
subspace gives bounded coefficient representatives before
integrating over the translations.  There are finitely many
walls and no accumulating crossing sequence.

The ordinary coefficient trace bound controls the first term
in PT8 by $C\epsilon\mu_T(K')$.  PT3 controls each remaining
term by $C\sqrt\epsilon\mu_T(K')$.  Their finite sum proves
PT7, including the strata where several coefficient walls
meet.  No simultaneous covector primitive is used or needed.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Weak continuity on compatible finite-PS tests]
\label{thm:r13-compatible-ps-weak-continuity}
Suppose $T_j\to T_0$ on all compact smooth real tests and
the currents satisfy the stated middle positivity and both
closedness equations, with uniformly bounded trace on each
compact subset.  Then for every fixed compatible finite-PS
compact test,
\[
                     \langle T_j,\theta\rangle
                              \longrightarrow
                     \langle T_0,\theta\rangle.
 \tag{PT9}
\]
The limit may charge coefficient walls.  No zero-wall-mass
hypothesis is required.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The limit has the same middle positivity and closedness and
the same local trace bounds.  For fixed $\epsilon$ the
convoluted test is smooth, so its pairings converge.  PT7
bounds the two approximation errors uniformly in $j$.
First pass to the limit in $j$, then let $\epsilon$ tend
to zero.  This proves PT9.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A constructive ambient extension for homogeneous tensors}

\begin{lemma}[Nodal extension from a geometric subfan]
\label{lem:r13-nodal-homogeneous-form-extension}
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite rational fan in $\mathbf R^N$.
Suppose a constant $(p,q)$ tensor is given on the span of
each cone, with identical tangential restrictions on common
faces.  Then it has a genuine ambient homogeneous
coefficient-degree-zero finite-PS extension.  If the data
are column-symmetric, the extension may be chosen symmetric.
This lemma extends regular forms, not their primitives.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Refine a complete rational hyperplane fan containing all
equations for the spans of the supplied cones, extensions
of their relative facet equations, and the coordinate
hyperplanes, and make a
common simplicial refinement.  This gives a complete
simplicial fan $\Delta$ such that the supplied support is
a subfan after subdivision.  The coordinate hyperplanes
remove lineality before triangulation.  Choose a vector
$v_r$ on every ray and its continuous homogeneous PL
nodal function $\varphi_r$: on a cone containing that ray
it is the corresponding coordinate, and on other cones
it is zero.  These formulas agree on shared faces.

Fix a global order of the rays.  For strictly increasing
ray multi-indices $I,J$ of lengths $p,q$ in that order,
consider their union.  If its rays span a face $\tau$
of $\Delta$ lying in the supplied subfan, let $a_{IJ}$
be the value of the supplied tensor on the corresponding
ordered ray vectors in its two columns.  The value is
independent of a containing supplied cone by compatibility.
If their union is not contained in any cone, or its smallest
face is not supplied, set $a_{IJ}=0$.  The finite sum
\[
     \widehat E=\sum_{I,J}a_{IJ}
                  d'_P\varphi_I\wedge d''_P\varphi_J
 \tag{PT10}
\]
with the standard column sign convention defines an actual
ambient finite-PS form.  On any full simplicial cone the
nonzero nodal differentials are its dual ray basis.  PT10
therefore has exactly the assigned tensor coefficients.
On a supplied cone every relevant smaller ray face is
supplied, so its restriction is the original tensor.
The same argument proves all shared-face compatibilities.
Column symmetry is preserved by making the symmetric
coefficient assignments.  This explicit scalar construction
does not presume an extension of independently chosen
source primitives or identify coincident source labels.
\end{proof}

Only geometric single-valued face data are covered by this
extension lemma.  Different actual source labels with
incompatible values on the same geometric image do not
define its input.  LE's leading energy already has a
supplied ambient presentation by the scalar first jets;
PT10 is an additional constructive extension option.

\subsection{The central scalar as a tangent-current pairing}

Return to the protected original setting of MT and LE.
Let $T$ be the full-fiber real background transpose, and
let $T_{\delta_j}=\delta_j^2(a_{\delta_j})_*T$ converge
to any critical tangent $T_0$, where
$a_\delta(x)=x/\delta$.  Let $E$ be a homogeneous
coefficient-degree-zero $(1,1)$ symbol with a supplied
compatible ambient finite-PS presentation.  This applies
in particular to LE's actual leading energy $Z_0$.

The smooth test transpose MT2 also agrees on this regular
PS pairing.  Indeed its cocoefficient Radon measures are
the proper transposes of the corresponding original
coefficient measures, by polarization of MT2.  Finite
Borel multiplication by the PS coefficients, with their
actual face values, is precisely the retained regular-PS
module action.  The normal-wall zero-coefficient conclusion
of PT3 removes any ambient representative ambiguity.  Thus
no higher-degree delta action is being inferred from the
smooth transpose alone.

\begin{theorem}[Every critical tangent has the same relevant paired value]
\label{thm:r13-leading-tangent-pairing}
For the cutoff $\rho$ of LE7,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \lim_j\lambda_{\delta_j,S}(E)
       &=-\langle T_0,E\wedge D\rho\rangle,\\
 c_S(P)&=-\langle T_0,Z_0\wedge D\rho\rangle.
 \end{split}
 \tag{PT11}
\]
The second equality holds for every critical tangent of
the protected background.  It is a full tensor pairing,
with all mixed entries and wall traces retained.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Homogeneity of the coefficient functions of $E$ gives the
exact scaling identity
\[
 \langle T_\delta,E\wedge D\rho\rangle
       =\langle T,E\wedge D[\rho(x/\delta)]\rangle.
 \tag{PT12}
\]
Both $(1,1)$ factors together contribute $\delta^{-4}$
under real pullback, and MT's prefactor $\delta^2$
leaves precisely the $\delta^{-2}$ of the displayed
Hessian.  The original Borel module identification just
explained makes the right side equal to
$\langle M_S(E),D\chi_\delta\rangle$.

MT supplies the uniform trace bounds of PT9 on each
compact real set.  The fixed test $E\wedge D\rho$ is
compatible finite PS.  PT9 therefore applies to the left
side of PT12, even if the tangent current charges walls.
This proves the first equality in PT11.  Taking $E=Z_0$
and using the unconditional leading reduction LE9 proves
the second.  Tangent uniqueness is not asserted or needed.
\end{proof}

If two supplied ambient extensions represent the same actual
symbol, the original Borel module pairings coincide at every
$\delta$.  PT9 consequently gives the same tangent pairing
for both extensions.  This is the precise independence needed
here; support containment alone would not justify multiplying
an arbitrary discontinuous extension by a tangent current.

\paragraph{Remaining analytic realization gate.}
PT11 does not put a critical tangent into the retained analytic
weak-background class, does not construct an original analytic
background from an arbitrary real cone current, and does not
prove its pairing is zero for an actual-zero leading energy.
The realized tangent family is constrained by all original
refinements.  It is not identified with every positive closed
real current on a selected fan or with the full old Killing
dual.  The remaining cancellation is exactly the vanishing
of the paired value in PT11 for those realized backgrounds.

\paragraph{Inputs.}
The real coefficient inequalities and critical compactness are
MT2--MT15, with the middle-positive normalization of PT1.
The original-to-real identification uses the retained R6
regular-PS Borel module, GP's complete proper fibers, and
LE's actual scalar first-jet construction.  The finite-wall
proof and nodal extension are supplied above.  No general
current restriction, arbitrary analytic pushforward, or GK
test extension is used.

title: A spherical formula for the realized critical residual
text:
geom13_spherical_tangent_reformulation.tex \section{A spherical formula for the realized critical residual}
\label{sec:r13-spherical-critical-residual}

Let $T_0$ be a critical tangent supplied by MT on
$\mathbf R^N$, $N\ge2$.  Thus it is a symmetric,
middle-positive, separately closed real supercurrent of
bidimension $(2,2)$.  Put
\[
 \beta=\sum_i d'x_i\wedge d''x_i,\qquad
 \mu=\tfrac12T_0\wedge\beta^2,\qquad
 \mu(B_R)=\nu R^2.
 \tag{SR1}
\]
MT gives zero coefficient mass at the origin, conicity,
and radial two-vector support.  All norms and spheres in
this section are those of these fixed protected real
coordinates.  The conclusions are a polar reformulation
and corollaries of MT--LE--PT; they do not constitute a
new general relation-annihilation theorem.

\subsection{The angular matrix measure and its normalization}

Use the standard column-positive convention to associate
to a symmetric $(2,2)$ test form $\eta$ its coefficient
operator $C_\eta$ on $\bigwedge^2\mathbf R^N$.  In
particular
\[
                    C_{\beta^2/2}=I.
 \tag{SR2}
\]
For symmetric $(1,1)$ coefficient matrices $E,H$, this
convention is characterized by
\[
\begin{split}
C_{E\wedge H}(u\wedge v,s\wedge t)
={}&E(u,s)H(v,t)+H(u,s)E(v,t)\\
 &-E(u,t)H(v,s)-H(u,t)E(v,s).
\end{split}
 \tag{SR3}
\]
Let $\mathsf Q$ be the positive semidefinite matrix-valued
Radon measure representing $T_0$ in this convention:
\[
 \langle T_0,\eta\rangle
       =\int\operatorname{tr}(C_\eta\,d\mathsf Q),
                 \qquad \operatorname{tr}\mathsf Q=\mu.
 \tag{SR4}
\]
The trace is the full matrix contraction, including off-diagonal
entries.

Write $r=|x|$, $\theta=x/r$, and let
\[
 A_\theta:\mathbf R^N\longrightarrow\bigwedge^2\mathbf R^N,
                     \qquad A_\theta v=\theta\wedge v.
 \tag{SR5}
\]
It restricts to an isometry on $\theta^\perp$.  The radial
support assertion of MT says that $\mathsf Q$ is supported
as a matrix on $A_\theta(\theta^\perp)$ at $\mu$-almost
every nonzero point.

\begin{proposition}[Polar coefficient measure]
\label{prop:r13-angular-critical-matrix}
There is a unique finite positive semidefinite matrix-valued
measure $\mathsf M$ on $\mathbb S^{N-1}$ such that
\[
 \mathsf M\theta=0,\qquad
 \sigma:=\operatorname{tr}\mathsf M,\qquad
                   \sigma(\mathbb S^{N-1})=2\nu,
 \tag{SR6}
\]
and, in polar coordinates,
\[
 A_\theta^*\,d\mathsf Q\,A_\theta
                         =r\,dr\,d\mathsf M(\theta).
 \tag{SR7}
\]
The notation $\mathsf M\theta=0$ means that the matrix
density with respect to $\sigma$ kills $\theta$ almost
everywhere.  Equation SR7 determines $\mathsf Q$ completely,
since its matrix support is radial.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Put $d\mathsf B=A_\theta^*d\mathsf Q A_\theta$ on
$\mathbf R^N\setminus\{0\}$.  It is positive semidefinite,
kills $\theta$, and has trace $\mu$, by the radial support
and the isometry in SR5.  The coefficient form of MT's
conicity is
\[
             \mathsf Q(\lambda E)=\lambda^2\mathsf Q(E)
                              \quad(\lambda>0).
 \tag{SR8}
\]
Since $A_\theta$ has degree zero under dilation, the same
equation holds for $\mathsf B$.

For a Borel set $G\subset\mathbb S^{N-1}$ define
\[
 \mathsf M(G)=2\mathsf B
       \bigl(\{0<r\le1,\ \theta\in G\}\bigr).
 \tag{SR9}
\]
For $0<a<b$, SR8 gives
\[
 \mathsf B\bigl(\{a<r\le b,\ \theta\in G\}\bigr)
              =\frac{b^2-a^2}{2}\mathsf M(G).
\]
These identities on Borel rectangles prove SR7 by the
uniqueness of finite measures on compact radial annuli.
Positivity, tangency and SR6 follow from the corresponding
properties of $\mathsf B$ and $\mu(B_1)=\nu$.
The same rectangle identity proves uniqueness.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Radial cutoffs read a full angular tensor}

Let $E$ be a symmetric $(1,1)$ symbol whose coefficients
are homogeneous of degree zero and have a supplied genuine
compatible finite-PS ambient presentation on a conical
subdivision.  It is locally bounded.  Its restriction to the
sphere is denoted by the same letter.  Put
\[
 E_{rr}(\theta)=E(\theta,\theta),\qquad
            E_{\rm tan}=E|_{\theta^\perp\times\theta^\perp}.
 \tag{SR10}
\]
All face values use the canonical tangential PS convention
of PT.  Since $\mathsf M$ is tangent, the contraction
$E_{\rm tan}:d\mathsf M$ equals $E:d\mathsf M$.

\begin{theorem}[Angular formula]
\label{thm:r13-angular-critical-pairing}
Let $\rho(x)=\psi(|x|)$ be any compact smooth radial
function equal to one near the origin.  Then
\[
 \boxed{
 \langle T_0,E\wedge D\rho\rangle
       =\int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}E_{\rm tan}:d\mathsf M
          -\int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}E_{rr}\,d\sigma.}
 \tag{SR11}
\]
In particular the pairing is independent of the choice of
such a radial cutoff.  The angular pairings retain all
coefficient walls and all mixed entries.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
On $r>0$ the matrix of $D\rho$ is
\[
       \psi''(r)\theta\theta^t
           +\frac{\psi'(r)}r(I-\theta\theta^t).
 \tag{SR12}
\]
For $u,v\perp\theta$, SR3 gives
\[
 C_{E\wedge D\rho}(\theta\wedge u,\theta\wedge v)
       =\psi''(r)E(u,v)
                +\frac{\psi'(r)}r E(\theta,\theta)(u,v).
 \tag{SR13}
\]
Here $(u,v)$ is the Euclidean inner product.  Radial
support removes all other coefficient blocks.  Combining
SR7 and SR13, and using the degree-zero homogeneity of
$E$, yields
\[
\begin{split}
\langle T_0,E\wedge D\rho\rangle
={}&\left(\int_0^\infty r\psi''(r)\,dr\right)
            \int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}E_{\rm tan}:d\mathsf M\\
 &+\left(\int_0^\infty\psi'(r)\,dr\right)
            \int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}E_{rr}\,d\sigma.
\end{split}
\]
All radial derivatives are supported in a compact annulus.
Their two integrals are $1$ and $-1$, respectively, because
$\psi=1$ near zero and vanishes near infinity.  This proves
SR11.

The use of finite-PS coefficients is legitimate by PT.
More explicitly, on a conical coefficient wall the normal
cocoefficients of $\mathsf Q$ vanish as measures.  Because
$\theta$ is tangent to that wall, SR5 transfers the same
annihilation to the corresponding normal entries of
$\mathsf M$.  Thus the displayed contractions do not depend
on ambient representatives of the face values.  Tangential
mass on the wall remains in both integrals.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Necessary angular constraints from closedness]
\label{cor:r13-angular-constant-tensor-balance}
For every smooth tangent vector field $v$ on the sphere,
\[
           \int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}e_{\mathbb S}(v):d\mathsf M=0,
           \qquad e_{\mathbb S}(v)=\operatorname{sym}\nabla_{\mathbb S}v.
 \tag{SR14a}
\]
Equivalently $\operatorname{div}_{\mathbb S}\mathsf M=0$
in the distributional tangent sense.  The matrix also satisfies
\[
       \int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}d\mathsf M
            =\int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}\theta\theta^t\,d\sigma.
 \tag{SR14}
\]
Equivalently, for every $a,b\in\mathbf R^N$,
\[
 \int (a^t d\mathsf M b)
                =\int(a\cdot\theta)(b\cdot\theta)\,d\sigma.
\]
The finite moment identity alone is not asserted sufficient.
The distributional condition is used in the real converse
below; original analytic realization is a separate question.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On the punctured real space put $b(r\theta)=r v(\theta)$,
using the Euclidean identification of vectors and covectors,
and let $E=e(b)$ be its symmetric derivative.  Since
$v\perp\theta$, direct differentiation gives
$E_{rr}=0$ and $E_{\rm tan}=e_{\mathbb S}(v)$.  The tensor
$E$ is full-exact: in the retained sign convention it is
\[
 E=d'\!\left(\tfrac12\sum_jb_jd''x_j\right)
           +d''\!\left(-\tfrac12\sum_jb_jd'x_j\right).
\]
Both closedness equations of $T_0$ therefore imply
$\langle T_0,E\wedge D\rho\rangle=0$.  To justify the
integration by parts, multiply the displayed primitive
forms by a smooth cutoff equal to one on a neighborhood
of the compact annular support of $D\rho$; the added
derivatives then have zero product with $D\rho$.
Apply SR11 to obtain SR14a.  This use of SR11 is legitimate
also for a smooth degree-zero homogeneous tensor on the
puncture: its proof needs only boundedness on the sphere
and the radial formula, and $D\rho$ is supported away
from zero.

Take $E$ to be any constant symmetric tensor.  It is smooth
and closed.  Separate closedness of $T_0$, tested against
the compact form $E\wedge d''\rho$, gives
$\langle T_0,E\wedge D\rho\rangle=0$.
Apply SR11 and vary the symmetric matrix $E$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The actual leading residual and arbitrary cutoffs}

Return to the PA--MT--LE--PT setting, with the same original
degree-one background $S$.  Let $Z_0$ be LE's full paired
leading tensor and $T_0$ any of its realized critical
background tangents.  Write
\[
 Z_0=\tfrac12\sum_\alpha c_\alpha
       \bigl(d'_P h_\alpha\wedge d''_P k_\alpha
                +d'_P k_\alpha\wedge d''_P h_\alpha\bigr),
 \tag{SR15}
\]
where $h_\alpha,k_\alpha$ are the actual ambient homogeneous
PL first jets.  Their spherical derivatives mean the
tangential derivatives of the restrictions to the sphere,
with all face restrictions retained.

\begin{theorem}[Spherical expression for the central coefficient]
\label{thm:r13-spherical-realized-residual}
With the normalization SR6,
\[
\boxed{
c_S(P)=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha
  \left(\int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}h_\alpha k_\alpha\,d\sigma
    -\int_{\mathbb S^{N-1}}
                  d_{\mathbb S}h_\alpha\otimes
                         d_{\mathbb S}k_\alpha:d\mathsf M\right).}
 \tag{SR16}
\]
Moreover, in the retained derivative convention,
\[
                     D(Z_0\wedge T_0)=-c_S(P)\delta_0
                                  \quad\hbox{on }\mathbf R^N.
 \tag{SR17}
\]
Consequently PT's formula for $c_S(P)$ is independent of
every compact smooth cutoff equal to one near zero, whether
or not it is radial.  The angular measure may depend on the
chosen critical tangent, but its value in SR16 does not.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Euler's identity for each homogeneous scalar gives
$d h_\alpha(\theta)=h_\alpha(\theta)$ in the radial
direction.  Thus the radial entry of SR15 is
$\sum c_\alpha h_\alpha k_\alpha$, and its tangential
entry is the corresponding symmetrized spherical gradient
product.  The symmetry of $\mathsf M$ makes its contraction
with that product equal to the unsymmetrized expression
in SR16.  Apply SR11 and PT11, which supplies the negative
of that pairing.

For the stronger distributional identity, let
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R^N)$ be arbitrary.  For
sufficiently small $\delta>0$, proper protection makes
$\eta_\delta=\eta(z/\delta)$ an original compact smooth
test on the whole inverse image.  The actual equality
$\mathcal A_S(P)=c_S(P)\delta_y=-D M_S(Z_P)$ gives
\[
       \langle T,Z_P\wedge D[\eta(z/\delta)]\rangle
                              =-c_S(P)\eta(0).
 \tag{SR18}
\]
Here $T$ is MT's unscaled full-fiber transpose.  If the
support of $\eta$ is contained in $B_R$, LE's complete-face
Taylor estimate and MT's mass bound imply
\[
 \left|\langle T,(Z_P-Z_0)\wedge D[\eta(z/\delta)]\rangle\right|
       \le C_\eta\delta^{-1}\mu_T(B_{R\delta})
                               =O_{S,\eta}(\delta).
 \tag{SR19}
\]
Indeed the coefficient error is $O(\delta)$ there and
the Hessian is $O(\delta^{-2})$.  This uses every point
of the protected inverse image, not only the distinguished
source point.

The exact scaling from PT12 identifies
$\langle T,Z_0\wedge D[\eta(z/\delta)]\rangle$ with
$\langle T_\delta,Z_0\wedge D\eta\rangle$.
Along the subsequence defining $T_0$, PT's compatible-PS
weak continuity passes this last pairing to
$\langle T_0,Z_0\wedge D\eta\rangle$.
Equations SR18--SR19 therefore give
\[
             \langle T_0,Z_0\wedge D\eta\rangle
                                     =-c_S(P)\eta(0).
\]
This is SR17.  Taking any cutoff with value one near zero
proves its asserted independence.  No claim that the formal
quadratic first-jet presentation is itself an actual zero
has been used.
\end{proof}

\subsection{An exact real classification, without analytic realization}

\begin{theorem}[Real conic currents and divergence-free angular matrices]
\label{thm:r13-real-angular-classification}
The polar construction SR7 is a bijection between the
following two classes:
\begin{enumerate}
\item finite symmetric positive semidefinite matrix-valued
measures $\mathsf M$ on $\mathbb S^{N-1}$ satisfying
$\mathsf M\theta=0$ and
$\operatorname{div}_{\mathbb S}\mathsf M=0$;
\item symmetric middle-positive separately $d'$- and
$d''$-closed real supercurrents $T$ of bidimension $(2,2)$
on $\mathbf R^N$ with
\[
                 \lambda^2(a_\lambda)_*T=T,
                 \qquad a_\lambda(x)=x/\lambda.
 \tag{SR20}
\]
\end{enumerate}
Their traces satisfy
$\mu_T(B_R)=\tfrac12\sigma(\mathbb S^{N-1})R^2$.
This classifies real currents only.  It does not characterize
which of them are critical tangents of original allowed
non-Archimedean backgrounds under all actual refinements.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Given $\mathsf M$ in the first class, define its radial
cocoefficient measure by
\[
           d\mathsf Q=r\,dr\,A_\theta d\mathsf M A_\theta^*.
 \tag{SR21}
\]
It has locally finite trace, is positive semidefinite,
and defines a middle-positive coefficient-Radon current
by SR4.  It is symmetric, satisfies SR20, and has the
displayed trace normalization.  It remains to prove both
closedness equations.

First suppose $d\mathsf M=B(\theta)\,d\omega(\theta)$,
where $B$ is a smooth symmetric tangent matrix and $d\omega$
is Euclidean spherical surface measure.  Relative to
Lebesgue measure, SR21 has cocoefficients
\[
 C_{ij,kl}(x)=r^{2-N}
  (\theta_i\theta_kB_{jl}-\theta_i\theta_lB_{jk}
          -\theta_j\theta_kB_{il}+\theta_j\theta_lB_{ik}).
 \tag{SR22}
\]
Extend the indices antisymmetrically from $i<j$ and $k<l$.
In these complementary cocoefficients, $d'T=0$ is exactly
$\sum_i\partial_i C_{ij,kl}=0$; the second closedness
equation is its column transpose.  If
$v=\operatorname{div}_{\mathbb S}B$, direct differentiation
using $B\theta=0$ and symmetry gives
\[
 \sum_i\partial_i C_{ij,kl}
       =r^{1-N}\theta_j(\theta_l v_k-\theta_k v_l).
 \tag{SR23}
\]
For completeness,
$\partial_i\theta_j=r^{-1}(\delta_{ij}-\theta_i\theta_j)$,
and
\[
 \sum_i\partial_i B_{il}
        =r^{-1}\bigl(v_l-\theta_l\operatorname{tr}B\bigr).
\]
In differentiating SR22, the first two terms contribute
$r^{1-N}(\theta_k B_{jl}-\theta_l B_{jk})$.
The derivatives of the last two terms cancel these,
the symmetric $B_{kl}$ terms, and the trace terms,
leaving precisely SR23.  Thus $v=0$ proves both
closedness equations on the punctured space.

For a finite matrix measure, average its tensorial rotation
translates against a smooth approximate identity of $SO(N)$.
This produces smooth tangent symmetric positive semidefinite
matrix densities, converging weakly to $\mathsf M$.
Distributional spherical divergence commutes with isometries,
so every average remains divergence-free.  The smoothing
assertion follows by differentiating the group convolution;
the rotation action is smooth and transitive on the sphere.
Their currents converge coefficientwise on every compact
annulus by SR21.  Distributional continuity of $d'$ and
$d''$ therefore proves closedness of the limiting current
on the punctured space.

To include the origin, use a smooth deletion cutoff which
changes from zero to one on $\epsilon<r<2\epsilon$ and
has first derivative bounded by $C/\epsilon$.  The error
in either closedness equation, against any fixed compact
test, is bounded by
\[
            C\epsilon^{-1}\mu_T(B_{2\epsilon})
                                     =O(\epsilon).
 \tag{SR24}
\]
It tends to zero.  Thus both equations hold globally.

Conversely, for any current in the second class, SR20 gives
$\mathsf Q(\lambda E)=\lambda^2\mathsf Q(E)$.
Its trace therefore has no atom at zero and has ball mass
$\nu R^2$ for a finite $\nu$.  Apply MT's annular
Stokes identity to this positive closed real current.
Its constant normalized ball mass forces the tangential
two-vector block to vanish, and positivity removes the
mixed blocks.  This is the radial support used in SR5.

crossed_box_full_tester_compact_gap.tex \section{A strict crossed Laurent box with a full-original-tester compact capacity gap}
\label{sec:r16-crossed-box-compact-gap}

\paragraph{Original category and the statement being tested.}
The construction uses the prescribed finite extension
$K/\mathbf Q_p$, its unchanged absolute value, and every original
classical normalized tester. It does not replace the tester class by
toric functions. A toric majorant will be used only to obtain an
\emph{upper bound at a specified Gauss atom}, by the frozen original
contact inequality. In particular no nonlinear pushforward formula
for arbitrary psh functions is assumed.

Fix a uniformizer $\pi$, and put
\[
       r=|\pi|,\qquad \lambda=-\log r>0,\qquad
       R=r^{-1},\qquad \kappa=(2\lambda)^{-q},
       \qquad q\ge2.
 \tag{CB1}
\]
Let
$X=(\mathbf A^{2q}_{K,X_1,\ldots,X_q,Y_1,\ldots,Y_q})^{\rm an}$.
Inside the compact radius-$R^3$ original affinoid polydisc, use
the strict Laurent box
\[
 \begin{split}
 V=\{\, &|X_i|<R,\ |Y_j|<R,\ |X_iY_j|<R
                         \quad(1\le i,j\le q)\,\},\\
 K_0=\{\, &|X_i|\le R,\ |Y_j|\le R,\ |X_iY_j|\le R
                         \quad(1\le i,j\le q)\,\}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{CB2}
\]
Thus $K_0\Subset\operatorname{Int}_X(B)$ for that affinoid $B$.
All the functions defining the upper inequalities are original
analytic functions and all thresholds are in $|K^\times|$. No
lower inequalities are needed for this allowed strict Laurent box.
The space $X$ is good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth and
pure of dimension $2q$.

Write $D=d'd''$, and define the original full cap currents
\[
 \begin{split}
 S_1&=\bigwedge_{j=1}^q
                   D\max\{\log|Y_j|,-2\lambda\}\wedge[X],\\
 S_2&=\bigwedge_{i=1}^q
                   D\max\{\log|X_i|,0\}\wedge[X],\\
 S&=2S_1+S_2.
 \end{split}
 \tag{CB3}
\]
Every logarithmic hinge is locally constant across its zero
divisor. These are original locally bounded positive cap products,
well defined on an ordinary neighborhood of $K_0$. They are
symmetric middle-positive of bidegree $(q,q)$ and separately
$d'$- and $d''$-closed. Their stronger special construction is not
a change in the positivity hypothesis of the statement refuted.

The R9 full-cap support and Fubini theorem identifies the carriers as
\[
 F_1=\operatorname{pr}_Y^{-1}(\zeta_{r^2,\ldots,r^2})\cap V,
 \qquad
 F_2=\operatorname{pr}_X^{-1}(\zeta_{1,\ldots,1})\cap V.
 \tag{CB4}
\]
These are the \emph{full fibers of the joint Gauss seminorms}.
They are not the entire coordinate norm levels, nor an intersection
of coordinate conditions with correlated points left unexamined.
On $F_1$ the free $X$ domain is the full radius-$R$ open
polydisc. On $F_2$ the free $Y$ domain is the same full open
polydisc. Indeed on the former carrier $|Y_j|=r^2$, and on the
latter $|X_i|=1$, so the product inequalities in (CB2) introduce
no additional free-coordinate restriction. The original cap
calibration has normal multiplicity one.

For every original classical psh $a:V\to[0,1]$, put
\[
 \mu_{i,a}=(Da)^q\wedge S_i,\qquad
 \mu_a=(Da)^q\wedge S=2\mu_{1,a}+\mu_{2,a}.
 \tag{CB5}
\]
All these are the original positive Radon top measures, on the
complete original test sheaf and every actual refinement. Define
\[
 C(E)=\sup_{a:V\to[0,1]\ {\rm original\ classical\ psh}}\mu_a(E),
 \qquad
 C^*(E)=\inf_{\substack{G\supset E\\G\ {\rm ordinary\ open\ in}\ V}}C(G).
 \tag{CB6}
\]
No boundary value is imposed on a normalized capacity tester.
No member of this family is silently placed in a zero-boundary
energy completion.

\subsection{The three original Gauss points}

Let $A,B,z_0$ denote the original joint product Gauss points with
the following radii:
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c|c}
       &X_1,\ldots,X_q&Y_1,\ldots,Y_q\\ \hline
 A     &(r,\ldots,r)&(r^2,\ldots,r^2)\\
 B     &(1,\ldots,1)&(1,r,\ldots,r)\\
 z_0   &(1,\ldots,1)&(r^2,\ldots,r^2).
 \end{array}
 \tag{CB7}
\]
All lie in the compact unit polydisc inside $V$. Set
$K=\{A,B\}$. The point $A$ belongs to $F_1\setminus F_2$,
and $B$ belongs to $F_2\setminus F_1$; $z_0$ belongs to their
intersection. In particular, the following calculation does not
replace $F_1\cap F_2$ by the singleton $\{z_0\}$.

\begin{theorem}[A compact raw/outer gap for every original tester]
\label{thm:r16-crossed-box-compact-capacity-gap}
For the fixed original field and every $q\ge2$, the strict box
and allowed background in (CB1)--(CB3) satisfy
\[
 \boxed{\qquad
 C(K)=\bigl(2+2^{1-q}\bigr)(2\lambda)^{-q}
       \ <\ 3(2\lambda)^{-q}\ \le C^*(K)<\infty .
 \qquad}
 \tag{CB8}
\]
The raw supremum on $K$ is attained by an explicit actual
continuous original normalized tester. There is also a sequence
of such actual normalized testers whose source measures converge
weakly on the original space to a measure with mass
$3(2\lambda)^{-q}$ on $K$.

Consequently the full general compact no-gain assertion FG1 is
\texttt{FALSE}, already on a strict Laurent box and a separately
closed allowed background extending across its closed box. The
same example refutes universal Borel raw/outer equality. It does
not assert failure for every background or every strict box.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
explicit full-original-tester compact gap, subject to the exact
source-hash audits in the companion ledger. The polynomial moving
atom calculation used below is the frozen R3 input, not a newly
claimed example. The new ingredients are the crossed strict box,
the asymmetric full cap pair, and the upper bound for every
actual original tester.

\subsection{Gauss majorization and an atomic comparison}

We prove the full-test comparison needed for (CB8), including
the use of auxiliary fields. They appear only in the
\emph{defining scalar curve tests} of an original classical
function; no Bedford--Taylor theory over an auxiliary field is
introduced.

\begin{lemma}[A full-cap Gauss majorant controls the Gauss atom]
\label{lem:r16-crossed-box-Gauss-atom}
Let $a:V\to[0,1]$ be any original classical psh function, possibly
discontinuous. Fix either carrier in (CB4), write $Z$ for its
$q$ free coordinates, and let $b$ denote the fixed normal joint
Gauss point. For $s\in(-\infty,\lambda)^q$, write $\sigma_b(s)$
for the original joint Gauss point with free radii $e^{s_i}$
and normal point $b$, and put
\[
                         \varphi(s)=a(\sigma_b(s)).
 \tag{CB9}
\]
Then $\varphi$ is finite, continuous, convex and coordinatewise
nondecreasing, with $0\le\varphi\le1$. On the entire full carrier,
at points where all free coordinates are nonzero,
\[
                  a(x)\le
                \varphi(\log|Z_1(x)|,\ldots,\log|Z_q(x)|).
 \tag{CB10}
\]
For every $s$ in the displayed real domain, one has
\[
                   \mu_{i,a}\{\sigma_b(s)\}
                       \le q!\operatorname{Vol}_q\partial\varphi(s).
 \tag{CB11}
\]
Lebesgue volume is in the original logarithmic coordinates and
their standard integral lattice. In particular there is no
unrecorded absolute-value or residue-degree rescaling.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
First prove (CB10). For an arbitrary point of the full carrier,
pass to a complete extension containing its completed residue
field, only to apply scalar curve tests. Hold all but one free
coordinate fixed and replace that coordinate by the variable on
the closed scalar disc of radius equal to its current norm.
The entire closed disc maps into $V$: its radius is strictly
less than $R$, and the fixed normal radii make all product
inequalities automatic. The pulled-back original function is
bounded subharmonic. Its value is at most its value at the
unique boundary Gauss point, by the scalar subharmonic maximum
principle on a closed disc with a slightly larger open disc
available. This principle applies to upper-semicontinuous
subharmonic functions, without a continuity hypothesis.

Repeat for all free coordinates, using the corresponding
completed residue fields if necessary. At the end every free
coordinate has been made Gauss-independent of the unchanged
normal base. For an original polynomial
$\sum_I c_I(Y)Z^I$, its resulting seminorm is exactly
$\max_I|c_I(b)|e^{I\cdot s}$. Thus its original image is
$\sigma_b(s)$. Uniform polynomial approximation on the compact
polydiscs gives the same identity for analytic functions.
This proves majorization on the \emph{entire} carrier, including
points with correlations before the free coordinates are replaced.
It is not a statement just on a chosen skeleton.

We next prove joint convexity. Fix an integral direction
$m\in\mathbf Z^q$ and a segment $s^0+t m$ in the real domain.
Over a complete extension containing the normal Gauss field,
choose independent Gauss coefficients $c_i$ of radii $e^{s_i^0}$.
Use the scalar annulus map
\[
                         Z_i=c_iT^{m_i}.
 \tag{CB12}
\]
At a scalar Gauss point of radius $e^t$, its original image
is precisely $\sigma_b(s^0+t m)$. Indeed, after grouping a
polynomial by the exponent $I\cdot m$ of $T$, the independent
Gauss coefficient norm in each group remains the maximum of
the individual monomial norms. The resulting norm is therefore
$\max_I |c_I(b)|e^{I\cdot(s^0+t m)}$. Negative exponents of
$T$ cause no problem on this scalar annulus. The original image
of the entire annulus stays in $V$ along the chosen segment.

Subtracting the affine harmonic interpolation of two boundary
values and applying the scalar annular maximum principle gives
convexity along that segment. The same conclusion holds for every
rational direction after rescaling. Separate convexity and the
bound $0\le\varphi\le1$ give a local Lipschitz bound on every
smaller real box: each coordinate secant slope is bounded by the
reciprocal distance to the boundary of a slightly larger box.
Changing one coordinate at a time proves interior continuity.
Approximating a real direction by rational directions now proves
full convexity. Finally a convex function of one coordinate on
$(-\infty,\lambda)$ which is bounded above cannot have a
negative secant slope. Each coordinate section is therefore
nondecreasing.

On an ordinary annular neighborhood of $\sigma_b(s)$ define
the original toric function
\[
                           h=\varphi(\log|Z_1|,\ldots,\log|Z_q|).
 \tag{CB13}
\]
Finite convex functions of original unit moments are continuous
classical psh by the frozen original convex-composition
calculus. Only this local annular neighborhood is needed; no
extension across zero coordinates is required. On its intersection
with the full carrier, (CB10) gives $a\le h$, and at
$\sigma_b(s)$ there is equality.

Here is the carrier-order bridge for the contact comparison.
Let $w=\max(a,h)$ on that neighborhood. The functions $w$ and
$h$ agree pointwise on the whole support of $S_i$. Their first
products agree because $(w-h)S_i=0$. Inductively every bounded
BT product is still supported there, and multiplication by
$w-h$ vanishes on its coefficient measures. The defining
recursion therefore gives
\[
                             \mu_{i,w}=\mu_{i,h}.
 \tag{CB14}
\]
This is equality on every original compact test and actual
refinement, using the fixed original background. It is not a
new restriction or division theorem for arbitrary currents.

The frozen R3 maximum inequality, with its strict Borel locality
proof, says
$\mu_{i,\max(a,h)}\ge
\mathbf1_{\{a\ge h\}}\mu_{i,a}$.
At the displayed Gauss point $a=h$, so (CB14) yields
\[
                     \mu_{i,a}\{\sigma_b(s)\}
                            \le\mu_{i,h}\{\sigma_b(s)\}.
 \tag{CB15}
\]
Ordinary order $a\le h$ off the carrier was neither needed nor
assumed.

For the \emph{toric function $h$}, original full-cap calibration
and Fubini give
$\mu_{i,h}\{\sigma_b(s)\}
=q!\operatorname{Vol}_q\partial\varphi(s)$.
The formula holds first for finite convex PL functions: the
top-degree corner mass is $q!$ times the slope-polytope volume,
and the normal cap has multiplicity one. Approximate a general
finite convex $\varphi$ uniformly on a protected real annular
stage by convex PL functions. The frozen bounded uniform BT
continuity, the original toric calibration on every compact
test, and Alexandrov weak continuity pass the full measure
identity to the limit. Equivalently the real measure is
$q!\operatorname{MA}_{\mathbf R}(\varphi)$ carried by the
continuous original joint Gauss section. Its atomic mass is the
displayed subgradient volume. This justifies (CB11) without any
pushforward equality for the original, possibly non-toric
function $a$.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Exact antecedents for the lemma.}
The scalar disc and annulus maximum principles are the same
classical curve facts used in frozen R14 NT2--NT3 and in R16
WQ7. Joint Gauss convexity for every bounded original tester is
already frozen R6,
\texttt{lem:r6-joint-gauss-convexity}, in
\texttt{capacity\_gauss\_convex\_reduction.tex}. The proof above
spells out its scalar-curve use on the present full caps; joint
convexity by itself is not claimed anew. The frozen R4 definition
of the actual classical class explicitly permits every analytic
curve after every complete isometric extension. Endpoint radii
may be realized in a further such extension when using closed
scalar annuli. The Gauss seminorm/Fubini identities are frozen R9.
The maximum inequality is frozen
\texttt{prop:r3-relative-contact-inequality}, included verbatim
in the R4 aggregate at the source
\texttt{base\_r3/sections/relative\_contact\_inequality.tex}.
Its proof uses strict Borel maximum locality and compact
Portmanteau after a decreasing maximum, not FG1. The toric
point mass normalization is the frozen R3 moving-atom
calculation. Only that toric calibration, and not its already
disproved extension to arbitrary nonlinear Gauss pushforwards,
is used in (CB15).

For primary scalar references see V.~Wanner,
\emph{Subharmonic functions and real-valued differential forms on
non-archimedean curves} (2019), Definition~3.1.5 and
Propositions~3.1.8--3.1.10,
\url{https://epub.uni-regensburg.de/40530/1/THESIS.pdf}.
The auxiliary fields for these scalar tests may be chosen complete
and algebraically closed; no current is transported to them.
For real Alexandrov measure and its weak continuity see
G.~De Philippis and A.~Figalli,
\emph{The Monge--Ampere equation and its link to optimal
transportation}, Section~2.1, formula~(2.2) and Proposition~2.4,
\url{https://people.math.ethz.ch/~afigalli/lecture-notes-pdf/The-Monge-Ampere-equation-and-its-link-to-optimal-transportation.pdf}.
Both primary statements were read directly for this audit.

\subsection{The upper bound for every original normalized tester}

Fix an arbitrary $a$ in (CB6), and put
\[
           t=a(z_0)\in[0,1],\qquad
           m_A=\mu_{1,a}\{A\},\qquad m_B=\mu_{2,a}\{B\}.
 \tag{CB16}
\]
Apply the lemma to $F_1$. The free-coordinate trace
$\varphi_X$ is defined on $(-\infty,\lambda)^q$; put
$v=\varphi_X(-\lambda,\ldots,-\lambda)\ge0$.
For every $p\in\partial\varphi_X(-\lambda,\ldots,-\lambda)$,
coordinate monotonicity gives $p_i\ge0$. The supporting-plane
inequality, first at the point $(0,\ldots,0)$ and then at
$(\lambda-\epsilon,\ldots,\lambda-\epsilon)$, gives
\[
        \lambda\sum_i p_i\le t-v,\qquad
        2\lambda\sum_i p_i\le1-v
                        \quad\hbox{after }\epsilon\downarrow0.
 \tag{CB17}
\]
The point with all free radii one and this normal base is
\emph{exactly} $z_0$. It is not the retraction of a different
residue-branch point. This exact choice of the asymmetric cap
radii is essential.

The nonnegative simplex
$\{p:\sum_i p_i\le c\}$ has volume $c^q/q!$.
Using (CB11), (CB17), and $v\ge0$ therefore yields
\[
                  m_A\le
                 \lambda^{-q}\min\{2^{-q},t^q\}.
 \tag{CB18}
\]

For $F_2$, let $\varphi_Y$ be the free $Y$ trace, and put
$b=(0,-\lambda,\ldots,-\lambda)$.
Coordinate monotonicity gives
\[
       \varphi_Y(b)\ge
          \varphi_Y(-2\lambda,\ldots,-2\lambda)=t.
 \tag{CB19}
\]
For $p\in\partial\varphi_Y(b)$ one has $p_i\ge0$, and
approaching the all-upper corner gives
\[
       \lambda p_1+2\la

text:
crossed_box_singletons_and_outer_bounds.tex \section{Individually regular points and compact discontinuity in the crossed box}
\label{sec:r16-crossed-singleton-outer-bounds}

\paragraph{Scope, role and status.}
This is a \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY} refinement of the single
crossed-box family CB, with zero additional principal-family count.
It proves two exact singleton outer capacities, a finite upper bound
on the already separated two-point outer capacity, and an explicit
failure of decreasing-compact continuity for the raw capacity.
The exact two-point outer value is not determined.

Fix the same original finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$, its unchanged
absolute value, a uniformizer $\pi$, $r=|\pi|$, $\lambda=-\log r>0$,
an integer $q\ge2$, and $\kappa=(2\lambda)^{-q}$. Work on the original
affine strict Laurent box
\[
 V=\{|X_i|<r^{-1},\ |Y_j|<r^{-1},\ |X_iY_j|<r^{-1}
                                      \quad(1\le i,j\le q)\}
 \tag{CO1}
\]
with exactly the extending background
\[
 S=2S_1+S_2,\qquad
 S_1=\bigwedge_{j=1}^qD\max(\log|Y_j|,-2\lambda)\wedge[X],
 \qquad
 S_2=\bigwedge_{i=1}^qD\max(\log|X_i|,0)\wedge[X].
 \tag{CO2}
\]
Here $D=d'd''$ and $X=(\mathbf A_K^{2q})^{\rm an}$.
All original compact tests, every ordinary germ and every actual
refinement are retained. The full carriers $F_1,F_2$ are the entire
fibers over the normal joint Gauss points of $Y$ radii $r^2$ and
$X$ radii one, respectively. They are not replaced by norm levels.
The original closed box is compact in the interior of the radius
$r^{-3}$ affinoid, and both backgrounds extend across it.

Keep the original points of CB:
$A$ has $X$ radii all $r$ and $Y$ radii all $r^2$;
$B$ has $X$ radii all one and $Y$ radii $(1,r,\ldots,r)$.
The distinct moving residue points $B_j$ of CB satisfy $B_j\to B$.
Write
\[
       K=\{A,B\},\qquad K_m=\{A,B,B_j:\ j\ge m\}.
 \tag{CO3}
\]
All capacities below use \emph{every} actual original classical
psh tester $a:V\to[0,1]$, including discontinuous upper-semicontinuous
ones, normalized on this entire $V$.

\subsection*{A sharp mass bound on each full cap}

For $i=1$ use free coordinates $Z=(X_1,\ldots,X_q)$ on $F_1$;
for $i=2$ use $Z=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_q)$ on $F_2$.
The coordinate inequalities on either entire fiber are precisely
the free radius-$r^{-1}$ polydisc inequalities. For numbers
$D_1,\ldots,D_q>0$ put
\[
 E_{i,\mathbf D}
   =F_i\cap\{\,|Z_l|\le\exp(\lambda-D_l)\quad(1\le l\le q)\,\},
 \qquad
 b_{\mathbf D}
   =\max\left\{-1,\,
           \frac{\log|Z_l|-\lambda}{D_l}\quad(1\le l\le q)\right\}.
 \tag{CO4}
\]
The latter is a global continuous actual psh function on $V$,
with $-1\le b_{\mathbf D}<0$, and extends across the closed box.
The finite floor removes coordinate poles.

\begin{lemma}[Full-tester inner-polydisc mass bound]
For every original normalized tester $a$ and either $i$,
\[
       \mu_{S_i,a}(E_{i,\mathbf D})
                            \le\prod_{l=1}^qD_l^{-1}.
 \tag{CO5}
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The full-cap toric calibration gives the exact original measure
\[
  \mu_{S_i,b_{\mathbf D}}
       =\left(\prod_lD_l^{-1}\right)\delta_{\zeta_{i,\mathbf D}},
 \tag{CO6}
\]
where the free joint Gauss radii are $\exp(\lambda-D_l)$ and
the normal radii are those of $F_i$. The product of the free slopes
is exactly the $q!$-normalized simplex volume; all normal
multiplicities are one. This calibrates only the displayed actual
toric function, not an arbitrary Gauss pushforward.

Fix $\delta>0$ and $c>1+\delta$, and put
\[
               v=\max\{a-1-\delta,\ c b_{\mathbf D}\}.
 \tag{CO7}
\]
It is a bounded actual classical psh function on the same original
$V$. On $E_{i,\mathbf D}$ one has $b_{\mathbf D}=-1$ and
$a-1-\delta\ge-1-\delta>-c$. The frozen strict Borel maximum
locality theorem therefore gives
\[
             \mathbf1_{E_{i,\mathbf D}}\mu_{S_i,v}
                   =\mathbf1_{E_{i,\mathbf D}}\mu_{S_i,a}.
 \tag{CO8}
\]
This uses no continuity of $a$ and no assertion that its strict
comparison superlevel is ordinary open.

We verify the total mass of $v$ directly. Every mixed tail with
background $S_i$ remains carried by $F_i$. Since $a-1-\delta\le-\delta$,
the coefficient $v-cb_{\mathbf D}$ is zero wherever
$b_{\mathbf D}>-\delta/c$. Its product with any such mixed tail
is thus supported in
\[
                  F_i\cap\{b_{\mathbf D}\le-\delta/c\}\Subset V.
 \tag{CO9}
\]
Indeed every free coordinate is then bounded by
$\exp(\lambda-D_l\delta/c)<r^{-1}$, while all normal radii
are fixed. This is a closed subset of a compact original
polydisc. On $F_1$ the normal $Y$ radii are $r^2<1$;
on $F_2$ the normal $X$ radii are one. In both cases the
individual and product inequalities have a strict uniform
margin, proving the asserted compact containment.

The original bounded mixed BT telescope gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mu_{S_i,v}-c^q\mu_{S_i,b_{\mathbf D}}
  =D\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}
       (v-cb_{\mathbf D})(Dv)^k
                (cDb_{\mathbf D})^{q-1-k}\wedge S_i.
 \end{split}
 \tag{CO10}
\]
Every coefficient current on the right is compactly supported
by (CO9). Testing by an original smooth scalar equal to one on
a neighborhood of those supports and the point in (CO6) gives
zero for the total derivative. Outside that compact the two
positive top measures agree, and the second is supported at
the displayed point. Consequently both total masses are finite and
\[
               \mu_{S_i,v}(V)=c^q\prod_lD_l^{-1}.
 \tag{CO11}
\]
Equations (CO8)--(CO11) imply the bound with the factor $c^q$.
Let $\delta\downarrow0$ and $c\downarrow1$ with $c>1+\delta$.
This proves (CO5).

Only local bounded original BT, strict Borel locality, compact
current differentiation and the exact full-cap calibration are
used. In particular (CO7) is not silently declared to satisfy
a different global energy boundary condition; no completed
boundary assertion or new-field BT theorem is needed.
\end{proof}

\subsection*{Exact singleton values and the two-point upper bound}

\begin{proposition}[The two singletons are outer regular]
In the original full tester class,
\[
       C_S(\{A\};V)=C_S^*(\{A\};V)=2\kappa,\qquad
       C_S(\{B\};V)=C_S^*(\{B\};V)=2\kappa.
 \tag{CO12}
\]
Consequently
\[
       (2+2^{1-q})\kappa=C_S(K;V)
                    <3\kappa\le C_S^*(K;V)\le4\kappa.
 \tag{CO13}
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $0<\epsilon<\lambda$ take the ordinary open neighborhoods
\[
 \begin{split}
 G_{A,\epsilon}
   &=\{\,|X_i|<\exp(-\lambda+\epsilon)\quad(1\le i\le q)\,\}
                                                          \cap V,\\
 G_{B,\epsilon}
   &=\{\,r<|Y_1|<e^\epsilon,\ 
          |Y_l|<\exp(-\lambda+\epsilon)\quad(2\le l\le q)\,\}
                                                          \cap V.
 \end{split}
 \tag{CO14}
\]
The first is disjoint from $F_2$, whose normal $X$ radii are
all one. The second is disjoint from $F_1$, whose normal
$Y_1$ radius is $r^2<r$. Applying (CO5) to their closures
in the free coordinate polydiscs gives, for every normalized $a$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mu_{S,a}(G_{A,\epsilon})&\le2(2\lambda-\epsilon)^{-q},\\
 \mu_{S,a}(G_{B,\epsilon})&\le
       (\lambda-\epsilon)^{-1}(2\lambda-\epsilon)^{1-q}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{CO15}
\]
Taking the supremum over all original testers and then
$\epsilon\downarrow0$ proves that each singleton outer capacity
is at most $2\kappa$.

The continuous actual normalized testers
\[
 \begin{split}
 a_A&=\max\{0,(L_X+\lambda)/(2\lambda)\},\\
 a_B&=\max\{0,\log|Y_1|/\lambda,\,
                       (\log|Y_l|+\lambda)/(2\lambda)\ (2\le l\le q)\}
 \end{split}
 \tag{CO16}
\]
are defined on all of $V$. Their full-cap traces and slope
products give
\[
                  \mu_{S,a_A}=2\kappa\delta_A,\qquad
                  \mu_{S,a_B}=2\kappa\delta_B.
 \tag{CO17}
\]
For the inactive component the trace is constant on its
entire full carrier, so its source is zero. These equalities
also follow directly from the same original trace recursion
used in CB. Thus each raw singleton capacity is at least
$2\kappa$, proving (CO12).

The union of the two neighborhoods in (CO14) contains $K$.
For each tester its positive measure on this union is at most
the sum of the two masses, so taking the supremum and using
(CO15) gives $C_S^*(K;V)\le4\kappa$. The exact raw value
and strict outer lower bound in (CO13) are the already proved
CB theorem. No interchange of an infimum and a supremum is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Raw capacity fails decreasing-compact continuity]
The compact sets $K_m$ in (CO3) decrease to $K$, are all contained
in the one compact $K_1\Subset V$, and satisfy
\[
                  C_S(K_m;V)\ge3\kappa
                       >C_S(K;V)\qquad(m\ge1).
 \tag{CO18}
\]
Hence the raw capacity is not continuous from above even along
this explicit compact sequence.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Compactness and the intersection follow from the original
convergence of the distinct $B_j$ to $B$. For any $j\ge m$,
the actual normalized CB tester has source
$\kappa(2\delta_A+\delta_{B_j})$, wholly supported on $K_m$.
Its mass there is $3\kappa$. Taking the supremum proves (CO18).
The common-core CY row may equally be used, with the identical
original source. The strict inequality is CB's positive gap.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Exact stopping point and failed inference.}
The two singletons are individually raw/outer regular, while their
union is not. Thus singleton regularity cannot be used to prove
finite-compact regularity by an additive argument: the raw capacity
is a supremum over one common normalized tester, not a measure.
The exact value of $C_S^*(K;V)$ inside the proved interval
$[3\kappa,4\kappa]$ remains \texttt{OPEN}.
In particular no atomic bound from CB has been applied to a
whole shrinking ordinary neighborhood. Its moving residue sources
prevent that replacement.

All displayed results here have \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY} status,
with CB and the bounded original BT/full-cap calculus as
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}. Elementary finite-measure subadditivity
and compact differentiation are \texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN}.
Universal compact raw/outer equality and raw decreasing-compact
continuity are \texttt{FALSE}; the additive and atom-to-neighborhood
shortcuts just described are \texttt{FAILED\_ATTEMPT}.
Any sharper outer estimate is \texttt{CONDITIONAL} on a new
uniform full-tester neighborhood bound, not a supplied theorem.
No extra \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} principal family is counted.
Restricted KC12/GQ/CTO, independent geometric Dirichlet
compatibility and literal ED automatic strong continuity remain
\texttt{OPEN}. No positivity cone is identified with another,
and no ordinary current equality is enlarged to all GK delta tests.
