b1_strong_subadditivity_counterexample_independent_proof.tex \section{An independent derivation of the three-arm obstruction}
\noindent\textbf{Status.} \texttt{PROVED-INTERNAL}: failure of strong subadditivity of the original outer capacity in every ambient dimension $n\ge2$, with remaining degree $q=1$. This does not refute Borel compact-inner regularity, because strong subadditivity is not a necessary axiom of a Choquet capacity.

Use the original torus, box $V$, normalized moment map $\tau:V\to Q=(-1,1)^n$, and smooth positive background $S=\beta^{n-1}[X]$ from the audited linear trace lemma. Put
\[
 \gamma=(n-1)!\lambda^{n-2}.
\]
That lemma, for every bounded original normalized classical psh tester $a$, gives a continuous convex $g:Q\to[0,1]$ with
\[
 \tau_*(Da\wedge S)=\gamma\Delta g.
 \tag{SA1}
\]
It uses the convex almost-everywhere representative of $a\circ\sigma$, not an unproved pointwise identification.

Fix $0<r<1/3$. In $(-1,1)^2$ let
\[
 C=\{(0,-s):0\le s\le r\},\quad
 D=\{(s,0):0\le s\le r\},\quad
 E=\{(-s,0):0\le s\le r\},\quad
 A=C\cup D,\quad B=C\cup E.
\]
Write $J=[-r,r]^{n-2}$, with the usual singleton and volume-one convention if $n=2$, and put
\[
 \widehat F=\tau^{-1}(F\times J)\quad(F=A,B,C,D,E),\qquad
 \kappa=\gamma(2r)^{n-2}.
\]
These are compact subsets in the original ordinary topology; no assumption that their inverse images consist only of skeleton points is made.

\begin{lemma}[Paired jumps on adjacent perpendicular arms]
For every convex $g:(-1,1)^2\to[0,1]$,
\[
 \Delta g(C)\le2r,\qquad
 \Delta g(A)\le {2r\over1-r},\qquad
 \Delta g(B)\le {2r\over1-r}.
 \tag{SA2}
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The slice formula gives
\[
 \partial_{xx}g(C)=\int_0^r
 \bigl(\partial_{x,+}g(0,-s)-\partial_{x,-}g(0,-s)\bigr)\,ds.
\]
The transverse Lebesgue factor in the other slice formula gives
$\partial_{yy}g(C)=0$. Every slice at $x=0$ has derivative jump at most $2$, by secants toward $x=\pm1$ and $0\le g\le1$. This proves the first bound. In particular, trace Hessian measures have no point atoms, so the common endpoint of the arms causes no additional term.

Set $L=(1-r)^{-1}$. Every subgradient $p$ of $g$ at a point of $[-r,r]^2$ satisfies $|p_1|+|p_2|\le L$: apply the supporting inequality at displacement $(1-r-\varepsilon)(\operatorname{sgn}p_1,\operatorname{sgn}p_2)$ and then let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

For almost every $s\in(0,r)$, the restrictions of $g$ to both axes are differentiable in their tangential directions at $(0,-s)$ and $(s,0)$. Thus all subgradients at the first point have the same second component $b$, and all those at the second have the same first component $c$. The projections of these compact subdifferentials onto the normal coordinate are intervals with endpoints the corresponding one-sided directional derivatives. Write their extremal elements as
\[
 p_C^+=(a,b),\quad p_C^-=(a-h,b),\qquad
 p_D^-=(c,d),\quad p_D^+=(c,d+k),
\]
where $h,k\ge0$ are exactly the normal derivative jumps.
Monotonicity of the subgradient map applied to $p_C^+$ and $p_D^-$ gives
\[
 (p_D^--p_C^+)\cdot(s,s)\ge0,
 \qquad c+d\ge a+b.
\]
The $\ell^1$ bounds on $p_C^-$ and $p_D^+$ give
\[
 h\le a+L-|b|,\qquad k\le L-|c|-d.
\]
Therefore
\[
 h+k\le2L+a-d-|b|-|c|
       \le2L+c-b-|b|-|c|\le2L.
\]
Only the normal components charge the respective arms: $\partial_{yy}g(C)=0$ and $\partial_{xx}g(D)=0$ by their transverse Lebesgue factors. Integrating $h+k$ in $s$ proves the bound for $A$. Reflection of the first coordinate proves the bound for $B$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The needed outer upper bound is non-circular]
For any compact $F\Subset Q$, the family $\mathcal C_n$ of convex functions $g:Q\to[0,1]$ satisfies
\[
 \inf_{F\subset U\Subset Q,\ U\text{ open}}\ \sup_{g\in\mathcal C_n}\Delta g(U)
       =\sup_{g\in\mathcal C_n}\Delta g(F).
 \tag{SA3}
\]
Consequently the right side, multiplied by $\gamma$, bounds the original $C_S^*(\tau^{-1}F;V)$ from above.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Interior slope bounds and the Arzela--Ascoli diagonal argument make $\mathcal C_n$ compact for locally uniform convergence. Under such convergence the positive measures $\Delta g$ converge weakly on each protected compact region: distributional convergence follows immediately, and uniform local mass bounds upgrade it to convergence against continuous compact tests.

Choose closed compact neighborhoods $F_j\downarrow F$ inside $Q$, and choose $g_j$ whose mass on $F_j$ is within $1/j$ of the supremum. Extract a locally uniformly convergent subsequence with limit $g$. For each fixed $m$, eventual containment $F_j\subset F_m$ and Portmanteau give
\[
 \lim_j\sup_{f\in\mathcal C_n}\Delta f(F_j)\le\Delta g(F_m).
\]
Let $m\to\infty$ and use continuity from above of this single locally finite measure. The result is at most $\sup_f\Delta f(F)$. Monotonicity supplies the reverse bound. Taking the interiors of the $F_j$ proves (SA3).

For every original tester the pushforward is given by (SA1), so its mass on the ordinary open set $\tau^{-1}U$ is at most $\gamma\sup_g\Delta g(U)$. Taking these particular original open neighborhoods gives the claimed outer upper bound. This argument uses compactness of the explicit convex family, not a general Borel outer-regularity theorem for the original tester family.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Strict failure of original outer strong subadditivity]
One has
\[
 C_S^*(\widehat C;V)=2r\kappa,\qquad
 C_S^*(\widehat A\cup\widehat B;V)\ge4r\kappa,
\]
whereas
\[
 C_S^*(\widehat A;V),\ C_S^*(\widehat B;V)
                         \le {2r\over1-r}\kappa.
\]
Since $\widehat A\cap\widehat B=\widehat C$, these imply
\[
 C_S^*(\widehat A\cup\widehat B;V)+C_S^*(\widehat A\cap\widehat B;V)
 -C_S^*(\widehat A;V)-C_S^*(\widehat B;V)
 \ge {2r(1-3r)\over1-r}\kappa>0.
 \tag{SA4}
\]
At $r=1/6$, the left two capacities sum to at least $\kappa$, while the right two sum to at most $4\kappa/5$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
For $n=2$, combine (SA2) and (SA3). The explicit normalized toric tester $|x|$ has trace source $2\delta_0(dx)\,dy$, so it gives $C$ mass $2r$. The tester $|y|$ gives $D\cup E$ mass $4r$. These provide the lower bounds using actual continuous classical psh testers and hence also lower bounds for outer capacity.

For general $n$, fix the last $n-2$ coordinates and apply the two-dimensional calculation to the resulting convex slice, then integrate over $J$. The $x$ and $y$ Hessian components acquire the factor $(2r)^{n-2}$. Every Hessian component in one of the other coordinate directions gives $(A\cup B)\times J$ zero mass: its transverse projection includes the planar three-arm set, which has two-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero; the slice masses are locally uniformly bounded. The same applies to $A\times J$, $B\times J$, and $C\times J$. The explicit testers $|x|$ and $|y|$ are independent of the other coordinates and give exactly the claimed lower bounds. Finally multiply by $\gamma$ from (SA1) and apply (SA3) to the compact products.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Limits of the conclusion.}
The capacity, normalization, background, field, absolute value, and full tester class are unchanged. The counterexample concerns strong subadditivity, not ordinary subadditivity. It is an obstruction to a proposed route to B1, not a counterexample to B1 itself. The compact-set outer argument above is confined to this explicit moment-trace setting and cannot be exported to arbitrary compact sets or arbitrary backgrounds. No claim of worldwide novelty is made without a separate literature comparison.

title: Failure of the classical total-mass calibration for relative extremals

b1_extremal_total_mass_obstruction.tex \section{Failure of the classical total-mass calibration for relative extremals}
\paragraph{Status and scope.}
This is an original-category obstruction to importing the classical
relative-extremal-function proof of Borel capacity regularity unchanged.
It is not a counterexample to B1. The background is smooth and strongly
positive, $q=1$, and the original dimension is any $n\ge2$. The exact
capacity calculation uses every original normalized classical psh tester,
not only toric testers. No equality of an actual envelope with its toric
trace is assumed, and no nonlinear pushforward identity is used.

Fix the prescribed finite $K/\mathbf Q_p$ and its absolute value,
$\lambda=-\log|\pi|>0$, the original torus $X=(\mathbf G_m^n)^{\rm an}$,
$t_i=\log|T_i|$, and
\[
 V=\{|t_i|<\lambda\ (1\le i\le n)\},\quad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^n d't_i\wedge d''t_i,\quad
 S=\beta^{n-1}\wedge[X],\quad q=n-(n-1)=1.
\]
Use normalized moments $x_i=t_i/\lambda$ and write
$\tau=(x_1,\ldots,x_n):V\to Q=(-1,1)^n$. Let
$\sigma:Q\to V$ be the joint original Gauss section and set
\[
 \gamma=(n-1)!\lambda^{n-2},\qquad A_n=n!2^n\lambda^{n-2}.
\]
For $0<r<1$, define
\[
 K_r=\tau^{-1}([-r,r]^n),\quad
 a_r=\max\left\{{\|x\|_\infty-r\over1-r},0\right\},\quad h_r=a_r-1.
 \tag{EC1}
\]
The compact original analytic domain $K_r$ has nonempty ordinary interior.
The functions $a_r$ and $h_r$ are actual continuous classical psh functions
formed from finite real maxima of original harmonic affine potentials on
the same ordinary representative. In particular $0\le a_r<1$ on $V$.

\begin{lemma}[A local linear trace identity for the full bounded tester class]
Let $a$ be any original bounded classical psh function on $V$. The bounded
Borel function $a\circ\sigma$ has a unique continuous convex representative
$g_a$ modulo Lebesgue null sets. As Radon measures on $Q$,
\[
 \tau_*(Da\wedge S)=\gamma\Delta g_a.
 \tag{EC2}
\]
Pointwise inequalities for actual functions pass to their canonical
convex traces. No assertion about arbitrary completed Borel representatives
is involved here.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$, $\varphi\circ\tau$ is an original compactly
supported smooth CLD scalar test: the moment map is proper over compact
subsets of $Q$. The current recursion, compact Stokes, and the frozen full
original top-form Gauss calibration yield
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_V(\varphi\circ\tau)\,d(Da\wedge S)
 &=\langle aS,D(\varphi\circ\tau)\rangle\\
 &=(n-1)!\lambda^{n-2}\int_Q(a\circ\sigma)\Delta\varphi\,dx.
 \end{split}
 \tag{EC3}
\]
The coefficient follows from
$D\varphi\wedge\beta^{n-1}=(n-1)!\Delta\varphi\,d\mathrm{vol}$
in unnormalized moment coordinates: the rescaling contributes
$\lambda^{-2}$ from differentiation and $\lambda^n$ from volume.

For completeness, convexity of the canonical trace need not be imported
from a completed zero-boundary theorem. Fix a unit vector $v\in\mathbf R^n$
and an orthonormal basis $w_2,\ldots,w_n$ of $v^\perp$. The constant
strongly positive $(n-1,n-1)$ form
\[
 \Theta_v=\bigwedge_{j=2}^n
 d'\langle w_j,t\rangle\wedge d''\langle w_j,t\rangle
\]
is separately closed. The positive bounded BT measure
$Da\wedge\Theta_v\wedge[X]$, tested against nonnegative
$\varphi\circ\tau$, gives by the same Stokes and top-form computation
\[
 0\le\lambda^{n-2}\int_Q(a\circ\sigma)\,\partial_{vv}\varphi\,dx.
\]
Thus every distributional second directional derivative of
$a\circ\sigma$ is nonnegative. Local mollifications have positive
semidefinite Hessian and are convex. They remain uniformly bounded on
protected compact boxes; the elementary interior slope bound for bounded
convex functions makes them locally equicontinuous. Subsequential locally
uniform limits produce a continuous convex representative $g_a$; convergence
in distributions identifies it with $a\circ\sigma$ almost everywhere.
Any two such representatives agree everywhere by continuity. Bounds and
order inequalities pass first almost everywhere and then everywhere.
This also proves the asserted canonical nature of the trace without
asserting equality at every individual Gauss point.

Equation (EC3) now identifies the two positive Radon measures in (EC2).
Only local boundedness, current recursion, positivity, and the full
original top-form calibration have been used. The energy and zero-boundary
assumptions imposed in R17 FP for its later conclusions are not used.
This is a linear degree-one identity, not an arbitrary higher-degree
Monge--Ampere pushforward assertion.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Exact capacity over all original normalized testers]
For every $0<r<1$,
\[
 \boxed{\quad C_S(K_r;V)=C_S^*(K_r;V)
             =A_n\,{r^{n-1}\over1-r}.\quad}
 \tag{EC4}
\]
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Let $a$ be any original tester with $0\le a\le1$. Then
$0\le g_a\le1$. Fix all coordinates other than $x_i$. The resulting
one-variable convex function $f$ has
\[
 f''([-r,r])=f'_+(r)-f'_-(-r)\le {2\over1-r}.
 \tag{EC4a}
\]
Indeed the right derivative is at most
$(1-f(r))/(1-r)\le1/(1-r)$ by comparison with secants approaching $1$;
the left derivative is at least
$(f(-r)-1)/(1-r)\ge-1/(1-r)$ by secants approaching $-1$.
Distributional slicing, obtained by Fubini from the definition of
$\partial_{ii}g_a$, integrates (EC4a) over the other $n-1$ coordinates
and gives
\[
 \partial_{ii}g_a([-r,r]^n)\le {2(2r)^{n-1}\over1-r}.
\]
Summing over $i$ and multiplying by $\gamma$ in (EC2) gives the upper
bound in (EC4) for every original tester. This is a slice computation,
not an assertion of an $n$-dimensional atom on a coordinate hyperplane.

For the explicit $a_r$, fix the other $n-1$ coordinates in the inner
cube. In the remaining coordinate the function is
$\max\{(|x_i|-r)/(1-r),0\}$, so its derivative measure on $[-r,r]$
has mass $2/(1-r)$, including its two endpoint atoms. Integrating these
slice measures gives exactly $2(2r)^{n-1}/(1-r)$ in each coordinate.
This also accounts for all edges and corners, without any extra mass.
Therefore
\[
 \Delta a_r([-r,r]^n)={2n(2r)^{n-1}\over1-r},
\]
so $a_r$ attains the full raw upper bound. For $r<s<1$, the open set
$\tau^{-1}((-s,s)^n)$ contains $K_r$ and its capacity is at most the just
computed value $C_S(K_s;V)$. Let $s\downarrow r$ and use
$C_S\le C_S^*$ to obtain the outer equality. This special exact
calculation does not revive universal compact raw/outer equality.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Obstruction to total-mass extremal calibration]
Every bounded actual classical psh function $u$ satisfying
\[
 h_r\le u\le0\text{ on }V,\qquad
 u\le-1\text{ on }\operatorname{Int}K_r
 \tag{EC5}
\]
has canonical convex trace $g_u=h_r\circ\sigma$ and
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_V Du\wedge S&={A_n\over1-r},\\
 \int_{V\setminus K_r}Du\wedge S
   &=A_n{1-r^{n-1}\over1-r}>0,\\
 {\displaystyle\int_V Du\wedge S\over C_S^*(K_r;V)}
   &=r^{1-n}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{EC6}
\]
In particular no such assignment of actual extremals can identify their
total relative source masses with the original capacities, even up to a
fixed multiplicative upper constant as the obstacle $K_r$ varies within
this one fixed original domain and smooth background.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The order-preserving trace lemma and continuity show $g_u=-1$ on
$[-r,r]^n$ and $g_u\le0$ on $Q$. If $R=\|x\|_\infty>r$, intersect the
ray through $x$ with the cubes of radius $r$ and $s$, where $R<s<1$.
Convexity between these two points, followed by $s\uparrow1$, gives
\[
 g_u(x)\le {R-1\over1-r}.
\]
The lower bound $u\ge h_r$ gives the reverse inequality. This proves
the trace identity without asserting equality off the Gauss section.

For $r<s<1$, flux through the cube of radius $s$ gives
\[
 \Delta g_u([-s,s]^n)={2n(2s)^{n-1}\over1-r}.
\]
Equivalently, the same slicing computation gives derivative jump
$2/(1-r)$ in each coordinate for almost every fixed choice of the other
coordinates in $[-s,s]^{n-1}$; integration yields the displayed formula
without invoking a boundary regularity theorem. Letting $s\uparrow1$ uses
only monotone convergence for this single Radon measure, not continuity
of an outer capacity. The inner mass is the value already computed in
(EC4). Multiplying by $\gamma$ and subtracting proves (EC6). For
$n\ge2$, $r^{1-n}\to\infty$ as $r\downarrow0$, proving the last assertion.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Application to a putative relative extremal function.}
Let
\[
 H=\sup\{v:v\text{ is original classical psh},\ v\le0\text{ on }V,
                                      \ v\le-1\text{ on }K_r\}.
\]
Replacing any competitor by $\max\{v,-1\}$ increases it and preserves
the constraints, so the envelope can be taken over bounded competitors.
The explicit $h_r$ is a competitor; hence $h_r\le H\le0$ and $H=-1$ on
$K_r$. Its ordinary upper semicontinuous regularization $H^*$ satisfies
$h_r\le H^*\le0$ and $H^*=-1$ on $\operatorname{Int}K_r$.
If $H^*$ is an actual classical psh function, (EC6) applies to it.
Consequently its source has positive mass away from the compact obstacle
and its total mass cannot equal (EC4). If psh-envelope existence is not
available, the conjunction of that existence assertion and the classical
total-mass calibration is still refuted. No envelope-existence theorem,
all-fiber envelope identity, or completed point representative is assumed.

\paragraph{Precise implication for B1.}
One cannot import the classical extremal proof simply by replacing
$(dd^c h)^n$ with $(Dh)^q\wedge S$ while keeping the original classical
psh competitor cone. Already for arbitrary original dimension $n\ge2$
and remaining degree $q=1$, the forced convex trace carries relative
source mass outside its obstacle. Enlarging the competitor cone to all
functions subharmonic for the trace operator changes the tester problem
and is not an admissible repair. Original outer Borel compact-inner
regularity remains OPEN; this is a failed analytic calibration, not a
failure of B1 itself.

\paragraph{Internal dependencies and review boundary.}
The proof uses the frozen bounded fixed-background BT recursion and
positivity, max stability of bounded classical psh functions, and the
full original top-form Gauss calibration (R17 FP6, source
8389d2ce81aa5fd1b563767a3c207a06d0b50e661fb06ee978da2d39634c49be.tex,
with its local calculation explicitly extended above). The directional
constant forms give a self-contained convex-trace argument. No energy
completion, abstract weak-compactness inference, general GQ/KC12 descent,
model/conormal restriction, or original raw/outer equality is imported.

title: Sharp binary rooftop energy obstruction in original smooth backgrounds
text:
original_sharp_rooftop_energy_obstruction.tex \documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb,amsthm}
\newtheorem{lemma}{Lemma}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\begin{document}
\title{Sharp binary rooftop energy obstruction in original smooth backgrounds}
\date{}\maketitle

The result below concerns a proposed sufficient estimate, not the literal
continuity question itself. It constructs one allowed original smooth
strongly positive background and bounded actual potentials for which
$e(P(u,v))>e(u)+e(v)$. It also proves that the uniform binary constant $2$ is sharp in degree
one across the original background class. This does not exclude constants
depending on a fixed background, direct finite-family bounds, or C1.

\paragraph{Original geometry and frozen inputs.}
Keep the prescribed finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$, its unchanged
absolute value, a uniformizer $\pi$, and $\lambda=-\log|\pi|>0$. Set
\[
 X=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^2)^{\rm an},\quad
 t=(\log|T_1|,\log|T_2|),\quad Q=(-\lambda,\lambda)^2,
 \quad V=t^{-1}(Q),
\]
\[
 \beta_t=d't_1\wedge d''t_1+d't_2\wedge d''t_2,
 \qquad S_0=\beta_t\wedge[X].
\]
The closed box lies in the ordinary interior of the larger original
Laurent affinoid $t^{-1}([-2\lambda,2\lambda]^2)$. All backgrounds below
extend to its ordinary neighborhood. We use the unchanged relative
strong completion with its encoded approximation boundary, and retain
the full original test sheaf. Here $n=2$, $p=q=1$ and $d=2$.
Frozen R17 FP1--FP6 supplies canonical finite convex Gauss traces,
their completed linear moment identity, and compact toric test pairings
for $S_0$. IF20--IF21 supplies full original toric calibration and
quadratic energy equality for bounded Lipschitz convex zero-boundary
potentials. The actual-core admission argument following IF20 supplies
finite mass, compact negative sublevels and canonical no loss for these
neighborhood-extendible functions. Frozen HC14--HC15 places every original
compact smooth scalar in the actual difference space. Finite relative
rooftops exist and have their frozen greatestness property.

\begin{lemma}[Identification of a bounded polyhedral toric rooftop]
Let $f_1,f_2$ be bounded Lipschitz convex functions on
$Q_0=(-1,1)^2$, continuous and zero on its boundary, negative inside,
with convex neighborhood extensions. Suppose their real convex envelope
$h=\operatorname{conv}(\min(f_1,f_2))$ has the same properties. Set
$F_i=f_i(t/\lambda)$ and $H=h(t/\lambda)$. Then the completed relative
rooftop for $S_0$ equals $H$ in the original relative quotient.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The IF20 actual-core argument admits all three functions. Their bounded
convex neighborhood extensions have finite Laplacian mass, compact strict
negative sublevels, finite energies and eventually unchanged deep
truncations. Thus $H\preceq P:=P_{S_0}(F_1,F_2)\preceq F_i$.
To justify trace order without evaluating a relative class at exceptional
Gauss points, replace any Borel representative of $P$ by its pointwise
clipping between $H$ and $\min(F_1,F_2)$. This agrees with $P$ outside
the fixed union of allowed relative null sets and hence represents the
same completed member. It satisfies the two order bounds everywhere.
The canonical convex trace $g_P$ agrees with this representative on the
Gauss section almost everywhere. Therefore
\[
 h(z)\le g_P(\lambda z)\le\min(f_1(z),f_2(z))
\]
almost everywhere, and hence everywhere by convex continuity. Greatestness
of the real convex envelope forces $g_P(\lambda z)=h(z)$.

This trace equality alone is not used as an injectivity assertion.
For every compact smooth real $\varphi$ on $Q$, frozen FP6 gives
\[
 B_{S_0}(P-H,\varphi\circ t)
       =-\int_Q(g_P-h(t/\lambda))\Delta\varphi\,dt=0.       \tag{1}
\]
Choose compact smooth $\varphi_k$ converging to $h(t/\lambda)$ in
$H_0^1(Q)$. Such approximation applies because $h$ is Lipschitz and
zero on the rectangle boundary. The compact pullbacks are actual energy
differences. Expanding their difference energy by FP6 and IF21 gives
\[
 B_{S_0}(\varphi_k\circ t-H,\varphi_k\circ t-H)
       =\int_Q|\nabla\varphi_k-\nabla(h(t/\lambda))|^2dt
          \longrightarrow0.                              \tag{2}
\]
Quadratic energy Cauchy--Schwarz and (1) imply $B_{S_0}(P-H,H)=0$.
Consequently
\[
 e_{S_0}(P)=e_{S_0}(H)+I_{S_0}(P,H).
\]
But $H\preceq P$ gives $e_{S_0}(P)\le e_{S_0}(H)$ by frozen energy
monotonicity. Thus $I_{S_0}(P,H)=0$ and the completed potentials are
the same relative member. No identification from trace equality alone,
and no restriction of the original test family, has occurred.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Uniformly comparable smooth backgrounds]
Let $S=A(t)\wedge[X]$ be smooth, separately closed and positive on a
neighborhood of the closed box, with constants $0<c\le C<\infty$ such that
\[
                    c\beta_t\le A\le C\beta_t.             \tag{3}
\]
Then its degree-one strong cone, relative null ideal and relative order
identify canonically with those for $S_0$. In particular their relative
rooftops agree.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The degree-one source of each fixed normalized tester is linear in the
background. Applying (3) to every tester, then taking suprema and ordinary-open
outer regularizations, gives two-sided capacity comparisons and hence
equality of the null ideals. The same source
comparisons for bounded actual psh functions give equivalence of finite
mass and power-energy bounds. Compact negative sublevels and the ordinary
boundary conditions are unchanged. The canonical no-loss estimates for
the truncations transfer by the same fixed constants, so the bounded
actual defining cores coincide with their printed qualifications.

For every difference $a-b$ of members of this common actual core, global
Green exchange and positivity of the quadratic energy forms for
$S-cS_0$ and $CS_0-S$ give
\[
 c I_{S_0}(a,b)\le I_S(a,b)\le C I_{S_0}(a,b).              \tag{4}
\]
Both residual backgrounds remain original positive separately closed
backgrounds. Thus the strong Cauchy defining rows and their equivalences
are the same. The capacity comparisons identify their limiting relative
Borel realizations. This proves equality of the completed cones with
their encoded approximation boundary, rather than imposing an ordinary
boundary value on an arbitrary completed member. Their relative orders
and admissible lower families are consequently identical, so greatestness
identifies their rooftops.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
In the original degree-one scope $q=1$, the universal binary estimate
\[
                       e(P(U,V))\le2\bigl(e(U)+e(V)\bigr)
\]
has optimal constant $2$, even when the backgrounds are smooth strongly
positive and the two obstacles belong to the bounded actual core.
Precisely, for every $0<C<2$ there are one allowed original smooth
background and bounded actual obstacles with
\[
                       e(P(U,V))>C\bigl(e(U)+e(V)\bigr).
\]
The background is allowed to depend on $C$. No assertion of sharpness
for a single fixed smooth background is made.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The upper bound follows from the frozen rooftop root inequality
$r(P(U,V))\le r(U)+r(V)$ and
$(r(U)+r(V))^2\le2(r(U)^2+r(V)^2)$, since $d=q+1=2$.

For sharpness fix $0<a<1$, and work in normalized coordinates
$(x,y)=t/\lambda\in Q_0=(-1,1)^2$. Put
\[
 u_a(x,y)=\max\left\{
 \frac{x-1}{1-a},-\frac{x+1}{1+a},
 \frac{y-1}{1+a},-\frac{y+1}{1-a}\right\},
 \qquad v_a(x,y)=u_a(y,x).
\]
These are convex pyramids over the four zero-height corners, with apices
$(a,-a,-1)$ and $(-a,a,-1)$, respectively. Their common real convex
envelope is
\[
 h_a(x,y)=\max\left\{
 \frac{|x|-1}{1-a},\frac{|y|-1}{1-a},\frac{|x+y|}{2}-1
                         \right\}.                         \tag{5}
\]
To verify this, denote the two planar apices by $A=(a,-a)$ and
$B=(-a,a)$ and the corners by $C_{\pm\pm}=(\pm1,\pm1)$.
The six affine branches in (5) are lower supporting planes through
the triples
\[
 (C_{--},C_{-+},B),\ (C_{--},C_{+-},A),\
 (C_{-+},C_{++},B),\ (C_{+-},C_{++},A),
\]
\[
                   (C_{--},A,B),\ (C_{++},A,B).
\]
They are below all six vertex heights and their projected triangles
tile the square. Affine interpolation on each triangle proves both
the common-minorant inequality and greatestness, by the same elementary supporting-plane argument. All three functions are
globally polyhedral convex, negative inside the square, Lipschitz,
continuous and zero on its boundary. Their original moment pullbacks
are therefore qualified bounded actual core potentials.

On the diagonal one has the exact profiles
\[
 u_a(s,s)=v_a(s,s)=\frac{|s|-1}{1+a},\qquad
 h_a(s,s)=|s|-1.
\]
Consequently, for $E_\ell(f)=\int_{-1}^1|(d/ds)f(s,s)|^2ds$,
\[
 E_\ell(u_a)=E_\ell(v_a)=\frac2{(1+a)^2},\qquad
 E_\ell(h_a)=2,
\]
and
\[
 \frac{E_\ell(h_a)}{E_\ell(u_a)+E_\ell(v_a)}
                         =\frac{(1+a)^2}{2}\longrightarrow2
                         \quad(a\uparrow1).                \tag{6}
\]

Use the same entirely smooth original backgrounds
\[
 S_{\delta,\varepsilon}
 =\left[\varepsilon\beta_t+
 \lambda^2D\!\left(\sqrt{((t_2-t_1)/\lambda)^2+\delta^2}\right)
                                                   \right]\wedge[X],
 \qquad\delta,\varepsilon>0.
\]
They satisfy
$\varepsilon S_0\le S_{\delta,\varepsilon}
\le(\varepsilon+2/\delta)S_0$ on the original neighborhood.
The preceding lemmas identify the completed rooftop of the two actual
obstacles with $h_a(t/\lambda)$ for every positive pair of parameters.
For $f\in\{u_a,v_a,h_a\}$, full original torus calibration and
global Green exchange give the following exact smooth energy formula.
Indeed the background matrix in the $t$ coordinates is
$\varepsilon I+\chi_\delta''(y-x)
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$;
its cofactor is
$\varepsilon I+\chi_\delta''(y-x)
\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$.
The factor $\lambda^2$ in the background definition makes the change
$t=\lambda(x,y)$ cancel in the energy integral. Local convex mollification
as in IF20 passes the calibration on all original tests to each
polyhedral potential; the zero-boundary compact clipping argument of
IF21 justifies global Green exchange. All coefficients are bounded and
smooth for fixed positive parameters. Thus
\[
 e_{\delta,\varepsilon}(f(t/\lambda))
 =\varepsilon\int_{Q_0}|\nabla f|^2dxdy
 +\int_{Q_0}\frac{\delta^2(f_x+f_y)^2}
                       {((y-x)^2+\delta^2)^{3/2}}\,dxdy.    \tag{7}
\]
For fixed $a$ the gradients are bounded. With $r=y-x$, the inner
cross-sectional integral of $(f_x+f_y)^2$ is continuous at $r=0$:
away from finitely many diagonal breakpoints the active plane is locally
fixed; if a whole interface lies on the diagonal, its adjacent affine
functions have the same tangential derivative. Dominated convergence
therefore applies to the cross sections. The nonnegative kernel in (7)
has total real-line mass $2$ and concentrates at zero, so
\[
 \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}e_{\delta,\varepsilon}(f(t/\lambda))
              =\varepsilon E_0(f)+2E_\ell(f),\qquad
 E_0(f)=\int_{Q_0}|\nabla f|^2dxdy.                         \tag{8}
\]
The limiting denominator below is strictly positive, and (6)--(8) give
\[
 \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\lim_{\delta\downarrow0}
 \frac{e_{\delta,\varepsilon}(h_a(t/\lambda))}
 {e_{\delta,\varepsilon}(u_a(t/\lambda))+
                         e_{\delta,\varepsilon}(v_a(t/\lambda))}
                         =\frac{(1+a)^2}{2}.                \tag{9}
\]
Given $C<2$, choose $a<1$ with the right side greater than $C$,
then choose a sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$, followed by
a sufficiently small positive $\delta$. Fix these parameters. The
resulting single original smooth background and two actual obstacles
give the required strict inequality. No potential or completion is
transferred to a singular limiting background.
\end{proof}


\paragraph{An explicit fixed smooth counterexample.}
The family above contains a particularly simple fixed example. Take
$a=1/2$ and $\varepsilon=\delta=1/100$. Then
\[
 u=\max\{2(x-1),-\tfrac23(x+1),\tfrac23(y-1),-2(y+1)\},
 \qquad v(x,y)=u(y,x),
\]
\[
 h=\max\{2(|x|-1),2(|y|-1),\tfrac12|x+y|-1\}.
\]
For the single original smooth background $S=S_{1/100,1/100}$ defined
above, the completed rooftop
of $U=u(t/\lambda)$ and $V_1=v(t/\lambda)$ is $H=h(t/\lambda)$.
The background form is bounded between $(1/100)\beta_t$ and
$(200+1/100)\beta_t$. Its full original smooth energy formula is (7).

Here is an exact evaluation rather than a numerical or limiting check.
For a triangle $T$ of area $A_T$ whose three vertex values of $L=y-x$
are $a_T<b_T<c_T$, affine cross-section integration gives
\[
 \int_T\chi_\delta''(L)
 =\frac{2A_T}{c_T-a_T}
  \left(\frac{\chi_\delta(c_T)-\chi_\delta(b_T)}{c_T-b_T}
       -\frac{\chi_\delta(b_T)-\chi_\delta(a_T)}{b_T-a_T}\right),
 \qquad \chi_\delta(r)=\sqrt{r^2+\delta^2}.                 \tag{10}
\]
For a plane $f=\alpha x+\gamma y+\kappa$ on $T$, its energy contribution
is $\varepsilon A_T(\alpha^2+\gamma^2)$ plus $(\alpha+\gamma)^2$
times (10). The four triangles joining each apex to its four boundary
edges give the obstacle energies; the six triangles in the theorem's
proof give the rooftop energy. All relevant vertex values of $L$ are
distinct. Exact substitution gives
\begin{align*}
 e_S(U)=e_S(V_1)
     &=-\frac{16\sqrt{10001}}{225}+\frac2{25}
                                  +\frac{2\sqrt{40001}}{45},\\
 e_S(H)&=-\frac{3\sqrt{10001}}{25}+\frac{13}{100}
                                  +\frac{2\sqrt{40001}}{25}.
\end{align*}
Consequently
\[
 e_S(H)-e_S(U)-e_S(V_1)
     =\frac{\sqrt{10001}}{45}
         -\frac{2\sqrt{40001}}{225}-\frac3{100}
     >\frac{100}{45}-\frac{2\cdot201}{225}-\frac3{100}
      =\frac{73}{180}>\frac25.                            \tag{11}
\]
The strict inequalities use only $\sqrt{10001}>100$ and
$\sqrt{40001}<201$. Thus coefficient-one energy subadditivity fails in
this one explicit smooth original background, with an exact positive gap.

\paragraph{Scope.}
The sharpness statement excludes a background-independent universal binary
constant strictly below $2$ across the original degree-one class. It does
not exclude a subcritical constant $C(S)<2$ for each fixed smooth
background, or a direct arbitrary-finite-family estimate
$e(P(U_i:i\in F))\le C(S,n)\sum_{i\in F}e(U_i)$ whose constant is
independent of $|F|$. It does not disprove SR8 or produce a strongly
convergent row with literal discontinuity. C1 remains open in the full
arbitrary-background scope on the basis of this argument.

\paragraph{Exact frozen source identity.}
The R17 whole source for FP1--FP6, IF20--IF21, and the actual-core and
compact-test qualifications has SHA-256
\texttt{8389d2ce81aa5fd1b563767a3c207a06d0b50e661fb06ee978da2d39634c49be}.
The finite relative rooftop definition and greatestness are recorded
in frozen R12 LG2, SHA-256
\texttt{5001a36a41048e2c6c94189dffcec2f0610537d90ddb64e8c0932770c861988d}.
The completion and positive quadratic energy form remain frozen inputs
in their exact original scopes. The explicit smooth energies above were
independently recomputed from the printed triangulations with exact
arithmetic; the strict final gap uses the displayed rational bounds.
\end{document}

title: Remaining C1 gate after the counterexamples
text:
REMAINING_C1_GATE.md # Remaining C1 gate after the counterexamples

Status: OPEN; the implications below are CONDITIONAL and are not new analytic estimates.

For one fixed allowed original background S and one actual strongly convergent row (u_j), a direct bound

    e_S(P(u_j:j in F)) <= C(S,row) sum_{j in F} e_S(u_j)

for all nonempty finite F, with the constant independent of |F|, would still suffice. Bounded row energies give r(P_F)<=constant*|F|^(1/(q+1)), hence the frozen SR6 packing criterion, and therefore literal L1 continuity. The new two-entry counterexample does not refute such a bound with a larger constant.

In q=1, repeated use of the binary estimate with constant 2 gives a worst-case quadratic energy budget in |F|, hence linear root growth, which is insufficient. A DIRECT finite-family constant 2 would instead give square-root growth, which is sufficient. These statements must not be conflated.

Even this direct uniform finite-family bound is stronger than necessary: frozen SR8 requires only that every subsequence contain, for every eta>0, some finite nonempty F with r(P_F)<eta|F|. The reviewed p_* criterion is the uniform SR6 asymptotic rate, not an equivalence with SR8.

A second surviving route is ordered rooftop energy continuity for a fixed background (OG6), with estimates depending on that background and the fixed lower reference. The new modulus counterexample rules out uniformity over changing backgrounds using only energy and I, but leaves this fixed-background statement untouched.

Exact stopping point: no original fixed-S strongly convergent row with positive literal ED-data discontinuity has been constructed. No general SR8 finite minorant budget, fixed-S ordered-rooftop continuity estimate, or positive restriction-tail estimate has been proved. C1 remains OPEN.

title: Remaining gates, false formulations, and the exact delta
text:
remaining_gates_and_status.tex \section{Remaining gates, false formulations, and the exact delta}
\label{sec:r11-remaining-gates}

The status of a universal assertion is not changed by
proving a qualified theorem with a specific boundary
class.  Conversely, a counterexample to an unqualified
assertion should not be recorded merely as an open
problem.  The following ledger distinguishes the two.

\subsection{The capacity and unbounded-calculus boundary}

\paragraph{Proved unbounded sector.}
The original arbitrary-background construction now includes
coefficient-finite non-polar closedness on ordinary germs;
compact-sublevel outer quasicontinuity; the exact no-loss
capacity-tail cone; its comparison, domination and
relative uniqueness; all positive power-energy classes;
all-degree curvature recursion and graded first-order
and energy currents; and their precise capacity and
strong-energy continuity statements.
On one original affinoid neighborhood, the new analytic
tester extension compares the full local capacities
on compact cores.
On strict analytic boxes with an extending background,
the finite-mass boundary tester core computes raw
capacity, and the full global $E^1$ Green and energy
geometry hold.
These are \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} results with the
individual assumptions printed in their modules.

\paragraph{General raw and outer capacities: \texttt{OPEN}.}
An unrestricted proof of
$C_S(K;V)=C_S^*(K;V)$ for every compact $K$,
or of raw/outer equality on every Borel set, is not
provided.  The elementary continuity of the outer
regularization on decreasing compact sets was already
frozen and is not the missing assertion.
The remaining weak-limit gate is concrete: for a
locally weakly convergent family of full normalized
original tester measures, one needs control on a
specified compact or Borel set by the raw tester
capacity, rather than merely the outer-capacity
bound inherited on opens.
No infimum over neighborhoods has been interchanged
with a supremum over testers.

The exact raw equality for the finite-mass core
(TC6) concerns two tester families on the same
domain.  The domain comparisons (AL8)--(AL9)
compare two capacities of the same kind.
The strict-gap equality (BC17) and the scalar
coarea estimates concern specified sets.
None of these statements proves the unrestricted
raw/outer assertion.

\paragraph{A single auxiliary energy tail: \texttt{FALSE}.}
The new fixed-tail example (FT2) compares the full
nonlinear capacity of one background with the
linear energy capacity of a particular auxiliary
tail: its point has positive nonlinear capacity
and zero auxiliary energy capacity. The frozen R6
example instead compares the BT and energy capacities
of the same degree-one background and gives a BT-null
compact set of positive energy capacity.
Together they explain why neither identifying
the two polar ideals nor controlling an entire
nonlinear tester family by one fixed linear
form resolves the raw-capacity gate.
They are not counterexamples to raw/outer
regularity itself.

\paragraph{Unrestricted recursion: \texttt{FALSE}.}
The logarithmic example (CR2) has a locally
coefficient-integrable multiplier
$uN_{q-1}$, yet
$D(uN_{q-1})=\delta_o$ while the non-polar
top product is zero.
No-loss and the printed integrability
condition repair that passage; every positive
power class supplies sufficient integrability.
The discarded polar residue cannot be removed
by redefining the measure on its pole after
differentiation.

\paragraph{Unrestricted endpoint continuity: \texttt{FALSE}.}
Uniform $E^\sigma$ energy and capacity convergence
alone do not give critical weighted continuity.
The shell family in (PS7) has a nonzero limiting
weighted atom.
The proved repairs are fixed-tuple tails,
uniform capacity-tail integrability, actual
decreasing lower barriers, or the strong
$E^1$ discrepancy topology with its derived
uniform tails.

\subsection{Poles, envelopes, and admissible representatives}

\paragraph{Complete compact-sublevel pole sets.}
The logarithmic construction gives one actual
representative of each such pole set in every
positive power class, simultaneously for all
allowed extending backgrounds.
This is \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}.
The ambient R2 pole/negligible statements on
their specified exhaustion domains remain
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}.
The unrestricted claim that a relative
capacity-null set must be an ambient or
compact-sublevel complete pole set is
\texttt{FALSE} without nondegeneracy and
domain qualifications.
An appropriate converse with explicit
nondegeneracy, representation and domain
hypotheses remains \texttt{OPEN}.

\paragraph{Ordinary upper regularization: \texttt{FALSE}.}
The all-power boundary-core example (PO1)--(PO7)
retains a common actual lower barrier, finite
mass, unit energies and even an actual
classical solution of the prescribed source.
Its ordinary upper-regularized Perron
supremum nevertheless loses the source.
This is a strengthening of the frozen
proper-support example, not a new proof
of the original bounded failure.

\paragraph{Relative completed envelopes: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}.}
The barrier completion constructs original
closed currents, derivatives and allowed
energy currents before asserting their
unbounded recursive identities.
Its unbounded relative Perron envelope
preserves Borel constraints and a common
source lower bound.
The completed barrier-constrained
variational problem has a unique relative
maximizer, a precise Euler inequality,
optimal weighted-data stability, and a
retraction on its finite-mass operator image.
These are actual existence statements in
an explicitly enlarged Borel potential
class.  They do not claim that every
completed potential has an ambient
classical representative.

\paragraph{Full relative strong completion: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}.}
The first-energy strong space removes the prescribed actual
lower barrier. Uniform deep tails and global weighted tightness
give its complete actual-Borel/current realization. Its full
comparison, domination, strict locality, exact truncation
carriers and finite-mass approximation retain the encoded
strong boundary class. The intrinsic capacity-layer formula
characterizes each power moment of an already constructed
completed member; its strict-gap raw/outer equality still
does not give unrestricted capacity regularity.

The exact intrinsic characterization now requires same-domain
bounded capacitary admissibility of every truncation and a
finite outer first-energy capacity integral. This removes
the need to prescribe a strongly Cauchy defining row, while
retaining a genuine analytic admissibility gate. It also
gives the precise monotone closure theorem. Every nonempty
strong completed family has a relative Perron envelope by
energy minimization over finite maxima, preserving source
lower bounds and Borel upper constraints.

For positive data dominated by a constant times one actual
first-energy top measure, the full strong cone has a unique
variational maximizer, sharp energy bounds and quantitative
data stability. Total source mass at the boundary may be
infinite. Literal datum integrals are proved continuous from
the completed tester estimate before maximization is used.
The source equation remains distinct even in this explicit
dominated class.
Within one fixed dominated interval, the actual completed
operator image is closed for the proved absolute
energy-dual distance. This is an approximation criterion:
it requires approximants already in that operator image
and does not assert that the image fills the interval.

\paragraph{Maximality implies the source equation: \texttt{FALSE}.}
The completed maximizer in (BV13), and even the
unconstrained strong-cone maximizer in (VF13), can
fail the prescribed current equation.
The R10 compact-source rigidity extends through
the new degree-zero current convergence to the
entire strong completion: a uniform first-energy
bound controls local convex Gauss traces by (SO3).
Thus a classical representative is not
the only missing issue: the constrained
admissible variation cone is itself a
substantive equation gate.
The exact proved condition is (BV8).
The current equation follows only under
additional valid variations, as explicitly
stated in the actual-class conditional
corollary.

\subsection{Dirichlet and obstacle problems}

\paragraph{The complete relative linear measure-data problem.}
For an arbitrary original degree-$(n-1,n-1)$
background on the printed affinoid part domain,
every finite signed energy-diffuse Radon datum
has a unique relative renormalized zero-boundary
solution.  Its original current equation,
exact level carriers, bounded-value coarea,
hard-curvature global total-variation convergence,
and reference independence are
\texttt{NEW\_PROVED}.
The signed finite-diffuse obstacle problem
likewise has a unique least majorant and
an exact positive contact reaction, under
the stated finite-curvature obstacle
assumption.
The reaction bound and source stability
are proved before and during the limiting
construction; contact is not inferred
from an uncontrolled weak restriction.

The word zero boundary here denotes the
specified part-space clipping and radiation
conditions.  It does not denote arbitrary
ordinary pointwise boundary values.
Unweighted energy of a measure-data
solution is not always Radon locally;
the explicit positive-data example
proves this assertion \texttt{FALSE}.
The chain and coarea theorems use only
the finite bounded-value energy measures
they actually require.

\paragraph{The nonlinear equation remains appropriately qualified.}
For $q>1$, the new calculus identifies the
derivative of every actual admissible
power-class segment and solves its
relative linearized signed diffuse
problem on a small part domain.
This is a \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY};
it does not realize an arbitrary energy
tangent as a classical variation.

An unrestricted assertion that every
capacity-controlled or finite-dual-energy
datum has an ambient classical solution
for every original $S$ is already
\texttt{FALSE} in the precise remaining-degree-one
moment example, now also in its unbounded
power classes and full strong completion.
The genuinely open nonlinear program is
therefore to specify a valid admissible
data class, potential class and boundary
condition, and prove existence, uniqueness,
comparison and suitable regularity there.
No theorem here removes those three
specifications.

\paragraph{A precise degree-one image criterion.}
For $q=1$ the strong first-energy completion embeds
isometrically as the closed cone $\mathcal C$ in the
original part Hilbert space. The full finite-$H$-dual
source equation is solvable in that cone exactly when
its Riesz vector lies in $\mathcal C$, equivalently
when the stated polar-cone inequalities hold.
The source-functional projection, its sharp stability,
and its exact polar defect are direct Hilbert consequences.
The original smooth core is a difference of actual
finite-mass common-collar potentials, so the cone has
dense linear span. Its properness shows why dense span
does not provide feasible two-sided directions at a
specified maximizer.
This is an exact criterion in the enlarged relative
class, not a constructive classification of all ambient
classical data or an identification of the BT and energy
polar ideals. Pairings with general signed $H$-dual data
remain continuous energy functionals unless their literal
measure interpretation is separately justified.

\subsection{The analytic relation quotient is still separate}

\paragraph{Full GQ: \texttt{OPEN}.}
For every compatible finite actual PS/PL
presentation $e$, the target is still
\[
 e=0\text{ as an actual analytic delta-form}
           \quad\Longrightarrow\quad A_S(e)=0
 \tag{OGQ}
\]
for every fixed original arbitrary $S$,
on every ordinary germ, after all actual
moment refinements, and against all original
complementary tests.
The positive-zero kernel, fixed-moment
top-real-degree signed relations, and the
R8--R10 matroidal, fan and actual analytic
sectors remain frozen inputs.
The new quotient of actual power-class
potentials modulo relative capacity
does not imply (OGQ).
No equality on the full GK delta-test
category has been silently added.

\paragraph{Low-real-degree CTO: \texttt{OPEN}.}
Signed constant-tensor order transfer in
$1<b<r$, including the critical
$b=2<r=3$ range, is not completed by
the new ordinary energy and capacity
identities.  They do not provide an
arbitrary positive lift of an actual
signed analytic relation.
The precise R10 conormal and order
sectors remain as frozen, with their
counterexamples to stronger assertions.

\paragraph{Other frozen open gates.}
$W_{\rm loc}$ density and the Gauss-residue
auxiliary-field quotient remain
\texttt{OPEN}.  They are not inputs to
any R11 new proof.
The old internal R/B/A2 results remain
authorized \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT},
and completed A2 geometric adelic
nefness remains completed.

\subsection{Verification, provenance and continuation}

Every module is retained as exact source,
with independent review records binding
the reviewed SHA256.
The standalone manuscript is generated
from those modules with a recorded source
map; its layout substitutions do not
change mathematics.
The exact midpoint script is an auxiliary
rational normalization check only.
The infinite-degree proof is the finite
binomial argument in (SM3)--(SM7), not
the finite range checked by the script.

Two provenance corrections are explicit.
The R6 polar-ideal separation was
rediscovered independently and excluded
from new-proof counts; its complete
draft remains in the failed-attempt record.
The bounded top weak maximum inequality
was already frozen in R3; R11 adds its
exact all-degree positive level-current
decomposition and the unbounded extension.
The R3/R4 bounded midpoint and constrained
retraction mechanisms are also credited;
R11 supplies the global unbounded domain
and the new sharp constant.

The minimal next tasks are mathematical:
raw weak-limit domination for the full
normalized tester family; a valid source
or variation criterion beyond the now
explicit false unrestricted one; completed
nonlinear contact/equation mechanisms with
their true boundary class; and the
independent full GQ/low-degree CTO gates.
The completed barrier calculus and
finite signed diffuse contact theorem
can be used as new inputs, with all their
domain and representative assumptions
carried forward.

\paragraph{External source used for the new measure-data extension.}
T.~Klimsiak and A.~Rozkosz,
\emph{On the structure of bounded smooth measures
associated with a quasi-regular Dirichlet form},
arXiv:1410.4927v2, Lemma 2.1:
\url{https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.4927}.
The exact finite-zero-energy nest input and
its hypotheses are stated in the main
Dirichlet proof.  General form-theoretic
facts already used in the frozen faithful
energy theory retain that earlier dependency
record; this round does not add an
unidentified PDE existence theorem.

text:
fixed_strict_source_density_nonopenness.tex \section{Fixed all-test strict sources need not have a density neighborhood of solvability}
\label{sec:r17-fixed-strict-source-nonopenness}

\paragraph{Status and precise purpose.}
This section proves a new original-category obstruction at a
\emph{fixed} reference source. It is not a new parameterized existence
theorem. The reference potential already permits both signs of every
original compact smooth scalar direction. Nevertheless arbitrarily
small strictly positive original smooth density changes can leave
the source image of the entire prescribed strong completion.
The proof uses remaining degree one, where a linear moment identity
is valid. No nonlinear Gauss-trace pushforward is asserted.

The new statements have status \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} relative to the
frozen R12--R16 chain, subject to the author-separated audit recorded
in the companion ledger. The existing simultaneous probe, canonical
convex Gauss traces, global Green energy, and literal fixed-source
domination are \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}; they are not reproved as
new. The full completed moment-Laplacian identity itself is already
SO6, following DO6--DO9; the additional $H_0^1$ boundary and
contraction statement below is new. Ordinary real Green theory
and almost-everywhere differentiability of a monotone function
are explicitly identified \texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN} inputs.

\subsection{One allowed original background, with all original tests retained}

Fix the prescribed finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$, its unchanged
absolute value, and an original uniformizer $\pi$. Set
$\lambda=-\log|\pi|>0$ and
\[
 \begin{split}
 X&=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^{2})^{\rm an},\qquad
 t=(\log|T_1|,\log|T_2|),\\
 Q&=(-\lambda,\lambda)^2,\qquad V=t^{-1}(Q),\\
 \beta&=d't_1\wedge d''t_1+d't_2\wedge d''t_2,
 \qquad S=\beta\wedge[X].
 \end{split}
 \tag{FP1}
\]
The closed box lies in the ordinary interior of the original compact
affinoid $t^{-1}([-2\lambda,2\lambda]^2)$, and $S$ extends to a
neighborhood of that larger box. All radii are in the original value
group. This is an allowed symmetric middle-positive separately
$d'$- and $d''$-closed background, here in fact supplied by a smooth
strongly positive form. This additional description is specific to
the counterexample; no general positivity cones are identified.
Here $n=2$, $p=1$, $q=1$, and $d=2$.

Let $\mathscr C$ be the unchanged relative Borel strong completion
with its printed approximation boundary condition, and let
$\mathbb D=\mathscr C-\mathscr C$. Its quadratic mixed energy is
$B$, so $I(a,b)=B(a-b,a-b)$. Write $\mu_u$ for its completed
source measure. Actual defining functions retain boundedness where
used, finite mass, compact strict negative sublevels, and the original
canonical no-loss conditions. No ordinary boundary value is simply
postulated for an arbitrary completed member.

Let $\sigma:Q\to V$ be the original joint Gauss section. Frozen
NF supplies a canonical finite nonpositive convex trace $g_u$ for
each $u\in\mathscr C$. It is additive, homogeneous, locally uniform
under strong convergence, and agrees with $u\circ\sigma$ only
Lebesgue-almost everywhere for a general relative representative.
All arguments below use this canonical trace; no point value of a
Borel class at an outer-null Gauss point is chosen.
The printed NF unit box is replaced by $Q$ using the same proof
after a real affine coordinate rescaling; the original field,
absolute value and moment map are unchanged. Formula (FP6) below
independently fixes the energy normalization in the present coordinates.

\subsection{The degree-one moment equation and its completed zero boundary}

\begin{lemma}[A continuous zero-boundary distribution with an energy bound]
Let $Q\subset\mathbf R^2$ be a bounded open rectangle. Suppose
$g\in C(\overline Q)$, $g|_{\partial Q}=0$, and for some $C<\infty$,
\[
 \left|\int_Qg\,\Delta\varphi\,dx\right|
                   \le C\|\nabla\varphi\|_{L^2(Q)}
                    \quad(\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)).
 \tag{FP2}
\]
Then $g\in H_0^1(Q)$ and $\|\nabla g\|_2\le C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Extend $g$ continuously by zero outside $Q$. Let $Q_\varepsilon$
be inner rectangles exhausting $Q$, and mollify with a nonnegative
even kernel of radius less than half the distance of
$Q_\varepsilon$ to $\partial Q$, obtaining $g_\varepsilon$.
For a smooth test on $Q_\varepsilon$, move the convolution onto
the test in (FP2). Its support stays in $Q$, and convolution
does not increase its $L^2$ gradient norm. Density therefore gives
\[
 \|\Delta g_\varepsilon\|_{H^{-1}(Q_\varepsilon)}\le C,
 \tag{FP3}
\]
where $H_0^1$ is normed by the gradient.

Let $H_\varepsilon$ be the harmonic extension of the smooth
boundary values $g_\varepsilon|_{\partial Q_\varepsilon}$.
Rectangles are regular for the ordinary Dirichlet problem. Equivalently
one may minimize the real Dirichlet energy with those smooth trace
values; the weak maximum principle and the elementary rectangle
barriers give its continuous boundary values. Then
$v_\varepsilon=g_\varepsilon-H_\varepsilon\in
H_0^1(Q_\varepsilon)$ and
$\Delta v_\varepsilon=\Delta g_\varepsilon$. Testing this equality
by $v_\varepsilon$ in (FP3) gives
$\|\nabla v_\varepsilon\|_2\le C$.
Extend $v_\varepsilon$ by zero to $Q$ and extract a weakly
convergent subsequence in $H_0^1(Q)$.

Uniform continuity of the zero extension of $g$ implies
$\sup_{\partial Q_\varepsilon}|g_\varepsilon|\to0$.
The maximum principle gives the same bound for
$\|H_\varepsilon\|_\infty$. Also $g_\varepsilon\to g$ uniformly
on compact subsets. Hence $v_\varepsilon\to g$ locally uniformly,
identifying its weak $H_0^1$ limit with $g$. Weak lower
semicontinuity proves the claimed energy bound. This argument
is the step excluding an uncontrolled harmonic boundary summand.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The completed moment identity retains the real zero boundary]
In (FP1), every $u\in\mathscr C$ satisfies
\[
 g_u\in H_0^1(Q),\qquad
 \|\nabla(g_u-g_v)\|_2^2\le I(u,v)
                              \quad(u,v\in\mathscr C),
 \tag{FP4}
\]
and
\[
                         t_*\mu_u=\Delta g_u
                   \quad\text{as Radon measures on }Q.
 \tag{FP5}
\]
Formula (FP5) is the frozen SO6 identity in this normalization.
The new conclusion is (FP4), including its boundary condition.
In particular, equality of two prescribed original source measures
fixes the corresponding real zero-boundary Poisson equation uniquely.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For an actual bounded admissible potential $a$ and
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$, original current recursion, compact
Stokes and the full original top-form Gauss calibration give
\[
 \begin{split}
 \int_V\varphi(t)\,d\mu_a
  &=\langle aS,D(\varphi\circ t)\rangle
    =\int_Qg_a\Delta\varphi\,dx,\\
 B(a,\varphi\circ t)&=-\int_Qg_a\Delta\varphi\,dx,\qquad
 B(\varphi\circ t,\varphi\circ t)
                         =\int_Q|\nabla\varphi|^2dx.
 \end{split}
 \tag{FP6}
\]
The factor is $(n-1)!=1$ with the unnormalized $\beta$ in (FP1).
The test $\varphi\circ t$ has compact original support because
$t$ is proper over compact subsets of $Q$. It is an exact difference
of admissible actual potentials by frozen HC14--HC15. Consequently
the full difference energy and its Cauchy--Schwarz inequality apply
to it. These identities use actual original tests and the fixed
smooth background, and require no unresolved delta-action quotient.

For two bounded actual admissible potentials $a,b$, put
$h=a-b$ and $g=g_a-g_b$. Each individual convex trace is continuous
in $Q$ and tends uniformly to zero at its boundary: otherwise a
sequence with value at most $-\epsilon$ would lie in the fixed
compact strict negative sublevel of the original potential while
its moments leave every compact subset of $Q$. Thus $g$ extends
continuously by zero to $\partial Q$. Formula (FP6) and the
positive energy matrix give (FP2) with $C=B(h,h)^{1/2}$.
The preceding lemma proves
\[
                 \|\nabla(g_a-g_b)\|_2^2\le B(a-b,a-b).
 \tag{FP7}
\]
In particular each actual trace lies in $H_0^1(Q)$.

Every completed member has a bounded actual strongly defining
row by the frozen clipping diagonal. In degree one, (FP7) makes
its traces Cauchy in $H_0^1(Q)$. Their NF locally uniform limit
is precisely $g_u$, so it is also the $H_0^1$ limit. Applying
this to two rows proves (FP4) with the original completed boundary
condition, rather than imposing a new boundary representative.
Pass in the first line of (FP6) using completed source continuity
on the fixed original compact test and the local convergence of
the traces. This proves (FP5). No expression involving a higher
power of $Dg_u$ has been used.
\end{proof}

\subsection{A real Poisson perturbation that destroys convexity}

We record the real lemma with all hypotheses needed for a possibly
nonsmooth reference trace. The reference Hessian may have a singular
positive part; no smoothness of the reference source density is assumed.

\begin{lemma}[Small smooth density changes of a locally strict convex source]
Let $g\in H_0^1(Q)$ be finite and convex on a rectangle $Q\subset
\mathbf R^2$. Put $\tau=\Delta g\ge0$. Suppose on a nonempty ball
$B\Subset Q$ that
\[
                         \tau\ge c\,dx\quad(c>0).
 \tag{FP8}
\]
There are $k_j\in C_c^\infty(B)$, $0\le k_j\le1$, and positive
$\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ after a subsequence, such that the unique
$H_0^1(Q)$ solution of
\[
                 \Delta v_j=(1+\epsilon_j k_j)\tau
 \tag{FP9}
\]
is not convex. Each $1+\epsilon_jk_j$ lies in $[1,3/2]$ after
discarding finitely many terms.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix a unit direction $e$ and an interior line segment in $B$
parallel to $e$. The convex restriction of $g$ to this segment
has a finite second-order expansion at almost every point:
its right derivative is monotone and is differentiable with finite
derivative almost everywhere; integrating that first-order
expansion gives the second-order expansion of the restriction.
Choose such a point $x_0$, so that explicitly
\[
 g(x_0+se)=g(x_0)+a s+\tfrac12 b s^2+o(s^2),
                         \qquad b\ge0.
\]
Put $A=b+1>0$. Thus $b$ is the second derivative, not the
coefficient of $s^2$. This one-dimensional fact
suffices; no second-order expansion in every direction is needed.
Let $G_Q(x,y)$ be the positive Dirichlet Green function for
$-\Delta$ on $Q$, and put
$K(y)=\partial_{ee,x}G_Q(x_0,y)$ for $y\ne x_0$.
With polar coordinates around $x_0$ and angle measured from $e$,
the fundamental solution and its harmonic correction give
\[
 K(y)=\frac{\cos(2\theta)}{2\pi r^2}+O(1),\qquad
                    r=|y-x_0|\downarrow0.
 \tag{FP10}
\]
Here the correction is uniformly bounded after two $x$ derivatives
on one fixed inner ball: its boundary data stay uniformly bounded
as $y$ ranges in that inner ball, and the maximum principle and
interior harmonic derivative estimate apply. In particular this
statement does not require a smooth boundary at the corners of $Q$.

Choose $R>0$ with $\overline B(x_0,R)\subset B$, small enough
that the leading term in (FP10) dominates the bounded remainder
on the fixed angular sectors $\cos(2\theta)\ge1/2$.
For $\delta_j\downarrow0$ take smooth radial cutoffs $\chi_j$
supported in $\delta_j<r<R$, equal to one on
$2\delta_j\le r\le R/2$, and between zero and one.
Choose a fixed smooth angular function $\zeta$ on the unit circle,
with $0\le\zeta\le1$, supported where $\cos(2\theta)>1/2$,
and equal to one on a smaller nonempty angular arc. Define
\[
 k_j(y)=\chi_j(r)\zeta((y-x_0)/r),
 \qquad k_j=0\text{ off that annulus}.
 \tag{FP11}
\]
These are smooth compact functions, with $0\le k_j\le1$ and
$Kk_j\ge0$ pointwise. On the smaller arc and middle annulus,
(FP10) gives $Kk_j\ge c_1r^{-2}$ for a fixed $c_1>0$.
Thus (FP8) implies
\[
 M_j:=\int_QK(y)k_j(y)\,d\tau(y)
       \ge c_2\log\frac{R}{4\delta_j}\longrightarrow+\infty.
 \tag{FP12}
\]
Any singular positive part of $\tau$ contributes with the same
nonnegative sign. For each fixed $j$, this integral is finite
because its support is compact and separated from $x_0$.

The distribution $k_j\tau$ belongs to $H^{-1}(Q)$: multiplication
of an $H_0^1$ test by the fixed compact smooth $k_j$ is bounded in
$H_0^1$, and $\tau=\Delta g\in H^{-1}$. Let $z_j\in H_0^1(Q)$
be its unique zero-boundary Poisson potential. It is harmonic near
$x_0$, and the Green formula, differentiated on that source-free
ball, gives
\[
                  \partial_{ee}z_j(x_0)=-M_j.
 \tag{FP13}
\]
This formula also holds for the present finite signed measure
on its compact support: convolve it there in $H^{-1}$, use the
smooth-source Green formula, and pass to the limit. The solutions
converge in $H_0^1$; on the source-free ball harmonic interior
estimates give convergence of every derivative, while the smooth
kernel on the compact source support passes through the measure
limit. This justifies (FP13) without pairing a singular kernel
with its pole.

Set $\epsilon_j=A/M_j$ and, if desired, pass to a subsequence
making these numbers decrease. Then $\epsilon_j\to0$ and the
unique solution of (FP9) is $v_j=g+\epsilon_jz_j$. Since
$k_j\tau\ge0$, the weak maximum principle also gives
$z_j\le0$, so this candidate remains nonpositive and retains
the zero boundary; the failed condition is convexity.
Its restriction to the chosen line has a second-order expansion
at $x_0$ with second coefficient $b-A=-1$. A convex function
cannot have such a negative coefficient, by its centered second
difference along $e$. Hence $v_j$ is not convex. Positivity of the density follows
for sufficiently large $j$ from $\epsilon_j<1/2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The fixed original source counterexample}

Say that a bounded actual admissible $w<0$ has the full
two-sided compact test property if
\[
 \text{for every real original compact smooth }\phi
 \text{ there is }s_\phi>0\text{ with }
       w+s\phi\text{ actual admissible whenever }|s|\le s_\phi.
 \tag{FP14}
\]
All actual refinements of $\phi$ are included. This condition is
nonempty: the frozen NP probe $\psi_0$ has it, is continuous and
bounded between $-1$ and zero, has finite mass and all finite
positive power energies, and retains its strict negative-sublevel
and no-loss boundary conditions. It is not a Banach interior claim.

\begin{theorem}[Failure of local density solvability at every such fixed source]
In the one fixed original geometry (FP1), let $w$ be any bounded
actual finite-mass reference with (FP14) and the printed actual
boundary and no-loss hypotheses. Then the following statements hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every nonempty real ball $B\Subset Q$, there are
strictly positive original smooth densities
$f_j=1+\epsilon_j k_j\circ t$, with $k_j\in C_c^\infty(B)$,
such that
\[
  1\le f_j\le\tfrac32,\qquad
  \|f_j-1\|_\infty\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad f_j\mu_w\notin\{\mu_u:u\in\mathscr C\}.
 \tag{FP15}
\]
In particular the reference $w$ is fixed throughout the sequence.
\item Every $f_j\mu_w$ is a positive original Radon datum,
literal and strongly continuous on the entire completed difference
quotient. The data share the same null ideal as $\mu_w$, and
\[
 \|\ell_{f_j\mu_w}-J(w)\|_*
                   \le\|f_j-1\|_\infty\|J(w)\|_*
                       \longrightarrow0.
 \tag{FP16}
\]
They have one common full original tester capacity bound and one
common fixed-source strong $L^1$ modulus.
\item There is also a sequence as in (FP15) which tends to one
in the original smooth compact-open topology on $V$, as well as
uniformly. For this additional assertion the compact supports of
$f_j-1$ escape every compact subset of $V$; no common compact
support is asserted.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First observe why the real lemma applies to the canonical trace
of the \emph{fixed} $w$. Choose a real compact smooth scalar
$\varphi$ equal to $|x|^2/2$ on a neighborhood of
$\overline B$. By properness $\varphi\circ t$ is an original
compact smooth scalar. Property (FP14) makes
$w-s(\varphi\circ t)$ actual psh for some $s>0$. Its canonical

text:
strong_completion_source_obstruction.tex \section{A compact-source obstruction even in the unrestricted strong completion}
\label{sec:r11-strong-completion-source-obstruction}

This section specializes only to the explicit counterexample background
(DO6), with $n\geq2$, $Q=(-1,1)^n$, and remaining degree $q=1$.
The field, norm, analytic space, and original test category are unchanged.
Write $U=t^{-1}(Q)$ and let $\sigma:Q\to U$ be the joint original
Gauss section.  The new potential space is precisely
$\widehat{\mathcal E}^{1}_{\rm str}(U)$ of
Definition~\ref{def:r11-strong-first-energy-completion}.
Its elements need not have an actual common lower barrier or an
ambient classical representative.  Their currents and multipliers
are those already constructed in (IC10)--(IC13).

The frozen inputs are exactly the R6 joint-Gauss convexity and
original calibration, and the R10 compact-source convex rigidity
listed in the power-class obstruction section.  The already proved
actual and fixed-barrier obstructions (DO7) and (BV13) are not
reproved here.  The new issue is whether the energy bound of an
arbitrary strongly Cauchy row still forces a finite convex trace
in its current limit.  The following estimate answers that issue.

\begin{lemma}[Local trace compactness from a first-energy bound]
\label{lem:r11-energy-bounded-convex-trace-compactness}
Let $(u_j)\subset\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(U)$ be actual classical
potentials with $\sup_j e_1(u_j)\leq M<\infty$.
Their finite convex Gauss traces $g_j=u_j\circ\sigma\leq0$ have
uniformly bounded $L^1$ norms on every compact real subbox of $Q$.
They are locally uniformly bounded and locally equicontinuous.
Consequently a subsequence converges locally uniformly on $Q$
to a finite convex function $g\leq0$.
No common pointwise lower barrier is assumed.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} in this precise
original moment example.  The compactness assertion concerns real
convex traces, not an asserted compactness of ambient classical psh
potentials in their original category.

\begin{proof}
The finite-convex-trace argument preceding (DO8) applies separately
to every actual $u_j$: its compact negative sublevels supply one
finite Gauss value, and extended convexity bounded above by zero
then gives finiteness everywhere.  Fix a compact real subbox
$B\Subset Q$ and put $K=\sigma(B)$, a compact ordinary analytic
set.  The normalized smooth original tester
\[
                v_0=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n t_i^2
           \quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
                D(v_0S)=2\sigma_*(dy).
 \tag{SO1}
\]
Let $\rho$ be the strict-box barrier from (TC2).
Choose $A>0$ so that $A\rho<-2$ near $K$ and set
\[
                     \psi=\max(v_0-2,A\rho).
 \tag{SO2}
\]
The exact core construction (TC7)--(TC8), with its harmless
constant rescaling, shows that $\psi$ is an actual bounded
finite-mass member of every positive power class.  In particular
$e_1(\psi)<\infty$, and it agrees with $v_0-2$ near $K$.
Original locality therefore gives
$\mathbf1_K\mu_\psi=2\sigma_*(\mathbf1_Bdy)$.
The global constant-one mixed energy inequality yields
\[
 \int_B(-g_j)\,dy
   =\frac12\int_K(-u_j)\,d\mu_\psi
   \leq\frac12\int_U(-u_j)\,d\mu_\psi
   \leq\frac12M^{1/2}e_1(\psi)^{1/2}.
 \tag{SO3}
\]
Every multiplier in this equation is the previously justified
actual multiplier.  This proves the local $L^1$ bound, including
the case $M=0$.

For completeness, the convex compactness step is elementary.
Fix a compact real set $C\Subset\operatorname{Int}(B)$ and
choose $\delta>0$ such that each Euclidean ball
$B(x,\delta)$ with $x\in C$ lies in $B$.
The functions $h_j=-g_j$ are nonnegative and concave.
For $z\in B(x,\delta/2)$, write $z=(x+y)/2$ with
$y\in B(x,\delta)$.  Concavity gives
$h_j(z)\geq h_j(x)/2$.  Integration implies
\[
 0\leq -g_j(x)
       \leq\frac{2}{\operatorname{vol}(B(0,\delta/2))}
                       \int_B(-g_j)\,dy.
 \tag{SO4}
\]
Thus the traces have uniform two-sided bounds on every compact
interior set.  Apply this bound on a slightly larger compact
set.  On any line through a point of the smaller set, the
monotone secant slopes of a convex function are then bounded
by its oscillation on the larger set divided by the fixed
distance to its boundary.  This gives a uniform Lipschitz
bound on every smaller compact subbox.  A finite-net
subsequence argument and a countable exhaustion yield local
uniform convergence of a subsequence.  Convexity and the
upper bound zero pass to its finite limit.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Strong completion does not create a nonzero compact source]
\label{thm:r11-strong-completed-compact-source-obstruction}
For the precise background just specified, let
$u\in\widehat{\mathcal E}^{1}_{\rm str}(U)$.
If the positive original measure $D(uS)=\widehat N_1(u)$
has tropical pushforward carried by a compact subset of $Q$,
then
\[
                              D(uS)=0.
 \tag{SO5}
\]
In particular, the nonzero positive compact source
$\mu=\sigma_*(\chi\,dy)$ of (DO9) is not $D(uS)$ for
any member of this unrestricted strong completion.
Thus passing from actual power-class potentials to the complete
relative strong first-energy space does not make finite-dual or
capacity-controlled data universally solvable.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as an extension
of the frozen source obstruction to the new strong completion
without an actual lower barrier.  The universal source-solvability
inference being rejected is \texttt{FALSE}.

\begin{proof}
Choose an actual strongly Cauchy defining row $(u_j)$ for $u$.
Its first energies are bounded by (EV9), or (IC2).
The preceding lemma supplies a subsequence of its Gauss traces
converging locally uniformly to a finite convex $g$.
The strong completed calculus gives the original coefficient
convergence $u_jS\to uS$, before applying any tropical test.
Consequently, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(Q)$,
\[
 \begin{split}
 \langle t_*D(uS),\varphi\rangle
   &=\lim_j\langle u_jS,D(\varphi(t))\rangle\\
   &=\lim_j\int_Qg_j\,\Delta\varphi\,dy
     =\int_Qg\,\Delta\varphi\,dy
     =\langle\Delta g,\varphi\rangle.
 \end{split}
 \tag{SO6}
\]
The pullback $\varphi(t)$ is an original compact smooth test:
inverse images of compact real subboxes in this original torus
are compact polyannuli.  Each identity uses the already fixed
all-original calibration.  It does not define the completed
current by a selected toric test subfamily.

The positive measure $\Delta g$ has compact support in $Q$.
The exact frozen R10 convex compact-marginal rigidity theorem,
valid here for $n\geq2$, gives $\Delta g=0$.
Hence $t_*D(uS)=0$.  Positivity makes the original measure zero:
for every compact ordinary $L\subset U$, its mass is at most
the mass of $t^{-1}(t(L))$, which is the zero pushforward
mass of the compact set $t(L)$.  Radon inner regularity
then gives (SO5).

The datum (DO9) is finite, nonzero, compactly supported,
dominated by one half of an actual normalized tester measure,
and has finite energy-dual size, as already proved there.
It contradicts (SO5) if it were a completed source.
No claim is made that this special background exhausts arbitrary
backgrounds; one allowed background suffices to disprove the
unqualified universal source assertion.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The resulting minimal equation gate.}
The strong completion solves a precise nonlinear Cauchy problem
and retains all-original closed curvature currents.  It does
not contain every solution of the larger relative linear
energy problem even when $q=1$.  The surviving convex trace
is an explicit obstruction.  A prospective general nonlinear
Dirichlet theorem must therefore specify an admissible operator
image or a different potential class; neither completion alone
nor a finite datum energy norm supplies the missing equation.
The analytic PS/PL relation quotient and low-real-degree CTO
are separate and are not used in this argument.
