title: A genuine action polar need not have a continuous-form primitive
text:
S22_divisor_action_polars_need_not_have_continuous_form_primitives.tex \section{A genuine action polar need not have a continuous-form primitive}
\label{sec:r24-divisor-polar-primitive-obstruction}

\paragraph{Status and precise failed inference.}
This is a \texttt{FAILED\_ATTEMPT} audit of the automatic-existence
step one might try to add to VP. Automatic supply of the specified
continuous-coefficient primitive is \texttt{FALSE}. We first prove
this for the explicit canonical representing current; the final
exact Hessian probes also exclude any alternative representative
satisfying both VP hypotheses. No uniqueness of current
representatives is assumed. The sufficient implication in VP
is unchanged.
No actual analytic relation with positive carrier seminorm is
constructed, and KC12, CM10 and CTO remain \texttt{OPEN}. This
companion has zero principal-theorem and zero result-family count.
All spaces, currents, smooth tests and compact tubes are over the
original \(K/\mathbf Q_p\) with its fixed absolute value.

Put
\[
 Y=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^2)^{\mathrm{an}},\qquad
 X=Y\times_K\mathbf D,\qquad
 i(y)=(y,0),\qquad p:X\longrightarrow Y,
 \tag{VE24.1}
\]
where \(\mathbf D=\{|T|<1\}\) is the original open unit disc.
Write \(s_j=\log|Z_j|\) for the two coordinates of \(Y\).
The analytic product, rather than a set-theoretic product of points,
is used throughout. The integration current
\(Q=i_*[Y]\) is an allowed original symmetric middle-positive,
separately closed current of degree \((1,1)\) on the pure
three-dimensional space \(X\). Its exact support is
\(F=i(Y)\). For the polar normalization below we use the
whole-domain absolute carrier \(G=X=\operatorname{supp}[X]\).
Thus no identification of the analytic section with a unit-hinge
absolute cap is required; \(Q\) is carried by the allowed \(G\).

Choose nonzero real nonnegative functions \(f,g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R)\),
with \(f\) nonconstant, and define
\[
 \eta_0=f(s_1)g(s_2),\qquad
 \beta_0=f(s_1)g(s_2)\,d's_2\wedge d''s_2.
 \tag{VE24.2}
\]
These are compact original smooth objects on \(Y\): the inverse
image of a compact rectangle of torus norms is compact. The standard
original torus integration calibration gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 I:=\int_Y D\eta_0\wedge\beta_0
 &=\left(\int_{\mathbf R}f''f\,ds_1\right)
        \left(\int_{\mathbf R}g^2\,ds_2\right)\\
 &=-\left(\int_{\mathbf R}(f')^2\,ds_1\right)
        \left(\int_{\mathbf R}g^2\,ds_2\right)<0.
 \end{split}
 \tag{VE24.3}
\]
Only the first diagonal Hessian term survives its wedge with
\(\beta_0\). The signs use the same positive scalar convention
\(D=d'd''\) as VP and the frozen product calibration. In particular,
\(D\eta_0\) is a nonzero original smooth current on \(Y\).

\subsection{The polar has the full original provenance}

Choose a compact original smooth disc cutoff \(\chi_0\), equal
to one near \(T=0\), and put
\(\eta=p^*\eta_0\,\chi_0\in\mathcal A_c^{0,0}(X)\).
For formal degree-two polynomials define
\[
 \Lambda(P)=c\langle\mathcal A_Q(P),\eta\rangle,
 \qquad 0<c\le 1/\max(1,K_\eta),
 \tag{VE24.4}
\]
where \(L\Subset X\) and \(K_\eta<\infty\) are a fixed
carrier-CLN stage and constant furnished by KC4 for this actual
background and test with the full absolute carrier \(G=X\).
KC2 and KC6, or the exact canonical-polar calculation AP1--AP2,
show that \(\Lambda\) is a genuine full unit polar for
\(q^{X,2}_{G,L}\). This quantifies over every
original \(\mathcal D(X)\) function, all three families of
permitted relations, and all actual refinements. It is not a
real-tensor model declared to be a polar.

Its ordinary pure-Hessian representing current is
\[
 T_\Lambda=cD\eta\wedge Q=c\,i_*(D\eta_0).
 \tag{VE24.5}
\]
It has degree \((2,2)\), bidimension \((1,1)\), compact support,
and both separate boundaries zero. For any smooth original
\(u,v\in\mathcal D(X)\), the original signed recursion and
integration by parts give
\[
 \Lambda([u][v])
       =\langle T_\Lambda,u\,Dv\rangle.
 \tag{VE24.6}
\]
The positive sign is the frozen rule
\(\langle D(uR),\eta\rangle=\langle uR,D\eta\rangle\)
for a separately closed current \(R\), here applied to
\(R=Dv\wedge Q\). Thus the first, intrinsic Hessian-representation
hypothesis of VP is satisfied. In particular no unproved local
harmonicity property of abstract polars is being invoked.

\subsection{Shrinking original cutoffs and product calibration}

Choose one smooth real profile \(\rho\) with
\(\rho=1\) on \(( -\infty,-1]\), \(\rho=0\) on \([0,\infty)\).
For integers \(N\ge1\), set
\[
 \chi_N(T)=\rho(\log|T|+N)\quad(T\ne0),\qquad \chi_N(0)=1.
 \tag{VE24.7}
\]
Each \(\chi_N\) is an original compact smooth scalar on the
disc. It is constant on an ordinary neighborhood of zero and
uses the genuine unit \(T\) on its transition annulus. On that
annulus its curvature is
\(\rho''(\log|T|+N)d'\log|T|\wedge d''\log|T|\). Consequently
\[
 \int_{\mathbf D}D\chi_N=0,\qquad
 \|D\chi_N\|_{\rm TV}=M_\rho:=\int_{\mathbf R}|\rho''(u)|\,du.
 \tag{VE24.8}
\]
The supports of \(\chi_N\) lie in \(\{|T|\le e^{-N}\}\).
There is no requirement that these radii lie in \(|K^\times|\).

We shall use the following exact original product calculation. If
\(\tau\) is an original compact smooth top form on the base, then
\[
 \int_{Y\times\mathbf D}p^*\tau\wedge D\chi_N
         =\left(\int_Y\tau\right)\left(\int_{\mathbf D}D\chi_N\right)=0.
 \tag{VE24.9}
\]
The equality is the one-center annular fiber integration in the
frozen SP calibration, equivalently DP10 and DP13 on the compact
support of this separated form. It holds for arbitrary original
base forms, with their actual local moment refinements; the base
need not be replaced by its two-coordinate real image. The same
calculation for the nonnegative annular density \(|\rho''|\)
and a compact positive top form \(\Omega\) on the base gives
mass \(M_\rho\int_Y\Omega\). By the frozen finite coefficient
domination, any finite collection of compact smooth top forms
\(\tau_j\) has such positive controls for its coefficient
variations. Therefore there are finite constants \(M_j\),
independent of \(N\), such that
\[
 \left|\int e\,p^*\tau_j\wedge D\chi_N\right|
       \le M_j\|e\|_{\operatorname{supp}\tau_j\times\{|T|\le e^{-N}\}}.
 \tag{VE24.10}
\]
The product in the supremum denotes the corresponding closed
analytic tube. The multiplier \(e\) may be continuous. Formula
(VE24.10) uses its existing coefficient-Radon measure, not a new
product of currents. Formula (VE24.9) also holds after a fixed
continuous base multiplier: approximate it uniformly on the
compact base support by original smooth scalars and apply this
same bound. This is the exact continuous-test extension used below.

\subsection{No continuous-form primitive, even locally at the section support}

\begin{proposition}[The primitive-existence shortcut fails for a genuine polar]
Let \(y_0\in\operatorname{supp}(D\eta_0)\). On no ordinary
neighborhood \(O\) of \(i(y_0)\) is there a finite expression
\[
                 V=\sum_{j=1}^m a_j\theta_j,
 \qquad a_j\in C(O,\mathbf R),\quad
       \theta_j\in\mathcal A^{1,1}(O),
 \tag{VE24.11}
\]
whose associated ordinary current satisfies
\(D[V]=T_\Lambda|_O\) on every original compact smooth test.
In particular \(T_\Lambda\) has no primitive of the specified
compact continuous-coefficient type VP24.2 on \(X\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Suppose (VE24.11) were given. The inverse image
\(V_0=i^{-1}(O)\) is an ordinary neighborhood of \(y_0\).
By the definition of current support there exists an original
\(\beta\in\mathcal A_c^{1,1}(V_0)\) such that
\[
                         J=\langle D\eta_0,\beta\rangle\ne0.
 \tag{VE24.12}
\]
Choose a compact original affinoid union \(A\Subset V_0\)
whose ordinary interior contains \(\operatorname{supp}\beta\).
Compactness of the actual product over \(A\), and the fact that
\(O\) contains its entire zero section, give \(r>0\) with
\(p^{-1}(A)\cap\{|T|\le r\}\subset O\).
One may first take a fixed larger closed disc and then use the
positive minimum of \(|T|\) on its compact complement of \(O\).
The zero locus of \(T\) in this actual product is exactly the
section. No topology of pairs of analytic points is used.

The exact section-horizontality lemma CC1--CC2, applied to the
finitely many \(\theta_j\), allows a smaller uniform \(r\)
for which, near this compact tube,
\[
                     \theta_j=p^*\theta_j^0,
                \qquad \theta_j^0=i^*\theta_j.
 \tag{VE24.13}
\]
For clarity, this follows from original analytic unit
presentations: every unit \(u\) occurring near the section has
unit restriction \(u_0\), and the ordinary inequality
\(|u-p^*u_0|<|p^*u_0|\) makes their norms equal.
The original forms and all their coefficient expressions thus
become horizontal. A finite compact cover gives one radius.
This is equality of actual original forms, not of a selected
real coefficient array.

For all large \(N\), the test
\(\omega_N=\chi_Np^*\beta\) is compactly supported in \(O\).
Every term in \(D\omega_N\), other than
\(D\chi_N\wedge p^*\beta\), has after wedging with
\(p^*\theta_j^0\) horizontal degree greater than two in at
least one column. For example the two first-derivative terms
have horizontal degrees \((3,2)\) and \((2,3)\), and the
\(\chi_Np^*D\beta\) term has degree \((3,3)\).
They vanish as pullbacks of actual forms on the two-dimensional
base. Thus the full differentiation, including its cutoff terms,
gives
\[
 \begin{split}
 \langle D[V],\omega_N\rangle
 &=\langle[V],D\omega_N\rangle\\
 &=\sum_j\int a_j\,p^*(\theta_j^0\wedge\beta)\wedge D\chi_N.
 \end{split}
 \tag{VE24.14}
\]
There is a positive double-transposition sign. No derivative
of a merely continuous \(a_j\) is introduced.

On the fixed compact tube the continuous function
\(a_j-p^*(i^*a_j)\) is zero on the section. Its supremum on
\(p^{-1}(A)\cap\{|T|\le e^{-N}\}\) tends to zero:
otherwise compact nested closed sets on which its absolute
value is at least some positive constant would meet the zero
section, a contradiction. This proof includes all correlated
points of the original analytic product.

Replace \(a_j\) in (VE24.14) by its horizontal continuous
section trace. The corresponding integral is exactly zero by
(VE24.9) and its continuous-multiplier extension. The error
tends to zero by (VE24.10), because the finitely many base
forms \(\theta_j^0\wedge\beta\) are fixed and compactly
supported. Hence
\[
                       \langle D[V],\omega_N\rangle\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{VE24.15}
\]
On the other hand (VE24.5) and \(\chi_N(0)=1\) give
\[
             \langle T_\Lambda,\omega_N\rangle=cJ\ne0
                    \quad\hbox{for every large }N.
 \tag{VE24.16}
\]
This contradicts the asserted all-original-test equality.
The global primitive in VP24.2 restricts to (VE24.11) near
any point after using its finitely many scalar domains, so it
is excluded as well. The point \(y_0\) exists by (VE24.3).
\end{proof}

\subsection{The same shrinking probes exclude alternative VP representatives}

The preceding contradiction concerned the explicit canonical current.
We now make each of its global detecting tests an exact Hessian test
of the same full polar. This excludes a different current with a VP
primitive without invoking any uniqueness theorem for current
representatives. Choose the already permitted profile \(\rho\)
in VE24.7 to take values in \([0,1]\), and set
\[
 u_N=\chi_Np^*\eta_0,\qquad v=s_2^2/2,
 \qquad u_NDv=\chi_Np^*\beta_0=:\omega_N.
 \tag{VE24.17}
\]
Here \(v\) is a global finite continuous smooth original psh
function; it need not have compact support. The actual test
\(u_NDv\) is compact because \(u_N\) is compact.

For completeness, \(u_N\in\mathcal D(X)\) follows from an
explicit global decomposition. For a nonnegative
\(k\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R)\), choose
\(M\ge\tfrac12\|k''\|_\infty\). Then
\[
 k(s_j)=\bigl(k(s_j)+Ms_j^2\bigr)-Ms_j^2
 \tag{VE24.18}
\]
is a difference of nonnegative original psh functions, since
both profiles are convex in the global unit logarithm. Apply
this to \(f\) and \(g\). For the disc factor put
\[
 q_N=\log\max\{e^{-N-2},|T|\}+N+2\ge0.
 \tag{VE24.19}
\]
It is original continuous psh on the entire disc, including
\(T=0\). For
\(M\ge\tfrac12\|\rho''\|_\infty\) and
\(C\ge\|\rho'\|_\infty\), both real functions
\[
 z\longmapsto\rho(z-2)+Mz^2+Cz,
 \qquad z\longmapsto Mz^2+Cz
 \quad(z\ge0)
 \tag{VE24.20}
\]
are nonnegative, convex and nondecreasing. Their compositions
with \(q_N\) are original psh and differ by exactly \(\chi_N\).
Below the truncation threshold both cutoff descriptions equal
one; above it \(q_N-2=\log|T|+N\). The elementary identity
\[
 ab=\tfrac12\bigl((a+b)^2-a^2-b^2\bigr)
       \qquad(a,b\ge0\hbox{ original psh})
 \tag{VE24.21}
\]
expresses each product as a difference of nonnegative psh
functions. Repeated finite signed expansion, exactly as in
IL1, proves \(u_N\in\mathcal D(X)\). The displayed formula
also makes \(u_N\) original smooth. This proof does not apply
an affinoid compact-smooth-core statement to the unbounded
whole torus; every decomposition is on the unchanged \(X\).

Suppose there were any ordinary current \(T'\) and a finite
compact primitive of the specified VP24.2 type satisfying
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 T'=D[V],\qquad V=\sum_j a_j\xi_j,
 \quad \xi_j\in\mathcal A_c^{1,1}(X),\quad
 a_j\text{ continuous near }\operatorname{supp}\xi_j,\\
 \Lambda([u][w])=\langle T',uDw\rangle
       \quad\text{for all original smooth }u,w\in\mathcal D(X).
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{VE24.22}
\]
Then (VE24.17) and the canonical representation (VE24.6) give
\[
 \langle T',\omega_N\rangle
       =\Lambda([u_N][v])
       =\langle T_\Lambda,\omega_N\rangle=cI\ne0.
 \tag{VE24.23}
\]
But the already proved argument (VE24.13)--(VE24.15), using
the fixed base detector \(\beta_0\), gives
\(\langle D[V],\omega_N\rangle\to0\). If a coefficient
\(a_j\) is initially defined only near the compact support
of \(\xi_j\), multiply it by a compact smooth scalar equal
to one near that support and extend continuously by zero.
This leaves \([V]\) unchanged and permits the same compact
tube argument. Thus (VE24.22) is impossible.

This final step uses only the exact Hessian tests (VE24.17).
It does not assert that all smooth current tests are generated
by Hessian tests, or identify \(T'\) with \(T_\Lambda\).
The universal existential supply of both VP hypotheses is
therefore false for the displayed genuine full polar, even
allowing a different ordinary representing current.

\paragraph{What this does and does not decide.}
The current \(T_\Lambda\) does have the compact singular
primitive \(c\eta Q\), since \(D(c\eta Q)=T_\Lambda\).
It is the finite continuous-coefficient smooth-form class that
fails. Nothing here excludes an appropriately defined singular
primitive interface, nor proves that a different representation
of \(\Lambda\) could not be useful. We do not infer uniqueness
of arbitrary current representatives from Hessian tests.
The local obstruction applies to the explicit canonical current
(VE24.5). The final Hessian-test argument additionally excludes
any global pair of representative and primitive satisfying
(VE24.22).

The background \(Q\) is carried by a proper analytic section;
it is an allowed middle-positive background, not an arbitrary
conormal tensor. The example is not offered as an Abhyankar
model counterexample or as an actual signed PL-zero detected
by a full polar. The purpose is to delimit the sufficient
criterion VP: its two hypotheses cannot always be supplied
together, even in the action-generated situation. A future primitive interface may retain genuine
singular carrier factors such as \(Q\); no theorem producing
such a representation for every full polar is supplied here.

\paragraph{Construction and review roles.}
The polar-duality researcher constructed the section-supported
example, shrinking-test proof and exact global Hessian probes. The root checked the
mechanism, specified the exact provenance and degree guards,
and requested the full product-calibration argument. Both are
constructors. Author-separated review is recorde

title: A global Killing obstruction invisible on every positive angular neighborhood
text:
joint13_punctured_three_fan_killing_obstruction.tex \section{A global Killing obstruction invisible on every positive angular neighborhood}
\label{sec:r13-punctured-three-fan-obstruction}

The following is a supplied finite coefficient example.  It has normal
fan dimension three, positive balancing, connected adjacency through
facets, bounded homogeneous finite-PA primitives on every positive
angular neighborhood, and zero branchwise Saint--Venant defect.  Its
complete global gauge equation is nevertheless inconsistent.  No
realization by an original analytic zero or by an SNC residue model
is asserted.

\subsection{Five rational hyperplanes and one exact stress}

In \(N=\mathbf R^4\), with coordinates \(x_0,x_1,x_2,x_3\), put
\[
 P_i=\ker(x_0+i x_1+i^2x_2+i^3x_3),\qquad 0\leq i\leq4,
 \qquad S_{ij}=P_i\cap P_j.
 \tag{PK1}
\]
Every four defining rows are independent, by the Vandermonde
formula.  Thus every \(P_i\) has dimension three, every
\(S_{ij}\) has dimension two, every triple intersection has
dimension one, and no nonzero point belongs to four of the planes.
Give their union the common fan induced by the five central
hyperplanes, followed by a finite rational simplicial refinement.
Denote this fan by \(\Sigma\).  Retain all five source labels.
The complete plane \(P_i\), with its induced lattice and weight
one, is balanced; therefore their sum is a positive balanced
three-cycle.  Its maximal cones are connected through facets,
since the complete fan in each plane is facet-connected and
every pair of planes meets in a two-plane.

Use the basis
\[
 p_{i1}=(-i,1,0,0),\quad
 p_{i2}=(-i^2,0,1,0),\quad
 p_{i3}=(-i^3,0,0,1)
 \tag{PK2}
\]
of \(P_i\).  For \(\Omega_i\in\bigwedge^2 P_i^*\), let
\(\omega_i\in\mathbf R^3\) be its coefficients on the pairs
\((p_{i1},p_{i2}),(p_{i1},p_{i3}),(p_{i2},p_{i3})\).
A common ordered basis of \(S_{ij}\), symmetric in \(i,j\), is
\[
 \begin{split}
 a_{ij}&=(ij,-i-j,1,0),\\
 b_{ij}&=(ij(i+j),-i^2-ij-j^2,0,1).
 \end{split}
 \tag{PK3}
\]
Consequently
\[
 \Omega_i(a_{ij},b_{ij})
       =\ell_{ij}\cdot\omega_i,
 \qquad
 \ell_{ij}=(i^2+ij+j^2,-i-j,1).
 \tag{PK4}
\]
Define the edge restriction map
\[
 D:(\mathbf R^3)^5\longrightarrow\mathbf R^{10},
 \qquad(D\omega)_{ij}
       =\ell_{ij}\cdot(\omega_i-\omega_j),\quad i<j.
 \tag{PK5}
\]

\begin{lemma}[The complete global edge equation]
\label{lem:r13-five-plane-edge-stress}
The map \(D\) has rank nine.  In the edge order
\(01,02,03,04,12,13,14,23,24,34\), its cokernel is detected by
\[
 s=(1,-3,3,-1,6,-8,3,6,-3,1).
 \tag{PK6}
\]
Thus \(D\omega=c\) has a solution if and only if
\[
                    \sum_{i<j}s_{ij}c_{ij}=0.
 \tag{PK7}
\]
For any subset of at most three plane labels, the corresponding
edge restriction map is surjective.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Set \(r_i=(i^3,-i^2,i)\).  Then
\(\ell_{ij}=(r_i-r_j)/(i-j)\).  The kernel of \(D\) consists
of the families satisfying
\((r_i-r_j)\cdot(\omega_i-\omega_j)=0\) on all edges.
The first four \(r_i\) are affinely independent.  There is a
unique affine map \(r\mapsto Ar+b\) taking their values to
the first four \(\omega_i\).  Put \(v_i=r_i-r_0\) for
\(1\leq i\leq3\).  The six edge equations among these four
vertices say
\(v_i^TAv_i=0\) and
\((v_i-v_j)^TA(v_i-v_j)=0\).  Their symmetric parts imply
\(A+A^T=0\), since the \(v_i\) are a basis.  The four equations
joining the fifth vertex to the first four then give
\[
       (r_4-r_i)\cdot(\omega_4-Ar_4-b)=0,
                          \qquad 0\leq i\leq3.
\]
Those differences span \(\mathbf R^3\), so
\(\omega_4=Ar_4+b\).  Conversely every such alternating
\(A\) and arbitrary \(b\) is in the kernel.  Its dimension
is six, and \(\operatorname{rank}D=15-6=9\).

Let \(\lambda=(1,-4,6,-4,1)\).  The fourth-difference identity
gives \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\) and
\(\sum_i\lambda_i r_i=0\).  Therefore
\[
 \sum_{i<j}\lambda_i\lambda_j
       (r_i-r_j)\cdot(\omega_i-\omega_j)=0.
\]
The coefficients
\(\lambda_i\lambda_j(i-j)/4\) are exactly PK6.  They give
one nonzero left kernel vector; the rank calculation makes
this the whole left kernel, proving PK7.

For at most two labels surjectivity is immediate.  For three
labels \(i<j<k\), the two rows \(\ell_{ij},\ell_{ik}\)
are independent: their last coordinates are one and their
second coordinates are distinct.  Choose \(\omega_i\) with
these two row values \(c_{ij},c_{ik}\).  Choose
\(\omega_j\) with row values zero on \(\ell_{ij}\) and
\(c_{jk}\) on \(\ell_{jk}\), and take \(\omega_k=0\).
These choices solve the three equations.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Finite-PA realization of arbitrary edge data}

Choose, for every ordered pair \(i\ne j\), an alternating form
\(\theta_{ij}\in\bigwedge^2S_{ij}^*\).  Define
\[
 c_{ij}=(\theta_{ij}-\theta_{ji})(a_{ij},b_{ij}),\qquad i<j.
 \tag{PK8}
\]
There is no relation among these ten numbers: one may specify
\(\theta_{ij}\) for \(i<j\) and take \(\theta_{ji}=0\).

\begin{lemma}[Prescribed tangential rotation traces]
\label{lem:r13-plane-trace-realization}
For each \(i\), there is a continuous homogeneous finite-PA
covector field \(b_i:P_i\to P_i^*\), with \(b_i(0)=0\), such that
\[
             b_i(x)|_{S_{ij}}=\theta_{ij}(x,\cdot)
                    \quad(x\in S_{ij},\ j\ne i).
 \tag{PK9}
\]
The fields can use one common finite rational fan refinement.
They have linear closed-cell extensions and bounded first
derivatives.  Their distributional strains
\(Z_i=e(b_i)\) are bounded piecewise constant tensors.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Take a common rational simplicial refinement of the arrangement
fan.  At a ray with a chosen generator \(v\in P_i\), impose
on its covector value the restrictions
\(\theta_{ij}(v,\cdot)\) for all \(j\) such that
\(v\in S_{ij}\).  There are at most two such labels.  With two,
the two planes \(S_{ij},S_{ik}\) intersect in the line
\(\mathbf Rv\), and both prescribed covectors are zero on
that line.  They therefore extend uniquely to a covector on
\(P_i=S_{ij}+S_{ik}\).  With one or no label, choose any
extension.  Use that one value for every cone containing the ray.

On each simplicial cone extend the assigned ray values linearly.
These extensions agree on shared faces and hence give a
continuous homogeneous finite-PA field.  On a cone contained
in \(S_{ij}\), its ray values have exactly the tangential
restriction in PK9.  Linearity proves PK9 on the whole cone.
Every coefficient has a linear extension across its closed cell.
Continuity removes the coefficient-wall jump measure from its
first distributional derivative, giving the assertion about
\(e(b_i)\).
\end{proof}

All tangential strains on \(S_{ij}\) are zero, since PK9 is a
Killing field there.  Thus these prescribed face strains agree
between the source planes.  Moreover every branchwise
Saint--Venant operator vanishes distributionally, including all
coefficient walls and the origin, because \(Z_i=e(b_i)\) on
the entire vector space \(P_i\).

\subsection{Every noncentral local gauge exists; the global one need not}

\begin{theorem}[Local normalized solvability does not force JF8]
\label{thm:r13-positive-angular-not-global-gauge}
For the strains \(Z_i\) constructed above, every nonzero point
of \(|\Sigma|\) has a conical angular neighborhood on which
there is a continuous finite-PA, fully incident-compatible
primitive, with central value zero and a linear radial bound.
A finite collection of these neighborhoods covers the link.

A global continuous finite-PS, fully incident-compatible
primitive of the same strains and central value exists if and
only if PK7 holds.  In particular, the choice
\[
                 c_{01}=1,\qquad c_{ij}=0\text{ otherwise}
 \tag{PK10}
\]
has every stated local primitive but has no global primitive.
Its complete JF7 condition holds on every face, whereas JF8 fails.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Fix a nonzero point \(x\) and let \(I(x)\) be its plane labels.
There are at most three.  A sufficiently small conical angular
neighborhood meets no other source plane.  The last assertion
of the edge-map lemma supplies forms \(\Omega_i\),
\(i\in I(x)\), solving all the edge equations among those
labels.  On this neighborhood use
\[
                       b_i^{\mathrm{loc}}(n)
                                  =b_i(n)-\Omega_i(n,\cdot).
 \tag{PK11}
\]
They have the same strains, vanish at the origin, and have
bounded first derivatives and an \(O(|n|)\) bound.
The edge equations and PK9 say that their tangential
restrictions agree on every \(S_{ij}\).

For completeness, this pairwise statement gives the complete
raw compatibility in this particular arrangement.  For two
planes it is the usual extension criterion on their intersection.
For three, extend the first two compatible covectors to one
covector on \(N=P_i+P_j\).  Its difference from the third
covector vanishes on \(S_{ik}\) and \(S_{jk}\).  These are
distinct two-planes spanning \(P_k\), so the difference is
zero.  Repeated sector copies in one plane use exactly the
same full covector.  Thus all simultaneous incident relations
are satisfied.  Compactness of a finite polyhedral link gives
a finite angular cover; its coefficient and angular subdivisions
can be chosen in common.  This proves the local assertion.

If PK7 holds, choose a global solution of PK5 and use PK11
on all five planes.  The same argument gives full compatibility
away from the origin.  At the origin all covectors are zero.
The JF extension theorem supplies an ambient finite-PA extension.

Conversely suppose a global compatible primitive exists.  On
each whole plane its sector restrictions agree as full covectors
at every internal face.  They therefore define a continuous
finite-PS covector \(g_i\) on \(P_i\).  Its full distributional
strain is \(Z_i\), since no coefficient jump measure is present.
Hence \(b_i-g_i\) has zero strain on the entire plane and is
an affine Killing field.  The common value at zero removes
its translation, leaving one constant form
\(\Omega_i\in\bigwedge^2P_i^*\), independent of all sector
subdivisions.  Compatibility along every \(S_{ij}\) gives
exactly \(D\omega=c\).  The edge-map lemma now forces PK7.
For PK10 its left side is one, a contradiction.

Finally, on a common fan subdivision all the supplied \(b_i\)
are homogeneous linear on each cone.  Every complete raw
incident defect is consequently a fixed normal-linear map on
each closed face.  This is JF7, including its full distributional
Hessian formulation and every internal coefficient wall.  The
inconsistency just proved is precisely the remaining JF8
condition.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The fixed-fan real current is also closed}

Identify a symmetric strain with its real superform of bidegree
\((1,1)\).  Let \(\iota_i:P_i\hookrightarrow N\) be the
closed linear embedding, with the lattice calibration and weight
one already specified.  Define the ambient current
\[
                   \mathcal T=\sum_{i=0}^4\iota_{i*}[Z_i],
                      \qquad D=d'd''.
 \tag{PK12}
\]
Here \([Z_i]\) is the current of the locally bounded intrinsic
form on the entire plane \(P_i\).  Since \(\dim P_i=3\)
and \(\dim N=4\), the ambient current has bidegree \((2,2)\).

\begin{proposition}[Closure against all fixed-fan real smooth tests]
\label{prop:r13-five-plane-coarse-current-closed}
The current \(\mathcal T\) satisfies \(D\mathcal T=0\)
against every compactly supported smooth real superform on
\(N\) of the complementary bidegree.  This remains true for
PK10, although its global compatible strain primitive does not
exist.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On each whole plane, write \(b_i=\sum_j b_{ij}\,dx_j\)
in linear coordinates and put
\[
 \beta_i=\tfrac12\sum_j b_{ij}\,d''x_j,
 \qquad
 \zeta_i=-\tfrac12\sum_j b_{ij}\,d'x_j.
\]
With the usual superform sign convention the full distributional
identity is
\(Z_i=d'\beta_i+d''\zeta_i\).  Its coefficients are those
of the symmetric derivative of \(b_i\); continuity of \(b_i\)
removes first-derivative jump measures.  The bicomplex identities
give \(D[Z_i]=0\), with every further derivative taken in
distributions.  The full plane has no boundary.

For a compactly supported smooth test form on \(N\), its
restriction to \(P_i\) is compactly supported and restriction
commutes with both derivatives.  The definition of current
derivatives therefore gives
\(D\iota_{i*}[Z_i]=\iota_{i*}D[Z_i]=0\).  Summing proves
the proposition.  All coefficient walls are included in this
calculation; no pointwise differentiation across them is used.
\end{proof}

This statement concerns real smooth tests on this fixed fan.
It does not assert an actual analytic current identity on every
original refinement, an analytic zero relation, or equality
against GK delta tests.  It shows that fixed-fan real current
closure plus all the positive angular primitives in the theorem
still does not imply JF8.

\paragraph{Ordinary topology does not remove this coefficient obstruction.}
The link \(X=|\Sigma|\cap S^3\) has
\(H_1(X;\mathbf R)=0\).  Indeed it is the union of five
2-spheres.  When a new sphere is added, its intersection with
the preceding union is a nonempty connected union of great
circles: any two of those circles meet.  On a common finite
triangulation, the Mayer--Vietoris sequence and induction give
zero first homology.  Nevertheless the normalized Killing
coefficient sheaf of KD has a nonzero descent class for PK10.
The obstruction belongs to that varying coefficient sheaf,
not to the constant-coefficient first homology of the link.

\paragraph{Consequence for the analytic program.}
A theorem supplying compatible normalized angular primitives
on one fixed actual tuple proves the local part of the joint
criterion.  To infer its global gauge one must additionally
show that the actual data annihilate the finite Killing stresses,
or prove a geometric vanishing theorem for the actual descent
class.  Positivity, balancing, facet connectivity, bounded radial
regularity, branchwise Saint--Venant compatibility, and local
solvability on every positive ray do not alone imply that
vanishing.  PK10 is a finite coefficient diagnostic; it is not
an actual analytic relation or a counterexample to A1.

title: A quantitative strain gap and the failure of fixed-control approximation on the supplied fan
text:
joint13_killing_stress_L1_gap.tex \section{A quantitative strain gap and the failure of fixed-control approximation on the supplied fan}
\label{sec:r13-killing-stress-l1-gap}

Keep the five planes, trace data, fields \(b_i\), strains \(Z_i\),
and edge stress \(s\) of PK.  Equip \(N=\mathbf R^4\) and its
subspaces with their Euclidean norms.  Write
\[
 B_R^i=P_i\cap B_R(0),\qquad
 D_R^{ij}=S_{ij}\cap B_R(0),\qquad
             \mathfrak s(c)=\sum_{i<j}s_{ij}c_{ij}.
 \tag{KG1}
\]
All tensor-measure total variations below use the Euclidean
Frobenius norm.  Changing to the fixed lattice calibrations
changes only the constants.

The two external analytic inputs are the classical
Korn--Poincare estimate in \(\mathrm{BD}\) and the bounded
\(\mathrm{BD}\) trace map on a bounded Lipschitz domain.
Here \(Eu=\operatorname{sym}Du\) denotes the full distributional
symmetric derivative.  In the form needed on a three-ball,
there is an affine Killing field \(K\) such that
\[
 \|u-K\|_{L^1(B_R)}\leq C R\,|Eu|(B_R).
 \tag{KG2}
\]
The trace estimate on a half-ball is
\[
 \|\gamma u\|_{L^1(\partial B_R^+)}
       \leq C\bigl(R^{-1}\|u\|_{L^1(B_R^+)}
                              +|Eu|(B_R^+)\bigr).
 \tag{KG3}
\]
We use KG2 only for continuous \(\mathrm{BD}\) fields on a
closed ball; hence they are also in \(L^2\).  KG2 follows by
Holder and scaling from the \(L^{3/2}\) estimate stated as
Theorem A.1 in Friedrich's paper cited below.  KG3 follows
by scaling from Babadjian's Theorem 3.2; for a continuous
field its trace is its usual boundary restriction.  No
\(L^1\) estimate for the full gradient is used.

\subsection{The finite Killing stress is stable in the strain-measure norm}

\begin{theorem}[Quantitative obstruction]
\label{thm:r13-strain-measure-gap}
There is a constant \(C>0\), depending only on the fixed
five-plane configuration, such that the following holds.
Let \(g_i\) be continuous covector fields on
\(\overline{B_R^i}\), belonging to \(\mathrm{BD}(B_R^i)\).
Assume that their tangential traces agree on every pair disk:
\[
                  g_i(x)|_{S_{ij}}=g_j(x)|_{S_{ij}}
                           \quad(x\in D_R^{ij}).
 \tag{KG4}
\]
Then
\[
 R^3|\mathfrak s(c)|
       \leq C\sum_{i=0}^4
             |Z_i\,\mathcal L^3-Eg_i|(B_R^i).
 \tag{KG5}
\]
In particular, when \(c_{01}=1\) and the other edge data
are zero, the sum on the right has a strictly positive lower
bound proportional to \(R^3\).  The conclusion applies to
the restrictions of any single smooth ambient covector field.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
First take \(R=1\).  Put
\(u_i=b_i-g_i\) and
\(\eta_i=|Eu_i|(B_1^i)\).  The full identity
\(Eb_i=Z_i\mathcal L^3\) gives exactly the error measure
appearing in KG5.  By KG2 choose
\[
 K_i(x)=k_i+\Omega_i(x,\cdot),\qquad
              \Omega_i\in\bigwedge^2P_i^*,
 \qquad r_i=u_i-K_i,
\]
with \(\|r_i\|_{L^1(B_1^i)}\leq C\eta_i\).
Its symmetric derivative is still \(Eu_i\).
Apply KG3 to either half-ball cut out by \(S_{ij}\).
Restriction can only decrease the \(L^1\) norm and the
variation of the derivative measure, so
\[
       \|r_i|_{D_1^{ij}}\|_{L^1(D_1^{ij})}
                           \leq C_{ij}\eta_i.
 \tag{KG6}
\]
Continuity identifies this trace from either side.  The
finitely many constants can be replaced by their maximum.

Let \(\widehat\theta_{ij}\) be the alternating form on
\(S_{ij}\) with
\(\widehat\theta_{ij}(a_{ij},b_{ij})=1\).  Denote the
coefficient vectors of \(\Omega_i\) by \(\omega_i\), as in
PK2--PK5.  On \(D_1^{ij}\), the common \(g\) trace cancels.
Using PK9 gives the exact identity of tangential covectors
\[
 (r_i-r_j)|_{S_{ij}}
 =\bigl(c_{ij}-(D\omega)_{ij}\bigr)
                 \widehat\theta_{ij}(x,\cdot)
                    -(k_i-k_j)|_{S_{ij}}.
 \tag{KG7}
\]
The disk is symmetric under \(x\mapsto-x\).  For any
linear map \(L\) and constant vector \(a\), the triangle
inequality gives
\[
       \int_{D_1^{ij}}|Lx|\,dx
                     \leq\int_{D_1^{ij}}|Lx-a|\,dx.
 \tag{KG8}
\]
Indeed integrate
\(2|Lx|\leq|Lx-a|+|-Lx-a|\).
The constant
\(\kappa_{ij}=\int_{D_1^{ij}}
                  |\widehat\theta_{ij}(x,\cdot)|\,dx\)
is strictly positive.  KG6--KG8 therefore imply
\[
       |c_{ij}-(D\omega)_{ij}|
                          \leq C'(\eta_i+\eta_j).
 \tag{KG9}
\]
Pair this inequality with the finite stress PK6.  Since
\(s^TD=0\), it gives
\( |\mathfrak s(c)|\leq C\sum_i\eta_i\).
There is no bound or convergence assumption on the translations
\(k_i\) or rotations \(\Omega_i\); the symmetric-disk
argument removes the translations and the stress removes
all rotations.

For general \(R\), replace \(g_i(x)\) on the unit ball by
\(R^{-1}g_i(Rx)\).  The target \(b_i\) is homogeneous of
degree one, and the variation of its strain error rescales
by \(R^{-3}\).  The unit-ball result yields KG5.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Smooth full-exact forms are included}

Let \(a=d'\beta+d''\zeta\) be a smooth real \((1,1)\)-form
on an ambient neighborhood of the closed ball.  Write
\(\beta=\sum p_j\,d''x_j\) and
\(\zeta=\sum q_j\,d'x_j\).  In the usual superform signs,
\[
 a_{ij}=\partial_i p_j-\partial_j q_i,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{sym}a=e(B),
       \qquad B=\sum_j(p_j-q_j)\,dx_j.
 \tag{KG10}
\]
Restriction to a linear plane commutes with this identity.
Consequently KG5 gives
\[
 \sum_i\int_{B_R^i}
       |Z_i-\iota_i^*\operatorname{sym}a|\,d\mathcal L^3
                    \geq C^{-1}R^3|\mathfrak s(c)|.
 \tag{KG11}
\]
This lower bound holds for all such \(a\), without bounds
on their coefficients or derivatives.

\subsection{A fixed finite positive current cannot dominate vanishing errors}

We make the current-order conclusion precise.  Work in an
ambient open neighborhood \(O\) of \(\overline{B_R(0)}\).
For a smooth full-exact \(a\), form the fixed-fan current
\[
 \mathcal E_a=\sum_i\iota_{i*}
       [Z_i-\iota_i^*\operatorname{sym}a].
 \tag{KG12}
\]
Let \(\mathcal Q\) be a fixed real current of bidegree
\((2,2)\) which is nonnegative on compactly supported
strongly positive smooth real \((2,2)\) tests.  For each
fixed constant strongly positive test form, its evaluation
on \(\mathcal Q\) is thus a locally finite positive Radon
measure.  Say that
\(-\epsilon\mathcal Q\leq\mathcal E_a\leq
\epsilon\mathcal Q\) when both differences are
nonnegative on all these tests.  This definition is sufficient
for the result; no identification of the strong, middle and
weak positivity cones is made.

\begin{corollary}[No vanishing fixed-control error on PK10]
\label{cor:r13-no-fixed-control-on-supplied-five-plane-fan}
If \(\mathfrak s(c)\ne0\), there is no sequence of smooth
full-exact \((1,1)\)-forms \(a_j\) and numbers
\(\epsilon_j\downarrow0\) satisfying
\[
             -\epsilon_j\mathcal Q\leq\mathcal E_{a_j}
                                      \leq\epsilon_j\mathcal Q
 \tag{KG13}
\]
on \(O\), for one fixed \(\mathcal Q\) as above.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For each \(P_i\), choose an orthonormal basis of its
three-dimensional tangent space.  The six scalar quadratic
probes in the directions \(e_a\) and \(e_a+e_b\),
\(1\leq a<b\leq3\), determine every symmetric matrix
entry by polarization.  For each direction choose a constant
decomposable positive ambient \((2,2)\)-form whose restriction
to \(P_i\) pairs with that quadratic probe, including its
fixed positive normalization.  Such a form is obtained from
two covectors spanning the perpendicular two-plane and their
double-primed copies.  Write these thirty forms as
\(\Psi_{i\nu}\).

For each \(\Psi_{i\nu}\), KG13 dominates the corresponding
scalar signed measure by
\(\epsilon_j\,\mathcal Q(\Psi_{i\nu})\).
Let
\(A_i=P_i\setminus\bigcup_{k\ne i}P_k\).
The five intrinsic three-dimensional error measures are
mutually singular: their intersections have three-dimensional
measure zero.  Restricting the scalar measure inequality to
\(A_i\) therefore isolates exactly the desired scalar
probe of the \(i\)-th strain error.  No other source plane
contributes on this Borel set.

Choose a nonnegative compact cutoff \(\chi\) in \(O\)
which is one on \(\overline{B_R(0)}\).  Polarization and
finite-dimensional norm comparison give a constant \(C_0\)
such that
\[
 \sum_i\int_{B_R^i}
       |Z_i-\iota_i^*\operatorname{sym}a_j|\,d\mathcal L^3
 \leq C_0\epsilon_j
       \sum_{i,\nu}\langle\mathcal Q,\chi\Psi_{i\nu}\rangle.
 \tag{KG14}
\]
Every term in the finite sum is finite and nonnegative,
and the sum is independent of \(j\).  Its right side tends
to zero, contrary to KG11.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{What this rules out.}
The same fixed supplied fan has all the local primitives and
fixed-fan \(d'd''\)-closure proved in PK, yet even arbitrarily
large smooth ambient full-exact coefficients cannot approach
its strain in the above fixed-positive-control order.  This
is a quantitative obstruction on retained real source planes.
No original analytic zero realizing PK10 has been constructed,
and KG does not refute the original analytic all-refinement
criterion.  Genuine actual unit refinements can change the
incident spaces and the associated stress; that operation is
not represented by a real subdivision of this fixed fan.

\paragraph{Primary analytic sources.}
M. Friedrich, \emph{A Korn--Poincare-type inequality for special
functions of bounded deformation}, arXiv:1503.06755v3,
Theorem A.1, states the classical \(\mathrm{BD}\)
Korn--Poincare estimate used in KG2 in arbitrary dimension.
J.-F. Babadjian, \emph{Traces of functions of bounded deformation},
arXiv:1308.5497v2, Theorem 3.2, proves the bounded trace map
on Lipschitz domains and its agreement with continuous
boundary restrictions.  Only these two analytic estimates
are imported; KG5--KG14 are the finite-configuration and
current-order deductions given here.

title: Graph pullback, the complete wall drift, and a finite core repair
text:
joint13_graph_pullback_wall_drift.tex \section{Graph pullback, the complete wall drift, and a finite core repair}
\label{sec:r13-graph-pullback-wall-drift}

A continuous piecewise-affine coordinate graph can repair a
coefficient obstruction by changing the full incident spaces.
Pulling its primitive back to the old real branch generally
creates normal jumps.  This section records their exact measure,
quantifies the drift required by PK, and separates a universal
real graph repair from the extra source branches of actual units.

\subsection{The full distributional graph chain rule}

Let \(U\subset\mathbf R^d\) be open and let
\(F:U\to\mathbf R^m\) be continuous and affine on each
cell of a finite polyhedral decomposition.  Let
\(B=\sum_{a=1}^m B_a(y)\,dy_a\) be a smooth covector on a
neighborhood of \(F(U)\).  On cell interiors define
\[
 g=F^*B=(DF)^TB(F),\qquad
 A=(DF)^T e(B)(F)\,DF.
 \tag{GD1}
\]
The cellwise field \(g\) is locally bounded and belongs to
\(\mathrm{BD}_{\rm loc}(U)\).  For an internal facet \(H\),
choose the unit normal \(\nu_H\) pointing from its minus
cell to its plus cell.  Continuity of \(F\) gives
\[
             DF^+-DF^-=c_H\otimes\nu_H,
                       \qquad c_H\in\mathbf R^m.
 \tag{GD2}
\]
A common refinement includes every internal facet of every
coordinate, including facets whose individual contributions
subsequently cancel.

\begin{proposition}[The weighted wall measure]
\label{prop:r13-graph-full-strain-chain-rule}
The full distributional symmetric derivative is
\[
 \begin{split}
 Eg&=A\,\mathcal L^d+\mathcal W_{F,B},\\
 \mathcal W_{F,B}
    &=\sum_{a=1}^m B_a(F)\,D^2F_a\\
    &=\sum_H\langle B(F),c_H\rangle\,
             \nu_H\otimes\nu_H\,
                     \mathcal H^{d-1}\!\llcorner H.
 \end{split}
 \tag{GD3}
\]
Multiplication in the middle line is by the continuous
function \(B_a(F)\).  All formulas remain valid when
\(DF\) has deficient rank.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On a cell the ordinary chain rule gives the regular symmetric
derivative \(A\).  The one-sided traces of \(g\) differ by
\[
             g^+-g^-=\langle B(F),c_H\rangle\nu_H.
 \tag{GD4}
\]
The distributional derivative of a piecewise smooth field is
its regular derivative plus its jump tensor with the oriented
facet normal.  Taking the symmetric part of GD4 gives the
last line of GD3.  There are no extra contributions on
intersections of two or more facets: the first derivative of
a locally bounded piecewise smooth field has the displayed
facet measure, and those intersections have zero facet
measure.  Applying the same jump calculation to the
piecewise constant gradient of each scalar \(F_a\) gives
the middle line.  This proves the equality as matrix-valued
measures, with every wall included.  None of the steps
inverts \(DF\).
\end{proof}

For a graph \(F(x)=(x,\phi_1(x),\ldots,\phi_r(x))\),
the old coordinate functions have zero Hessian, so
\[
       \mathcal W_{F,B}
           =\sum_{a=1}^r B_{d+a}(F)\,D^2\phi_a.
 \tag{GD5}
\]
The sum is taken before its total variation.  It is the
joint weighted wall measure, not a collection of unrelated
coordinatewise bounds.

If a wall is rational for a lattice \(\Lambda\), let
\(\nu_0\in\Lambda^*\) be its primitive oriented conormal.
When the gradient jump of a scalar coordinate is
\(q\nu_0\), its Hessian, using the ambient lattice measure,
is
\[
                    q\,\nu_0\otimes\nu_0\,\lambda_H,
 \tag{GD6}
\]
where \(\lambda_H\) is the induced lattice measure on the
wall.  Indeed the quotient of the wall and ambient lattice
covolumes is \(|\nu_0|\), which cancels the conversion
from \(\nu_0\) to the Euclidean unit normal in GD3.
Thus the primitive slope \(q\) and the facet carrier are
both retained.  Formula GD6 is a real lattice normalization;
no analytic source multiplicity is replaced by one.

\subsection{The trace version of the strain gap}

The KG estimate extends to noncontinuous branch fields with
specified tangential traces.  More precisely, let
\(g_i\in\mathrm{BD}(B_R^i)\cap L^2(B_R^i)\).  For each pair \(i,j\),
use the bounded trace map on the two half-balls cut out by
\(S_{ij}\).  Suppose that the tangential restrictions of
both one-sided traces of \(g_i\) and both one-sided traces
of \(g_j\) agree almost everywhere on \(D_R^{ij}\).
Then
\[
 R^3|\mathfrak s(c)|\leq
         C\sum_i|Z_i\mathcal L^3-Eg_i|(B_R^i).
 \tag{GD7}
\]
To prove this, apply the same branchwise Korn--Poincare
projection as in KG.  The half-ball estimate is applied
to either chosen one-sided trace.  The trace of the given
continuous \(b_i\) is its usual value, while the assumed
common tangential traces of \(g_i\) cancel in KG7.  The
symmetric-disk argument and the finite stress pairing are
unchanged.  This proof requires no trace on a codimension-two
set and no continuity of the normal components of \(g_i\).

Now let \(F:|\Sigma|\cap\overline{B_R(0)}\to\mathbf R^m\)
be one continuous finite-PL map, with restrictions \(F_i\)
to the five complete source planes of PK.  Let \(B\) be
smooth on a neighborhood of its compact image.  Write \(A_i\) and
\(\mathcal W_i\) for the regular and wall terms of GD3
on \(P_i\).  The piecewise fields \(g_i=F_i^*B\) satisfy
the trace hypothesis of GD7.  Indeed the two restrictions
of \(F\) agree on \(S_{ij}\); their tangential derivatives
there agree almost everywhere, independently of their
one-sided normal derivatives.  Pairing with the continuous
value \(B(F)\) preserves this equality.

\begin{corollary}[A repair must carry a definite wall drift]
\label{cor:r13-graph-repair-drift-lower-bound}
There is a constant \(C>0\) depending only on the PK
configuration such that
\[
 R^3|\mathfrak s(c)|\leq C\sum_i
       \left(\int_{B_R^i}|Z_i-A_i|\,d\mathcal L^3
                          +|\mathcal W_i|(B_R^i)\right).
 \tag{GD8}
\]
If the refined regular strain pulls back exactly to \(Z_i\)
on every old cell, then
\[
        \sum_i|\mathcal W_i|(B_R^i)
                   \geq C^{-1}R^3|\mathfrak s(c)|.
 \tag{GD9}
\]
The same positive lower bound holds for the limit inferior
of the drift masses when the sum of the regular strain
errors tends to zero.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The pullbacks are locally piecewise smooth, hence belong
to \(\mathrm{BD}\) on the bounded balls, and have the
common tangential traces just checked.  Substitute GD3
into GD7 and use the triangle inequality for measure
variation.  This gives GD8 and its two consequences.
\end{proof}

In particular a graph which is linear on each entire old
source plane has \(\mathcal W_i=0\).  It cannot repair
PK10, even if its ambient space is enlarged.  A piecewise
linear graph can repair it only with nonzero combined
wall drift.  A real subdivision with no change of
coordinate map has zero such drift.

\subsection{An explicit universal real hat-graph repair}

For the particular PK fields there is a concrete graph
repair, before any claim about actual units.  On each
source plane put
\[
                         q(n)=\tfrac12 b_i(n)(n).
 \tag{GD10}
\]
This is one continuous homogeneous piecewise-quadratic
function on \(|\Sigma|\).  On an intersection \(S_{ij}\),
PK9 gives \(b_i(n)(n)=\theta_{ij}(n,n)=0\), so the
values agree between the planes.  On a coefficient cone,
write \(b_i(n)=L_\sigma n\).  Then
\[
                  \operatorname{Hess}(q|_\sigma)
                         =\operatorname{sym}L_\sigma=Z_\sigma.
 \tag{GD11}
\]
This is the regular-cell Hessian; the full Hessian can
also have the wall measures of GD3.

Take a finite common simplicial fan on which \(q\) is
quadratic.  Choose one nonzero rational vector \(v_\rho\)
for each geometric ray, and let \(\phi_\rho\) be its
nodal piecewise-linear coordinate: it takes value one
at \(v_\rho\), value zero at the other selected ray
vectors, and is linear on every cone.  These are
continuous functions on the entire fan.  Define the
ordinary quadratic polynomial
\[
 \begin{split}
 Q(y)&=\sum_\rho q(v_\rho)y_\rho^2\\
 &\quad+\sum_{\{\rho,\rho'\}\text{ spanning a two-face}}
   \bigl(q(v_\rho+v_{\rho'})-q(v_\rho)-q(v_{\rho'})\bigr)
                                      y_\rho y_{\rho'}.
 \end{split}
 \tag{GD12}
\]
Every coefficient is well defined by the common closed-face
values of \(q\).  Polarization in the ray basis of a
simplicial cone proves
\[
                    q=Q((\phi_\rho)_\rho).
 \tag{GD13}
\]
For the graph
\(F(n)=(n,(\phi_\rho(n))_\rho)\), take the smooth ambient
covector \(B=dQ\), with zero old-coordinate components.
It vanishes at the origin and satisfies
\[
                  F^*e(B)|_\sigma=Z_\sigma
 \tag{GD14}
\]
on every old coefficient cone.  It is one ambient covector
on this refined graph, so all of the graph's simultaneous
incident relations hold.  Formula GD9 shows that its old
pullback has unavoidable wall drift when \(\mathfrak s(c)\ne0\).
The graph alone is not asserted to be a balanced actual
source cycle.

\subsection{Actual unit realization on a supplied split SNC core}

There is a finite original-field algebraic construction
which realizes these nodal coordinates on a supplied SNC
core.  Its conclusion deliberately stops at that core.

\begin{lemma}[Simultaneous semilocal boundary generators]
\label{lem:r13-semilocal-boundary-generators}
Let \(V\) be a smooth projective integral variety over the
original finite residue field \(k\), and let
\(D_1,\ldots,D_r\) be distinct prime boundary Cartier
divisors.  Let \(Z\) be any finite set of closed points
meeting every \(D_i\).  There are functions
\(f_1,\ldots,f_r\in k(V)^\times\) and one open
neighborhood of \(Z\) such that
\[
                     \operatorname{div}(f_i)=D_i
                      \quad\hbox{on that neighborhood}.
 \tag{GD15}
\]
In particular
\(\operatorname{ord}_{D_j}(f_i)=\delta_{ij}\) for all
\(i,j\), and every additional zero or pole component
avoids \(Z\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A finite set of points of a projective variety lies in an
affine open: use a sufficiently high very ample power,
surjectivity of evaluation at the finite reduced subscheme,
and a section nonzero at each point.  Work in the semilocal
ring \(A=\mathcal O_{V,Z}\) of such an affine open.
Each invertible ideal \(\mathcal O_V(-D_i)\otimes A\)
is free of rank one.  Explicitly, choose a nonzero generator
in each of its finitely many one-dimensional residue
fibers; the Chinese remainder theorem lifts these choices
to one element \(f_i\) of the ideal.  Nakayama's lemma
at every maximal ideal makes this a generator over \(A\).
As the ideal is embedded in the fraction field \(k(V)\),
this is a nonzero rational function.  Its generating
property holds on an open neighborhood of each point of
\(Z\).  Intersect finitely many such neighborhoods for
all \(i\).  Equality of the invertible ideals gives GD15.
Every \(D_j\) meets that neighborhood, so its generic
order is the stated Kronecker delta.  The assertion about
extra components follows from the same divisor equality.
No extension of \(k\) is used.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Finite actual hat coordinates on the retained core]
\label{cor:r13-actual-hats-on-supplied-snc-core}
Assume the fixed original analytic model germ of R12 TC
is supplied with a split simplicial SNC core on a smooth
projective threefold \(V\) over \(k\).  Suppose its
finitely many retained monomial cones are centered at
triple points of the boundary, with compatible ray labels
\(D_i\), and that its old coordinate map faithfully
parameterizes the geometric core fan.  Use the actual
order vectors of the divisorial valuations as its selected
ray vectors; their old projected vectors need not be
primitive.  Coefficient data on coincident geometric cones
must agree, while all actual source labels and their
calibrations are retained.

There is one finite tuple of actual norm-one units over
the original \(K\), retaining the old coordinates, whose
new moment coordinates, with convention \(-\log|\cdot|\),
equal \(\phi_i\) on every retained
closed old monomial cone, after one common central
shrinking.  Thus any given continuous \(q\) which is quadratic on
each core cone and has polynomial representation GD12 has
the regular-cell identity GD14 on its actual refined
core graph.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let \(Z\) contain all retained triple points.  If necessary,
add one closed point on each boundary component not
already meeting \(Z\).  Apply the semilocal lemma.
At a retained triple point with regular normal parameters
\(z_1,z_2,z_3\), the function \(f_i\) is the corresponding
parameter times a unit if \(D_i\) passes through the
point, and is a unit otherwise.  Its order vector is
therefore exactly the desired nodal vector.

Apply the frozen finite same-field residue-unit lifting
result R6 to the finite list \(f_i\).  The TC monomial
comparison evaluates their unit factors with norm one
on all sufficiently near-central positive monomial
parameters.  The finite list of functions and charts
has one common collar and ordinary central shrinking.
Hence their log values are the stated normal parameters.
Continuity extends these equalities to all closed cone
faces, including commensurable radii.  Retaining the old
coordinates retains their old graded rank, so every
old full-source point remains in the new full source.
These points form the asserted refined core graph.

The normal coefficient one is the actual divisorial
order in GD15.  When an old projected ray has a
nontrivial primitive index, that index remains its
projection index; it is not absorbed into a coefficient
or a source weight.  The polynomial identity GD13 and
the ordinary linear chain rule on every core cone now
give GD14.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The remaining complete-source equation.}
The functions \(f_i\) generally have additional zero and
pole divisors outside \(Z\).  Their new incident branches
and any branches exposed along old double curves remain
in the complete actual refinement.  GD14 proves nothing
about the strain equation on those branches.  To obtain
an actual refinement theorem one must construct or verify
an extension with the correct strains on that entire
new source family, with its labels, weights, primitive
indices and later refinements.  The semilocal lemma does
not supply that extension.  In particular its core graph
cannot replace the absolute cap carrier.  The full
wall drift GD3 and the quantitative lower bound GD9
explain why disregarding those added directions loses
essential data.

\paragraph{Dependencies and scope.}
GD3--GD6 and GD10--GD15 are direct distributional and
finite algebraic calculations.  GD7--GD9 use the reviewed
KG estimate and the same two primary \(\mathrm{BD}\)
inputs.  The conditional analytic core corollary uses
the frozen R6 same-field unit lift and the supplied
R12 TC monomial comparison only on its stated core.
No equality against all original analytic tests or all
GK delta tests is inferred from these real coefficient
identities.

title: A residue-field section is stronger than finite unit lifting
text:
geom13_residue_field_section_obstruction.tex \section{A residue-field section is stronger than finite unit lifting}
\label{sec:r13-residue-field-section-obstruction}

Let \(k\) be the original finite residue field.  Finite
surjectivity from a residue local ring, used in ML and UA,
does not supply a field section preserving all algebraic
relations.  The following example stays over \(k\).

\begin{proposition}[A smooth proper divisor without a rational coefficient-field section]
\label{prop:r13-no-rational-residue-field-section}
There are a smooth projective rational threefold \(V/k\)
and a smooth proper integral divisor \(D\subset V\) such
that the residue map
\[
             \mathcal O_{V,\eta_D}\longrightarrow k(D)
\tag{RE1}
\]
has no \(k\)-algebra section defined on the whole field
\(k(D)\).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Choose the smooth plane cubic \(E\subset\mathbf P^2_k\)
defined by
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Y^2Z=X^3-XZ^2,&\operatorname{char}k\ne2,\\
 Y^2Z+YZ^2=X^3,&\operatorname{char}k=2.
 \end{cases}
\tag{RE2}
\]
In odd characteristic its affine possible singular
points have \(Y=0\) and \(X\in\{0,1,-1\}\);
the derivative in \(X\) is respectively \(1,-2,-2\).
The point at infinity is smooth because its derivative
in \(Z\) is nonzero.  In characteristic two the three
partial derivatives are \(X^2,Z^2,Y^2\), with no
common projective zero.  Thus \(E\) is smooth in
either case, and a smooth plane cubic has genus one.

Put
\[
 V=\mathbf P^2_k\times\mathbf P^1_k,
 \qquad D=E\times\mathbf P^1_k.
\tag{RE3}
\]
These are smooth and projective, and \(D\) is a
Cartier divisor.  Their function fields are
\(k(V)=k(x,y,s)\) and \(k(D)=k(E)(s)\).
If RE1 had a field section, its composition with
the inclusion in \(k(V)\), restricted to \(k(E)\),
would give a \(k\)-embedding
\[
                         k(E)\hookrightarrow k(x,y,s).
\tag{RE4}
\]
It would define a dominant rational map
\(\mathbf P^3_k\dashrightarrow E\).

Base change to an algebraic closure.  Choose two
points in its open domain having distinct images,
and take the projective line through them.  The
restricted rational map on that line is nonconstant.
It induces an inclusion
\(\bar k(E)\subset\bar k(t)\).  The field-theoretic
L\"uroth theorem, valid in every characteristic,
makes this intermediate field rational.  This
contradicts the genus-one property.  Therefore
RE4, and hence the proposed section, cannot exist.
\end{proof}

The proposition refutes the stronger prescription
of choosing all rational residue lifts as one
relation-preserving coefficient-field section.
Every fixed finite list still lifts individually
through RE1, and the ordinary product and finite
strict-comparison arguments of CC, UA and UF are
unaffected.

\begin{corollary}[Two units and one relation need not lift exactly]
\label{cor:r13-finite-relation-no-exact-lift}
Let \(x_E,y_E\in k(E)^\times\subset k(D)^\times\)
be the affine coordinates of RE2.  There are no units
\(X,Y\in\mathcal O_{V,\eta_D}^\times\) reducing to
\(x_E,y_E\) and satisfying the corresponding equation
\[
 \begin{cases}
 Y^2=X^3-X,&\operatorname{char}k\ne2,\\
 Y^2+Y=X^3,&\operatorname{char}k=2.
 \end{cases}
\tag{RE5}
\]
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Such units would define a homomorphism from the
integral affine coordinate ring of \(E\) to \(k(V)\).
Its kernel is prime.  A nonzero prime in this
one-dimensional affine domain is maximal and has
residue field algebraic over \(k\).  This is
incompatible with the transcendental residues
\(x_E,y_E\).  Hence the homomorphism is injective
and extends to \(k(E)\hookrightarrow k(V)\),
contradicting the proof above.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The estimate left outside the core fiber.}
The direct polynomial comparison in UF has
\(|\widehat A-A_0|<1\).  In its completed core
fiber \(|A_0|=1\), which gives the needed relative
strict inequality.  On a different ray a chosen
surface numerator can instead have order \(a>0\),
while the first normal error has order \(m>0\).
The comparison then requires \(a<m\); it need
not follow when \(a\ge m\).  A finite Taylor
cancellation alone supplies only a finite error
order; absent an additional divisibility or
relative bound, it does not control arbitrary
later rays.  The proposition
explains why a universal rational coefficient
section cannot be assumed to remove all such
errors.  It is not a counterexample to finite
controlled correction or to intrinsic descent.

\paragraph{Classical input checked.}
The all-characteristic algebraic form of L\"uroth's
theorem was checked in M.~Musta\c t\u a,
\emph{Lecture 1. Definitions and first examples},
Theorem~2.1 and its algebraic proof on pp.~4--6,
\url{https://public.websites.umich.edu/~mmustata/lecture1_rationality.pdf},
accessed 2026-11-15.  Only that classical field theorem
is imported; the divisor-section obstruction above
is the displayed deduction.

title: An irreducible selector whose norms do not extend across every boundary
text:
geom13_hensel_boundary_nonextension.tex \section{An irreducible selector whose norms do not extend across every boundary}
\label{sec:r13-hensel-boundary-nonextension}

Let \(K\) be the original finite extension of \(\mathbf Q_p\),
with its original absolute value, and let \(k\) be its residue
field.  Work on the original three-dimensional torus with
coordinates \((A,C,S)\).  Let \(y\) be its unit-radius Gauss
point, so its residue field is \(k(a,c,s)\).  Put
\[
 P(V)=V^2-V-A,\qquad Z=C^2-C-A,
 \qquad F(E)=P(C+E)
       =E^2+(2C-1)E+Z.
\tag{HB1}
\]
The zero-slice divisor \(D=\{c^2-c-a=0\}\) in the smooth
residue model is smooth and irreducible.  Indeed its derivative
with respect to \(a\) is \(-1\).  Moreover \(V^2-V-a\) is
irreducible over \(k(a,s)\): a rational root, viewed as a
rational function of \(a\) over \(k(s)\), can have no finite
pole, since a pole of order \(m\) would give one of order
\(2m\) in its square minus itself.  It is therefore a
polynomial in \(a\), whose square minus itself has even
positive degree, or degree zero, and cannot equal \(a\).
The polynomial is separable in every residue characteristic.
Thus HB1 is an actual irreducible etale zero-slice presentation
at the generic point of \(D\); its derivative \(2c-1\) there
is nonzero.

Let \(\mathcal H_F\) be the strict ordinary Hensel domain
HN3, and let
\(\alpha=C+e\) be its selected root.  Since \(A\) is a
unit and the product of the two roots of \(P\) is \(-A\),
\(\alpha\) is an analytic unit on this domain.  At the
generic zero-slice point its residue is the nonzero element
\(c\in k(D)\), so this is one of the allowed finite
surface units.

\begin{proposition}[Two ordinary branches of the selected norm]
\label{prop:r13-hensel-two-ordinary-branches}
The original ordinary open domains
\[
 \mathcal B_0=\{0<|A|<1,\ 0<|C|<1\},\qquad
 \mathcal B_1=\{0<|A|<1,\ |C-1|<1\}
\tag{HB2}
\]
are contained in \(\mathcal H_F\).  At every actual point
of these domains one has
\[
             |\alpha|=|A|\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal B_0,
       \qquad |\alpha|=1\quad\hbox{on }\mathcal B_1.
\tag{HB3}
\]
No extension of the ground field or restriction to a moment
source locus occurs in these identities.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
On \(\mathcal B_0\) one has \(|2C-1|=1\) and
\(|Z|<1\).  On \(\mathcal B_1\), writing \(C=1+W\),
one has \(|2C-1|=|1+2W|=1\) and
\(|Z|=|W+W^2-A|<1\).  Thus HN3 holds on both ordinary
sets, in every residue characteristic.  On the first set,
\(|C|<1\) and \(|e|<1\) imply \(|\alpha|<1\).
The equation \(\alpha^2-\alpha=A\) then gives
\(|\alpha|=|A|\).  On the second set,
\(|\alpha-1|=|C-1+e|<1\), so \(|\alpha|=1\).
\end{proof}

For \(0<r<1\), let \(q_r\) be the actual Gauss point
with radii \((r,1,1)\) in \((A,C,S)\).  For \(0<s<1\)
let \(x_0(r,s)\) be the Gauss point with radii
\((r,s,1)\) in \((A,C,S)\), and let \(x_1(r,s)\) be
the Gauss point with these same radii in \((A,C-1,S)\).
These are points of the original analytic space for all
real \(r,s\) in the displayed intervals, including
commensurable radii.  The Gauss maximum formula gives
\[
 \lim_{s\to1^-}x_0(r,s)=q_r
       =\lim_{s\to1^-}x_1(r,s),
       \qquad \lim_{r\to1^-}q_r=y.
\tag{HB4}
\]
For the first equality, the closed unit discs in the
\(C\)-variable centered at zero and at one have the
same Gauss norm; the two formulas agree on every
polynomial.  Uniform approximation on a fixed affinoid
neighborhood extends this convergence to all analytic
functions.  At \(q_r\), the two summands of \(Z\) of
degree one and two in \(C\) have independent Gauss
monomials, so \(|Z|=1\), and HN3 fails there.

\begin{theorem}[Failure of an entire central continuous extension]
\label{thm:r13-hensel-no-entire-central-continuous-extension}
Let \(U\) be any original ordinary neighborhood of
\(y\), and let \(G\) be any finite tuple of actual
analytic units on \(U\).  There is no continuous
function
\[
                     \Psi:t_G(U)\longrightarrow\mathbf R
\tag{HB5}
\]
such that
\[
             \Psi(t_G(x))=-\log|\alpha(x)|
                     \qquad(x\in U\cap\mathcal H_F).
\tag{HB6}
\]
In particular no finite actual refinement supplies a
continuous piecewise affine extension on the entire
central moment image for this selected norm.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Choose \(r<1\) sufficiently close to one that
\(q_r\in U\).  By HB4, both \(x_i(r,s)\) belong
to \(U\) for all \(s\) sufficiently close to one.
They lie in \(\mathcal B_i\), respectively.  The
actual moment map is continuous, so both moment
families converge to \(t_G(q_r)\).  Equations
HB3 and HB6 would give the two different limiting
values \(-\log r>0\) and zero for the continuous
function HB5 at this same point.  This is impossible.
The argument applies to every finite tuple \(G\),
not only to the coordinates used to exhibit HB4.
\end{proof}

All coefficients of \(P\) have norm at most one
at \(y\), and
\[
                         |\operatorname{Res}(P,V)(y)|
                              =|-A(y)|=1.
\tag{HB7}
\]
Thus the all-conjugate resultant hypotheses of HN14
hold.  The selected logarithm nevertheless lacks the
entire extension in HB5.  There is no contradiction:
its value tends to zero along every approach to
\(y\) in the selected domain, whereas HB4 gives
two different limits at each nearby excluded point
\(q_r\).  Protected continuity on the realized
selected domain, and continuity after adjoining the
single original center, are the precise surviving
statements.  This example refutes the stronger
extension shortcut; it does not obstruct an intrinsic
differential construction using actual local root
domains or a separately justified singular pairing.

title: The quadratic mass threshold for a central residual action
text:
joint13_point_residual_mass_threshold.tex \section{The quadratic mass threshold for a central residual action}
\label{sec:r13-point-residual-mass-threshold}

An ordinary punctured action theorem leaves a current supported
at its central complement.  This note records a quantitative
sufficient condition for removing that residual and the critical
scaling which a singular background can attain.  It concerns the
already defined action of one presentation, as in OL.

\subsection{A fixed-presentation cutoff estimate}

Fix an original ordinary domain, a finite actual coordinate tuple
\(t\), an original compact complementary smooth test \(\eta\),
and an allowed original background \(S\).  Retain the quadratic
return identity which writes the relevant action, up to its fixed
sign, as
\[
                  A=D M_S(Z),\qquad D=d'd''.
\tag{CR1}
\]
The singular full-exact term \(A_0\) in the original decomposition
has not been replaced by a smooth coefficient primitive.  CR1
uses its separately justified scalar-module return identity.

Suppose \(A\) is supported in a relatively closed set \(E\), and
suppose a fixed finite smooth moment map \(t\) has constant value
\(t_0\) on \(E\cap\operatorname{supp}\eta\).  Shrink the fixed
compact test neighborhood so that all cutoffs used below remain
inside the original domain.  Write
\[
 r=|t-t_0|,\qquad
 \rho_\delta=\chi(r/\delta),\qquad
 \chi=1\text{ on }[0,1],\quad \chi=0\text{ on }[2,\infty),
\tag{CR2}
\]
where \(\chi\) is a fixed smooth function, constant near zero.
Although \(r\) need not be smooth at its zero set, \(\rho_\delta\)
is a legitimate original smooth cutoff.  Its value is one on
an ordinary neighborhood of the relevant part of \(E\).
Neither injectivity of \(t\) nor exhaustion of \(E\) by its
zero fiber is needed for the estimate.

Assume the retained degree-one positive-module order estimate
for the represented bounded tensor \(Z\), and fix a positive
control \(Q\) with \(\pm[Z]\le C Q\) on this presentation.
Choose one positive complementary dominator \(\Xi_\eta\) for
the finitely many coefficient forms obtained from \(\eta\),
\(d'\eta\), \(d''\eta\), and \(D\eta\) by adjoining the
coordinate differentials of \(t\).  This is the ordinary finite
coefficient domination used in the retained order interface.
In particular it is chosen after the fixed test and before
\(\delta\).  Let
\[
                    \mu_{S,\eta}=Q\wedge S\wedge\Xi_\eta
\tag{CR3}
\]
denote its finite positive top-degree measure on the compact
test neighborhood.  The existence and positivity of this
measure are part of the displayed module hypotheses, rather
than an identification of the different positivity cones.

\begin{proposition}[Second-order residual bound]
\label{prop:r13-quadratic-residual-mass-threshold}
For \(0<\delta<1\),
\[
 |\langle A,\eta\rangle|
       \le C_\eta\delta^{-2}
            \mu_{S,\eta}\bigl(\operatorname{supp}\eta
                                  \cap\{r\le2\delta\}\bigr).
\tag{CR4}
\]
Consequently the sufficient condition
\[
  \mu_{S,\eta}\bigl(\operatorname{supp}\eta
                      \cap\{r\le2\delta\}\bigr)=o(\delta^2)
\tag{CR5}
\]
removes this residual pairing.  If CR5 holds for every allowed
original \(S\) and every original test, in their actual finite
presentations, then the punctured action identity extends
across \(E\) with those same quantifiers.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Ordinary locality and the support condition give
\[
 \langle A,\eta\rangle
   =\langle A,\rho_\delta\eta\rangle
   =\langle M_S(Z),D(\rho_\delta\eta)\rangle,
\tag{CR6}
\]
with the harmless fixed current sign suppressed.  The full
Leibniz rule contains the four types
\[
 \rho_\delta D\eta,\qquad
 d'\rho_\delta\wedge d''\eta,\qquad
 d''\rho_\delta\wedge d'\eta,\qquad
 D\rho_\delta\wedge\eta.
\tag{CR7}
\]
Their coefficient bounds in the fixed coordinates are,
respectively, \(C_\eta\), \(C_\eta\delta^{-1}\),
\(C_\eta\delta^{-1}\), and \(C_\eta\delta^{-2}\).
All are supported in \(\operatorname{supp}\eta\cap\{r\le2\delta\}\).
The finite positive domination and \(\pm[Z]\le C Q\)
therefore give CR4.  This proof includes the mixed terms
in CR7.  It does not restrict a current to a radial line.
Taking \(\delta\downarrow0\) under CR5 gives the stated
conclusions.  Each later actual refinement merely gives
another legal instance of the same original order estimate;
no new test class is inferred.
\end{proof}

The assertion is conditional on CR5.  A finite radial fiber
may contain additional points away from \(E\); their mass
also appears in CR4.  The estimate does not discard them
using the vanishing of the action there.  Proving a better
carrier estimate, or using a different family of original
cutoffs, is a separate way to improve CR4.

\subsection{A closed positive background can attain the critical rate}

The rate in CR5 does not follow solely from bounded finite-PS
coefficients, separate closedness and positivity of \(S\),
and point support of \(D M_S(Z)\).  The following supplied
real example retains all of those latter properties.

Use real superforms on \(\mathbf R^3\) with coordinates
\((x,y,z)\).  Let \(H=\{z=0\}\), let \(S=[H]\) be its
positive integration current of bidegree \((1,1)\), and set
\[
 Z=\tfrac12{\bf1}_{\{x>0,y>0\}}
                   (d'x\wedge d''y+d'y\wedge d''x).
\tag{CR8}
\]
Give all coefficient faces their tangential pullbacks.  This
is a bounded finite closed-cell PS tensor with compatible
face pullbacks: on a face contained in \(x=0\) or \(y=0\)
both terms pull back to zero.  The full plane \(H\) is
separately \(d'\)- and \(d''\)-closed, and \([H]\) is
positive for all the usual positivity tests in this degree.
The facewise product in this example is simply
\(M_S(Z)=\iota_*[\iota^*Z]\), where \(\iota:H\hookrightarrow
\mathbf R^3\).

Normalize the positive supervolume on \(H\) by
\(d'x\wedge d''x\wedge d'y\wedge d''y\).  Direct
distributional differentiation gives
\[
               D M_S(Z)=-\delta_0.
\tag{CR9}
\]
Indeed the cross entry of the symmetric coefficient matrix
is \(Z_{xy}=\tfrac12{\bf1}_{x>0}{\bf1}_{y>0}\), while
its two diagonal entries vanish.  In these conventions the
coefficient of \(D[Z]\) on the plane is
\(\partial_y^2 Z_{xx}+\partial_x^2Z_{yy}
             -2\partial_x\partial_y Z_{xy}\), which is
\(-\delta_{(0,0)}\).  The proper linear inclusion commutes
with these distributional derivatives, proving CR9.

For the ordinary Euclidean positive coefficient control,
the measure CR3 on \(H\) is a positive constant multiple
of its two-dimensional area.  Therefore
\[
                   \mu_{S,\eta}(B_\delta(0))\asymp\delta^2
\tag{CR10}
\]
when the fixed test is nonzero near the origin.  The
second-derivative factor in CR4 is exactly critical.

This example does not come from an actual analytic-zero
relation.  Its ambient \(D[Z]\) is nonzero on the
\(z\)-axis, so it does not satisfy the original ambient
closed-current input either.  Its conclusion is exactly
that bounded coefficients and a closed positive background
do not supply a general point-support removal theorem.
The missing original-range input must use the actual-zero
structure, a stronger background mass estimate, or an exact
residual pairing argument.  The local positive-face and
punctured identities alone do not provide that input.

\paragraph{Sources and scope.}
The analytic premises are the retained QA scalar-module
return and the fixed-presentation positive order interface,
as used in NSA12, together with ordinary locality OL3.
CR4 and the real computation CR8--CR10 are the new elementary
deductions.  No support theorem for general currents, no
ordinary-to-GK passage, and no analytic realization of the
real example is asserted.
