title: Why countably many Radon probes cannot recover full original capacity
text:
countable_measure_capacity_obstruction.tex \section{Why countably many Radon probes cannot recover full original capacity}
\label{sec:r12-countable-measure-capacity-obstruction}

The exact energy-normalized capacity in the preceding section is
controlled by one original Radon measure. Its null ideal is therefore
different in nature from the full original tester capacity. The
following all-dimensional example proves that the distinction cannot
in general be removed by replacing that measure by a countable family.
This is a counterexample within the allowed background class, not a
restriction on the backgrounds of the positive theorems.

Fix integers $n\geq q\geq1$ and a real number $L>0$. Work over the
original finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$ with its unchanged absolute
value. On $X=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^n)^{\rm an}$ put
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 t_i=\log|T_i|,\qquad
 V=\{x:-L<t_i(x)<L\text{ for }1\leq i\leq n\},\\
 Y=\{T_{q+1}=\cdots=T_n=1\},\qquad R=[Y]|_V.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{CM1}
\]
If $q=n$, $Y=X$. The current $R$ is an original symmetric strongly
positive, hence middle-positive, separately closed current of degree
$(n-q,n-q)$. It extends across the closed box. Taking a larger compact
polyannulus supplies the precise strict-box hypothesis. In particular
no original field, absolute value or boundary convention has changed.

For $a\in(-L,L)^q$, denote by $x_a$ the original Gauss point of $Y$
with radii $(e^{a_1},\ldots,e^{a_q})$. These points exist for arbitrary
real $a$, without a value-group or algebraic-closure assumption.
The map $a\mapsto x_a$ is a continuous injection. Define on the
whole original domain $V$
\[
                      h_a=\frac{1}{2L}
                                  \max_{1\leq i\leq q}|t_i-a_i|.
 \tag{CM2}
\]

\begin{lemma}[A full original normalized tester at every Gauss point]
\label{lem:r12-gauss-singleton-full-capacity}
The function $h_a$ is an original continuous classical psh function
with $0\leq h_a\leq1$ on $V$. Its full original top current is
\[
                         (Dh_a)^q\wedge R=L^{-q}\delta_{x_a}.
 \tag{CM3}
\]
Consequently
\[
             C_R(\{x_a\};V)\geq L^{-q},\qquad
             C_R^*(\{x_a\};V)\geq L^{-q}.
 \tag{CM4}
\]
These are assertions for the unrestricted original normalized tester
family on the whole $V$, not for a fixed finite presentation class.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of the
frozen original bounded BT calculus, its integration-current
projection formula, and the elementary toric convex PL calibration.
The explicit calibration below fixes its normalization. It is not a
new instance of the arbitrary-background analytic relation quotient.
The exact frozen torus locator is R6
\path{sections/capacity_gauss_convex_reduction.tex},
\texttt{eq:r6-toric-convex-laplacian}, whose source SHA256 is
\texttt{2ab2277e81fdad829815f0fe30dc6e921f1d0d8c1fb70de71b718fe4f9d83e38}.
It explicitly distinguishes the all-original-test toric identity
from a mere pushforward identity. The original real-radius
calibration is also recorded in R6
\path{sections/capacity_laminar_graphs.tex},
\texttt{eq:r6-arbitrary-radius-capacity}. The targeted nested
archive and source checks are retained in
\path{checks/targeted_r6_calibration.json}.

\begin{proof}
The function in (CM2) is the pullback of a convex real PL function
under an actual original unit moment. Convex smoothing and the frozen
bounded uniform convergence theorem make it original classical psh.
For all $x\in V$, $|t_i(x)-a_i|<2L$, which proves its normalization.

On the coordinate subtorus $Y$, the subgradient at $a$ is the
cross-polytope
\[
                  P_a=\operatorname{conv}
                   \left\{\frac{e_i}{2L},-\frac{e_i}{2L}:1\leq i\leq q\right\},
             \qquad \operatorname{vol}(P_a)=\frac{1}{q!L^q}.
 \tag{CM5}
\]
Here is a direct smooth calculation that also checks support on
the full original test sheaf. Put
\[
 F(z)=\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^q
              \bigl(e^{z_i/(2L)}+e^{-z_i/(2L)}\bigr)\right),
       \qquad g_\epsilon(t)=\epsilon F((t-a)/\epsilon).
 \tag{CM5a}
\]
Then $0\leq g_\epsilon-h_a\leq\epsilon\log(2q)$ on the entire
real moment cube. The Hessian of $F$ is the positive definite
covariance matrix of the affinely spanning vectors
$\{\pm e_i/(2L)\}$ with strictly positive exponential weights.
The map $\nabla F$ is a diffeomorphism onto the interior of $P_a$:
for any interior $v$, the strictly convex function $F(z)-v\cdot z$
is coercive, since the support function of $P_a$ exceeds $v\cdot z$
by a positive multiple of $|z|$. It has one critical point;
the positive Hessian gives the smooth inverse. Change of variables
therefore gives
\[
                   \int_{\mathbf R^q}\det(\nabla^2F(z))\,dz
                          =\operatorname{vol}(P_a).
 \tag{CM5b}
\]
Since $\det\nabla^2g_\epsilon(t)
=\epsilon^{-q}\det\nabla^2F((t-a)/\epsilon)$, its finite
measure converges weakly to $\operatorname{vol}(P_a)\delta_a$.
This follows directly by dominated convergence after the displayed
change of scale; no general Monge--Ampere continuity theorem for
unrestricted unbounded potentials is involved.

For completeness the elementary original torus integration formula
has its full-test meaning here. At any point $x$ of the $q$-torus
outside its Gauss skeleton, some Laurent polynomial $f=\sum_m c_mT^m$
satisfies
$|f(x)|<\max_m |c_m|e^{m\cdot t(x)}$. This strict inequality persists
on an ordinary neighborhood. At each point of that neighborhood at
least two monomials attain the displayed maximum, by the ultrametric
inequality. Its moment image thus lies in the tropical hypersurface
of $f$, of real dimension at most $q-1$. Every smooth moment-pulled
$(q,q)$ form vanishes there by the definition of original CLD pullback.
The resulting smooth top measure is therefore carried by the original
Gauss skeleton. On that skeleton canonical torus tropical integration
has weight one and gives, for every compact original smooth scalar
test $\eta$,
\[
  \int_Y \eta\,(Dg_\epsilon)^q
       =q!\int_{(-L,L)^q}\eta(x_t)
                          \det\nabla^2g_\epsilon(t)\,dt.
 \tag{CM5c}
\]
Skeleton support is what makes this an identity on all original
tests, not merely a statement about the moment pushforward.
The normalization agrees with the unit simplex radial shell (PO6).
Now (CM5b), continuity of $t\mapsto\eta(x_t)$ and the uniform
bounded-potential convergence theorem give
$q!\operatorname{vol}(P_a)\eta(x_a)=L^{-q}\eta(x_a)$.
For $q<n$, the frozen integration-current projection formula applies
this same calculation on $Y$ and pushes the Dirac measure into the
original ambient $V$. Thus all original tests and all actual
moment refinements are retained in (CM3).
Using $h_a$ as a permitted normalized tester gives the first
inequality in (CM4); monotonicity of the ordinary-open outer
regularization gives the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[No countable Radon family controls the full capacity-null ideal]
\label{thm:r12-no-countable-radon-capacity-control}
For the allowed data (CM1), let $(\nu_j)_{j\geq1}$ be any countable
family of positive Radon measures on $V$. There is one original
point $x_a$, lying in a fixed ordinary relatively compact window
independent of the measures, such that
\[
            \nu_j(\{x_a\})=0\quad\hbox{for every }j,
                  \qquad C_R^*(\{x_a\};V)\geq L^{-q}>0.
 \tag{CM6}
\]
Hence the full original outer-capacity-null ideal cannot be
characterized as the simultaneous null ideal of countably many
positive Radon measures. In particular, there is no single Radon
measure $\nu$ and function $F:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with
$F(0)=0$ such that
\[
                         C_R^*(A;V)\leq F(\nu(A))
 \tag{CM7}
\]
for every Borel subset of that window.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as an
all-dimensional obstruction to the proposed countable Radon
control mechanism. The proposed universal equivalence and (CM7)
are \texttt{FALSE}.

\begin{proof}
Choose the fixed window
$W=\{-3L/4<t_i<3L/4\ (1\leq i\leq n)\}\Subset V$
and the compact uncountable Gauss set
\[
                    K_G=\{x_a:a\in[-L/2,L/2]^q\}\subset W.
 \tag{CM8}
\]
Each $\nu_j$ is finite on $K_G$. A finite measure has at most
countably many atoms there: for each positive integer $m$, only
finitely many atoms have mass at least $1/m$. Thus the union,
over all $j$, of the atoms of $\nu_j$ in $K_G$ is countable.
Choose $x_a$ outside it. All the vanishing assertions in (CM6)
follow, while (CM4) gives the strictly positive full capacity.
Applying the proposed (CM7) to this singleton would give
$L^{-q}\leq F(0)=0$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Strict null-ideal separation for the parameter energy capacity]
\label{cor:r12-parameter-capacity-strict-null-ideal}
In every $n\geq q\geq1$, choose (CM1) and use the empty parameter
tuple in the parameter finite-energy construction. For any one of
its allowed probes $\psi$, there is a Borel singleton $A\subset W$
such that
\[
                  \mathfrak c_\psi(A)
                    =\mathfrak c_\psi^{\rm o}(A)=0,
                         \qquad C_R^*(A;V)>0.
 \tag{CM9}
\]
The same singleton can be chosen simultaneously for any countable
family of such probes and their energy-normalized capacities.
\end{corollary}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} explicit
strict separation, using the already proved exact null ideal
in (PC12).

\begin{proof}
The empty parameter tuple makes conormality automatic; it does
not change the current $R$. Apply (CM6) to the finite positive
Radon measure $\omega=(D\psi)^q\wedge R$, or to the countable
family of these measures. Formula (PC12) gives precisely the
two zeros in (CM9), whereas (CM4) gives its last inequality.
All resulting capacities still use their explicitly different
admissible families. No comparison of those families has been
suppressed.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{What this does not contradict.}
The geometry-only probe detects specified normal or Jensen defects
by closedness and two-sided original test perturbations; it was
never asserted to dominate every normalized source measure.
Countable cofinality of original smooth test stages is likewise
not countable cofinality of all normalized nonlinear tester
\emph{measures}. The band formulas choose their essential
suprema for each fixed set and parameter control; they do not
claim a single countable list detecting every analytic set.
Thus (CM6) is an obstruction to a particular route to unrestricted
capacity, not a counterexample to its Choquet regularity or to
the analytic PS/PL relation quotient.

title: Null moment fibers and positive duals which are not literal data
text:
null_fibers_and_nonliteral_duals.tex \section{Null moment fibers and positive duals which are not literal data}
\label{sec:r12-null-fibers-nonliteral-duals}

The first part uses precisely the proper original moment and
background factorization (ML12), with $1\leq q<r$:
\[
 t:V\longrightarrow Q\subset\mathbf R^r,\qquad
 S=(t^*\beta_0)^{r-q}\wedge R,\qquad
 \beta_0=\sum_{i=1}^r d'x_i\wedge d''x_i.
 \tag{NF1}
\]
Here $R$ is an arbitrary allowed original symmetric middle-positive
separately closed $(n-r,n-r)$-current. Properness means that the
inverse image of every compact real set is compact in the ordinary
analytic open $V$. All capacities use every normalized original
bounded classical tester on $V$, without restricting its actual
moment refinements. The factorization is a printed hypothesis for
these geometric null-set conclusions, not a property of every $S$.

\begin{lemma}[A closed order-zero supercurrent has no sub-top atom]
\label{lem:r12-closed-current-no-atom}
Let $T$ be an order-zero real supercurrent of bidegree $(q,q)$
on $Q$, with $q<r$ and $d'T=0$. Every coefficient measure of
$T$ has zero mass at each point. In particular, if $T$ is
middle-positive, the positive measure
$T\wedge\beta_0^{r-q}$ has no atoms.
\end{lemma}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of
distributional closedness and the coefficient-measure definition;
the elementary proof is included. Separate $d''$-closedness and
positivity are not needed for the first assertion.

\begin{proof}
Fix $x\in Q$ and write the vector of coefficient measures near
$x$ as its atom at $x$ plus a vector of measures having no atom
there. Let $k=r-q\geq1$, let $\eta$ be any constant form of
degree $(k-1,k)$, and choose $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbf R^r)$.
For small $\epsilon>0$ the compact test
\[
               \varphi_\epsilon(y)\eta
           =\epsilon\varphi((y-x)/\epsilon)\eta
\]
is supported in $Q$. Closedness gives
$\langle T,d'\varphi_\epsilon\wedge\eta\rangle=0$.
The coefficients of $d'\varphi_\epsilon$ are uniformly bounded.
Thus the contribution from the atom-free part tends to zero,
because its variations on these shrinking balls tend to zero.
The contribution of the atom is its pairing with
$d'\varphi(0)\wedge\eta$. Every covector can occur as
$d'\varphi(0)$, and forms $\xi'\wedge\eta$ of these degrees
span the entire complementary coefficient space $(k,k)$.
The atomic tensor therefore pairs to zero with every coefficient
test and is zero. This works at every point.
The trace is a fixed finite linear combination of coefficient
measures, so it has no atom either.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Full original outer capacity vanishes on each proper moment fiber]
\label{thm:r12-null-proper-moment-fibers}
Under (NF1), let $H\Subset Q$ be compact. For sufficiently
small $\epsilon>0$ put
\[
 \omega_H(\epsilon)=
   \sup_{x\in H}\ \sup_{\substack{v\text{ original bounded classical psh on }V\\
                                  0\leq v\leq1}}
     \bigl((Dv)^q\wedge S\bigr)
                           \bigl(t^{-1}(B(x,\epsilon))\bigr).
 \tag{NF2}
\]
This is finite and
\[
                  \lim_{\epsilon\downarrow0}\omega_H(\epsilon)=0.
 \tag{NF3}
\]
Consequently, for every $x\in Q$,
\[
                    C_S^*(t^{-1}\{x\};V)=0.
 \tag{NF4}
\]
The same holds for the inverse image of any countable subset
of $Q$. The conclusions concern the full original capacity
and ordinary open neighborhoods, not a toric-only tester capacity.
No numerical power rate is asserted in (NF3).
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as a
uniform full-tester null-fiber statement in every sub-top
degree. It uses the new positive moment lifts and the frozen
arbitrary-background relative CLN estimate.

\begin{proof}
For every tester in (NF2), its original bounded lift is
\[
             T_v=t_*\bigl((Dv)^q\wedge R\bigr),\qquad
             \nu_v=T_v\wedge\beta_0^{r-q}
                       =t_*\bigl((Dv)^q\wedge S\bigr).
 \tag{NF5}
\]
These are the actual currents and exact unnormalized trace
identity of (ML15)--(ML17). On each compact $H'\Subset Q$,
properness makes $t^{-1}(H')$ compact. The original relative
CLN estimate on a slightly larger compact set, with
$\|v\|_\infty\leq1$, bounds $\nu_v(H')$ uniformly over
the full tester class. This proves finiteness in (NF2).
The trace coefficient lemma (ML4)--(ML5) makes the family
of lifts locally sequentially compact. Every limiting lift
is again positive, symmetric and separately closed.

If (NF3) failed, there would be $\delta>0$,
$\epsilon_j\downarrow0$, $x_j\in H$, and normalized
testers $v_j$ with
$\nu_{v_j}(B(x_j,\epsilon_j))\geq\delta$.
After subsequences, $x_j\to x\in H$ and $T_{v_j}\to T$
locally on all real tests. Its trace $\nu$ is the local vague
limit of $\nu_{v_j}$. For any sufficiently small fixed
$\rho>0$, eventually
$B(x_j,\epsilon_j)\subset\overline B(x,\rho)\Subset Q$.
Portmanteau on this compact set gives
\[
      \delta\leq\limsup_j\nu_{v_j}(\overline B(x,\rho))
                              \leq\nu(\overline B(x,\rho)).
\]
Letting $\rho\downarrow0$ gives $\nu\{x\}\geq\delta$,
contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:r12-closed-current-no-atom}.
This proves the uniform assertion.

The sets $t^{-1}(B(x,\epsilon))$ are ordinary open
neighborhoods of the compact fiber $t^{-1}\{x\}$.
Their raw capacities are exactly the inner supremum in
(NF2). Taking their decreasing numerical bound in the
definition of outer capacity proves (NF4). Countable
subadditivity of the frozen outer capacity gives the last
assertion. Neither a Radon disintegration over residue
fields nor a change of the original field has occurred.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Canonical convex traces of the complete energy class}

For the remainder take the allowed original example
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 X=(\mathbf G_{m,K}^{r})^{\rm an},\quad
 Q=(-1,1)^r,\quad V=t^{-1}(Q),\quad t_i=\log|T_i|,\\
 1\leq q<r,\quad S=\beta^{r-q}\wedge[V],\quad
 \beta=\sum_i d't_i\wedge d''t_i,\quad
 \sigma:Q\longrightarrow V\text{ the original joint Gauss section}.
 \end{gathered}
 \tag{NF6}
\]
These data satisfy (ED1) and (NF1). The frozen R6
\texttt{lem:r6-joint-gauss-convexity}, used in R11
\texttt{comparison/power\_class\_source\_obstruction.tex}
before the choice of its background, says that a bounded
original classical psh potential has a finite convex
restriction to $\sigma(Q)$. That assertion is independent
of the remaining degree $q$. We use it as an exact
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}; no nonlinear identity between
a Gauss trace Hessian and the original top measure is used.

\begin{proposition}[All-degree completed Gauss traces and point evaluation]
\label{prop:r12-completed-gauss-evaluation}
Every $u\in\mathscr C$ for (NF6) has a canonical finite
nonpositive continuous convex function $g_u$ on $Q$.
It is the locally uniform limit of the Gauss traces of any
actual bounded strong defining row. It agrees with the
chosen relative Borel representative $u\circ\sigma$ only
Lebesgue-almost everywhere, not necessarily at every point.

The assignment is additive and positively homogeneous on
$\mathscr C$, and extends linearly to $\mathbb D_S$.
For each $x\in Q$, the formula
\[
                         \ell_x(u)=-g_u(x)
 \tag{NF7}
\]
defines an order-reversing functional in
$\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*$. For every original compact
smooth scalar $\phi$ on $V$,
\[
                              \ell_x(\phi)=-\phi(\sigma(x)).
 \tag{NF8}
\]
Nevertheless this functional is not literal integration
against a Radon measure on all relative Borel representatives
in $\mathbb D_S$.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} for the
full-degree strong class and the nonliteral positive dual
phenomenon. The old bounded Gauss convexity is not recounted
as a new result.

\begin{proof}
Fix real compact sets $H\Subset\operatorname{Int}H'\Subset Q$.
Patch the quadratic $|t|^2/2-C$ to a large multiple of the
strict-box barrier, as in (ML25), to obtain an actual
bounded first-energy potential $\psi$ equal to that quadratic
on $t^{-1}(H')$. All factors are unnormalized, so locality
and the original torus calibration give
\[
           \mathbf1_{t^{-1}(H')}\mu_\psi
                   =\mathbf1_{t^{-1}(H')}\beta^r\wedge[V]
                   =r!\,\sigma_*(\mathbf1_{H'}\,dx).
 \tag{NF9}
\]
For any actual bounded first-energy potential $a$,
the mixed energy inequality implies
\[
              \int_{H'}(-a\circ\sigma)\,dx
                          \leq\frac{r(\psi)^q}{r!}\,r(a).
 \tag{NF10}
\]
For two such potentials, the completed tester estimate
(EV1) controls their trace difference in $L^1(H')$ by
a quantity tending to zero under strong convergence on
an energy-bounded set.

We recall explicitly the elementary convex compactness step.
If $g\leq0$ is finite convex on a ball $B(x,2\rho)$,
then $-g$ is nonnegative and concave. For
$y=(x+z)/2\in B(x,\rho)$, concavity gives
$-g(y)\geq(-g(x))/2$. Hence
$-g(x)\leq2\operatorname{vol}(B(x,\rho))^{-1}
\int_{B(x,\rho)}(-g)$. An $L^1$ bound on a larger
compact set therefore bounds $|g|$ on an interior compact
set. Secant-slope estimates for convex functions then give
a uniform Lipschitz bound on a still smaller compact set.
Thus an $L^1_{\rm loc}$-Cauchy row of these convex functions
converges locally uniformly to one finite continuous convex
function: compactness gives subsequential limits, and its
$L^1$ limit makes them identical.

Choose an actual bounded strongly defining row for $u$;
such a row is supplied by the R11 clipping diagonal.
The traces are convex by the frozen input, are locally
$L^1$-bounded by (NF10), and are $L^1$-Cauchy by (EV1).
The preceding argument defines $g_u$ and proves independence
of the row. Their $L^1(\mu_\psi)$ convergence to the
relative Borel class, using (NF9), proves the almost-everywhere
identification in the statement. Exact cone addition and
homogeneity, followed by local $L^1$ limits, give the stated
linearity. Equal Borel difference presentations give equal
traces almost everywhere, hence everywhere by continuity.

The point bound from (NF10) yields, for each fixed $x$,
\[
                     0\leq-g_u(x)\leq C_x r(u),
 \tag{NF11}
\]
with a finite constant independent of $u$. Extending by
differences and infimizing proves boundedness of $\ell_x$
on $\mathbb D_S$. If $h=a-b\succeq0$, its relative
exceptional set is $\mu_\psi$-null. Thus
$g_a-g_b\geq0$ almost everywhere on each core, and continuity
makes the inequality hold at every point. This proves order
reversal. For a strongly convergent cone row, (EV1) and
(NF9) again give local $L^1$ convergence of its convex
traces; the uniform convex bounds give local uniform
convergence. Consequently $\ell_x$ is strongly continuous.

The all-degree original test decomposition (HC14)--(HC15)
writes $\phi=a-b$ as an exact difference of actual bounded
finite-mass common-collar potentials. Their actual Gauss
traces give (NF8), including every refined non-toric original
test. In particular any Radon measure giving the same
original test restriction must be $\delta_{\sigma(x)}$.
But (NF4) makes $\{\sigma(x)\}$ outer-capacity null.
Changing a Borel representative at this point does not
change its class, whereas literal integration against this
Dirac measure changes. For example, change the value of
the strictly negative patched $\psi$ there to zero.
Thus the functional cannot be literal Radon integration
on all representatives of $\mathbb D_S$. This does not
conflict with its canonical-trace definition.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Literal positive data are not closed in the energy dual norm]
\label{thm:r12-literal-dual-data-not-closed}
In (NF6), for every $x\in Q$ there are finite positive Radon
measures $\mu_\epsilon$, each dominated by a finite constant
times one actual bounded first-energy source, such that
their literal integration functionals satisfy
\[
               \|\ell_{\mu_\epsilon}-\ell_x\|_*
                                      \leq C_x'\epsilon\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{NF12}
\]
All these functionals and their limit are order reversing
and strongly continuous. The limit is not a literal Radon
datum on the relative Borel quotient. The same measures
converge on every original compact smooth scalar test to
$\delta_{\sigma(x)}$, which charges a full outer-capacity
null set.

This does not contradict closedness of $J(\mathscr C)$:
the approximating data here are not source functionals.
Their nonzero compact tropical carriers already exclude
that possibility by (ML20).
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED}} as a
counterexample to the blanket identification of the positive
strong energy dual with literal finite-energy Radon data.
That identification, and norm-closedness of the literal
positive datum class without a uniform diffuseness gate,
are \texttt{FALSE}.

\begin{proof}
Choose a nonnegative smooth probability density
$\theta_\epsilon$ supported in $B(x,\epsilon)\Subset Q$
and set $\mu_\epsilon=\sigma_*(\theta_\epsilon\,dx)$.
On one fixed larger compact core, (NF9) gives
$\mu_\epsilon\leq(\|\theta_\epsilon\|_\infty/r!)\mu_\psi$.
The mixed energy inequality and (EV1) therefore make
each a literal member of $\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*$.
For $u\in\mathscr C$ with $r(u)\leq1$, the proof of
(NF11) also gives a common Lipschitz constant for $g_u$
on this core. The almost-everywhere identification of the
representative gives
\[
 \left|\ell_{\mu_\epsilon}(u)-\ell_x(u)\right|
       =\left|\int(g_u(x)-g_u(y))\theta_\epsilon(y)\,dy\right|
       \leq C_x'\epsilon.
\]
The exact cone formula for the operator dual norm (ED10)
proves (NF12). Evaluation on continuous original compact
tests proves the ordinary measure convergence. The previous
proposition proves that its limit is nonliteral on the
relative quotient. Finally the carrier of each tropical
pushforward is a nonempty compact subset of $Q$, so the
source obstruction applies to every approximating measure.
All constructions remain on the original field and norm.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The exact surviving distinctions.}
There are now three separate notions: a bounded Banach-dual
functional, a strong-continuous order-reversing functional,
and a literal positive Radon datum whose integrals ignore
the relative null ideal. The first need not be strongly
continuous by (CG11)--(CG14), and the second need not be
literal by (NF7)--(NF12). The capacity-modulus condition
(CD1)--(CD2) supplies the third with all required continuity.
The nonlinear source image is a further, closed proper subset,
with the normal and contact obstructions already proved.
None of these distinctions closes OPEN-GQ or identifies
relative null sets with all pluripolar or negligible sets.

title: Energy balls need not be weakly compact in either Banach realization
text:
energy_ball_weak_compactness_obstruction.tex \section{Energy balls need not be weakly compact in either Banach realization}
\label{sec:r12-energy-ball-weak-compactness-obstruction}

The weak-$*$ compact datum family in (CW14) does not by itself
supply a weakly compact family of candidate potentials. The
following consequence of the proved pole example makes that
obstruction explicit. It is a statement about the two new
Banach norms, not about failure of the complete strong topology.

Fix $n>q\geq1$ and the original radial-mixture background
$S$ of (PO3), on its original unit polydisc $V$. Retain the
original field and absolute value. Put $d=q+1$ and use the
already proved actual potentials
\[
 \psi_j=\max\!\left(\log\max_{1\leq i\leq n}|T_i|,-j\right),
 \qquad
 u=\log\max_{1\leq i\leq n}|T_i|,
                    \qquad j=1,2,\ldots .
 \tag{WB1}
\]
The value of $u$ at the origin is $-\infty$. It represents
a member of the same no-loss first-energy cone, and (PO7)
gives
\[
       e(u)=1,\qquad e(\psi_j)=1-e^{-j},\qquad
                               I(\psi_j,u)=e^{-j}.
 \tag{WB2}
\]
The pole functional is continuous on both $\mathbb D_S$
and $\mathbb L_S$ and satisfies
\[
                   L_\infty(u)=1,\qquad L_\infty(\psi_j)=0.
 \tag{WB3}
\]
All these statements are exactly the earlier original-current
pole construction, including its actual Borel representatives.

\begin{proposition}[No weak cluster and nonreflexivity in every remaining degree]
\label{prop:r12-energy-ball-nonreflexivity}
For the allowed data just specified, the sequence $(\psi_j)$
has no weakly convergent subnet, and in particular no weakly
convergent subsequence, in either $\mathbb D_S$ or
$\mathbb L_S$. Consequently
\[
      \mathcal B_{\mathscr C}
            =\{v\in\mathscr C:r(v)\leq1\}
 \tag{WB4}
\]
is not weakly compact in either Banach space, and neither
$\mathbb D_S$ nor $\mathbb L_S$ is reflexive.

This holds in every remaining degree $q\geq1$ by the
specified example in every $n>q$. It does not say that
these spaces are nonreflexive for every possible background
$S$, including the zero or other degenerate backgrounds.
\end{proposition}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}} of
the present round's exact Banach realizations, source-functional
continuity and pole functional. The proposed universal weak
compactness of bounded potential energy balls is
\texttt{FALSE}. The weak closedness of norm-closed convex
sets and weak compactness of bounded closed balls in a
reflexive Banach space are \texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN}
functional-analysis facts.

\begin{proof}
Let $E$ denote either $\mathbb D_S$ or $\mathbb L_S$.
The proved realization theorems say that the same cone
$\mathscr C$ is norm closed and convex in $E$, and that
\[
                         \|v\|_E=r(v)\qquad(v\in\mathscr C).
 \tag{WB5}
\]
It is therefore weakly closed, by the Hahn--Banach
separation theorem. Every source functional $J(a)$,
$a\in\mathscr C$, is continuous on $E$. In the lattice
case this uses its proved literal extension (OL6),
not a newly assumed extension of an arbitrary dual.
On the cone these source functionals are also continuous
for the strong discrepancy topology, by the frozen
tester estimate and (NI4).

Suppose that a subnet $(\psi_{j_\gamma})$ converges
weakly in $E$ to $v$. The subnet indices are cofinal
in the integer row, so (WB2) still makes it converge
strongly to $u$. Weak closedness gives $v\in\mathscr C$.
For every fixed $a\in\mathscr C$, the weak and strong
continuities just stated give, respectively,
\[
      J(a)(v)=\lim_\gamma J(a)(\psi_{j_\gamma})=J(a)(u).
 \tag{WB6}
\]
Choose $a=v$ and $a=u$. The exact energy-discrepancy
identity then yields
\[
              I(v,u)=(J(v)-J(u))(v-u)=0.
 \tag{WB7}
\]
The strong cone is separated, so $v=u$ as its original
relative Borel class. On the other hand, continuity of
$L_\infty\in E^*$ and (WB3) would give
$L_\infty(v)=0$, whereas $L_\infty(u)=1$. This is a
contradiction. It proves the absence of a weakly
convergent subnet in either space.

The sequence lies in (WB4), by (WB2) and (WB5).
Every net in a compact space has a convergent subnet;
thus (WB4) is not weakly compact. Finally (WB4) is
the intersection of the norm-closed convex cone with
the closed unit ball, so it is weakly closed in that
ball. If $E$ were reflexive, its closed unit ball
would be weakly compact, making (WB4) weakly compact
as well. This contradiction proves nonreflexivity.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{Consequence for the compact-capacity attempt.}
The mechanism ``bounded first energies imply weakly compact
potential candidates; then use weak-$*$ compactness of the
localized source data'' is invalid in these Banach realizations.
The first assertion is disproved by (WB1)--(WB7), even though
the displayed row actually converges strongly. This does not
contradict strong completeness of $\mathscr C$, completeness
of the curvature metric $d_J$, or the weak-$*$ compactness
of the specified datum family in the \emph{dual} space.
It also gives no counterexample to (FG1), to compact ordinary
outer regularity, or to the analytic relation quotient.

\paragraph{Exact dependency snapshots.}
The energy-difference closed-cone theorem is
\path{energy/energy_difference_banach.tex}, SHA256:
\begin{quote}\small
\nolinkurl{12bde9976ef8d8dcb3abbfc23f71f8e1a1ae37a6195de0dcdd13f09c5c0f5f45}.
\end{quote}
The lattice realization and source extension are
\path{nonlinear/order_energy_lattice_completion.tex}, SHA256:
\begin{quote}\small
\nolinkurl{754db6baac08f682e94d5342aa3e757914f3442592bd10cb288f8f2c7ce1bb69}.
\end{quote}
The exact energies and pole dual are
\path{nonlinear/radial_pole_order_dual_obstruction.tex}, SHA256:
\begin{quote}\small

The source strong-continuity and discrepancy identity are

title: Round 13：失败路线、修复和第一开放门槛
text:
FAILED_ROUTES_AND_OPEN_GATES.md # Round 13：失败路线、修复和第一开放门槛

本文件记录命题级边界，不把一种方法失败等同于总目标被反驳。每项的证明与原范围见精确结果登记。

## 1. 已在本轮修复的问题

1. **只在自由半径点核对曲线比较。** CC 在所有充分小的正实对数半径直接计算完整 graded residue 与 primitive slope；可公度半径含额外 Laurent residue variables，常数域次数保持。
2. **只检测分开的边缘符号。** CS/SD 对整个 raw incident relation 空间进行一次带权 Stokes，保留混合关系与完整配对 Hessian。
3. **Picard 完成之后仍使用完成之前的核。** 最后 faithful separator 放在 SP 完成之后；新的零旧列标记和 tangent satellites 都纳入。
4. **表面单位组依赖后选环带。** UA 先冻结有限 trace 空间、几何、单位与中央提升，再选任意紧区间。
5. **只有一个 Gauss 截面落入乘积。** UF 的有限有理包控制整个完成后核心纤维，再用 properness 得到普通开邻域。
6. **为证明局部作用先要求全局原函数。** PA 固定一个旧 P_τ。其外由原始 OR 处理，其内由有限顶锥/二维面/射线族覆盖；普通 locality 允许局部元组不同。
7. ** chosen direct lift 的 horn 失败使标量比较完全停滞。** HN 在实际选定根定义域上用 QE 和 Gauss 变量证明有限范数识别；它不要求 direct lift 在每个角区都近似正确。

## 2. 已反驳的捷径

| 捷径 | 反证 | 原范围限制 |
|---|---|---|
| 所有正角向局部原函数 + D=d′d″ current 闭 ⇒ 全局原函数 | PK/HP 非零 Killing 类 | 实有限 fan；不声称 actual analytic zero 实现 |
| 上述资料自动给固定 Q 误差趋零 | KG 的正 strain-measure 差距 | 固定实 fan；actual graph refinement 可改变问题 |
| PL 坐标图仅按 Jacobian 运输 strain | GD 的 Hessian wall drift | 精确分布链式法则，含秩退化 |
| 所有 residue units 可提升成域 section 或保留全部有限方程 | RE 椭圆曲线除子 | 不否定逐个有限单位提升 |
| 一个 chosen direct lift 的比较自动覆盖整个中心邻域 | LH 全普通点 sharp horn | 加一个实际单位即可修复该例，故非普遍反例 |
| Hensel 有限范数图 + 中心 resultant bound ⇒ 整个邻域连续延拓 | HB 不可约 V²−V−A 的两支极限 | 否定每个有限实际 tuple 的整邻域延拓，不否定局部根域构造 |
| 正闭 S、有界 PS Z、点支撑 ⇒ 残余零 | CR 的闭正实平面例，临界 δ² 质量 | 例子不是 actual zero，ambient D[Z]≠0 |
| 剩余秩三仅在可数 moment 层，所以不带质量 | PA12 原始环面单位 Gauss 原子 | 这是正 BT 测度，不是 actual zero 的作用 |

## 3. 不可交换的两个源清单

R11 FA 在指定旧源 P 上忠实。加入分离函数 g 后，P 保持被忠实嵌入；这不意味着新 tuple (f,g) 的整个 S_(f,g) 都被同一坐标图忠实嵌入。

PA 用一个冻结的旧 P_τ 做几何清单。其余实际点用原始 scalar rank 条件处理。若要求一个全局原函数或固定 Q 序列，就不能据此删除新源；GD/HS 的全新源 strain 与相容性仍需要证明。

## 4. 中心质量：第一条未证估计

PA 在给定模型中只留下 c_S(P)δ_y。完整 cutoff 计算给出 C δ^-2 μ(B_2δ)。从有界系数与有限测度不能推出 μ(B_2δ)=o(δ²)；CR 给出临界阶的实诊断。MT 已利用完整受保护转置与闭性证明 O(δ²)，LE 据此把高阶 scalar jets 的贡献降为 O_S(δ)。剩余 leading paired class 的消去仍未证明。

原始背景 S 的“剩余数值除子类”尚未构造。可以合法定义实际 cap 势的 BT 原子 m_S(L,M)=(Dq_L∧Dq_M∧S)({y})。但不能先假定 m_S 经过 L·M 的数值类分解，再用数值关系证明 actual-zero 下降；该分解本身就是需要证明的下降步骤。

R6 已证明固定连续 BT slots 对同一普通域上的背景弱收敛连续，并已在 W_loc（正闭实际 delta 背景的同域 ordinary 弱闭包）解决相应作用。尚未证明任意允许 S 都局部属于 W_loc。不能把这个未证密度放进定义或当作文献常识。

详见 `notes/geom13_central_background_cap_audit.md`。

## 5. 全局 exact-lift 与受控逼近仍未完成的部分

- JF7 的每个 raw Hessian 条件必须对整个最终 incident family 成立；局部分支或边缘因子分别张成不够。
- 即使 JF7 成立，JF8 仍是非平凡全局 Killing 类。PK/HP 不允许从局部覆盖自动去掉它。
- GD 的实际 nodal units 修复指定旧核心；HS 的新源投影在旧二维骨架，且一个旧面上可解相对 jet。不同旧面在旧射线上的相容性仍未解决。
- 在 HS 明确给定的 incidence、Picard 和实际 jet transport 前提下，旧 paired quotient 可以单射保留。纯 subdivisions 或 permissible blowups 不构成一般杀类机制。
- HN 不提供跨所有新根边界的连续 covector。HB 给出了不可延拓的实际边界，需保留局部根域或使用 singular/direct pairing。

## 6. 外部来源边界

- Ducros finite Gauss separation 使用原域部分及 erratum，不使用为 universal base change 提供的扩域条款。
- Luxton–Qu 的已核对 schön compactification 定理带有代数闭、特征零假设，不能直接移植到固定有限剩余域。
- DHLY 固定 skeleton 的有限生成结论没有证明所有 ordinary added sources 的闭合；其特定 defect 例不能当作原有限 K 反例。
- HN 使用 ACVF 的 valuation-dominance QE，包含混合特征的情况；没有以 equicharacteristic-zero Pas 结果替代。
- Parallel 深度检索因连接要求未产生结果。没有把它记为完成的研究或来源；已直接核对可访问的原始论文。

## 7. 总目标仍 OPEN

一般原始 A1/GQ/KC12/RV4/PSO12/13、variable-PS/CTO、GK 高次接口、一般普通粘合与自然性仍 OPEN。C1 coefficient-one 和 B1 raw=outer 继续按历史已反驳范围保留。当前局部模型结果不允许改变域、绝对值、positivity cone 或 absolute carrier，也不允许把 current 等式当作全部 GK tests 等式。

## 8. 临界 tangent 与 PS 配对接口已闭合，实际消去仍 OPEN

MT 的弱子列收敛最初只在 smooth real tests 上成立。PT 直接核对了保留的 R6 `lem:r6-weighted-pws-error`（来自 R4 71.1–71.2、71.4）：对每个系数墙，法向对角质量在宽 ε 条带中为 O(ε)，混合项由 middle-positive 矩阵的 Cauchy–Schwarz 得到 O(√ε)。因而相容 finite-PS tests 可一致平滑，即使极限给墙及其交面正质量，配对仍收敛。这个估计是旧成果；本轮明确验证其与真实背景临界缩放的接口。

结合 MT 的完整系数转置和 LE 的实际标量一阶化，已证明对每个临界 tangent T₀ 都有

\[
c_S(P)=-\langle T_0,Z_0\wedge D\rho\rangle.
\]

这一配对保留所有联合符号与面值，且不依赖 tangent 唯一性。尚未证明每个实际可实现 T₀ 都消去 actual zero 的 Z₀；也未证明 T₀ 属于实际 W_loc 类。随意选一个正闭实圆锥 current 或旧 Killing 对偶都不能替代这个实际可实现族。


## 9. 球面实分类不等于实际联合可实现性

SR 已将临界实正闭圆锥 current 精确分类为有限 PSD、切向、球面散度零的矩阵测度 M，并把实际中心系数写成完整的质量项减梯度项。实闭性和该角向平衡仍未推出 actual-zero 配对消去。应研究实际关系的 Z₀ 与原背景的 M 在同一原芽、所有实际细化上的联合限制。不能单独扩大两个边缘的允许集合，再把它们的任意配对当成原问题；也不能把实分类误写成实际背景实现定理。


## 10. 球面对称梯度的第一条仍缺少的墙估计

令 φ=Σc_α h_α k_α，v=½∇_S φ。每个共同线性胞腔内，Hess_S h_α=−h_α g_S，因此

\[
e_S(v)=(Z_0)_{\rm tan}-(Z_0)_{rr}g_S.
\]

若 v 是全局光滑切向场，SR14a 立即消去球面配对。但通常 φ 仅连续分片光滑，v 的跳跃为墙的法向方向；其分布 strain 还带法向–法向墙项。宽 ε 平滑使该项出现 ε^{-1} 系数。PT 的正闭条带估计只能给

\[
\varepsilon^{-1}M_{nn}(\{|\ell|\lesssim\varepsilon\})
=O(1),
\]

不能给 o(1)。球面与固定环带中的欧氏法向比较只改变有界常数；Mθ=0 保证切向投影不改变该法向收缩。故逐胞腔 strain 解不是已有消去证明。下一步须利用 actual-zero 的完整联合关系消去这些临界墙通量，或构造另一个具备合法全局墙控制的原函数。这里只标出已有估计不能闭合的位置，不声称原范围反例。

title: Remaining minimal gates and failed inferences
text:
remaining_gates_and_failed_attempts.tex \section{Remaining minimal gates and failed inferences}
\label{sec:r24-remaining-gates}

\paragraph{Status.}
This register is a scope audit, not an additional theorem.
All original field, norm, topology, carrier, test, refinement and
positivity conventions are those in Section~\ref{sec:r24-main-scope}.
The positive implications cited below are proved in their exact
source modules.  No listed open statement is used as an input to
an unconditional conclusion.

\subsection{The unchanged principal gate}

\paragraph{KC12: \texttt{OPEN}.}
For every actual signed PL-zero on the same original ordinary
germ and its correct absolute cap carrier, prove that the exact
KC5 carrier-CLN seminorm is zero on every required compact control
stage, in every relevant degree.  Equivalently, by the frozen
full-polar duality, prove annihilation by every genuine full
original carrier polar.  A zero on the absolute integration
background is not itself such a certificate.  Neither a finite
chosen family of tests nor a representation by an arbitrary real
current replaces this universal assertion.

The R17 real primitive theorem remains valid with its radial-hull
support.  This round does not prove that an actual analytic zero
has zero real double derivative on that hull.  A primitive lift
on the original analytic carrier is not obtained merely by
retaining a support in a real target.  The same caution applies
to convolution: no zero-preserving analytic convolution has
been constructed.

\subsection{Harmonic localization and finite-cover return}

\paragraph{NC12/HE7/IL20: \texttt{OPEN}.}
For each unchanged original \(U,F,L\), each genuine full
degree-\(b\) polar, and every fixed signed global tail tuple,
prove local harmonic annihilation of its intrinsic first-slot
measure.  By HL and HC, it is enough to establish the exact
local-unit drift assertion.  In the protected affinoid setting
its one-function form is
\[
 \nu_{\ell_{a,r},v_3,\ldots,v_b}\big|_{\{|a|>r\}}=0,
 \qquad \ell_{a,r}=\log\max\{r,|a|\},                 \tag{RG24.1}
\]
for every original analytic \(a\), every \(r>0\), every
full polar, and all tails.  The measure is already defined on
\(U\); it is its Borel restriction that occurs in (RG24.1).
The assertion does not assume a full polar on the smaller
ordinary open.  HL settles the class of continuous harmonic
witnesses, but it supplies no missing global harmonic extension.

\paragraph{ST19 and LG4 in mixed degree \(b\ge2\): \texttt{OPEN}.}
LC proves an exact conditional arbitrary-companion transfer
for one global upstairs unit logarithm.  Even under its explicit
locality assumption, the further transfer of an arbitrary
whole-carrier harmonic trace and of every original local ambient
generator is not proved.  Thus an arbitrary upstairs KC5
decomposition still has no general reverse certificate estimate
through a finite etale cover.  The degree-one full-domain return
is already settled in the frozen FR/LG chain and is not reopened.

One may not apply the assumed harmonic-locality theorem to
\(\Lambda\circ\mathcal T\) before showing that this transported
functional kills the full upstairs relation ideal.  That would
use the required harmonic and ambient descent in order to prove
it.  LC avoids this circularity by working directly with the
existing downstairs full polar and its already constructed
Radon measures.

\paragraph{LG7: \texttt{OPEN}.}
The R23 finite-tuple geometry and smooth actual-delta faithfulness
give an original Abhyankar model for the chosen analytic relation.
The actual-zero relation on that model still has to yield its
full carrier certificate.  Returning the full seminorm certificate
through the finite cover is a second gate if a downstairs
\emph{seminorm} conclusion is required.  For all-original-background
action, the frozen LG reduction already uses complete finite-etale
base change and EC directly from the model certificate and does
not require that reverse seminorm theorem.  Finite preparation
of a unit tuple, numerical positivity, and a smooth pullback
identity do not establish either gate.

\subsection{The coupled cap and the two different scalar obstructions}

\paragraph{CM10: \texttt{OPEN}.}
For the specified actual normal cap, numerical harmonicity of
the PL trace on its intrinsic Gauss fiber gives the known actual
coupled zero and arbitrary-background action zero.  It has not
been shown to give the unchanged full-polar certificate after
cap multiplication.  HC24.2a now identifies an arbitrary original
continuous harmonic trace witness exactly with Picard zero.
The completed residue field of the cap may have a function-field
residue, so the finite residue field of the original \(K\)
cannot be substituted for it.

CZ24 completes the ordinary zero-product family for this
interface and retains a quantitative same-carrier estimate.
Its bound still uses positive-tail costs on the larger
\(G\cap L\).  It does not by itself compare the full carrier
seminorms.  It also does not cancel the exact cutoff commutators
in HC.  A literal local witness at every point of a compact cap
stage and a single global \(G\)-harmonic factor are different
statements.

\paragraph{RV4 and the scalar-boundary action target: \texttt{OPEN}.}
For the quadratic PS energy form \(Z\), one still needs the
balanced covector lift RV4, or an alternative direct action
annihilation.  The raw coordinate coefficient of a covector
times a cap is not intrinsic, because the frozen normal-factor
example has a zero covector product with a nonzero scalar cap.
After RV4 the separately closed PS remainder has the exact
formula
\[
                 D_\delta q=A-\gamma .                    \tag{RG24.2}
\]
The scalar boundary \(\gamma\) is retained.
RV15 asks for \(\gamma=0\) as an actual germ.  AP24 supplies
a weaker sufficient target: one finite continuous ordinary
potential \(v\), on one representative chosen before \(S\)
and the tests, with
\[
                            [\gamma]=D[v].                 \tag{RG24.3}
\]
The local DC property then follows from the exact degree-one
order argument.  Existence in (RG24.3) is not proved.

An alternative sufficient interface is transfer of the particular
covector relation AP24.9 to the ordinary arbitrary-background
identity AP24.10.  This is beyond the scalar continuous-coefficient
R6 theorem.  The compactness theorem for already represented
curvature intervals does not supply a potential for every closed
current dominated by a represented curvature.  A convergent
represented net on the same domain would have to be constructed
first.

\subsection{Strictly rejected shortcuts}

\paragraph{A common-domain harmonic comparator: \texttt{FALSE}.}
BC constructs one fixed quadratic finite etale cover and unit
such that, for every initial ordinary neighborhood, a later
legal upstairs DC weight produces a local strict-defect unit
logarithm with no harmonic extension to that whole neighborhood.
The fixed-weight preparation remains possible; the refuted
claim puts the neighborhood before every later weight.
Neither the polynomial involved nor any of its polar values is
shown to be a KC counterexample.

\paragraph{Finitely many local coefficient kernels: \texttt{FALSE}.}
IK fixes just two original positive cap cycles.  On every Gauss
neighborhood their intrinsic restriction kernels include the
distinct lines \(a+Nb=0\), for every integer \(N\ge1\).
A finite number of fixed additional moment coordinates does
not change these intrinsic local equalities.  This refutes the
literal finite-constant-type approach to coefficient gluing.
It does not refute a finite generated object with genuinely
variable relations and an appropriate specialization operation.
Such an object and operation have not been constructed here.
It also does not refute the elementary finite-subfamily detector
for a fixed finite-dimensional global vector space.

\paragraph{One scalar for all intersecting branches: \texttt{FALSE}.}
AP24.13--AP24.14 exhibit two intersecting original cap currents
whose distinct constant coefficients cannot be represented by
one continuous coefficient multiplying their sum.  This simple
diagnostic already has an explicit continuous PL potential and
does not have RV15's centered homogeneity.  It is not a new
counterexample family for the principal problem.

\paragraph{Fixed-outer harmonic witnesses on shifted caps.}
FM24--FQ24 give an exact obstruction to this particular construction.
For a fixed finite PL trace and one fixed outer ordinary domain,
one sufficiently near negative-level complete-fiber
witness already gives a harmonic witness for the original trace
on a fixed smaller germ.  In particular, a trace with a nonzero
residue Picard class cannot acquire a sequence of such witnesses,
or uniformly approximate witnesses on the protected complete cap
stages, even if their norms are unbounded.  The factor-two estimate
is first proved on irrational levels; compact-image upper
semicontinuity extends it to all nearby levels without Gauss
saturation.  The sufficient same-domain
cap approximation estimate has no witness-norm cost: its remainder
is \(\varepsilon J_h\prod J_i\).  The failure is therefore
geometric extension of the witnesses, not control of their norms.

This is an obstruction only to that stronger witness construction.
It neither supplies nor refutes a genuinely coupled certificate,
and the positive scalar approximation gap is not a positive lower
bound for a full carrier-CLN seminorm.  Witnesses on domains
depending on the level, and agreement only on a general closed
carrier slice, are not covered by the proof.  No norm-level/full-
Gauss-fiber identification at rational levels is asserted.

\paragraph{Affine coefficients without the full closedness premise.}
HB24 computes \(\gamma=-hD_\delta h\) for
\(h=\max(0,s_1,s_2)\), with \(D\gamma=-\delta_x\).
It therefore cannot be a finite sum of original smooth harmonic
coefficients times separately closed scalar forms.  The source
\(A=d'h\wedge d''h\) is not separately closed, so this does
not refute the RV hypotheses.  A supplied representation
\(\gamma=\sum\ell_iD_\delta v_i\) with harmonic \(\ell_i\)
would suffice for the ordinary arbitrary-background action gate;
neither its construction under the genuine RV hypotheses nor
the balancing of its separately extracted scalar faces is proved.

\paragraph{Higher nilpotence as quadratic division:
\texttt{FAILED\_ATTEMPT}.}
CA24 retains the exact hypothetical polynomial identities and
shows that, for dimension at least two, their degree-three-or-higher
relations do not force the desired quadratic product to vanish.
The explicitly stated abstract implication is false.  The graded
algebra used to show this is not an actual polar, analytic relation,
or allowed background.  The geometric coupled cap remains open.
Positive-point certificates are used only for their specified
positive presentations and their initial germ preparations;
an unbounded family does not thereby receive one common domain.

\subsection{Original-category pressure checks}

No positive conclusion changes the original field or norm.
Finite residue-field extensions used to describe an original
analytic seminorm are not new fields for arbitrary-background
current theory.  Ordinary domains are chosen before the
subsequent objects quantified in each theorem; BC and IK spell
out failures of stronger uniform choices.

Every cap carrier is the complete support supplied by the
frozen cap theorem.  A real norm level, a chosen Gauss section,
and a real radial hull are not substituted for it.  All lower
dimensional and singular boundary terms remain in HC and AP.
The BC example is a scalar continuation obstruction; IK is an
intrinsic restriction-kernel obstruction; CA is only a formal
failed-inference witness.  None supplies the entire actual-zero,
same-germ, full-polar, arbitrary-background conjunction needed
to label KC12 false.

For a fixed-stage conclusion, KC6 is applied to the tests whose
required control stage is that stage.  An all-current conclusion
uses the premise at every \(L_\eta\).  The distinction is
explicit in CZ24 and remains in the result register.  No smooth
test equality has been promoted to unrestricted GK delta-test
equality, and no top-degree point-cycle result is counted again
as an all-degree theorem.

\paragraph{Next proof obligation.}
A useful continuation should attack one of the concrete interfaces
above: prove original local-unit drift annihilation for a genuine
full polar; construct the missing continuous scalar boundary
potential or covector transfer; or prove a coupled Picard/cap
certificate with an unchanged ordinary representative and
quantitative remainder.  Merely naming an analytic relation
complex, invoking local contractibility, or choosing a finite
test family does not address these obligations.

title: Non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor theory：内部成果审计、任务清单与研究计划
text:
AUDIT_AND_PLAN_ZH.md # Non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor theory：内部成果审计、任务清单与研究计划

日期：2026-11-14。性质：已有结果的源文、依赖与状态审计，加上后续研究计划；不是 R25 冻结证明包，没有新增数学定理。

## 一、审计结论

现有理论远不止连续势或二次关系的准备工作。任意固定原始背景上的有界 BT 七项性质和势无关性，环境背景的局部极性/容量理论，限定范围的无界正幂能量微积分，严格 Laurent 域上的强第一能量完成，以及相对线性测度数据问题和非线性变分/相容性判据，已经有内部证明。

真正仍未闭合的主线是：一般实际解析关系下降及变量 PS/CTO/测试兼容；修正后的任意相对背景外容量正则性；literal ED-bounded 测度的强积分连续性；独立且可验证的非线性源相容性条件。域与边界/实际 classical 代表的扩展也须分层处理。

“完成”在本报告中意味着冻结源文有明确证明，在所列原假设及采纳的 R/B/A2 输入下可用；本轮未重新独立验证所有历史证明。文件哈希检查只证明字节一致性，不证明数学正确。

## 二、版本与核查范围

- 外层 R24 handoff 与内嵌 R24 的 SHA-256、大小已重新核对。
- R24 的 644 个清单成员重新检查大小和 SHA-256，未发现不一致。
- 执行恢复脚本后，R23 313 个、R22 2258 个成员通过其恢复核验；未覆盖不同字节的已有文件。
- 顺嵌套链提取了 R3–R20 的主要文本，R3 包内保留 R1/R2 原源。对旧包记录了 archive hashes；不声称本轮逐个重新校验全部更早 manifest。
- 重点核对 R1–R4 有界/环境势论、R5/R6 势商及连续系数模、R10 PS current 模、R11 无界/能量/线性问题、R12/R16/R17 数据/容量/相容性，以及 R18/R24 关系下降。
- R21 历史完整 ZIP/PDF 没有字节恢复；沿用保留/重建源文及既有新审查的资格说明。
- 包内 evidence/ 是选定原始模块的字节不变副本，不是完整历史档案；SOURCE_INDEX.json 给出其原路径和 SHA-256。

## 三、共同数学范围与三类不能混同的空间

原始有限 K/Qp、原绝对值；good、Hausdorff、boundaryless、quasi-smooth 原始解析空间（逐纯维分支处理）；ordinary opens/germs；全部原始紧支 smooth CLD tests 与 actual refinements；S 对称、middle-positive、分别 d'、d'' 闭。令 D=d'd''，q=n-p。

局部定理不自动成为全局边界定理。很多全局能量结果要求一个严格 Laurent box，闭包紧含在原 affinoid 内部，S 延拓到闭包的 ordinary 邻域。

必须分清：actual classical psh 类；按相对外容量等价的 Borel/strong E1 完成类；q=1 faithful part-energy/renormalized 解类。q=1 能量方程普遍可解，不意味着其解属于 classical-approximation 正锥。完成边界也不等于普通逐点边界。

## 四、在原范围内已经完成的理论

### C01　R/B/A2 冻结基础

R/B 原始连续正则化、局部有界 classical psh 背景[1]微积分及普通代数局部化；A2 指定范围 geometric adelic nefness。

**范围限制：**授权 INTERNAL_INPUT，不是此次独立重证；A2 不列为待攻。

**源文：**S01, S02。

### C02　任意固定原始 S 的有界 BT 七项性质

存在、正性、分别闭性、对称性、势多线性、ordinary restriction/gluing、加权联合递减连续性。

**范围限制：**局部有界 classical 势；固定 S；全部原始 smooth CLD tests/actual refinements。

**源文：**S01, S02。

### C03　CLN 与容量控制

局部有限-test CLN、系数 Radon 控制、限定可积条件的 L1/截断估计。

**范围限制：**不提供无条件移动背景连续性。

**源文：**S01, S02。

### C04　曲率核与势无关性

D[u]=D[v] => u-v 实际连续 pluriharmonic，且 D(uS)=D(vS)；有局部有界 classical 势的曲率 currents 可混合并粘合。

**范围限制：**不只连续势；不定义两个完全任意正闭 currents 的积。

**源文：**S04。

### C05　连续标量系数曲率模

局部有界 classical 曲率的连续标量系数关系与顺序传递；多槽模正乘积。

**范围限制：**一般变量系数输出不自动 separately closed；不等于所有高次 actual relations。

**源文：**S05。

### C06　既有 PS current 模

有限 PS 系数乘原始允许 currents 的微分、内禀曲率运算及 witness independence。

**范围限制：**对象先是既有原始 current；不等于全 variable-PS analytic delta quotient。

**源文：**S06, S07。

### C07　有界容量完成与单调极限

actual increasing supremum、相对 Borel 完成、q.e. 独立性、局部拟连续性、strict maximum locality。

**范围限制：**一般相对类不能以 ambient usc envelope 替代。

**源文：**S02。

### C08　环境 [1] 极性/Choquet 理论

局部 pluripolar/outer-null/negligible 等价；限定 exhaustion domain 的 extremal mass、raw/outer Borel 正则性与 Choquet。

**范围限制：**ambient scope，不能推广到所有相对 S；不声称任意空间单一全局 untwisted 极函数。

**源文：**S02, S03。

### C09　极集限制与有界比较

从全域已定义的 S 得到 pole-set restriction closedness/BT compatibility；compact-gap comparison；相对容量意义 domination。

**范围限制：**一般 S 可给 ambient 极集正质量；无条件逐点 domination 错误。

**源文：**S02。

### C10　无界 nonpolar 产品

系数局部有限下的非极 mixed limit separately closed；no-loss 容量尾判据。

**范围限制：**保留 compact-sublevel boundary、局部质量条件；不能省略 no-loss。

**源文：**S08, S11。

### C11　正幂能量类

E^sigma，sigma>0，容量积分刻画、all-degree recursion、first-order/energy currents 与精确指数预算。

**范围限制：**端点稳定需一致尾可积或相应强拓扑；仅能量有界不够。

**源文：**S08。

### C12　E1 全局 Green 与强完成

strict box/延拓背景的 Green 对称、常数1混合能量不等式、强完成 Borel 实现、比较/支配、强单调闭包。

**范围限制：**完成边界不等于普通逐点边界，完成成员未必 ambient classical。

**源文：**S08, S09。

### C13　Perron/obstacle

有界和强能量相对 envelope、finite rooftop、源下界和 Borel constraints 保持。

**范围限制：**最大元/变分最大化不自动解指定源方程。

**源文：**S08, S09, S12, S16。

### C14　相对线性测度方程

q=n-p=1，finite signed energy-diffuse Radon datum 的 renormalized zero-boundary solution、chain/coarea、clipping、obstacle contact。

**范围限制：**affinoid part domain 与其 clipping/radiation boundary；不是 ambient classical psh 普遍解。

**源文：**S08, S10, S11。

### C15　能量对偶与非线性变分

Banach difference space、order-energy lattice、norm-closed source image、strong-continuous 数据唯一变分投影/normal residual。

**范围限制：**源像不因此 weak*-closed/convex；变分解与源解分开。

**源文：**S12, S15。

### C16　精确源相容性判据

literal strong Radon data 的 Xi=0 单probe判据；有subsolution时 Perron–variational gap；后续正compact-test判据。

**范围限制：**判据已证；从独立几何/数据假设推出判据未证。

**源文：**S13, S16。

### C17　已受控测度和参数模型

source domination/capacity domination 的 literal strong 积分连续性；closed parameter bands/disintegration/指定Lp模块兼容源。

**范围限制：**不替代所有 relative 数据；parameter-annihilated 条件原样保留。

**源文：**S12, S16。

### C18　full-polar 内禀 normal current

带任意解析权重的 NC3 散度、全部 smooth presentation quotient、NC8 内禀流与边界。

**范围限制：**R18 已证；NC12 漂移消灭及其后奇异配对仍开放。

**源文：**S18。

### C19　R24 标量与 cap 工具

原始连续 harmonic=classical PH=局部unit logs；HC/CZ same-carrier cap 控制；AP 给定连续势的作用等式。

**范围限制：**分别保留 exact support、whole carrier、stage 与 existence 前提。

**源文：**S19, S21。

## 五、必须从“待证明”中删除的错误命题

这些反例是理论的一部分，不是证明技术暂时不足。应保留其精确量词和限定条件。

### F01　任意相对 S 的全部紧集/Borel raw capacity = outer capacity

R16 crossed box 全tester反例；raw decreasing-compact continuity 也失败。

源文：S14, S15, S25。

### F02　所有 capacity-controlled / finite-energy datum 自动是指定完成空间的源

严格源、正smooth density、任意小扰动仍可不相容。

源文：S11, S16, S17。

### F03　变分最大化/relative Perron 直接给源等式

仅提供 Euler inequality / subsolution；需 normal residual=0。

源文：S11, S12, S13。

### F04　任意 S 下相对 envelope 可换成 ambient usc envelope

可丢失原始 source；relative 与 ambient 类须分开。

源文：S02, S11。

### F05　仅能量有界+容量收敛给临界 weighted continuity

有端点反例；一致tails/强拓扑是修正条件。

源文：S08, S11。

### F06　无界 nonpolar 产品无条件满足递归

可遗失极性剩余 Dirac；no-loss/可积前提不可删。

源文：S11。

### F07　任意相对容量零集等于 ambient 极集，或无条件逐点支配

退化/支撑使原断言错误；ambient 局部结论已经完成。

源文：S02, S11。

### F08　每个 full polar 都有指定连续系数 smooth-form 双原函数

R24 VE 排除，含更换 Hessian 代表；适当奇异原函数未被排除。

源文：S22。

### F09　global full polar 任意局部化/固定域全权重 harmonic comparator/有限局部常系数核

NL/BC/IK 已排除相应强断言；不是 KC12 反例。

源文：S18, S19, S20。

最重要的容量修正：R16 中 q≥2 的 crossed-box 例子，κ=(2λ)^(-q)，H={A,B}，满足

    C_S(H;V) = (2+2^(1-q)) κ < 3κ ≤ C_S^*(H;V) ≤ 4κ.

这里 supremum 是全部原始 normalized classical testers，包括非连续者，不是只在 toric testers 上计算。旧 R2/R11 将任意相对背景 raw/outer 问题记为 OPEN；该无条件命题到 R16 已为 FALSE。环境背景 [1] 的已证合格域定理不受此反例推翻。

## 六、仍待完成的数学任务

各 A1 子路线是备选/互补，不是必须机械顺序完成的全部条件。P1 表示优先主线，P2 表示扩展主线，P3 表示非必经路线；这不是预计用时。

### A1　一般 actual PL 关系的任意背景作用下降（P1）

- [ ] **目标：**证明 actual signed PL-zero => A_S(P)=0；KC12 same-germ qzero 是更强充分路线。
- **已有而不应重做：**有界BT、R5势商、R18内禀流均已存在。
- **验收条件：**原K/原范数/same germ/全测试细化/所有合法degrees及mixed tails；不增加S假设。
- **依赖：**C02, C04, C05, C18, C19。
- **依据：**S18, S19, S20。

### A1-RV　二次作用的 RV/AP 路线（P1-备选路线）

- [ ] **目标：**RV4 balanced covector lift，加上 gamma 连续普通势或必要 covector relation action transfer；也可直接证明完整作用恒等式绕过两步。
- **已有而不应重做：**给定连续势的作用比较已证明；曲率order interval不是势存在性。
- **验收条件：**对实际RV产生的类的一般定理；一般维数、任意S；两个缺口不可混称一个。
- **依赖：**C05, C06, C19。
- **依据：**S21, S20。

### A1-NC　NC12 加奇异配对路线（P1-备选路线）

## 七、推荐研究顺序

### 阶段 0：固化全理论地图，而非重新证明基础

把本报告的 C/F/A–E 索引接入唯一结果登记；每条定理附原始假设、势类、背景类、边界、测试、确切源码和依赖。R/B/A2 保持授权输入。早期 OPEN 到后期 CLOSED 或 FALSE 的变化必须有后继定理，不按最近摘要覆盖整条历史。

本次已经形成分主题的状态核对和选定源文索引，但还不是逐条历史命题的最终专著依赖数据库。

### 阶段 1：三条并行主线，不让所有势理论等待 KC12

1. **解析微积分线 A：**以 general arbitrary-S action descent 为终点，先处理一般维数二次关系的真实缺口。RV/AP、NC12+singular pairing、Abhyankar model certificate 三条路线按能给出实际证明的程度选择。NC3/NC8 已有；仅重述它们不算进展。
2. **容量线 B：**研究原外容量的 Borel compact inner regularity；另行提出足以排除 crossed-box 的 tester recovery 条件。不能再把 universal raw=outer 当作主目标。
3. **数据/方程线 C：**literal ED 强 L1 连续性和非线性源相容性并行。前者拓展可用数据类，后者必须从独立条件得到 Xi=0；证明前者不等于所有数据可解。

### 阶段 2：完成真正跨层的接口

A 的作用下降若完成，再逐项检查高次数传播、variable-PS、signed CTO、完整 GK 测试与 ordinary gluing。二次成立不自动等于任意次数；已知 current 模上的 PS witness independence 不自动等于实际 delta-form relation quotient。

B/C 的结果若成立，再用于 qualified equilibrium/contact formulas、可验证源类的存在/唯一性/稳定性，以及 D 的域/边界和 classical 代表问题。已经建立的强空间比较和 Perron 不重新计为新成果。

### 阶段 3：专题书的统一成型

建议按读者理解顺序，而不是 R1–R24 时间顺序组织：

I. 原始解析范畴、psh、CLD/实际 delta 微积分及正性；
II. 任意固定背景的有界 BT、曲率商与系数模；
III. 相对容量、环境极性、比较/包络及必要反例；
IV. 无界 nonpolar/正幂能量微积分与强完成；
V. 相对线性方程、非线性变分、源相容性和合格 Dirichlet 理论；
VI. 实际解析关系、测试传递、自然性及已建立的全局应用。

成书时只使用已审定的定理；开放问题单列。完整理论包含正确的非存在与范围边界，不等于逐字复制复情形中在本范畴下已经被否定的命题。

## 八、每轮研究的实际进展标准

每轮至少输出以下之一：解决现有精确开放断言；严格缩小它且证明返回主目标的蕴含；在原始全部量词下给出真实反例并建立合格替代目标。新增定义、更多同类参数例、重复的 normal-current/散度公式、仅换术语的条件性归约，不自动算主线推进。

每个新结论需检查：same germ、correct absolute carrier、全部原始 tests/refinements、正性锥、奇异边界项、合法次数、普通拓扑与完成边界、是否偷用未证 quotient、是否误把 scalar/real 对象当作 original full polar。每个估计明确固定背景还是允许移动背景；每个解明确所在空间。

## 九、继续研究提示词

请以本审计的 R24 冻结链为基础继续发展整套 non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor theory，目标是专题专著，而非拆成小论文。先读本报告、TASK_REGISTER.json、SOURCE_INDEX.json；正式新证明仍以完整 R24 handoff 及依赖原源为依据，本轻量证据包不是完整父链替代品。

\large Fourth research record: original-test functoriality,\\
faithful energy forms, capacities, and limits of relative solvability}

\begin{abstract}
This continuation retains the arbitrary fixed-background bounded
Bedford--Taylor calculus proved in the preceding records. It develops
uniform approximation of tangentially compatible original piecewise
CLD tests, reconstructs finite etale traces from finitely many Newton
polygons, and proves preservation of the bounded potential curvature
kernel under disc projections and arbitrary analytic morphisms over
the prescribed original field. Exact spreading of original tests from
algebraic parameter fibers, combined with the known full Gauss-fiber
formula, further gives scalar kernel transfer to finite extensions
of finite polyradius Gauss residue fields. A separate exact finite-coefficient
descent reduces the remaining scalar question to residue fields of
finite-dimensional algebraic parameter points, without solving those
general fibers. In remaining degree one, a bounded
continuous psh function provides a faithful curvature measure with
exactly the coefficient-null ideal of the background. The associated
energy form is regular, strongly local and coercive. Its Poisson
problem has unique energy solutions; its capacity controls relative
BT outer capacity in one direction, and complete pole sets give an
orthogonal form decomposition. In every remaining degree, complete
pole carriers yield qualified capacity additivity, while finite tester
pasting and a constrained variational retraction extend the relative
theory. A smooth nonpolar example shows that a bounded classical
subsolution does not suffice for solvability in the global bounded-row
psh completion; an explicit non-psh energy solution isolates the
obstruction. General potential quotients, arbitrary-background raw
capacity regularity, and unrestricted completed-psh Dirichlet
existence remain open or false in the precise scopes recorded here.
\end{abstract}

\section{Scope, inputs, and conventions}
\label{sec:inputs}

Fix a finite extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$ with its given absolute value.
Let $X$ be a good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth $K$-analytic
space of pure dimension $n\geq1$, and let $U\subset X$ be an ordinary open
set. We use only the original Chambert--Loir--Ducros sheaf
$A^{a,b}$, its compactly supported smooth tests, and its original
calibration. We assume $0\leq p\leq n$. A current of bidegree $(p,p)$ acts on
$A_c^{n-p,n-p}$. We write $D=d'd''$.

The class $\Cb(U)$ consists of the actual real-valued, locally bounded,
upper-semicontinuous classical psh functions of \textup{B}, Definition
2.2: pullback to every analytic curve after every complete isometric
extension is subharmonic. No function is changed on a null or polar
set. A norm in this report always means the actual pointwise bound
\[
 \|u\|_{V,\infty}=\sup_{x\in V}|u(x)|,
\]
even where the traditional notation $L^\infty(V)$ is used. There is
no unspecified reference volume measure behind this notation.

\subsection{The accepted internal results}

The user has authorized the following theorems as established inputs.
They have been checked for scope and dependencies, but their proofs
have not been re-audited in this project.

\begin{description}
\item[\textup{R}.] \emph{Continuous CLD-positive potentials and adelic
mixed measures}, 10 November 2026, 19 pages.
Theorem 2.9 gives local uniform smooth positive approximation of finite
continuous original-current-positive potentials on smooth
quasi-projective algebraic analytifications over a $p$-adic completion.
Lemma 3.1 gives finite coefficient Radon control for the original
positive cone and stability under a fixed continuous multiplier.
Lemma 3.2 smooths pure Fubini--Study metrics on their original line.
Proposition A.1 gives regularized maxima with exact inactive branches.
Theorem 2.10 identifies positivity of the prescribed Yuan--Zhang
integrable adelic mixed measure under its stated hypotheses.

\item[\textup{B}.] \emph{Locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic
functions and mixed currents}, 10 November 2026, 32 pages.
Theorems 2.5--2.7 identify $\Cb$ with the local decreasing PL class,
and construct strongly positive mixed currents and weighted joint
decreasing continuity with background $[1]$.
Definition 2.4 and Lemma 7.2 specify actual-space coefficient Radon
measures and Borel multiplication.
Theorem 4.4, Lemma D.2, and Proposition 7.1 provide the common
projective line, frame, ordinary neighborhood, and decreasing pure
Fubini--Study approximants for a finite family of decreasing sequences.
Lemma D.4 supplies ordinary algebraic neighborhoods without changing
$K$. These common-domain inputs are needed in
Lemma~\ref{lem:common-majorants}; separate local regularizations with
shrinking domains would not suffice.

\item[\textup{A2}.] \emph{A non-Archimedean criterion for geometric
adelic nefness}, revised 12 October 2026, 31 pages.
Theorem 1.1 is the completed same-model geometric nefness theorem under
its number-field, integrable adelic line, and full Cartier-boundary
hypotheses. It preserves the open line and its prescribed
identifications. This is an accepted global application, not an open
problem in the present project. It is not used to prove the local
relative BT theorems below.
\end{description}

Any use of the broader analytic setting passes through the local
algebraic neighborhoods already supplied by \textup{B}. A finite
extension of $\mathbf Q_p$ can be realized as a number-field completion;
the use of \textup{R} does not change the prescribed absolute value.
No argument below makes a new base change or renormalizes integration.

\subsection{Three positivity cones}

On a finite original moment presentation, strongly positive forms are
generated by decomposable squares. Positive forms are represented by
positive semidefinite symmetric coefficient tensors. Weakly positive
forms are nonnegative on decomposable vectors. These cones need not
coincide in middle degree. A \emph{positive current} in this report is
nonnegative on positive complementary original forms, as in
\textup{R}, Convention 2.2. A strongly positive current is nonnegative
on weakly positive complementary forms, as in \textup{B}, Convention
2.3. Thus the arbitrary background considered here is not assumed
strongly positive.

We use the finite-matrix domination from \textup{R}, not a decomposition
of every symmetric test into decomposable squares. The latter would
lose a middle-degree annihilator unless one had strong positivity and
used the separate argument in \textup{B}, Lemma 5.1. Wedge with a
positive $(1,1)$-form preserves the original positive cone. More
generally, wedge with a strongly positive form preserves it; these are
the only cone-preserving wedge operations used in the proofs.

\section{Ordered products and relative finite-test estimates}
\label{sec:relative-cln-agent}

Throughout this section, $K/\mathbf Q_p$ is finite with its prescribed
absolute value. The space $X$ is good, Hausdorff, boundaryless and
quasi-smooth, of pure dimension $n$. All open sets are ordinary open sets,
and all forms are original CLD forms. We write $D=d'd''$.
The word \emph{positive} means dual positivity for the original positive
form cone used in R, Convention 2.2. It does not mean strong positivity.
The background $S$ is a symmetric positive $(p,p)$-current satisfying
$d'S=d''S=0$.

\begin{abstract}
Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be finite with its prescribed absolute value.
On an ordinary open in a good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth
$K$-analytic space, we prove that the actual difference of two
locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic functions with equal
original CLD curvature is continuous and classically pluriharmonic.
It follows that their relative curvatures agree for every fixed
symmetric original-positive separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed
background current. The mixed bounded Bedford--Taylor calculus
therefore descends in its differentiated slots to currents with
bounded classical local potentials.

The proof supplies the two gates left open in the fourth record:
kernel preservation after every complete scalar extension and
ordinary continuity of the actual curvewise harmonic difference.
The first uses prescribed smooth rows, finite-etale traces, full
analytic fiber potentials including type IV, and a simultaneous
product induction. The second uses a Shilov bound proved without
ambient semicontinuity, polynomial Noether coordinates, and exact
logarithmic interpolation on strictly semistable alteration charts.
All equalities are tested on the full original CLD test sheaf.
Explicit scope tests exclude weaker closedness, arbitrary bounded
upper-semicontinuous representatives, and an unrestricted passage
to relative energy or capacitary completions. The previously
proved seven fixed-background BT properties are retained as inputs.
An exact global finite-dimensional curvature hypothesis yields
local uniform compactness of normalized classical potentials.
Without that hypothesis, a two-intersection example shows that
the relative classical image can fail to be closed in total
variation even when no boundary values are prescribed.
\end{abstract}

\section{The question, conventions, and frozen inputs}
\label{sec:r5-inputs}

The question left open in the fourth record was
\begin{equation}
 D[u]=D[v]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D((u-v)S)=0,
 \qquad u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U),
 \label{eq:r5-main-question}
\end{equation}
for an arbitrary fixed symmetric positive separately closed
background current $S$. The equality on the left is an equality
of original CLD currents with background $[1]$. It must not be
silently interpreted as equality after multiplication by a
singular coefficient measure. The actual point values of $u$
and $v$ matter on the right.

The original ground field throughout the main theorem is a finite
extension $K/\mathbf Q_p$ with its given absolute value. An
\emph{allowed space} is good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth,
and of pure dimension. All opens are ordinary topological opens.
We set $D=d'd''$. A $(p,p)$-current on a space of dimension $n$
acts on original compact smooth $(n-p,n-p)$-forms. Unless a
different degree is explicitly stated, positivity is the original
positive cone of R, namely the symmetric quadratic-form cone of
\cite[Definition 5.1.1(c) and \S5.4]{CLD12}. It is not identified
with either strong or weak positivity.

The coefficient-Radon arguments use this middle cone directly.
They do not invoke the strong-test order-zero assertion as printed
in \cite[Proposition 7.2.9]{CLD25}. Section
\ref{sec:r5-weak-order-zero-tropical} gives an explicit closed
real-tropical counterexample to that broader assertion and checks
the distinct 2012 hypotheses. This does not change R's stipulated
cone or any of the authorized internal inputs.

The word \emph{actual} means that no function is replaced on a
null, polar, or coefficient-null set. For a locally bounded Borel
function $a$ and a coefficient-Radon current $T$, multiplication
means
\[
             \langle aT,\eta\rangle
                  =\int a\,d\mu_{T,\eta}
\]
on the actual Berkovich space. A measure specified only on one
tropical image does not give this operation.

\subsection{Logical structure of the new argument}

The analytic part extends the prescribed-row finite-etale
kernel argument to auxiliary complete fields. A continuous
potential for the \emph{full} analytic fiber of every nonrigid
point of the affine line then closes the scalar-extension
gate, including type IV. The product kernel is propagated
simultaneously in every finite product dimension. The
resulting analytic-map kernel gives actual harmonicity on
all curve pullbacks, including their type-I and type-IV values.

The geometric part does not assume that a curvewise harmonic
function is upper semicontinuous. It proves its Shilov bound
by finite flat coordinates and normalized algebraic curve
slices. Strictly semistable alteration charts supply continuous
logarithmic interpolation of their finite Shilov data. The
Shilov bound identifies the actual function with those
interpolants, and proper compact descent proves continuity.

classical psh. Applying the existing first-order positive
construction to the arbitrary background $S$ makes
$D((u-v)S)$ and its negative positive, which proves
\eqref{eq:r5-main-question}. The quotient is therefore
downstream of all the kernel and continuity arguments.

\section{Field-independent tools for prescribed smooth positive rows}
\label{sec:r5-prescribed-rows-package}

Let $F$ be a complete non-Archimedean field with its given absolute
value.  Let $U$ be a good Hausdorff boundaryless $F$-analytic space of
pure dimension $n\geq1$.  We use only the original CLD smooth forms,
their canonical integration, and $D=d'd''$.  A current is positive
in the original positive cone used in R, and all currents called
positive below are symmetric.  This is not a convention identifying
the positive, strongly positive and weakly positive cones.

A \emph{prescribed smooth positive row} for a function $u$ on an
ordinary open $O$ means original smooth functions $u_j$ on that
same $O$, with positive $(1,1)$-forms $Du_j$, such that $u_j$
decreases pointwise to the actual finite locally bounded function
$u$.  Whenever a continuous potential is used below, its smooth
positive approximation is likewise part of the hypotheses.  No
regularization theorem over $F$ is asserted.  In particular, these
results may be applied to rows already obtained over the original
finite extension of $\mathbf Q_p$ and then pulled back by an
analytic map or by scalar extension.

\subsection{Positive coefficient measures over the given field}

\begin{lemma}[Finite positive controls and actual coefficient measures]
\label{lem:r5-field-independent-radon}
\label{lem:r5-prescribed-coefficient-control}
Let $T$ be an original positive current of bidegree $(p,p)$ on $O$,
and put $q=n-p$.  For every original compact smooth complementary
test $\eta$, there is a signed Radon measure $\mu_{T,\eta}$ on $O$
such that
\[
 \langle T,a\eta\rangle=\int a\,d\mu_{T,\eta}
\]
for every original smooth scalar $a$.  The assignment is compatible
with finite localization, relations between original forms, and
common original moment refinements.

There are finitely many original positive compact smooth tests
$\Theta_\ell$ and a constant $C_\eta$, depending only on a fixed
presentation of $\eta$ and its compact support stage, such that
\[
 |\mu_{T,\eta}|\leq
 C_\eta\sum_\ell\mu_{T,\Theta_\ell}.
 \tag{R}
\]
The same controls work after adjoining additional scalar moments.
Consequently a fixed locally bounded Borel multiplier $a$ defines
the original current $aT$.  If $T_j\to T$ weakly and all these
currents are positive, then $aT_j\to aT$ for every fixed continuous
multiplier $a$.  Weak convergence alone is not claimed to allow
an arbitrary fixed discontinuous multiplier.
\end{lemma}

\begin{abstract}
This record continues the arbitrary-background bounded Bedford--Taylor
calculus and actual bounded-classical potential quotient proved in
R4--R5. Its main further result identifies the positive cone of the
actual bounded classical difference class: if $a,b\in\mathcal C_b$,
then $D[a-b]\ge0$ in the original CLD cone if and only if $a-b$ is
itself classical psh. The proof establishes order transfer on every
complete extension and analytic test map, retains actual curve endpoint
values, and recovers ambient upper semicontinuity through proper-fiber
maxima of finite Shilov interpolants. Curvature order and continuous
coefficient relations therefore transfer to every fixed allowed
positive closed background, including discontinuous potential slots.
The resulting mixed order estimates give qualified total-variation
stability. Arbitrary assigned bounded Borel representatives remain
outside these assertions.

In the actual delta-test category, every total-degree $(1,1)$ delta-form
acts over every allowed background with ordinary locality. Constant
real cycle relations act in all degrees, and every real delta-form has
an exact finite local generation by piecewise smooth coefficients and
constant cycles. Full actual analytic delta-testing is constructed for
the local weak closure of positive closed delta-form backgrounds,
including all their bounded BT tails, smooth regular flags, singular
effective Cartier divisors, integrable extended classical potential
curvatures, and integrable diffuse barycenters. The higher-degree analytic-relation
kernel for an arbitrary background remains open.

An actual bounded classical potential below the curvature of a
continuous potential is automatically continuous. Normalized families
with a compact continuous family of upper potentials are compact in
local uniform topology. Their actual mixed images are weakly closed on
the same domain, and their represented curvature quotients have joint
weak stability even with a varying positive closed background. A local
finite Shilov normalization also gives weighted stability for the
specified representatives; it does not identify arbitrary weights by
curvature alone.

In remaining degree one, sharp Hardy and strong capacitary constants
are respectively one and four. The universal finite-energy threshold
for concave capacity-growth moduli is determined. A compact Gauss set
has zero relative BT capacity but positive energy capacity; a measure
on it has a bounded continuous energy solution but no local bounded
classical difference potential. Exact convex-envelope and diffuse
carrier capacities give further qualified Borel regularity results.
Exact continuous classical interpolation on a fast polar Cantor set
gives explicit capacities for arbitrary bounded Borel radial graphs
and filled tubes over that diffuse parameter set.

For Dirichlet theory, completed degree-one feasibility has an exact
energy-dual criterion, while higher-degree variation criteria retain
explicit feasibility hypotheses. Counterexamples rule out unrestricted
relative Hessian root concavity and show that the actual zero-boundary
classical Monge--Ampere image can be nonconvex in every remaining degree
at least two, even for sums of smooth analytic-subspace integration
currents. All new proofs, direct consequences, failed routes and
unresolved gates have separate status labels.
\end{abstract}

settles order, and its proof uses no higher-degree delta extension.
The latter extension question retains the separate scopes below. This round uses Mihatsch's actual analytic
delta-form sheaf $B$, as defined by compatible data on all skeletons
and all refinements. Its total bidegree is used unless a tridegree is
displayed. The external map $B\to D$ is faithful, but faithfulness

We prove the following sufficient mechanism. Let
$\mathcal W^p(V)$ be the ordinary weak closure, on one fixed ordinary

backgrounds. Full actual delta-testing is constructed for

such backgrounds stay in that class. Smooth regular flags and their

equality of this class with all allowed backgrounds is not assumed.

\begin{abstract}
Over the original finite extension of $\mathbf Q_p$ and with its original
absolute value, we develop an unbounded Bedford--Taylor calculus for
arbitrary original symmetric middle-positive separately closed backgrounds.
We prove coefficient-controlled closedness of non-polar products, an exact
no-loss capacity-tail criterion, unbounded comparison and domination,
all-degree power-energy recursion, and graded first-order and energy
stability on every original refined test. Exact level currents yield
coarea, nonsmooth chain formulas, weak maxima and quantitative pole
representatives. On explicit strict analytic boxes we obtain full global
first-energy Green symmetry, the constant-one mixed energy inequality,
the sharp midpoint modulus, and a complete relative strong first-energy
space without a prescribed actual lower barrier. It has comparison,
domination, intrinsic truncation carriers, and bounded finite-mass
approximation. Explicit dominated data have a unique variational
maximizer on this full space. A separate barrier completion gives an
unbounded constrained variational retraction.
In remaining degree one we solve
the complete finite signed diffuse renormalized zero-boundary problem,
including exact level carriers and global total-variation convergence of
clipping curvatures, and its finite-diffuse obstacle problem. Counterexamples
preserve the boundary, integrability,
endpoint and classical-admissibility gates. Frozen results and rediscoveries
are distinguished from new proofs. General nonlinear classical Dirichlet
existence and the analytic PS/PL quotient remain unresolved in their
appropriate, explicitly stated scopes.
\end{abstract}
