\section{Fixed scope, proof dependencies, and the R11 advance}
\label{sec:r11-scope-main-results}

\subsection{The original analytic category is unchanged}

Throughout, $K$ is the fixed original finite extension of
$\mathbf Q_p$, equipped with its original absolute value.
The space $X$ is good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth,
and pure of dimension $n$.  Opens are ordinary analytic
opens.  We write $D=d'd''$.
Unless a statement explicitly specializes its degree,
$S$ is an arbitrary original symmetric middle-positive,
separately $d'$- and $d''$-closed $(p,p)$-current, and
$q=n-p\geq1$.
It is neither replaced by a smooth or geometric current
nor approximated by a special background class.
Smooth and integration backgrounds appear only in
explicit counterexamples to universal assertions.

All current identities are identities on every original
compactly supported smooth CLD complementary test form.
Every actual finite moment refinement of such a test
is permitted.  Middle, strong, and weak positivity cones
are distinct: rank-one squares and strongly positive
forms serve as coefficient controls, while the actual
positive-current assertions use the middle-positive
background and the correct complementary cone.
No ordinary current equality is automatically an
equality on an additional family of GK delta tests.

The terms classical psh, bounded BT product, original
coefficient-Radon measure, and classical extension to
complete-field curve tests retain their frozen meanings.
The seven bounded BT properties, relative CLN and
bounded energy calculus are \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}.
For a locally bounded classical tuple the notation is
\[
 T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)
              =Du_1\wedge\cdots\wedge Du_k\wedge S.
 \tag{M1}
\]
Every new unbounded object is constructed and justified
from those bounded inputs, with its own stated mass or
energy hypothesis.  Multiplication by an unbounded
potential is never performed before coefficient
integrability has been proved.

\subsection{The exact frozen continuation point}

The immediate baseline is the complete R10 archive,
whose exact SHA256 is
{\small\nolinkurl{4891735a31504e5154d7e027efb2fdf739dbf4645fb963f45a4b4943360b1402}}.
Its 226 listed manifest files and ZIP checks passed.
The archive is included unchanged under
\path{previous/NA_BT_R10_Complete_Archive_2026-11-11.zip}.
Its nested R9 archive has SHA256
{\small\nolinkurl{dafae83ac877f4bd5648ef7939de39f9f5bf114c6e7a711fe3f6732a3f3a68a4}};
the original authorized R8 archive has SHA256
{\small\nolinkurl{378c2ef39f98fb60dca80f3300cb6ec0bf5f0c370a6f93adc95714a8cd5c3254}}.
The complete earlier chain is retained through those exact archives.

R11 does not rewrite the matroidal, two-fan, polytopal,
real-product, actual quadratic-cover, intrinsic PS
curvature, or cap-order results already frozen in that
chain.  The internal research papers R, B and A2 keep
their authorized \texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT} status.
A2's completed geometric adelic nefness is not reopened.
Targeted source lookbacks in this round concern only
a specific dependency or novelty claim; they are not
new audits of the old inputs.

Each formal result below prints its status.
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{ll}
\texttt{EXTERNAL\_KNOWN}&\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}\\
\texttt{DIRECT\_COROLLARY}&\texttt{NEW\_PROVED}\\
\texttt{CONDITIONAL}&\texttt{OPEN}\\
\texttt{FALSE}&\texttt{FAILED\_ATTEMPT}
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
The last status preserves discarded routes and valid rediscoveries.
A new definition is distinguished from a theorem.
The word new means a proved R11 delta relative to the
frozen research chain, not a claim of priority over
the entire mathematical literature.

\subsection{Three domain levels and three distinct boundaries}

The new results have different domain hypotheses.
They must not be merged into an unconditional global
theorem by dropping those hypotheses.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The coefficient-controlled non-polar closedness
and general local mixed-energy criteria are ordinary-local
statements on the allowed analytic space.
\item The all-degree capacity controls require the
specified ordinary domain to have compact closure
inside the interior of one original affinoid.
The analytic compensator theorem proves why this
hypothesis controls every original refined test.
\item Global finite-mass tester approximation, full
$E^1$ Green calculus and the explicit simultaneous
pole representatives use a strict analytic Laurent
box, with the original $S$ defined on a neighborhood
of its closed box.  Arbitrary currents on arbitrary
opens are not asserted to extend across their boundary.
\end{enumerate}

For a negative extended classical potential $u$,
the compact-sublevel condition is
\[
 \mathrm{BG}(u,0):
       \quad\overline{\{u<-t\}}\Subset V
                              \quad\hbox{for every }t>0.
 \tag{M2}
\]
More generally, the comparison theorems use exactly
the printed compact positive-margin gaps.
This is an ordinary boundary condition.
It differs both from finite truncation loss and from
the zero-boundary condition in a relative energy
completion.  The last is specified by the closure
of the original compact smooth core and, for
unbounded measure data, by clipping membership and
vanishing radiation.

\subsection{Non-polar products and the exact no-loss cone}

For an actual negative classical tuple, put
$u_{i,j}=\max(u_i,-j)$ and
$E_j=\bigcap_i\{u_i>-j\}$.
The finite-level restrictions
\[
 {\bf1}_{E_j}\,
       T_{S,k}(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{k,j})
 \tag{M3}
\]
form a consistent increasing family of positive
coefficient measures.  Theorem
\ref{thm:r11-closed-nonpolar-product}
proves that their locally coefficient-finite limit
is separately closed on every original test.
The proof controls derivatives of bounded cutoffs
by a positive energy identity.  It does not assert
that an individual restricted current is closed.
The pole union need not be ordinary closed.

For one potential, write
$\mu_{u,j}=T_{S,q}(u_j,\ldots,u_j)$,
$\mu_u$ for its non-polar top measure, and
$\nu_{u,j}={\bf1}_{\{u\leq-j\}}\mu_{u,j}$.
The no-loss boundary cone is
\[
 \mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)
   =\{u\leq0:\ u\text{ extended classical psh},
       \ \mathrm{BG}(u,0),\ \nu_{u,j}(V)\longrightarrow0\}.
 \tag{M4}
\]
The exact capacity-tail criterion is
\[
 u\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
       t^q C_S(\{u<-t\};V)\longrightarrow0
 \tag{M5}
\]
within the printed boundary class.
Here the raw capacity is computed from the entire
normalized bounded classical tester family on the
same domain; its ordinary-open outer regularization
is denoted $C_S^*$.

The new comparison theorem needs no loss on the lower
potential and the stated compact-gap condition.
It yields the corresponding domination and uniqueness
modulo outer relative capacity.
Every compact-sublevel classical potential, even
before imposing no loss, has the proved
$O(t^{-q})$ deep-sublevel capacity bound and is
locally quasicontinuous for the relative outer
capacity.  General raw/outer equality is not
an input to these results.

\subsection{Power classes and the all-degree calculus}

For $\sigma>0$ the power class is
\[
 \mathcal E^\sigma_{S,\partial}(V)
     =\{u\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V):
                  e_\sigma(u):=\int_V(-u)^\sigma\,d\mu_u<\infty\}.
 \tag{M6}
\]
The capacity integral
\[
 J_\sigma(u)=
       \int_0^\infty t^{q+\sigma-1}
                        C_S(\{u<-t\};V)\,dt
 \tag{M7}
\]
characterizes this class with the stated boundary
hypothesis.  It controls mixed energies, exact
truncation tails, and nonmonotone stability in the
full localized capacity topology (PE16).
Finite non-polar energy alone, without no loss,
does not define this class.

On the one-affinoid domain, every finite tuple in a
positive power class has closed positive original
mixed products in every degree.  The complete
recursive equation holds for every $\sigma>0$:
\[
                D(u_iN_\alpha)=N_{\alpha+e_i},
                   \qquad |\alpha|\leq q-1.
 \tag{M8}
\]
All original coefficient multipliers are justified
before differentiation.  With $k=|\alpha|$, the
natural exponent budgets are
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{object with weight growth }W^a&
                    \text{fixed-family integrability budget}\\ \hline
 N_\alpha&a+k\leq q+\sigma\\
 d'(u_iN_\alpha),\ d''(u_iN_\alpha)&a+k+1\leq q+\sigma\\
 \Gamma_{N_\alpha}(u_i,u_l)&a+k+2\leq q+\sigma .
\end{array}
 \tag{M9}
\]
Energy terms are asserted only within their printed
degree range.  The endpoint budget is valid for a
fixed family, and for varying families under
uniform tail integrability.
A uniform bound of power energies alone gives
strict-exponent stability, not unconditional
endpoint continuity.
The explicit shell example sends the critical
weighted top measures to a nonzero rigid-point
mass although the potentials converge in the
specified localized capacity to zero.

On the strict boxes, the finite-mass boundary core
computes every raw Borel capacity exactly.
The new full global $E^1$ Green symmetry then gives
the optimal constant-one inequality
\[
 \int_V(-u_0)M(u_1,\ldots,u_q)
              \leq\prod_{i=0}^{q}e_1(u_i)^{1/(q+1)} .
 \tag{M10}
\]
It also gives global Aubin--Mabuchi variation and
strict concavity on the relative capacity quotient.
This is an integrated energy argument using the
positive energy matrix.  It does not assume a
pointwise Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for $S$.

\subsection{Relative completions and the sharp strong geometry}

On those same strict boxes, put
\[
 \mathscr I_S(u,v)=\int_V(u-v)(d\mu_v-d\mu_u),\qquad
 \mathscr A_S(u)=-\frac{e_1(u)}{q+1}.
 \tag{M12}
\]
The new first-energy tester estimate gives quantitative
control of every local original outer capacity by
$\mathscr I_S(u,v)^{2^{-q}}$ on bounded-energy sets.
The sharp uniform midpoint inequality is
\[
 \mathscr A_S\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)
       -\frac{\mathscr A_S(u)+\mathscr A_S(v)}2
      \geq\frac{1-2^{-q}}{2(q+1)}\mathscr I_S(u,v).
 \tag{M13}
\]
Its constant is optimal on every same-background class
containing a potential of positive first energy.
The proof is the all-degree finite binomial argument,
not an extrapolation from a finite numerical check.

The barrier completion first constructs Borel limits
above an actual $E^\sigma$ lower barrier, retaining
the original closed currents and their complete
recursive and graded calculus. Its comparison and
domination hold for the full normalized tester capacity;
strict Borel maximum locality and the exact nonpolar
truncation carriers are proved after the construction.
A completed envelope and an unbounded barrier-constrained
variational retraction are then defined without ordinary
upper regularization.

There is also a larger strong first-energy completion
$\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_{\rm str}$, defined by actual
$\mathscr I_S$-Cauchy rows without a prescribed common lower barrier.
The new uniform deep-tail and global boundary-tightness
proofs construct its actual Borel representatives, every
original current and critical multiplier, and its global
mixed energies. The resulting space is complete and satisfies
\[
 \widehat{\mathscr I}_S(u_j,u)\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \begin{cases}
 u_j\longrightarrow u\text{ in all local truncated outer capacities},\\
 \widehat e_1(u_j)\longrightarrow\widehat e_1(u).
 \end{cases}
 \tag{M14}
\]
Completeness uses an explicitly proved uniform continuity
modulus for the discrepancy, not an assumed triangle
inequality. The limit is not asserted to be an ambient
classical psh function or to have compact negative sublevels.
Its boundary class is the printed strong approximation class.

The characterization can also be made intrinsic: every bounded
truncation must be an admissible same-domain bounded capacitary
limit, and
\[
                  \int_0^\infty t^q
                        C_S^*(\{u<-t\};V)\,dt<\infty.
 \tag{M16}
\]
These two conditions are equivalent to membership in the
strong first-energy space. The proof first constructs legal
finite-mass barrier stages and only then the unbounded
current; it does not assume the sought product.
Comparison, domination, strict maximum locality and intrinsic
nonpolar carriers hold throughout this space. Increasing

\[
                         d'S=d''S=0.
 \tag{M1}
\]
Strong and weak positivity are not substituted for this middle cone.

supported smooth complementary CLD forms, after all actual tropical
moment refinements. Ordinary current equality is never silently
promoted to equality on all GK delta tests.

The bounded arbitrary-background BT calculus of R4 and the exact
R11 energy and relative boundary results are
\texttt{INTERNAL\_INPUT}. The internal papers R, B and A2 remain

\subsection{The energy domain and the precise completion}

The global energy results have the following domain hypothesis.
There is one compact original affinoid $B$ and a compact closed
Laurent box
\[

\]

A bounded continuous negative box barrier $\rho$ with compact
negative sublevels and finite top mass is part of the proved
R11 construction (TC3)--(TC4).

For Borel sets $E\subset V$, the raw and outer capacities are
\[

negative-sublevel boundary condition, the proved canonical
truncation no-loss condition, and finite first energy.

                       \mathscr C=
                       \widehat{\mathcal E}^{1}_{\rm str}(V)
 \tag{M4}
\]
is a distinct space of actual Borel classes modulo local
ordinary-open outer capacity zero. Its boundary condition is
strong approximation by the actual class, not a newly asserted
ordinary boundary value. Its members need not have ambient
classical representatives or a common actual lower barrier.

Write $\widehat N_k$ for its original mixed currents and
$\widehat\mu_u=\widehat N_q(u^{[q]})$. Its global mixed energy,
energy root, and strong discrepancy are
\[
 \begin{split}
 B(u_0,\ldots,u_q)&=\int_V(-u_0)\widehat N_q(u_1,\ldots,u_q),\\
 e(u)&=B(u^{[d]}),\qquad r(u)=e(u)^{1/d},\\
 I(u,v)&=e(u)+e(v)-B(u,v^{[q]})-B(v,u^{[q]}).
 \end{split}
 \tag{M5}
\]
The exact frozen inputs used below are symmetry and the constant-one
mixed energy inequality; positive integrated energy matrices; strong
completeness and all-original weighted current continuity; finite
maxima and monotone closure; the full relative Perron theorem; and
the original test decomposition into two actual finite-mass
potentials. Their sources are R11 (GE7)--(GE18), (EV1)--(EV8),
(IC10)--(IC22), (CC1)--(CC11), (CI1)--(CI8), (SE1)--(SE8), and
(HC14)--(HC15). They are retained with (M2). This record does not
turn them into theorems on arbitrary unrestricted domains.

\subsection{Closed bands provide a genuinely original conditional calculus}

The first mechanism does not require (M2). Let $s_i=\log|f_i|$
be unit-logarithm parameters on an ordinary open $U$. A positive
closed current $R$ is parameter-annihilated if
\[
                   d's_i\wedge R=d''s_i\wedge R=0
                   \quad\text{for every }i.
 \tag{M6}
\]
For every arbitrary original $S$, the derived current
$\Omega_s\wedge S$, where
$\Omega_s=\bigwedge_i d's_i\wedge d''s_i$, has this property
in the permitted degree. The background $S$ itself is unchanged.

\begin{theorem}[Closed bands and bounded parameter-family products]
\label{thm:r12-main-bands}
Let $R$ satisfy (M6), be symmetric middle-positive and separately
closed, and have degree $(P,P)$. Then every Borel parameter band
$\mathbf1_{\{s\in E\}}R$ is again an original positive separately
closed current. Ordinary-locally, there is a finite Radon measure
$\nu$ and a measurable family $R_a$ of original currents on the
same ambient $U$ such that
\[
 R=\int R_a\,d\nu(a),\qquad
 \mathbf1_{\{s\in E\}}R=\int_E R_a\,d\nu(a).
 \tag{M7}
\]
Outside one common null set, all $R_a$ are positive, separately
closed, parameter-annihilated, and carried by $s=a$ on every
original coefficient. They retain the entire original test sheaf.

Let $Y$ be an allowed original $K$-analytic space and let
$\pi:U\to Y$ be an original analytic map. For each $i$, let
$H_i(a,y)$ be jointly Borel, uniformly bounded on compact
parameter/reference products, with every actual slice $H_i(a,\cdot)$
locally bounded original classical psh. Put
$h_i(x)=H_i(s(x),\pi(x))$. For $P+k\leq n$, the intrinsic recursion
\[
 D\bigl(h_1D(h_2\cdots D(h_kR)\cdots)\bigr)
       =\int T_{R_a,k}(H_1(a,\pi(\cdot)),\ldots,H_k(a,\pi(\cdot)))
                                                        \,d\nu(a)
 \tag{M8}
\]
is positive, separately closed and mixed symmetric. It obeys local
relative CLN bounds, Borel parameter linearity, and full weighted
joint decreasing continuity when every specified family
$H_{i,m}$, including any scalar-weight slot, decreases on the
whole parameter/reference product to an admissible slice family,
with the printed compact slice bounds.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} (restatement).}
The complete proofs are in
Sections~\ref{sec:r12-closed-parameter-bands},
\ref{sec:r12-original-current-disintegration}, and
\ref{sec:r12-bounded-borel-family-bt}.
Conditional currents remain on the original $K$-space. No
residue-field BT theory, geometric inverse pushforward, or
product-test spanning assertion is used.

\subsection{Energy duals separate variational and source questions}

Under (M2), form $\mathbb D_S=\mathscr C-\mathscr C$ with
\[
 \|h\|_{\rm ed}
     =\inf_{h=a-b}\bigl(r(a)+r(b)\bigr),\qquad
 J(u)(h)=-\int_V h\,d\widehat\mu_u.
 \tag{M9}
\]
The first infimum is over $a,b\in\mathscr C$.
The strong-continuous dual consists of the norm-dual functionals
continuous on every strongly convergent cone row.

\begin{theorem}[A closed source image and an exact source gap]
\label{thm:r12-main-energy-source}
The normed space $(\mathbb D_S,\|\cdot\|_{\rm ed})$ is an
actual Borel Banach space and $\|u\|_{\rm ed}=r(u)$ on the cone.
The image $J(\mathscr C)$ is norm closed in $\mathbb D_S^*$, and
$\|J(u)-J(v)\|_*$ is a complete metric inducing the strong topology.

For every strong-continuous dual functional $\ell$, there is a
unique $u=\Pi(\ell)$ and normal residual $n$ such that
\[
 \ell=J(u)+n,\qquad n(v)\leq0\ (v\in\mathscr C),\qquad n(u)=0.
 \tag{M10}
\]
This is the unique maximizer of $\ell(v)-e(v)/d$, not automatically
a source solution.

Let $\mu$ be a literal positive Radon datum with a strong-continuous
energy functional and at least one completed subsolution.
Let $H_\mu$ be the greatest relative subsolution furnished by
the frozen Perron theorem, and let $u_\mu=\Pi(\ell_\mu)$. Then
\[
 \Delta_S(\mu)=e(H_\mu)-e(u_\mu)\geq0,\qquad
 I(H_\mu,u_\mu)\leq q\Delta_S(\mu).
 \tag{M11}
\]
Moreover $\Delta_S(\mu)=0$ if and only if $\mu$ is the original
top measure of a member of $\mathscr C$. When it exists, this
potential is unique and equals both $H_\mu$ and $u_\mu$.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} (restatement).}
The proofs are in
Sections~\ref{sec:r12-energy-difference},
\ref{sec:r12-nonlinear-dual-source}, and
\ref{sec:r12-perron-variational-gap}.
A capacity modulus with
$\int_0^1 F(s)s^{-1-1/d}\,ds<\infty$ supplies an explicit
class of literal signed data in this dual, without requiring
domination by a single source.

There is also a distinct order-energy Banach lattice $\mathbb L_S$,
with
\[
 \|h\|_{\mathbb L_S}
       =r(P(-|h|)),\qquad
 P(f)=\sup_{\rm rel}\{v\in\mathscr C:v\preceq f\}.
 \tag{M12}
\]
It provides new literal scalar multipliers for every original
completed mixed current. The potential cone stays closed and
unchanged. The old weighted total-variation source distance is
the dual norm on this lattice; it is not the signed distance
in (M9).

\begin{theorem}[One geometry-only probe detects literal source solvability]
\label{thm:r12-main-single-normal-probe}
Under (M2), there is one bounded continuous original classical
finite-mass potential $\psi_0$, depending only on the analytic box,
with $-1\leq\psi_0<0$. Let $\mu$ be a literal positive Radon datum
whose energy functional is strong-continuous, and put
$u=\Pi(\ell_\mu)$ and $n=\ell_\mu-J(u)$. Then
\[
 \Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu)=-n(\psi_0)\geq0,
 \qquad
 \Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu)=0
       \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \widehat\mu_u=\mu
       \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mu\in\widehat\mu(\mathscr C).
 \tag{M17}
\]
For every original real compact smooth scalar $\phi$, there is
$\varepsilon_\phi>0$, depending on the original finite test stage
and $\phi$ but not on $S$ or $\mu$, such that
\[
 \left|\int\phi\,d(\widehat\mu_u-\mu)\right|
              \leq \varepsilon_\phi^{-1}\Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu).
 \tag{M18}
\]
No subsolution family is assumed. For a nonliteral energy dual,
zero in (M17) implies only zero compact-test shadow, not zero
functional on the entire energy space.
\end{theorem}

\noindent\textbf{Status: \texttt{NEW\_PROVED} (restatement).}
Section~\ref{sec:r12-single-probe-normal-residual} constructs
$\psi_0$ so that $\psi_0\pm\varepsilon_\phi\phi$ are actual
admissible potentials. Applying the normal inequalities to these
two perturbations proves (M18). Literalness then identifies the
zero shadow with the entire original source equation. This proves
a testable exact criterion, not automatic vanishing of $\Xi$.

\subsection{A complete specified parameter module, not an ambient replacement}

Assume (M2) with $R$ as background, with the unit parameters $s_i$
defined on an ordinary neighborhood of $K_0$ and with (M6) holding
there. Let $R$ have degree $(P,P)$ and set
$k=n-P\geq1$, $d_R=k+1$. The geometry-only probe may be chosen
for this degree as well. Write
\[
 \omega=(D\psi_0)^k\wedge R,\qquad
 \theta=s_*((-\psi_0)\omega),\qquad
 h_c=\psi_0 c(s),\quad c\in L^{d_R}_+(\theta).
 \tag{M19}
\]
These are explicitly defined relative Borel parameter potentials;
they need not be ambient classical psh.

\begin{theorem}[Parameter energy, compatible sources, and attained capacity]
\label{thm:r12-main-parameter-module}
The mixed products of the potentials (M19) are intrinsic positive
separately closed original currents on every original test, for
$0\leq j\leq k$:
\[
 T_{R,j}(h_{c_1},\ldots,h_{c_j})
    =\left(\prod_{i=1}^j c_i(s)\right)(D\psi_0)^j\w

title: Moving interfaces separate energy topologies and produce a non-Radon dual functional

moving_seams_topology.md # Moving interfaces separate energy topologies and produce a non-Radon dual functional

Status: PROVED-INTERNAL after author-separated internal audit; a higher-dimensional interface realization of an already frozen mechanism, not a new topology-separation principle. This is an explicit original-category example, not a counterexample to the unresolved C1 assertion for literal positive Radon data. It uses remaining degree q=1 in every space dimension n>=2; it does not identify q=1 with dimension one.

## 1. Exact frozen meanings

The recovered exact R12 source `12bde9976ef8d8dcb3abbfc23f71f8e1a1ae37a6195de0dcdd13f09c5c0f5f45.tex` defines

    D_S=C-C,
    ||h||_ed=inf{ r(a)+r(b): a,b in C, h=a-b},
    r(a)=e(a)^(1/2) for q=1.                            (T1)

This is ED3. The same source explicitly says it is not the discrepancy I or a Hilbert norm. ED6 only bounds I by the energy-difference norm, and explicitly does not identify their topologies. ED11 gives the separate source-functional estimate delta_*(mu_u,mu_v)<=I(u,v)^(1/2) when q=1. We use these exact scopes. Frozen R12 CG1–CG10 already proves strict separation and constructs a positive ED-bounded functional outside the strong dual on an annulus. Its exact recovered source has SHA256 30c2041787270a4a075953adc6440df5be1e67cc001210287478034a7b64e3de. The example below realizes the same mechanism with moving hypersurface masses for every n>=2 and smooth fixed background; it does not uncover a contradiction or a new general separation principle.

## 2. Actual potentials with moving spheres

Use the fixed original torus, Laurent box, field, norm, and parent max-reference w, quadratic on a protected ball. Here take S=beta^(n-1)[X], so q=1. Choose radii 0<a<b with Bbar_b inside that quadratic region. On its closure let m=min(-w)>0. Choose one t in (0,1/2) with t b^2/2<m/2. For each R in [a,b] define

    psi_R(x)=(R^2-|x|^2)/2 on B_R, and 0 outside,
    u_R=w+t psi_R(torus moment).

The interior Hessian is (1-t)I, the exterior is the original w, and the sphere Hessian jump is t R nu tensor nu dS. Thus u_R is actual continuous psh, negative, with the same ordinary zero boundary and the same finite-mass/bounded-energy/no-loss qualifications as the parent. This argument is independent of the q>=2 polynomial construction.

For q=1, distributional differentiation directly gives

    mu_(u_R)-mu_w
       =t (n-1)! sigma_*[-n 1_(B_R) dx+R dS_R].          (T2)

Full original tests are retained: mollify the convex local profile, apply the smooth calibration, and pass D of the order-zero coefficient current to the uniform limit. The sphere term can also be read directly from the jump of the first derivatives. Write omega=area(S^(n-1)) for the unit sphere.

For r,s in [a,b], the potential difference is compactly supported in B_b. Its gradient is zero inside B_min(r,s), equals plus or minus t x in the intervening annulus, and is zero outside B_max(r,s). The actual Green identity, or direct real integration by parts with (T2), therefore gives

    I(u_r,u_s)
       =t^2 (n-1)! omega/(n+2) |r^(n+2)-s^(n+2)|.       (T3)

The potentials converge uniformly as r->s. Their energies also converge: all source differences are supported in the protected compact ball, the sources converge vaguely by (T2), their masses are uniformly bounded, and the potentials converge uniformly; outside the ball both potentials and sources are unchanged. Thus (T3) is convergence in the frozen strong discrepancy sense on this bounded-energy family.

## 3. A uniform lower bound in the energy-difference norm

Let r!=s and h=u_r-u_s. For any decomposition h=A-B with A,B in the full completed cone C, linearity at q=1 gives mu_A-mu_B=mu_(u_r)-mu_(u_s) as original Radon measures. The right side has positive sphere component

    t (n-1)! r sigma_*(dS_r)

on E_r=sigma(partial B_r); neither the other sphere nor the absolutely continuous bulk terms charge E_r. Positivity of mu_A and mu_B therefore forces mu_A to dominate that component. The mixed energy inequality gives

    r(w) r(A) >= integral(-w) dmu_A
       >= t (n-1)! m omega r^n
       >= t (n-1)! m omega a^n=:c0>0.

Here r(w)>0: its smooth positive source on the protected ball and w<0 give positive energy. Taking the infimum over ALL completed decompositions in (T1), not only toric ones, proves

    ||u_r-u_s||_ed >= c0/r(w)  whenever r!=s.            (T4)

Hence strong discrepancy convergence, uniform convergence, and convergence of individual energies do not imply energy-difference norm convergence. The lower bound concerns a fixed original background and the full completed difference norm. No pointwise-order assumption has been substituted for additive order.

This also separates two source distances already distinguished in ED13. The signed source-functional dual norm tends to zero by ED11 and (T3). But the absolute weighted-variation expression tested against w/r(w) is bounded below by c0/r(w), and the ordinary total variation cannot tend to zero because the two sphere measures are mutually singular with masses bounded below. Signed cancellation is essential here.

## 4. An explicit bounded positive cone functional that is not literal Radon integration

Choose distinct R_j in [a,b] converging to R_* in (a,b), with R_j!=R_*. Let

    E=union_j sigma(partial B_(R_j)),
    F=(-w) 1_E.

E is Borel: each sphere image is compact, and the union is countable. F is a bounded nonnegative Borel function supported in a fixed original compact set. For A in C define

    ell(A)=integral F dmu_A.

This is finite, additive and positively homogeneous, because q=1 sources are linear and

    0<=ell(A)<=integral(-w)dmu_A<=r(w)r(A).

Extend to D_S by ell(A-B)=ell(A)-ell(B). The extension is well-defined: equality of two potential differences gives equality of their linear original source differences. Equation (T1) gives

    |ell(h)|<=r(w)||h||_ed.                             (T5)

So ell is a bounded real functional on the energy-difference Banach space, nonnegative on its cone. But mu_w(E)=0, and (T2) gives

    ell(u_(R_j))=t(n-1)! R_j integral_(partial B_Rj)(-w(sigma(x))) dS_x >=c0,
    ell(u_(R_*))=0.                                    (T6)

Thus ell is not strongly discrepancy-continuous on the cone, even on this uniformly bounded actual family. This explicitly separates the whole ED Banach dual from the subspace of functionals continuous for the frozen strong cone topology.

Moreover ell cannot be represented by literal integration against any signed locally finite original Radon measure nu on potentials. The differences h_j=u_(R_j)-u_(R_*) are supported in the fixed original compact set K=trop^{-1}(Bbar_b), and

    ||h_j||_infty <= t |R_j^2-R_*^2|/2 ->0.

A signed locally finite Radon measure therefore satisfies

    |integral h_j dnu| <= ||h_j||_infty |nu|(K) ->0,

whereas ell(h_j)>=c0 by (T6). This contradiction works with either sign convention for representation. No density of moment tests or all original smooth scalars is required.

This functional is not a positive Radon datum and therefore does NOT refute C1. Positivity on the energy cone and ED boundedness cannot replace literal Radon representation or strong continuity, exactly as already demonstrated abstractly by the frozen CG example.

## 5. Status boundaries

The exact sphere-source formula and full-cone lower bound are a new explicit high-dimensional realization within this work, with no global originality claim. The separation mechanism and dual-class obstruction were already proved in R12 CG1–CG10; do not count them again as a new C1 result. It neither changes the three completion definitions nor solves the arbitrary positive-Radon continuity gate. General A1/GQ/KC12/RV4, C1/SR8, B1, and C2 remain OPEN.

nonradial_seam_extension.md # Sphere seams over a nonradial strictly convex reference

Status: PROVED-INTERNAL derivation, submitted to the root for independent review. This extends the exact seam formula beyond references constant on the sphere. It is a local real Hessian calculation transferred through the frozen smooth full-test calibration and bounded BT continuity, not an arbitrary-background source theorem.

## 1. Assumptions and statement

Fix n≥2, 2≤q≤n, 0<α<1, and B=B_R centered at zero. Let v be C^{2,α} on a neighborhood of Bbar_{2R}, and let z∈C^{2,α}(Bbar), with z=0 on ∂B. Assume both D²v and D²(v+z) on their relevant closed regions are uniformly positive definite. Write

    b(ξ)=∂νz(ξ),       A_T(ξ)=D²v(ξ)|_{T_ξ∂B},

and assume b≤0. Let V=v+z inside B and V=v outside. The function is continuous and convex, since its bulk Hessians are positive and its gradient jump is −bν. Define

    J_v(b)(ξ)=∫_{b(ξ)}^0 σ_{q−1}(A_T(ξ)+(t/R)I_T)dt.     (NS1)

Then the real Hessian measure obtained as the limit of smooth convex convolutions of V has bulk density σ_q(D²V) off the sphere and sphere density J_v(b)dS. In particular it has the distribution/measure formula

    σ_q(D²V)_{measure}
      =1_B σ_q(D²v+D²z)dx
       +1_{outside B} σ_q(D²v)dx
       +J_v(b)dS_{∂B}.                                  (NS2)

The subscript in (NS2) denotes the approximated Hessian measure, not the undefined pointwise polynomial of a matrix-valued distribution. No singular matrices are multiplied.

The formula remains valid if v has nonconstant boundary values. Its proof below therefore deliberately does not use a bounded Newton-flux argument.

## 2. Boundary Hessian structure

Because z vanishes on the sphere, ∇z=bν there. Differentiating twice along a great circle gives D²z|_T=(b/R)I_T. Thus its two tangent Hessian limits at ξ are

    A_T(ξ)+(b(ξ)/R)I_T     on the inside,
    A_T(ξ)                on the outside.

Both are positive definite by the assumptions. Their affine interpolants are consequently positive definite. The function b belongs to C^{1,α} on the sphere, hence is Lipschitz.

Integration by parts across the interface gives the weak Hessian

    D²V=(D²v+1_B D²z)dx + (−b)ν⊗ν dS.                 (NS3)

This identity also proves convexity for b≤0. Conversely any convex gluing of the specified two C² pieces forces b≤0 by the normal one-dimensional slope condition.

## 3. Boundary-layer calculation with actual convolutions

Choose a nonnegative radial C∞ mollifier ρ supported in the unit ball, with integral one, and write ρ_ε(x)=ε^{−n}ρ(x/ε). Use V_ε=V*ρ_ε on a slightly smaller neighborhood of Bbar_R. These are actual smooth convex functions and converge locally uniformly to V.

In the thin layer, parametrize x=ξ+εsν(ξ), ξ∈∂B, |s|≤2. Use an orthonormal frame at ξ with its last vector ν(ξ). Radiality makes the following one-dimensional profiles independent of the chosen tangential frame:

    k(s)=∫_{R^{n−1}} ρ(y′,s)dy′,
    η(s)=∫_{y_n>s} ρ(y)dy.

They satisfy η′=−k, η=1 for s≤−1, and η=0 for s≥1. A point y=x−εa is in B if and only if a_n>s+O(ε) for bounded a. Therefore the fraction of its convolution kernel on the inside tends uniformly to η(s). Hölder continuity of the bulk Hessians, the smooth sphere geometry and the bounded compact support of ρ give the tangent block

    (D²V_ε)TT=A_T(ξ)+η(s)(b(ξ)/R)I_T+o(1),              (NS4)

uniformly in ξ,s. More precisely the bulk error is O(ε^α)+O(ε), and the singular surface contribution to TT is O(ε).

To see the latter estimates and the normal scale directly, parametrize nearby sphere points by tangent variables εu. Their normal is ν(ξ)+O(ε), with tangent component O(ε), and their surface element is ε^{n−1}(1+O(ε²))du. In convolution (NS3), the normal-normal surface contribution is

    (−b(ξ)) k(s)/ε + O(1),

uniformly. The O(1) follows from Lipschitz variation of b and smooth variation of the kernel argument under the quadratic sphere graph. Mixed surface entries are O(1); tangent surface entries are O(ε). Bounded bulk Hessians therefore yield

    (D²V_ε)nn=(−b(ξ))k(s)/ε+O(1),
    (D²V_ε)nT=O(1).                                    (NS5)

These are absolute estimates; they remain valid at points where b=0.

For a symmetric block matrix with tangent block A, mixed vector u and normal entry c, the elementary-symmetric expansion is

    σ_q([[A,u],[u^T,c]])
       =c σ_{q−1}(A)+σ_q(A)−u^T T_{q−2}(A)u.           (NS6)

Here σ_q(A)=0 if q exceeds its size, and T_0=I. Identity (NS6) follows by expanding each principal q-minor: those omitting the normal coordinate give σ_q(A), while those including it have determinant c det(A_I)−u_I^T cof(A_I)u_I. Summation gives the Newton tensor in the final term. In particular the remainder beyond c σ_{q−1}(A) is uniformly bounded when A,u are bounded.

Combining (NS4)--(NS6) gives the uniform layer limit

    ε σ_q(D²V_ε)(ξ+εsν)
      →(−b(ξ))k(s)σ_{q−1}(A_T(ξ)+η(s)b(ξ)I_T/R).       (NS7)

It also gives a uniform bound on the left-hand side. The uniform limit here uses α>0, bounded C² norms, and the Lipschitz boundary coefficient; there is no unproved control of products of singular measures.

## 4. Passage to measures and evaluation of the normal integral

Away from the sphere V_ε converges in C² on compact subsets of either side. Thus its density converges to the printed bulk density. In a tubular neighborhood the normal coordinates above have volume element

    dx=ε(1+εs/R)^{n−1}ds dS(ξ).

Use (NS7), its uniform bound, and continuity of an arbitrary compactly supported real test φ to pass to the limit in the layer integral. The limiting surface density is

    ∫_{−2}^2 (−b)k(s)σ_{q−1}(A_T+η(s)bI_T/R)ds.

For b<0, substitute η′=−k and then t=bη. Since η decreases from 1 to 0, this equals

    ∫_b^0 σ_{q−1}(A_T+tI_T/R)dt.

For b=0 both expressions are zero. This proves (NS1)--(NS2), including convergence against arbitrary continuous compact real tests. For completeness, one may first integrate over the fixed layer of thickness 2ε, where the preceding uniform bounds apply, and then over its complement; densities on the latter remain uniformly bounded because the convolution sees only a single C² piece. No mass is omitted in an intermediate shrinking region.

Since the tangent interpolants are uniformly positive definite, J_v(b)≥0 and J_v(b)=0 if and only if b=0. If their common lower eigenvalue bound is c_T>0, then

    J_v(b)≥binom(n−1,q−1)c_T^{q−1}(−b).

Likewise an upper eigenvalue bound gives the corresponding upper estimate. Thus zero seam is equivalent to matched normal derivatives within this specified piecewise-C² class.

## 5. Original non-Archimedean source formula

Let W be a known actual bounded admissible reference on the original torus box, equal to v(t) on the protected moment patch; assume it retains the neighborhood extension and actual-core qualifications used in the parent construction. Define U=W+ztilde(t), with ztilde zero outside B. The above real convexity makes U actual psh locally, and it glues to W outside B. A separately checked uniform budget preserves negativity, ordinary boundary values and lower-barrier bounds. Compact CLN and boundedness then supply finite mass/energy and unchanged deep truncations in the same way as before.

For S=β^{n−q}[X], the frozen smooth full-test calibration of each V_ε is

    μ_(V_ε)=K_q σ_*(σ_q(D²V_ε)dx),    K_q=q!(n−q)!.

For any original compact smooth scalar η, its pullback η∘σ is a continuous real test on the compact moment stage. The convergence just proved applies to it. Frozen bounded BT continuity under local uniform convergence passes the left-hand side to μ_U. A moment cutoff equal to one near Bbar gives the full source identity

    μ_U=μ_W+K_q σ_*{
      [σ_q(D²v+D²z)−σ_q(D²v)]1_B dx + J_v(b)dS} .        (NS8)

The exterior source remains unchanged. All original compact smooth scalar tests and their actual moment refinements are retained. The formula is not asserted for arbitrary positive backgrounds S or arbitrary GK delta tests.

## 6. A check exposing the limitation of the earlier flux proof

When v is constant on the sphere, the tangential gradient in the layer is O(ε), so the earlier bounded Newton-flux proof applies. If v has nonconstant boundary values, the tangential gradient can be O(1), while the tangent Newton-tensor block is O(ε^{−1}). The flux can then have a concentrated tangential part, and taking only the difference of its classical normal boundary values is invalid.

For an explicit check, add the affine function a·x to the quadratic reference p, and choose z=k(|x|²−R²)/2 inside B, with −1<k<0. This changes no Hessian, so the true seam density must be independent of a. The naive expression [F_out−F_in]·ν/q instead acquires the additional term

    C1(a·ν)/q [1−(1+k)^{q−1}],

which is generally nonzero. The missing concentrated tangential flux cancels it. The boundary-layer proof (NS3)--(NS7) correctly depends only on the Hessian tangent block and gives the affine-invariant density (NS1).

This is a check on the proof method, not a counterexample to (NS1). It explains why the new nonradial-base proof cannot simply repeat the constant-boundary flux argument.

order_ideal_interface.md # The constructed range and the original additive order ideal

Status: root derivation for independent review. The statements below are an interface lemma and direct corollaries of this round's source constructions and the frozen R17 LI2--LI8 module. They are not a proof of LI13, general C1, or general C2.

## 1. An actual embedding for clamped corrections

Use the original torus reference w from the parent: it is quadratic on B_(2R), negative on the original Laurent box, and extends as bounded psh to a neighborhood of its closure. Let m=min_(Bbar_R)(-w)>0. Let X=C^{2,alpha}(Bbar_R), with norm controlling the supremum and every Hessian entry, and let h have zero Dirichlet and normal traces on the sphere. Write tilde h for its zero extension. Set

    C_w=2 max{n,1/m},    a=C_w ||h||_X.

Then both a w+tilde h and a w-tilde h are actual admissible nonpositive psh functions. For h=0 use the zero cone element. For nonzero h, on B_R their Hessians are aI +/- D^2h>=0 and their values are at most -a m+||h||_infty<0. The matched zero gradient introduces no interface current. Outside B_R they equal a w, and the open collar glues them to the unchanged reference. Their ordinary boundary values, lower-barrier bounds, neighborhood extensions, finite masses, bounded energies and no-loss properties follow exactly as in the parent actual-core qualification. In particular this proves additive cone inequalities, not just inequalities of values.

This elementary construction works for every permitted original background S extending to the same compact neighborhood: actual psh positivity is established before wedging with S, and compact CLN gives the required finite masses. If w represents a nonzero element in that background's frozen completed cone, R17 LI2--LI4 therefore give

    tilde h in X_w,
    ||tilde h||_w <= C_w ||h||_X,
    ||tilde h||_ed <= 2 r(w) C_w ||h||_X.               (O1)

Here r(w)=e(w)^(1/(q+1)) and ||.||_ed is precisely the frozen energy-difference norm, not a newly identified Q-order or capacity norm. If w is zero in that relative cone, the same additive inequalities force the displayed differences to be zero there; no nonzero principal-ideal claim is made.

For a known nonradial reference W with D^2v>=cI on the changed ball, replace n by n/c and m by min(-W). The same proof applies; all constants depend on that specified reference.

For the graph construction with S=beta^(n-q)[X], (O1) and the proved Hölder Lipschitz bound give

    ||u_g-u_g'||_ed <= [4 r(w) C_w ||K||/C1] ||g-g'||_{C^alpha}. (O2)

If C_w||h(g)||_X<=a0<1, the already frozen additive-order mixed positivity yields actual Borel Radon bounds

    (1-a0)^q mu_w <= mu_(u_g) <= (1+a0)^q mu_w.          (O3)

This is a consequence of the explicit two-sided psh construction, not a deduction from pointwise order. Likewise LI6 and polynomial telescoping give

    |mu_(w+h)-mu_(w+k)|
      <= q(1+a0)^(q-1) ||h-k||_w mu_w                  (O4)

for two perturbations in that ideal ball. These are the frozen polynomial domination consequences restricted to the newly constructed graph. They do not prove an inverse on all L-infinity data, and do not resolve strong continuity for arbitrary literal Radon data.

## 2. Compatible nearby sources outside this principal ideal

The positive sphere compensator gives a useful opposite check. Define the continuous compact real function

    psi(x)=(R^2-|x|^2)/2 for |x|<R, and psi=0 outside.

For 0<t<=t0<1/2, with t0 additionally chosen small enough for negativity of w+t0 psi, put u_t=w+t psi. In the ball its Hessian is (1-t)I; at the sphere its gradient jump is t R nu. Hence u_t is an actual bounded psh potential with the same exterior, ordinary boundary and core qualifications as w. This is a direct explicit instance of `seam_proof.md`, not a new general existence mechanism.

Let E be the image of the sphere under the Gauss section and put d_t=1-(1-t)^q>0. The full original source formula is

    mu_(u_t)-mu_w
      = -n! d_t sigma_*(1_B dx)
        +q!(n-q)! [C1 R/q] d_t sigma_*(dS).             (O5)

The bulk and sphere terms are mutually singular, carried respectively by the disjoint sets sigma(B) and sigma(boundary B), and have opposite signs. Their topological supports need not be disjoint. Since C1/q=binom(n,q)/n and |B|=R|sphere|/n,

    ||mu_(u_t)-mu_w||_TV=2 n! |B| d_t ->0.             (O6)

Here total variation means the total mass of the absolute signed measure, without the alternative probabilistic factor 1/2. The original moment map and Gauss section are continuous and the sphere is compact, so E is a compact Borel set in the Hausdorff analytic space. Smooth calibration gives mu_w(E)=0, whereas (O5) gives mu_(u_t)(E)>0.

Nevertheless u_t-w does not belong to X_w for any t>0. If it did, frozen LI6 applied to the finite polynomial expansion of mu_(w+(u_t-w)) would make every term absolutely continuous with respect to mu_w, and hence mu_(u_t)<<mu_w. That contradicts the positive mass on E. Equivalently, at the real profile level no finite multiple of the smooth reference curvature on the sphere controls both signs of the nonzero singular jump.

This absence of a finite X_w norm is compatible with convergence in the frozen strong energy-difference space. The curve is affine:

    u_t-w=(t/t0)(u_(t0)-w),

where u_(t0) and w are fixed cone members. Homogeneity of ||.||_ed therefore gives ||u_t-w||_ed ->0. More explicitly let A=w+u_(t0). Then

    (1/t0) A+psi=(2/t0)u_(t0),
    (1/t0) A-psi=(2/t0)w.

Thus psi belongs to the larger actual principal ideal X_A, with norm at most 1/t0, and LI4 gives ||u_t-w||_ed<=2 r(A)t/t0. This is one common controlling potential for the entire explicit family, not a claim that every strongly convergent family admits such a control.

The consequence for the research program is precise: even a full local graph inside X_w cannot be asserted to exhaust a strong energy neighborhood of compatible actual sources. New interface masses can appear in compatible potentials arbitrarily close to w in that strong norm. This is not a counterexample to C1; the constructed family actually has good continuity and a common larger ideal. It also does not identify any of the three completions.

## 3. A common ideal for the fixed-interface graph

Retain A=w+u_(t0)=2w+t0 psi from section 2. On B_R its Hessian is (2-t0)I, on the sphere it has positive Hessian surface coefficient t0 R, and on the unchanged exterior it equals 2w. Let k be any C^{2,alpha} function on Bbar_R with zero Dirichlet trace, not necessarily zero normal trace, and extend it by zero. Put b_k=partial_nu k. Its distribution Hessian has bulk D^2k and surface coefficient -b_k in the normal direction. If a satisfies

    a(2-t0)>=||D^2k||_op,
    a t0 R>=||b_k||_infty,
    a min_(Bbar_R)(-A)>=2||k||_infty,

then both aA+tilde k and aA-tilde k are actual admissible psh functions: their bulk Hessians and their normal surface coefficients are nonnegative, their values are nonpositive with a strict negative margin on the changed compact set, and outside they equal aA. Their finite mass and core conditions follow by the same original neighborhood/CLN argument. Since all three right-hand sides are bounded by a fixed constant times ||k||_{C^{2,alpha}}, there is a finite C_A with

    ||tilde k||_A<=C_A ||k||_{C^{2,alpha}}.              (O7)

For k=0 use zero. Applied to differences of the two-parameter solutions in `prescribed_surface_graph.md`, this proves Lipschitz continuity in the frozen energy-difference norm on each common parameter budget. For reference w, one also has w in X_A, so LI6 gives measure domination and Lipschitz source estimates in X_A. For a different nonradial reference W, enlarge the anchor to A_W=A+W: X_A is contained in X_(A+W), and W belongs to that larger ideal. Thus LI6 yields those source estimates with the common enlarged anchor A_W; W in X_A is not assumed. These are direct polynomial/order consequences for the explicit fixed-interface sector, not general C1.

## 4. Why a single ideal does not cover arbitrarily moving interfaces

Fix 0<R_-<R_+ inside the quadratic protected region, and one small t>0 preserving negativity for every radius in that interval. For each R in [R_-,R_+] construct the section-2 actual potential u_R=w+t psi_R. Let E_R be the Gauss image of its radius-R sphere. These are pairwise disjoint compact Borel sets, all lying in one fixed original compact moment annulus, and mu_(u_R)(E_R)>0 by the full source formula. The reference has mu_w(E_R)=0.

There cannot be a single cone member A such that every u_R-w belongs to X_A. Indeed replace A by A+w, so that both w and all those differences belong to X_(A+w). LI6 would then imply mu_(u_R)<<mu_(A+w) for every R. The locally finite Radon measure mu_(A+w) would have positive mass on uncountably many pairwise disjoint Borel subsets E_R of one compact set. This is impossible: for each positive integer m only finitely many disjoint subsets can have mass >=1/m, and every positive mass exceeds 1/m for some m.

The conclusion does not say that no countable family has a common control, and it makes no claim about continuity of R->u_R in the frozen energy-difference norm. Uniform convergence of the real profiles as R varies is not automatically convergence in that norm. This is only a precise limitation of a single-principal-ideal method on this explicit uncountable family.

prescribed_surface_graph.md # Prescribed interface data and the nonlinear bulk graph

Status: root derivation, pending separate audit. This organizes the clamped graph and the sphere compensator into one constructive statement. It is a restricted actual-source theorem on the original torus, not arbitrary-background C2. No assertion of literature novelty is made.

## 1. Known reference and free parameters

Let W be the known bounded actual reference from `root_extensions.md`, with a C^{2,alpha} strictly convex real profile v on a protected neighborhood of Bbar_R, with D^2v>=cI there. Keep the original field, norm, ordinary representative and S=beta^(n-q)[X], n>=2, 2<=q<=n. Use the already constructed operators

    L=L_v,  N=N_v,  D_v,  T,  E,  K=K_v,  Pi=Pi_v,  Q=Q_v,
    Y_v=L Z.

Here Q is the complementary projection, not the geometric moment box; at a nonquadratic reference its image is not asserted to be ordinary harmonic. This notation is confined to this document.

Choose as free prescribed parameters a small real g in Y_v and a small boundary function psi in C^{1,alpha}(sphere) with psi<=0. They do not come from an assumed nonlinear solution. Epsi is the explicit normal-trace lifting in the main proof.

Let M>=||K|| and suppose the polynomial estimate ||N(h)-N(k)||_Y<=L_*(r)||h-k||_X holds on the radius-r X-ball. Choose r with M L_*(r)<=1/2 and sufficiently small to preserve the strict Hessian and negative-value margins. Require

    ||Epsi||_X + M ||g||_Y <= r/2.                      (P1)

Define the actual iteration

    h_0=Epsi,
    h_(j+1)=Epsi+K[g-N(h_j)].                           (P2)

Every iterate has zero Dirichlet boundary value and normal derivative psi, since K takes values in Z. Because N(0)=0, ||N(h)||<=L_*(r)||h|| on the ball. Thus (P1) and M L_*(r)<=1/2 show that (P2) maps that ball into itself and is a contraction of factor at most 1/2. It converges in C^{2,alpha} to h=h(g,psi), with

    ||h||_X<=2(||Epsi||_X+M||g||_Y),
    ||h-h_j||_X<=2^(1-j)||h_1-h_0||_X,
    ||h_1-h_0||_X<=M(||g||_Y+||N(Epsi)||_Y).            (P3)

For two parameter pairs in the common budget, subtraction gives

    ||h(g,psi)-h(g',psi')||_X
       <=2(||E(psi-psi')||_X+M||g-g'||_Y).              (P4)

These formulas provide a convergent construction and error budget for all angular modes at once.

## 2. The exact bulk datum

Since L K=Pi and Pi g=g, applying L to the fixed point gives

    F_v(h)=g+L Epsi+Q N(h)=:f(g,psi).                   (P5)

The identity Pi L E=0 follows from Pi=L P D_v, D_v L E=E, and P E=0. Consequently Pi f=g. The complementary component L Epsi+Q N(h) is forced by the boundary parameter, rather than being silently discarded. For a supplied small bulk datum f and supplied psi, the necessary and sufficient condition in this small profile class is

    Q f = L Epsi + Q N(h(Pi f,psi)),                    (P6)

with the budget (P1) for Pi f. Necessity follows by applying Pi to the source equation and uniqueness of the contraction; sufficiency is (P5). It is an exact functional condition with geometric approximation bounds, not a finite-step decision test.

## 3. The full original Radon source

Let A_T(x) be the restriction of D^2v(x) to the tangent space of the sphere. The independent boundary-layer calculation in `nonradial_seam_extension.md` supplies

    J_v(psi)(x)=integral_(psi(x))^0
          sigma_(q-1)(A_T(x)+(s/R) I_T) ds.             (P7)

The small norm budget makes both endpoint tangent matrices strictly positive. Since psi<=0, J_v(psi)>=0, and it is zero exactly where psi=0. Zero extension of h is continuous. The jump of its gradient traces is -psi nu and its distribution Hessian has surface part (-psi)nu tensor nu dS; the inside and outside Hessians are positive and this surface Hessian is positive, so the glued potential U=W+tilde h is actual psh. The separate negative-value budget and unchanged exterior give the same bounded actual core qualifications as the parent.

The source equation, on every original compact smooth scalar test, is

    mu_U=mu_W+q!(n-q)! sigma_*[
                 1_B f(g,psi) dx+J_v(psi) dS].         (P8)

The bulk density is positive after adding the reference, by strict convexity; the surface contribution is nonnegative; the exterior is unchanged. This constructs genuine positive Radon data including a prescribed type of singular part. It is not a replacement of the originally supplied datum: (P5) and (P7) explicitly state all components of the datum that this construction realizes.

The proof of (P8) must use the boundary-layer theorem; merely applying the clamped C^{1,1} formula when psi is nonzero would lose the surface measure. The extension is generally Lipschitz and piecewise C^{2,alpha}, not C^1 across the sphere.

## 4. A quadratic reference permits direct prescription of surface density

For the parent's quadratic reference v=|x|^2/2, A_T=I_T and

    J(psi)=C1 R/q [1-(1+psi/R)^q],
    C1=binom(n-1,q-1).

Hence any sufficiently small prescribed nonnegative s in C^{1,alpha}(sphere) has the explicit boundary parameter

    psi_s=R[(1-q s/(C1 R))^(1/q)-1] <=0.                (P9)

Here s is the normalized real Hessian surface density: its actual non-Archimedean measure is q!(n-q)! sigma_*(s dS). Choose s small enough that the positive radicand and the norm budget (P1) hold. Independently choose small g with zero moments against every harmonic polynomial on the ball. Then (P2), using K_v=K_quadratic/C1, gives an actual source with precisely that surface component and normalized bulk density

    f(g,s)=g+C1 Delta Epsi_s+Q N(h(g,psi_s)).            (P10)

At s=0 this is the clamped harmonic graph. At constant psi=-tR and g=0, Epsi=-t(|x|^2-R^2)/2 has constant Hessian, N(Epsi) is constant harmonic, and the projected nonlinear correction vanishes. The construction recovers exactly u_t=w+t(R^2-|x|^2)/2 in the ball, including the total-mass compensation from `order_ideal_interface.md`.

The nonquadratic formula (P7) is still explicit in a prescribed psi. Do not automatically claim that C^{1,alpha} surface density can be inverted to C^{1,alpha} psi when v is only C^{2,alpha}: the coefficient A_T then has only C^alpha regularity. Direct surface-density inversion at that regularity is not included. Extra reference regularity would have to be specified and checked.

## 5. What this does and does not accomplish

The construction supplies an infinite-dimensional nonlinear range with independently prescribed linear bulk component and interface component, an actual convergent potential algorithm, and a full-original-test source identity. It avoids the earlier false step of feeding unprojected nonlinear residuals into a compact linear inverse. The surface family also shows why the clamped principal ideal does not exhaust every strong neighborhood of compatible potentials.

The original general C2 problem is still open: no arbitrary positive Radon data theorem, no arbitrary current-background inverse, and no quotient/refinement descent mechanism is obtained. The construction uses a known strictly elliptic real moment profile and a specified smooth toric background. Any Xi=0 conclusion is only the already frozen consequence of this actual source construction under its exact hypotheses.

range_graph_audit.md # Independent audit: a clamped projection and nonlinear source graph

Status: PROVED-INTERNAL in the precise real Hölder / fixed torus sector below, subject to the root's final source audit. This is an author-separated internal audit, not peer review or formal verification. It neither proves the original full LI13 nor solves arbitrary-background C2. The analytic ingredients are classical Poisson extension, Dirichlet Schauder theory, and contraction mapping; no originality claim is made.

## 1. Spaces and the linear Dirichlet inverse

Fix n >= 2, 0 < alpha < 1, R > 0, and B = B_R(0). Write

    Y = C^{0,alpha}(Bbar),
    X = {h in C^{2,alpha}(Bbar): h|boundary B = 0},
    Z = {h in X: partial_nu h|boundary B = 0}.

All functions and operators are real. Use usual Banach Hölder norms. Let D:Y -> X be the unique bounded inverse of the positive-sign Laplacian Delta = sum_i partial_ii. This is the classical Dirichlet Schauder isomorphism, not an assumed inverse on a compact-support ideal. A source actually opened by the root is Larry Guth, MIT 18.156 Lecture 7, notes transcribed by Cole Graham, PDF dated February 20, 2015 and hosted with the Spring 2016 course: Theorem 1 and Corollary 1 give existence/uniqueness on a ball, Theorem 2 gives the global C^{2,alpha} estimate, and Proposition 2 gives the Laplacian case. Scaling yields B_R. URL:

https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-156-differential-analysis-ii-partial-differential-equations-and-fourier-analysis-spring-2016/091bf989a474217c56f80bbb84cead6e_MIT18_156S16_lec7.pdf

The normal trace T:X -> C^{1,alpha}(partial B), Th = partial_nu h, is bounded.

## 2. An explicit bounded right inverse of normal trace

For psi in C^{1,alpha}(partial B), let Hpsi be its harmonic Poisson extension and set

    Epsi(x) = (|x|^2 - R^2)/(2R) Hpsi(x).                 (G1)

Then E:C^{1,alpha}(partial B) -> X is bounded, TE = identity, and Delta(Epsi) is harmonic. The apparent regularity issue in (G1) is real: one must not simply assert that Hpsi is C^{2,alpha}. It is generally only C^{1,alpha}. The vanishing prefactor supplies the missing derivative.

Here is an explicit justification of the needed regularity, including the Poisson boundary estimate. By scaling take R = 1. The kernel is

    P(x,y) = (1 - |x|^2)/(omega_{n-1} |x-y|^n),

with y on the unit sphere. Near the boundary let delta = 1 - |x| and y0 = x/|x|. The affine function

    ell(y) = psi(y0) + grad_S psi(y0) dot (y-y0)

has |psi(y)-ell(y)| <= C ||psi||_{C^{1,alpha}} |y-y0|^{1+alpha}; this holds locally by the surface Taylor formula and globally after changing C. The Poisson integral reproduces ell, because ell is affine and harmonic. For m = 1,2,3, direct differentiation of P and 1-|x|^2 <= 2|x-y| give

    |D_x^m P(x,y)| <= C_m |x-y|^{1-n-m}.

When |x| >= 1/2, |x-y| is comparable with delta + |y-y0|. Integrating the differentiated kernel against psi-ell gives

    |DHpsi| <= C ||psi||_{C^{1,alpha}},
    |D^2 Hpsi(x)| <= C ||psi||_{C^{1,alpha}} delta^{alpha-1},
    |D^3 Hpsi(x)| <= C ||psi||_{C^{1,alpha}} delta^{alpha-2}. (G2)

For example the near-diagonal integral for order m is bounded by a constant times

    integral_0^1 r^{n-1+alpha} (delta+r)^{1-n-m} dr.

It is bounded for m=1, of order delta^{alpha-1} for m=2, and of order delta^{alpha-2} for m=3. The part of the sphere separated from y0 is bounded uniformly. Interior derivatives are bounded by differentiating the smooth kernel on |x| <= 3/4.

The middle bound in (G2) implies DHpsi is C^{0,alpha} on the closed ball. For completeness, for x,y at separation d small, if their distances from the boundary are at least 2d, integrate D^2Hpsi along the segment; the ball's distance function is concave, so the result is <= C d^alpha. Otherwise both points lie within 3d of the sphere. Move each a distance of order d radially inwards, join the moved points in a region of depth at least c d, and integrate delta^{alpha-1} along the two radial pieces. Each contribution is <= C d^alpha. The interior case and d bounded below are immediate. Thus the gradient extends Hölder continuously; the ordinary Poisson approximate-identity property identifies the function's boundary value with psi. This proves the C^{1,alpha} bound without invoking a missing C^{2,alpha} boundary datum hypothesis.

Let a(x) = (|x|^2-1)/2. Each entry G = a D^2Hpsi tends to zero at the boundary and obeys

    |G| <= C delta^alpha,   |DG| <= C delta^{alpha-1}.      (G3)

These estimates give G in C^{0,alpha}(Bbar), with zero boundary trace. Indeed, when |x-y| >= delta(x)/2, both boundary depths are <= 3|x-y| and the first estimate gives the result. Otherwise the segment stays at comparable depth and the second estimate gives |G(x)-G(y)| <= C delta(x)^{alpha-1}|x-y| <= C |x-y|^alpha.

Now D^2(aHpsi) = (D^2a)Hpsi + Da tensor DHpsi + DHpsi tensor Da + aD^2Hpsi. Every summand is C^{0,alpha} up to the boundary with bounded norm. The interior second derivatives therefore extend continuously, proving Epsi is C^{2,alpha} on the closed ball. Rescaling proves boundedness for general R. Since a = 0 and partial_nu a = 1 on partial B_R, Epsi has boundary value zero and normal derivative psi. Finally

    Delta(Epsi) = (n/R) Hpsi + (2/R) x dot grad Hpsi.       (G4)

Both terms are harmonic in B, because Delta(x dot grad Hpsi) = 2 Delta Hpsi + x dot grad Delta Hpsi = 0. Equation (G4) extends continuously to the boundary by the established regularity.

## 3. Complemented clamped range and all harmonic moments

Define bounded operators

    P = I_X - ET : X -> Z,
    Pi = Delta P D : Y -> Y,
    Q = I_Y - Pi = Delta E T D,
    K = P D = D Pi : Y -> Z.                             (G5)

The equality K = D Pi follows from uniqueness of the Dirichlet Laplace problem. Since TE = I, P is a projection onto Z. Consequently Pi is a projection onto Y0 := Delta Z, Q is its complementary projection, and Y0 is closed. For g in Y0, Delta Kg = g; for every h in Z, K Delta h = h. Also K Pi = K.

By (G4), Qf is harmonic. Moreover Q is the identity on harmonic functions in Y. To see this without assuming higher boundary regularity, if f is harmonic then v = Pi f is also harmonic (it is f-Qf), and v = Delta z for z = P Df in Z. Green's formula against any smooth harmonic polynomial H gives integral_B H v = 0. Approximate v uniformly on Bbar by harmonic polynomials: first replace v(x) by v(r x), 0 < r < 1, using its boundary continuity, then use the harmonic Taylor expansion of v(r x) on a slightly larger ball. It follows that integral_B v^2 = 0, so v = 0. Thus Qf = f.

More generally,

    Y0 = {f in Y: integral_B H f = 0 for every harmonic polynomial H}. (G6)

One inclusion follows from the two zero boundary traces of z in Z and Green's formula. For the converse, Pi f has zero such moments, hence so does Qf; Qf is harmonic and the same uniform approximation argument gives Qf = 0. The identity

    integral_B H Qf = integral_B H f                     (G7)

holds for every harmonic polynomial H and, by approximation, every harmonic function continuous on Bbar. Therefore Q agrees on Y with the L^2 orthogonal harmonic Bergman projection. The proof establishes its C^{0,alpha} boundedness in this ball setting; that boundedness was not assumed.

This is an actual construction of a bounded inverse on the closed clamped range. It does not give an inverse on all C^{0,alpha} data, on a positive order ideal, or with the old completed-order norm.

## 4. An explicit convergent graph of nonlinear source data

Fix 2 <= q <= n. Put C1 = binom(n-1,q-1), C2 = binom(n-2,q-2), and

    F(h) = sigma_q(I + D^2h) - binom(n,q)
         = C1 Delta h + N(h),
    N(h) = sum_{k=2}^q binom(n-k,q-k) sigma_k(D^2h).       (G8)

The expansion is the elementary principal-minor identity. N is a continuous polynomial X -> Y with N(0)=DN(0)=0. Choose an equivalent X norm controlling every entry of D^2h in the Hölder algebra norm sup + seminorm. On the X ball of radius r one may use the explicit bound

    ||N(h)-N(k)||_Y <= L(r)||h-k||_X,
    L(r) = sum_{j=2}^q j b_j r^{j-1},
    b_j = binom(n-j,q-j) binom(n,j) j! .                 (G9)

Each determinant has at most j! products, and telescoping a product supplies the factor j. In particular L(r) -> 0 as r -> 0. Also ||N(h)||_Y <= A(||h||_X), A(t)=sum_{j=2}^q b_j t^j.

Let M >= ||K||_{Y -> X}. Choose r > 0 so M L(r)/C1 <= 1/2. For any supplied g in Y0 with ||g||_Y <= C1 r/(2M), define

    h_0 = 0,
    h_{j+1} = (1/C1) K[g - N(h_j)].                     (G10)

Every iterate is in Z. The map in (G10) preserves the closed X ball of radius r and is a contraction of factor at most 1/2 there. The preservation follows from ||T_g(0)|| <= M||g||/C1 <= r/2 and the contraction estimate. Thus the sequence converges in C^{2,alpha} to a uniquely defined small clamped h(g), with

    ||h(g)||_X <= 2M||g||_Y/C1,
    ||h(g)-h_j||_X <= 2^{1-j} M||g||_Y/C1.              (G11)

All inputs of (G10) are the given g, the explicitly constructed linear operator K, and the Hessian polynomial N. No unknown optimizer or nonlinear source solution is used as an assumption.

Define the harmonic correction to the datum by

    b(g) = Q N(h(g)),   f(g) = g + b(g).                 (G12)

Then, because Delta K = Pi and Pi g=g,

    Pi F(h(g)) = g,   Q F(h(g)) = b(g),
    F(h(g)) = f(g).                                     (G13)

The correction is harmonic on the ball and satisfies

    ||b(g)||_Y <= ||Q|| A(2M||g||_Y/C1) = O(||g||_Y^2).  (G14)

It can be approximated by b_j(g)=QN(h_j) with the certified error

    ||b(g)-b_j(g)||_Y <= ||Q|| L(r) 2^{1-j} M||g||_Y/C1. (G15)

For two admissible data, the same contraction argument gives

    ||h(g)-h(g')||_X <= (2M/C1)||g-g'||_Y.                (G16)

Thus (G12) parametrizes a genuine infinite-dimensional set of admissible nonradial data with no finite-angular cutoff. For a prescribed small f, exact membership in this local clamped source range is the data-defined condition

    Qf = b(Pi f),                                       (G17)

provided Pi f is within the parameter budget. Necessity follows by applying Pi to F(h)=f and uniqueness of (G10) among small clamped h. Sufficiency is (G13). Equality in (G17) is not generally decidable from a finite number of approximations; the geometric error budget only certifies approximations and nonzero discrepancies. It must not be advertised as a finite test.

The graph is a classical local analytic graph (analytic implicit-function theorem for the polynomial map h -> Pi F(h), whose derivative C1 Delta:Z ->Y0 is an isomorphism). Analyticity is not needed for the constructive existence result (G10)-(G15). A direct second-order expansion, requiring only the displayed estimates, is

    b(g) = C2 Q sigma_2(D^2[(1/C1)K g]) + O(||g||_Y^3).  (G18)

Indeed h(g)-(1/C1)Kg = O(||g||^2), the quadratic polynomial changes by O(||g||^3), and terms of degree at least three in N are O(||g||^3). Constants are fixed by n,q,alpha,R and the chosen norms.

## 5. Agreement with the preceding obstruction

Use h_* = x_1 chi(|x|), with nonzero smooth annular chi compactly supported in B, and H = x_1^2-x_2^2 from the verified parent second_order_lift_obstruction.md. Put g_* = C1 Delta h_*. This lies in Y0 and K g_* = C1 h_*. The parent identity is

    I_* = integral_B H sigma_2(D^2h_*)
        = 2 area(S^{n-1})/[n(n+2)] integral_0^R r^{n+1}(chi')^2 dr > 0.

Equations (G7) and (G18) imply

    integral_B H b(sg_*) = C2 I_* s^2 + O(|s|^3).         (G19)

So the straight data line s g_* misses the small clamped nonlinear range for every sufficiently small nonzero s. The graph supplies precisely a nonzero harmonic correction at order two. It does not falsely iterate the old compact inverse on an uncorrected nonlinear residual. This is consistent with, and sharper than, the old obstruction to a twice differentiable family of compact corrections. Uniqueness against larger convex competitors can be supplied separately via the integrated Newton tensor; it is not needed for this local graph claim.

## 6. Transfer to the original actual source problem

Use exactly the original field, ordinary torus box, background S=beta^{n-q}[X], and admissible max-reference w from parent_radial_source_proof.md, with w quadratic on B_(2R). Nothing here makes that specified background arbitrary. Choose r further small enough that ||D^2h||_op <= 1/2 and ||h||_infty is less than half the fixed negative margin of w on B_R. The first follows, for example, by n r <= 1/2 in the entrywise norm above.

For the constructed h(g) in Z, its zero extension tilde h is C^{1,1}; its distribution Hessian is the bounded piecewise Hessian, with no hypersurface measure because both the function and its gradient have matching traces. On the protected patch, |x|^2/2 + tilde h has positive distribution Hessian, hence is convex. Therefore u_g=w+tilde h(t) is an actual continuous psh function on the same ordinary representative, with the same ordinary boundary, negative values and bounded finite-mass/no-loss core qualifications as the parent. The root's separate source audit must explicitly use the C^{1,1} seam argument, since the old smooth radial proof had a zero collar.

For completeness, the full source argument is local convolution of the convex C^{1,1} patch. Its smooth convex mollifications converge locally uniformly, have uniformly bounded Hessians, and their Hessians converge almost everywhere to the piecewise Hessian. Each has the frozen full-original-test smooth top-form formula. Dominated convergence of the polynomial densities, and frozen bounded BT continuity on the left, give the same identity for the limit. Thus no interface mass is hidden:

    mu_{u_g} = mu_w + q!(n-q)! sigma_*(1_B f(g) dx).       (G20)

All original compact smooth scalar tests are retained; outside the protected patch, locality leaves mu_w untouched. The constructed datum is positive: inside B it is the strictly positive density of sigma_q(I+D^2h(g)); an independent norm check is ||f(g)||_infty < binom(n,q), obtainable from (G14) by shrinking the input budget; outside B it equals the known positive mu_w. No claim is made about arbitrary original GK delta tests, arbitrary S, completed nonlinear optimizers, or identifications among the three completions.

The substantive difference from merely restating Xi=0 is the verified operator E, projection Pi, clamped inverse K, and convergent data construction (G10)-(G15). Any Xi=0 consequence is only a corollary under the frozen module's exact assumptions. General C2, C1, B1, A1/GQ/KC12/RV4 and the other open interfaces remain open.
