root_extensions.md # Extensions and cross-checks of the clamped nonlinear range construction

Status: candidate proofs written by the root author, submitted for independent review. The main range construction is in `range_graph_audit.md`; the present text supplies a second derivation of its projection estimate, an extension to known strictly convex nonradial references, and conservation checks. These are restricted-sector results and classical-method combinations, not a claim to solve general C2 or to establish worldwide novelty.

## 1. A second proof of the Hölder projection bound

This proof does not use the normal-trace lifting from the main proof. Work first on the unit ball B in R^n, n>=2; V=|B| and omega=nV. Let

    A(x,y)=1-2 x.y+|x|^2|y|^2,
    P(x,y)=(1-|x|^2|y|^2) A(x,y)^(-n/2),
    R(x,y)=(n P(x,y)+2 x.grad_x P(x,y))/omega.

The last kernel is the harmonic Bergman kernel relative to ordinary Lebesgue measure. Its normalization follows directly by expanding the extended Poisson kernel in spherical harmonics: for a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree l the radial integral contributes 1/(n+2l), which cancels the factor n+2l from the numerator. Thus the integral operator Q reproduces harmonic polynomials and is their L2 orthogonal projection; the symmetry of the kernel follows since P depends on x.y and |x|^2|y|^2 and the two Euler derivatives agree. In particular integral_B R(x,y)dy=1. A primary reference for this classical kernel is Karel Stroethoff, *Harmonic Bergman Spaces*, MSRI Publications 33 (1998), section 2, formulas (2-3)--(2-6), and section 4, formula (4-7). Its ordinary Lp theorem is not being cited as a Hölder theorem.

Direct differentiation gives, with a=|x|^2|y|^2,

    R(x,y)=[n(1-a)^2-4aA]/[omega A^(1+n/2)].

Since 1-a<=2 sqrt(A), |grad_x A|<=2 sqrt(A), and the variables stay in the unit ball, this implies

    |R(x,y)|<=C A^(-n/2),
    |grad_x R(x,y)|<=C A^(-(n+1)/2).                    (E1)

The derivative bound can also be obtained by differentiating the displayed numerator: the derivative of (1-a)^2 is O(sqrt A), the derivative of aA is O(sqrt A), and the numerator is O(A). Multiplying the latter by the derivative of A^(-1-n/2) gives the same bound.

For f in C^{0,alpha}(Bbar), take x=r theta, r>=1/2, delta=1-r. Since A=|theta-r y|^2 and theta.(theta-y)>=0,

    A >= delta^2+r^2|theta-y|^2
      >= c(delta+|theta-y|)^2.

Differentiate Qf under the integral for interior x and subtract the constant f(theta), using integral grad_x R=0. Equation (E1) gives

    |grad Qf(x)| <= C [f]_alpha
       integral_B |theta-y|^alpha/(delta+|theta-y|)^(n+1)dy
      <= C [f]_alpha delta^(alpha-1).                   (E2)

Indeed polar integration about theta bounds the integral by a constant times integral_0^2 t^(n-1+alpha)/(delta+t)^(n+1)dt; substitute t=delta s and use alpha<1. On the inner half-ball the kernel derivative is bounded. Also Qf(0)=V^(-1) integral_B f.

For clarity, the weighted gradient bound in (E2) implies an actual C^alpha bound, not merely a growth condition. For two interior points x,y at distance d<1/2, put x'=(1-d)x and y'=(1-d)y. Each radial segment from x to x', or from y to y', has function variation at most C d^alpha by integrating (1-r)^(alpha-1). The segment [x',y'] lies at depth at least d, has length at most d, and contributes at most C d^alpha. Distances >=1/2 are handled by the uniform bound obtained by radial integration from the origin. Therefore

    ||Qf||_{C^alpha(Bbar)} <= C(n,alpha)||f||_{C^alpha(Bbar)}. (E3)

Rescale for B_R. Since Qf has the same harmonic moments as f, Green's formula gives that D(I-Q)f has both zero boundary traces. This recovers the main clamped inverse K=D(I-Q) without using a fictitious compact-support inverse on all data. It is also a separate check that no angular-frequency cutoff is hidden in the construction.

## 2. Known nonradial strictly convex references

Let v be a specified C^{2,alpha} real function on the protected ball B_(2R), with D^2v>=c I, c>0, on a neighborhood of Bbar=Bbar_R. It is known input, not an unknown solution. Suppose an already constructed bounded actual reference W agrees with v(t) plus a known constant on that protected neighborhood. Keep S=beta^(n-q)[X], with 2<=q<=n. Outside the changed closed ball W is left unchanged and retains its assumed actual psh/core properties.

Define

    F_v(h)=sigma_q(D^2v+D^2h)-sigma_q(D^2v),
    L_v h=T_{q-1}(D^2v):D^2h,
    N_v(h)=F_v(h)-L_v h.

The Newton tensor has C^alpha coefficients and is uniformly positive: its eigenvalues are sums of (q-1)-fold products of the eigenvalues of D^2v, so each is at least binom(n-1,q-1)c^(q-1). It is bounded above by a constant determined by ||v||_{C^{2,alpha}}. The classical ball Dirichlet Schauder isomorphism therefore supplies an actual bounded inverse D_v:Y->X for L_v. Unlike LI13, this is an inverse in ordinary Hölder spaces with zero Dirichlet values only.

Use the explicit universal boundary lifting E and trace T from the main proof, put P=I-ET, and define

    K_v=P D_v,
    Pi_v=L_v K_v,
    Q_v=I-Pi_v=L_v E T D_v.                              (E4)

Because D_v L_v is identity on X, Pi_v is a bounded projection onto Y_v=L_v Z, and K_v=D_v Pi_v. In particular K_v L_v h=h for h in Z. All these operators are constructed from the known v and the classical Dirichlet inverse. The complement image Q_v Y need not consist of harmonic functions for the ordinary Laplacian; no such identification is claimed.

For sufficiently small prescribed g in Y_v, iterate

    h_0=0,
    h_{j+1}=K_v[g-N_v(h_j)].                             (E5)

The polynomial N_v has zero value and first derivative at zero, and satisfies ||N_v(h)-N_v(k)||_Y<=L_v^*(r)||h-k||_X on the r-ball, with L_v^*(r)->0. This follows by expanding the principal minors with their known C^alpha coefficient functions; ordinary Hölder multiplication gives the estimate. Choose r with ||K_v||L_v^*(r)<=1/2 and ||g||_Y<=r/(2||K_v||). Also shrink r so ||D^2h||op<=c/2 and the negative margin of W on the protected ball is preserved. Then (E5) converges with the same geometric tail estimate as the main proof. It yields

    F_v(h(g))=g+Q_v N_v(h(g)).                            (E6)

The correction is quadratic in ||g||_Y; exact local membership is Q_v f=Q_v N_v(h(Pi_v f)). This equality is a convergently evaluable data condition, not in general a finite decision test. For generation rather than testing, g is free in the explicitly defined closed linear range and (E5)-(E6) generate its compatible datum.

There is an equivalent moment description of that linear range when desired. The Newton tensor is divergence-free distributionally, first for smooth v by antisymmetry of the Hessian minors, and then for C^{2,alpha} v by local smooth approximation. If phi solves L_v phi=0 with smooth boundary values, Green's formula for z=D_v g gives

    integral_B phi g = integral_boundary phi (nu.T_{q-1}(D^2v).nu) partial_nu z.

Here z has zero Dirichlet trace, so its gradient on the boundary is purely normal. The coefficient nu.T.nu is continuous and strictly positive. Since arbitrary smooth boundary functions occur as traces of these known linear harmonic extensions, g lies in Y_v precisely when all these moments vanish. This identity can be justified for C^{2,alpha} v and z using C^2 approximation in the integration-by-parts formula; no third classical derivatives are required. Alternatively the directly defined projection Pi_v already provides the criterion and needs no Green formula.

Zero extension of h(g) is C^{1,1}, its gradient matches at the sphere, and the protected profile v+tilde h is convex distributionally. The main local convolution proof, with bounded Hessian density rather than any singular interface, gives

    mu_(W+tilde h)=mu_W+q!(n-q)! sigma_*(1_B F_v(h) dx).  (E7)

The exterior remains exactly W. Positivity of the displayed datum follows either from the controlled positive Hessian or from a strict lower bound on the known reference density and the explicit smallness bound on F_v(h). Ordinary boundary and bounded actual-core qualifications are inherited as in the parent proof. This extends the construction past radial reference profiles, but retains a specified smooth toric background and strict ellipticity. It is not a theorem for arbitrary middle-positive current S.

## 3. Conservation and checks on the nonlinear harmonic correction

Return to the quadratic reference and Q in the main theorem. If h in Z, its zero extension is compactly supported and C^{1,1}. For each 1<=k<=n and every affine function a,

    integral_B a sigma_k(D^2h) dx=0.                    (E8)

Proof: mollify the compact zero extension, retaining compact support in a slightly larger ball. For smooth compact functions the Newton identities give k sigma_k=div(T_{k-1} grad h) and div T_{k-1}=0. Integrating against affine a once gives -(1/k) integral grad a.T_{k-1}grad h. Integrating again gives zero because grad a is constant and the tensor is divergence-free. For k=1 the tensor is the identity, so the same formula applies. Mollified Hessians are uniformly bounded and converge almost everywhere; dominated convergence proves (E8). This argument uses no positivity of h itself.

Consequently the exact graph correction b(g)=QN(h(g)) has zero integral and zero first moments. Since b is harmonic on the ball centered at zero, the mean-value identity and the degree-one harmonic coefficients imply

    b(g)(0)=0,     grad b(g)(0)=0.                      (E9)

The correction begins in harmonic degrees >=2. A nonzero b(g) cannot have one sign. Thus one must not describe this construction as adding a positive measure to fix compatibility; it alters the density in both directions, with positivity secured by the strictly positive reference density and the explicit small budget.

If g is radial and lies in Y0, the uniquely constructed h(g) is radial because all operators and the iteration commute with rotations. Then b(g) is radial harmonic and hence constant; (E8) forces b(g)=0. This recovers the prior radial weighted-mass construction within the common small Hölder regime. The parent radial result itself has a distinct, explicit C0 smallness budget and is not replaced by this narrower Hölder argument.

Nonradial data do not automatically require a nonzero correction. Take a finite collection of disjoint protected balls and on each prescribe a translated radial smooth density with zero weighted integral, sufficiently small for the parent radial construction. The associated explicit corrections have disjoint supports. Their sum is nonradial in general, and every Hessian polynomial is pointwise the sum of the separate perturbations; hence its exact source is the prescribed sum. Each summand has zero harmonic moments by the spherical mean-value property and zero mass. The total datum lies in Y0 and, within the graph's small budget, has b(g)=0 by uniqueness. This direct corollary prevents a false rigidity inference from the one explicit nonradial obstruction.

For q=2, integration by parts also gives, for any H smooth and harmonic on a neighborhood of Bbar,

    integral_B H b(g) = (1/2) integral_B D^2H(grad h(g),grad h(g)). (E10)

Here the coefficient binom(n-2,q-2) is 1. The identity follows from sigma_2=((Delta h)^2-|D^2h|^2)/2 and two integrations by parts, using clamped boundary traces; alternatively apply the compact mollification argument. It matches the positive degree-two moment for h=x_1 chi(r) in the prior obstruction. For q>2 there are additional higher-minor terms, so (E10) must not be reused without them.

## 4. Limits of the method

The fixed-reference construction uses an actual classical Schauder inverse and a verified boundary projection. Its constants depend on a strict ellipticity lower bound and on C^alpha coefficient bounds. No uniformity as the current background becomes singular or the reference Hessian degenerates is established. R17 LI20-LI21 already show why broad all-test admissibility and bounded energies do not imply the different, stronger order-ideal inverse LI13; that frozen obstruction is retained, not rediscovered here. The new Hölder graph is not an order-ideal saturation theorem and does not compare the Q-order, strong E1, and Borel-capacity completions.

The general C2 task still requires independently checkable conditions covering arbitrary permitted S and genuine original data, with source equality on the full original test class. No conclusion about arbitrary non-toric potentials or general completed solutions follows from the compact convex-profile obstruction.

seam_proof.md # A full-test sphere compensator for small nonradial Dirichlet data

Status: PROVED-INTERNAL derivation in the specified toric sector, submitted to the root for separate review. This is not general C2. Dependencies are the verified classical Dirichlet/Schauder construction, elementary Hessian/Newton identities proved below, frozen bounded-BT local uniform continuity, and frozen smooth full-test Gauss calibration. No arbitrary-psh pushforward formula is assumed.

## 1. Setup and statement

Use the parent's actual reference w, equal to p(x)=(|x|²−L²)/2 on B_{2R}, on the same ordinary torus representative V, with S=β^{n−q}[X], n≥2 and 2≤q≤n. Let z∈C^{2,α}(Bbar_R) satisfy z=0 on ∂B_R and

    I+D²z≥cI>0,     ||D²z||op≤r<1/2.

Write b=∂νz on the sphere and f=σ_q(I+D²z)−binom(n,q). Initially z can be any such known Dirichlet function; later z=z(f) is the already constructed Picard limit for prescribed small f. Define ztilde=z inside B_R and zero outside, and U=w+ztilde. It is continuous. All assertions below about the original BT source assume b≤0, which ensures convexity. The exact density is

    J(b)= C1 R/q [1−(1+b/R)^q],  C1=binom(n−1,q−1).       (S1)

Then, on all original compact smooth scalar tests,

    μ_U=μ_w+K_q σ_*(f 1_{B_R} dx + J(b) dS_{∂B_R}),
    K_q=q!(n−q)!.                                       (S2)

The surface term is essential. It vanishes exactly when b=0. All forms, measures, coordinates, field and absolute value remain the original ones, but the result uses this specified smooth toric background.

## 2. Classical geometry and convexity at the sphere

On the sphere, tangential derivatives of z vanish and ∇z=bν. For a unit tangent vector e, choose a unit-speed great-circle curve γ with γ(0)=x, γ′(0)=e and γ″(0)=−ν/R. Twice differentiating z(γ)=0 gives

    D²z(e,e)=b/R.

Polarization gives D²z|_{T∂B}=(b/R)I. In particular |b|/R≤r. The inside Hessian of v=p+z is positive definite; outside v=p. Across the sphere the gradient jump (outside minus inside) is −bν. Its distribution Hessian is therefore

    D²v = (I+1_B D²z) dx + (−b) ν⊗ν dS.                (S3)

One can verify (S3) by integrating the first derivatives by parts on the two sides; continuity of v prevents any derivative-of-surface term. Thus b≤0 makes this matrix-valued distribution positive, and v is convex on B_{2R}. Conversely, if the glued function is convex, restriction to each normal line gives outside slope at least inside slope, hence b≤0. This equivalence uses the fixed exterior p.

The convex local function glues to w because it equals p on the open annulus R<|x|<2R. Negativity is preserved by the separate small uniform bound on z; boundary values and all actual-core qualifications are the same as the parent's construction. If the scheme is used outside this uniform budget, negativity must be checked rather than inferred from convexity alone.

## 3. Newton divergence and the smoothing estimate

Let T_{q−1}(A) be the matrix derivative of σ_q at a symmetric matrix A. For smooth v,

    tr(T_{q−1}(D²v) D²v)=q σ_q(D²v),
    div T_{q−1}(D²v)=0.

The first identity is Euler's identity for the homogeneous polynomial. For the second, expand T through alternating generalized Kronecker symbols; differentiating each Hessian factor produces a third derivative symmetric in the differentiated and row indices, while the alternating symbol changes sign under their exchange. Terms cancel. Hence

    q σ_q(D²v)=div F_v,
    F_v=T_{q−1}(D²v)∇v.                                (S4)

We justify the distributional limit of this flux, rather than multiplying singular Hessians. Let v_ε=v*ρ_ε on a protected subball of B_{2R}, with a nonnegative smooth compactly supported mollifier. It is smooth convex and converges locally uniformly to v. Formula (S3) gives its Hessian. In the ε-neighborhood of the sphere, use the orthonormal frame with last vector ν(x)=x/|x|. If y is on the sphere with |y−x|≤ε, its normal has tangential components O(ε/R) in this frame. The mollified surface measure has total density O(ε⁻¹). Consequently the surface contribution to the nn Hessian block is O(ε⁻¹), its mixed block is O(1), and its tangential block is O(ε); adding bounded bulk gives

    (D²v_ε)nn=O(ε⁻¹),
    (D²v_ε)nT=O(1),    (D²v_ε)TT=O(1).                  (S5)

All constants here are uniform in ε on a fixed protected neighborhood and may depend on R and the C² bounds. Also ∇_T v_ε=O(ε) in that layer: on the sphere v is constant, so the two classical gradients there are normal; moving a distance O(ε) changes their tangential components by O(ε), including the O(ε/R) change of normal direction. The normal gradient is O(1).

Each Newton-tensor entry is a sum of minors. Its nn entry involves only tangential Hessian entries, so is O(1). Its nT entries are also O(1): an off-diagonal derivative minor with one excluded normal row/column cannot contain the nn entry. The TT block is O(ε⁻¹), since a minor contains the nn entry at most once. Thus

    F_{v_ε}=T_{q−1}(D²v_ε)∇v_ε=O(1)                  (S6)

even in the layer: the only potentially O(ε⁻¹) block multiplies an O(ε) tangential gradient. Away from the sphere, convolution converges in C² locally to the classical pieces; the thin layer has volume O(ε). Therefore F_{v_ε} converges in local L¹ to the piecewise classical flux F_v.

Passing to distributions in (S4) is now justified. The divergence of a piecewise continuous flux has boundary part (F_out−F_in)·ν dS. On the sphere,

    ∇v_in=(R+b)ν,
    (D²v_in)|_T=(1+b/R)I,
    T_{q−1}(D²v_in)ν·ν=C1(1+b/R)^{q−1}.

Mixed Hessian entries do not enter this normal-normal cofactor. Consequently

    F_in·ν=C1 R(1+b/R)^q,       F_out·ν=C1 R,

and the boundary density of σ_q is exactly J(b) in (S1). The interior density is binom(n,q)+f; outside it is binom(n,q).

Because the v_ε are convex, σ_q(D²v_ε) dx are positive. Their mass on every protected compact set is uniformly bounded: test (S4) against a smooth cutoff equal to one there and use (S6), which holds globally on that compact region. Distribution convergence therefore improves to vague convergence against arbitrary continuous compactly supported real tests. This step is needed for η∘σ, which need not be an ordinary smooth function in these moment coordinates.

## 4. Transfer to all original tests

For each smooth toric v_ε the retained smooth calibration gives the full source measure K_q σ_*(σ_q(D²v_ε)dx), paired against every original compact smooth scalar η. On the moment patch the corresponding real test is the continuous function η∘σ. The vague convergence just proved passes this right-hand side to the bulk-plus-surface formula. Frozen bounded-BT continuity under local uniform convergence of continuous psh potentials passes the left-hand side to the source of v. A compact moment cutoff equal to one near Bbar_R separates this computation from the unchanged exterior w, proving (S2).

No replacement of the original test class is made. The proof derives this nonsmooth toric formula from smooth approximants with a controlled interface. It does not assert a general nonlinear pushforward theorem for all psh potentials.

## 5. Prescribed negative bulk data produce a positive seam compensator

Take any sufficiently small prescribed f∈C^{0,α}(Bbar_R) with f≤0. The preceding Picard construction produces a unique small z=z(f), with positive Hessian and zero Dirichlet data. Since

    f=F(z)−F(0)=a^{ij}∂ijz,

where a is the integrated Newton tensor along I+tD²z and is uniformly positive, the classical minimum principle gives z≥0. The elementary one-sided derivative at the zero boundary then gives b≤0. Hence U is actual convex/psh and (S2) applies. The data on the right are positive independently of any optimizer: the bulk density binom(n,q)+f stays positive by the small norm condition, J(b)≥0, and the exterior source is unchanged. The normal trace b is evaluated from the explicit convergent Dirichlet iteration with its previously proved error bounds.

This describes a prescribed bulk perturbation with a determined compensating sphere measure. It does NOT solve the seam-free equation with datum μ_w+K_qσ_*(f dx). It is not a finite-test characterization, since evaluating b exactly may involve an infinite limit. The construction avoids an unknown nonlinear optimizer but still uses the established local nonlinear Dirichlet solve as a computational procedure.

Integrating (S4), or simply comparing its unchanged outer flux, gives the exact balance

    ∫_B f dx + ∫_∂B J(b)dS=0.                           (S7)

For a check, if f is the small negative constant f0, set k=(1+f0/binom(n,q))^{1/q}−1 and z=k(|x|²−R²)/2. Then b=kR and J=−Rf0/n; (S7) follows from |B_R|=R|∂B_R|/n. This is a calibration check, not a substitute for the nonradial proof.

## 6. Strengthened obstruction for the previous straight data line

For f_s=s C1Δ(x1χ(|x|)), the separate audited expansion proves b(f_s)≠0 for all sufficiently small nonzero s. It also has ∫_B f_s=0. Apply the classical inside flux identity, which is valid without any sign assumption on b:

    ∫_B f_s dx=C1 R/q ∫_∂B[(1+b/R)^q−1]dS=0.          (S8)

Because 1+b/R>0 and b is continuous and nonzero, (S8) forces b to take both positive and negative values. In particular the unique small interior Dirichlet solution cannot be convexly glued to the unchanged quadratic exterior: positivity of b at any point violates the one-dimensional convexity condition.

The separate comparison argument identifies every C² convex interior Dirichlet solution with this small solution; it does not require the competitor to be small. Thus there is no actual correction whose real moment profile is C² on the closed fixed ball, convex after gluing to the specified exterior, and has the desired seam-free source. This removes the explicit clamped assumption in that profile class. It does not address non-toric original potentials, general completed solutions, weaker profiles not covered by a comparison theorem, or modified exterior values.

For a general small datum, (S1) separately shows that a convex gluing with no sphere source must have b=0: J≥0 and J=0 exactly at b=0. This implication remains restricted to the piecewise C² profile class just proved.

source_transfer_and_review.md # Root audit of the source transfer and the two main constructions

This is a mathematical audit of the printed sources, separate from the two agents that produced `range_graph_audit.md`, `dirichlet_audit.md`, and `seam_proof.md`. It is not peer review or formal verification. Hash checks establish byte identity only.

## Frozen input and a direct continuity calculation

We retain the previously verified fixed-background bounded BT core: mixed products of bounded continuous actual psh functions are symmetric, positive, separately closed, and satisfy the current recursion D(uT); compact CLN bounds and order-zero control apply on the original test spaces. Max stability and smooth full-test torus calibration are also retained. This run does not reopen the entire R1--R24 proof chain or invisible R21 bytes.

The local uniform continuity needed below follows directly from those core properties, rather than from an unspecified new convergence theorem. For two k-tuples of bounded continuous actual psh functions u_i and v_i, the mixed-product telescoping identity gives

    product_i Du_i wedge S - product_i Dv_i wedge S
      = sum_i D[(u_i-v_i) T_i],

where T_i is the mixed product using earlier u factors and later v factors, wedged with S. Each T_i is positive and separately closed. On an original compact smooth test eta, order-zero control and compact CLN give

    |< D[(u_i-v_i)T_i], eta >|
       = |< (u_i-v_i)T_i, D eta >|
       <= C_eta ||u_i-v_i||_infty,

provided all potentials have one common bound on a fixed slightly larger compact neighborhood. The constant is independent of the converging sequence; it is the compact CLN bound applied to the fixed controls for D eta. All multiplications by the continuous difference are the original order-zero multiplications in the frozen core. Thus locally uniform convergence gives convergence on every original smooth test. This is a direct corollary, not a new foundational BT theorem and not the unresolved strong continuity of arbitrary literal Radon data.

For the torus constructions, this calculation can be used entirely inside the protected moment neighborhood. Mollifications need not be global competitors: they are smooth convex functions on that neighborhood, where the local BT products are defined. A compact moment cutoff splits any original test into the changed neighborhood and the unchanged exterior. Properness of the torus moment map over compact real sets gives the required original compact supports.

## Root check of the clamped projection and graph

Read the full exact text of `range_graph_audit.md`. The critical regularity step is valid: the Poisson extension of C^{1,alpha} boundary data need not be C^{2,alpha}; multiplication by the defining quadratic factor supplies that missing derivative. Subtracting the tangent affine polynomial is legitimate when differentiating the kernel at a fixed point: the affine polynomial is held fixed during that differentiation and its higher derivatives vanish. The estimates delta D^2H=O(delta^alpha), D(delta D^2H)=O(delta^(alpha-1)) imply Hölder continuity by the two-case argument printed in that proof.

TE=I gives P^2=P and both traces of P h vanish. The identities K=D Pi and K Pi=K use the actual Dirichlet inverse. Hence the nonlinear iteration never assumes that its unprojected residual is in the clamped range. Applying Delta to the fixed-point equation gives C1 Delta h=g-Pi N(h); adding N(h) gives exactly g+Q N(h), with the plus sign shown in the source. The determinant expansion coefficients binom(n-k,q-k), including C1 and C2, agree with expansion of sigma_q(I+A) by principal minors.

The image of Q is harmonic by the explicit formula for Delta E. The moment argument identifies Q with the harmonic Bergman projection without assuming it has a Hölder bound from an Lp theorem. A second kernel-based proof has been supplied by the root in `root_extensions.md` and is being independently checked. The graph is infinite dimensional; no finite spherical-harmonic truncation is used.

For zero extension, h=0 and normal derivative zero imply the full gradient has zero boundary trace. The extension is globally C^{1,1} on the protected real patch, with distribution Hessian equal to its bounded piecewise Hessian. Consequently mollified Hessians have a common bound and converge almost everywhere. Dominated convergence of all Hessian minors proves that the real source density has no sphere mass. The preceding original BT telescoping estimate passes the left side of the smooth Gauss calibration to the actual limit. Therefore the full source equality is valid on every original compact smooth scalar test, including tests not pulled back from the original moment coordinates.

Negativity is a separate budget. It follows by requiring ||h||_infty to be less than half the positive margin min_B(-w), not from convexity alone. The unchanged exterior and the parent neighborhood extension give ordinary boundary values, the explicit lower barrier, finite total mass by compact CLN, bounded energies and eventually unchanged deep truncations. No representative is prescribed for an arbitrary completion element.

Conclusion: PASS for the stated fixed-background small Hölder graph. The term PROVED-INTERNAL refers to the exact theorem in these hypotheses, reusing the frozen bounded core; general C2 and LI13 stay OPEN.

## Root check of the spherical interface formula

Read the full exact text of `seam_proof.md`. The outward gradient jump is exterior minus interior = -b nu, so a convex gluing requires b<=0. The sign in the measure formula is consequently positive when b<0. The sphere tangential Hessian is (1+b/R)I: differentiating the constant boundary value twice along a great circle gives D^2z(e,e)=b/R. This also bounds |b|/R by the Hessian norm when n>=2.

The key smoothing argument does not multiply singular Hessians. In a layer of thickness epsilon, the convolved rank-one surface Hessian has normal-normal entry O(epsilon^-1), mixed entries O(1), and tangential entries O(epsilon). Adding the bounded bulk preserves these bounds. A Newton cofactor with one normal row or column removed cannot contain the large normal-normal entry; only its tangential block can grow as epsilon^-1. The latter multiplies tangential gradient O(epsilon), because both one-sided gradients of the continuous profile are normal on the sphere. Thus the full Newton flux is uniformly bounded in the layer, and its integral over that layer tends to zero.

Away from the sphere the flux converges classically; hence it converges locally in L1 everywhere. Its distributional divergence has the jump of the classical normal flux. The interior flux equals C1(R+b)(1+b/R)^(q-1); the exterior flux equals C1 R. Division by q yields

    J(b)=C1 R/q [1-(1+b/R)^q].

The polynomial is positive for -R<b<0 and zero exactly at b=0. Local mass bounds for the positive mollified densities follow by a compact cutoff and the uniform flux bound, so convergence holds against continuous compact real tests. That is sufficient for eta composed with the Gauss section. Local uniform BT convergence then proves the original full-test formula with this surface measure.

At C^{2,alpha} regularity the Newton divergence identity and integration by parts hold by C^2 approximation of the classical pieces on the closed ball; they do not require third classical derivatives. A C^2 extension to a slightly larger neighborhood followed by convolution suffices for this auxiliary real calculation. This regularity point is now explicit.

The constant-density check gives J=-Rf0/n and exactly cancels the negative bulk total mass; it agrees with the formula but is not its proof. For arbitrary small f<=0, the integrated Newton tensor minimum principle gives z>=0 and hence b<=0, so the construction applies without a radial assumption. It prescribes the interior datum and determines an additional sphere measure. It must not be advertised as solving the same datum after silently adding that measure.

Conclusion: PASS for the explicit sphere-compensated family and its full original source formula.

## Root check of the stronger individual obstruction

For the parent's h_*=x_1 chi(r), the Dirichlet iteration gives z_s=s h_*-(C2/C1)s^2 D[sigma_2(D^2h_*)]+O_{C^{2,alpha}}(|s|^3). Green's formula pairs its boundary normal trace with H=x_1^2-x_2^2 to a strictly negative nonzero coefficient at order s^2. Thus the trace is nonzero for every sufficiently small nonzero s, with an actual remainder estimate, not an assumed differentiable family.

The source line has zero total added mass. The exact interior Newton flux identity therefore forces the integral of (1+b/R)^q-1 on the sphere to be zero. Since b is continuous, |b|/R<1/2, and b is not identically zero, b has both signs. The inside solution cannot be convexly glued to the fixed exterior quadratic profile.

For another C^2 convex interior solution, integrate the Newton tensor along the segment from the constructed strictly convex solution. It is uniformly elliptic because the segment Hessian is at least (1-t)cI and the integral of (1-t)^(q-1) is 1/q. The maximum principle identifies the two Dirichlet solutions. Thus the obstruction excludes each individual sufficiently small nonzero datum in the fixed C^2 convex patch class, even if a competitor was not assumed small. It does not exclude non-toric original potentials, arbitrary completion elements, or a changed exterior potential.

Conclusion: PASS as a restricted original-category obstruction. Its stronger scope compared with the parent smooth-family obstruction is recorded; no general nonexistence theorem is inferred.

## Nonradial reference and final interface review

Root read the full `nonradial_seam_extension.md` and checked (NS3)--(NS7). The distribution Hessian contains only the rank-one normal surface matrix; in convolution its TT part is O(epsilon), nT part O(1), and nn part O(epsilon^-1). The smooth bulk TT interpolation is the convex segment A_T+eta b I/R. Every q-principal minor has at most one nn entry, so multiplying its density by epsilon eliminates the bounded remainder. Coarea and eta'=-k give the stated integral from b to zero, with positive sign. This proof correctly avoids using a bounded Newton flux when the boundary gradient has nonzero tangential component. The affine-reference check detects exactly why the earlier flux proof could not be reused. PASS under the printed strict convexity and regularity assumptions.

The corrected prescribed-surface graph has matching zero function traces and normal gradient-trace jump -psi nu. Its Hessian, not its distribution gradient, carries the surface measure. The normalized real sphere density s must be multiplied by K_q=q!(n-q)! for the original source. The explicit inverse for psi(s) is certified only for the quadratic reference; general C^{2,alpha} v has only C^alpha tangent Hessian coefficients. These corrections were independently audited.

For `order_ideal_interface.md` §§3--4, the bulk/surface positivity budgets prove (O7). With a nonradial reference W use A+W for source domination; W in X_A has not been asserted. The uncountable moving-radius obstruction uses only absolute continuity for each radius, not a uniform bound on the ideal norms. It is therefore valid in the full completed cone.

The moving-sphere ED separation proof passed separate audit. Its mathematical mechanism was already proved in R12 CG1--CG10, whose exact source was recovered and read this run. This realization in every n>=2 is retained as an illustrative extension, not a new C1 breakthrough. The simplified non-Radon proof uses uniform convergence on one fixed compact set and local total variation of a signed Radon measure.

title: Theorem 1.1 — Bounded products with a fixed background
text:
Bounded products with a fixed background Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 1.1 (Bounded products with a fixed background). Let \(S\) be a background of degree \((p,p)\) on \(U\) , and put \(q=n-p\) . For \(0\le k\le q\) there are unique recursively defined coefficient Radon currents \[T_{S,0}=S,\qquad T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k) =D\bigl(u_1T_{S,k-1}(u_2,\ldots,u_k)\bigr), \qquad u_i\in\mathcal C_b(U). \tag{1.1}\] The multiplication in this formula uses the given Borel functions and the coefficient measures on the analytic space. The currents are positive, symmetric as currents, and separately \(d'\) - and \(d''\) -closed. The operation is invariant under permutations of the differentiated slots, additive and positively homogeneous in each such slot, local for ordinary restriction, and independent of the regularization used to compute them. If \(u_{i,j}\downarrow u_i\) in \(\mathcal C_b(U)\) for \(0\le i\le k\) , with locally bounded limits, then \[u_{0,j}T_{S,k}(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{k,j}) \longrightarrow u_0T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k) \tag{1.2}\] on every original compact smooth complementary test. In top degree this is local weak convergence of signed Radon measures against compactly supported continuous functions. Finally, if \(D[u_i]=D[v_i]\) for every differentiated slot, then \[T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)=T_{S,k}(v_1,\ldots,v_k).\]

title: Theorem 1.2 — Continuous coefficient action and its order completion
text:
Continuous coefficient action and its order completion Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 1.2 (Continuous coefficient action and its order completion). For every background \(S\) of degree \((p,p)\) and \(r\le n-p\) , the formula \[\Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r) =\sum_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_r} \left(\prod_{i=1}^r f_{i,\alpha_i}\right) T_{S,r}(g_{1,\alpha_1},\ldots,g_{r,\alpha_r}) \tag{1.4}\] is independent of all presentations (1.3) . It defines a symmetric \(C(U,\mathbf R)\) -multilinear local operation, positive when every slot is positive. Each completion \(\widehat E_Q\) embeds faithfully and isometrically into the actual symmetric coefficient Radon currents. These embeddings are compatible under change of control. The operation \(\Phi_{S,r}\) extends uniquely to \(\mathscr M^1_{\rm ord}\) , locally and independently of the approximating sequences. If \(-M_iQ_i\le A_i,B_i\le M_iQ_i\) and \(-\delta_iQ_i\le A_i-B_i\le\delta_iQ_i\) , then \[-E R_S\le \Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r)-\Phi_{S,r}(B_1,\ldots,B_r) \le E R_S, \tag{1.5}\] where \[R_S=\Phi_{S,r}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r),\qquad E=\sum_{i=1}^r\delta_i\prod_{j\ne i}M_j.\] The output is separately closed whenever it is obtained as a limit of separately closed mixed approximants.

title: Theorem 1.3 — The complete relative first-energy space
text:
The complete relative first-energy space Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 1.3 (The complete relative first-energy space). Under (1.6) , every strongly Cauchy row in \(\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(V)\) has a unique limit in \(\mathscr C\) . There are intrinsic mixed curvature, first-order and energy currents, and global mixed energies on \(\mathscr C\) , independent of all defining rows and outer-capacity-null representatives. The mixed energy is symmetric and satisfies \[\widehat B(u_0,\ldots,u_q) \le\prod_{i=0}^q\widehat e(u_i)^{1/d}. \tag{1.7}\] The completed discrepancy \(\widehat I\) separates relative classes and is complete. Moreover, \[\widehat I(u_j,u)\to0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} u_j\to u\text{ in every local truncated outer capacity},\\ \widehat e(u_j)\to\widehat e(u). \end{cases} \tag{1.8}\] For a finite tuple, let \(F\) be continuous on the nonpositive orthant and satisfy \(|F(x)|\le A(1-\sum_i x_i)^a\) , with \(a\ge0\) . Give a curvature current with \(k\) curvature slots the degree budget \(b=k\) ; for a first-order or energy current over \(k\) curvature slots put \(b=k+1\) or \(b=k+2\) , respectively. In the legal bidegrees, if \(a+b\le q+1\) , these multipliers are coefficient-integrable and their weighted currents converge on every original compact smooth test under strong convergence of the tuple. The global mixed weighted top measures also converge. The actual classical class is strongly dense.

title: Theorem 1.4 — Variational sources and one geometric probe
text:
Variational sources and one geometric probe Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 1.4 (Variational sources and one geometric probe). Under (1.6) , \(\mathbb D_S\) is Banach and \[J(u)(h)=\widehat B(h,u^{[q]})=-\int h\,d\widehat\mu_u\] defines an injective map with norm-closed image in \(\mathbb D_S^*\) . The metric \(\|J(u)-J(v)\|_*\) is complete and induces the strong topology on \(\mathscr C\) . Every \(\ell\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*\) has a unique variational maximizer \[u=\Pi(\ell)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in\mathscr C} \bigl(\ell(v)-\widehat e(v)/d\bigr)\] and a unique decomposition \(\ell=J(u)+n\) with \(n(v)\le0\) for every \(v\in\mathscr C\) and \(n(u)=0\) . There is one bounded continuous classical \(-1<\psi_0<0\) , determined by the Laurent box and having finite top mass, such that \(\psi_0\pm\epsilon_\phi\phi\in\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(V)\) for every original compact smooth real scalar \(\phi\) and some \(\epsilon_\phi>0\) . The choice of \(\psi_0\) and \(\epsilon_\phi\) works for every extending allowed background. For a literal positive Radon datum as above, set \(u=\Pi(\ell_\mu)\) and \[\Xi_{\psi_0}(\mu)=J(u)(\psi_0)-\ell_\mu(\psi_0)\ge0.\] Then \[\Xi_{\psi_0}(\mu)=0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widehat\mu_u=\mu \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \mu=\widehat\mu_v\text{ for some }v\in\mathscr C.\] The solution is unique. For every such datum and every original compact smooth scalar test, \[\left|\int\phi\,d(\mu-\widehat\mu_u)\right| \le\epsilon_\phi^{-1}\Xi_{\psi_0}(\mu).\]

title: Theorem 1.5 — The finite diffuse relative Dirichlet equation
text:
The finite diffuse relative Dirichlet equation Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 1.5 (The finite diffuse relative Dirichlet equation). In the preceding domain, let \(\mu\) be a finite signed Radon measure on \(F\) whose variation vanishes on every \(c_V\) -polar Borel set. There is a unique \(u\in L^1(F,\lambda)\) with a finite energy-quasicontinuous representative, \(T_ku\in H\) for every \(k>0\) , the original chain identity \[D(\Phi(u)S)=\Phi'(u)\mu+\Phi''(u)\Gamma_S(u)\] for every \(\Phi\in C^2(\mathbf R)\) with compactly supported first derivative, and \(k^{-1}\mathcal E(T_{2k}u-T_ku)\to0\) . Here \(\Gamma_S(u)\) is the compatible sigma-finite energy measure of its clippings. This solution satisfies \(D(uS)=\mu\) on every original compact scalar test and is independent of the faithful reference measure. If \(\mu_j\to\mu\) in total variation, then \[\|u_{\mu_j}-u_\mu\|_{L^1(\lambda)}\to0, \qquad \mathcal E(T_ku_{\mu_j}-T_ku_\mu)\to0 \quad(k>0).\]

title: Lemma 2.1 — Finite test control
text:
Finite test control Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 2.1 (Finite test control). Every positive current is of coefficient Radon type. For each compact original test \(\eta\) there is a nonnegative compact trace test \(\Theta\) and a constant \(c_\eta\) such that \[|\langle T,h\eta\rangle| \le c_\eta\|h\|_\infty\langle T,\Theta\rangle \tag{2.2}\] for positive \(T\) and bounded Borel \(h\) on the chosen compact stage. The positive cone is weakly closed and pointed. If positive currents \(T_j\) converge on all original tests, their coefficient variations are uniformly bounded on each compact stage. Thus \(f_jT_j\to fT\) for locally uniformly convergent continuous \(f_j\to f\) .

title: Proposition 2.2 — Classical regularization
text:
Classical regularization Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 2.2 (Classical regularization). For every \(u\in\mathcal C_b(U)\) and every \(x\in U\) there is one ordinary neighborhood \(W\) of \(x\) and continuous semipositive rational PL functions \(p_j\) over \(K\) , defined on \(W\) , with \(p_j\downarrow u\) . The class \(\mathcal C_b\) is stable under decreasing locally bounded limits. For finitely many decreasing families with locally bounded endpoints, the common projective extension construction gives one such neighborhood for all rows. Continuous members of these rows admit smooth positive uniform approximants on smaller fixed neighborhoods. Smooth majorants of each bounded member can consequently be chosen pointwise convergent and locally uniformly bounded.

title: Proposition 2.3 — First order and ordered products
text:
First order and ordered products Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 2.3 (First order and ordered products). If \(R\) is a background and \(u\in\mathcal C_b\) , then \(D(uR)\) is positive, symmetric, separately closed and of coefficient Radon type. Iterating this operation defines (1.1) . The ordered products are local and separately additive and positively homogeneous in the potentials. They are independent of the approximants used in the first-order construction.

title: Proposition 2.4 — Relative local mass estimate
text:
Relative local mass estimate Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 2.4 (Relative local mass estimate). Fix compact test stages \(L\Subset W\) and \(k\le q\) . For each finite original coefficient presentation on \(L\) there is a constant \(C\) and a compact positive trace test \(\Theta\) on \(W\) such that \[\|T_{S,k}(u_1,\ldots,u_k)\|_{L} \le C\prod_{i=1}^k\|u_i\|_{L^\infty(W)} \langle S,\Theta\rangle\] whenever the displayed bounds are finite. Here the left side denotes the sum of the coefficient variations in that finite presentation. The estimate is local and may be applied after every actual refinement.

title: Lemma 3.2 — A smooth psh collar
text:
A smooth psh collar Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 3.2 (A smooth psh collar). Under the assumptions of lemma 3.1 , there are compact polynomial norm boxes \[x\in\operatorname{Int}C_1,\qquad C_1\subset\operatorname{Int}C_{\mathrm{mid}},\qquad C_{\mathrm{mid}}\subset\operatorname{Int}C_2\Subset W,\] a smooth psh function \(b\) on a neighborhood of \(C_2\) , and a nonnegative original smooth cutoff \(\chi\) compactly supported in \(\Omega=\operatorname{Int}C_2\) , with the following properties. After adding one constant \(c\) to all the original functions, put \[v_{i,j}=\max\{u_{i,j}+c,b\},\qquad v_i=\max\{u_i+c,b\}.\] Then: \(v_{i,j},v_i\in\mathcal C_b(\Omega)\) and \(v_{i,j}\downarrow v_i\) ; \(v_{i,j}=u_{i,j}+c\) and \(v_i=u_i+c\) on a neighborhood of \(C_1\) ; \(\chi=1\) on a neighborhood of \(C_{\mathrm{mid}}\) ; all \(v_{i,j},v_i\) equal \(b\) on one fixed neighborhood of \(\operatorname{supp}d'\chi\cup\operatorname{supp}d''\chi\) ; each patched function \(v\) has smooth psh majorants \(v_\nu\geq v\) converging pointwise to \(v\) , uniformly bounded on \(\operatorname{supp}\chi\) , and equal to \(b\) on that same collar. title: Lemma 3.3 — Green exchange on a common collar
text:
Green exchange on a common collar Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 3.3 (Green exchange on a common collar). Let \(Q\) be a symmetric positive \(d'\) - and \(d''\) -closed current of bidegree \((n-1,n-1)\) on \(\Omega\) . Let \(\chi\in A_c^{0,0}(\Omega)\) . Suppose that \(a\) is smooth, \(g\) is locally bounded Borel, and both equal one smooth function \(b\) on a neighborhood of \(\operatorname{supp}d'\chi\cup\operatorname{supp}d''\chi\) . Whenever \(D(gQ)\) has coefficient Radon type, one has \[\langle aD(gQ),\chi\rangle =\langle gD(aQ),\chi\rangle.\] In this statement positivity of \(a\) and \(g\) is not required.

title: Lemma 3.4 — Monotonicity of the ordered trace integral

Monotonicity of the ordered trace integral Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 3.4 (Monotonicity of the ordered trace integral). Let \(S\) have bidegree \((p,p)\) , let \(0\leq k\leq n-p\) , and let \(\alpha\) be a smooth, positive, \(d'\) - and \(d''\) -closed form of bidegree \((n-p-k,n-p-k)\) such that wedging it with a positive current preserves positivity. For \(0\leq i\leq k\) , suppose \(f_i,g_i\in\mathcal C_b(\Omega)\) , \(f_i\leq g_i\) , and all these functions equal the same smooth psh function \(b\) near the derivative support of \(\chi\) . Define, using the ordered products, \[J(f_0;f_1,\ldots,f_k) =\langle f_0T_{S,k}(f_1,\ldots,f_k),\chi\alpha\rangle.\] Then \[J(f_0;f_1,\ldots,f_k) \leq J(g_0;g_1,\ldots,g_k).\]

An upper bound for decreasing weights Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:

Let \(P_j,P\) be positive coefficient Radon currents of one bidegree, with \(P_j\to P\) on all original compact smooth tests. Let \(a_j\downarrow a\) be locally uniformly bounded functions.
