title: Theorem 4.1 — The bounded-difference criterion
text:
The bounded-difference criterion Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 4.1 (The bounded-difference criterion). For \(h\in\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}(U)\) , \[D[h]\ge0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h\in\mathcal C_b(U).\] Both sides concern the given actual function.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 12.

title: Theorem 4.2 — The actual curvature kernel
text:
The actual curvature kernel Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 4.2 (The actual curvature kernel). The equality \[\ker\bigl(D:\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}(U)\longrightarrow\mathcal D'^{1,1}(U)\bigr) =\mathscr{PH}(U)\] holds for actual functions. In particular, if \(u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U)\) and \(D[u]=D[v]\) , the difference \(u-v\) is continuous and both its signs are classical psh.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 12.

title: Theorem 4.3 — Background invariance and order
text:
Background invariance and order Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 4.3 (Background invariance and order). Let \(S\) be a background of degree \((p,p)\) , with \(p<n\) . For \(u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U)\) , \[D[u]\ge D[v]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D(uS)\ge D(vS).\] Equality of the ambient curvatures gives equality of the displayed relative curvatures. The same replacement is valid in every differentiated slot of a mixed product whose other slots are fixed.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 12.

title: Corollary 4.4 — Gluing local-potential currents
text:
Gluing local-potential currents Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Corollary 4.4 (Gluing local-potential currents). Suppose each \(\alpha_i\) is a \((1,1)\) -current locally of the form \(D[a_i]\) with \(a_i\in\mathcal C_b\) . For \(k\le n-p\) there is a unique positive separately closed current \(\alpha_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\alpha_k\wedge S\) whose expression on such a neighborhood is \(T_{S,k}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) . It is symmetric, local, additive and positively homogeneous in these current slots.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 13.

title: Corollary 4.5 — Continuous curvature domination
text:
Continuous curvature domination Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Corollary 4.5 (Continuous curvature domination). Let \(u\in\mathcal C_b(U)\) , let \(g\) be continuous classical psh, and suppose \(0\le D[u]\le C D[g]\) for \(C\ge0\) . Then \(u\) and \(Cg-u\) are continuous classical psh functions.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 13.

title: Theorem 5.1 — Transfer of continuous coefficient relations
text:
Transfer of continuous coefficient relations Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 5.1 (Transfer of continuous coefficient relations). Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_m\in\mathcal C_b(U)\) and \(f_1,\ldots,f_m\in C(U,\mathbf R)\) . For a fixed background \(S\) , put \[A=\sum_i f_iD[g_i],\qquad A_S=\sum_i f_iD(g_iS).\] Then \(A\ge0\) implies \(A_S\ge0\) . In particular, \(A=0\) implies \(A_S=0\) on every original complementary test.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 13.

title: Example 5.2 — A Borel coefficient can destroy a relation
text:
A Borel coefficient can destroy a relation Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Example 5.2 (A Borel coefficient can destroy a relation). On the bidannulus \(U=\{r<|T_1|<R,\ r<|T_2|<R\}\) , where \(0<r<1<R\) , take \(Y=\{T_2=1\}\cap U\) and \(g=\max(0,\log|T_1|)\) . The first-order analytic-divisor nonconcentration theorem gives \(\mathbf1_YD[g]=0\) as an ambient coefficient Radon current. The subvariety formula and the slope jump on the \(T_1\) -annulus give \[\mathbf1_YD(g[Y])=D(g[Y])=i_*\delta_{\zeta_{0,1}}\ne0, \qquad i:Y\hookrightarrow U.\] Here \(\zeta_{0,1}\) is the radius-one Gauss point; the slope jump is one. A compact nonnegative original scalar test equal to one near that point has integral one. This is the obstruction to Borel coefficient transfer described in [ Order , Section Products in the continuous coefficient curvature module ].
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 14.

title: Lemma 6.1 — Signed products
text:
Signed products Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 6.1 (Signed products). Let \(Q_i\in\mathscr M^1\) be positive and suppose \(-M_iQ_i\le A_i\le M_iQ_i\) , where \(M_i\ge0\) . Then \[-\Bigl(\prod_iM_i\Bigr)R_S \le\Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r) \le\Bigl(\prod_iM_i\Bigr)R_S, \qquad R_S=\Phi_{S,r}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_r). \tag{6.1}\] The difference estimate (1.5) also holds.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 14.

title: Theorem 6.2 — Faithful realization
text:
Faithful realization Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 6.2 (Faithful realization). The completion \(\widehat E_Q(U)\) embeds isometrically into the actual symmetric coefficient Radon \((1,1)\) -currents. Its image is the closure of \(E_Q(U)\) for the ambient order norm defined by \(Q\) . If an actual current is obtained using controls \(Q\) and \(R\) , its two realizations agree in the completion controlled by \(Q+R\) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 15.

title: Theorem 6.3 — Extension of the mixed operation
text:
Extension of the mixed operation Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 6.3 (Extension of the mixed operation). The maps \(\Phi_{S,r}\) extend uniquely to symmetric locally \(C(U,\mathbf R)\) -multilinear operations on \(\mathscr M^1_{\rm ord}\) , continuous for every common finite family of local order controls. They are positive, local, compatible with gluing, and satisfy the signed and difference estimates. Their supports satisfy \[\operatorname{supp}\Phi_{S,r}(A_1,\ldots,A_r) \subset\operatorname{supp}S\cap\bigcap_i\operatorname{supp}A_i. \tag{6.3}\] If the mixed products along an order-convergent approximation are separately closed, their limit is separately closed.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 15.

title: Corollary 6.4 — Fixed-generator approximation by curvatures
text:
Fixed-generator approximation by curvatures Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Corollary 6.4 (Fixed-generator approximation by curvatures). Suppose locally \[A=\sum_{i=1}^N f_iD[g_i],\qquad A_j=\sum_{i=1}^N f_{i,j}D[g_i]=D[v_j],\] where \(g_i\) and \(v_j\) are finite continuous local classical psh differences, \(f_i,f_{i,j}\) are continuous, and \(f_{i,j}\to f_i\) locally uniformly. Then \(\Phi_{S,1}(A)\) is separately closed for every allowed background \(S\) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 16.

title: Proposition 6.5 — A support-conormal certificate
text:
A support-conormal certificate Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 6.5 (A support-conormal certificate). Let \(A_i=D[g_i]\) for continuous classical psh differences, and set \(T_i=D(g_iS)\) and \(F_i=\operatorname{supp}A_i\) . Then \(\operatorname{supp}T_i\subset F_i\) . If a smooth function \(h\) vanishes on \(F_i\) , then \(d'h\wedge T_i=d''h\wedge T_i=0\) . Suppose smooth covectors admit an identity \[\theta_i=\sum_a f_{ai}\eta_a+\sum_j b_{ij}d'h_{ij},\qquad \sum_i f_{ai}A_i=0,\qquad h_{ij}|_{F_i}=0,\] with continuous scalar coefficients and original smooth \(\eta_a,h_{ij}\) . Then \(\sum_i\theta_i\wedge T_i=0\) . The same assertion holds after interchanging the two differential columns.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 16.

title: Definition 7.1 — The actual boundary power classes
text:
The actual boundary power classes Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Definition 7.1 (The actual boundary power classes). The boundary condition \(\mathrm{BG}(u,0)\) means \(\overline{\{u<-t\}}\Subset V\) for every \(t>0\) . The class \(\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V)\) consists of negative extended classical potentials satisfying this condition and \(\nu_{u,j}(V)\to0\) . For \(\sigma>0\) , set \[\mathcal E^\sigma_{S,\partial}(V) =\left\{u\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V): e_\sigma(u)=\int_V(-u)^\sigma\,d\mu_u<\infty\right\}.\] The integral is over the finite-value locus, to which \(\mu_u\) is carried. Write \(\mathcal E^1=\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(V)\) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 16.

title: Theorem 7.2 — Analytic truncation estimates
text:
Analytic truncation estimates Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 7.2 (Analytic truncation estimates). The following statements hold. A locally coefficient-finite product (7.1) is separately closed on all original tests. This is an ordinary-local assertion. Under \(\mathrm{BG}(u,0)\) , \(\mu_u\) is locally finite and \[u\in\mathcal F_{S,\partial}(V) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad t^qC_S(\{u<-t\};V)\to0.\] For \(\sigma>0\) and \(u\) satisfying \(\mathrm{BG}(u,0)\) , put \[J_\sigma(u)=\int_0^\infty t^{q+\sigma-1}C_S(\{u<-t\};V)\,dt.\] Then \(J_\sigma(u)<\infty\) exactly when \(u\in\mathcal E^\sigma_{S,\partial}(V)\) , and \[\frac{\sigma}{2^{q+\sigma}}J_\sigma(u) \le e_\sigma(u) \le\frac{\sigma2^q}{1-2^{-\sigma}}J_\sigma(u). \tag{7.2}\] Raw and outer capacities agree on these ordinary open sublevels. For a finite tuple \(\mathbf u\) in this power class and a multi-index \(\gamma\) with \(k=|\gamma|\le q\) , its unbounded mixed curvature \(N_\gamma\) is defined, positive and separately closed. For \(k\le q-1\) , \[D(u_iN_\gamma)=N_{\gamma+e_i},\qquad \mathcal J'_{\gamma,i}=d'(u_iN_\gamma),\quad \mathcal J''_{\gamma,i}=d''(u_iN_\gamma). \tag{7.3}\] The first-order currents are of coefficient Radon type. When \(k+2\le q+\sigma\) , the energy matrix is also of coefficient Radon type and is given by \[G^\gamma_{ih} =\tfrac12\left[D(u_i u_hN_\gamma) -u_iN_{\gamma+e_h}-u_hN_{\gamma+e_i}\right]. \tag{7.4}\] It is positive semidefinite in the middle cone. Put \(\kappa=q+\sigma\) , \(w=\sum_i u_i\) , \(W=1-w\) , and \(J_w(R)=\int_R^\infty t^{\kappa-1}C_S(\{w<-t\};V)\,dt\) . For a curvature, first-order or energy coefficient current \(P\) , assign the degree budget \(b=k,k+1,k+2\) , respectively. If \(a+b\le\kappa\) , the actual and canonically truncated coefficients have the uniform tail bound \[\int_{\{w\le-R\}}W^a\,|d\mu_{P,\eta}| \le C_\eta R^{a+b-\kappa}J_w(R/4),\qquad R\ge1, \tag{7.5}\] with the corresponding bound for every bounded truncation. Canonical truncations converge in local coefficient total variation, including continuous tuple multipliers of growth at most \(W^a\) . Bounded actual Borel capacity limits of classical functions in \([-R,0]\) have an intrinsic bounded calculus, including first-order and energy currents. Its degree- \(b\) coefficients satisfy \[|\mu_{P_R,\eta}|(E)\le C_\eta R^bC_S^*(E;V). \tag{7.6}\] These currents are independent of defining rows and outer-null changes, and bounded continuous tuple weights pass under capacity convergence. There is a bounded continuous classical barrier \[\rho=\max\left(-1,\max_a\log\frac{|f_a|}{R_a}, \max_b\log\frac{r_b}{|g_b|}\right) \tag{7.7}\] on a neighborhood of \(K_0\) , with \(-1\le\rho<0\) on \(V\) , compact negative sublevels, and \(\mu_\rho(V)<\infty\) . For \(u\in\mathcal E^\sigma\) , the bounded finite-mass potentials \(\max(u,j\rho)\) decrease to \(u\) . Fixed lower-barrier families have critical weighted convergence, including global mixed-energy convergence in first energy.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 17.

title: Lemma 7.3 — Global bounded Green exchange
text:
Global bounded Green exchange Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 7.3 (Global bounded Green exchange). Let \(a,b\le0\) be bounded classical potentials with compact negative sublevel closures. If \(D(aQ)\) and \(D(bQ)\) have finite total mass, then \[\int_V(-a)D(bQ)=\int_V(-b)D(aQ)=\int_V\Gamma_Q(a,b).\] The diagonal energy is finite, and the cross energy has finite total variation.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 18.

title: Theorem 7.4 — First mixed energy
text:
First mixed energy Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 7.4 (First mixed energy). For \(u_0,\ldots,u_q\in\mathcal E^1\) , the finite functional \[B(u_0,\ldots,u_q)=\int_V(-u_0)N_q(u_1,\ldots,u_q)\] is symmetric and separately additive and positively homogeneous. For \(Q=N_{q-1}(c_2,\ldots,c_q)\) , \[\int_V\Gamma_Q(a,b)=B(a,b,c_2,\ldots,c_q),\qquad |B(a,b,\mathbf c)|^2\le B(a,a,\mathbf c)B(b,b,\mathbf c). \tag{7.8}\] The energy matrix stays positive on finite real linear combinations of the potentials, and all cross energies have finite total variation. Moreover, \[B(u_0,\ldots,u_q)\le\prod_{i=0}^q e(u_i)^{1/d},\qquad e(u+v)^{1/d}\le e(u)^{1/d}+e(v)^{1/d}. \tag{7.9}\] The constant one is optimal whenever the class contains a positive energy potential.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 18.

title: Theorem 7.5 — Uniform energy tests
text:
Uniform energy tests Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 7.5 (Uniform energy tests). Put \(\alpha=2^{-q}\) . For \(u,v,\psi\in\mathcal E^1\) and \(M=\max\{e(u+v),e(\psi)\}\) , \[\int_V|u-v|\,d\mu_\psi \le2^{(q-1)\alpha}I(u,v)^\alpha M^{1-\alpha}. \tag{7.12}\] For a mixed top measure, replace \(\psi\) by the sum of its \(q\) potentials and divide the bound by \(q!\) . At \(M=0\) the integral is zero.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 19.

title: Proposition 7.6 — Sharp midpoint bound
text:
Sharp midpoint bound Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 7.6 (Sharp midpoint bound). For \(u,v\in\mathcal E^1\) , \[\mathscr A\left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right) -\frac{\mathscr A(u)+\mathscr A(v)}2 \ge c_q I(u,v),\qquad c_q=\frac{1-2^{-q}}{2(q+1)}. \tag{7.17}\] This constant is optimal if a positive-energy potential exists.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 20.

title: Lemma 8.1 — Uniform deep tails and global weighted tightness
text:
Uniform deep tails and global weighted tightness Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 8.1 (Uniform deep tails and global weighted tightness). Every strongly Cauchy actual row has bounded first energies and \[\begin{aligned} \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_j \int_{\{u_j<-R\}}(-u_j)\,d\mu_{u_j}&=0,\\ \lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_j \int_R^\infty t^q C_S(\{u_j<-t\};V)\,dt&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{8.2}\] For finitely many strongly Cauchy actual rows \(u_{i,j}\) , \(0\leq i\leq q\) , the finite positive Radon measures \[(-u_{0,j})M(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{q,j}) \tag{8.3}\] are uniformly tight on \(V\) . The same conclusions hold if the indices of the finitely many rows tend independently to infinity.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 21.

title: Definition 8.2 — Strong relative first-energy completion
text:
Strong relative first-energy completion Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Definition 8.2 (Strong relative first-energy completion). Let \(\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_{\rm str}(V)\) consist of actual Borel functions \(u:V\to[-\infty,0]\) which are limits of an actual strongly Cauchy row in every local truncated outer \(S\) -capacity. Equality means local outer-capacity equality. The capacities may equivalently be taken on all compact cores in the fixed domain \(V\) , by the analytic capacity-domain comparison in theorem 7.2 . A choice of actual defining row is not part of the element of this quotient.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 22.

title: Proposition 8.3 — Borel limits of all strongly Cauchy actual rows
text:
Borel limits of all strongly Cauchy actual rows Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 8.3 (Borel limits of all strongly Cauchy actual rows). Every row satisfying (8.1) has a limit in definition 8.2 , unique modulo local outer-capacity zero. Every member of that space is finite and continuous locally outside ordinary open sets of arbitrarily small outer capacity. Its pole set is locally outer-capacity zero.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 22.

title: Theorem 8.4 — Canonical critical calculus in the strong completion
text:
Canonical critical calculus in the strong completion Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 8.4 (Canonical critical calculus in the strong completion). For a finite tuple \(\mathbf u\) in \(\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_{\rm str}(V)\) , with actual strongly Cauchy defining rows \(\mathbf u_j\) , there are intrinsic coefficient-Radon original currents \[\widehat N_\gamma(\mathbf u),\qquad \widehat{\mathcal J}'_{\gamma,i},\quad \widehat{\mathcal J}''_{\gamma,i},\qquad \widehat G^\gamma_{ih}. \tag{8.10}\] Curvatures have \(k=|\gamma|\leq q\) ; first-order and energy currents have \(k\leq q-1\) . All energy degrees are included, since \(k+2\leq q+1=d\) . Curvatures are separately closed, symmetric and middle-positive; energy matrices are positive. First-order and energy currents are not asserted to be closed. For any continuous \(F\) on the nonpositive orthant satisfying \(|F(x)|\leq A(1-\sum_i x_i)^a\) , the actual multiplier limit \[F(\mathbf u_j)P_j \longrightarrow F(\mathbf u)\widehat P \qquad(a+b\leq d) \tag{8.11}\] holds on every original compact smooth complementary test and every actual moment refinement. Here the degree budget \(b\) is \(k\) , \(k+1\) , or \(k+2\) for curvature, first-order, or energy. All these multipliers are coefficient-integrable. The currents and weighted limits are independent of defining rows and of outer-capacity-null representatives, and they annihilate the joint pole set. They satisfy all original recursive identities, including \[\begin{aligned} D(u_i\widehat N_\gamma)&=\widehat N_{\gamma+e_i},\\ d'(u_i\widehat N_\gamma)&=\widehat{\mathcal J}'_{\gamma,i},\qquad d''(u_i\widehat N_\gamma)=\widehat{\mathcal J}''_{\gamma,i} \qquad(k\leq q-1), \end{aligned} \tag{8.12}\] and the actual three-term energy identity obtained by placing hats on (7.4) . For \(q+1\) completed slots, the global mixed energy is finite and \[B(u_{0,j},\ldots,u_{q,j}) \longrightarrow \widehat B(u_0,\ldots,u_q) :=\int_V(-u_0)\widehat N(u_1,\ldots,u_q). \tag{8.13}\] The corresponding positive weighted measures converge against every bounded original smooth scalar test, including those without compact support. The assertion also permits independent indices tending to infinity in the defining rows.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 22.

title: Lemma 8.5 — Uniform discrepancy continuity on energy balls
text:
Uniform discrepancy continuity on energy balls Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 8.5 (Uniform discrepancy continuity on energy balls). The completed space is closed under finite sums and nonnegative scalar multiples. Its mixed energy is symmetric, positive and multilinear on that cone, and satisfies the constant-one Hölder inequality. The formulas (7.12) , (7.13) , (7.14) and the sharp midpoint inequality (7.17) hold in the completion, with their actual Borel multipliers and local capacities. In particular, \(\widehat I\geq0\) , and it vanishes exactly on equal relative classes. If \(\widehat e(a),\widehat e(a'),\widehat e(b)\leq M\) , then \[\big|\widehat I(a,b)-\widehat I(a',b)\big| \leq L_q M^{1-\alpha}\widehat I(a,a')^\alpha, \qquad L_q=2(q+1)2^{(q-1)\alpha}3^{d(1-\alpha)}. \tag{8.18}\] The assertion at \(M=0\) means that both sides are zero.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 24.

title: Theorem 8.6 — Completeness and the intrinsic strong topology
text:
Completeness and the intrinsic strong topology Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 8.6 (Completeness and the intrinsic strong topology). Every \(\widehat I\) -Cauchy sequence in \(\widehat{\mathcal E}^1_{\rm str}(V)\) converges to a unique relative class in that space, with discrepancy tending to zero. The actual classical class is strongly dense. For members \(u_j,u\) of this space, one has \[\widehat I(u_j,u)\longrightarrow0 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \left\{ \begin{array}{l} u_j\longrightarrow u\text{ in all local truncated outer capacities},\\ \widehat e(u_j)\longrightarrow\widehat e(u). \end{array}\right. \tag{8.20}\] Strongly convergent finite tuples have every original local weighted-current limit in (8.11) , including all its critical endpoints, and the global mixed-energy and weighted-measure limits (8.13) . The weighted limits here are original-current limits.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 24.

title: Proposition 8.7 — Monotone closure
text:
Monotone closure Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 8.7 (Monotone closure). For completed potentials \(a\le b\) relatively quasi-everywhere, \[0\le\widehat I(a,b)\le\widehat e(a)-\widehat e(b).\] An increasing sequence in the strong cone converges strongly to its pointwise monotone Borel limit. The same holds for a decreasing sequence with uniformly bounded energies. Equalities and monotonicity are understood outside one locally outer-null set.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 25.

title: Definition 9.1 — Energy-difference space and its norm
text:
Energy-difference space and its norm Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Definition 9.1 (Energy-difference space and its norm). Let \(\mathbb D_S=\mathscr C-\mathscr C\) be the real vector space of such Borel differences modulo local outer-capacity equality. Define \[\|h\|_{\rm ed} =\inf\{r(a)+r(b):a,b\in\mathscr C,\ h=a-b\}. \tag{9.1}\]
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 26.

title: Lemma 9.2 — Continuous extension of the mixed energy
text:
Continuous extension of the mixed energy Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 9.2 (Continuous extension of the mixed energy). There is a unique symmetric real \(d\) -linear form on \(\mathbb D_S\) extending \(B\) , and it satisfies \[|B(h_0,\ldots,h_q)|\leq\prod_{i=0}^q\|h_i\|_{\rm ed}. \tag{9.2}\] Moreover \(\|u\|_{\rm ed}=r(u)\) for every \(u\in\mathscr C\) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 26.

title: Theorem 9.3 — Actual Borel realization and Banach completeness
text:
Actual Borel realization and Banach completeness Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 9.3 (Actual Borel realization and Banach completeness). Formula (9.1) is a norm, \(\mathbb D_S\) is complete for that norm, and \(\mathscr C\) is a closed convex cone in this Banach space. Norm convergence implies convergence in the full local outer \(S\) -capacity topology. More precisely, with \(C_0=d2^d\) , one has \[C_S^*(\{|h|>t\};V)\leq C_0 t^{-d}\|h\|_{\rm ed}^{d} \qquad(h\in\mathbb D_S,\ t>0). \tag{9.3}\] For \(u,v\in\mathscr C\) , \[I(u,v)\leq\bigl(r(u)^q+r(v)^q\bigr)\|u-v\|_{\rm ed}. \tag{9.4}\]
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 26.

title: Definition 9.4 — Curvature as an energy-dual functional
text:
Curvature as an energy-dual functional Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Definition 9.4 (Curvature as an energy-dual functional). For \(u\in\mathscr C\) put \[J(u)(h)=B(h,u^{[q]})=-\int_Vh\,d\widehat\mu_u \qquad(h\in\mathbb D_S). \tag{9.7}\] The displayed integral is literal and absolutely convergent: for \(h=a-b\) , \(|h|\leq(-a)+(-b)\) off a common null set, and the two mixed first energies are finite. The current measure ignores that exceptional set. Thus \(J(u)\) is a genuine functional in \(\mathbb D_S^*\) , with its original current interpretation.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 27.

title: Theorem 9.5 — Exact dual norm and strong continuity of curvature
text:
Exact dual norm and strong continuity of curvature Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 9.5 (Exact dual norm and strong continuity of curvature). For every continuous linear functional \(\ell\) on \(\mathbb D_S\) , \[\|\ell\|_*= \sup_{\substack{a\in\mathscr C\\r(a)\leq1}}|\ell(a)|. \tag{9.8}\] For \(u\in\mathscr C\) one has \(\|J(u)\|_*=r(u)^q\) . For \(u,v\in\mathscr C\) and \(R=\max(r(u),r(v))\) , \[\begin{aligned} \|J(u)-J(v)\|_*&\leq qR^{q-1}\|u-v\|_{\rm ed},\\ \|J(u)-J(v)\|_*&\leq\sqrt q\,R^{(q-1)/2}I(u,v)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \tag{9.9}\] At \(R=0\) both sides mean zero; for \(q=1\) the power \(R^0\) is one. In particular strong convergence of potentials gives norm convergence of their source functionals, in every remaining degree.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 27.

title: Theorem 9.6 — A complete curvature-dual metric and closed source image
text:
A complete curvature-dual metric and closed source image Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 9.6 (A complete curvature-dual metric and closed source image). The image \(J(\mathscr C)\) is norm closed in \(\mathbb D_S^*\) . The formula \[d_J(u,v)=\|J(u)-J(v)\|_* \tag{9.11}\] defines a complete metric on \(\mathscr C\) , inducing precisely the strong discrepancy topology. For \(u,v\in\mathscr C\) , \[\begin{aligned} I(u,v)&\leq(r(u)+r(v))d_J(u,v),\\ d_J(u,v)&\leq\sqrt q\, \max(r(u),r(v))^{(q-1)/2}I(u,v)^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \tag{9.12}\]
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 28.

title: Definition 9.7 — The strong-continuous energy dual
text:
The strong-continuous energy dual Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Definition 9.7 (The strong-continuous energy dual). Let \(\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*\) consist of those \(\ell\in\mathbb D_S^*\) for which \[u_j,u\in\mathscr C,\ I(u_j,u)\to0 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ell(u_j)\to\ell(u). \tag{9.13}\]
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 29.

title: Lemma 9.8 — A closed dual class containing every curvature
text:
A closed dual class containing every curvature Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 9.8 (A closed dual class containing every curvature). The class \(\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*\) is a norm-closed linear subspace of \(\mathbb D_S^*\) , and \(J(\mathscr C)\) is contained in it. Consequently the norm-closed linear span of all curvature functionals is contained in this class.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 29.

title: Theorem 9.9 — All-degree variational normal decomposition
text:
All-degree variational normal decomposition Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 9.9 (All-degree variational normal decomposition). For every \(\ell\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*\) , the functional \[F_\ell(v)=\ell(v)-e(v)/d\qquad(v\in\mathscr C) \tag{9.15}\] has a unique maximizer \(u=\Pi(\ell)\) . Every maximizing sequence converges strongly to \(u\) . Equivalently, there is a unique pair \((u,n)\) with \[\ell=J(u)+n,\qquad u\in\mathscr C,\quad n\in\mathscr C^\circ, \quad n(u)=0. \tag{9.16}\] The residual also lies in \(\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*\) . Define the nonnegative support gauge \[p(\ell)=\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathscr C\\r(v)\leq1}}\ell(v). \tag{9.17}\] Then \[\begin{aligned} e(u)&=\ell(u),\qquad r(u)^q=p(\ell)\leq\|\ell\|_*,\\ \sup F_\ell&=\frac qd\,p(\ell)^{d/q}. \end{aligned} \tag{9.18}\] If \(\ell\) is nonnegative on \(\mathscr C\) , then \(p(\ell)=\|\ell\|_*\) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 29.

title: Theorem 9.10 — A quantitative nonlinear retraction of source functionals
text:
A quantitative nonlinear retraction of source functionals Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 9.10 (A quantitative nonlinear retraction of source functionals). Put \(\mathcal P(\ell)=J(\Pi(\ell))\) on \(\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm{s}}^*\) . This is a retraction onto the norm-closed image \(J(\mathscr C)\) , and is positively homogeneous of degree one. For \(\|\ell\|_*,\|m\|_*\leq R\) , with \(R>0\) , one has \[\begin{aligned} I(\Pi(\ell),\Pi(m))&\leq2R^{1/q}\|\ell-m\|_*,\\ \|\mathcal P(\ell)-\mathcal P(m)\|_* &\leq\sqrt{2qR}\,\|\ell-m\|_*^{1/2}. \end{aligned} \tag{9.20}\] The first inequality has the more precise right side \((\ell-m)(\Pi(\ell)-\Pi(m))\) . If \(n=\ell-\mathcal P(\ell)\) and \(R=\|\ell\|_*>0\) , then \[\left(\sqrt{qR+\|n\|_*}-\sqrt{qR}\right)^2 \leq\operatorname{dist}_*(\ell,J(\mathscr C))\leq\|n\|_*. \tag{9.21}\] In particular a nonzero residual is a quantitative obstruction to source-image approximation, not merely a failure of one chosen maximization algorithm.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 30.

title: Lemma 9.11 — Countable exact moments and compensators
text:
Countable exact moments and compensators Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 9.11 (Countable exact moments and compensators). There are compact moment cores \(K_l\Subset V\) and smooth classical psh functions \(a_l\) on \(V\) , with \(0\le a_l\le1\) , such that every original compact smooth scalar test can be localized to finitely many of these cores. On each selected core, \(Da_l\) dominates a positive multiple of the identity form in all the moment directions of the localized test and its smooth partition. The same assertion holds after every actual finite refinement.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 30.

title: Proposition 9.12 — A simultaneous geometric probe
text:
A simultaneous geometric probe Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Proposition 9.12 (A simultaneous geometric probe). There is a bounded continuous classical potential \(\psi_0\) determined by the box alone such that, for every extending allowed \(S\) , \[-1<\psi_0<0,\qquad \rho\le\psi_0,\qquad \mu_{\psi_0}(V)\le\mu_\rho(V)<\infty.\] It has compact negative sublevels and ordinary zero boundary value. For every original real compact smooth scalar \(\phi\) , there is \(\epsilon_\phi>0\) , independent of \(S\) , such that \[\psi_0+t\phi\in\mathcal E^1_{S,\partial}(V), \qquad |t|\le\epsilon_\phi. \tag{9.22}\] These functions are bounded continuous classical psh, lie between \(-1\) and \(0\) , and have finite total top mass. On a fixed finite presentation one may choose \[\epsilon_\phi\ge \frac{c_{\mathfrak a}}{\max(1,\|\phi\|_{2,\mathfrak a})}, \tag{9.23}\] where \(\|\cdot\|_{2,\mathfrak a}\) is the sum of the real \(C^2\) norms of its representatives on that presentation.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 31.

title: Theorem 9.13 — One probe detects the literal source equation
text:
One probe detects the literal source equation Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 9.13 (One probe detects the literal source equation). Suppose \(\ell=J(u)+n\) is a normal pair, with \(u\in\mathscr C\) , \(n(v)\le0\) for every \(v\in\mathscr C\) , and \(n(u)=0\) . Set \[\Xi_{\psi_0}(\ell,u)=J(u)(\psi_0)-\ell(\psi_0)=-n(\psi_0)\ge0.\] For every original real compact smooth scalar \(\phi\) , \[|n(\phi)|\le\epsilon_\phi^{-1} \Xi_{\psi_0}(\ell,u). \tag{9.24}\] Now let \(\mu\) be positive Radon with \(\ell_\mu\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*\) , and let \(u=\Pi(\ell_\mu)\) . Then the following are equivalent: \(\displaystyle\Xi_{\psi_0}(\mu) :=\int_V(-\psi_0)\,d\widehat\mu_u -\int_V(-\psi_0)\,d\mu=0\) ; \(\widehat\mu_u=\mu\) on every original compact smooth scalar test; there exists \(v\in\mathscr C\) with \(\widehat\mu_v=\mu\) . The solution in (iii) is unique and equals \(u\) . For all data in this class, \[\left|\int_V\phi\,d(\mu-\widehat\mu_u)\right| \le\epsilon_\phi^{-1}\Xi_{\psi_0}(\mu). \tag{9.25}\] The same \(\psi_0\) works for every extending background, every legal remaining degree, and every actual refinement of the original tests.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background: curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations. PDF page 32.

title: Corollary 9.14 — Additive strictness and dense admissible sources
text:
Additive strictness and dense admissible sources Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Corollary 9.14 (Additive strictness and dense admissible sources). Under the literal hypotheses of theorem 9.13 , if \(u=v+\varepsilon\psi_0\) for some \(v\in\mathscr C\) and \(\varepsilon>0\) , then \(\widehat\mu_u=\mu\) . For any \(a\in\mathscr C\) , the potentials \(a+\varepsilon\psi_0\) admit both signs of every compact smooth direction, tend to \(a\) in the energy-difference norm, and satisfy \[\|J(a+\varepsilon\psi_0)-J(a)\|_* \le(r(a)+\varepsilon r(\psi_0))^q-r(a)^q.\] Their sources are therefore dense in \(J(\mathscr C)\) .

title: Theorem 10.3 — Strong clipping convergence for signed nest data
text:
Strong clipping convergence for signed nest data Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 10.3 (Strong clipping convergence for signed nest data). Let \(\mu_j=\mathbf1_{F_j}\mu\) be the finite-energy nest restrictions from the finite-energy nest in the proof of theorem 10.1 , and put \(u_j=-G\mu_j\) . For every \(k>0\) , \[T_ku_j\longrightarrow T_ku_\mu \quad\hbox{strongly in }H. \tag{10.14}\]

title: Theorem 10.4 — Full signed renormalized chain and energy distribution
text:
Full signed renormalized chain and energy distribution Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 10.4 (Full signed renormalized chain and energy distribution). For \(u=u_\mu\) , the increasing compatible energy measure \(\Gamma_S(u)=\lim_k\Gamma_S(T_ku)\) is sigma-finite, finite on every bounded value strip, and zero on every exact scalar level. If \(\Phi\in C^2(\mathbf R)\) has bounded first derivative and compactly supported second derivative, then \[D(\Phi(u)S)=\Phi'(\widetilde u)\mu +\Phi''(\widetilde u)\Gamma_S(u) \tag{10.19}\] on all original compact smooth tests. Every term is coefficient- defined, and the right side is a finite signed Radon measure. If in addition \(\Phi'\) has compact support, then \(\Phi(u)-\Phi(0)\in H\) . For every \(0\le a<b\) , \[\mathcal E(T_bu-T_au) =-\int(T_b\widetilde u-T_a\widetilde u)\,d\mu. \tag{10.20}\] The scalar energy image has density \[\widetilde u_*\Gamma_S(u)=k_\mu(t)\,dt,\qquad k_\mu(t)= \begin{cases} \mu\{\widetilde u<t\},&t<0,\\ -\mu\{\widetilde u>t\},&t>0. \end{cases} \tag{10.21}\] This density is nonnegative and bounded by \(B_\mu\) almost everywhere; its value at zero is immaterial. In particular all bounded-value weighted energy measures used here are finite Radon measures.

title: Lemma 10.6 — Finite signed Radon data in the $H$ level theorem
text:
Finite signed Radon data in the $H$ level theorem Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Lemma 10.6 (Finite signed Radon data in the \(H\) level theorem). Let \(v\in H\) and suppose \(D(vS)=\sigma\) is a finite signed Radon measure on the original tests. Then the conclusion (10.10) and its exact carrier assertion holds, with a finite diffuse positive level measure, without assuming finite energy integral of \(|\sigma|\) .

title: Theorem 10.7 — Exact level carriers and coarea for all signed diffuse data
text:
Exact level carriers and coarea for all signed diffuse data Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 10.7 (Exact level carriers and coarea for all signed diffuse data). For every finite signed energy-diffuse datum and every real \(t\) , \[\mathbf1_{\{\widetilde u\ne t\}}L_t(u;S)=0. \tag{10.25}\] For every bounded compactly supported Borel scalar \(\theta\) , \[\int\theta(t)L_t(u;S)\,dt =\theta(\widetilde u)\Gamma_S(u) \tag{10.26}\] as finite signed Radon measures. The hard-curvature variation bounds (10.23) hold on the complete original space and every actual moment refinement.

title: Definition 10.8 — The signed renormalized zero-boundary class
text:
The signed renormalized zero-boundary class Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Definition 10.8 (The signed renormalized zero-boundary class). For the specified finite signed diffuse datum, a candidate is \(v\in L^1(F,\lambda)\) with a finite energy-quasicontinuous representative and \(T_kv\in H\) for every \(k>0\) . Use the compatible sigma-finite energy measure of its clippings. Require the original current identity \[D(\Phi(v)S)=\Phi'(\widetilde v)\mu +\Phi''(\widetilde v)\Gamma_S(v) \tag{10.27}\] for every \(\Phi\in C^2(\mathbf R)\) with compactly supported first derivative, and the radiation condition \(k^{-1}\mathcal E(T_{2k}v-T_kv)\to0\) . These conditions specify the boundary and solution class without using the transposition identity in their definition.

title: Theorem 10.9 — The complete finite-diffuse relative renormalized Dirichlet problem
text:
The complete finite-diffuse relative renormalized Dirichlet problem Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 10.9 (The complete finite-diffuse relative renormalized Dirichlet problem). Every finite signed energy-diffuse Radon datum has exactly one candidate in definition 10.8 . It is the transposition solution \(u_\mu\) , and all its original current, exact-level, coarea and global curvature-variation conclusions above hold. The construction and solution class are independent of the chosen faithful reference measure.

title: Theorem 10.10 — Strong clipping and smooth-curvature stability
text:
Strong clipping and smooth-curvature stability Bedford–Taylor products with a positive closed background:
curvature quotients, relative energy and source equations  Theorem 10.10 (Strong clipping and smooth-curvature stability). Suppose \(\|\mu_j-\mu\|_{\rm TV}\to0\) , and write \(u_j=u_{\mu_j}\) , \(u=u_\mu\) for the unique intrinsic renormalized solutions of \(D(u_jS)=\mu_j\) , \(D(uS)=\mu\) . Then, for every fixed \(k>0\) , \[\|T_ku_j-T_ku\|_H\longrightarrow0. \tag{10.29}\] In particular, for any fixed \(k,l>0\) , the finite original energy measures converge in global total variation: \[\Gamma_S(T_ku_j,T_lu_j) \longrightarrow\Gamma_S(T_ku,T_lu). \tag{10.30}\] If \(\Phi\in C^2(\mathbf R)\) has bounded first derivative and compactly supported second derivative, then \[D(\Phi(u_j)S)\longrightarrow D(\Phi(u)S) \quad\hbox{in global total variation}. \tag{10.31}\] If, more restrictively, \(\Phi'\) has compact support, then \(\Phi(u_j)-\Phi(0)\to\Phi(u)-\Phi(0)\) strongly in \(H\) . For this latter class both original first-order currents \(d'(\Phi(u_j)S)\) and \(d''(\Phi(u_j)S)\) converge in local coefficient total variation, against every original compact complementary smooth test and every actual moment refinement. The zero-order multipliers \(\Phi(u_j)S\) converge in that same local coefficient sense under the hypotheses of (10.31) .

title: Definition 1.1 — Background and classical potential
text:
Background and classical potential An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Definition 1.1 (Background and classical potential). An allowed background on an ordinary open \(U\) is a symmetric CLD middle-positive current \(S\) of bidegree \((p,p)\) satisfying \(d'S=d''S=0\) . Middle positivity is the CLD cone detected by the signed column-square tests \(\eta\wedge J\eta\) in complementary degree; its coefficient matrices are positive semidefinite in those presentations. Put \(q=n-p\) . The class \(\mathcal C_b(U)\) consists of real-valued, locally bounded, upper-semicontinuous classical psh functions. Classical psh means that pullback to every analytic curve, after every complete isometric extension of the ground field, is subharmonic. The bounded Bedford–Taylor product is denoted by \[T_{S,0}=S,\qquad T_{S,b}(u_1,\ldots,u_b) =\mathrm D\bigl(u_1T_{S,b-1}(u_2,\ldots,u_b)\bigr),\quad b\le q. \tag{1.1}\] For finite differences of such potentials the notation denotes the signed multilinear extension.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 3.

title: Definition 1.2 — Admissible finite scalar presentations
text:
Admissible finite scalar presentations An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Definition 1.2 (Admissible finite scalar presentations). A finite family of continuous real scalars is admissible if, locally on one ordinary representative, it is expressed through an actual unit tuple \(t_f=(-\log|f_1|,\ldots,-\log|f_N|)\) on its complete moment image, with one finite coefficient complex, and has the following properties. Each scalar is PL or piecewise smooth with a smooth extension near each closed coefficient cell. It belongs to the actual degree-zero delta-form sheaf and has its full curvature \(\mathrm D_\delta h\in\mathscr B^{1,1}\) . It is also a finite difference of continuous classical psh functions on that representative. Write \(\mathscr P_{\mathrm{adm}}\) for the resulting local scalar sheaf. Its PL subsheaf is denoted by \(\mathscr P\) . Every finite continuous PL presentation in actual unit moments belongs to this class by local convex-difference decomposition.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 4.

title: Conjecture 1.3 — Descent of actual analytic relations
text:
Descent of actual analytic relations An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Conjecture 1.3 (Descent of actual analytic relations). Let \(n\ge1\) , \(1\le b\le n\) , and let \(P\) be a finite signed admissible PL/PS presentation at an ordinary germ \((X,x)\) over the fixed \(K\) . Suppose \(\kappa_b(P)=0\) as an actual analytic delta-form germ. There is an ordinary representative \(U\) of this germ, chosen for \(P\) , such that for every \(0\le p\le n-b\) and every allowed background \(S\) of bidegree \((p,p)\) on \(U\) , \[\mathcal A_S(P)=0\quad\hbox{on }U. \tag{1.4}\] The equality holds on every original compact smooth complementary CLD test and after every actual refinement of the presentation. The field, its absolute value and the carrier of \(S\) remain the given ones.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 4.

title: Theorem 2.1 — Bounded relative calculus
text:
Bounded relative calculus An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Theorem 2.1 (Bounded relative calculus). Let \(S\) be an allowed background of degree \((p,p)\) on \(U\) , and let \(u_1,\ldots,u_b\in\mathcal C_b(U)\) , where \(b\le n-p\) . The recursion (1.1) defines a coefficient-Radon current, independent of the decreasing regularizations used in its construction. It is positive, separately \(d'\) - and \(d''\) -closed, symmetric in the differentiated slots, and additive and positively homogeneous in each slot. It commutes with ordinary restriction and gluing. For decreasing rows \(u_{i,j}\downarrow u_i\) in \(\mathcal C_b(U)\) , including a bounded weight slot \(u_{0,j}\downarrow u_0\) , one has \[u_{0,j}T_{S,b}(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{b,j}) \longrightarrow u_0T_{S,b}(u_1,\ldots,u_b) \tag{2.1}\] on all original compact smooth tests. In top degree this is local weak convergence of measures on compact continuous scalar tests. Each differentiated slot depends only on its curvature current.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 6.

title: Proposition 3.1 — Two sufficient quadratic certificates
text:
Two sufficient quadratic certificates An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Proposition 3.1 (Two sufficient quadratic certificates). Let \(P\) be an actual quadratic relation on an ordinary germ. Either of the following constructions proves its action vanishes for every allowed background of degree \(p\le n-2\) : an actual local identity \(\alpha_P=d'\beta+d''\zeta\) ; full-exact symmetric approximants \(a_j=d'\beta_j+d''\zeta_j\) , one fixed positive represented control \(Q\) , and \(\varepsilon_j\downarrow0\) , all chosen on an ordinary representative before the background and tests, such that \[-\varepsilon_jQ\le[\alpha_P]-[a_j]\le\varepsilon_jQ \tag{3.6}\] in the established order module, with its all-background degree-one action estimate.

Vanishing of the carrier-CLN certificate An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Question 3.2 (Vanishing of the carrier-CLN certificate). Let \(P\) be an actual signed PL-zero germ of degree \(b\ge2\) . On an ordinary representative, is \[q^{U,b}_{F,L}(P)=0\] for every required compact stage \(L\) and the original absolute cap carrier (3.8) , with the generator space in (3.7) unchanged?

Local approximation of backgrounds An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Question 3.3 (Local approximation of backgrounds). Does every allowed background of degree \((p,p)\) belong to \(\mathcal W^p_{\mathrm{loc}}\) ? title: Problem 3.4 — From curvature products to differential calculus
text:
From curvature products to differential calculus An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 3.4 (From curvature products to differential calculus). Construct, in the original analytic category, the additional interfaces needed for a graded differential action: descent for higher coupled relations, descent with variable finite piecewise-smooth coefficients, compatibility of the resulting differential operators, and the extension from ordinary-current tests to the intended delta-form test classes. For each interface, identify its object sheaf and prove its local presentation independence, differential identities and stated functoriality.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 10.

Quadratic descent in finite residue rank at most two An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Theorem 4.1 (Quadratic descent in finite residue rank at most two). Fix a finite continuous PL or PS scalar presentation through \(f\) , whose coefficient functions extend smoothly near the closed cells of one finite coefficient complex. Let \(P=\sum c_

There are also full-exact symmetric approximants satisfying (3.6) with one fixed represented positive control, chosen before every subsequent background, test and refinement. title: Theorem 4.2 — Punctured quadratic action and a central residual
text:
Punctured quadratic action and a central residual An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Theorem 4.2 (Punctured quadratic action and a central residual). Let \((Y,y)\) be a supplied normal-three model germ as above, and let \(P\) be a fixed finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS quadratic presentation with \(\kappa_2(P)=0\) . There is an ordinary representative \(U\) such that, for every allowed background \(S\) of degree \(p=0\) or \(1\) , \[\mathcal A_S(P)|_{U\setminus\{y\}}=0. \tag{4.4}\] For \(p=0\) the action vanishes on \(U\) . For \(p=1\) there is a scalar \(c_S(P)\) such that \[\mathcal A_S(P)=c_S(P)\delta_y. \tag{4.5}\] All equalities use the original compact smooth tests and actual refinements. The representative and its ordinary cover are fixed for \(P\) before \(S\) and its tests are chosen.

title: Conjecture 4.4 — Cancellation of the realized critical pairing
text:
Cancellation of the realized critical pairing An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Conjecture 4.4 (Cancellation of the realized critical pairing). For every supplied normal-three model germ, every actual quadratic relation in the finite closed-cell PL/PS class, every allowed degree-one background, and every common protected presentation, the right-hand side of (4.11) is zero.
