title: Question 5.1 — Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity
text:
Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Question 5.1 (Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity). For every strict Laurent box (2.6) , every allowed extending background \(S\) , and every Borel \(E\subset V\) , is \[C_S^*(E;V)\overset{?}{=}\sup\{C_S^*(H;V): H\subset E,\ H\text{ compact}\} \tag{5.3}\] The question includes the local relatively compact case and its passage to an exhaustion of \(V\) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 14.

title: Problem 5.2 — Detection and tester recovery
text:
Detection and tester recovery An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 5.2 (Detection and tester recovery). Find intrinsic conditions on \((V,S)\) and a class of sets under which normalized actual classical testers recover the intended compact masses and relative quasi-everywhere statements determine the desired pointwise representatives. The conditions should distinguish the relative null ideal from ambient pluripolarity and remain valid for the full tester class in (5.1) .
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 15.

title: Question 6.1 — Literal strong continuity
text:
Literal strong continuity An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Question 6.1 (Literal strong continuity). For every fixed allowed \(S\) and strict Laurent box, does (6.3) imply \[I(u_j,u)\longrightarrow0\quad\overset{?}{\Longrightarrow}\quad \int_V|u_j-u|\,\mathrm d\mu\longrightarrow0 \qquad(u_j,u\in\mathscr C) \tag{6.4}\]
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 16.

title: Theorem 6.2 — Projection and the normal-probe criterion
text:
Projection and the normal-probe criterion An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Theorem 6.2 (Projection and the normal-probe criterion). For every \(\ell\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*\) there is a unique \(u=\Pi(\ell)\in\mathscr C\) maximizing \[\ell(v)-\frac{e(v)}{q+1} \quad(v\in\mathscr C).\] Its normal residual \(n=\ell-J(u)\) satisfies \[n(v)\le0\quad(v\in\mathscr C),\qquad n(u)=0. \tag{6.9}\] There is one bounded continuous strictly negative actual classical potential \(\psi_0\) , depending only on the box, for which every literal positive Radon datum \(\mu\) with \(\ell_\mu\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*\) has \[\Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu):=-n(\psi_0)\ge0, \qquad \Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu)=0 \Longleftrightarrow\widehat\mu_{\Pi(\ell_\mu)}=\mu \Longleftrightarrow\mu\in\widehat\mu(\mathscr C). \tag{6.10}\] When the equation is soluble, its member of \(\mathscr C\) is unique. For every original compact smooth scalar test \(\varphi\) there is a finite constant \(C_\varphi\) , independent of \(S\) and \(\mu\) , such that \[\left|\int_V\varphi\, \mathrm d(\widehat\mu_{\Pi(\ell_\mu)}-\mu)\right| \le C_\varphi\Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu). \tag{6.11}\]
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 17.

title: Problem 6.3 — A checkable description of compatible sources
text:
A checkable description of compatible sources An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 6.3 (A checkable description of compatible sources). For a specified geometry \((V,S)\) , characterize substantial classes of literal positive Radon data \(\mu\) for which \(\ell_\mu\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*\) and \(\Xi_{S,\psi_0}(\mu)=0\) . The hypotheses should be verifiable from \(\mu\) , the geometry and explicitly supplied reference objects. Determine the corresponding existence, uniqueness and stability theorems in \(\mathscr C\) , together with precise obstructions outside these classes.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 17.

title: Problem 7.1 — A domain theory with explicit boundary control
text:
A domain theory with explicit boundary control An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 7.1 (A domain theory with explicit boundary control). Find geometric conditions on an ordinary domain \(V\) and an allowed background \(S\) that imply the barrier construction, the global Green formula and uniform boundary tightness needed for the strong completion. Determine when exhaustion by relatively compact subdomains preserves the no-loss class, the source measures and the specified boundary condition.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 19.

title: Problem 7.2 — Classical representatives of completed potentials
text:
Classical representatives of completed potentials An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 7.2 (Classical representatives of completed potentials). Characterize pairs \((V,S)\) and subclasses of \(\mathscr C\) for which every completed Borel class has a canonical ambient classical psh representative. Establish the continuity, comparison and boundary properties of that representative, and identify a relative detection condition that promotes quasi-everywhere equality to the intended pointwise equality.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 19.

title: Problem 7.3 — Relative singularity invariants
text:
Relative singularity invariants An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 7.3 (Relative singularity invariants). For explicit classes of negative actual potentials and allowed backgrounds, determine which non-polar masses, no-loss conditions and energy integrability properties are invariant under bounded changes of singularity. Construct the associated envelopes and comparison theorems, specifying their ordinary domains, boundary conditions and relative null ideals. Describe how these invariants change under proper geometric modifications in mapping classes for which the required current operations are defined.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 19.

title: Problem 7.4 — Finite-energy Green products
text:
Finite-energy Green products An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 7.4 (Finite-energy Green products). Construct classes of Green currents satisfying (7.1) for which mixed products and local intersection pairings are defined by integrable truncation limits. Prove independence of the admissible presentations and truncations, Green symmetry, and agreement with the existing smooth, formal and delta-form products on their common domains. State proper-intersection or replacement hypotheses that control products along the cycles.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 20.

title: Problem 7.5 — Adelic finite-energy intersection
text:
Adelic finite-energy intersection An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program:
analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry  Problem 7.5 (Adelic finite-energy intersection). For a specified class of adelic metrized line bundles on a quasi-projective variety, define local finite-energy intersection terms that extend the established continuous ones. Find explicit summability and boundary conditions under which their sum defines a global intersection pairing, independent of approximation and compatible with the product formula. Prove the resulting variation, projection and positivity statements under stated geometric positivity hypotheses.
excerpt: Exact numbered statement in An intrinsic non-Archimedean Bedford–Taylor program: analytic relations, relative capacities and source geometry. PDF page 20.

title: Fixed-neighborhood regularization of continuous current-positive functions
text: For a finite continuous function, positivity as an original CLD current is equivalent to local uniform approximation by smooth functions with positive curvature on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. After one further shrinking, the approximation can be chosen decreasing and uniform. The ground field is the original finite extension of Q_p with its original absolute value. The space is the analytification of a smooth quasi-projective algebraic space. This statement does not cover arbitrary upper-semicontinuous functions.
excerpt: For a finite continuous function, positivity as an original CLD current is equivalent to local uniform approximation by smooth functions with positive curvature on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. After one further shrinking, the approximation can be chosen decreasing and uniform.

title: Contact rigidity and curve detection
text: On a smooth projective Y with an ample line bundle, a uniformly Fubini–Study lower metric and a finite continuous curve-positive upper metric coincide if the upper metric dominates the lower one and their contact integral against the lower Monge–Ampère measure vanishes. The upper metric only needs the stated curve positivity. The lower Monge–Ampère measure is already defined; the result does not assume an unconstructed measure for the upper metric.
excerpt: On a smooth projective Y with an ample line bundle, a uniformly Fubini–Study lower metric and a finite continuous curve-positive upper metric coincide if the upper metric dominates the lower one and their contact integral against the lower Monge–Ampère measure vanishes.

title: Complete-intersection curve approximation over the original field
text: A single normalized complete-intersection curve realizes the specified approximation of Green pairings and measures while preserving the original valuation and normalization. Retain the projective and ample hypotheses, the fixed collection of tests, and the precise conditions on the approximating curves.
excerpt: A single normalized complete-intersection curve realizes the specified approximation of Green pairings and measures while preserving the original valuation and normalization.

title: Envelopes on regular models and the curve criterion
text: Under the regular-model hypotheses, the envelope is continuous and orthogonal, one-sided Fubini–Study obstacles have the stated O(1/m) approximation, and projective semipositivity is detected on curves. The regular-model hypothesis is part of this result. The separate normal-model extension belongs to B05.
excerpt: Under the regular-model hypotheses, the envelope is continuous and orthogonal, one-sided Fubini–Study obstacles have the stated O(1/m) approximation, and projective semipositivity is detected on curves.

title: Continuous potentials with moving closed positive backgrounds
text: Recursive mixed products of continuous current-positive potentials and symmetric closed positive backgrounds are positive, closed and symmetric in the differentiated slots. Locally uniform convergence of the potentials and weak convergence of the backgrounds give the stated joint continuity for nets and independence of curvature representatives. Continuity of the potentials is essential here. The continuous CLD calculus is a foundational input, separately identified from the project's extension to bounded classical potentials.
excerpt: Recursive mixed products of continuous current-positive potentials and symmetric closed positive backgrounds are positive, closed and symmetric in the differentiated slots. Locally uniform convergence of the potentials and weak convergence of the backgrounds give the stated joint continuity for nets and independence of curvature representatives.

title: Positivity of specified Yuan–Zhang local mixed measures
text: For the specified integrable adelic data, local continuous CLD positivity implies positivity of the corresponding local mixed measures. Retain the line-bundle identification and boundary-completion hypotheses. Positivity of these measures is not by itself arithmetic nefness.
excerpt: For the specified integrable adelic data, local continuous CLD positivity implies positivity of the corresponding local mixed measures.

title: Decreasing PL regularization of bounded classical psh functions
text: Locally bounded classical psh functions admit decreasing semipositive rational PL regularizations over the original field on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. Conversely, the stated bounded decreasing limits remain classical psh. Classical psh is defined using every analytic curve after every complete isometric extension. Spaces are good, Hausdorff, boundaryless and quasi-smooth; the limits retain local boundedness.
excerpt: Locally bounded classical psh functions admit decreasing semipositive rational PL regularizations over the original field on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. Conversely, the stated bounded decreasing limits remain classical psh.

title: All-degree mixed currents and actual Borel weights
text: For the background [1], the bounded calculus gives coefficient Radon mixed currents that are strongly positive, separately closed and symmetric in the differentiated slots. Multiplication uses the given locally bounded Borel function and coefficient measures on the analytic space. All original tests and their common refinements are retained. The measure is not replaced by a measure on a single tropical image.
excerpt: For the background [1], the bounded calculus gives coefficient Radon mixed currents that are strongly positive, separately closed and symmetric in the differentiated slots. Multiplication uses the given locally bounded Borel function and coefficient measures on the analytic space.

title: Joint decreasing continuity for bounded classical potentials
text: Mixed currents are jointly continuous under decreasing bounded classical approximations, including an undifferentiated potential in the same decreasing classical psh approximation, using its given Borel representative. In top degree this is local weak convergence against compactly supported continuous tests. This result starts with background [1]. Its extension to a fixed arbitrary allowed background is recorded separately as M01.
excerpt: Mixed currents are jointly continuous under decreasing bounded classical approximations, including an undifferentiated potential in the same decreasing classical psh approximation, using its given Borel representative. In top degree this is local weak convergence against compactly supported continuous tests.

title: Étale compatibility and the degree formula
text: The bounded products satisfy the stated compatibility for pulled-back potentials, the finite étale degree formula, and descent when the underlying descended function is already bounded classical psh. Keep the precise morphism and normalization hypotheses. This is not a general construction of pullbacks of singular currents.
excerpt: The bounded products satisfy the stated compatibility for pulled-back potentials, the finite étale degree formula, and descent when the underlying descended function is already bounded classical psh.

title: Uniform correction and envelopes on normal models
text: A fixed vertical test-ideal correction in mixed characteristic yields continuity and orthogonality of the relevant ample envelopes on normal models and supplies the regularization input. This is an internal foundational result with a supplied proof under its original hypotheses. Its novelty and independent proof acceptance remain separate questions.
excerpt: A fixed vertical test-ideal correction in mixed characteristic yields continuity and orthogonality of the relevant ample envelopes on normal models and supplies the regularization input.

title: Bounded Bedford–Taylor products with a fixed background
text: For any fixed allowed background S, the recursive mixed currents exist and are positive, separately closed, symmetric and multilinear in the potential slots. They restrict and glue on ordinary opens and satisfy weighted joint decreasing continuity. Potentials are bounded classical psh. S is a fixed symmetric, CLD middle-positive, separately closed current. Every original smooth test and actual finite refinement remains in the test class.
excerpt: For any fixed allowed background S, the recursive mixed currents exist and are positive, separately closed, symmetric and multilinear in the potential slots. They restrict and glue on ordinary opens and satisfy weighted joint decreasing continuity.

title: Local CLN bounds, coefficient measures and Green identities
text: Local CLN estimates on finite test families control coefficient measures, Borel multiplication, truncation and the qualified Green-energy identities. The constants depend on a fixed larger ordinary neighborhood, the tests and S. These estimates do not assert continuity for arbitrary moving backgrounds with discontinuous potentials.
excerpt: Local CLN estimates on finite test families control coefficient measures, Borel multiplication, truncation and the qualified Green-energy identities.

title: The curvature kernel and independence of potentials
text: If bounded classical potentials u and v have equal curvature currents, their difference is represented by an actual continuous pluriharmonic function. Consequently D((u−v)S)=0 for every allowed S, and bounded mixed products depend only on the curvature classes. This settles the potential quotient. General relations between higher-degree actual currents are a separate open descent problem.
excerpt: If bounded classical potentials u and v have equal curvature currents, their difference is represented by an actual continuous pluriharmonic function. Consequently D((u−v)S)=0 for every allowed S, and bounded mixed products depend only on the curvature classes.

title: Curvature order for represented differences
text: For a given difference h=a−b of bounded classical potentials, positivity of Dh is equivalent to h being classical psh. The difference representative is part of the hypothesis. The result does not assert that every positive (1,1)-current has such a potential.
excerpt: For a given difference h=a−b of bounded classical potentials, positivity of Dh is equivalent to h being classical psh.

title: Mixed products on a continuous curvature module
text: The finite current module generated by the specified curvature products with continuous coefficients has representation-independent products, positivity and the stated order control. A variable coefficient need not produce a closed output. This module is smaller than the sought algebra of all higher actual delta-forms.
excerpt: The finite current module generated by the specified curvature products with continuous coefficients has representation-independent products, positivity and the stated order control.

title: Intrinsic differentials on the existing piecewise-smooth current module
text: For finite piecewise-smooth coefficients multiplying currents already in the allowed module, the differentials, reconstruction and independence of witnesses are intrinsic. This does not settle the general quotient by relations between actual delta-forms with variable piecewise-smooth coefficients.
excerpt: For finite piecewise-smooth coefficients multiplying currents already in the allowed module, the differentials, reconstruction and independence of witnesses are intrinsic.

title: Faithful completion with respect to a fixed order gauge
text: Completion with respect to a fixed Q gives faithful actual currents and a unique intrinsic local positive order-continuous extension of the specified action. The order completion is a defined subspace of actual currents. It is not identified with all positive closed currents or with the strong first-energy completion.
excerpt: Completion with respect to a fixed Q gives faithful actual currents and a unique intrinsic local positive order-continuous extension of the specified action.

title: Relative quasicontinuity and capacity completion
text: Bounded classical potentials are locally quasicontinuous for the relative capacity, decreasing sequences converge in capacity, and the Borel completion is independent outside relative capacity-null sets. Strict-maximum locality holds in the stated form. Relative capacity-null sets must be distinguished from ambient pluripolar sets for general S.
excerpt: Bounded classical potentials are locally quasicontinuous for the relative capacity, decreasing sequences converge in capacity, and the Borel completion is independent outside relative capacity-null sets. Strict-maximum locality holds in the stated form.

title: Ambient polarity and Choquet capacity
text: For background [1], the local pluripolar, outer-capacity-null and negligible sets coincide. Under the stated exhaustion hypotheses, the extremal-mass description, Borel regularity and Choquet properties hold. The background [1] and the exhaustion hypotheses are substantive. The full package is not asserted for every relative background.
excerpt: For background [1], the local pluripolar, outer-capacity-null and negligible sets coincide. Under the stated exhaustion hypotheses, the extremal-mass description, Borel regularity and Choquet properties hold.

title: Polar restrictions, comparison and relative domination
text: The prescribed restrictions of backgrounds on whole neighborhoods remain closed and compatible with the bounded products. The compact-gap comparison and relative quasi-everywhere domination results hold. A general S can charge ambient pluripolar sets. Quasi-everywhere conclusions are not silently strengthened to pointwise assertions.
excerpt: The prescribed restrictions of backgrounds on whole neighborhoods remain closed and compatible with the bounded products. The compact-gap comparison and relative quasi-everywhere domination results hold.

title: Closed parameter bands and conditional currents
text: Conormal Borel parameter bands give separately closed restrictions and conditional currents on the original analytic space. One exceptional set works for all original tests and refinements, and the qualified band-capacity completion follows. The parameter-annihilation, conormal and disintegration hypotheses are retained. Raw-capacity and outer-capacity identifications apply only to the specified bands.
excerpt: Conormal Borel parameter bands give separately closed restrictions and conditional currents on the original analytic space. One exceptional set works for all original tests and refinements, and the qualified band-capacity completion follows.

title: Inner regularity on saturated sets of finite Hausdorff measure
text: In the specified moment box with S₀=β^(n−1)[X], the saturated Borel sets of finite (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure have the proved inner-regularity property. The stated one-sided background-order extension also holds. This is a special class of sets and backgrounds. It does not settle inner regularity for all Borel sets and all S.
excerpt: In the specified moment box with S₀=β^(n−1)[X], the saturated Borel sets of finite (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure have the proved inner-regularity property. The stated one-sided background-order extension also holds.

title: Relative non-pluripolar products by truncation
text: Common truncations and Borel restrictions define positive coefficient measures. Under local finiteness of the coefficient masses, their non-pluripolar limit is separately closed. S may charge ambient pluripolar sets. The individual restricted finite-stage currents need not be closed.
excerpt: Common truncations and Borel restrictions define positive coefficient measures. Under local finiteness of the coefficient masses, their non-pluripolar limit is separately closed.

title: A capacity-tail criterion for boundary no-loss
text: In the specified boundary class, no loss of mass is equivalent to the vanishing of t^q C_S({u<−t}) as t tends to infinity. The associated comparison and domination results hold. Keep the compact-sublevel boundary conditions, local mass hypotheses and the source's capacity convention.
excerpt: In the specified boundary class, no loss of mass is equivalent to the vanishing of t^q C_S({u<−t}) as t tends to infinity. The associated comparison and domination results hold.

title: Positive-power energy classes in every exponent
text: For every σ>0, the capacity integral with weight t^(q+σ−1) characterizes the stated power-energy class. Its mixed calculus extends through all legal degrees with the specified no-loss conditions. Boundary and completion hypotheses remain part of the theorem. Membership in an energy class alone does not establish solvability of a source equation.
excerpt: For every σ>0, the capacity integral with weight t^(q+σ−1) characterizes the stated power-energy class. Its mixed calculus extends through all legal degrees with the specified no-loss conditions.

title: Degree budgets for mixed, first-order and energy currents
text: The mixed recursion D(u_i N_α)=N_(α+e_i) and the first-order and energy constructions hold under their strict or critical degree and weight budgets. Limits at the critical budget require the stated integrability and uniform-tail hypotheses. A uniform energy bound alone is insufficient there.
excerpt: The mixed recursion D(u_i N_α)=N_(α+e_i) and the first-order and energy constructions hold under their strict or critical degree and weight budgets.

title: Level currents, coarea and nonsmooth scalar calculus
text: The construction gives actual positive level currents, the Stieltjes and coarea formulas, the stated maximum-level defects, and all-power representatives for the specified complete polar sets. Retain the source integrability, the full original test class and the stated hypotheses of each scalar chain rule.
excerpt: The construction gives actual positive level currents, the Stieltjes and coarea formulas, the stated maximum-level defects, and all-power representatives for the specified complete polar sets.

title: Global Green calculus and mixed-energy constant one
text: On a closed strict Laurent box, the global Green symmetry, mixed-energy Hölder inequality with optimal constant one, and the sharp midpoint estimate hold. S extends to an ordinary neighborhood of the closed box and q=n−p. The constant in this inequality is distinct from the rooftop energy constant.
excerpt: On a closed strict Laurent box, the global Green symmetry, mixed-energy Hölder inequality with optimal constant one, and the sharp midpoint estimate hold.

title: The strong first-energy completion
text: The strong E¹ completion has an actual Borel realization without a common lower barrier. The critical current and energy limits, comparison, domination, truncation and finite-mass approximation hold in the stated space. Retain the boundary and source-class hypotheses. Completion elements are not automatically ambient classical psh functions.
excerpt: The strong E¹ completion has an actual Borel realization without a common lower barrier. The critical current and energy limits, comparison, domination, truncation and finite-mass approximation hold in the stated space.

title: Capacity characterization of the strong topology
text: Strong energy discrepancy tends to zero exactly when local truncated outer-capacity convergence and convergence of the energies hold. The corresponding monotone closure and critical continuity follow. S and the completion are fixed. Energy boundedness on its own is not this convergence criterion.
excerpt: Strong energy discrepancy tends to zero exactly when local truncated outer-capacity convergence and convergence of the energies hold. The corresponding monotone closure and critical continuity follow.

title: Rooftops, Perron envelopes and obstacle problems
text: Relative envelopes, finite rooftops, Borel obstacle constraints and preservation of a common lower source are constructed. The constrained variational problem has its stated unique maximizer. The maximizer and its Euler inequality do not by themselves imply a nonlinear source equation; the residual must also vanish.
excerpt: Relative envelopes, finite rooftops, Borel obstacle constraints and preservation of a common lower source are constructed. The constrained variational problem has its stated unique maximizer.

title: The energy-difference Banach space and the closed source image
text: The actual Borel energy-difference space and order-energy lattice have the stated Banach structure. The nonlinear source image is norm closed, and its source metric is complete. No weak-star closedness or convexity is inferred. Positive continuous dual functionals need not be literal measure integrals.
excerpt: The actual Borel energy-difference space and order-energy lattice have the stated Banach structure. The nonlinear source image is norm closed, and its source metric is complete.

title: Variational projection and its normal residual
text: Strong continuous dual data have a unique variational projection and normal-residual decomposition, with quantitative retraction, source-image gap and stability estimates. This takes place in the stated cone completion. Solving the source equation additionally requires the normal residual to vanish.
excerpt: Strong continuous dual data have a unique variational projection and normal-residual decomposition, with quantitative retraction, source-image gap and stability estimates.

title: A single geometric probe for source compatibility
text: For a literal positive Radon datum that is strongly continuous, the nonnegative probe Ξ=−nψ₀ vanishes exactly when the full original source equation holds. It controls the residual on every compact test. The criterion does not require an assumed subsolution. Conditions checkable directly from the datum that force Ξ=0 remain an open problem.
excerpt: For a literal positive Radon datum that is strongly continuous, the nonnegative probe Ξ=−nψ₀ vanishes exactly when the full original source equation holds. It controls the residual on every compact test.

title: Literal data under fixed domination or capacity control
text: Fixed-source domination, the qualified capacity-Dini domination and the fixed-mass capacity-control hypotheses imply literal integral continuity, the stated dual compactness and joint limits. Some qualified data can have infinite boundary mass. The conclusion is not claimed for every literal energy-difference-bounded datum.
excerpt: Fixed-source domination, the qualified capacity-Dini domination and the fixed-mass capacity-control hypotheses imply literal integral continuity, the stated dual compactness and joint limits.

title: Signed diffuse Dirichlet data in remaining degree one
text: In remaining degree q=1, every finite signed energy-diffuse Radon datum has the stated unique canonical renormalized zero-boundary solution in the faithful part-energy space, with the original equation, clipping and radiation properties. The ambient dimension can be arbitrary. The faithful regular strongly local coercive part form and energy-capacity diffuseness are required. The solution is not automatically in the classical psh cone or nonlinear strong E¹ cone.
excerpt: In remaining degree q=1, every finite signed energy-diffuse Radon datum has the stated unique canonical renormalized zero-boundary solution in the faithful part-energy space, with the original equation, clipping and radiation properties.

title: Stability of signed data and obstacle contact
text: Total-variation convergence gives strong convergence of fixed clippings, their energy measures and the qualified smooth scalar-curvature expressions. The finite-curvature obstacle problem has the stated contact reaction. Moving hard-level atoms require additional conditions; their unconditional convergence is not asserted.
excerpt: Total-variation convergence gives strong convergence of fixed clippings, their energy measures and the qualified smooth scalar-curvature expressions. The finite-curvature obstacle problem has the stated contact reaction.

title: Parameter energy models and radial source inversion
text: In the specified parameter models, the L^(k+1) energy and capacity formulas give the compatible L^((k+1)/k) source inverse. In the radial model, the flux-tail condition characterizes the stated inversion and stability. These are results for the prescribed parameter and radial families. The existence and uniqueness scopes are retained separately from the general source problem.
excerpt: In the specified parameter models, the L^(k+1) energy and capacity formulas give the compatible L^((k+1)/k) source inverse. In the radial model, the flux-tail condition characterizes the stated inversion and stability.

title: Small nonradial interfaces and nonlinear source graphs
text: In prescribed smooth toric backgrounds, the small Hölder graph and sphere-interface constructions give normal-trace lifting, a clamped inverse, all harmonic-moment conditions and a convergent nonlinear source graph. Keep the separate hypotheses on sphere densities, exterior traces and moving interfaces. These are specified-model results, not an arbitrary-background inverse theorem.
excerpt: In prescribed smooth toric backgrounds, the small Hölder graph and sphere-interface constructions give normal-trace lifting, a clamped inverse, all harmonic-moment conditions and a convergent nonlinear source graph.

title: Degree-one action and constant-coefficient cycle relations
text: The actual degree-one action is defined, and the specified relations between ambient cycles with constant real coefficients descend in every degree. General higher-degree coupled relations between actual curvature forms remain separate.
excerpt: The actual degree-one action is defined, and the specified relations between ambient cycles with constant real coefficients descend in every degree.

title: Higher action on the local weak closure of geometric backgrounds
text: Higher action descends on W_loc, the stated ordinary-local weak closure of positive closed actual delta-backgrounds, using the full actual test class and the required Bedford–Taylor tail estimates. Whether W_loc exhausts all allowed backgrounds remains open.
excerpt: Higher action descends on W_loc, the stated ordinary-local weak closure of positive closed actual delta-backgrounds, using the full actual test class and the required Bedford–Taylor tail estimates.

title: Full-polar normal currents and divergence
text: The NC3 divergence statement holds for all analytic weights. The smooth-presentation quotient, intrinsic normal current and its boundary are constructed. Vanishing of the general harmonic drift and the required singular pairings remains open.
excerpt: The NC3 divergence statement holds for all analytic weights. The smooth-presentation quotient, intrinsic normal current and its boundary are constructed.

title: Continuous harmonic potentials and scalar boundary action
text: The source identifies the specified continuous harmonic, classical pluriharmonic and local unit-logarithm cases. When a continuous potential v is given, the action has the form M_S α=D(vS). The existence of that continuous potential is a hypothesis. This does not construct one for an arbitrary full-polar relation.
excerpt: The source identifies the specified continuous harmonic, classical pluriharmonic and local unit-logarithm cases. When a continuous potential v is given, the action has the form M_S α=D(vS).

title: Full-carrier CLN certificates
text: The stated HC, CZ and tail conditions control the full absolute carrier. A zero carrier seminorm forces the action to vanish for every allowed S. The existence of such a certificate for every actual zero relation remains open.
excerpt: The stated HC, CZ and tail conditions control the full absolute carrier. A zero carrier seminorm forces the action to vanish for every allowed S.

title: Controlled full-exact approximation as a sufficient criterion
text: An approximation by full-exact representatives with one fixed Q gives zero action for every allowed background. The construction retains the singular component A₀. Q is fixed before S, the tests and their refinements. The approximation hypothesis is not established for every actual zero relation.
excerpt: An approximation by full-exact representatives with one fixed Q gives zero action for every allowed background. The construction retains the singular component A₀.

title: Ordinary quadratic descent in joint residue rank at most two
text: For finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS tuples of joint residue rank at most two, the quadratic actual zero relations admit the stated ordinary strain primitives and fixed-Q approximations, hence have zero action for every S. The ambient dimension is arbitrary. Rank refers to the original joint tuple, and comparisons use the union tuple.
excerpt: For finite continuous closed-cell PL/PS tuples of joint residue rank at most two, the quadratic actual zero relations admit the stated ordinary strain primitives and fixed-Q approximations, hence have zero action for every S.

title: A canonical quadratic quotient in low residue dimension
text: The quadratic action descends canonically on germs with residue dimension s_K≤2, giving the stated sheaf map on surfaces. The assertion is quadratic. It does not establish descent in all higher degrees.
excerpt: The quadratic action descends canonically on germs with residue dimension s_K≤2, giving the stated sheaf map on surfaces.

title: Actual curve stars, unit completion and joint Stokes
text: The marked-curve construction, full analytic weights, finite Picard unit completion, final faithful separator and paired Hessian Stokes identity hold in the stated normal-three setting. Radii must satisfy the stated commensurability conditions. New marks have zero old projection, and completion is performed before faithful separation.
excerpt: The marked-curve construction, full analytic weights, finite Picard unit completion, final faithful separator and paired Hessian Stokes identity hold in the stated normal-three setting.

title: Ordinary localization around the whole central fiber
text: After freezing the required units, finite rational controls and properness cover the whole central fiber. The ordinary product localization gives the stated fixed-Q approximation. This covers the entire central fiber, not just the Gauss section. Product valuations retain their joint structure.
excerpt: After freezing the required units, finite rational controls and properness cover the whole central fiber. The ordinary product localization gives the stated fixed-Q approximation.

title: Vanishing off the center and the top-degree point residual
text: In the specified normal-three model, for a fixed quadratic actual zero relation, the action vanishes on the punctured neighborhood for every allowed S. A closed coefficient current supported at one point vanishes below top degree; in top degree the residual is c_S(P)δ_y. Vanishing of c_S(P) for a general degree-one background remains open.
excerpt: In the specified normal-three model, for a fixed quadratic actual zero relation, the action vanishes on the punctured neighborhood for every allowed S. A closed coefficient current supported at one point vanishes below top degree; in top degree the residual is c_S(P)δ_y.

title: Critical trace mass and protected transposition
text: In the supplied normal-three model, transposing all original tests gives the specified positive closed supercurrent of bidimension two. Its normalized trace mass μ(B_r)/r² is monotone, its growth is O(r²), and its critical density is finite. The real monotonicity statement is a known input. The project's interface retains the original background S and its protected tests.
excerpt: In the supplied normal-three model, transposing all original tests gives the specified positive closed supercurrent of bidimension two. Its normalized trace mass μ(B_r)/r² is monotone, its growth is O(r²), and its critical density is finite.

title: Leading jets and the piecewise-smooth tangent pairing
text: In the supplied normal-three model, the higher-jet O(δ), wall-normal O(ε) and mixed O(√ε) estimates justify the tangent pairing and the formula c=−⟨T₀,Z₀Dρ⟩. Tangent uniqueness is not required. The remaining cancellation for actual joint data has not been proved.
excerpt: In the supplied normal-three model, the higher-jet O(δ), wall-normal O(ε) and mixed O(√ε) estimates justify the tangent pairing and the formula c=−⟨T₀,Z₀Dρ⟩.

title: Spherical classification of critical tangent currents
text: The critical current has the stated spherical description by a positive-semidefinite tangential divergence-free tensor M, with σ=tr M and the complete mass-minus-gradient formula for the central residual. The real-current classification is established internally. The class of pairs realized by actual joint analytic data is not yet characterized.
excerpt: The critical current has the stated spherical description by a positive-semidefinite tangential divergence-free tensor M, with σ=tr M and the complete mass-minus-gradient formula for the central residual.

title: Failure of universal equality between raw and outer capacity
text: The crossed-box constructions disprove universal equality of relative raw and outer capacity, including the stated compact/Borel and full-tester versions. They also obstruct the corresponding decreasing-compact continuity of raw capacity. They do not refute the ambient [1] result, qualified parameter-band statements or the still-open Borel inner regularity of the outer capacity.
excerpt: The crossed-box constructions disprove universal equality of relative raw and outer capacity, including the stated compact/Borel and full-tester versions. They also obstruct the corresponding decreasing-compact continuity of raw capacity.

title: Failure of relative strong subadditivity
text: An actual torus model with q=1, n≥2 and S₀=β^(n−1) disproves the proposed strong subadditivity of relative outer capacity. This does not disprove ordinary subadditivity or Borel inner regularity.
excerpt: An actual torus model with q=1, n≥2 and S₀=β^(n−1) disproves the proposed strong subadditivity of relative outer capacity.

title: Failure of the relative extremal total-mass formula
text: The specified model disproves the proposed equality between relative capacity and the total mass of its extremal function, with discrepancy of order r^(1−n). The obstruction concerns that total-mass formula under its stated model assumptions; it does not replace the qualified capacity statements already proved.
excerpt: The specified model disproves the proposed equality between relative capacity and the total mass of its extremal function, with discrepancy of order r^(1−n).

title: The sharp obstruction to rooftop energy constant one
text: Constant one fails for the rooftop energy inequality. Across the specified backgrounds, constant two is sharp, already in an actual two-dimensional q=1 model with a smooth strongly positive background. This does not refute literal strong continuity for one fixed S or the constant-one Green–Hölder inequality.
excerpt: Constant one fails for the rooftop energy inequality. Across the specified backgrounds, constant two is sharp, already in an actual two-dimensional q=1 model with a smooth strongly positive background.

title: Critical continuity requires tail control
text: Energy boundedness together with capacity convergence is insufficient for the proposed critical continuity. Unqualified non-pluripolar recursion can also lose a polar Dirac mass. The correct formulations retain no-loss, integrability, uniform-tail or strong-topology hypotheses as appropriate.
excerpt: Energy boundedness together with capacity convergence is insufficient for the proposed critical continuity. Unqualified non-pluripolar recursion can also lose a polar Dirac mass.

title: The nonlinear source image need not be open
text: Small positive smooth perturbations of a source density can leave the full strong-completion source image even near a strict reference potential. This obstruction is distinct from solvability for diffuse data in the q=1 renormalized part-energy space.
excerpt: Small positive smooth perturbations of a source density can leave the full strong-completion source image even near a strict reference potential.

title: Failure of continuous smooth-form double primitives
text: An actual full-polar relation need not have the proposed continuous smooth-form double primitive, even after changing the Hessian representative. Singular primitives are not excluded by this example. It is not a counterexample to KC12.
excerpt: An actual full-polar relation need not have the proposed continuous smooth-form double primitive, even after changing the Hessian representative.

title: Real Killing-gluing and fixed-Q obstructions
text: Local strain and D-closedness do not force global Killing gluing. A real finite-fan model gives a positive L¹ gap for the specified fixed-Q approximation problem. The real obstruction has not been realized as an actual analytic zero relation and therefore is not a counterexample to the general actual-descent conjecture.
excerpt: Local strain and D-closedness do not force global Killing gluing. A real finite-fan model gives a positive L¹ gap for the specified fixed-Q approximation problem.

title: Hessian-wall drift in PL graph pullback
text: The Jacobian-only strain chain rule fails for piecewise-linear graphs: the Hessian contribution on the wall must be retained. The correction includes rank-loss loci. One cannot erase these terms when passing to an actual graph or common refinement.
excerpt: The Jacobian-only strain chain rule fails for piecewise-linear graphs: the Hessian contribution on the wall must be retained.

title: Limits of finite unit lifting and Hensel boundary extension
text: Finite unit lifts do not give a residue-field section preserving every algebraic relation. Norm recognition on a chosen Hensel root domain does not give continuous extension over the whole central fiber; the V²−V−A example separates these claims. The individually constructed unit lifts remain valid. The obstruction concerns their unsupported global strengthening.
excerpt: Finite unit lifts do not give a residue-field section preserving every algebraic relation. Norm recognition on a chosen Hensel root domain does not give continuous extension over the whole central fiber; the V²−V−A example separates these claims.

title: Critical r² mass growth does not remove a point residual
text: Positivity, closedness, bounded piecewise-smooth data and point support do not suffice to eliminate a critical central mass. Gauss atoms also obstruct the proposed lower-rank mass-null argument. The real critical example is not an actual-zero counterexample. Stronger cancellation for actual joint data remains open.
excerpt: Positivity, closedness, bounded piecewise-smooth data and point support do not suffice to eliminate a critical central mass. Gauss atoms also obstruct the proposed lower-rank mass-null argument.

title: Countable-measure and nonliteral-dual obstructions
text: A countable family of Radon measures need not detect the full capacity-null ideal. The recorded examples also show nonreflexivity, positive continuous duals with a nonliteral Dirac shadow, and failure of literality under unqualified norm limits. The qualified compactness and literal-closure results under fixed domination are preserved.
excerpt: A countable family of Radon measures need not detect the full capacity-null ideal. The recorded examples also show nonreflexivity, positive continuous duals with a nonliteral Dirac shadow, and failure of literality under unqualified norm limits.

title: General actual-relation descent in every degree
text: Establish descent of every actual analytic curvature relation against every allowed background, with ordinary locality and compatibility under actual refinements. The general quadratic case is already open. Higher-degree descent and the differential algebra require additional work.
excerpt: Establish descent of every actual analytic curvature relation against every allowed background, with ordinary locality and compatibility under actual refinements.

title: KC12 and controlled primitives in general
text: Establish the proposed controlled full-exact approximation using the actual joint covector data and a fixed Q, or prove vanishing of the action by another route. KC12 is a sufficient route under its precise hypotheses, not a completed general theorem or a logically necessary route to every descent result.
excerpt: Establish the proposed controlled full-exact approximation using the actual joint covector data and a fixed Q, or prove vanishing of the action by another route.

title: Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity
text: Determine whether relative outer capacity is inner regular on Borel sets and establish the required exact recovery by tests. The failures of raw–outer equality and strong subadditivity do not settle this question. The special saturated finite-Hausdorff-measure case is retained.
excerpt: Determine whether relative outer capacity is inner regular on Borel sets and establish the required exact recovery by tests.

title: Literal energy-difference boundedness and strong L¹ continuity
text: For one fixed S, determine whether a literal energy-difference-bounded datum is continuous in L¹ along strong E¹ convergence, including general nonzero limits and the allowed infinite-mass setting. Fixed domination and the qualified capacity-control subclasses are known. Counterexamples that change S do not settle this question.
excerpt: For one fixed S, determine whether a literal energy-difference-bounded datum is continuous in L¹ along strong E¹ convergence, including general nonzero limits and the allowed infinite-mass setting.

title: Source conditions that can be checked before solving
text: Find stable geometric conditions on a datum that force the normal probe Ξ to vanish, without assuming an unknown solution or membership in the source image. The conditions should persist under the intended approximation and iteration. Neither arbitrary positive data nor all small smooth perturbations can be admitted.
excerpt: Find stable geometric conditions on a datum that force the normal probe Ξ to vanish, without assuming an unknown solution or membership in the source image.

title: Interfaces for variable coefficients, order and full delta tests
text: Complete the variable piecewise-smooth quotient, curvature-order transfer, full GK delta-test interface, and the required ordinary gluing and naturality. Equality on smooth currents does not automatically extend to the enlarged test class. Each interface needs a separate statement and proof.
excerpt: Complete the variable piecewise-smooth quotient, curvature-order transfer, full GK delta-test interface, and the required ordinary gluing and naturality.

title: Cancellation at the actual joint normal-three center
text: Prove cancellation of the central residual for the actual joint pair (Z₀,M), or identify the precise scope in which such cancellation is valid. The currently available strip estimate ε^(−1)M_nn=O(1) does not give the o(1) needed for the missing step.
excerpt: Prove cancellation of the central residual for the actual joint pair (Z₀,M), or identify the precise scope in which such cancellation is valid.

title: Domains, boundaries and classical representatives
text: Extend the theory to the intended larger classes of domains and boundary data, identify classical representatives where justified, and establish the qualified pullback, pushforward and gluing statements. Keep the different completions and pointwise boundary assertions distinct. These extensions are not consequences of notation alone.
excerpt: Extend the theory to the intended larger classes of domains and boundary data, identify classical representatives where justified, and establish the qualified pullback, pushforward and gluing statements.

title: Descent of actual analytic relations
text: For every finite K/Q_p with its original norm, every good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth ordinary germ of pure dimension n, every 1<=b<=n and every finite signed admissible continuous closed-cell PL/PS presentation P with actual delta curvature kappa_b(P)=0, there is an ordinary representative chosen for P on which A_S(P)=0 for every symmetric middle-positive separately d-prime and d-double-prime closed background S of degree p<=n-b, on all original compact smooth complementary CLD tests and all actual refinements including rank loss. Admissible scalars have their existing full delta curvature and are finite differences of continuous classical psh functions. Degree one; potential independence and the continuous-coefficient curvature module. Quadratic finite presentations with s_f(x)<=2, in arbitrary ambient dimension. Quadratic normal-three supplied models on the ordinary puncture; central vanishing in specified sufficient cases. The established local weakly approximable background class, within its testing scope. Prove joint wall-flux cancellation for the realized critical pair; then general-germ return and higher coupled relations.
excerpt: For every finite K/Q_p with its original norm, every good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth ordinary germ of pure dimension n, every 1<=b<=n and every finite signed admissible continuous closed-cell PL/PS presentation P with actual delta curvature kappa_b(P)=0, there is an ordinary representative chosen for P on which A_S(P)=0 for every symmetric middle-positive separately d-prime and d-double-prime closed background S of degree p<=n-b, on all original compact smooth complementary CLD tests and all actual refinements including rank loss. Admissible scalars have their existing full delta curvature and are finite differences of continuous classical psh functions.

title: Cancellation of the realized critical pairing
text: For every supplied original smooth normal-three model germ, finite admissible continuous closed-cell PL/PS quadratic actual zero P, allowed degree-one S and common protected moment presentation, the spherical expression sum c_alpha(integral h_alpha^1 k_alpha^1 d sigma - integral d_S h_alpha^1 tensor d_S k_alpha^1 : d M) is zero. The pair (Z_0,M) must arise jointly from the original relation and background. Vanishing critical density nu. An actual full-exact leading-energy identity on a neighborhood of the whole protected central fiber. Each scalar first jet is one ambient linear function. Previously established bounded-potential and W_loc background cases. Use actual-zero geometry to cancel the critical wall flux while retaining charged coefficient walls and mixed entries.
excerpt: For every supplied original smooth normal-three model germ, finite admissible continuous closed-cell PL/PS quadratic actual zero P, allowed degree-one S and common protected moment presentation, the spherical expression sum c_alpha(integral h_alpha^1 k_alpha^1 d sigma - integral d_S h_alpha^1 tensor d_S k_alpha^1 : d M) is zero. The pair (Z_0,M) must arise jointly from the original relation and background.

title: Carrier-CLN vanishing
text: For every actual signed PL-zero germ of mixed degree b>=2, does the unchanged carrier-CLN seminorm q^{U,b}_{F,L}(P) vanish at every required compact stage for the original absolute cap carrier F and the specified harmonic/ordinary-zero-product/ambient-cycle generator space? Degree one. The forward implication q=0 => all allowed background actions vanish. The existing harmonic recognition and cap zero-product certificates. Construct the unchanged seminorm certificates or determine an actual full-polar obstruction.
excerpt: For every actual signed PL-zero germ of mixed degree b>=2, does the unchanged carrier-CLN seminorm q^{U,b}_{F,L}(P) vanish at every required compact stage for the original absolute cap carrier F and the specified harmonic/ordinary-zero-product/ambient-cycle generator space?

title: Local approximation of backgrounds
text: Does every allowed background of degree (p,p) lie in the ordinary-local weak closure W_loc^p of positive separately closed actual delta-form backgrounds on fixed ordinary representatives? Which intrinsic hypotheses characterize that closure? Full actual delta testing in W_loc. Stability of W_loc under bounded BT tails. Construct positive closed actual approximants with the required original test convergence, or exhibit a background outside this closure.
excerpt: Does every allowed background of degree (p,p) lie in the ordinary-local weak closure W_loc^p of positive separately closed actual delta-form backgrounds on fixed ordinary representatives? Which intrinsic hypotheses characterize that closure?

title: Higher and variable-coefficient differential interfaces
text: Construct the specified graded differential actions for higher coupled analytic relations, variable finite PS coefficients, differential-operator compatibility and the intended delta-form test classes, with exact object sheaves and mapping classes. Bounded current calculus Continuous-coefficient module and its order completion Degree-one delta action Quadratic finite closed-cell PS interface in low residue rank Prove each quotient, differential and testing interface separately with its actual boundaries and permitted maps.
excerpt: Construct the specified graded differential actions for higher coupled analytic relations, variable finite PS coefficients, differential-operator compatibility and the intended delta-form test classes, with exact object sheaves and mapping classes.

title: Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity
text: For every strict Laurent box V compactly inside an original affinoid interior and every allowed S extending past its closure, is C_S^*(E;V)=sup_{H compact subset E} C_S^*(H;V) for every Borel E subset V? Capacity uses all original classical psh testers 0<=u<=1 on the whole V. Qualified ambient [1] theory. For q=1, S_0=beta^{n-1}[X] on the analytic torus box, saturated Borel inverse images of finite H^{n-1} sets compactly inside the moment box. The latter class persists under the stated one-sided positive background order control. Obtain uniform Borel remainder estimates for the actual tester family; handle exhaustion to non-relatively-compact Borel sets.

title: Tester recovery and relative detection
text: Find intrinsic conditions on (V,S) and set classes ensuring actual normalized-tester recovery of intended compact masses and promotion of relative q.e. conclusions to specified pointwise representatives. Ambient and qualified relative comparison results Finite-Hausdorff saturated range Identify geometric support or approximation hypotheses that imply uniform tester recovery and detection.
excerpt: Find intrinsic conditions on (V,S) and set classes ensuring actual normalized-tester recovery of intended compact masses and promotion of relative q.e. conclusions to specified pointwise representatives.

title: Literal energy-dual strong continuity
text: For a fixed allowed S on a strict Laurent box, suppose a positive Radon measure annihilates the relative null ideal, all completed Borel differences are literally integrable, and its integral functional is bounded on the entire energy-difference Banach space. Does I(u_j,u)->0 imply integral |u_j-u| d mu ->0 for every strong row? No finite-total-mass hypothesis is added. Source-dominated data Specified capacity-dominated classes Existing sufficient ordered-rooftop and finite-minorant reductions Prove fixed-S ordered-rooftop continuity or the weaker finite-minorant sublinear budget, or construct a positive literal datum satisfying all hypotheses that fails continuity.

title: Checkable compatible source classes
text: For specified (V,S), describe substantial literal positive Radon data classes by conditions on the data, geometry and supplied reference objects, and derive strong continuity plus Xi=0, existence, uniqueness and stability in the prescribed strong completion. Norm-closed source image Unique variational projection for strong-continuous functionals Exact Xi normal-probe criterion Qualified source-compatible data classes Specified finite-mode inverse results Identify the range of the linearization at a known reference and prove both inverse estimates and nonlinear stability of its boundary/moment constraints.
excerpt: For specified (V,S), describe substantial literal positive Radon data classes by conditions on the data, geometry and supplied reference objects, and derive strong continuity plus Xi=0, existence, uniqueness and stability in the prescribed strong completion.

title: Domain and boundary extension
text: Find geometric domain/background conditions yielding barriers, global Green formula, uniform boundary tightness and an exhaustion theorem preserving no loss, source currents and the specified boundary completion. Strict Laurent boxes with extending backgrounds Specified affinoid part-form linear domains Replace each use of the Laurent-box hypotheses by explicit geometric estimates.

title: Classical representatives of completed classes
text: Characterize pairs (V,S) and subclasses of the strong completion admitting canonical ambient classical psh representatives, with precise continuity, comparison, boundary and q.e.-to-pointwise detection statements. Actual bounded classical core Relative Borel realization and quasicontinuity Bounded potential quotient Connect the curvature quotient and relative capacity through a proved representative theorem.
excerpt: Characterize pairs (V,S) and subclasses of the strong completion admitting canonical ambient classical psh representatives, with precise continuity, comparison, boundary and q.e.-to-pointwise detection statements.

title: Relative singularity invariants
text: For explicit actual potential/background classes, determine invariance of non-polar masses, no-loss conditions and energies under bounded changes of singularity; construct envelopes/comparison and specify behavior under permitted proper modifications. No-loss and positive-power energy capacity-tail characterizations Non-polar products with local coefficient finiteness Start with controlled model singularities and prove truncation-mass stability under a specified modification.

title: Finite-energy Green products
text: Define Green classes D g_Z + delta_Z = omega_Z with integrable truncation products and local intersection pairings; prove approximation independence, symmetry and agreement with existing smooth/formal/delta theories under explicit intersection hypotheses. Global first-energy Green symmetry Existing GK and Mihatsch Green constructions Continuous Chern products in R scope Construct a first energy class of Green expressions and prove the cycle pairing and comparison theorem.
excerpt: Define Green classes D g_Z + delta_Z = omega_Z with integrable truncation products and local intersection pairings; prove approximation independence, symmetry and agreement with existing smooth/formal/delta theories under explicit intersection hypotheses.

title: Adelic finite-energy intersection
text: For specified adelic metrized line bundles on a quasi-projective variety, extend local finite-energy intersection terms and impose explicit placewise summability and boundary conditions yielding a global approximation-independent pairing with variation, projection and justified positivity. Continuous Chern products and specified local Yuan–Zhang measure positivity Separate geometric adelic-nefness input under its own hypotheses Prove one local metric-change formula and a summable global domination compatible with the product formula.
excerpt: For specified adelic metrized line bundles on a quasi-projective variety, extend local finite-energy intersection terms and impose explicit placewise summability and boundary conditions yielding a global approximation-independent pairing with variation, projection and justified positivity.

title: Background currents and classical potentials
text: On an ordinary open U of pure dimension n, an allowed background is a symmetric CLD current S of bidegree (p,p) with d'S=d''S=0, positive on the signed column-square tests \eta\wedge J\eta of complementary degree. Equivalently, its coefficient matrices in these presentations are positive semidefinite. Write q=n-p. The class \mathcal C_b(U) consists of real-valued, locally bounded, upper-semicontinuous functions whose pullback to every analytic curve is subharmonic, after every complete isometric extension of K. These are the classical psh potentials used here. With D=d'd'', the bounded product is the recursively constructed current \[T_{S,0}=S,\qquad T_{S,b}(u_1,\ldots,u_b)=D\bigl(u_1T_{S,b-1}(u_2,\ldots,u_b)\bigr),\quad b\le q.\] Finite differences of these potentials are handled by signed multilinear extension.
excerpt: On an ordinary open U of pure dimension n, an allowed background is a symmetric CLD current S of bidegree (p,p) with d'S=d''S=0, positive on the signed column-square tests \eta\wedge J\eta of complementary degree. Equivalently, its coefficient matrices in these presentations are positive semidefinite. Write q=n-p.

title: Admissible scalar presentations
text: Choose analytic units f_1,\ldots,f_N on one ordinary open U, and put t_f=(-\log|f_1|,\ldots,-\log|f_N|). A finite family of continuous real functions is admissible when all its members are expressed on the complete image t_f(U) using one finite coefficient complex, are piecewise linear or piecewise smooth with a smooth extension near each closed cell, belong to the actual degree-zero delta-form sheaf with full curvature D_\delta h\in\mathscr B^{1,1}(U), and are finite differences of continuous classical psh functions on that same U. Here \mathscr B=B_{\mathrm{Mih}} is the analytic delta-form sheaf, and “full” derivatives include polyhedral boundary terms. A refinement adjoins actual analytic units and retains the whole refined image, including faces where the induced tangent map loses rank.

title: The residue rank of a presentation
text: For the finite unit tuple f at x, let \mathscr F_f(x)=\widetilde K^{\mathrm{gr}}(\widetilde f_1(x),\ldots,\widetilde f_N(x)) be its graded residue field and put \[\begin{aligned}d_f(x)&=\operatorname{trdeg}^{\mathrm{gr}}_{\widetilde K^{\mathrm{gr}}}\mathscr F_f(x),\\r_f(x)&=\dim_{\mathbf Q}\operatorname{Span}_{\mathbf Q}{-\log|f_i(x)|+\mathbf Q\log|K^\times|}_i,\\s_f(x)&=d_f(x)-r_f(x).\end{aligned}\] Thus s_f(x) is the transcendence degree of the tuple's field of normalized residues. title: The absolute cap carrier
text: For a prescribed ordinary localization O, analytic units f_1,\ldots,f_c, and real levels a_i, write x_+=\max{x,0}. The absolute cap carrier is the closed support \[F=\operatorname{supp}T_{[O],c}((\log|f_1|-a_1)_+,\ldots,(\log|f_c|-a_c)_+).\] Here [O] is the integration current on O. The support is selected by this positive product; it is fixed independently of cancellation in a signed relation.

title: The permitted carrier relations
text: Let \mathcal D(U) be the real vector space of finite differences of continuous, locally bounded classical psh functions, and let \mathcal P^b(U)=\operatorname{Sym}^b_{\mathbf R}\mathcal D(U). A factor h is F-harmonic if near every point of F, its restriction to F agrees with a continuous function of zero current curvature. The subspace \mathcal Z_F^b(U) is the linear span of exactly three kinds of expressions: monomials with an F-harmonic factor; monomials whose ordinary pointwise product vanishes on all of F; and finite identities already zero in one common ambient real PL cycle algebra, pulled back by the original moment map. An equality arising only after analytic pullback is not added to this generator space.

title: Locally weakly approximable backgrounds
text: The class \mathcal W^p_{\mathrm{loc}} is the ordinary-local weak closure of positive, separately d'- and d''-closed actual delta-form backgrounds of bidegree (p,p). A background belongs to it when, near every point on a fixed ordinary representative, it lies in that closure. Weak convergence means convergence of the pairing with every original compact smooth complementary CLD test on that representative.

title: A supplied normal-three model germ
text: This is a smooth integral model germ (Y,y) over K^\circ, of relative dimension three, with \lvert\mathcal H(y)^\times\rvert=\lvert K^\times\rvert and residue field F=\widetilde{\mathcal H(y)} of transcendence degree three over \widetilde K, together with the following geometric data over the original field. The finite residue tuple has a smooth projective simple-normal-crossings model of F; its labelled monomial cones, their lattice-normalized slopes and residue-degree weights, and all lower strata are realized by actual Gauss families on the ordinary germ. This realization covers the complete source of the fixed tuple, and the families converge ordinarily to y, uniformly in their angular parameters. These lifting and realization data are part of “supplied”, in addition to the two field conditions.

title: A protected moment presentation
text: A protected presentation is a finite actual moment map t:U→\Omega\subset\mathbf R^N containing the chosen scalar tuple, with t(y)=0, such that the entire inverse image t^{-1}(L) is compact in U for every compact L\Subset\Omega. For a degree-one background on the three-dimensional model, its transpose is the real supercurrent of bidimension (2,2) defined by \[\langle T_S,\eta\rangle=\langle S,t^*\eta\rangle,\qquad\eta\in\mathcal A_c^{2,2}(\Omega).\]

For a degree-one background on the three-dimensional model, its transpose is the real supercurrent of bidimension (2,2) defined by \[\langle T_S,\eta\rangle=\langle S,t^*\eta\rangle,\qquad\eta\in\mathcal A_c^{2,2}(\Omega).\]

title: Critical tangent currents
text: Set \beta=\sum_i d'z_i\wedge d''z_i, μ_S=\tfrac12T_S\wedge\beta^2, and \nu=\lim_{r\downarrow0}μ_S(B_r)/r^2. A critical tangent of this background and protected presentation is a local weak subsequential limit \[T_0=\lim_{j→\infty}\delta_j^2(a_{\delta_j})_*T_S,\qquad a_\delta(z)=z/\delta,\qquad\delta_j\downarrow0.\] The established growth theorem gives such conic, positive, separately closed limits with μ_{T_0}(B_R)=\nu R^2.

title: Coupled relations and the differential extension problem
Strict Laurent box
text: Let B\subset X be a compact affinoid, let f_a,g_b be analytic on B, and choose positive real numbers R_a,r_b. The domain used for the energy theory is \[K_0={|f_a|\le R_a,\ |g_b|\ge r_b}\Subset\operatorname{Int}_X(B),\qquad V={|f_a|<R_a,\ |g_b|>r_b}\ne\varnothing.\] The background S must be defined on an ordinary neighborhood of K_0. Its remaining degree is q=n-p\ge1, where S has bidegree (p,p).

title: Relative capacity and normalized testers
text: A normalized tester on V is an actual locally bounded classical psh function h\in\mathcal C_b(V) with 0\le h\le1, defined on the whole of V. For a Borel set E\subset V, set \[C_S(E;V)=\sup_{h\in\mathcal C_b(V),\,0\le h\le1}T_{S,q}(h,\ldots,h)(E),\qquad C_S^*(E;V)=\inf_{\substack{E\subset G\subset V\\G\ {\rm ordinary\ open}}}C_S(G;V).\] The second formula also defines C_S^* for arbitrary subsets. All null-set and quasi-everywhere statements below use this outer capacity with the specified background S.

title: Relative null sets and completed representatives
text: A set N\subset V is locally S-outer-null if C^*_{S|\Omega}(N\cap L;\Omega)=0 for every ordinary open \Omega\subset V and compact L\Subset\Omega. Such sets form the relative local null ideal. A statement holds relatively quasi-everywhere if its exceptional set is in this ideal; two Borel representatives define the same relative class when {u\ne v} is locally outer-null. Local truncated capacity convergence of u_j to u means, for every such \Omega,L and every R,\delta>0, \[C^*_{S|\Omega}\!\left(L\cap{|\max(u_j,-R)-\max(u,-R)|>\delta};\Omega\right)\longrightarrow0.\]

title: Non-polar products
text: For negative extended classical potentials u_1,\ldots,u_b, let u_i^{(j)}=\max(u_i,-j) and E_j=\bigcap_i{u_i>-j}. Their non-polar product is the coefficient-measure limit \[\langle Du_1\wedge\cdots\wedge Du_b\wedge S\rangle=\lim_{j→\infty}\mathbf1_{E_j}T_{S,b}(u_1^{(j)},\ldots,u_b^{(j)}),\] whenever the increasing coefficient limits are locally finite. For b=q and a repeated potential u, denote the resulting top-degree measure by μ_u.

title: Strong first-energy completion
text: For u_i\inE¹_{S,\partial}(V), define B_S(u_0,\ldots,u_q)=\int_V(-u_0)\,T_{S,q}(u_1,\ldots,u_q) and e(u)=B_S(u,\ldots,u). Here T_{S,q} denotes the non-polar extension of the bounded product. Set \[I(u,v)=e(u)+e(v)-B_S(u,v,\ldots,v)-B_S(v,u,\ldots,u).\] A sequence is strongly Cauchy if \sup_{j,k\ge N}I(u_j,u_k)→0. The cone \mathscr C=\widehat{\mathcal E}^{1}_{\rm str}(V) consists of its Borel limits in every local truncated outer capacity, identified modulo the relative local null ideal. The completed energy and discrepancy are obtained from these approximating sequences; strong convergence means I(u_j,u)→0.

title: Energy differences and literal energy-dual measures
text: Set r(u)=e(u)^{1/(q+1)}. The energy-difference Banach space and its norm are \[\mathbb D_S=\mathscr C-\mathscr C,\qquad \|h\|_{\rm ed}=\inf_{h=a-b,\ a,b\in\mathscr C}{r(a)+r(b)}.\] Differences are Borel functions modulo the relative local null ideal. A positive Radon measure μ is a literal energy-dual datum if it vanishes on that ideal, every h\in\mathbb D_S is absolutely μ-integrable, and \ell_μ(h)=-\int_Vh\,dμ satisfies |\ell_μ(h)|\le C_μ\|h\|_{\rm ed} for all h. Its total mass on V may be infinite. The strong-continuous dual \mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^* consists of those \ell\in\mathbb D_S^* for which I(u_j,u)→0 in \mathscr C implies \ell(u_j)→\ell(u). Literal strong continuity asks for the stronger integral statement \int_V|u_j-u|\,dμ→0.

title: Source map, variational projection and normal probe
text: For u\in\mathscr C, let \widehatμ_u be its completed top-degree BT measure. The source map is J(u)(h)=-\int_Vh\,d\widehatμ_u. Its image J(\mathscr C)\subset\mathbb D_S^* is the source image. For \ell\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*, the variational projection is \Pi(\ell)=\operatorname*{argmax}_{v\in\mathscr C}{\ell(v)-e(v)/(q+1)}. Its normal residual is n=\ell-J(\Pi(\ell)), characterized by n(v)\le0 for v\in\mathscr C and n(\Pi(\ell))=0. Choose the bounded continuous classical potential -1<\psi_0<0 supplied by the geometric-probe construction: for every original compact smooth scalar \varphi, one has \psi_0\pm\varepsilon_\varphi\varphi\inE¹_{S,\partial}(V) for some \varepsilon_\varphi>0, with the same choices for all extending backgrounds. For a literal positive datum with \ell_μ\in\mathbb D_{S,\mathrm s}^*, its normal-probe defect is Ξ_{S,\psi_0}(μ)=-n(\psi_0). Its vanishing is equivalent to \widehatμ_{\Pi(\ell_μ)}=μ. The checkable-source problem asks for conditions on the given data that force this vanishing.

title: Boundary control in the completion
text: The actual boundary condition is \overline{{u<-t}}\Subset V for every t>0; the boundary condition on \mathscr C is inherited by strong approximation from E¹_{S,\partial}(V). For the weighted measures m_j=(-u_{0,j})T_{S,q}(u_{1,j},\ldots,u_{q,j}) of finitely many strongly Cauchy sequences, uniform boundary tightness means: for every \varepsilon>0, some compact H\Subset V satisfies \sup_jm_j(V\setminus H)<\varepsilon. This is the property whose preservation is sought under domain exhaustion.

title: Local singularity type
text: For negative actual classical potentials, u\preceq v near x means that u\le v+C on some ordinary neighborhood of x, for a finite constant C. They have the same local singularity type when both u\preceq v and v\preceq u. Thus bounded changes of singularity mean mutual bounded comparison, with the background S kept fixed when relative masses and energies are compared.
