They have the same local singularity type when both u\preceq v and v\preceq u. Thus bounded changes of singularity mean mutual bounded comparison, with the background S kept fixed when relative masses and energies are compared.

title: Green currents and the finite-energy extension
text: For a cycle Z of codimension r, let \delta_Z be its integration current and let \omega_Z be the prescribed representative of its class. A Green current is a current g_Z of bidegree (r-1,r-1) satisfying Dg_Z+\delta_Z=\omega_Z on the original compact smooth test forms. The finite-energy Green problem asks to construct classes of such currents for which mixed products are limits of integrable truncations, with presentation independence and Green symmetry. Choosing those classes and their intersection hypotheses is part of the problem.
excerpt: For a cycle Z of codimension r, let \delta_Z be its integration current and let \omega_Z be the prescribed representative of its class. A Green current is a current g_Z of bidegree (r-1,r-1) satisfying Dg_Z+\delta_Z=\omega_Z on the original compact smooth test forms.

title: Local finite-energy integrals for the arithmetic problem
text: The local input is the mixed-energy functional B_S(u_0,\ldots,u_q)=\int_V(-u_0)\,T_{S,q}(u_1,\ldots,u_q) on the stated finite-energy classes, using the non-polar product, together with its completed extension. The background, domain and boundary condition are part of the data. An adelic finite-energy intersection is the construction sought in Problem 7.5: select metrized line bundles with local terms extending the continuous intersection theory, and prove that the place-by-place sum converges and is independent of approximation. The admissible global metric class, summability and boundary conditions are to be specified by that construction.
excerpt: The local input is the mixed-energy functional B_S(u_0,\ldots,u_q)=\int_V(-u_0)\,T_{S,q}(u_1,\ldots,u_q) on the stated finite-energy classes, using the non-polar product, together with its completed extension. The background, domain and boundary condition are part of the data.

title: Local regularization
text: On relatively compact coordinate subdomains, psh functions admit decreasing smooth psh regularizations. Locally bounded classical psh potentials admit decreasing semipositive rational PL approximation over the original field, on one fixed ordinary neighbourhood. The decreasing approximants are rational PL; continuous stages also admit smooth positive approximation. This does not classify all current-positive functions as classical psh. The fixed-neighbourhood construction retains the original finite extension K/Q_p and its norm. The separate continuous current-positive regularization input has its own algebraic analytification hypotheses; it is not silently identified with this result. B01 B05 R01
excerpt: Locally bounded classical psh potentials admit decreasing semipositive rational PL approximation over the original field, on one fixed ordinary neighbourhood. The decreasing approximants are rational PL; continuous stages also admit smooth positive approximation. This does not classify all current-positive functions as classical psh.

title: Mixed products and continuity
text: Locally bounded psh potentials have positive, symmetric mixed products against a fixed positive closed current, with decreasing continuity. The fixed-background calculus is positive, separately closed, symmetric and local, with CLN estimates and weighted joint decreasing continuity. The weight is also a decreasing classical psh potential. Discontinuous potentials with an arbitrary moving background are not covered. The background is fixed, symmetric, middle-positive and separately d′- and d″-closed. The original compact smooth CLD tests are retained. The theorem includes the undifferentiated psh weight; it is not continuity for arbitrary moving Borel weights. B02 B03 M01 M02
excerpt: The fixed-background calculus is positive, separately closed, symmetric and local, with CLN estimates and weighted joint decreasing continuity. The weight is also a decreasing classical psh potential. Discontinuous potentials with an arbitrary moving background are not covered.

title: Intrinsic products
text: Where defined, non-pluripolar products depend on the currents, not on the choice of their local potentials. Individual curvature independence is proved. Continuous-coefficient degree-one relations and quadratic relations of joint residue rank at most two are handled. Full analytic-relation descent remains open. It is an additional quotient problem, not simply the classical change-of-potential theorem. The low-rank result concerns finite presentations in any ambient dimension. In the supplied normal-three models, the punctured action and central spherical pairing are established; cancellation of that pairing is not yet proved in general. M03 M04 M05 G07 G08 O01 O07
excerpt: Individual curvature independence is proved. Continuous-coefficient degree-one relations and quadratic relations of joint residue rank at most two are handled. Full analytic-relation descent remains open. It is an additional quotient problem, not simply the classical change-of-potential theorem.

title: Capacity and quasicontinuity
text: A psh function is continuous outside open sets of arbitrarily small ambient Bedford–Taylor capacity. Relative quasicontinuity and bounded decreasing convergence in capacity are established for the specified potential class and background. Relative capacity depends on the background and tester family. It is not automatically the ambient capacity of the complex benchmark. The relative theory uses the full family of normalized classical psh testers, not a selected finite test family. The ambient S=[1] theory and arbitrary-background relative theory are kept distinct. C01 C02
excerpt: Relative quasicontinuity and bounded decreasing convergence in capacity are established for the specified potential class and background. Relative capacity depends on the background and tester family. It is not automatically the ambient capacity of the complex benchmark.

title: Borel regularity and extremals
text: On bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains, ambient outer capacity is Choquet; compact capacity equals the extremal Monge–Ampère mass. The qualified ambient Choquet theory is available. Relative inner regularity is proved for specified finite-Hausdorff saturated sets and controlled backgrounds. Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity remains open. Universal raw-to-outer equality and extremal total-mass formulas are false. The relative positive case has remaining degree q=1 on a torus box, with S₀=βⁿ⁻¹[X] and fully saturated inverse images of Borel moment sets of finite (n−1)-dimensional Hausdorff measure, plus the stated one-sided background comparison. It is not a theorem for arbitrary Borel sets. Classical Borel capacitability is compact inner regularity of outer capacity; that is the open target, not raw=outer on every set. C05 N01 N02 N03 O03
excerpt: The qualified ambient Choquet theory is available. Relative inner regularity is proved for specified finite-Hausdorff saturated sets and controlled backgrounds. Borel inner regularity of relative outer capacity remains open. Universal raw-to-outer equality and extremal total-mass formulas are false.

title: Polar sets and comparison
text: On bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains, ambient outer-null sets are pluripolar. Bounded psh functions satisfy comparison and domination with boundary hypotheses. For S=[1], local polar, outer-null and negligible sets coincide. Compact-boundary-gap comparison and the specified relative domination principles are proved. An arbitrary background may charge ambient polar sets. Pointwise detection from a relative capacity class needs additional geometry. The S=[1] equivalence is local; the Choquet and extremal package retains its exhaustion-domain assumptions. The relative domination proposition initially gives a raw-capacity conclusion: it must not be relabelled as outer-null without an additional argument. C02 C03
excerpt: For S=[1], local polar, outer-null and negligible sets coincide. Compact-boundary-gap comparison and the specified relative domination principles are proved. An arbitrary background may charge ambient polar sets. Pointwise detection from a relative capacity class needs additional geometry.

title: Unbounded, non-polar products
text: On compact Kähler manifolds, non-pluripolar products are well-defined and closed. Monotone Monge–Ampère continuity is available in the full-mass class. Common truncations yield closed non-polar products when coefficient masses are locally finite. In the stated boundary class, no loss is characterized by a capacity tail. The local relative construction does not automatically supply the global compact-Kähler finiteness package. Finiteness and no-loss assumptions matter on both sides. Within the stated zero-boundary class, no loss is equivalent to t^q C_S({u<-t};V)→0. The negative sublevels must have ordinary closures compact in V. Closedness belongs to the locally coefficient-finite limit, not necessarily to each restricted truncation current. BEGZ Example 1.3 also excludes unrestricted local unbounded products in complex geometry. U01 U02 N05
excerpt: Common truncations yield closed non-polar products when coefficient masses are locally finite. In the stated boundary class, no loss is characterized by a capacity tail. The local relative construction does not automatically supply the global compact-Kähler finiteness package. Finiteness and no-loss assumptions matter on both sides.

title: Finite energy and completion
text: On a compact connected Kähler manifold, (E¹,d₁) is the metric completion of smooth Kähler potentials. Power-energy classes and mixed Green–Hölder estimates are constructed. The relative strong first-energy completion has an intrinsic Borel realization and is complete. Canonical ambient classical psh representatives and extension beyond the specified domains remain separate problems; the completion alone does not supply them. The domain is a strict Laurent box with closure compact inside an affinoid interior and a background extending to an ordinary neighbourhood of that closure. Strong convergence is capacity convergence plus energy convergence. All positive power classes and the stated weighted-current degree budgets are retained. Order completion of currents, strong completion of potentials and capacity-Borel realization are not identified. U03 U04 E01 E02 E03
excerpt: Power-energy classes and mixed Green–Hölder estimates are constructed. The relative strong first-energy completion has an intrinsic Borel realization and is complete. Canonical ambient classical psh representatives and extension beyond the specified domains remain separate problems; the completion alone does not supply them.

title: Envelopes and rooftops
text: In a fixed Kähler class, rooftop envelopes contract d₁ and express it through the Aubin–Mabuchi energy. Relative Perron envelopes, finite rooftops and the stated Borel obstacle problems are constructed in the completed cone. The fixed-background ordered-rooftop estimates proposed for literal-dual continuity are still a route to prove, not a consequence of existence. The envelope uses the relative quasi-everywhere order in the completed cone; it is not automatically ordinary ambient upper-semicontinuous regularization. Darvas’s d₁ formula is not the coefficient-one inequality for the project’s different homogeneous energy. E04 N04 O04
excerpt: Relative Perron envelopes, finite rooftops and the stated Borel obstacle problems are constructed in the completed cone. The fixed-background ordered-rooftop estimates proposed for literal-dual continuity are still a route to prove, not a consequence of existence.

title: Strong integral continuity
text: For μ=MA(v) with v\inE¹ in a fixed compact Kähler class, d₁-convergence implies L¹(μ)-convergence. The energy-difference space is Banach. Strong literal integral continuity is proved under fixed-source domination or the stated capacity-control hypotheses. For fixed S, does global literal energy-dual boundedness imply strong L¹(μ)-continuity? The source-class benchmark does not answer this larger question. The question assumes a positive Radon measure annihilating the relative null ideal, literal integrability of every completed Borel difference, and a bounded integral functional on the entire energy-difference Banach space. Total mass need not be finite. Nonliteral functionals, bounds on only one witness sequence, and changing-background examples do not refute this fixed-background question. Q01 Q04 N12 O04
excerpt: The energy-difference space is Banach. Strong literal integral continuity is proved under fixed-source domination or the stated capacity-control hypotheses. For fixed S, does global literal energy-dual boundedness imply strong L¹(μ)-continuity? The source-class benchmark does not answer this larger question.

title: Prescribing a source measure
text: In a fixed compact Kähler class, a normalized finite-energy measure is the Monge–Ampère measure of a unique finite-energy current. The source image is norm closed. Strongly continuous data have a unique variational projection. For such literal positive data, the equation holds exactly when Ξ=0. Data-side conditions forcing Ξ=0 remain to be found beyond compatible classes. Smooth positive perturbations need not remain in the source image. Here the positive Radon datum defines a literal, norm-bounded integral functional on all completed differences, with a strongly continuous restriction to the cone. The defect is evaluated using the variational projection; its vanishing is an exact criterion, not an independent test already computable from arbitrary data. A variational maximizer need not satisfy the equation in the prescribed potential cone. Source compatibility is separate from strong integral continuity. Q01 Q02 Q03 Q07 Q08 N06 O05
excerpt: The source image is norm closed. Strongly continuous data have a unique variational projection. For such literal positive data, the equation holds exactly when Ξ=0. Data-side conditions forcing Ξ=0 remain to be found beyond compatible classes. Smooth positive perturbations need not remain in the source image.

title: Boundary-value problems
text: On bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains, continuous boundary data and a nonnegative continuous density admit a unique continuous psh Monge–Ampère solution. For remaining degree q=1, finite signed energy-diffuse data have a unique renormalized zero-boundary solution in the faithful part-energy space. Not the same equation: this is a signed linear problem, not a general nonlinear Monge–Ampère boundary-value theorem. Here q=n−p=1 is the remaining degree, not a restriction to ambient dimension one. The faithful, regular, strongly local, coercive part-form hypotheses and energy-capacity diffuseness are retained. The solution space is not identified with the classical psh cone or the nonlinear strong first-energy cone; clipping and total-variation stability hold in the stated linear space. Q05 Q06
excerpt: For remaining degree q=1, finite signed energy-diffuse data have a unique renormalized zero-boundary solution in the faithful part-energy space. Not the same equation: this is a signed linear problem, not a general nonlinear Monge–Ampère boundary-value theorem.

title: Unconditional relative capacity identities
text: Raw capacity need not equal its outer regularization, even on compact sets. A universal extremal total-mass formula also fails. This contrasts with the stated ambient complex theorem, not with every complex relative capacity. The ratio in the internal mass example varies with scale.
excerpt: Raw capacity need not equal its outer regularization, even on compact sets. A universal extremal total-mass formula also fails.

title: Strong subadditivity of relative outer capacity
text: An original torus example with q=1 and n≥2 violates strong subadditivity. Ordinary subadditivity survives. This does not settle Borel inner regularity. No general classical strong-subadditivity theorem is being asserted here.
excerpt: An original torus example with q=1 and n≥2 violates strong subadditivity. Ordinary subadditivity survives.

title: A universal coefficient-one rooftop bound
text: For the project’s rooftop energy inequality in remaining degree one, constant 1 is false; constant 2 is sharp across allowed backgrounds. The inequality is e(P_S(u,v))≤ C(e(u)+e(v)). This is not Darvas’s d₁ contraction formula. It does not invalidate the mixed Green–Hölder constant 1 or settle fixed-S literal continuity.
excerpt: For the project’s rooftop energy inequality in remaining degree one, constant 1 is false; constant 2 is sharp across allowed backgrounds.

title: Universal solvability under small smooth perturbations
text: A fixed strict source admits smooth positive density perturbations converging uniformly to 1 that lie outside the strong-completion source image. These data retain source domination and literal strong continuity. Solving the signed linear equation in a larger part-energy space does not restore a solution in the prescribed cone.
excerpt: A fixed strict source admits smooth positive density perturbations converging uniformly to 1 that lie outside the strong-completion source image.
